en: The Gaṇḍavyūha Sūtra.
1 // The Chapter on the Introduction // Om, homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Thus have I heard.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, in the Great Arrayed Gabled Hall, together with about five thousand bodhisattvas, headed by the bodhisattvas Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.
Namely, by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jñānottarajñānin, by Sattvottarajñānin,
and by Asaṅgottarajñānin.
And by Kusumottarajñānin,
and by Sūryottarajñānin, and by Candrottarajñānin.
And by Vimalottarajñānin, and by Vajrottarajñānin, and by Virajottarajñānin.
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vairocanottarajñānin.
And with Jyotirdhvaja, and Merudhvaja, and Ratnadhvaja.
And with Asaṅgadhvaja, and Kusumadhvaja, and Vimaladhvaja.
And with Sūryadhvaja,
Ruciradhvaja, and Virajadhvaja.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vairocanadhvaja;
And with Ratnatejas, and Mahātejas, and Jñānavajratejas.
And by Vimalatejas,
and by Dharmasūryatejas, and by Puṇyaparvatatejas.
And by the splendor of the light of knowledge;
and by the splendor of universal glory;
and by the splendor of universal radiance.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaprabhaśrītejas.
And with Dhāraṇīgarbha,
Gaganagarbha, and Padmagarbha;
And by Ratnagarbha,
and by Sūryagarbha, and by Guṇaviśuddhigarbha.
And with Dharmasamudragarbha, and Vairocanagarbha, and Nābhigarbha;
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Padmaśrīgarbha.
And by Sunetra, and by Viśuddhanetra, and by Vimalanetra.
And with Asaṅganetra,
and Samantadarśananetra, and Suvilokitanetra.
And with Avalokitanetra,
and with Utpalanetra,
and with Vajranetra.
And with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnanetra, and Gagananetra, and Samantanetra.
And with the Devamukuṭa,
the Dharmadhātupratibhāsa-maṇimukuṭa, and the Bodhimaṇḍamukuṭa.
And with the Diśvairocana-crown;
and with the crown-jewel containing the matrix from which all Buddhas arise;
and with the crown risen above all world-systems.
And with the crown of universal Vairocana;
and with the crown of the unconquerable;
and with the jewel crown established upon the lion-thrones of all the Tathāgatas.
and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantadharmadhātugaganapratibhāsamukuṭa;
And with Brahmendracūḍa, and Nāgendracūḍa, and Sarvabuddhanirmāṇapratibhāsacūḍa.
And with Bodhimaṇḍacūḍa;
and with Sarvapraṇidhānasāgaranirghoṣamaṇirājacūḍa;
and with Sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalapramuñcanamaṇiratnanigarjitacūḍa.
And with [the Bodhisattva] Sarvākāśatalāsaṃbhedavijñaptimaṇiratnavibhūṣitacūḍa (Adorned-Crest with Jewels Manifesting the Undifferentiated Surface of All Space);

and with [the Bodhisattva] Sarvatathāgatavikurvitapratibhāsadhvajamaṇirājajālasaṃchāditacūḍa (Crest Covered by a Net of King-Jewels Reflecting the Miraculous Displays of All Tathāgatas); and with [the Bodhisattva] Sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣacūḍa (Crest Resounding with the Wheel of Dharma of All Tathāgatas).
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvatryadhvanāmacakranirghoṣacūḍa.
And with Mahāprabha, and Vimalaprabha, and Vimalatejaḥprabha.
And by Ratnaprabha, and by Virajaprabha, and by Jyotiṣprabha.
And Dharmaprabha, and Śāntiprabha, and Sūryaprabha.
And with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vikurvitaprabha, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva Devaprabha.
And with Puṇyaketu,
Jñānaketu, and Dharmaketu.
And by Abhijñāketu,
Prabhāketu, and Kusumaketu.
And Bodhiketun, and Brahmaketun, and Samantāvabhāsaketun.
And with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maṇiketun.
And with the voice of Brahmā,
and with the voice of the ocean,
and with the voice of the resonance of the earth.
And by Lokendraghoṣa,
and by Śailendrarājasaṃghaṭṭanaghoṣa, and by Sarvadharmadhātuspharaṇaghoṣa.
And with a voice like the thundering roar of the ocean of the entire realm of phenomena; and with a voice that crushes the mandalas of all Māras;
and with a voice like the thundering roar of the clouds of the method of great compassion.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvajagadduḥkhapraśāntyāśvāsanaghoṣa, and by Dharmodgata,
and by Viśeṣodgata.
And by Jñānodgata, and by Puṇyasumerūdgata, and by Guṇaprabhāvodgata.
And Yaśodgata, and Samantāvabhāsodgata, and Mahāmaitryudgata.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has emerged from the accumulation of gnosis, and who has emerged from the lineage and family of the Tathāgatas.
And with Prabhāśrī, and with Pravaraśrī, and with Samudgataśrī.
And by Vairocanaśrī,
and by Dharmaśrī, and by Candraśrī.
And Gaganashrī, and Ratnashrī, and Ketushrī.
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jñānaśrī.
And by Śailendrarāja, and by Dharmendrarāja, and by Jagadindrarāja.
And by Brahmendrarāja,
and by Gaṇendrarāja,
and by Devendrarāja.
And by Śāntendrarāja, and by Acalendrarāja, and by Ṛṣabhendrarāja.
And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pravarendrarāja.
And with a tranquil voice,
and with an unattached voice,
and with a voice like the resonance of the earth.
And with the voice that resounds like the ocean,
and with the voice that has the resonance of thunderclouds,
and with the voice that illuminates the Dharma.
And with a voice like the resonance of space; with a voice like the thundering of the roots of virtue of all sentient beings;
and with a voice that exhorts according to former vows.
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Māramaṇḍalanirghoṣasvara;
And by Ratnabuddhi,
and by Jñānabuddhi,
and by Gaganabuddhi.
And by Asaṅgabuddhi,
and by Vimalabuddhi,
and by Viśuddhabuddhi.
And with Viśālabuddhi, who possesses the intellect that illuminates the three times; and with Samantāvalokabuddhi.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Dharmadhātunayāvabhāsabuddhi;

Led by these, there were about five thousand bodhisattvas, all of whom had set out through the vows and conduct of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra; whose range was unimpeded by pervading all buddha-fields;
who possessed infinite empowerments of bodies by approaching all Tathāgatas;
and whose eye-spheres were purified by the absence of obscuration through seeing all the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas.

Through their manifestations, they have reached the immeasurable state by never ceasing to approach the gateways of the perfect awakening of all Tathāgatas; they possess infinite light by having attained the illumination of the knowledge of the methods of the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas;
and they provide inexhaustible explanations of qualities throughout infinite eons through the purity of their analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*).
By means of manifesting form-bodies to the world according to its inclinations, through a purity that is not constrained by the sphere of knowledge as vast as the element of space;
by being free from darkness, through the thorough understanding of the realm of sentient beings as being without a self or a life-principle;
and by possessing wisdom equal to the sky, through the radiation of a web of light-rays throughout the entire realm of phenomena.

And there were five hundred great disciples of great supernatural power, all of whom had fully awakened to the intrinsic nature of the principle of truth; who had directly realized the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); who had entered into the fundamental nature of phenomena (*dharmaprakṛti*); who had emerged from the ocean of existence; whose sphere of activity was the sky of the Tathāgatas;

who had turned back the fetters, latent tendencies, and habitual propensities; who made their home in the unattached abode; who dwelt in the tranquility of space; who had completely severed longing for the Buddhas, as well as doubt and hesitation; and who had entered the path of resolute conviction in the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom.
And by the lords of the world, who had previously performed their duties under former Victors,
who were dedicated to the welfare and happiness of the entire world, who were unasked spiritual friends,
who were committed to protecting other beings, and who had descended into the bliss of knowledge that exists for the excellence of the world.

They possessed minds that never abandon any sentient being; they had emerged into the domain of the Buddha’s teaching; they were committed to protecting the Tathāgata’s dispensation; they were born from the vow to sustain the lineage of the Buddhas; they were oriented toward being born into the family and clan of the Tathāgatas;
and they longed for the wisdom of omniscience.

Then, indeed, this thought occurred to those bodhisattvas with their retinues, to those śrāvakas of great supernatural power, and to those lords of the world with their retinues: "It is not possible for the world, including its gods, to [comprehend] the domain of the Tathāgata, the range of the Tathāgata's knowledge, the empowerment of the Tathāgata, the power of the Tathāgata, the fearlessness of the Tathāgata, or the samādhi of the Tathāgata."

To comprehend, to plunge into, to resolve upon, to discern, to understand, to investigate, to analyze, to differentiate, to elucidate, or to establish within the mental continuums of other beings the dwelling of the Tathāgata, the sovereignty of the Tathāgata, the body of the Tathāgata, and the wisdom of the Tathāgata— [this is impossible].

Except through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, the miraculous display of the Tathāgata, the majestic power of the Tathāgata, the former vows of the Tathāgata, the well-performed roots of virtue from previous buddhas, the protection of spiritual friends, the purification of the eye of faith and knowledge, the attainment of the illumination of noble resolve, the purification of the bodhisattva’s superior intention, and the undertaking of the vow for omniscience through that superior intention.

"May the Blessed One indeed [reveal the truth] for us Bodhisattvas according to our inclinations, and for all sentient beings, by virtue of their diversity of disposition, their diversity of resolve, their diversity of awakening, their attainment of a diversity of verbal conventions, their establishment on various sovereign stages, their purity of various faculties, their various applications of intent, and their various spheres of volition."

He would display their former setting out toward omniscience for those who rely on the various qualities of the Tathāgatas and who are oriented toward the various directions of the teachings of the Dharma;
he would display their former accomplishment of the bodhisattva vows;
and he would display their former purification of the mandala of the bodhisattva perfections.
He would manifest the miraculous display of ascending the stages of a bodhisattva in the past; he would manifest the fulfillment and accomplishment of the mandala of past bodhisattva practices;
and he would manifest the illumination of the array of accomplishments of the past bodhisattva vehicle.
He would manifest the purification of the array of the former bodhisattva path;
he would also manifest the arrays of the accomplishment of the oceans of methods for the former bodhisattva’s departure [from the world];
and he would also manifest the arrays of the oceans of miraculous transformations of the former bodhisattva’s realization.
He may also manifest oceans of the former lives of bodhisattvas; he may also manifest oceans of miraculous transformations at the gateway of perfect enlightenment;
and he may also manifest the sovereign power of the Tathāgata’s miraculous transformations in setting the wheel of Dharma in motion.

He may also manifest oceans of the miraculous transformations of the purification of the Tathāgata’s buddha-fields; he may also manifest the gateways of skillful means for disciplining the realm of sentient beings by the Tathāgata;
and he may also manifest the sovereign majesty of the city of the Dharma of the Tathāgata’s omniscience.
He may also manifest the illumination of the paths of all sentient beings by the Tathāgatas;
he may also manifest the miraculous displays of entering the abodes of sentient beings as a Tathāgata;
and he may also manifest the acceptance of offerings from sentient beings as a Tathāgata.

He may also manifest the miracles of the Tathāgata’s teaching on the merit and offerings of all sentient beings; he may also manifest the perceptions of the Buddha’s reflection within the mental movements of all sentient beings;
and he may also manifest the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata for the sake of sentient beings.
He should also manifest the miracles of the Tathāgata’s teachings and instructions for all sentient beings;
he should also manifest the miraculous transformations within the range of the inconceivable Buddha-samādhis of the Tathāgata for all sentient beings.

Then the Blessed One, knowing with his own mind the reflection in the minds of those bodhisattvas, entered the samādhi called Lion’s Yawn, which is the body of great compassion, the gateway of great compassion, preceded by great compassion, following the sky of the dharma of great compassion, and the array that illuminates the world.
And as soon as the Blessed One had entered [meditative absorption], the Great Array Pavilion became established, vast and without end or middle.
Its ground was an array of the invincible vajra-earth, its surface established with nets of all kinds of jewel-kings, strewn with many precious flower-blossoms,
scattered with great precious jewels, adorned with pillars of beryl, and beautifully decorated with the arrangement of the jewel-king that illuminates the world.

It was a mass composed of all kinds of jewels, adorned with a peak of Jāmbūnada gold and mani-gems; it possessed a pure array of countless balconies, gateways, palaces, windows, and railings made of every kind of jewel;

it displayed an arrangement of mani-jewels resembling the lords of all worlds and an array of mani-jewels like the ocean of the world-system; it was covered entirely by mani-jewels, with parasols, banners, and flags raised high; and through the faces of its arrays of gateways and arches, it manifested an array of radiating nets of light-rays from the *dharmadhātu*.
On the outside, there was an array of platforms on the ground of the inexpressibly vast assembly circle, with jeweled gem-stūpas serving as stairways to the directions on all sides,
most exquisitely divided and adorned;
and the entire Jeta Grove became established with vastly expanded length and breadth.
And by the power of the Buddha, those buddha-fields—equal in number to the atoms of unspeakably many buddha-fields—became established with vast length and breadth;

they were adorned with various arrays of all kinds of jewels, their ground surfaces were established as variegated with unspeakable gems, they were encircled by walls of incalculable mani-jewels, and they became established with arrays of rows of various jeweled palm trees.

And within them, immeasurable rivers of fragrant water stood, filled with fragrant waters swirling in endless eddies, turbid with floods of all kinds of jewel-flowers, flowing in a clockwise direction, and arrayed with the resounding echoes of the voices of all Buddhas;
there were also inconceivable rows of jewel-white lotuses, and jewel-trees whose surfaces were adorned by arrays of blossoming lotuses rising from every kind of gem.

And there stood inconceivable rows of multi-storied pavilions made of various jewels, covered with nets of all kinds of precious gems, adorned with arrays of light from the nets of rays of innumerable jewel-gems,
featuring innumerable jewel-gem palaces and arrays of every kind of precious gem, emitting caskets of all fragrances, and arrayed with layers of all types of incense;
as well as immeasurable jeweled banners.

In this way, there were banners of cloth, banners of flags, banners of jeweled bands, banners of flowers, banners of ornaments, banners of garlands, banners of nets of all kinds of jewel-bells, banners of royal jewel-parasols radiating universal light,
banners of the king of jewel-gems resounding with the wheel of the names of all Tathāgatas, and banners of the king of lion-lovely jewel-gems.

There stood the victory banners of the jewel-kings of mani-gems, resounding with the ancient vows of all Tathāgatas; victory banners of mani-jewel kings reflecting the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); and arrays of victory banners adorned with every kind of ornament, beautifully distributed in all directions.
Furthermore, the entire Jeta Grove became established as an adornment for the expanse of the sky, filled with inconceivable clouds of celestial palaces.

It was adorned by a canopy of clouds of incalculable trees of every fragrance; it was adorned by a canopy of clouds of inexpressible Sumeru mountains of every array; it was adorned by the sweet resonance of the chorus of praises to all the Tathāgatas, like clouds of inexpressible musical instruments and cymbals.
It was adorned with clouds of unspeakably many jewel-lotuses;
it was adorned with the sweet resonance of clouds of praises to the Tathāgatas by Bodhisattvas seated upon divine jewel-gem-studded lion-thrones made of unspeakably many jewels;
it was adorned with clouds of mani-jewel forms facing [the Buddha], resembling the images of unspeakably many lords of gods.

It became adorned with clouds of unspeakably white pearl nets, adorned with clouds of unspeakably red pearl gabled mansions covering all, and adorned with the raining down of clouds of unspeakably diamond-essence pearls.
For what reason?
Because that root of merit of the Tathāgata is inconceivable,
and that accumulation of the Tathāgata’s pure qualities is inconceivable.
Inconceivable is the empowerment of the Tathāgata’s buddha-sovereignty; inconceivable is the miraculous manifestation of the Tathāgata’s single body pervading all world-systems;

inconceivable is the display of the empowerment that causes all the arrays of all Buddha-fields to enter and converge within the single body of every Tathāgata; and inconceivable is the display of the representation of the reflection of the entire realm of phenomena within a single atom-dust of the Tathāgatas.
Inconceivable is the manifestation, within a single pore of the Tathāgatas,
of the succession of all Tathāgatas throughout the limits of the past;
inconceivable is the illumination, by a single ray of light from the mouth of the Tathāgatas, of the expansion of atoms of dust in all world-systems.
Inconceivable is the Tathāgatas’ emanation of clouds equal in number to the atoms of all world-systems from a single pore, pervading all Buddha-fields;
inconceivable also is the Tathāgatas’ manifestation of the cycles of dissolution and evolution of all world-systems from a single pore.
And just as this Jeta Grove is established, purified by such purity of a Buddha-field, so too is it.

In this way, throughout the ten directions, all world-systems as far as the ultimate limit of the realm of phenomena and the realm of space—completely pure, established, adorned, and embellished; pervaded by the body of the Tathāgata; converging at the Jeta Grove; filled with bodhisattvas; well-arranged as oceans of circles of the Tathāgata’s assemblies; and raining down clouds of every kind of array—remain thus.
They were illuminated by the radiance of all jewels; adorned with a rain of clouds of every kind of precious gem;
adorned with a covering of clouds of the arrays of all buddha-fields;
adorned with a rain of clouds of all celestial bodies; and adorned with a rain of clouds of every flower.
They were adorned with the expansion of well-flowered buds;
they were treasure-troves that released a rain of excellent robes of various beautiful colors from clouds of all kinds of garments;
and they were adorned by the pouring down of continuous streams covered by clouds of magnificent arrays of all manner of garlands and wreaths.
They were adorned by a rain of clouds of various fragrant incenses arising from all directions, whose forms resembled the bodies of all living beings;

they were adorned by a rain of fine powders from nets of jewels, covered by clouds of nets of all kinds of jewel-flowers; they were adorned by clouds of all kinds of jeweled banners and pennants, which, held in the hands of celestial maidens, revolved and turned within the expanse of the sky;

they were adorned by the sweet resonance produced by the striking together of musical instruments attached to the stamens of upward-pointing stalks upon circular mandalas of various jeweled petals made of all kinds of precious lotuses.
Various ornaments consisting of nets of images made of all kinds of jewels, lion-cages, and necklaces and garlands variegated with diverse gems were seen standing there.
As soon as the Blessed One had entered this Tathāgata-samādhi called the Lion’s Yawn,
at that very moment, beyond world-oceans in the eastern direction equal in number to the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
[there was] the world-system Kanakameghapradīpadhvajā, [where dwelt] the Tathāgata Vairocanaśrītejorāja.
From that buddha-field, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vairocanapraṇidhānanābhiraśmiprabha, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields,
having been permitted by that Blessed One, rose up from that ocean-like assembly circle and approached the Sahā world-system,
adorning the expanse of the sky with clouds of various arrays.
That is to say, raining down a rain of clouds of celestial flowers,
emitting a rain of clouds of celestial fragrances,
and scattering a rain of clouds of celestial jewel-lotuses.
They released a rain from clouds of divine garlands, showered down a rain from clouds of divine jewels,
and poured forth a rain from clouds of divine ornaments.
Manifesting clouds of celestial jewel parasols,
raining down showers of fine celestial garments of various wonderful colors,
and establishing clouds of celestial jewel banners and pennants in the expanse of the sky;

Illuminating the expanse of the sky with beautiful arrays of clouds of all kinds of jewels, he approached the Blessed One together with his retinue; having paid homage to the Blessed One, he took his place facing the eastern direction,
[establishing] gabled palaces covered by nets of *samantavyūha* jewel-gems, with interiors like lotuses made of the king of light-shining jewels.
Having manifested lion thrones, he sat down cross-legged, having empowered the bodies of the bodhisattvas so that they were covered with networks of wish-fulfilling king-jewel ornaments.
In the southern direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
from the world-system named Vajrasāgaragarbhā, the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Samantāvabhāsaśrīgarbharāja,
there came the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Duryodhanavīryavegarāja, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Having been authorized by that Blessed One, he then rose up from the ocean-like assembly circle and approached the Sahā world-system,
sustaining all the oceans of worlds covered with nets of garlands of every kind of fragrance,
and sustaining the expansions of all Buddha-fields covered with nets of garlands of every kind of jewel necklace.
He sustained all lineages of buddha-fields covered by great nets of flower-garlands; he sustained all successions of buddha-fields covered by great nets of garland-strings;
and he sustained all circles of assemblies in buddha-fields, supported from below by great vajra-chains.

He empowered all the systems of Buddha-fields so that they were covered by nets of every kind of jewel; he empowered all world-systems so that they were embraced on all sides by garlands of every kind of cloth; he manifested all Buddha-fields so that they were covered by nets of clusters of necklaces and garlands of images made of every kind of gem; and he empowered all fields so that they were covered by nets of necklaces and garlands of precious jewels emitting glorious rays of light.
He empowered all buddha-fields so that they were covered by nets of strings of the king of Vaiḍūrya jewels, which radiated light from all arrays of rays;
he empowered all world-systems so that they were supported by networks of necklaces and strings of lion-lovely jewel-gems.
Then, approaching the Blessed One together with his retinue, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stationed himself toward the southern direction.
Having miraculously created gabled palaces made of jewels that illuminate the world and lion thrones with lotus-calixes of gems that radiate light in all directions,
he sat down cross-legged, having empowered his bodhisattva bodies so that they were covered with ornaments of nets of every kind of jewel and flower.

In the western direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, from the world-system called Maṇisumerūvirocanadhvajapradīpa, the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Dharmadhātujñānapradīpa,
there came the Bodhisattva named Samantaśrīsamudgatarāja, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans.
Permitted by the Blessed One, he then rose from the circle of the assembly and proceeded toward the Sahā world-system,
pervading the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with clouds of Mount Sumeru-like banners of various colors and fragrances as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
and pervading the entire realm of phenomena with clouds of various fragrant flowers as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Pervading the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with clouds of *Sumeru*-like incense of many colors and fragrances, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
pervading the entire realm of phenomena with clouds of various colors and fragrances, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

and pervading the entire realm of phenomena with clouds of *Sumeru*-like kings of jewels arising from the radiance of his pores, possessing colors identical to all articles of luxury, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.

Pervading the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with clouds of Sumeru mountains of *maṇi* jewels named "Luminous Banner," which consist of various arrays of circles of light and are as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields; pervading the entire realm of phenomena with clouds of Sumeru mountains of various arrays of sovereign *vajragarbha* jewels of diverse colors,

and pervading the entire realm of phenomena with clouds of Sumeru mountains of *jāmbūnada* gold *maṇi* jewels whose range reflects all world-systems, each as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.

He sustained the expanse of the sky as covered by clouds of Sumeru mountains made of the finest jewel-kings that reflected all the mountains of the dharma-realm, equal in number to the atoms within ineffable Buddha-fields;

and he pervaded the entire domain of the dharma-realm with clouds of Sumeru mountains made of the finest jewel-kings that reflected the marks of all Tathāgatas, equal in number to the atoms within ineffable Buddha-fields.

With clouds of Sumeru-mountains of jewel-kings whose sounds proclaim the conduct of bodhisattvas, manifesting the reflections of the former practices of all Tathāgatas— equal in number to the atoms within ineffable Buddha-fields— they pervaded the sky of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with clouds of Sumeru-mountains of jewel-kings reflecting the seats of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Tathāgatas, equal in number to the atoms within ineffable Buddha-fields. Spreading through the ten directions, they approached the Blessed One together with their retinue, and having paid homage to the Blessed One, [they remained there].
Relying upon the western direction,

he manifested multi-storied pavilions covered with nets of pearls from the body of the King of All Fragrances, as well as lion thrones whose cores were lotuses made of the jewel-gems of the Banner of the Reflection of the Lord of Gods; having manifested these, he sat down cross-legged on seats covered with the finest gold and jewels and adorned with crowns of the King of Thought.
Having empowered the bodies of the bodhisattvas.
In the northern direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,

in the world-system called Ratnavastrāvabhāsadhvaja, from the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Dharmadhātugaganaśrīvairocana, there came the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Asaṅgaśrīrāja, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans.
Permitted by the Blessed One, he then rose up from the ocean-like assembly circle and approached the Sahā world-system,
presiding over the expanse of the sky adorned with clouds of banners of all kinds of jewels,
and presiding over the expanse of the sky adorned with clouds of yellow-colored, yellow-shining jewel-garments.

He presided over the expanse of the sky adorned by clouds of jewel-garments perfumed with various fragrances; he presided over the expanse of the sky adorned by clouds of jewel-kings with sun-like banners as their garments; he presided over the expanse of the sky adorned by clouds of golden-glory-blazing jewel-garments.

He presided over the expanse of the sky adorned with clouds of garments of the king of jewels blazing with light; he presided over the expanse of the sky adorned with clouds of variegated jewel-garments reflecting the images of all luminaries;
he presided over the expanse of the sky pervading the ten directions with clouds of jewel-garments shining like the surface of the Pāṇḍukambala stone.

Presiding over a canopy of clouds of Vairocana-Śrījvalanāvabhāsa jewel-kings’ garments that pervaded the ten directions, presiding over a canopy of clouds of Vairocana jewel-kings’ garments that blazed with light and pervaded the ten directions,
and presiding over a canopy of clouds of Sāgara-vyūha jewel-kings’ garments covering the expanse of the sky, he approached the place where the Blessed One was.

Together with his retinue, he paid homage to the Blessed One and, taking his position in the northern direction, he manifested palatial towers made of the king of ocean-born jewels and lion thrones with cores of beryl and lotuses; having assumed the cross-legged posture, he sat down, presiding over the bodies of the bodhisattvas which were covered by nets of the king of lion-striding jewels and crowned with crests of light-bannered jewels.
In the northeastern direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,

from the world-system called Sarvamahāpṛthivīrājamaṇiraśmijālapramuktā belonging to the Tathāgata Anilambhacakṣus, there came forth the Bodhisattva named Dharmadhātusunirmitapraṇidhicandra, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans.
Permitted by the Blessed One, he then rose up from the ocean-like assembly circle and approached the Sahā world-system.
There, he sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of jewel-pavilions,
and he sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of fragrance-pavilions.
He sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of incense-pavilions;
he sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of sandalwood-pavilions;
he sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of flower-pavilions.
He sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of jeweled gabled palaces; he sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of vajra gabled palaces;
he sustained all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of golden gabled palaces.
Sustaining all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of cloth-palaces,

and sustaining all the expansions of world-systems covered by clouds of lotus-palaces, he approached the Blessed One together with his retinue; having paid homage to the Blessed One, he took his place in the northeastern direction, [manifesting] great jewel-palaces with peaks whose doors face the entire realm of phenomena and are composed of all kinds of jewels.

Having miraculously created lion thrones with lotus-calices made of incomparable king-of-scented-gems, he sat down cross-legged; and having empowered the bodies of the bodhisattvas, which were covered by nets of flower-kings and adorned with jeweled crowns bound with various networks of sheaths, he took his seat.
In the southeastern direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,

from the world-system called Gandhameghavyūhadhvajā, which belongs to the Tathāgata Nāgeśvararāja, there came forth the Bodhisattva named Dharmārciṣmattejorāja, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many oceans of worlds.
Permitted by the Blessed One, he then emerged from the ocean of methods of the assembly circle and proceeded toward the Sahā world-system,
covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of golden-hued light-mandalas,
and covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of light-mandalas of jewels of infinite colors.
Covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of light-orbs the color of the ūrṇā-hair of the Tathāgata;
covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of light-orbs the color of various precious jewels;
covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of light-orbs from the interior of lotuses.
Covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of jewel-tree branch-circles and the colored light-orbs of the finest gems;

covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of the colored light-orbs of the Tathāgata’s uṣṇīṣa; and covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of the colored light-orbs of Jāmbūnada gold.
Covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of light-mandalas having the color of the sun’s radiance,

and covering the entire expanse of the sky with clouds of moon-light-circle-colored mandalas, he approached the Blessed One, and together with his retinue, having paid homage to the Blessed One, he took his place toward the southeastern direction, [bringing] the Vimalavairocana-maṇi-śrī-kusuma gabled palace.

Having miraculously manifested lion-thrones with lion-vajra-jewel-lotus cores, he sat down, having crossed his legs in the lotus posture, and empowered his bodhisattva bodies so that they were covered by king-jewels blazing with jewel-rays.
In the southwestern direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields,
from the world-system called Maṇisūryapratibhāsagarbhā, which belongs to the Tathāgata Dharmacandrasamantajñānāvabhāsarāja, there came forth the bodhisattva named Sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇajñānadhvaja.

Accompanied by bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an unspeakable ocean of world-systems, he was permitted by that Blessed One; then, rising from that ocean-like assembly circle, he approached the Sahā world-system,
emitting from every pore of his body clouds of flower-radiance as vast as the realm of space.
From all the pores of his skin, he emitted clouds of light from all musical instruments as vast as the realm of space;
from all the pores of his skin, he emitted clouds of light from precious jewels as vast as the realm of space;
and from all the hair-pores, he emitted clouds of light from various fragrant incenses, perfumed incense, and jeweled garments as vast as the realm of space.
From all the pores of his skin, he emitted clouds of lightning-flame-like dragon-transformations as vast as the realm of space;
from all the pores of his skin, he emitted clouds of radiance from Vairocana-jewel-gems as vast as the realm of space;
and from all the pores of his skin, he emitted clouds of radiance from blazing golden jewels as vast as the realm of space.
Emitting from all the pores of his skin clouds of blazing rays from the king of jewels, the Śrīgarbha, as vast as the realm of space,
and emitting from all the pores of his skin clouds of jewel-rayed light that illuminates the three times like an ocean of the Tathāgata’s mindfulness, as vast as the realm of space—
he approached the Blessed One together with his retinue, and having paid homage to the Blessed One, [stood before him].
Resting against the southwestern direction, he manifested great jeweled gabled palaces made of the great maṇi-jewel called *Samantadigabhimukharaśmijālavindusaddharmadhātuprabhāsa*,
and lion thrones with lotus-calix seats of fragrant lamp-flame jewels; having manifested these, he sat down cross-legged,
covered by nets of the finest *vimalagarbha* jewel-kings and wearing crowns bound with the finest jewel-kings that resound with the resolve of all sentient beings.
Having empowered the bodies of the bodhisattvas.
In the northwestern direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,

from the world-system called Vairocana-śrī-praṇidhi-garbha— specifically from the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Samantavairocana-śrī-meru-rāja— there came the Bodhisattva named Vairocana-praṇidhi-jñāna-ketu, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans.
Permitted by the Blessed One, he then rose from the circle of the assembly and proceeded toward the Sahā world-system,

emitting from all his primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, and from his entire body, clouds of reflections of the bodies of Tathāgatas reaching back through all three times;

and emitting from all his primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, and from his entire body, clouds of reflections of the bodies of Bodhisattvas reaching back through all three times.

From all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, and from his entire body, he emitted clouds of bodily reflections of the assemblies of Tathāgatas present throughout the three times; from all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, and from his entire body, he emitted clouds of bodily reflections of the emanation-wheels of Buddhas present throughout the three times; from all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, and from his entire body, he emitted clouds of bodily reflections of the former lives of the Tathāgatas present throughout the three times.

From all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of the skin, and from his entire body, he emitted clouds of reflected images of the bodies of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas attained throughout the three times; from all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of the skin, and from his entire body, he emitted clouds of reflected images of the forms of the bodhi-maṇḍa trees and the bodies of tathāgatas attained throughout the three times;

and from all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of the skin, and from his entire body, he emitted clouds of reflected image-bodies of the buddha-transformations attained throughout the three times.

Emitting from all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, and from his entire body, clouds of reflections of the bodies of the lords of the world throughout all the three times;
and emitting from all the primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, and from his entire body, clouds of completely pure Buddha-fields throughout all the three times—
pervading the entire realm of space moment by moment— he approached the Blessed One together with his retinue.

Having paid homage to the Blessed One, he took his position leaning toward the northwestern direction; having miraculously manifested palatial towers with interiors of king-of-jewels that radiate light in all directions, and lion thrones with lotus-calix interiors of world-illuminating jewels, he sat down cross-legged,
presiding over the bodies of the bodhisattvas which were covered by nets of pearls of invincible luster and adorned with crowns of jewels whose light shines everywhere.
In the downward direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, from the world-system called Sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalavairocana,

belonging to the Tathāgata Asaṅgajñānaketudhvajarāja, there came forth the Bodhisattva named Sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇajñānavikrāmī, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans.
Permitted by the Blessed One, he then emerged from that ocean-like assembly circle and approached the Sahā world-system,
emitting from all the pores of his skin the resonant sounds of the production of the linguistic expressions and mantras of the oceans of all living beings,
and thundering the clouds of sounds of the methods for the birth of Bodhisattvas throughout the three times.
He emitted the sounds of oceans of methods for accomplishing the vows of all bodhisattvas;

he emitted the sounds of clouds of oceans of methods for the purification and fulfillment of all bodhisattva perfections; he emitted the sounds of oceans of methods for pervading all buddha-fields with the entire mandala of all bodhisattva conduct.

He emitted the sounds of an ocean of methods for the miraculous manifestations of the attainment of all bodhisattvas; he emitted oceans of sounds for the miraculous manifestations of the methods for awakening to enlightenment by approaching the seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Tathāgatas and dispersing Māra and the Kali age; and he roared with clouds of sounds from an ocean of names and methods of sūtras for turning the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
Emitting the sounds of the methods and means of the Dharma for disciplining the Wheel of Time (Kālacakra) which disciplines all worlds,

and emitting the ocean-like sounds of the methods and principles of the Dharma— characterized by the excellence of roots of virtue, timely means, and the attainment of omniscience according to one's vows—
he approached the Blessed One together with his retinue; having paid homage to the Blessed One, he took his place leaning toward the lower direction.

Having miraculously manifested celestial palaces with interiors reflecting all Tathāgatas and containing peaked towers that were treasuries variegated with every kind of jewel, as well as lion thrones whose interiors were supported by lotuses pierced through by every kind of gem,

he sat down cross-legged, having empowered his bodhisattva bodies so that they were crowned with crest-jewels bearing banners reflecting all sites of enlightenment and covered by nets of the finest jewels illuminating all buddha-fields.
In the upward direction, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,

from the world-system called Akṣayabuddhavaṃśanirdeśā (Exposition of the Inexhaustible Lineage of Buddhas), which belongs to the Tathāgata Samantajñānamaṇḍalapratibhāsanirghoṣa (Resounding Manifestation of the Universal Sphere of Wisdom), there came forth the Bodhisattva named Dharmadhātupraṇidhitalanirbheda (Piercing the Foundation of the Vows of the Dharma-realm), together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans.
Permitted by the Blessed One, he then rose up from the ocean-like assembly circle and approached the Sahā world-system;
from all his primary marks and secondary signs, from all the pores of his skin, from his entire body,
from all his major and minor limbs, from all his paths of speech, and from all his robes and retinue, [there emerged] that of himself and of his entire retinue of bodhisattvas.

And [he saw] the oceans of former lives associated with the perfection of giving belonging to the Blessed One Vairocana, to all the Tathāgatas of the past reaching back to the limit of the beginning, to all the Tathāgatas of the future reaching to the limit of the end— whether already prophesied or not yet prophesied— and to all the Tathāgatas of the present established throughout the expansion of all fields in the ten directions.

He made manifest the reflections of all recipients and all garments to be given within the primary marks, the secondary characteristics, the pores, the face, all the limbs and members of his body, the paths of speech, and the entire retinue of his body;
and he displayed as reflected images the oceans of past practices associated with the perfection of all ethical discipline.
He manifested oceans of past deeds that appeared before him, associated with the perfection of all forms of patience, even those involving the cutting off of his limbs and members;

he manifested oceans of past deeds that appeared before him, associated with the impetus and prowess of all bodhisattva vigor; and he manifested oceans of past deeds that appeared before him, associated with the attainment of the search for and accomplishment of the ocean of meditative concentrations of all Tathāgatas.

He manifested oceans of past lives that had reached the state of manifestation, which were associated with the quest for the Dharma to perfect the course of the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas, and which revealed the physical forms and countenances resulting from the great resolve to renounce all possessions; he also manifested oceans of past lives that had reached the state of manifestation, which were associated with the joy of seeing all Tathāgatas and the delight of all Bodhisattva paths for the sake of the entire world.

He manifested oceans of past practices that had reached the state of manifestation, being associated with the arrays of purification through the gateways for accomplishing the ocean of vows of all bodhisattvas;

he manifested oceans of past practices that had reached the state of manifestation, being associated with the purity of the heroic strides in accomplishing the perfections of power of all bodhisattvas;

and having pervaded the vast and expansive realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with clouds of all miraculous transformations, he manifested oceans of past practices associated with the mandalas of wisdom of all bodhisattvas.

Manifesting those who had attained the state of radiance, he approached the Blessed One together with his retinue; having paid homage to the Blessed One, he took his position facing the upward direction, miraculously created a peaked palace of various arrays of all vajra-lords, as well as lion thrones made of blue lotus hearts for the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and others adorned with vajra-lord rain-showers, and sat down cross-legged, covered by nets of the finest blazing jewel-kings of every kind.
They empowered the bodies of the bodhisattvas, who were adorned with crowns bound with crest-jewels and necklaces of king-of-jewels that resounded with the names of the Tathāgatas of the three times.
And all those bodhisattvas, together with their retinues, were perfected through the vows and conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;

they possessed the eye of pure wisdom for beholding the feet and faces of all Tathāgatas; they had attained the perfect mastery of the ocean-like sounds of the eyes, sutras, and methods of the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas;

they had reached the supreme perfection of attaining all the masteries of the bodhisattvas; and they were perfected in the miraculous displays that manifest at every moment in approaching all Tathāgatas.

Their domain is the pervasion of all world-systems with a single body; their bodies shine forth, emerging from the circles of assemblies of all Tathāgatas; their domain is the manifestation of the convergence and appearance of all world-systems within a single atom of dust; they are intent upon arriving at the proper time for the ripening and disciplining of all living beings; and their domain is the thundering of the clouds of the Dharma wheels of all Tathāgatas from every pore.

They have attained the thorough knowledge of the realm of all sentient beings as being like an illusion; they have entered into all Tathāgatas as being like a reflection; they have emerged through the knowledge of rebirth in all states of existence as being like a dream; they are purified by the knowledge of the maturation of all karma as being like a reflected image; they possess the super-knowledges of the arising of all things as being like a mirage; and they have entered into the expansion of all world-systems as being like a magical creation.

They had attained the illumination of the knowledge of the ten powers of a Tathāgata; they possessed the prowess of the fearless roar of the bull and the lion; they had entered the ocean of inexhaustible analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*); they had attained the knowledge of the dharma-expressions and mantras for the entire world-ocean; their sphere of activity was the unattached knowledge of the space-like realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
they had attained the unobstructed knowledge of all phenomena; and they were purified by the mandala of the knowledge of all the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) of bodhisattvas.

They possess the vigor that agitates all the circles of Māra; they are established in the power of knowledge regarding all three times; they have attained unobstructed omniscience; their sphere of activity is the non-abiding sky; their vigor is like the sky, reaching the stage of omniscience without effort; their sphere of knowledge is the non-apprehension of all states of existence;

they are extended by the ocean-like knowledge of the principles of the entire realm of phenomena; and they have entered the gateway of knowledge that perceives all world-systems without differentiation.
They have emerged from the miraculous transformations that bring together all world-systems; they manifest bodies born into every lineage within all world-systems;
they have penetrated the various forms—subtle, vast, expansive, or condensed—of all world-systems; they have attained the knowledge of the convergence of vast fields into subtle objects;

they follow the knowledge of subtle objects within vast fields; they have attained the dwelling in a single moment of mind that is one with all Buddhas; and they possess the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas.
Having attained the knowledge that is undeluded regarding the oceans of all directions, they pervaded all oceans of directions with miraculous transformations in a single moment of thought.
The entire Jeta Grove was filled with bodhisattvas endowed with such immeasurable qualities, namely, through the empowerment of the Tathāgatas.

And those great śrāvakas— Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Revata, Subhūti, Aniruddha, Nandika, Kapphiṇa, Kātyāyana, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, and others who were their leaders— did not see in the Jeta Grove those Buddha-arrays, the bull-like majesty of the Buddha, the Buddha’s playful sport, the Buddha’s miracles, the Buddha’s sovereign power, the miraculous transformations of the Buddha’s conduct, the Buddha’s majestic influence, the Buddha’s empowerment, or the purity of the Buddha-field.

Nor did he perceive that inconceivable domain of the bodhisattvas, the assembly of bodhisattvas, the gathering of bodhisattvas, the congregation of bodhisattvas, the approach of bodhisattvas, the miraculous transformations of bodhisattvas,
the supernatural feats of bodhisattvas, the circle of the bodhisattva’s retinue, the bodhisattvas’ presence in all directions, or the magnificent array of the bodhisattva’s lion throne.

The dwelling of a bodhisattva, the abode of a bodhisattva, the playful mastery of a bodhisattva’s samādhis, the observation of a bodhisattva, the unfolding of a bodhisattva, the valorous stride of a bodhisattva, the worship of Tathāgatas by a bodhisattva, the prophecy of a bodhisattva, the maturation of a bodhisattva, the heroic exertion of a bodhisattva, the purification of the dharma-body of a bodhisattva, and the fulfillment of the wisdom-body of a bodhisattva.

They beheld the physical manifestation of the bodhisattva’s vow, the perfection of the bodhisattva’s form-body, the purity of the excellence of the bodhisattva’s marks, the array of the bodhisattva’s infinite circle of light and power, the emission of the bodhisattva’s net of rays, the dispatching of clouds of bodhisattva emanations, the pervading of the network of directions by the bodhisattva, and the miraculous display of the sphere of the bodhisattva’s conduct.
For what reason? Because of their lack of commonality with roots of goodness;
for they have not accumulated those roots of goodness that lead to the vision of all the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, the purities of the arrays of qualities of all Buddha-fields contained within the world-systems of the ten directions had not previously been described to them;
nor had the various miraculous displays of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, been described to them;
nor, while wandering in saṃsāra in the past, had they ever encouraged sentient beings toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment or toward the perfections.
Furthermore, they have not established the arousal of the thought of enlightenment within the mental continuums of others;
nor have they applied themselves to ensuring that the lineage of the Tathāgatas remains uninterrupted;
nor have they exerted themselves for the sake of gathering in all sentient beings.

Furthermore, those bodhisattvas had not been encouraged by them to practice the perfections; nor, while wandering in saṃsāra in the past, had they taken hold of the ground of wisdom that is preeminent for all the world; nor had they accumulated roots of merit conducive to omniscience.

Nor did they know the miraculous displays and supernormal powers for purifying all buddha-fields, which are fully accomplished through the supramundane roots of goodness of the Tathāgatas; nor did they know the manifestation within the range of the Bodhisattva’s vision, which arises from the uncommon supramundane roots of goodness directed toward awakening as its object and from the vows of the great Bodhisattvas; nor did they know that these are produced by the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) that has emerged through the Tathāgata’s empowerment and is like an illusion.
These [manifestations]—which have as their basis the grasping of various perceptions by bodhisattvas who are like dreams; which increase the force of joy of great bodhisattvas;
and which are the cognitive range of the eye of wisdom of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra—are not shared with any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Therefore, those great śrāvakas, headed by the foremost pair and the auspicious pair, did not see that miraculous display of the Tathāgata.
They do not hear, they do not know, they do not understand.
They do not descend into it,
they do not resolve upon it, they do not attain it,
and they do not attend to it.
They do not look, they do not gaze, they do not contemplate.
They do not contemplate it.
Why is that? Because this is the domain of the Buddha's wisdom.
It is not within the range of the śrāvakas;
therefore, those great śrāvakas, though staying right there in the Jeta Grove, did not see those miraculous displays of the Buddha,
for they lacked the roots of merit necessary to perceive them.
Yet their eye of wisdom was not purified such that they might behold those miraculous displays of the Buddhas,
nor did they possess meditative concentration.
By which they might enter into vast miraculous transformations and empowerments within a limited object;
yet those eight liberations do not exist,
nor does that supernatural power.
That is not his bull-like prowess, nor that strength, nor that sovereign power.
Neither that place, nor that perception, nor the range of the eye exists there.

by which they might perceive it, or see it, or descend into it, or realize it, or pervade it, or survey it, or experience it, or enter upon it, or manifest it to others, or teach it, or indicate it, or describe it, or demonstrate it, or present it, or bring it forth;
Or they might encourage, engage, and establish sentient beings therein—
in that nature of the Buddha’s miraculous transformations.
They would urge sentient beings [toward it],
yet that knowledge does not exist within them.
For what reason?
For they have departed by means of the Śrāvaka vehicle,
attained through the path of the Śrāvakas,
perfected the circle of Śrāvaka conduct, and are established in the fruit of the Śrāvakas.
Relying on the knowledge that illuminates the truth, established in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*),
having reached the ultimate state of absolute peace, their minds were devoid of great compassion; indifferent toward the entire world and having accomplished their own purpose,
they assembled right there in the Jeta Grove.
They sat down;
they sat before the Blessed One, to his left, to his right, and behind him, facing the Blessed One.
Yet, they did not see those Buddha-miracles in the Jeta Grove.

For what reason? Because it is not possible for those who have not accumulated the knowledge of omniscience, who have not fully realized the knowledge of omniscience, who have not set out toward the knowledge of omniscience, who have not directed their intention toward the knowledge of omniscience, who have not brought forth the knowledge of omniscience, and who have not cultivated the knowledge of omniscience.
It is impossible for those who have not purified the knowledge of omniscience to enter into, practice, behold, or realize that miraculous display of the Tathāgata’s samādhi.
Why is that?
For that is to be known by the range of vision of noble-born bodhisattvas,

not by the range of vision of śrāvakas. Therefore, those great śrāvakas, though staying right there in the Jeta Grove, did not see those miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata, the empowerments of the Buddha, the purification of the buddha-field, or the assembly of bodhisattvas.
It is just as if, on both banks of the great river Gaṅgā, many hundreds of thousands of pretas had gathered—

afflicted by hunger and thirst, naked and without clothing, their skin and bodies scorched, withered by wind and sun, harassed by flocks of crows, and terrified by wolves and jackals— who do not see that great river Gaṅgā.
Furthermore, some see it as parched, waterless, and filled with ashes because they are obscured by obstructive karma;
in the very same way, those elder great śrāvakas, though staying right there in the Jeta Grove, did not see those miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata.
They do not descend [into the stages], because their eyes are shrouded by the cataracts of ignorance which are the adversaries of omniscience,
and because they have not been sustained by the roots of virtue belonging to the stage of omniscience.

It is just as if, for example, a man were to fall into sloth and torpor while a great day was underway in the midst of a vast multitude of people; having fallen asleep and entered into a dream, he would see right there in that very place a city of the gods— the abode of the Sudarśana wheel— and the entire surface of Mount Sumeru with its trees, its circles of gardens, crowded with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of apsarases, and inhabited by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sons of the gods.
One would see kalpavṛkṣa trees strewn with various divine flowers, from which were released diverse divine garments, pearl necklaces, jeweled ornaments, garlands, and baskets;
and one would see musical-instrument trees emitting the charming and sweet sounds of various kinds of divine music.
One would see various arrays of delightful sports and games;
one would hear the sweet sounds of the songs and instrumental music of hosts of divine apsarases;
and one would perceive oneself as being situated there.
And he would see that entire region adorned with divine arrays,
while that whole multitude of people would neither see nor know it.
One should not look [around],
while remaining in that very place.
For what reason?
For just as that very person, having entered into a dream, perceives those things,
yet while remaining in that very place does not see that great multitude of people;

even so, those bodhisattvas and those lords of the world, being oriented toward awakening, through the vast empowerment of the Buddha and by virtue of having thoroughly purified their own roots of merit—
And by the fulfillment of the vow for omniscience; by the thorough mastery of the qualities of all Tathāgatas;
by being well-established on the path of the bodhisattva’s great array; by the complete perfection of the emergence of all aspects of the phenomena of the knowledge of omniscience;
and by the purity resulting from the fulfillment of the specific vows of the conduct of the Samantabhadra bodhisattva.
And by means of traversing the circle of knowledge of all the bodhisattva stages, by means of sporting in the dwellings of all bodhisattva samādhis,
and by means of investigating the unimpeded range of all bodhisattva knowledge, they behold and enter that inconceivable bull-like sovereignty of the Buddhas and the playful display of the Buddhas.
They experience [this],
yet those great śrāvakas, headed by the foremost pair and the auspicious pair, neither see nor know it, because they are devoid of the eye of a bodhisattva.

It is just as if, for example, on the Himalayas, the king of mountains, which is strewn with mines of medicinal herbs, there were a man who had mastered the spells, sciences, and knowledge of medicinal herbs, and who, understanding all the methods for medicinal herbs, performed the work of gathering them. And right there on that lord of mountains, there might be cattle, oxen, sheep, bears, deer, hunters, or other men who are ignorant of the methods of medicinal herbs, [yet they would observe] his application of the means regarding the taste, potency, post-digestive effect, and power of those herbs.
They do not understand.

In the very same way, those bodhisattvas who have entered the domain of the Tathāgata’s knowledge and emerged from the domain of the bodhisattva’s miraculous transformations understand that domain of the Tathāgata’s samādhi-transformations;

whereas those great śrāvakas, headed by the foremost pair and the auspicious pair, dwelling right there in the Jeta Grove, content with their own affairs and indifferent to the affairs of others, remain in equanimity, abiding in the happiness of the present life.
They dwell in comfort,
yet they do not understand that range of the Tathāgata’s miraculous displays within the domain of his samādhi.

It is just as if this great earth were enriched with all kinds of mines of jewels, filled with hundreds of thousands of treasuries, and replete with various infinite gems. Suppose there were a man there who was learned in the knowledge of the methods for discerning the lineages of jewels; one whose mind was purified therein, well-trained in the sciences of their classification and the arts of their extraction, and supported by the power of vast merit—such a person would take from it whatever jewels he desired and properly satisfy himself.
One should properly attend to one's mother and father and support one's children and wife;
furthermore, one should share with other beings who are aged, sick, poor, fallen into misfortune, or deprived of food and clothing.
And one would experience various delights of wealth.
However, those beings who do not know the methods for accessing jewel-mines and treasure-troves—
those who have not performed meritorious deeds and whose eye of wisdom regarding jewels is unpurified— do not recognize the jewel-mines or the treasure-troves.
And they wander about right there; they do not take up the jewels, nor do they perform any work with the jewels.

Thus, those bodhisattvas in that Jeta Grove— possessing the eye of wisdom that is utterly pure regarding the inconceivable domain of the Tathāgata, and having entered the inconceivable domain of the Tathāgata’s wisdom— beheld those miraculous displays of the Buddhas and entered the oceans of the methods of the Dharma.
They bring forth oceans of samādhis,
apply themselves to the worship and service of the Tathāgatas,
and exert themselves for the sake of upholding all dharmas.
And they gather all sentient beings through the four means of attraction;
yet those great śrāvakas neither see nor know those miraculous displays of the Tathāgata, nor that great assembly of the host of bodhisattvas.
It is just as if, for example, a man with eyes bound by a cloth garment were to reach an island of jewels;
he might walk about there on that island of jewels,
or stand still.
He might sit down or prepare a bed,
yet he would not see that mine of jewels.
Neither jewel-trees, nor precious garments, nor precious perfumes.
He would not see all those jewels,
nor would he fully understand those jewels— whether by way of their qualities, their value, or their utility—
and he would not take possession of them.
And they would not experience the function of jewels;
those with unobstructed vision would see and understand all this.

In the very same way, those bodhisattvas, having reached the island of the jewel of the Dharma, have before them the unsurpassed jewel of the Tathāgata, the ornament of all worlds, standing in the Jeta Grove—[possessing] inconceivable [qualities]. (Gv)
They see him manifesting the miraculous transformations of a Buddha;
yet those great śrāvakas remain right there at the feet of the Blessed One, sustaining themselves,
and do not perceive that miraculous display within the scope of the Tathāgata’s samādhi.
And they did not see that great assembly of bodhisattvas, that great mine of jewels.
Why is that?

Because the eye of wisdom of those whose eyes of wisdom were bound by the stains of ignorance—which is the adversary of omniscience—was not purified; it was not the unattached eye of wisdom of the bodhisattvas.

Nor had they realized the entry into the succession of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), by which they might have beheld that inconceivable miracle of the Tathāgata’s sovereign power and miraculous transformations through meditative absorption (samādhi).
It is just as if there were a purification of the eye called "Stainless Radiance," which does not coexist with any darkness or gloom;
suppose some man were to obtain it.

Endowed with the pure vision of the *viraja-prabhāsavatī*, he would move about in the midst of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings who had gathered together— people whose eyes were clouded by the darkness of night and whose various modes of conduct and deportment were obscured by the gloom.
He should walk about,
stand, or sit down.
He might assume various modes of deportment,
yet those people would not see that man.
They would not perceive him as he manifests various modes of conduct;
yet that man would see that great multitude of people dwelling in various modes of conduct, facing various directions, of various forms, various colors, and wearing various garments.
In exactly the same way, the Tathāgata, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas, with his eye of pure and unattached wisdom, knows and sees the entire world.
He displays the miraculous manifestation of the great Buddha’s meditative absorption;
yet those great śrāvakas do not see that miraculous manifestation of the Tathāgata’s great wisdom and meditative absorption, nor do they see that retinue of the great assembly of bodhisattvas.
It is just as if, for example, a monk in the midst of a great multitude of people were to enter the meditative absorption on the totality of earth, or the totality of water, or the totality of fire.
or the totality of air, or the totality of blue, or the totality of yellow;
Whether it be the red totality, the white totality,
or the divine totality.
He might enter into a meditative absorption that encompasses the activities of all sentient beings, or one that encompasses all sounds and cries, or one that encompasses all objects of perception.

And that great multitude of people would not see that mass of water, nor that light of the blazing fire, nor those various spheres of totality for the body, up to and including all the spheres of totality for objects of perception,
except for those who have attained the dwelling of the meditative absorption and meditative attainment thereof.
In the very same way, when the Tathāgata displays this miraculous manifestation of the domain of his inconceivable Buddha-samādhi, those great śrāvakas who do not see it,
yet those bodhisattvas who have set out upon the path of the Tathāgata, enter into that domain of the Tathāgata.
Just as, for example, a man who has achieved the power of ointment becomes invisible to the entire multitude of people as soon as his eyes are anointed with it;
whether walking, standing, or sitting, he perceives the entire multitude of people—
exactly so the Tathāgata has transcended the worldly sphere of all living beings, entered the sphere of omniscient knowledge, and is to be perceived by the eye of the wisdom of Bodhisattvas.
He beholds the entire world,
yet those great śrāvakas do not see those miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata.
It is just as if a person had a deity born together with him who was constantly following him; that deity sees the person,
but that person does not see the deity.

In the same way, the Tathāgata, abiding in the domain of the knowledge of the omniscient one, displays great miraculous transformations of a Buddha in the midst of a vast assembly of the bodhisattva host;
yet those great śrāvakas neither see nor know that miraculous display of the Tathāgata’s power nor that miraculous display of the circle of the bodhisattva assembly.

It is just as if, for example, a monk who has attained the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states were to enter the cessation of perception and feeling; he would neither perceive nor feel, and his six sense faculties would no longer experience any activity whatsoever.
And yet he has not entered final nirvana;
all worldly conventions continue to operate in that place,
yet he does not perceive them.
It does not experience [sensation], namely, by virtue of the sustaining power (*adhiṣṭhāna-adhipatya*) of that very meditative attainment (*samāpatti*).
In exactly the same way, those great śrāvakas dwell right there in the Jeta Grove,
and they possess the six sense faculties (*ṣaḍindriya*).
And they do not see that miraculous display of the Tathāgata’s mastery and power of transformation through samādhi;
they do not enter into it,
nor do they fully comprehend it.

They do not discern it; they do not enter into that assembly of great bodhisattvas, nor the miracle of the bodhisattvas, nor the supernatural manifestation of the bodhisattvas; they neither see nor know it.
For what reason?
Because the domain of the Buddhas is profound, vast, immeasurable, difficult to see, difficult to awaken to, and difficult to fathom; it transcends all worlds.
The domain of the Buddhas is inconceivable and cannot be taken away by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Consequently, those great śrāvakas, remaining right there at the feet of the Blessed One in the Jeta Grove, did not see those Buddha-transformations;

nor did they see or know that assembly of great bodhisattvas and that Jeta Grove—which was a convergence of the arrays of qualities of inconceivable and incalculable pure world-systems—because they had not become fit vessels for such things.
Then, the bodhisattva Vairocanapraṇidhānābhiracitaprabha, through the empowerment of the Buddha, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:
Behold the inconceivable Buddha-enlightenment of the Essence of Beings;
on the banner of victory, the Jina displays the miraculous power of a Buddha. // 1 //
The inconceivable domain of the self-arisen ones proceeds;
therein the world is deluded, not knowing the qualities of a Buddha. // 2 //
The profound, immeasurable, and inconceivable miracle of the Kings of Dharma proceeds, wherein the world does not penetrate.
The perfectly awakened ones possess infinite qualities and are beautifully adorned with the marks;
yet those phenomena which have been manifested by the perfectly awakened ones are indeed without marks.
The Jina displays his miraculous transformations in the grove called Jetavana—transformations that are profound, without end or middle, and difficult to express through the paths of speech. (5)
The Bodhisattvas do not see a gathering of great beings;
they have come from inconceivable millions of realms to behold the Jina.
Endowed with their vows, their conduct and sphere of activity are unimpeded;
it is impossible for the entire world to understand their inner intention.
All the Pratyekabuddhas and all the Śrāvakas do not understand their conduct, nor do they know the range of their minds. (8)
Bodhisattvas of great wisdom, invincible and unconquered, bearing the banner of heroes, unconfused, and intent upon the stage of primordial knowledge. (9)
Those of great renown, having entered immeasurable meditative absorptions, pervade the entire realm of phenomena and manifest their miraculous transformations. (10)
Then, indeed, the bodhisattva Duryodhanavīryavegarāja, having surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s empowerment, spoke these verses at that time:
“Behold the sons of the Sugatas, who possess the womb of merit and great wisdom, who have reached the path of the conduct of awakening, and who bring security to the entire world. (11)
To those who are wise, possessed of infinite intelligence, whose minds are perfectly concentrated, and whose sphere of activity is vast, profound wisdom that has neither center nor end; (12)
In the great forest called Jetavana, adorned with magnificent arrays, filled with bodhisattvas, and serving as the hermitage of the perfectly enlightened Buddha.
Behold the many oceans, without abode or foundation, where they have come from the ten directions and are seated upon lotus thrones. (14)
They are without fixed abode, without exertion, free from conceptual proliferation, and without attachment;
their minds are unattached and stainless, and they are devoted to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). // 15 //
Those great heroes, whose banner is wisdom and whose vajra-minds are unshakable,
manifest nirvāṇa even while phenomena have not ceased.
They had come from ten million incalculable buddha-fields in the ten directions,
having approached the Perfectly Awakened One while being free from the perception of duality.
Behold this miraculous manifestation of the Self-Existent Śākyasiṃha, by whose empowerment these bodhisattvas have gathered here. (18)

The sons of the Conquerors have reached the further shore of the distinction between mere conventional usage and the non-distinction among the qualities of a Buddha and within the planes of the dharma-realm. (19)
The Sages abide at the limit of the non-differentiation of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), and they effect the differentiation of the Dharma through inexhaustible steps. // 20 //
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Samantaśrīsamudgatatejorāja, having surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s empowerment, spoke these verses at that time:
"Behold the vast mandala of wisdom of the Essence of Beings;
having discerned the proper and improper time, he teaches the Dharma to living beings. (21)
Crushing the opposing disputants gathered from various non-Buddhist sects, he displays his miraculous transformations to sentient beings according to their inclinations. (22)
The Fully Awakened One is not confined to a single location, nor does the Buddha follow after the directions; the Great Sage has not transcended the immeasurable and the measurable. (23)
Just as the sun, moving through the sky, illuminates according to the number of days,
so too does the Teacher who possesses knowledge, empowered by non-attachment to the three times.
Just as the orb of the moon shines forth on a full-moon night, so too does one behold the Leader, completely filled with pure qualities. // 25 //
Just as the solar orb moves here through the atmosphere yet does not actually stand anywhere here, so too is the miraculous display of the Buddha.
Just as the sky is not dependent upon any direction or any field, so too should the miraculous power of a Buddha, the lamp of the world, be understood. // 27 //
Just as the earth is the foundation for all embodied beings in the world, so does the Wheel of Dharma stand as the foundation for the Lamp of the World in the world. (28)
Just as the wind blows swiftly through the sky without adhering to anything, so too does the nature of a Buddha operate throughout the world-systems. (29)
Just as the numbers of all fields are established within the mass of water, so too are the Buddhas of the three times established within the mass of gnosis. // 30 //
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Asaṅgaśrīgarbharāja, surveying the ten directions through the empowerment of the Buddha, spoke these verses at that time:
"Just as a mountain peak rises high, formed of diamond, so has the Buddha arisen in the world, the protector of all the world. // 31 //
Just as the water in the ocean is immeasurable and undisturbed,
so indeed does the vision of the Buddha cut through the thirst of the world.
Just as Mount Meru rises out from the waters of the ocean, even so has the Lamp of the World emerged from the ocean of Dharma. (33)
Just as the ocean is full, a great mine of all kinds of jewels, so too is the self-arisen one’s wisdom inexhaustible, awakening [beings] in every moment. // 34 //
The Leader’s wisdom is profound, incalculable, and immeasurable;
it reveals that which is infinite and inconceivable, by means of which the Buddha performs his miraculous transformations. (35)
Just as a skilled magician displays the characteristics of an illusion, so the Buddha, master of wisdom, displays his miraculous transformations. // 36 //
Just as a pure wish-fulfilling gem fulfills all desired objects, so too does the Victor fulfill the aspirations of those whose intentions are pure. // 37 //
Just as the Vairocana jewel radiates light like the sun, so too does the purity of omniscience illuminate the dispositions of the world. (38)
In the same way, the jewel at the face of the directions is well-established with its eight facets;
likewise, the unimpeded radiance illuminates the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). // 39 //
Just as water that is turbid becomes clear through the light of the moon, which is pure in its radiance, so too is the sight of the Buddha; it purifies the faculties of the world. // 40 //

Then, indeed, the bodhisattva Dharmadhātupraṇidhisunirmitacandrarāja, having surveyed the ten directions through the empowerment of the Buddha, spoke these verses at that time: "Just as the directions here have been made of a single color by sapphire, so does the color of awakening make the people behold the Buddha. (41)
In each and every one of these, that Buddha displays immeasurable and diverse miraculous transformations that purify the bodhisattvas. // 42 //
And that [sphere] is exceedingly diverse, profound, boundless, and difficult to approach;
it does not enter into the world, which is within the range of knowledge of the wise. (43)
And he beholds the perfected arrays, purified by the form of a Buddha, through the accomplishment of the bodhisattvas and their entry into the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). // 44 //
The Jina displays inconceivable Buddha-fields,
which are filled on all sides by Buddhas surrounded by assemblies of the wise.
The Teacher, the bull among the Śākyas, has arisen as one who has mastery over all phenomena;
for this immeasurable miracle of his is now unfolding.
Behold the immeasurable conduct of various kinds belonging to the wise;
