he of boundless splendor displays infinite miraculous transformations.
The Lord of the World instructs the sons of the Conqueror in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu);
they become those whose range is the non-attached knowledge regarding all phenomena. (48)
Through the empowerment of the Lord of Men, the Wheel of Dharma turns, filled with hundreds of miracles and purifying all worlds. (49)
In the realm of the essence of being, they are purified by the mandala of gnosis;
possessing vast wisdom, these great elephants liberate all the worlds. // 50 //
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Dharmārcis-mat-tejorāja, having surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s empowerment, spoke these verses at that time:
“Those disciples who are disciplined by the Supreme Sage throughout the three times...”
They do not perceive the lifting up and setting down of the feet of the Perfectly Awakened One. // 51 //
Even those Pratyekabuddhas, the Protectors, throughout all three times without exception, do not perceive even the lifting up or setting down of a footstep. (52)
How much less will all sentient beings—who are like dogs bound by a tether and shrouded in the darkness of ignorance—be able to recognize the Guide? (53)
This Jina cannot be measured by means of valid cognitions;
the Buddha possesses unimpeded knowledge and has transcended the path of speech. (54)
Steadfast, with the radiance of the full moon and beautifully adorned with the primary marks,
he dwells through miraculous transformations, exhausting immeasurable eons.
Contemplating each Buddha individually with a well-concentrated mind, one may pass through ineffable and inconceivable millions of eons. (56)
Even a Buddha, though he gazes upon them, cannot reach the limit of even a single portion of the qualities of the Self-Existent One; for the qualities of a Buddha are indeed inconceivable. (57)
And those who have made their vow there, and those whose minds find delight therein—
they too shall all have such a sphere of activity, and they shall be very difficult to behold.
Those of great prowess in the accumulation of merit and wisdom, established in the stainless mind of the wise, indeed enter this method which is infinite. (59)
Their aspiration shall be vast, and their restraint of mind vast;
having entered the domain of the Victors, they shall attain vast awakening.
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Sarvamāramaṇḍalavikiraṇajñānadhvajarāja, having surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s empowerment, at that time spoke these verses:
Because they possess a body of unattached gnosis, the Self-Existent Ones are bodiless;
their domain is inconceivable gnosis, and they cannot be conceived by thought. (61)
The Buddha-body is fully perfected through inconceivable pure deeds; it is unstained by the three worlds and radiant with the primary and secondary marks. // 62 //
It is the universal illumination in the world, purified by the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu);
it is the gateway to the awakening of the Buddhas and the great mine of all-knowledge. // 63 //
Stainless and free from conceptual proliferation, he is devoid of all attachments;
like the sun for the world, he emits the rays of primordial wisdom.
It cuts through the terror of existence, purifies the triple world, brings the bodhisattvas to fulfillment, and likewise is the source of the awakening of the Buddhas. (65)
Perceiving infinite colors and independent of all colors,
he nevertheless displays those inconceivable colors to all embodied beings.
No one can reach the limit of the Buddha's knowledge, for the awakening of a Buddha, which has been purified by him, is inconceivable even in a single moment. (67)
The inexhaustible exposition of knowledge is changeless by its very nature; in a single moment, all the Victors belonging to the three times are manifested therein. (68)
One who possesses infinite activity and wisdom, seeking awakening, should always reflect thus:
"Even that which is called 'mind'—in this mind, no mind arises. (69)
The qualities of a Buddha, by which the Perfectly Awakened Ones are manifested, are beyond the scope of all verbal expression, profound, transcending the path of speech, and inconceivable. (70)
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Vairocanapraṇidhānaketudhvaja, surveying the ten directions through the Buddha’s empowerment, spoke these verses at that time:
"Those whose mindfulness is undeluded, pure, well-ascertained in the arising of Dharma, and possessed of inconceivable intelligence—they are inexhaustible oceans of awakening. (71)
Their minds are resolved upon this, for this is the sphere of their conduct;
their knowledge regarding this is unshakable, and they have severed all doubt.
No weariness arises in them, nor does their mind falter; their minds proceed with the qualities of a Buddha as their ultimate goal. (73)
In them there arises faith, born from the root and fully emerged;
for their delight is in this wisdom that is without support and free from abode.
Complete with wholesome qualities accumulated over ten million eons, all these incomparable seekers of wisdom dedicate them toward that same goal. (75)
They wander through saṃsāra, yet they do not rely upon saṃsāra; resolved in the qualities of a Buddha, they delight in the domain of the Buddhas. // 76 //
Whatever worldly prosperity occurs within the realm of sentient beings—all that has been abandoned by the wise, for they are firmly established in the Buddha. (77)
The world always proceeds, bound and relying on what is in vain; therein, those who act without attachment always remain intent upon the welfare of sentient beings. // 78 //
Their conduct is incomparable and inconceivable to all embodied beings; they contemplate the happiness of the world by which suffering is brought to an end. (79)
Purified by the wisdom of awakening, they have compassion for all the worlds;
having become a light for the world, they are the liberators of all the world. // 80 //
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇajñānavikrāntarāja, through the empowerment of the Buddha, surveyed the ten directions and at that moment spoke these verses:
"The sound of the word 'Buddha' is extremely difficult to encounter even in hundreds of millions of eons; how much more so is the sight [of him], which is supreme and cuts through all doubts! (81)
That Lamp of the World has been seen; he has reached the ultimate realization of all phenomena, the merit-field of the three worlds that purifies all sentient beings. (82)
For those who behold the irreproachable essence of beings in his form-body (rūpakāya),
no satiety arises even in tens of millions of billions of eons.
Beholding the form-body of the Lord of Men, the sons of the Conqueror,
being unattached and seeking the welfare of others, dedicate their own merit toward enlightenment.
This physical body of the Great Sage is the gateway to the enlightenment of a Buddha, from which the unimpeded and inexhaustible analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) emerge. (85)
Having illuminated inconceivable and infinite beings, the Great Sage causes them to enter the Mahāyāna and grants them the prophecy of supreme enlightenment.
This field, consisting of great merit, is proclaimed as the circle of wisdom;
it illuminates the immeasurable world and increases the mass of merit. // 87 //
It cuts through the web of suffering and purifies the aggregate of knowledge;
there is no fear of miserable rebirths for those by whom the Victor has been propitiated here. (88)
As they behold the Supreme among Men, a vast mind arises;
an incalculable power of wisdom, radiant as the moon, is born. (89)
Having seen the Buddha, the supreme among men, they become fixed in enlightenment; and this certainty arises within them: "I shall become a Tathāgata. (90)
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātutalabhedajñānābhijñārāja, having surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s empowerment, spoke these verses at that time:
"Having seen the Sage, the Bull of the Śākyas, who is endowed with infinite virtues..."
The mind of those who dedicate [their merit] becomes purified in the Mahāyāna. // 91 //
For the sake of all sentient beings, the Tathāgatas arise— those who possess great compassion, who are steadfast, and who turn the wheel of Dharma. (92)
How could all embodied beings ever be able to repay the Buddhas—who are dedicated to the welfare of sentient beings—even in hundreds of millions of eons? (93)
It would be better to spend ten million eons in the most dreadful states of woe as a matured being than never to behold the Teacher, who has turned away from all attachments.
Whatever mass of suffering arises within the realm of all sentient beings, all of that must be endured for the sake of the Buddhas; but not the failure to see them. 95.
Whatever various states of miserable rebirth exist separately throughout this entire world, it would be better to dwell there for a long time than to never hear the name of the Buddhas. 96.
It would be better to dwell even in hell for eons in each of those states than to remain elsewhere far removed from the enlightenment attained by the Victors. (97)
For what reason is dwelling for a long time in the states of woe desired?
Because the sight of the Lord of Jinas increases wisdom. (98)
All sufferings are severed upon seeing the Jina, the Lord of the World; and entry arises into the wisdom that is the domain of the perfectly awakened ones. 99.
Having seen the Buddha, the supreme among men, one exhausts all obscurations and increases immeasurable merit by which awakening is attained. (100)
The sight of the Buddha cuts through the doubts and uncertainties of sentient beings;
it fulfills their aspirations, both mundane and supramundane. (101)
(Gv 25) 2 Samantabhadra: Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, having surveyed the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas, [spoke].

To a still greater degree, by dividing, expanding, teaching, clarifying, revealing, illuminating, radiating light, and instructing through the principle of the *dharmadhātu*, [he does so] by means of the equality of the space-element, the equality of the three times, the equality of the *dharmadhātu*, the equality of the realm of sentient beings, the equality of all world-systems, the equality of all lineages of karma, and the equality of the inclinations of sentient beings.

Through the equality of the inclinations of sentient beings, the equality of the manifestation of phenomena, the equality of the time for maturing sentient beings, and the equality of the faculties of the entire world—
thus did he fully reveal to those bodhisattvas the Tathāgata-samādhi called "The Lion’s Yawn" by means of ten explanatory points.
What are these ten?

Namely, the exposition of the succession of all Buddhas and the succession of fields within every atom of the measure of Buddha-fields included throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
Namely, the exposition of following the qualities of the Tathāgatas through kalpas reaching the furthest limit of the future within all Buddha-fields as vast as the realm of space.
Namely, the exposition that demonstrates the ocean-like gateways of manifest enlightenment, which are without end or middle, regarding the arising of Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields.
That is to say: the exposition on abiding facing the seat of enlightenment within the circles of the Tathāgatas’ assemblies in Buddha-fields as vast as the realm of space;
the exposition on emitting from every pore emanations resembling the bodies of all Buddhas of the three times, pervading the dharma-realm in a single moment of thought;
and the exposition on the radiance of a single body pervading the level ground of all oceans of fields throughout the oceans of all directions.

Namely: the teaching that demonstrates the empowerment through which the miraculous displays of the Buddha-ground are gathered together across all objects and throughout all three times; the teaching that demonstrates the ocean of eons of various Buddha-miracles within the succession of fields of the three times, equal in number to the atoms of all lands;
and the teaching on the manifestation of Bodhisattvas through the boundless empowerment of the resonance from every pore of the ocean of Buddhas' vows throughout all three times.

Namely, the teaching on the empowerment until the furthest limit concerning the manifestation of the lion-thrones of Buddhas equal in measure to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas, the undifferentiated seats of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), and the turning of the various wheels of Dharma.

For indeed, O Sons of the Conqueror, having taken these ten as the foremost, I follow this teaching of the Samādhi of the Lion’s Stretching, which is equal in number to the atoms of unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Nevertheless, O Sons of the Conqueror, this is the domain of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.

Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, illuminating the explanation of the meaning of this very Lion’s Yawn Tathāgata-samādhi, looking toward the face of the Tathāgata through the Buddha’s empowerment, surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly circle,

beheld the infinite and centerless miraculous manifestations of the Tathāgata-samādhi within the inconceivable domain of the Buddhas, and [beheld] the nature of phenomena as an inconceivable illusion produced by primordial wisdom.

Having contemplated the equality of the Buddhas of the three times as being inconceivable, and having contemplated all the methods of the Dharma, the expressions, and the paths of speech that are inconceivable, infinite, and without middle, at that moment he spoke these verses:
"The oceans of the Victor’s fields, each with a single hair, are equal in number to the atoms of all fields."
There the Buddha sat upon his throne, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas. // 1 //

Seated upon a lotus throne at the seat of awakening, the Leader is seen within each single pore, having pervaded the vast realm of phenomena throughout oceans of many fields, amidst the most excellent of trees. // 2 //
On a single hair-pore, as many Victors as there are atoms in all fields are seated, surrounded by assemblies of Bodhisattvas, proclaiming the conduct of universal excellence. // 3 //
Seated within a single field, having pervaded the expanse of all fields, numerous and inexhaustible clouds of bodhisattvas come from all directions throughout the ten quarters. // 4 //

May those Bodhisattvas, who are as numerous as the atoms in ten million fields and whose radiance is an ocean of Bodhisattva virtues, arise within the assemblies; may they pervade the ten directions with the Dharma-realm of the Teacher. 5.
Manifesting the appearance of all buddha-fields, oceans of the wisdom of the Victors, the Kings of Dharma, they, established in the conduct of Bhadra, approached the assemblies of all the Buddhas. 6.
Seated throughout the expansion of all fields, their sphere of experience is the joy of the conduct of Bodhisattvas;
gentle and serene, they hear the clouds of Dharma while practicing in a single field for ten million eons.
Bodhisattvas wander on their course, illuminating the conduct that is an ocean of Dharma;
they enter oceans of vows, established in the sphere of the stages of the Victors. // 8 //
Arising from the diverse dharmas of various Jinas within the auspicious thoughts of universal conduct,
they enter into the vast miraculous transformations of the oceans of praise for all the qualities of the Buddhas.
Having pervaded the excellent realm of phenomena with bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields,
may they constantly emit clouds of bodies that rain down the Dharma for the sake of awakening. 10.

Then the Blessed One, in order to further establish those bodhisattvas in this very lion’s yawn samādhi of a Buddha, emitted from the circle of hair between his eyebrows, from the space between his brows, a ray of light named "Illumination of the Three Times through the Universal Door of the Dharma Realm.
This ray was accompanied by a retinue of rays as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, [extending] throughout the oceans of all world-systems in the ten directions.
He illuminated the entire expansion of all buddha-fields.

Then indeed, those bodhisattvas who had assembled in the Jeta Grove saw [the Lord] in all the buddha-fields throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), reaching to the limits of the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*),
within as many atoms as there are in all buddha-fields, and contained within every atom of those buddha-fields that are gathered together.
In Buddha-fields of various powers, various purities, various foundations, and various configurations, he was seen reaching the excellent seat of enlightenment,

seated upon the lion-throne of a Bodhisattva, honored by all the lords of the world, surrounded by a host of Bodhisattvas, and either realizing unexcelled perfect enlightenment or turning the wheel of Dharma by pervading the entire realm of phenomena.
By means of his circle of voice, [he was heard] in assemblies as vast as ineffable buddha-fields;
in some places he had gone to the abodes of gods, in some to the abodes of nāgas, in some to the abodes of yakṣas, in some to the abodes of gandharvas,
in some to the abodes of asuras, in some to the abodes of garuḍas, in some to the abodes of kinnaras, and in some to the abodes of mahoragas.
In some places he was seen in the palaces of lords of men, and in others within the human world— in villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals—
teaching the Dharma through various miraculous transformations.

They saw him teaching the Dharma through various modes of deportment, various types of physical forms, various manifestations of the gateways of samādhi, various supernormal powers of samādhi, various origins from diverse families and lineages, various manifestations of color, various circles of radiance, various emissions of networks of light rays, various circles of sound, various circles of assemblies, various empowerments of speakers, various empowerments of teachings, various words and phrases, and various etymological explanations.

And as many bodhisattvas as there were in those various circles of assemblies beheld the Tathāgata’s profound transformations of buddha-samādhi throughout world-systems that reach the furthest limits of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), extending to the very boundaries of the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), situated in the ten directions, converging in the infinite revolutions of the quarters,
within oceans of all directions, through various gateways of the directions of phenomena, having attained various designations of direction, and converging in various directions.
In various directions, in the followings of various directions, and in the oceans of various directions— namely, in the eastern direction,
the southern, the western, the northern, the northeast, the southeast, the southwest, the northwest, the nadir, and the zenith;

in the directions of the bodies of fields, in the directions of the bodies of sentient beings, in the directions of the conceptual designations of sentient beings, and even in the directions reaching to the furthest limits of the past.

In the ten directions of the present; in the directions of depositing and grasping even the finest hairs within every path of space; in the directions of the continuous succession of atoms of all fields; in the directions of entering and descending into the directions; in the directions arisen from the formation of various karmas;
and in the paths of direction that reach the surface of space—without end or middle—even along the path of a single hair.

Following after equanimity, they have attained a manifestation within the minds of all beings in the entire world— having entered into the equanimity of the undifferentiated expanse of the three times and possessing a voice equal to the perceptions of all sentient beings without distinction;
appearing before the bodies of all beings, they approach every assembly in forms that manifest everywhere,
with wisdom undifferentiated throughout all eons and with universal equanimity in all buddha-fields.

They beheld the miraculous manifestations of the Tathāgata, which manifest forms directly before sentient beings according to their inclinations, and which never cease to proclaim all the Buddha-dharmas and to discipline all sentient beings.
All of them had been gathered by the Blessed One Vairocana through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), owing to their commonality with his former practice of wholesome conduct.
They were matured through seeing, hearing, recollecting, and attending upon [the Buddhas];
they had previously resolved their minds upon unexcelled perfect enlightenment;
and as they approached those Tathāgatas, they were sustained by roots of virtue.

Because they are well-sustained by the means for maturing omniscience through their commonality with roots of goodness, they enter into that inconceivable miraculous display of the meditative absorption of the Blessed One Vairocana, which is as vast as the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and extends to the limits of the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*);
some enter into the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*), while others enter into the form-body (*rūpakāya*).
Some [saw] the prior attainment of the bodhisattva path;
some, the fulfillment of the perfections; and some, the array of the purification of the circle of conduct.

Some [displayed] the miraculous transformations of the bodhisattva stages; some, the miraculous transformations of perfect enlightenment; and some, the miraculous transformations of the undifferentiated meditative absorptions of the Buddha’s dwelling.
Some enter the ocean of the Tathāgata’s powers and fearlessnesses; some enter the ocean of the Buddha’s analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*).
In this manner, they enter oceans of the Buddha’s miraculous transformations, as numerous as the unspeakable atoms of ten Buddha-fields.

Through various inclinations, various paths, various gateways, various entrances, various descents, various methods, various followings, various directions, various vessels, various lands, various worlds, various realizations, various accumulations, various transformations, various skillful means, and various meditative concentrations,
they enter those oceans of the Buddha’s transformations by means of various entries into meditative concentration.
That is to say, they enter by means of the bodhisattva concentration called "The Array of the Entire Dharmadhātu."
by the bodhisattva samādhi that illuminates the object of unattached knowledge regarding all three times;
by the bodhisattva samādhi that is the light of knowledge regarding the indivisibility of the depths of the dharma-realm;
and by the bodhisattva samādhi that enters the depths of the domain of the Tathāgatas.
by the bodhisattva samādhi called Illumination of the Expanse of Space;

by the bodhisattva samādhi called Opening for the Ascending of the Ten Powers of the Tathāgatas; and by the bodhisattva samādhi called the Majestic Display of the Valiant Stride of the Buddha’s Fearless Array.

By means of the bodhisattva-samādhi called the "Womb of the Revolving Methods of the Entire Dharmadhātu," the bodhisattva-samādhi called the "Moon Pervading the Resonance from the Limbs of the Entire Dharmadhātu," and the bodhisattva-samādhi called the "Universal Array of Dharma-Radiance," those bodhisattvas enter into those oceans of the Buddha-vikurvas of the Blessed One Vairocana.
And by the bodhisattva samādhi called the Banner of the Dharma King’s Unattached Cloth; by the bodhisattva samādhi called Beholding the Ocean of Buddhas Free from All Obstructions;
and by the bodhisattva samādhi called the Banner of the Body’s Reflection that Does Not Differentiate Any State of Existence in the World.
By means of the bodhisattva samādhi that enters the domain of the indivisibility of the Tathāgata’s body;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi whose womb is compassion, which revolves in accordance with all worlds;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi empowered by the empowerment of the foundation of the words of all dharmas.
by the bodhisattva samādhi that is the mandala of illumination in the state of ultimate peace and perfect tranquility;
by the bodhisattva samādhi that is the manifestation of universal emanations, well-constructed and without objective support;
and by the bodhisattva samādhi that is the empowerment of the universal convergence of all buddha-fields.

By means of the bodhisattva samādhi that brings forth the manifestation of perfect awakening in all buddha-fields; by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that reveals the power of the lords of all worlds;
and by means of the revelation of the mandala of non-attachment to the distinctions of all worlds.

by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that is the empowerment arising from the mother of all Tathāgatas, and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that enters into the practice of all ocean-like qualities;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that sustains the future limit through the manifestation of all miraculous transformations without exception;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that enters the oceans of the former spiritual practices of all Tathāgatas;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that sustains the lineage of all Tathāgatas throughout the future.
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that is the empowerment of the resolute conviction in the purification of the oceans of all realms in the ten directions of the present;

by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that illuminates the dwelling in a single moment of mind of all Buddhas; and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that enters the limit of non-attachment toward all objects of perception.
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that manifests a single buddha-field within all world-systems,
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that brings forth the emanation of all buddha-bodies;
By means of the bodhisattva samādhi that penetrates the ocean of all sense faculties like a vajra-lord;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that is the empowerment of the embryo within the single body of all Tathāgatas;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that dwells in every moment following the principles of the entire realm of phenomena throughout ten million moments of mind.

By means of the bodhisattva samādhi that manifests the cessation of the expansion of all realms within the dharma-dhātu; by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that abides at the summit of the foundation of the Dharma;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that empowers the non-distinction between the bodies of all sentient beings in all buddha-fields.
by the bodhisattva samādhi that is the convergence facing toward the whirlpool of all-knowledge;
by the bodhisattva samādhi that is the differentiation of the thorough knowledge of the characteristics of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena;
and by the bodhisattva samādhi that is the mandala of the non-differentiation of the three times within a single moment of mind.
by means of the bodhisattva-samādhi whose womb is the body of the principle of the dharma-realm in every moment of mind;
by means of the bodhisattva-samādhi which is a lion following the lineage of all Tathāgatas;
by means of the bodhisattva-samādhi which is the mandala of the eye of wisdom regarding the dharma-realm of all objective referents;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that undertakes the powerful stride of the ten powers;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that is the eye-circle of universal vision regarding all objects of focus;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that brings forth the radiant manifestation of the essence of all mandalas of colors.

By means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Unshakable Whirlpool," by the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Teaching on the Convergence of All Dharmas into a Single Dharma," and by the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Analysis of the Words, Phrases, and Etymologies of the Path of Speech of a Single Dharma," those bodhisattvas enter into those oceans of the miraculous transformations of the Buddha Vairocana.
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that teaches the Dharma through the empowerment of the banners of all Buddhas;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that illuminates the limits of the three times without attachment; and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi of non-differentiated knowledge that follows all eons;

by means of the bodhisattva samādhi included within the ten powers of the subtle principle; by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that accomplishes all eons of the bodhisattva’s practice which cannot be interrupted; and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called the Cloud Facing Toward the Swift Speed in All Directions.
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that manifests the miraculous transformations of perfect awakening; by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that is the secure banner untouched by any sensation;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that brings forth the adornments of the sky of all arrays.
By means of the bodhisattva samādhi that produces clouds of emanated forms of the world moment by moment;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "Stainless Moonlight of the Tathāgatas in the Sky";
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Empowerment of All Tathāgatas in the Sky."
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called Radiance of the Array of the Faculties of All Dharmas, by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called Lamp Illuminating the Meaning of All Dharmas,
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called Illumination of the Mandala of the Ten Powers;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called the Banner of the Buddhas of the Three Times;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called the Womb of All Buddhas;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called the Commencement and Culmination of Every Single Moment.
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called the Inexhaustible Matrix of Merit; by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called the Illumination that Tames through the Vision of Infinite Buddhas;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called the Vajra-Lion Foundation of All Dharmas.
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that accomplishes universal communication through the manifestation of the emanations of all Tathāgatas;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that culminates in traversing the days of all Tathāgatas;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that is the single continuity of the three times.

By means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Sound Released from the Universal Radiance of All Phenomena Primordially Quiescent," by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "Transcending the Limits of Vision of All Buddhas," and by means of the [samādhi] awakened within the lotus-pond of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) without exception; (Gv 30)

by the bodhisattva samādhi called "Contemplation of the Sky-like Dharma Without Abode," and by the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Revolving Convergence of the Oceans of the Single Direction and the Ten Directions."
By means of the bodhisattva samādhi that enters the foundation of the entire realm of phenomena;
by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that contains the essence of all oceans of phenomena; and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi of the tranquil body that emits light upon all sentient beings.
By means of the bodhisattva samādhi that accomplishes all supernormal knowledges through a single moment of thought;

by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that is the empowerment for constant, universal, and all-encompassing perfect awakening; and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that enters into the realization of the single array of the entire realm of phenomena.
by the bodhisattva samādhi of the illumination of the body of the mindfulness of all Buddhas;

by the bodhisattva samādhi of the superknowledge of the specific knowledge of the various grounds of all worlds; by the bodhisattva samādhi of the pervasion of one's own body throughout the infinite methods of the dharma-realm in every moment of thought;

By means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Radiance of the Array of the Single Principle of All Phenomena within the Dharmadhātu," by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Splendor of the Wheel of the Mandala of All Buddha-qualities," and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Practice of Vows for Gathering the Realm of Sentient Beings through the Indra’s Net."

By means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "the non-differentiation of the foundations of all world-systems," by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "the universal stride of the miraculous manifestation of lotus-glory," and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi called "the supernormal knowledge of the wisdom that transforms the bodies of all sentient beings."

by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that empowers the body to face all sentient beings; by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that possesses the superknowledge of the method for discerning the oceans of vocal qualities and the mantras of all worlds;
and by means of the bodhisattva samādhi that possesses the superknowledge of the wisdom that discerns the various levels of all worlds.
by the bodhisattva samādhi whose womb is the indivisible treasury of great compassion;
by the bodhisattva samādhi that enters the millions of realms of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas;
and by the bodhisattva samādhi of the lion’s stretch that surveys the palaces of liberation of all the Tathāgatas.

By means of these primary gateways for entering the categories of bodhisattva samādhis— which are as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields— those bodhisattvas enter into the oceans of the miraculous displays of the Lord Vairocana’s buddhahood,

and they recollect the miraculous displays of their former shared conduct. In every single moment of mind, through their entry that pervades the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), those bodhisattvas further...
They were present before the Blessed One, having arrived at the Jeta Grove, seated upon lion thrones with interiors of various vast jewel-lotuses as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;

they had emerged through the miraculous displays of great wisdom and supernormal powers, had reached the stages of those possessing sharp wisdom and supernormal powers, moved within universal knowledge, were born from the lineage that is the source of wisdom, were oriented toward the wisdom of the omniscient one, possessed the eye of knowledge free from darkness, and had attained the state of being charioteers for sentient beings.

They have attained equality with all Buddhas; they always practice the Dharma without conceptualization; they have penetrated the objective referents of all phenomena; they take as their objective referent the primordial tranquility of the nature of all phenomena; they are supreme in abiding in the nirvana that is utterly peaceful for all worlds; they do not abide in the diversity of all worlds; they travel to all fields without a fixed dwelling; they do not abide in any station of all phenomena; and they do not abide in any palace of all phenomena through noble exertion.
Those who have undertaken the maturation and discipline of the entire world; who show the secure path for all beings; whose sphere of activity is the palace of elevated wisdom and liberation;

whose bodies of knowledge follow the limit of passionlessness; who have emerged from the ocean of all existences; who perceive the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the entire world; whose mandala is the radiance of the wisdom-ocean; and whose minds of great compassion are perfectly concentrated in the *sāgaravatīdhātu* samādhi.

They had thoroughly penetrated the principle of phenomena as being like an illusion; they had entered all world-systems as being like a dream; they had realized the vision of all Tathāgatas as being like a reflection; they understood the communication of all sounds, voices, and resonances as being like an echo; they had realized the knowledge of the manifestation of all phenomena as being like a magical creation; their aspirations regarding the spheres of experience were perfectly purified; and they were endowed with skill in the purification of the universal mandala of wisdom.

They were those whose minds were utterly tranquil and profoundly pacified; whose domain was the knowledge of the lineage of all *dhāraṇīs*; who possessed the power of unshakable meditative concentration and universal prowess; whose vision reached the limit of the stability of the *dharmadhātu*; who had attained the dwelling of non-apprehension regarding all phenomena; who roamed the ocean of infinite wisdom; who had reached the further shore of the perfection of knowledge (*jñāna-pāramitā*); who had acquired the empowerment of the perfection of insight (*prajñā-pāramitā*); who had reached the further shore of the entire world through the perfection of supernormal powers (*ṛddhi-pāramitā*); and who had attained mastery over the perfection of meditative concentration (*samādhi-pāramitā*).

They possess unerring knowledge regarding skill in the welfare of all Tathāgatas; they know the methods for manifesting skill in the Dharma; they possess mastery over etymological knowledge and supernormal powers; they are clouds of Dharma through the power of inexhaustible eloquence; they roar the bull-like and lion-like roar of fearlessness; they delight in the joy of the non-abiding Dharma; their eyes are opened wide upon all phenomena, free from darkness; they are moons of knowledge that perceive the existence of all worlds; and they are orbs of wisdom whose rays are the conventions and methods of all truths.

To those whose encircling walls of merit are like the vajra of wisdom; who have transcended all similes and comparisons; who have sprouted as the shoots of the faculties and wisdom regarding all phenomena;

who possess the banners of heroes and the vigor that crushes the banners of all Māras; who possess the splendor of the mandala of infinite wisdom; whose bodies rise above the entire world; whose prajñā is unobstructed regarding all phenomena; who are awakened by the knowledge of the limit of exhaustion and non-exhaustion; and who are established in the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) following the universal limit.

They possess the eye of wisdom that discerns the signless conventional reality; they are skilled in the signs for accomplishing all the practices of bodhisattvas; their sphere of activity is non-dual knowledge; they clearly perceive the destinies of all worlds; they have attained the manifestation of movement through all Buddha-fields without a fixed abode; they are free from the darkness of all phenomena; they have entered the mandala of knowledge that is devoid of gloom; and they are dedicated to illuminating the Dharma in all directions.

They are the most excellent fields of merit for all living beings, whose hearing and sight are never in vain and who are moons of aspiration; they are Sumeru mountains of merit risen above all worlds, heroes who subdue the wheels of all opposing disputants, and those who cause the sounds and voices of all buddha-fields to resound.

They are those for whom the vision of all buddha-bodies is never satiated, who exercise mastery over the manifestation of the bodies of all buddhas, and who possess a physical empowerment that accords with the discipline of the world.

They are those whose single body pervades the expansion of all fields; who have purified the mandala of their formative activity; who possess the great vessel of the vehicle of unobstructed, sky-like great wisdom; who illuminate the entire realm of phenomena with bodies that are mandalas of wisdom; who are suns of wisdom risen for all worlds; who possess the power to act according to the inclinations appropriate to all worlds; who possess the knowledge that penetrates the intentions and faculties of all worlds; who have attained all phenomena within an unobstructed sphere of activity; and who have realized the nature of all phenomena as being without arising.
They had increased their conduct through the wisdom of the mutual convergence of the subtle and the vast; they were certain regarding the course of the profound stage of the Buddhas;

they possessed the knowledge of the conventional usage of profound meanings, phrases, and syllables; they indicated inexhaustible phrases, syllables, and meanings; they spoke by entering into a single phrase the ocean of all sūtras; they were sustained by the body of the wisdom of vast dhāraṇīs; they were sustained by a power that follows them for infinite eons; and they had penetrated the wisdom that perceives the dwelling together of unspeakable eons within a single moment of thought.
They possessed the superknowledge of knowing all worlds in a single moment of thought across the three times; they manifested infinite oceans of Buddha-qualities through the retention of all dharmas;
they were irreversible in turning the wheel of Dharma that leads all beings to knowledge; they had attained the illumination of the wisdom of the Buddha’s domain;
they were perpetually absorbed in the Samādhi of Excellent Vision; and they possessed the superknowledge of the wisdom that discerns all dharmas in their ten millionfold divisions without attachment.

They sported with the knowledge whose domain is the liberation of the distinctions of all phenomena; they were empowered by the auspicious arrays of all objective referents; they had entered the directions of the dharma-realm following the ten directions; they had converged into the dharma-realm that transcends all spatial divisions; they awakened to enlightenment within the atoms of dust, both subtle and vast; and they manifested all colors from their nature of gold.

From those bodhisattvas who had gathered and were seated in Jeta Grove— bodhisattvas who had come together from various directions, whose wombs of wisdom and merit were increased by infinite qualities of uniform knowledge, who were praised, lauded, and extolled by all the Buddhas, and whose descriptions of the qualities of their inexhaustible words and syllables [were endless]—
and as they were entering the ocean of the Tathāgata’s qualities and were illuminated by the rays of the Tathāgata, from all their bodies...

From the gabled pavilions, from the articles of enjoyment for bodhisattvas, and from those bodhisattva thrones— from the entire Jeta Grove— there issued forth, by the very nature of things, great arrays of miraculous transformations born of the surge of joy through the attainment of the light of the inconceivable Dharma of bodhisattvas and the attainment of the surge of joy;
these then pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
That is to say, at every moment of mind, vast clouds of networks of light rays, which bring satisfaction to all the world, issued forth and pervaded the ten directions.

Clouds of all kinds of jewels and bells issued forth, resonating with the thunderous sounds of clouds that proclaim the praises of the qualities of the Tathāgatas of all three times, and they pervaded the ten directions.

Clouds of musical instruments for all the world issued forth from all objects, accompanied by the sweet sounds of music representing the ripening of the karma of all sentient beings, and they pervaded the ten directions as they continued to resound.

Clouds in the form of the manifestation of the various practices of all bodhisattvas through their diverse vows issued forth and pervaded the ten directions, thundering with the sounds and voices of all bodhisattva vows. Clouds of bodhisattva bodies adorned with the primary marks and secondary characteristics issued forth and pervaded the ten directions, proclaiming the successive lineages of Buddhas appearing in all buddha-fields.

Clouds of bodhimandas resembling all the Tathāgatas of the three times issued forth and, displaying the arrays of the departure through the supreme awakening of all Tathāgatas, they pervaded the ten directions.
From all objects of perception, clouds of the bodies of all dragon-kings issued forth and, raining down showers of every kind of fragrance, they pervaded the ten directions.
Clouds of bodies resembling all the lords of the world issued forth and, proclaiming the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, they pervaded the ten directions.

From all focal points, clouds appearing as Buddha-fields entirely pure and composed of every kind of jewel issued forth; displaying the turnings of the wheel of Dharma of all the Tathāgatas, they pervaded the ten directions.

With these as their foremost, clouds of great arrays and miraculous transformations, equal in number to the atoms within ineffable Buddha-fields, issued forth through the empowerment of those Bodhisattvas and by virtue of the nature of reality that attains the illumination of the inconceivable ocean of Dharmas.
and //
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, displaying all these very miraculous transformations through the empowerment of the Buddha, surveyed the ten directions and at that time spoke these verses:
"As he gazes upon the Jeta Grove, the infinite and vast empowerment of the Buddha has set forth.
From it, clouds of bodies for all purposes emerge and pervade every direction. (11)
The infinite-colored, vast, pure, and variegated arrays of the sons of the Sugatas are seen by all from their seats, appearing as reflections upon those objects of perception. (12)
Clouds of jewel-rays with various arrays radiate, pervading other realms;
from the pores of the Sugatas' sons, the sounds of the Buddhas roar forth.
With physical forms resembling those of Brahmā and Indra, their deportment serene and their bodies pure,
they emerge from the flowers of the trees and depart, proclaiming the factors of meditative concentration.
Bodhisattvas equal to Samantabhadra, their limbs adorned with the primary and secondary marks, inconceivable and innumerable, issue forth as emanations empowered by a single pore of the Sugata. (15)

Seated in the Jeta Grove, they roar forth those clouds of magnificent arrays—oceans of the utterance of praises for the sons of the Sugatas who have arisen throughout the three times; these are oceans of virtues.

All the various and manifold great oceans of karma belonging to the multitude of sentient beings in every direction are heard even from within the hollows of the trees in Jeta’s Grove as they issue forth. (17)

Whatever miraculous transformations of all the Victors dwelling here in the three times throughout every field appear, they manifest individually, each as numerous as the atoms beneath that field, as objects of focus. (18)

Within each single pore, distinct and manifold Buddhas, as vast as oceans and clouds, illuminate the abodes of the Jinas; and within those abodes, too, there are clouds of Buddhas at every moment. 19.
Pervading all directions as vast as the world-systems, they bring sentient beings to maturity through skillful means;
and from their radiances issue forth ocean-like clouds of masses of fragrant rays and flowers.
Innumerable, supreme celestial palaces, resplendent with all manner of sublime arrays, pervade every direction, reaching all buddha-fields and all seats of enlightenment. (21)

(34) Indeed, those fields of great medicinal herbs, which extend throughout all directions without exception and abide in the three times, have been purified by the sons of the Sugatas through the various modes of conduct of Samantabhadra. // 22 //
The various arrays, purified by world-systems as numerous as immeasurable oceans of eons,
are also seen in their entirety within the sky of the Jeta Grove through the power of manifestation.

Then, indeed, as the mental continuums of those bodhisattvas were illuminated by the Buddha-samādhi, each individual bodhisattva entered into gates of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
they applied themselves with even greater intensity to the task of gathering in the welfare of the entire world.
As they remained thus in meditative equipoise, from each single pore of their skin issued forth rays of light equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
And from each individual ray of light, there issued forth clouds of emanated bodhisattvas, equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many buddha-fields;
their bodies resembled those of the lords of all worlds, their forms appeared in the faces of all beings, and their bodies were suited to the ripening of all sentient beings.
Having issued forth, they pervaded the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) in all directions, awakening, ripening, and disciplining sentient beings.

They manifested indications of the mind through gateways such as the manifestation of passing away from celestial palaces equal in number to the atoms within inexpressible Buddha-fields; through gateways of manifesting rebirth in all worlds; through gateways of manifesting the maṇḍala of the bodhisattva’s conduct; and through gateways of manifesting dreams.

They did so through gateways of the departure via the vows of all bodhisattvas; through gateways of the excellence of world-systems; and through gateways of manifesting the practice of the perfection of generosity.

Through gateways that are mandalas for the accomplishment and fulfillment of all the qualities of the Tathāgatas; through gateways that demonstrate the perfection of patience by means of the severing of limbs and members; through gateways that demonstrate the perfection of vigor by means of the miraculous transformations of great Bodhisattvas; through gateways that possess the resonance of the light illuminating the mandala of the path to the Buddha-knowledge of all Bodhisattvas’ meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments;
and through gateways that demonstrate the relinquishing of countless bodies for the sake of seeking every single word, syllable, and meaning of the Dharma of all Buddhas.

Through the gateways of approaching all Tathāgatas and inquiring about all dharmas; through the gateways of the ocean-like illumination of the methods for fulfilling omniscience, which lead to approaching the world according to its proper time and disposition; through the gateways of manifesting the banner of power that cannot be crushed by any Māras or external disputants, consisting of the entire equipment of merit and wisdom of all Bodhisattvas; through the gateways of manifesting the stages of knowledge possessed of the superknowledges of all arts and crafts; and through the gateways of manifesting the stages of knowledge possessed of the superknowledges of the specialized knowledge of the entire world.

By means of gateways that manifest the stages of knowledge endowed with the superknowledge of knowing the specific inclinations of all sentient beings; by means of gateways that manifest the stages of knowledge endowed with the superknowledge of uprooting the various afflictions and habitual tendencies through the application of entering the faculties of all sentient beings; and by means of gateways that manifest the stages of knowledge endowed with the superknowledge of knowing the various karmic practices of all sentient beings—through these and other such gateways for gathering sentient beings through skillful means for their maturation and discipline, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, those bodhisattvas entered into the abodes of all sentient beings.
They were seen: some in the abodes of gods, some in the abodes of nāgas, some in the abodes of yakṣas, some in the abodes of gandharvas,
some in the abodes of asuras, some in the abodes of garuḍas, some in the abodes of kinnaras, and some in the abodes of mahoragas.
Some were in the abodes of the lords of Brahma;

some in the abodes of the lords of men; some in the cities of Yama; some in all the abodes of pretas; some in all the worlds of hell; and some in all the destinies of animal births—with undifferentiated great compassion, with undifferentiated vows, with undifferentiated knowledge, and with undifferentiated [wisdom].

Through the application of gathering sentient beings, for the sake of maturing and disciplining those beings who are to be disciplined by sight, those to be disciplined by hearing, those to be disciplined by recollection, those to be disciplined by the circle of sounds, those to be disciplined by the resonance of the river of names, those to be disciplined by the circle of light, and those to be disciplined by the emission of networks of rays— according to the inclinations of sentient beings— the Bodhisattvas at the edge of the Jeta Grove displayed various magnificent arrays of miraculous transformations.
They were seen pervading the entire expanse of all world-systems and the realms of all sentient beings,
yet they did not stir from the presence at the feet of the Tathāgata.
Some were seen pervading the ten directions, accompanied by their own palaces, gabled halls, seats, and retinues.
They do not move from the feet of the Tathāgata;
yet some are seen emitting clouds of emanations for the sake of maturing sentient beings,
while they themselves do not move from the circle of the Tathāgata’s assembly.
Some appeared in the form of śramaṇas, some in the form of brāhmaṇas, some in the form of those possessing the physical appearance and stature of all various ascetic marks,

some in the form of physicians, some in the form of merchants, some in the form of those living by pure means of livelihood, some in the form of dancers, some in the form of artisans, and some in the form of the foundation of all crafts; they were seen approaching all villages, towns, market towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals.

Following the course of time by the power of time, through the differentiation of the manifestation of corresponding bodies, the differentiation of the color and shape of corresponding bodies, the differentiation of voice, the differentiation of mantras, the differentiation of modes of conduct, and the differentiation of postures, they engage in the bodhisattva practice which is like a magical illusion for all the world, which illuminates the entire mandala of arts and crafts, and which is a lamp providing the light that illumines the wisdom of all the world.

While practicing the bodhisattva conduct— which is an array of empowerments for all truths, a radiance that illuminates all phenomena, a purification that establishes the vehicles in all directions, and a lamp for the mandala of all dharmas— they were seen approaching all villages, towns, market towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals in order to mature and discipline sentient beings.
(36) The Spiritual Friends / 3 Mañjuśrī:
Then Mañjuśrī, the youthful prince, who was situated in the Pratiṣṭhāna gabled hall together with bodhisattvas of similar conduct, with the Vajrapāṇis who were his constant followers,
and with the deities belonging to the body of the Śarīra, whose minds were intent upon serving all Buddhas through vows and dedicated to providing strength to all the worlds—
And by the deities belonging to the body of words who were bound by former vows;
and by the earth-deities who were intent on hearing the Dharma;
and by the deities of springs, lakes, pools, ponds, oceans, and rivers, who were impelled by great compassion.
and by the deities of fire, blazing with the radiance of the power of the light of wisdom; by the deities of wind, wearing bound crowns;
by the deities of the directions, possessing the knowledge that illuminates all quarters; and by the deities of night, who are intent upon dispelling the darkness of ignorance.
and by the deities of the day who are devoted to manifesting the days of the Tathāgata;

and by the deities of space who are devoted to the circular array resembling the sky of the entire realm of phenomena; and by the deities of the ocean who are devoted to ferrying across the ocean of existence for all living beings.
by mountain deities whose minds were uplifted by the peaked pavilions of roots of goodness, being devoted to the accumulation of the equipment for omniscience;
by river deities devoted to the adornment of the bodies of all living beings and to the vows empowered by the praise of all Buddhas;
and by city deities devoted to the protection of the cities that are the minds of all living beings.

Together with the lords of the nāgas who were resolved upon the aspiration for the city of all dharmas, the lords of the yakṣas who were dedicated to the protection of all sentient beings, the lords of the gandharvas who were engaged in increasing the force of joy in all sentient beings, and the lords of the kumbhāṇḍas who were engaged in turning back the state of existence as a preta;

and by the lords of the *garuḍas*, who had undertaken the vow to rescue all beings from the ocean of existence; and by the lords of the *asuras*, who were born from the vow to perfect the power of the body of a Tathāgata that transcends all worlds;
and by the lords of the *mahoragas*, who, having attained joy at the sight of the Tathāgata, bowed their bodies in prostration.
With their faces upturned by the lords of the gods, whose minds were distressed by the cycle of existence (saṃsāra),
and with their bodies bowed down by the lords of the Brahmās, who had attained great reverence;

Thus praised and honored with great reverence by means of such a perfection of the array of the Bodhisattva’s heroic strides, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī emerged from his own abode, circumambulated the Blessed One hundreds of times, and having honored him in many ways,
departed from the presence of the Blessed One and set out for the southern region to wander through the countryside.

Then, indeed, through the power of the Buddha, the venerable Śāriputra saw Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta departing from the Jetavana with such a perfection of the array of bodhisattva miracles, proceeding toward the southern direction.
Having seen him, this thought occurred to him: "What if I were to set out on a journey through the countryside together with Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta?"
Surrounded and escorted by about sixty monks, he emerged from his own monastery and approached the Blessed One.

Having arrived, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, gazed upon the Blessed One, and, being permitted by the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times. Departing from the presence of the Blessed One, he went to where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was.
He was surrounded and escorted by those sixty monks, as well as by his co-residents— both seniors and juniors who had recently gone forth— namely, the monk Sāgarabuddhi and the others.
He was surrounded and escorted by sixty monks, headed by the monk Mahāsudata, as well as Puṇyaprabha, Mahāvatsa, Vibhudatta, Viśuddhacārin, Devaśrī, Indramati, Brahmottama, and the monk Praśāntamati.

And all those monks had previously performed services for former Victors, planted roots of merit, possessed long-cultivated resolute faith, were purified by trust and confidence, practiced great volition, were capable of surveying the directions of the Buddhas, had minds perfected in the realization of the intrinsic nature of the essence of phenomena, had intellects dedicated to the welfare of others, yearned for the qualities of the Tathāgatas, and were to be disciplined by the Dharma-teachings of Mañjuśrī.
Then, as the Venerable Śāriputra was walking along the road, he beheld all those monks and [addressed] Sāgarabuddhi:

He addressed the bhikṣu: "Behold, Sāgarabuddhi, the inconceivable purity of the body of the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, as seen by the world including the gods; behold his adornment with the primary and secondary marks, the purity of his halo of light, and the array of networks of rays that inspire immeasurable beings."
As he proceeds, there appears an eightfold path—a complete retinue that pacifies immeasurable suffering, adorned with the arrays of the path well-sustained by former roots of merit;
there appear arrays of strides upon the path facing all directions; and on his left and right, great treasuries of merit, perfectly arrayed, overflow.
And through the outflow of the roots of merit from their past service to former Buddhas, magnificent arrays emerge from the cavities of all the trees.
All the lords of the world pay homage, raining down clouds of offerings.

From the tufts of hair between the eyebrows of all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions, circles of networks of light rays issue forth; thundering with all the Buddha-dharmas, they descend upon the crown of [the Bodhisattva’s] head.

In this manner, the Venerable Śāriputra demonstrated, spoke, proclaimed, elucidated, praised, revealed, analyzed, and clarified for those monks the immeasurable arrays of qualities regarding the progression upon the path of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, headed by these [qualities].
In whatever way the venerable Śāriputra proclaimed the qualities of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, [in that same way he did so].
In such and such a manner, the minds of those monks become purified and serene;
the force of joy increases, and rapture arises.
Their mental continuums become pliable, their faculties become serene, and their gladness increases.
Mental distress is abandoned,
the impurity of the mind departs,
and all obscurations are turned back.
The vision of the Buddha becomes manifest before them, their minds are directed toward the qualities of a Buddha, and the faculties of a bodhisattva become purified.
The surges of serene confidence toward the bodhisattvas arise,
great compassion is born,
and one enters the mandala of the perfections.
Great vows arise, and oceans of Buddhas appear in the ten directions.
Having thus attained such a sublime surge of faith in omniscience, they said this: "May the preceptor lead us into the presence of this true person. Then, indeed...
The Venerable Śāriputra, together with three other monks, approached where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was and said this to him: "Mañjuśrī, these monks desire to see you.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, accompanied by a vast display of the miraculous power of a bodhisattva and an assembly circle as extensive as the entire earth, turned back with the gaze of an elephant and looked toward those monks.

Then those monks, having bowed their heads at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and joined their palms in reverence, said this: "By this root of merit from seeing you, O virtuous man, as well as whatever other roots of merit we possess that you and our preceptor know,"
And by that root of merit which was directly witnessed by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, may we become exactly like this, just as you are.
May we obtain such a body,
such a voice,
and such marks.
Such are these miraculous transformations as are yours.

When this had been said by those monks, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta spoke thus to those monks: "Monks, a son of good family or a daughter of good family who has set out in the Mahāyāna and is endowed with ten types of tireless mental resolve enters the stage of the Tathāgata."
How much more so the stage of a bodhisattva!
By which ten?
Namely: by generating a mind free from weariness in beholding, attending upon, honoring, and serving all Tathāgatas;
By generating a mind of indefatigable perseverance in the accumulation of all roots of merit; by generating a mind of indefatigable perseverance in the search for all dharmas;
and by generating a mind of indefatigable perseverance in the application of all the perfections of a bodhisattva.
By generating a mind free from weariness in accomplishing all the samādhis of the bodhisattvas;

by generating a mind free from weariness in entering the successions of all time-periods; and by generating a mind free from weariness in purifying the pervasions throughout the oceans of all buddha-fields in the ten directions.

By generating a mind free from weariness in the ripening and disciplining of the realm of all sentient beings; by generating a mind free from weariness in the accomplishment of the bodhisattva conduct throughout all fields and eons;

and by ripening the realm of all sentient beings through the sequential ripening of even a single sentient being by means of the application of the perfections equal in number to the atoms within all buddha-fields.
By generating a mind free from weariness in the accomplishment of the powers of a single Tathāgata—

monks, a faithful son or daughter of good family who is endowed with these ten types of generation of a mind free from weariness proceeds toward all roots of virtue and turns away from all states of cyclic existence.
It rises above all worldly lineages and transcends all the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
it is born within the lineages of the families of all Tathāgatas.
He becomes accomplished in the vows of the bodhisattvas,
purified in the practices of all the qualities of the Tathāgatas,
and thoroughly cleansed in all the conducts of the bodhisattvas.
He fully realizes all the powers of the Tathāgatas, crushes all Māras and proponents of opposing views,
and traverses all the stages of the bodhisattvas.
One draws near to the stage of a Tathāgata.
Then, indeed, those monks, having heard this method of the Dharma, attained the samādhi called "The Unobstructed Eye-Sphere that Reveals All Buddhas.
By the power of which they beheld the Tathāgatas residing in world-systems throughout the infinite and boundless ten directions, along with their circles of assemblies;
and they beheld, without exception, all the sentient beings born within those world-systems.
And he saw those world-systems with their various distinctions;
moreover, he understood by means of calculation even the atoms of dust that existed within those world-systems.
They also saw the dwellings, palaces, and enjoyments of those beings, which were composed of various jewels;
they heard the oceans of melodic tones of those Tathāgatas,
and they understood that teaching of the Dharma through its various words, phrases, etymologies, mantras, names, and designations.
They surveyed the minds, faculties, and inclinations of those beings;
they recollected ten cycles of births in the past and future limits;
and they entered into the ten ways of articulating and bringing forth the wheels of Dharma of those Tathāgatas.

They entered into the ten abodes of the miraculous transformations of supernatural power, the ten ways of bringing forth the methods of teaching, and the ten ways of bringing forth the words of instruction.
They also entered into the ten ways of bringing forth the modes of the ten analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) of those Tathāgatas.
Upon the simultaneous attainment of this samādhi, they perfected ten thousand factors of the mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*).
They entered ten thousand samādhis;
they purified ten thousand limbs of the perfections;
having attained great radiance and being illumined by the mandala of great wisdom, they acquired the ten supernormal knowledges of a bodhisattva.

Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having exhorted those who had attained the sprouts of soft and subtle supernormal knowledges and were firmly established in the arousal of the thought of enlightenment, established them in the conduct of a bodhisattva that is universally good.
Established in the conduct of a bodhisattva that is universally good, they entered into oceans of great vows and brought them forth.
Through the purity of mind brought forth by those oceans of great vows, they attained purity of body;
through purity of body, they attained lightness of body,
by means of which purity of body— (Gv 39)

By means of the lightness of body, they expanded those gateways of supernormal knowledge and attained supernormal knowledges that do not fall away; by the attainment of those supernormal knowledges, they did not move from the presence at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
And in the ten directions, they manifested clouds of the bodies of all Tathāgatas for the sake of the complete perfection of all Buddha-dharmas.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having established those monks in unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, traveled by stages through the countryside on his tour and arrived at a great city in the southern region named Dhanyākara.
Having arrived, he went to a great forest grove to the east of the great city of Dhanyākara called Vicitrasāradhvajavyūha.
It was a shrine inhabited by former Buddhas and empowered by the Tathāgata for the sake of maturing sentient beings, its name and sound resounding throughout infinite realms;

it was there that the Blessed One, while formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, relinquished many difficult sacrifices, and at that spot on earth where gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans were constantly and perpetually eager to offer worship.
Having arrived there together with his retinue,

Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta proclaimed there a discourse on the Dharma titled *The Illumination of the Method of the Dharmadhātu*, from which flowed hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of other discourses.
As he was proclaiming it, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nāgas approached from the great ocean.

Having heard that method of the Dharma, they came to loathe the state of being a nāga and, longing for the qualities of a Tathāgata, they turned away from the nāga state and took rebirth among gods and humans.
Among them, ten thousand nāgas became irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
As he was teaching that Dharma, over the course of time, an infinite and boundless realm of sentient beings was disciplined through the three vehicles.
The people of Dhanyākara heard that Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had arrived at this city of Dhanyākara and was dwelling right here in the Vicitrasāradhvajavyūha caitya.

Upon hearing this, laymen and laywomen, as well as boys and girls— headed by the layman Mahāprajña, the guild-leader— each with a retinue of five hundred, departed from the city of Dhanyākara and went toward where Mañjuśrī was.
They approached the presence of Kumārabhūta.
There, he was together with the lay follower Mahāprajña, as well as the lay followers Sudatta, Vasudatta, Puṇyaprabha, Yaśodeva, Somaśrī, Somanandin, Sumati, Mahāmati, and Rāhulabhadra.
Together with the lay follower Bhadraśrī and surrounded and preceded by five hundred other lay followers led by him,
he approached where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was; having bowed his head at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, he sat down to one side.
There, the laywoman named Mahāprajñā, together with the laywomen Suprabhā, Sugātrā, Subhadrā, Bhadraśrī, Candraprabhāsā, Ketuprabhā, Śrībhadra, and Sulocanā,
surrounded and escorted by five hundred laywomen headed by these, approached where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was.
Having bowed his head at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, he sat down to one side.
There, the merchant’s son Sudhana was together with the merchant’s son Suvrata, and with Suśīla, Svācāra, Suvikrāmin, Sucintin, Sumati, Subuddhi, Sunetra, Subāhu,
and Suprabha— the merchant’s son— and with five hundred other merchant’s sons headed by these.

Surrounded and escorted by his retinue, he approached where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was; having bowed his head at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, he sat down to one side.
There, the maiden Subhadrā— the daughter of the householder Mahāprajña— accompanied by the maidens Bhadrā, Abhirāmavatī, Dṛḍhamatī, Śrībhadra, Brahmadattā, Śrīprabhā, and Suprabhā,
and surrounded and escorted by five hundred maidens headed by these, approached where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was.
Having bowed his head at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta three times, he sat down to one side.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, perceiving that those men, women, boys, and girls had gathered and were seated in the city of Dhanyākara, overcame them by the sovereign power of his manifestation according to their inclinations; gladdened them by the sovereign power of great loving-kindness;
brought forth a teaching of the Dharma by the sovereign power of great compassion; and [discerned] their mental dispositions by the sovereign power of primordial wisdom.
Having reflected with great analytical knowledge and desiring to teach the Dharma, he looked toward the merchant’s son Sudhana.
As for why the merchant’s son Sudhana is called "Sudhana":
as soon as the merchant’s son Sudhana had entered his mother’s womb, seven sprouts of the seven precious gems appeared in that house, beautifully distributed throughout the entire dwelling.
And beneath those jewel-sprouts were seven great treasures,
from which those jewel-sprouts had emerged, having pierced through the surface of the earth and risen up, consisting of gold, silver, beryl, crystal, red pearl, emerald,
and the seventh treasure, musāragalva.

When he was born at the end of ten months, fully developed in all his major and minor limbs, then those seven great treasures— measuring seven cubits in length, breadth, and height— rose up from the surface of the earth, opened wide, and shone forth with brilliant splendor;
and five hundred vessels made of various jewels appeared in that house.
Namely, vessels of ghee, vessels of oil, vessels of honey, and vessels of fresh butter,
each filled with every kind of requisite;
that is to say, vajra-vessels filled with all kinds of perfumes and fragrant vessels.
Stone vessels filled with various garments;
gemstone vessels filled with various kinds of food, both hard and soft, and the finest flavors;
and golden vessels filled with various jewels and silver dust.
Silver vessels filled with gold-colored powder;
gold and silver vessels filled with beryl and precious gems;
and crystal vessels filled with musāragalva.
Vessels of musāragalva filled with crystal gems;
vessels of emerald filled with red pearls; and vessels of red pearls filled with emeralds.
There were vessels made of *jyotirdhvaja* jewel-gems filled with water-purifying jewel-gems, and vessels made of water-purifying jewel-gems filled with *jyotirdhvaja* jewel-gems;
these were the foremost among them.

Indeed, five hundred jeweled vessels rained down upon all the treasuries and storehouses in the house of the merchant’s son Sudhana, showering down wealth, grain, silver, gold, and various kinds of jewels.
Because such vast prosperity had appeared in his house as soon as he was born, the fortune-telling brahmins, his parents, and his circle of kinsmen gave him the name Sudhana, Sudhana.
The merchant’s son Sudhana, indeed, had performed his duties under previous Victors and planted roots of merit;

he possessed noble resolve, an intention following after spiritual friends, and an irreproachable conduct of body, speech, and mind. He was devoted to purifying the path of the Bodhisattvas, oriented toward omniscience, and had become a vessel for the Buddha-dharmas. His intention was purified through its realization, and he was perfected in the unattached mind of enlightenment.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having looked upon the merchant’s son Sudhana, greeted him with joy and taught him the Dharma— namely, concerning all the qualities of a Buddha, concerning the attainment of the emergence of all the qualities of a Buddha,
concerning the infinity of all Buddhas, concerning the entry into the succession of all Buddhas, and concerning the purification of the circles of assemblies of all Buddhas.

He taught the Dharma beginning with the array of the wheels of Dharma and the parinirvāṇa of all Buddhas; beginning with the purity of the primary and secondary marks of the form-bodies of all Buddhas; beginning with the perfect accomplishment of the Dharma-body of all Buddhas; beginning with the array of the eloquence of all Buddhas; beginning with the purity of the array of the circles of light of all Buddhas; and beginning with the equality of all Buddhas.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened Sudhana the merchant’s son and that great multitude with a discourse on the Dharma, and having caused them to resolve their minds upon unexcelled perfect enlightenment and recalled their former roots of virtue, bestowed his empowerment for the teaching of the Dharma according to the inclinations of sentient beings in the great city of Dhanyākara.
Having calmed himself, he departed.

Then, having heard from Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta this such majesty of the Buddha’s qualities, Sudhana the merchant’s son, with his supreme longing for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, followed closely behind Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and praised him with these verses:
Through your power, O Great-Minded One, I have set out for enlightenment for the benefit of embodied beings; hear from me that certainty which has become mine, whose range is infinite. (1)
That great city, consisting of the three worlds, has the waters of joy as its moat, is raised upon the walls of pride and arrogance, and provides access to the destinies of all sentient beings. (2)

Enveloped by the darkness of the ignorance of delusion and scorched by the fire of passion and hatred, the foolish and unwise always take refuge there, having fallen under the power of Māra and Īśvara. // 3 //
Tightly bound by the snares and shackles of craving, rendered barren by all forms of deceit and guile,
their eyes blinded by doubt and indecision, they have set out upon the false path of the world. (4)
Always thoroughly subdued by envy and avarice, they have fallen into the unfortunate states of hungry ghosts, animals, and hell-beings;
tormented by birth, sickness, old age, and death, they wander bewildered through the wheel of rebirths.
O you whose mandala is purified by compassion, who radiates the light of the rays of wisdom, arisen for the sake of exhausting the ocean of afflictions like the sun—shine upon me! 6.

With the full orb of the cultivation of loving-kindness, emitting the moonlight rays of merit and bestowing happiness, you shine forth like the full moon, having risen from the abodes of all sentient beings. (7)
Accumulated with the treasury of all white virtues, you are established in the sky of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
with the jewel of the Wheel of Dharma as your vanguard, act as a king and instruct me. (8)

O Caravan Leader, you who have exerted yourself with the resolve of the vehicle of enlightenment, who have accumulated vast merit and wisdom, and who have set out for the welfare of all sentient beings—protect me! 9.

Armed with the firm armor of patience as its essence, with the sword of wisdom and the extended arms of compassion, you are a hero in the face of the battle against the realm of Māra; please carry me across. 10.
Abiding upon the peak of the Dharma-Meru, brought to peace by the supreme samādhi of the apsarases, and crushing the asura Rāhu of the afflictions—you who have become Śakra, look upon me! 11.
In the city of the abode of the ignorant within the three realms, you are certain in the discipline of afflictions and karma;
O lamp, show me the way through the confusion of the wheel of causes, stages, and destinies. (12)
Turn me back from the path leading to the miserable realms; purify the path leading to the happy realms;
and lead me to the door of liberation, which transcends all worldly destinies. 13.
