This door to liberation, which is blocked by the seal of false grasping and obstructed by the notions of permanence, self, and pleasure—open it for me quickly with the sharp eye of the power of true knowledge. 14.
Expert in the paths of truth and non-falsity, confident in the methods of knowing the way, and certain in the subduing of all Māras, please show me the path to awakening. 15.

Established on the ground of the attainment of right view, nourished by the waters of all the qualities of a Buddha, and raining down the flowers of the virtues of the Buddha-dharma, show me the path to enlightenment. 16.
O Teacher of the Path, show me those Victors of the past, those of the future, and those present sun-like Victors—the Sugatas, the essence of beings—who have gone to every direction. (17)

Skilled in the methods of the mechanical devices of karma, and expert in the mechanical devices of the chariot of the Dharma-vehicle, you are firmly resolved in the methods of the vehicle of knowledge; show me the vehicle of enlightenment. (18)

Mount me upon the vehicle of enlightenment, which has the wheel-maṇḍala of aspiration and resolve, is firmly established on the axle of patience, the vajra, and compassion, and is adorned with the jewels of the qualities of faith. 19.

Bestow upon me this sublime vehicle, which is a pure mandala possessing all dhāraṇīs, adorned with a roof of peaks of loving-kindness, beautifully decorated, auspicious, and endowed with the analytical knowledge of the garland of bells. (20)
Adorned with couches for the celibate life, filled with the harmonious union of women, and resounded by the beating of the drum of Dharma—bestow upon me this sovereignty of vehicles. (21)

Reveal to me that supreme vehicle, which is adorned with the four means of attraction as its treasury, decorated with the jewel-strings of the qualities of inexhaustible gnosis, and restrained by the excellent leather thongs of self-control and moral shame. (22)

O you whose splendor is the auspicious mandala of the rays of renunciation, who are anointed with the sandalwood of ethical discipline and compassion, and who are firmly joined by the solid joints of the arrow of patience—quickly place the supreme [teachings] before me. (23)

O you who are irreversible in the discipline of all beings, elevated upon the samādhi-cage of meditative concentration, and who carry the union of the essence of wisdom—establish me in that most excellent Dharma-vehicle! 24.

Purifying the wheel of vows and the wheel of destinies, with a firm foundation of the great Dharma-retention, well-constructed and perfectly established as a machine of wisdom—cause me to ascend the vehicle of Dharma. 25.

Bring to me the vehicle of wisdom, which is purified by the conduct of Samantabhadra, which possesses a courageous stride that gazes upon sentient beings without delay, and which everywhere displays the prowess of pure conduct. 26.
That firm knowledge, established with the essence of a diamond, well-perfected by the noble ones and firmly grounded,
which completely cuts through all obscurations— mount me upon that auspicious vehicle! 27.
Mount me upon the vehicle of enlightenment—vast, stainless, equal to the world, a refuge for all beings, bringing happiness, as expansive as the realm of phenomena, and brilliantly shining. 28.

Please cause me to mount the Dharma-vehicle, which severs the mass of suffering that arises from that [cycle], purifies the wheel of dust consisting of karma and afflictions, and crushes all Māras and adversaries. (29)

O you whose sphere of knowledge extends in all directions, who are the arrayed expanse of the sky of the dharma-realm, please bring to me the Dharma-vehicle that fulfills the intentions of all sentient beings. 30.

Mount for me the Dharma-vehicle, which is as pure as the sky, immeasurable and inexhaustible; it is free from the darkness of false views and stainless; it is established for the benefit of all sentient beings. 31.

Impelled by the force of that great wind, sustaining the world-system through the power of the wind of aspiration, and establishing all beings upon the ground of the city of peace—mount me upon this vehicle of Dharma! 32.

Mount me upon that supreme vehicle, which is like the great earth and its mountains, which carries the burden through the power of the force of compassion, and which sustains the world with the perfection of wisdom. 33.

Just as the sun protects the life-sustaining world through its gathering of vast circles of rays, so may you reveal to me the sun of wisdom, which possesses the pure radiance of the supreme dhāraṇīs. 34.

O Noble One, you who have been trained for many, countless eons and are skilled in the ground of all methods of causal reasoning— grant me the firm vajra of wisdom by which the city of the conditioned may be shattered. (35)

In that ocean of vast wisdom where you were trained—where those of incomparable oceans of intellect have been schooled, and where the excellence of being sprinkled with all the qualities of a Buddha resides—O Noble One, please tell me well: what is it like? (36)
There, with eyes fully ascended and adorned with the crown of the king of knowledge,
and with heads bound by the excellent turban of the Dharma, they shall behold the city of the King of Dharma.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, looking with the gaze of a nāga, said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son! It is well that you, having resolved upon unexcelled perfect enlightenment, follow after spiritual friends;
that you consider it necessary to inquire about the conduct of a bodhisattva, desiring to fulfill the path of a bodhisattva."
For this, noble son, is the beginning;
this is the natural outflow for the perfect accomplishment of omniscience:
namely, the serving, honoring, and attending upon spiritual friends.
"Therefore, noble son, you should be untiring in attending upon spiritual friends.
Sudhana said: "Noble one, in detail, how should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct? How should they practice?"
How should a bodhisattva undertake the bodhisattva practice?
How should a bodhisattva conduct themselves in the bodhisattva practice?
How should a bodhisattva bring the bodhisattva practice to fulfillment?
How should a bodhisattva purify the bodhisattva practice?
How should a bodhisattva enter the bodhisattva practice?
How should a bodhisattva bring the bodhisattva practice to fulfillment?
How should a bodhisattva follow the bodhisattva practice?
How should a bodhisattva take hold of the bodhisattva practice?
How should a bodhisattva expand the bodhisattva practice?
"How does the Bodhisattva’s maṇḍala of the conduct of Samantabhadra become fulfilled?
Then Mañjuśrī, the Youthful Prince, addressed Sudhana, the merchant's son, in verses:
"Excellent, O ocean of pure merit, you who have indeed come into my presence!"
With a mind characterized by vast compassion, you seek supreme enlightenment. // 38 //
For the sake of liberating the entire world, you have made a vast and peerless vow for spiritual practice;
you shall become a protector of the world—this is the method of the conduct of awakening.
Those Bodhisattvas who are very firm and whose minds are untiring as they course through saṃsāra, indeed attain the Samantabhadra conduct, which is unconquered and unattached. 40.
O Puṇyaprabha, Puṇyaketu, Puṇyākara, and Puṇyasāgara, you have attained purity because you have practiced the Samantabhadra vow for the sake of the world. (41)
You shall behold the Buddhas of infinite and boundless meditative absorption throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
and by the power of your mindfulness, you shall uphold their clouds of Dharma.
Though you behold the Jinas in the ten directions, you shall purify the ocean of vows for those Buddha-fields within which you practice the conduct of awakening. (43)
Those who, having entered these oceans of methods, abide upon the stage of a Buddha,
become all-seeing by training under the Lords of the World.

Having practiced for many eons throughout the expanse of all fields, performing deeds as numerous as the atoms within those fields, you shall touch the auspicious Samantabhadra conduct and attain the spreading of enlightenment. 45.
One should practice throughout infinite and middleless oceans of eons in all realms without exception,
and one should fulfill the vows within the conduct of Samantabhadra, the supreme and universal one.
Behold the millions of beings who, having heard of your vow, have conceived a joy born of that vow;
they who aspire to awakening through the wisdom of Samantabhadra. (47)
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having spoken these verses, said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: “Excellent, excellent, noble son!

It is well that you, having resolved your mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, consider the conduct of a bodhisattva to be something that must be thoroughly sought. Rare, noble son, are those beings who resolve their minds upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.”
Therefore, those beings who, having generated the mind set on unexcelled perfect enlightenment, seek out the conduct of a bodhisattva, are most rare to find.
For this reason, noble son, a bodhisattva must become certain regarding true spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) for the sake of attaining the knowledge of omniscience;
he must remain untiring in his search for spiritual friends.
You should never be satiated in beholding spiritual friends;
you should be receptive and respectful toward the instructions of spiritual friends;
and you should remain unimpeded in regard to the skillful means and conduct of spiritual friends.
"Noble son, right here in the southern region there is a country named Rāmāvarānta.
There is a mountain there called Sugrīva,
and a monk named Meghaśrī dwells there."
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one apply oneself? How should the conduct of a bodhisattva be undertaken?"
How should one practice the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should the conduct of a bodhisattva be fulfilled?
How should it be purified?
How should it be entered?
How should it be brought forth?
How should it be followed?
How should it be taken up?
How should it be expanded?
How does the bodhisattva’s maṇḍala of the Samantabhadra conduct become complete?
Noble son, that spiritual friend will instruct you in the maṇḍala of the conduct of Samantabhadra.

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, joyful, elated, uplifted, and filled with rapture and gladness, bowed his head at the feet of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta. He circumambulated Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta hundreds of thousands of times, gazed upon him hundreds of thousands of times, and— his heart following with love for the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)— could not bear the sight of the spiritual friend being out of view.
With his face bathed in tears, he departed from the presence of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta. // 1 //
(Gv 48) 4. Meghaśrī.
Then, indeed, Sudhana the merchant’s son proceeded by stages until he arrived at the region of Rāmāvarānta.

Having approached the vicinity of Rāmāvara and wandering through the countryside, he— who had cultivated roots of merit in the past— enjoyed pleasures that were agreeable to his mind and based on his previous deeds. Then, having gone toward the mountain of Sugrīva and ascended Mount Sugrīva,
he set out toward the eastern direction in search of the monk Meghaśrī.
In this manner, he set out toward the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, and northwestern directions;
seeking the monk Meghaśrī, he looked upward as well as downward.
After the passing of seven days, he saw the monk Meghaśrī walking back and forth on the slope of a certain mountain peak.
He approached the monk Meghaśrī, bowed his head at the feet of the monk Meghaśrī, circumambulated the monk Meghaśrī, and standing before him with palms joined, said this: "Indeed,..."
"May the Noble One know that I have generated the mind set upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct, nor how one should practice it."
How should the conduct of a bodhisattva be undertaken?
How should one practice the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should the conduct of a bodhisattva be brought to fulfillment?
How is it to be purified? How is it to be entered? How is it to be brought forth?
How is it to be followed? How is it to be taken as an object of focus? How is it to be expanded?

"How does the mandala of the conduct of Samantabhadra become fulfilled for a bodhisattva? I have heard, Noble One, that you give instruction and admonition to the bodhisattvas; therefore, may the Noble One tell me how bodhisattvas set forth toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
When this had been said, the monk Meghaśrī spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!

That you, having resolved upon unexcelled perfect enlightenment, inquire about the conduct of a bodhisattva—this is indeed difficult, noble son, this is most difficult: namely, the thorough seeking of the bodhisattva's conduct and the thorough seeking of the bodhisattva's sphere of activity."

The thorough seeking of the purification of the Bodhisattva’s departure; the thorough seeking of the purification of the Bodhisattva’s path; the thorough seeking of the purification of the vastness of the Bodhisattva’s conduct;

the thorough seeking of the purification of the manifestation of the Bodhisattva’s supernormal powers; the manifestation of the Bodhisattva’s liberations; the manifestation of the Bodhisattva’s compassionate activity throughout the world;
the Bodhisattva’s conformity to the world according to its inclinations; and the manifestation of the gates of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa for Bodhisattvas.
It is the investigation and pursuit of the examination of the stains and fears regarding the faults of the conditioned and the unconditioned.
Noble son, by the sovereign power of the strength of my resolve, through the purification of the eye of wisdom and faith,
by the illumination of the light of non-retrogressive knowledge, and by the universal gaze that faces all directions with unimpeded range throughout all spheres—

Through vision free from all obscurations, through the skill of Vipaśyin, through the purity of the range of the universal eye, through the purity of the body, through the skill of bowing the body by facing the flow of the streams of all directions, and through the power of dhāraṇī that sustains the clouds of all Buddha-dharmas, I behold the Tathāgatas facing me from all the realms of all directions.
That is to say, in the eastern direction, I see one Tathāgata; I see two, ten,
and even a hundred Buddhas.
Even a thousand Buddhas, even a hundred thousand Buddhas, even ten million Buddhas.
Even a hundred koṭis of Buddhas, even a thousand koṭis of Buddhas, even a hundred thousand koṭis of Buddhas.

I see even hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, up to Tathāgatas who are immeasurable, incalculable, infinite, inconceivable, incomparable, all-pervading, boundless, unattainable, and inexpressible.
I see Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa; I see Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in a world-system of four continents;
and I see Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in a thousandfold, a two-thousandfold, and a three-thousandfold great thousandfold Buddha-field.
I see Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields;
likewise, those as numerous as the atoms in a hundred Buddha-fields,
and even those as numerous as the atoms in a thousand Buddha-fields.
Even those as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields,
even those as numerous as the atoms in millions of Buddha-fields,
and even those as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of millions of Buddha-fields.
Even those as numerous as the atoms in thousands of millions of Buddha-fields,
even those as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-fields,
and even those as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddha-fields.
I see Tathāgatas even as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
just as in the eastern direction,
so too in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions— I see even a single Tathāgata.
I behold even as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

Surveying each of the directions, I see Tathāgatas of various colors, various forms, various miraculous transformations, and various displays of heroic power; they possess diverse arrays of circles of assemblies and emit networks of light rays of many colors and many hues.

I see Tathāgatas who have roared the lion’s roar of the bull among Buddhas; they manifest arrays of the purification of various Buddha-fields and abodes, which are purified by various measures of lifespan and which inform the world according to its inclinations; they display the miraculous transformations of the gates of the purification of various modes of perfect awakening.
O noble son, of this [samādhi] called "The Light that Collects the Cognitions of All Objects through Universal Gates,"...
Having attained the recollection of the Buddha,
[he thought]: "How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the qualities of the Bodhisattvas, whose mandalas of infinite wisdom are purified?"

Those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha as a universal orb of light, by virtue of facing and beholding the purity and array of the mandalas of all Tathāgatas and all Buddha-fields;

those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha established for all the world, through the purity of seeing the Tathāgata who manifests to the world according to its inclinations;
and those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha established in the ten powers, by following the immeasurable powers of the ten Tathāgatas.

Those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha through the superimposition of dharmas, by means of beholding clouds of the bodies of all Tathāgatas in the form of hearing the Dharma;
those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha as the womb illuminating the directions, by means of entering the unconfused oceans of Buddhas in all the oceans of directions;

and those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha through entry into the ten directions, by means of entering the bull-like power of the miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas with subtle objects of focus.

Those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas established throughout eons, through the cognition of beholding all Tathāgatas at every moment; those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas established throughout time, by virtue of never being separated from the vision and dwelling with all Tathāgatas at all times; and those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas established throughout buddha-fields, through the cognition of beholding the Buddha-bodies that arise in all buddha-fields and are unsurpassed.

Those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas established throughout the three times, by virtue of the convergence of their own mental dispositions with the mandala of the Tathāgatas of the three times;

those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas established upon objective referents, through the cognition that perceives the manifestation of the succession of all Tathāgatas as objective referents;

and those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas established in tranquility, through the cognition of the parinirvāṇa of all Tathāgatas in all world-systems in a single instant.
Those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha established through departure, by means of perceiving the movement of all Tathāgatas in all dwellings in a single day;

those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha established through expansion, by means of perceiving the bodies of the Buddhas filling the cross-legged postures within each and every realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); and those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha established through subtlety, by means of entering upon an incalculable number of appearances of Buddhas' births within the path of a single hair.

Those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha as a manifested array, through the manifestation and communication of the display of perfect enlightenment in all world-systems in a single instant; those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha as a functional manifestation, through the attainment of the illumination of wisdom regarding the displays of the wheel of Dharma in the arising of all Buddhas;

those who have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddha as a superimposed manifestation, through the attainment of the reflection of all Tathāgatas appearing according to the inclinations of their own minds; those who...
They have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas as projected by karma, by virtue of manifesting the reflections of the karma accumulated by all living beings;

they have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas as projected by miraculous transformations, through the universal communication that perceives the vast miraculous displays of the Buddhas filling the lotus-pools of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) without exception;
and they have attained the gateway of the recollection of the Buddhas as projected upon the sky, by beholding the sky of the *dharmadhātu* arrayed with clouds of the Tathāgatas' forms.
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region is a district called Sāgaramukha.
There dwells a monk named Sāgaramegha.
Go to him and ask:
"How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one practice?"
Noble son, that spiritual friend will illuminate for you, cause you to enter into the causes for the accumulation of roots of virtue,
and generate for you the vast stage of accumulation.
He will extol the powerful force of the momentum of vast roots of merit;
he will generate the cause for the vast accumulation of the thought of awakening;
and he will sustain the cause for the vast illumination of the Mahāyāna.
He will manifest the vast power of the equipment of the perfections; he will purify the vast method for entering the ocean of conduct;
and he will cleanse the vast circle of his vows.
He will cause the vast array of universal gateways for liberation to flourish;
he will cause the vast power of great compassion to increase.

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the monk Meghaśrī, circumambulated the monk Meghaśrī hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at him, departed from the presence of the monk Meghaśrī. // 2 //
(Gv 51) 5. Sāgaramegha. Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, reflecting upon that instruction from his spiritual friend, [proceeded].
Recalling that world, contemplating that bodhisattva liberation,
and following that method of bodhisattva samādhi,
Beholding that ocean-like method of the Bodhisattvas, resolving with devotion toward that circle of Buddhas, and longing for that direction of the vision of the Buddhas, he—
Contemplating that ocean of Buddhas,
recollecting that succession of Buddhas,
and following that path of the Buddhas,

Beholding that sky of the Buddhas, he proceeded by degrees toward the region of the horizon known as Sāgaramukha, where the monk Sāgaramegha resided; having approached the monk Sāgaramegha, he bowed his head at the feet of the monk Sāgaramegha and circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times.

Having circumambulated him and stood before the monk Sāgaramegha with palms joined in reverence, he said this: "Noble one, I have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, desiring to descend into the unsurpassed ocean of gnosis.
Yet, I do not know how bodhisattvas turn back from the lineage of the world."
They turn toward the lineage of the Tathāgatas; they cross over the ocean of saṃsāra;
they descend into the ocean of the wisdom of omniscience.
They rise above the stages of foolish worldlings,
they are established in the family of the Tathāgatas,
and they turn back from the stream of saṃsāra.
They proceed within the stream of the bodhisattva’s conduct;
they turn back from the wheel of destinies in the ocean of saṃsāra; and they revolve the wheel of the bodhisattva’s vows and conduct.
They crush the entire mandala of Māra;
they illuminate the radiance arising from the entire mandala of the Buddhas;
and they dry up the ocean of craving.
They increase the waters of great compassion;
they close the doors to all unfavorable conditions, the states of woe, and the miserable destinies;
and they open the gates to heaven and nirvana.
They break open the door-panels of the city of the triple world;
they throw open the door-panels of the gateway to omniscience;
they abandon all craving for worldly requisites.
They generate the vow to gather in all living beings.
When this had been said, the monk Sāgaramegha spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son, that you have resolved your mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment!
For, noble son, the resolve for enlightenment does not arise in sentient beings who have not planted roots of merit."
They had attained the illumination of skillfulness through all gates; they were illumined by the light of the knowledge of the meditative concentrations of the path containing skillful means;

they had accumulated the provisions of a vast ocean of merit; they never ceased the accumulation of all that is pure; their skillful means were supported by all spiritual friends and remained untiring; they were indifferent to body and life; they were free from grasping at any object; their minds were like the earth, level without depression or elevation; and they were permeated by natural compassion and affection.
The thought of awakening arises for those beings who are facing the dwelling in all states of existence and who desire the domain of the Tathāgatas;
that is to say, the mind of great compassion for the sake of protecting all sentient beings,
and the mind of great loving-kindness for the sake of bringing harmony to the entire world.
A mind of happiness for the sake of pacifying the mass of suffering of the entire world; a mind of benefit for the sake of turning back all unwholesome dharmas;
a mind of compassion for the sake of protecting from all fears.
An unattached mind for the sake of turning back all obscurations; a vast mind for the sake of pervading the entire realm of phenomena;
an infinite mind for the sake of following the equality that converges with the realm of space.
The stainless mind for the sake of perceiving all Tathāgatas; the pure mind for the sake of the pervasive diffusion of knowledge that leaves nothing remaining throughout the three times;
the gnosis-mind for the sake of turning back all obscurations to knowledge and for the sake of entering the ocean of the omniscient one’s knowledge.
"Noble son, for twelve full years I have dwelt here in this region of the ocean’s mouth, taking this great ocean as my object of focus and bringing it before me;

that is to say, reflecting upon the vastness and immeasurability of the great ocean, its stainless clarity, its profoundity and difficulty of fathoming, its gradual slope and stable foundation, its variety of many jewel-mines, and the boundlessness of its masses of water."

Reflecting upon the inconceivable and sublime variety of colors, their infinite nature, their diverse and noble perfuming of the foundations, their being covered by great clouds, and their intermediate fullness,
it occurred to me, son of good family: "Is there indeed anyone else in this world who is more vast, more extensive, more immeasurable, and more profound than this ocean of my mind?"

And it was most wonderful. Noble son, as I was thus engaged in correct reflection and mental attention, a great lotus appeared beneath the great ocean, with a stem of sapphire and diamond, adorned with a crest-jewel of great lapis lazuli, and petals of vast, stainless Jāmbūnada gold.
It was an array of black sandalwood buds, possessed of filaments made of emerald gems, as vast in measure as the expansive ocean;
its central shaft was supported by a hundred thousand lords of the asuras, it was covered by a variegated net of jewels from a hundred thousand precious gems,

it was showered upon by clouds of fragrant water from a hundred thousand lords of the nāgas, and it had jeweled tassels and necklaces of gems hanging from the mouths of a hundred thousand lords of the garuḍas.
It was beheld with benevolent minds by a hundred thousand lords of the kinnaras; it was honored by the prostrations and services of a hundred thousand lords of the mahoragas;

it was worshipped by the bodies of a hundred thousand lords of the rākṣasas bowing low; it was enriched by the praises and songs of diverse musical instruments from a hundred thousand lords of the gandharvas;
and it was showered upon by clouds of divine flowers, perfumes, garlands, incense, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags from a hundred thousand lords of the devas.

It was honored by the prostrations of the heads of a hundred thousand Brahma-kings; it was saluted with palms joined in reverence by a hundred thousand deities of the Pure Abodes; it was worshipped by the seven jewels brought forth by a hundred thousand lords of men who had turned the ten wheels; it was venerated by the rising homage of a hundred thousand deities of the oceans;

it was illuminated by the array of light-rays from a hundred thousand *jyotīrasa* jewel-gems; and it was adorned by the perfectly arranged and firmly set placement of a hundred thousand jewels of pure merit.
It had a pure interior of one hundred thousand *vairocana* jewel-gems; it possessed the great majesty and splendor of one hundred thousand *śrīmaṇi* jewel-gems;
it was infinitely illuminated by one hundred thousand *vicitrakośa* jewel-gems; it was beautifully adorned by the stability and excellence of one hundred thousand *jambūdhvaja* jewel-gems;
it featured an invincible array of one hundred thousand *vajrasiṃha* jewel-gems; and it was accumulated through the noble heat of one hundred thousand *sūryagarbha* jewel-gems.
It was adorned with hundreds of thousands of various colors of beautiful mani-jewels, and it blazed with the inexhaustible array of light from hundreds of thousands of cintā-rāja-maṇi jewels.

That great lotus was born from the supramundane roots of virtue of the Tathāgata; it was directed toward the aspirations of Bodhisattvas, making itself known to all directions, emerged from the Dharma that has arrived, produced by karma free from impurities, an array of the method of the state of non-affliction, and its manifestation was equal in nature to a dream.
It is sealed with the principle of the unconditioned nature of phenomena, conforms to the principle of non-attachment, pervades the dharma-realm throughout the families of the ten directions,

and is filled with the radiance of the power of the Buddha’s domain; its limit of arrays of forms, qualities, structures, and colors cannot be reached even in hundreds of thousands of incalculable eons.
And I see that great lotus as completely filled and pervaded by the cross-legged posture of the Tathāgata’s body.
And I see that body of the Tathāgata from here up to the very summit of existence.
And I see the inconceivable array of that Tathāgata’s seat.
Inconceivable arrays of the circles of assemblies;
inconceivable arrays of circles of light;
inconceivable perfection of the primary marks; inconceivable variety of the secondary characteristics; and inconceivable bull-like majesty of the Buddhas.
The inconceivable miraculous power of the Buddhas;
the inconceivable purity of the Tathāgata’s physical marks;
and the inconceivable quality of having the crown of the head invisible.
I see his inconceivable and vast tongue; I hear the inconceivable arrays of the Buddhas' eloquence;
[I perceive] the inconceivable and immeasurable power.
I follow the inconceivable purity of the array of fearlessnesses; I pursue the inconceivable accomplishment of the powers of analytical knowledge;
and I recollect the inconceivable realization of my former bodhisattva conduct.
I behold the inconceivable miraculous display of perfect enlightenment;
I hear the inconceivable thundering of the clouds of Dharma, and the inconceivable array of the basis for the manifestation of universal vision.
I behold the inconceivable and immeasurable differentiation of the body into left and right, and the inconceivable attainment of the body for the sake of sentient beings.

And that Tathāgata, extending his right hand and stroking my head, [taught] the Dharma discourse named *Samantanetra*, which reveals the domain of all Tathāgatas, elucidates the conduct of Bodhisattvas, illuminates the distinctions within the depths of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), illuminates the convergence of the mandala of all phenomena, provides the light for the purification of the forms of the mandalas of all buddha-fields, and scatters the mandalas of all opposing disputants.

He reveals that which crushes all Māras and all heretical doctrines, which brings satisfaction to the realm of all sentient beings, which illuminates the dense thickets of the minds of all sentient beings,

which makes known the intentions of all sentient beings according to their inclinations, and which shines forth the revolution of the wheel of the faculties of all sentient beings. And I uphold, maintain, propagate, and deeply contemplate this Dharma-discourse called *Samantanetra* with such a form of retention.
If one were to write it down, the ink required would equal the volume of the waters of the great ocean,

and the collection of writing brushes would be as vast as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains; yet even then, not even a single verse, a single gateway of the Dharma, a single method of the Dharma, a single source of the Dharma, or a single distinction of a word of the Dharma from this discourse on the Dharma would have been exhausted.
Exhaustion is perceived,
but there is no deficiency, nor exhaustion, nor obsession, nor final termination.

Thus, noble son, for twelve full years I have upheld this *Samantanetra* Dharma-discourse. By such a form of upholding, through the illumination of the light of hearing, grasping, and retaining, I master incalculable recitations in a single day; and through the illumination of the light of the *Śāntamukha* dhāraṇī, I penetrate incalculable recitations.
By means of the illumination of the *śāntamukha* dhāraṇī, I penetrate incalculable cycles;
by means of the illumination of the *anantāvarta* dhāraṇī, I enter into incalculable cycles;
and by means of the illumination of the *bhūmyavacāraṇānugama* dhāraṇī, I discern and collect incalculable cycles.
By means of the illumination of the *tejovatī* dhāraṇī, I master incalculable chapters; by means of the illumination of the *padmavyūha* dhāraṇī, I bring forth incalculable chapters;
by means of the illumination of the *svaravivikta* dhāraṇī, I fully reveal incalculable chapters.
By the illumination of the Gaganagarbha-dhāraṇī, I distribute incalculable chapters;
by the illumination of the Jyotiṣakūṭa-dhāraṇī, I expand incalculable chapters; by the illumination of the Sāgaragarbha-dhāraṇī, I establish incalculable chapters.

And whatever beings approach me from the eastern direction— whether gods or lords of gods, nāgas or lords of nāgas, yakṣas or lords of yakṣas, asuras or lords of asuras, garuḍas or lords of garuḍas, mahoragas or lords of mahoragas, humans or lords of humans, or Brahmās or lords of Brahmās—
I establish and settle all of them right here in this Dharma-discourse, which illuminates the conduct of the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, called the Universal Eye.

For all of them, I cause them to take delight in this Universal Eye Dharma-discourse; I define it, illuminate it, praise it, demonstrate it, analyze it, expand upon it, clarify it, reveal it, release it, and shed its light.

Just as it is in the eastern direction, so it is for those beings who approach from the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions—
as described previously.
“Noble son, I know only this single Dharma-discourse.”
How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the virtues of the Bodhisattvas—who have descended into the ocean of all Bodhisattva practices by following their purified vows;
who have descended into the ocean of all vows in order to sever the continuity of dwelling through all kalpas;

who have descended into the saṃsāra of all beings to act in accordance with their inclinations; and who have descended into the ocean of the minds of all the world-systems through the manifestation of wisdom?
For the sake of generating the vision of the unimpeded knowledge of the Ten Powers for those who have entered the ocean of all virtues;
for the sake of not missing the proper time for ripening and disciplining those who have entered the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings;
and for the sake of the accomplishment of the vow for the purification of all buddha-fields by those who have entered the ocean of all fields.
By the power of their vow to serve and worship the Tathāgatas, having entered the ocean of all Buddhas;
by their cognitive discernment, having entered the ocean of all dharmas;
and by their conformity to practice, having entered the ocean of all virtues.
For those who have entered the ocean of mantras of the entire world, it is for the sake of accomplishing the turning of the wheel of Dharma within all mantras.
Go, son of good family;
here in this very southern region, sixty yojanas from here, is the path to Laṅkā called Sāgaratīra.
There dwells a monk named Supratiṣṭhita.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva purify the conduct of a bodhisattva?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the monk Sāgaramegha, circumambulated the monk Sāgaramegha hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at him, departed from the presence of the monk Sāgaramegha. // 3 //
(Gv 55) 6. Supratiṣṭhita.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, recollecting that instruction from his spiritual friend and that Dharma-discourse called Samantanetra, [proceeded].
And while reflecting upon that miraculous display of the Tathāgata,
upholding those clouds of Dharma words and syllables,
and entering those oceans of Dharma gateways, he—
And while surveying that method of Dharma, plunging into those turnings of Dharma,
and entering that sky of Dharma, he—
Purifying that circle of Dharma and reflecting upon that island of the jewel of Dharma,
he proceeded by stages toward the shore of the ocean along the path to Laṅkā; having arrived there, he gazed toward the eastern direction out of a desire to see the monk Supratiṣṭhita.
In this manner, he looked toward the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions, desiring to see the monk Supratiṣṭhita.
He saw the monk Supratiṣṭhita walking back and forth in the expanse of the sky, surrounded by an incalculable hundred thousand deities;
and he beheld that expanse of the sky strewn with clouds of divine flowers and resounding with the music of an incalculable multitude of divine instruments.

He saw the vault of the sky adorned with countless silk banners and streamers by the lords of the gods during their act of worship for the monk Supratiṣṭhita; and he heard from the vault of the sky the sounds of countless divine, charming words of praise and the resonance of all kinds of musical instruments and songs performed by the lords of the *kiṃnaras*, accompanied by the rising thunder of inconceivable clouds of *kālāguru* incense produced by the lords of the *nāgas*.

He saw inconceivable clouds of fine, shimmering garments spread across the expanse of the sky, sent by great lords of the *mahoragas* with hearts full of joy, appearing in forms that inspired longing for the monk Supratiṣṭhita;
and he saw inconceivable clouds of precious jewels presided over by the lords of the *asuras* in the sky, radiating the light of an inconceivable array of virtues;

and he saw inconceivable hosts of *garuḍa* lords in the sky, possessing the noble forms, strength, and stature of humans, surrounded by retinues of *garuḍa* lord-maidens, supreme in non-violence, with their palms joined in reverence.

And by the sovereign power of the monk Supratiṣṭhita’s loving-kindness (*maitrī*), he saw hundreds of thousands of inconceivable lords of yakṣas with their retinues, possessing deformed bodies, situated in the expanse of the sky;
and he saw hundreds of thousands of inconceivable lords of rākṣasas with their retinues moving about in the expanse of the sky, intent upon protecting the monk Supratiṣṭhita;

and he saw hundreds of thousands of inconceivable lords of Brahmās in the expanse of the sky with palms joined in reverence, engaged in offering praises through intended, pleasing, and agreeable words of address.

And he saw hundreds of thousands of inconceivable deities belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm situated in their celestial palaces in the expanse of the sky, engaged in the act of worshipping the monk Supratiṣṭhita.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, seeing the monk Supratiṣṭhita walking back and forth in the sky, was satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and cheer; with palms joined, he paid homage to the monk Supratiṣṭhita and spoke thus: "Noble one, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
And I do not know: how should a bodhisattva seek the qualities of a Buddha?
How should a bodhisattva fully accomplish the qualities of a Buddha?
How should a bodhisattva gather the qualities of a Buddha?
How should a bodhisattva serve the qualities of a Buddha?
How should a bodhisattva cultivate the qualities of a Buddha?
How should a bodhisattva follow the qualities of a Buddha?
How should a bodhisattva gather together the qualities of a Buddha?
How should a bodhisattva cultivate the qualities of a Buddha? How should a bodhisattva purify the qualities of a Buddha for the sake of accomplishing all the tasks of a bodhisattva?
"How should a bodhisattva comprehend the qualities of a Buddha? I have heard, Noble One, that you grant instruction and advice to bodhisattvas;
therefore, may the Noble One tell me: how should a bodhisattva apply himself to the qualities of a Buddha?"
By practicing in such a way, one becomes never separated from the vision of the Buddhas;
by being free from dwelling in false views, one becomes never separated from the vision of the Bodhisattvas;
and for the sake of unifying all the roots of virtue of all Bodhisattvas, one becomes never separated from the Buddha-qualities.
He is never separated from the pursuit of wisdom through all the vows of the bodhisattvas;
he is never separated from the conduct of a bodhisattva for the sake of accomplishing all the tasks of a bodhisattva;
and he is never separated from the pervading of all buddha-fields in order to dwell in all eons without weariness.

He is never separated from the vision of the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas for the sake of purifying all world-systems; he is never separated from dwelling in the conditioned for the sake of perceiving the miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas;
and he is never separated from hearing the Dharma for the sake of following his own body through all states of existence, destinies, deaths, and births, which are like emanations.

He is never separated from the light of knowledge for the sake of receiving the cloud of Dharma of all Tathāgatas, and for the sake of following and pursuing the realization of knowledge of the three times.
When this had been said, the monk Supratiṣṭhita spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: “Excellent, excellent, noble son!
It is well that you, having resolved upon unexcelled perfect enlightenment, inquire about the qualities of a Buddha, the qualities of omniscience, and the qualities of the Self-Existent One.
Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called ‘The Gate of Non-attachment.’”

"Son of good family, by taking up, setting forth, following, analyzing, examining, scrutinizing, illuminating, and radiating this bodhisattva liberation called the 'Gate of Non-attachment,' I have attained the light of knowledge named 'The Limit of Non-attachment.
Through its attainment, I have no attachment regarding the illumination of the mental activities of all sentient beings."
There is no attachment to the thorough knowledge of the death and rebirth of all sentient beings; there is no attachment to the entries into the gateway of recollecting former abodes;
there is no attachment to the co-dwellings of the entire world throughout future eons.
There is no attachment to the perceptions of all beings in the present time;
there is no attachment to the thorough knowledge of the sounds, mantras, and conventional expressions of all sentient beings;
there is no attachment to the severing of the doubts of all sentient beings.
There is no attachment to entering into the perceptions of time— whether night, day, moments, or hours;
nor is there any attachment to the bodiless pervasion throughout the buddha-fields of the ten directions, namely,
by means of the attainment of non-abiding in existence and the absence of volitional construction.
"By the power of this unconditioned supernatural faculty, noble son, I walk, stand, and sit here in the sky."
I sit down,
I assume various modes of deportment,
I vanish within and reappear.
I smoke and I blaze;
being one, I become many,
and having become many, I become one.
I experience manifestation and disappearance;
I pass unhindered through walls and through enclosures, just as if through space;
and I travel cross-legged through the sky, just like a winged bird.
I perform the act of emerging from and sinking into the earth as if in water; I walk upon water without adhering to it as if upon the earth;
I emit smoke and blaze forth like a great mass of fire.
I cause even the earth to tremble;
I even stroke with my hand these two, the moon and the sun, who possess such great supernatural power (*maharddhika*), such great majesty (*mahānubhāva*), and such great splendor (*mahaujaska*);
and I extend my body as far as the world of Brahmā (*brahmaloka*).
Having made the world covered by clouds of masses of perfumes and incense, I blaze forth.
Having made the world covered by clouds of the radiance of all jewels, I emit clouds of emanations resembling all living beings.
Emitting clouds of networks of light with infinite colors, I go out into all directions—that is to say, I go out toward the eastern direction.
(Gv 57) I go forth toward the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions.
In each single moment of thought, I transcend one world-system in the eastern direction;
likewise two, ten, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand, and even ten million world-systems.
I transcend even a hundred koṭis of world-systems, a thousand koṭis of world-systems, a hundred thousand koṭis of world-systems,

and even a hundred thousand niyutas of koṭis of world-systems; I transcend immeasurable world-systems, incalculable ones, inconceivable ones, incomparable ones, unmeasurable ones, all-pervasive ones, limitless ones, those that have reached no boundary, and even world-systems that are ineffably ineffable.
And those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who reside, remain, and maintain themselves in those world-systems—
in each of those oceans of world-systems and in each of those expanses of world-systems—
In those various directions of world-systems,
in those various successions of world-systems,
and in those various convergences of world-systems,
In each of those various occurrences of world-systems,
in each of those various descriptions of world-systems,
and in each of those various gateways to world-systems.
In each of those descriptions of the arrangement of world-systems,
in each of those entries into world-systems,
and in each of those arrays of the seats of enlightenment within world-systems,
In each of those world-systems and assembly circles where the Blessed Buddhas teach the Dharma,

I approach each one of those Tathāgatas, raining down clouds of offerings— equal in number to the atoms within infinite Buddha-fields— with various bodies equal in number to the atoms within infinite Buddha-fields, and with each single body.
Having approached, I perform worship without ceasing with all flowers, all perfumes, all garlands, all ointments, all garments, all banners, all flags, all canopies, all nets, and all images;
and whatever those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, speak, teach, utter, reveal, extol, illuminate, instruct, explain, and manifest—
I fully understand and master all of that;
and I recollect all the purification of the buddha-fields of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
just as it is in the eastern direction.
In the same way, I transcend even one world-system in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions;
I transcend two, ten, a hundred, and even as many world-systems as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
And those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who dwell, remain, and maintain themselves in those world-systems—
In each of those oceans of world-systems, in each of those purifications of world-systems,
and indeed in all those world-systems within their respective circles of assemblies, I see them all as they teach the Dharma.
I perform worship to those Tathāgatas with all kinds of flowers, up to and including all forms of offerings.
Whatever those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, speak, and whatever they manifest through their power, I understand it all and take it up.
And I remember all that purity of the Buddha-fields of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
And those beings to whom I appear,
and with whom I associate,
they all become destined for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
And whatever beings come within my range of vision—
whether they be subtle or gross, inferior or superior, happy or suffering— I empower their bodies to be of that same size, so as not to let the time for their ripening and discipline pass by.
And whatever beings approach me, I establish them all right here in this Bodhisattva liberation called "Universal Speed," which culminates in "Infallible Valor.

Noble son, I know only this Bodhisattva liberation called "The Entrance of Non-attachment," which accords with the ripening of all beings and consists in the practice of honoring and attending upon the Tathāgatas with universal speed.

What is possible for me [to know] regarding those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the ethical discipline of great compassion, the ethical discipline of practice in the Mahāyāna, the ethical discipline of never departing from the bodhisattva path, the ethical discipline of non-attachment, the ethical discipline of not failing the womb of the bodhisattva’s intention, the ethical discipline of not abandoning the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), the ethical discipline of focusing upon the qualities of a Buddha, and the ethical discipline of never being separated from the mental attention to omniscience?

It is impossible to know the conduct or to describe the virtues of those Bodhisattvas whose morality is equal to space, whose morality does not rely on any world, and whose morality is undecayed, unimpaired, unbroken, flawless, untarnished, stainless, pure, and free from dust and impurity.
Go, son of good family,
right here in the southern region to the Draviḍa city named Vajrapura;
there dwells a Draviḍa named Megha.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one practice?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of the monk Supratiṣṭhita, circumambulated the monk Supratiṣṭhita hundreds of thousands of times, and departed from the presence of the monk Supratiṣṭhita. // 4 //
(Gv 59) 7 Megha:
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, recollecting that light of the Dharma, was overcome by a surge of serene faith in the Dharma.

He maintains the mental attention of the perception of following the Buddhas; he is devoted to ensuring that the lineage of the Three Jewels is not interrupted; recollecting his spiritual friends, his mind illuminates the worlds of the three times; his mental activity follows great vows; he is intent on the practice of protecting the realm of all sentient beings;
his mind does not rely on delight in any conditioned things; he proclaims the lineage of dispassion; and he is supreme in his profound realization of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.
Unwavering in his vow for the purification of all world-systems and dwelling without reliance upon the circles of assemblies of all Buddhas,
he gradually approached the Dravidian city named Vajrapura. While searching for Megha the Dravidian,
he saw him in the middle of the city, seated upon a lion-throne at a crossroads for the sake of dharma-discourse before ten thousand living beings.
He was fully proclaiming the Dharma discourse titled "The Array of the Revolution of the Wheel of Syllables."

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of Megha the Dravidian, circumambulated Megha the Dravidian hundreds of thousands of times, and standing before him with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus: "Noble one, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
And I do not know: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one practice?
How does a bodhisattva’s generation of the mind of enlightenment as a bodhisattva not perish?
How does the intention become firm through tirelessness amidst all states of existence?
How is the resolute intention purified through being unassailable?
How is the power of great compassion generated through tirelessness?
How does one enter the power of dhāraṇī through the purity of universal gates?
How does the light of wisdom arise, which is the light that dispels the cataracts regarding all phenomena, by means of scattering the veil of the cataracts of all ignorance?
How does one enter the power of analytical knowledge (*pratisaṃvid*) for the sake of perfecting the circle of voice and skill in meaning, phenomena, etymological definitions, and eloquence?

How does the power of mindfulness prevail through the unbroken retention of all the wheels of the Buddhas' Dharma? How is the power of movement purified through following after the light of the movement toward all directions of all phenomena?
How is the power of meditative concentration of a bodhisattva perfected through the supreme discernment that ascertains the meaning of all phenomena?
Then, out of reverence for the Bodhisattva, Megha the Dramiḍa rose from that lion-throne, descended,

and prostrated with his entire body before the merchant’s son Sudhana. He then showered the merchant’s son Sudhana with heaps of golden flowers, and scattered priceless jewel-gems and sublime sandalwood powder over him.
He covered [the Buddha] with many hundreds of thousands of garments dyed in various wonderful colors;

having scattered and strewn over him many beautiful and delightful fragrant flowers of various hues, and having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped Sudhana with various other kinds of offerings, he paid homage.
He said this to the merchant’s son: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
It is well that you have resolved your mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Noble son, for one who has resolved their mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment..."

He has set out for the non-interruption of the lineage of all Buddhas; he is devoted to the correct communication of the lineage of dispassion; he has set out for the purification of the lineage of all fields;
and he is present for the ripening and disciplining of the lineage of all sentient beings.
He is applied to the thorough investigation of the lineage of all phenomena as they truly are;
he abides in non-contradiction with the lineage of all actions; he is applied to the fulfillment of the lineage of all bodhisattva practices;
and he has set out for the non-interruption of the lineage of all vows.
He has set out for the sake of following after the knowledge of the lineage of all three times;
he is diligent for the sake of strengthening the lineage of resolute faith;
he is empowered by the entire mandala of all Tathāgatas and is attended by them with their mindfulness.
It conforms to the equality of all Buddhas and is rejoiced in by all Bodhisattvas.
Rejoiced in by all noble ones,
honored by all Brahmās and Indras,
and protected by all lords of the gods.
He was honored by all the lords of yakṣas and welcomed by all the lords of rākṣasas.
He is praised by all the lords of nāgas, extolled by all the lords of kinnaras,
and sought after by all the lords of the world.
For the sake of completely severing the three types of miserable destinies in all world-systems; for the purpose of turning back from all paths of unfavorable conditions and evil rebirths;

for the purpose of transcending the path of all poverty; for the attainment of the excellence of gods and humans; for the non-separation from the sight of spiritual friends; for the unchanging hearing of the sublime Buddha-dharma; for the purification of the intention of the mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*); and for the arising and origination of the causes of the mind of awakening.

For the sake of attaining the illumination of the bodhisattva path, for the sake of following after the wisdom of the bodhisattvas, and for the sake of abiding upon the bodhisattva stages—this thought occurred to me, noble son: "The bodhisattvas are performers of what is difficult;
their appearance and manifestation are hard to encounter; they are the consolation of the world."
Bodhisattvas are like parents to all sentient beings;
bodhisattvas are like ornaments to the world with its gods;
bodhisattvas are like a refuge for those afflicted by suffering.
Bodhisattvas are like a shelter for the protection of the entire world;
bodhisattvas are like vital breath for those afflicted by various fears and calamities;
bodhisattvas are like whirlwinds for the purpose of supporting the entire world from falling into the precipices of the three lower realms.
Bodhisattvas are like the earth, because they cause the roots of virtue of all sentient beings to increase;
bodhisattvas are like the ocean, because they contain within them a treasury of inexhaustible jewels of merit;
bodhisattvas are like the sun, because they produce the illumination of the light of wisdom.
Bodhisattvas are like Mount Sumeru because they have risen up through their roots of merit;
bodhisattvas are like the moon because they have emerged as the moon of wisdom at the seat of enlightenment;
bodhisattvas are like heroes because they crush the entire army of Māra.
Bodhisattvas are like heroes for the sake of reaching the city of the self-arisen Dharma;
they are like fires because they consume the self-attachment of all sentient beings;
they are like clouds because they pour down the vast rain of the Dharma.
Bodhisattvas are like rain, for they cause the sprouts of the faculties of sentient beings—such as faith and the rest—to flourish.
Bodhisattvas are like ferrymen, for they show the way to the shore of the ocean of Dharma.
Bodhisattvas are like bridges, for they carry all sentient beings across the ocean of saṃsāra.
Bodhisattvas are like sacred fords, because they are accessible to all sentient beings.
Thus, having praised the bodhisattvas before the merchant’s son Sudhana with these words, Megha Drāmiḍa gave his approval to the merchant’s son Sudhana.
As he uttered this speech that gladdens the bodhisattvas, a mass of light issued forth from his mouth, by which mass of light the thousandfold world system was filled.
And those beings who perceived that light—
whether they were gods of great supernatural power, or gods,
or nāgas of great supernatural power, or nāgas—
Whether they be yakṣas of great supernatural power or yakṣas, gandharvas of great supernatural power or gandharvas, asuras of great supernatural power or asuras;
Or Garuḍas possessing great supernormal power, or Garuḍas;
or Kinnaras possessing great supernormal power, or Kinnaras;
or Mahoragas possessing great supernormal power, or Mahoragas.
Whether they be humans of great supernatural power or non-humans, or whether they be Brahmās of great supernatural power or other Brahmās.
Illumined by that light, they approached Megha Dramiḍa;
with their intentions empowered by Megha Dramiḍa, with palms joined in reverence, their bodies and minds gladdened,
filled with sublime joy, established in great veneration, having struck down the banner of Māra, free from deceit and guile, and with their faculties serene.
Megha Drāmiḍa extensively proclaimed, revealed, introduced, and guided them toward that very Dharma-discourse, the Array of the Revolution of Wheel-Syllables.
He followed after him, and having heard it, they all became irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then, sitting again upon the Dharma-seat, he said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Noble son, I have attained the light of the *dhāraṇī* called Sarasvatī."
Thus, within the world-systems of one thousand, two thousand, and three thousand worlds, I understand the divine mantras of the gods;
likewise, I understand the mantras of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and Brahmās.
I understand the diversity of the divine mantras of the gods.
In this way, I understand the diversity of the mantras of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and Brahmās;
I understand the unity of the mantras of the gods.
In this way, I understand the unity of the mantras of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and Brahmās.
I understand the secret mantras of the gods;
likewise, I understand the secret mantras of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and Brahmās.
I understand all the conventional mantras and designations of beings belonging to the animal realm.
I understand the mental designations of the beings in the hells; I understand the mental designations of the beings in the world of Yama;
I understand the mental designations of the noble ones.
I understand the designations of non-noble mantras;
I understand the intentions, speech, and expressions of the mantra-beings who are bodhisattvas.

I penetrate and have faith in the oceans of the vocal qualities and sounds of the Tathāgatas attained throughout the three times, as they are joined with the speech and mantras of all sentient beings.
In every single moment of mind, just as I here enter into the ocean of all the conventions, etymologies, mantras, and designations of sentient beings within this trichiliocosm,

so too do I enter into them in the eastern direction— in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of world-systems that are immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, boundless, limitless, and beyond description—
likewise in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, and southwestern directions.
In the western-northern direction, below and above, throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of immeasurable world systems, even unto those that are ineffable beyond expression,

I enter the ocean of all the conventional usages, verbal expressions, mantras, and designations of sentient beings— namely, I understand the divine mantras of the gods, up to the Brahma-mantras of the Brahmas.
Noble son, this is the illumination of the Sarasvatī dhāraṇī that I know regarding the bodhisattvas;
how could I possibly know the conduct of the bodhisattvas or describe their qualities?
Those who have entered the oceans of various states of perception;
those who have entered the oceans of mantras of various perceptions regarding all worlds;
and those who have entered the oceans of explanations of the various names of worlds.
Those who have entered the oceans of the various conventional expressions, designations, and linguistic usages that describe the entire world;
those who have entered the oceans of the connections between all words;
and those who have entered the oceans of the ultimate meanings of words.

Those who have entered the oceans of conventional expressions that take as their single object of focus all objects of focus throughout the three times; those who have entered the oceans of explanations of successive words;
those who have entered the oceans of explanations of successive verses of two lines.
Those who have entered the oceans of explanations for the distinctions of words;
those who have entered the oceans of explanations for the discipline through the distinctions of words for all phenomena;
those who have entered the oceans of mantras for all living beings.
Those who have entered the array of the purification of the entire mandala of sounds; those who have emerged from the distinctions of the movement of tens of millions of wheels of syllables.
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region is a country named Vanavāsī.
There dwells a merchant chief named Muktaka.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva apply himself to the bodhisattva conduct? How should he set it forth? And how should his mind be concentrated?"
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of Megha the Dramiḍa; honoring him with reverence for the Dharma,
manifesting the root-characteristic of born faith, and perceiving that omniscience is attained by following spiritual friends, he remained there.

With tears on his face, weeping, he circumambulated Megha Draviḍa many hundreds of thousands of times; looking back at him again and again, he prostrated himself and departed from the presence of Megha Draviḍa. // 5 //
(Gv 63) 8. Muktaka:
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, reflecting upon that very array of light from the *bodhisattva-sarasvatī-dhāraṇī*, set out.
Entering that very ocean of the bodhisattva’s method of mantras,
recollecting that very purification and purity of the bodhisattva’s mind,
and accomplishing that very production of the accumulation of the bodhisattva’s wholesome latencies;
Purifying that very gateway to the maturation of bodhisattvas, refining that very wisdom of bodhisattvas for gathering sentient beings,
strengthening that very purity of the power of a bodhisattva’s intention, and supporting that very power of a bodhisattva’s resolute intention;
purifying that very lineage of bodhisattva resolve,
honoring that very goodness of the bodhisattva’s intention and mind,
and furthering that very bodhisattva’s exertion;

The merchant’s son Sudhana possessed an array of mental continuity that was untiring in its resolve and vows; his valorous energy was irreversible, and his mental determination was never turned back. Endowed with the power of faith that cannot be diverted, his mind was as indestructible as a diamond or the Nārāyaṇa-strength.
He accepted the instructions of all spiritual friends with skillful receptivity, his sphere of wisdom remained unimpaired, and he was oriented toward universal purity through all gateways.

His sphere of activity was the purity of unimpeded knowledge; he possessed the light of the method of all-pervading eye-knowledge; he had attained the illumination of the *dhāraṇīs* of all stages; his mind was directed toward the penetration of the depths of the *dharmadhātu*; he was characterized by the manifestation of the nature of universal, non-abiding, arrayed purity; he reached the pinnacle of a sphere that is homeless, unequaled, and non-dual; he was purified through the gateway of knowledge that transcends all conceptualizations; and he manifested arrays that remove obstacles regarding the distinctions between the families and directions of all quarters.

He is one who cannot be turned back by the distinctions of the directions of the world-levels; he is one who does not retreat from the distinctions of the directions of the levels of Dharma; he is one for whom the ultimate is the representation of seeing the distinctions of the directions and lineages of the Buddhas;

he is a knower whose wisdom conforms to the distinctions of the directions and lineages below; his intellect is perfected by the beautiful wheel of Dharma; his mind is illuminated by the world through the forms of the Samantaraucira-jñāna-samādhi;
his mental body conforms to the ground of all objective spheres; his continuum is illuminated by the lightning of Tathāgata-wisdom; and he is born from the force of the serene waves of omniscience.

Never parted from the impulse of serene faith in the Buddha-dharma, permeated by the impulse of the Tathāgata’s empowerment, illuminated by the light that follows his own mind in accordance with all Buddhas, endowed with the vow to pervade the entire network of world-systems with his own body, and supreme in accomplishing the convergence of his own body within the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), he eventually reached that forest-dwelling district after twelve years.
Searching for that merchant Muktaka, he saw him;
having seen him, he prostrated himself with his whole body, stood before him with palms joined in reverence, and spoke thus: "Noble sir, I have gained a great gain."
He has encountered the auspicious friend Megha.
Why is that? For it is rare to behold spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
The appearance of virtuous friends is difficult to encounter, difficult to return to, difficult to approach,
difficult to attend upon, difficult to find, difficult to dwell with, difficult to please, and difficult to follow; yet,
this meeting with the virtuous friend Megha has now come to pass.
Noble one, I have generated the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; that is to say,

for the sake of honoring all buddhas, for the sake of pleasing all buddhas, for the sake of beholding all buddhas, for the sake of making all buddhas known, for the sake of attaining the equality of all buddhas, for the sake of following the vows of all buddhas, and for the sake of fulfilling the vows of all buddhas.

For the sake of illuminating the wisdom through which all Buddhas attain realization; for the sake of manifesting the very bodies of all Buddhas; for the sake of manifesting one's own conduct through the attainment of all Buddhas; for the sake of directly perceiving the miraculous transformations of all Buddhas through supernormal knowledge; for the sake of purifying the powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas; for the sake of never being satiated by hearing the teaching of all dharmas;
for the sake of hearing and grasping the teaching of the Buddha-dharma of all Buddhas; and for the sake of upholding the teaching of the Buddha-dharma of all Buddhas.

For the sake of the analytical exposition of all the Buddha-dharmas; for the sake of upholding the teaching of all Buddhas; for the sake of the oneness of all Buddhas and all sentient beings; for the sake of the commonality of all bodhisattvas; for the purification of all bodhisattva practices; for the fulfillment of all bodhisattva perfections;
for the purification of the accomplishment of all bodhisattva vows; and for the sake of obtaining the treasury of the empowerment of all Buddhas upon all bodhisattvas.
For the sake of the light of inexhaustible wisdom that is the treasury of the dharma-store of all bodhisattvas; for the purpose of following after the treasury of the storehouse of all bodhisattvas;

for the accomplishment of the treasury of the immeasurable qualities of all bodhisattvas; for the attainment of the ultimate limit in training sentient beings through the treasury of the storehouse of the great compassion of all bodhisattvas;

for the manifestation of the treasury of the storehouse of the miraculous transformations of all bodhisattvas; and for the mastery over one's own mind through the treasury of the storehouse of the sovereign powers of all bodhisattvas.
For the sake of the array of all modes of the treasury and storehouse of the purification of all bodhisattvas,

noble one, it is with such a mind that I have approached here; with such an intention, such a desire, such a delight, such a disposition, such a supreme resolve, and such a focus upon the sphere of activity.
Thus oriented toward this realization, thus supreme in purity, thus intent upon this array, thus humble in mind, thus engaged in virtuous practice, and with faculties thus directed,
I have heard that the Noble One gives instruction and admonition to the bodhisattvas.
It does not teach a method; it illuminates the following along; it teaches the path.
He causes one to descend into the ford,
he opens the door of the Dharma,
and he cuts through doubts.
He dispels doubt, extracts the thorn of indecision,
and removes the stain of uncertainty.
It illuminates the depths of the mind,
removes the impurities of the mind, and clarifies the continuity of the mind.
It removes crookedness of mind,
refreshes the fever of the mind,
and turns it away [from unwholesome states].
It turns back the mind from cyclic existence, turns it away from unwholesome states,
and separates it from the hells.
He causes them to move out from their dwellings,
liberates them through non-attachment,
and turns them away from all clingings.
He brings them face-to-face with omniscience,
turns them toward the entry into the city of Dharma,
and establishes them in great compassion.
He establishes them in great loving-kindness, causes them to enter the conduct of a bodhisattva, and settles them in the cultivation of the gateways of meditative concentration.

He establishes [the mind] in the gateways of following along, pervades it through the contemplation of intrinsic nature, and analyzes it by means of the following of the powers in order to follow the equality of all worlds with the mind.
May the Noble One tell me this: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should he apply himself? How should he practice?

"How does the circle of the bodhisattva’s conduct quickly become purified for one who is thus engaged? Then, at that time, the merchant Muktaka entered the entrance to the bodhisattva-samādhi called "The Convergence of All Buddha-fields," preceded by the entrance to the *dhāraṇī* of infinite revolutions, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata and the sustaining power of his former roots of merit.

And through the attention of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and the bestowal of the light of wisdom, as soon as the merchant Muktaka had entered that meditative absorption, such a purification of the body was established that,
by means of that purification of the body, he beheld the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields.

Together with the purification of the Buddha-fields, including their circles of assemblies; together with the purity of radiance, including their cohabitation in former practices and the miraculous transformations of Buddhas; together with the equipment of their vows, including the arrays of the departure through practice and the purity thereof; together with the manifestation of perfect enlightenment, the illumination of the wheel of Dharma, the ripening of sentient beings, and the ultimate limit of the Dharma—all these were contained within every part of his body.
They were seen to have entered therein:

the various arrays of Buddha-fields, which were mutually unmixed, mutually unobstructed, mutually well-distinguished, and mutually well-established with various types of configurations; they were correctly perceived, adorned with various circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas, and displaying the various miraculous transformations of Buddhas.
They were seen manifesting themselves;

established in the various systems of the vehicles and methods, they illuminated the gateway of various vows. In some world-systems, they were seen born in the Tuṣita heaven, performing all the works of a Buddha; in others, they were seen descending from the Tuṣita heaven.
In some places, while still within their mothers' wombs, they displayed various miraculous transformations; in other places, being born, they exhibited the play of childhood.

In some places they are seen in the midst of the inner apartments; in some, departing [from the city]; in some, having reached the excellent seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*), performing the great array of miraculous transformations and defeating the army of Māra;
and in some, surrounded by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas, being entreated by Brahmās and Indras to turn the wheel of the Dharma.
In some places they are seen turning the wheel of Dharma; in some places they have gone to the abodes of all sentient beings; in some places they are seen entering final nirvana.
In some world-systems the distribution of the relics of Tathāgatas who have entered final nirvana is seen;
in some places gods and humans of the Buddha-fields are seen adorning the shrines of the Tathāgatas.
And whatever those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, speak among the various classes of beings, in the various worlds of beings, in the various destinies of beings,

in the various births of beings, in the various assemblies of beings, in the various transformations of the roots of merit of beings, in the various transformations of the destinies of beings, in the various transformations of the inclinations of beings, in the various transformations of the resolute convictions of beings, and in the various transformations of the faculties of beings—

In the revolutions of various times; in the diverse mixtures of the karma of sentient beings; in the various degrees of disparity in the karma of sentient beings; in the various manifestations of the world of sentient beings; in the ways of sentient beings as they wander through the conduct of various realms of existence; in the oceans of sentient beings with their various intentions and applications; and in the expansions of sentient beings purified by the various disparities of their faculties yet still under the influence of the latencies and proclivities of various afflictions.
