By means of displays of various miraculous transformations of the intellect; by various etymological explanations; by the production of various tones, vocal qualities, and sounds; by the citation of various methods of the sūtras; by the turning of various gateways to dhāraṇīs; by the emergence of various methods of analytical knowledge (*pratisaṃvid*); by the turning of various oceans of names of truths; by various lion’s roars of the bulls among Buddhas; by displays of various miracles of teaching the roots of virtue to sentient beings; by miraculous transformations displaying various faces and recollections; by various lion’s roars of the prophecies for bodhisattvas; and by the various expansions of the wheel of Dharma of the Tathāgatas—within those that are infinite and without center.

In assembly circles that are infinitely diverse, mutually dependent, variously pure, vast, and where subtle assembly circles converge— ranging from those measuring one *yojana* to ten *yojanas*, up to assemblies as vast as world-systems containing atoms as numerous as the sands of unspeakably many Buddha-fields— in all these assembly circles, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, teach the Dharma with the speech of a Tathāgata which follows after every tone, limb of voice, sound, and resonance.
The merchant’s son Sudhana heard all of that, took it up, retained it, set it in motion, and contemplated it;
he beheld that miraculous display and that inconceivable preeminence of the bodhisattva’s samādhi.

Then the merchant Muktaka, mindful and self-possessed, arose from that samādhi and said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Noble son, I enter into and emerge from a Tathāgata-liberation called 'Unobstructed Array.
Noble son, as I enter into and emerge from this Tathāgata-liberation of the Unobstructed Array, in the eastern direction—"

In the world-system called Jāmbūnada-prabhāsavatī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Tāreśvararāja appears within the range of vision together with the entire circle of his assembly of bodhisattvas, headed by the bodhisattva Vairocanagarbha. In the southern direction, in the world-system called Sarvabalavegavatī, there is a Tathāgata named Samantagandhavitāna.
The Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the entire circle of the assembly of bodhisattvas headed by the Bodhisattva Cintārāja, appeared before his eyes.
In the western direction, in the world-system called Sarvagandhaprabhāsavatī, there is a Tathāgata named Merupradīparāja.
The Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, together with the entire circle of the assembly of bodhisattvas headed by the Bodhisattva Asaṅgacitta,
comes within the range of vision. In the northern direction, in the world-system called Kāṣāyadhvajā, there is the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Awakened One named Vajrapramardana.

Together with the entire circle of the assembly of bodhisattvas, headed by the bodhisattva Vajrapadavikrāmin, he appeared before his eyes. In the northeastern direction, in the world-system called Sarvaratnarucirā, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Anilambhacakṣurvairocana, together with the bodhisattva Anilambhasunirmita as his foremost attendant.
The entire assembly-circle of all bodhisattvas came within the range of his vision.
In the southeastern direction, in the world-system called Gandhārciḥprabhāsvarā, there dwells the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Gandhapradīpa,
together with the Bodhisattva Sarvadharmadhātutalabhedaketurāja as his foremost attendant.
He appeared before the eyes of the assembly of bodhisattvas.

In the southwestern direction, in the world-system called Sūryakesaranirbhāsā, there dwells the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Samantamukhajñānavirocanaghoṣa, together with the bodhisattva Samantakusumārciḥpralambacūḍa as his foremost attendant.
He appeared before the eyes of the entire assembly of bodhisattvas.

In the northwestern direction, in the world-system called Gandhālaṃkāraruciraśubhagarbhā, there dwells the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Apramāṇaguṇasāgaraprabha, together with the bodhisattva Asaṅgakāyaraśmitejomati as his foremost attendant.
The entire assembly circle of all bodhisattvas comes within the range of his vision.
In the downward direction, in the world-system called Ratnasiṃhāvabhāsajvalanā, there dwells the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Dharmadhātuvidyotitaraśmi,
together with the bodhisattva Dharmadhātvarcirvairocanasaṃbhavamati as his foremost attendant.
He appears before the eyes of the entire assembly of bodhisattvas.

In the upward direction, in the world-system named Lakṣaṇaruciravairocanā, there dwells a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Apratihataguṇakīrtivimokṣaprabharāja, together with the bodhisattva Asaṅgabalavīryamati as his foremost attendant.
The entire assembly circle of all bodhisattvas comes into the range of his vision.
Thus, noble son,
with these ten Tathāgatas as the foremost, I behold in the ten directions as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields;
yet those Tathāgatas do not come here.
And I do not go there;
rather, at whatever time I desire, at that very time I behold the Tathāgata Amitābha in the world-system Sukhāvatī.
In the world-system Candanavatī, I behold the Tathāgata Vajrābha; in the world-system Gandhavatī, I behold the Tathāgata Ratnābha;
in the world-system Padmavatī, I behold the Tathāgata Ratnapadmābha.
In the world-system Kanakavatī, I see the Tathāgata Śāntābha; in the world-system Abhirati, I see the Tathāgata Akṣobhya; in the world-system Supratiṣṭhā, I see the Tathāgata Siṃha.
In the world-system called Mirror-Disc Radiance, I see the Tathāgata Candrabuddhi; in the world-system called Variegated Jewel-Glory-Swan, I see the Tathāgata Vairocana.
Thus, noble son, in whichever direction and in whichever world-system I desire to see whichever Tathāgata, [I see him].

I see each and every Tathāgata; in whichever time-period, upon whichever object, and in whichever former life I desire to see a Tathāgata; for whatever purpose of miraculous manifestation, and for whatever purpose of disciplining sentient beings I desire to see a particular Tathāgata.
I see each and every one of those Tathāgatas;
yet those Tathāgatas do not come here, nor do I go there.
Therefore, noble son, not perceiving any coming of the Tathāgatas from anywhere, nor perceiving any going of my own body to anywhere,
and perceiving the representation of the Tathāgatas to be like a dream—
Understanding the representation of cognition as being identical to a dream, understanding the representation of cognition of the Tathāgatas as being identical to a reflection,
and understanding the representation of cognition of one's own mind as being like a vessel of clear water;
Understanding the representation of forms created by the Tathāgatas as being like an illusion, understanding the representation of one's own mind as being like an illusion,
and understanding the voice of the Tathāgata as being like the resonance of an echo in a mountain valley;
Understanding that even the non-informative [action] is like an echo, I thus follow and thus recollect that the support of their own minds is the source of all the Buddha-dharmas for Bodhisattvas.
The purification of all buddha-fields is based on the empowerment of one's own mind;
the conduct of all buddhas and bodhisattvas is based on the empowerment of one's own mind; and the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings is based on the empowerment of one's own mind.
The empowerment of one's own mind is the accomplishment of the vows of all bodhisattvas;
the empowerment of one's own mind is the attainment of the city of omniscience.
The empowerment of one’s own mind is the playful mastery of the inconceivable liberation of a bodhisattva; the empowerment of one’s own mind is the perfect awakening to the enlightenment of a Buddha;
the empowerment of one’s own mind is the miraculous display of the preeminent power that encompasses the entire realm of phenomena.
The empowerment of one's own mind is the knowledge that thoroughly integrates all conceptual constructions into their subtle state.
Regarding this, noble son, it occurs to me: "One's own mind alone must be supported by all roots of virtue;
one's own mind alone must be moistened by the clouds of Dharma;
one's own mind alone must be purified of objective referents."
One's own mind alone must be made firm through vigor;
one's own mind alone must be pacified through patience;
one's own mind alone must be directed toward the pursuit of knowledge.
One's own mind alone should be refined by means of wisdom;
one's own mind alone should be brought forth swiftly through mastery;
one's own mind alone should be expanded toward equality with the Buddhas.
One’s own mind alone is to be illuminated by the ten powers of the Tathāgatas.
Noble son, I know, enter, and emerge from this liberation of the Tathāgata called the Array of Non-attachment.

But what can I [know] of the Bodhisattvas whose minds are unattached, whose range of activity is the dwelling of non-attachment, who have attained the samādhi in which all present Buddha-dharmas are manifest before them, and who have attained the samādhi of the gate of awakening that reaches the limit of non-extinction?

To know the conduct or to describe the qualities of those who have attained equality regarding the three times; who understand the methods of the meditative absorption that penetrates the universal foundation; whose bodies are perfectly distributed throughout all buddha-fields; who dwell within the undifferentiated domain of the Buddhas; whose range of activity faces all directions; who survey the mandala of gnosis without turning their backs; and for whom the evolution and dissolution of their own physical forms within all world-systems are clearly perceived.
And neither in themselves nor in the world-systems does a dualistic perception arise for them.
Go, son of good family,
right here in the southern region, to the peak of Jambūdvīpa named Milaspharaṇa. There dwells a monk named Sāradhvaja.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one apply oneself?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the merchant Muktaka, circumambulated the merchant Muktaka hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at him again and again, he praised and reflected upon the merchant Muktaka’s innumerable virtues.

Longing [for them], not abandoning them, weeping and lamenting, born of affection for the spiritual friend, taking refuge in the spiritual friend, intent on pleasing the spiritual friend, not disturbing the wisdom of the spiritual friend, perceiving that omniscience is dependent upon the spiritual friend, his intention was followed by the spiritual friend.
The practice accomplished through the skillful means of a spiritual friend is dependent upon the mental state directed toward that spiritual friend:
regarding spiritual friends as mothers, by way of avoiding all that is unbeneficial; and regarding spiritual friends as fathers, by way of generating all wholesome qualities.
He departed from the presence of the merchant Muktaka. // 6 //
(Gv 68) 9. Sāradhvaja.
Then, indeed, Sudhana, the merchant’s son, reflecting upon that very instruction of the merchant Muktaka, [proceeded].
Practicing according to the instruction of the merchant Muktaka, he recollected the inconceivable liberation of the bodhisattvas,
recollected the inconceivable light of the bodhisattvas' wisdom,
and followed the entry into the inconceivable penetration of the realm of phenomena.
Entering the inconceivable method of the assembly of bodhisattvas,
beholding the inconceivable miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas,
and resolving with faith in the inconceivable convergence of Buddha-fields.
He followed after the inconceivable array of the Buddha’s empowerment;

he conceived the inconceivable preeminence of the establishment of the bodhisattva’s samādhis and liberations; and he plunged into the inconceivable unobstructed nature of the distinctions between world-systems.
Practicing that firm resolve for the inconceivable deeds of a bodhisattva,
and emulating the stream of those inconceivable bodhisattva-deeds and vows,
he proceeded in due order until he arrived at Mīlaspharaṇa, the peak of Jambudvīpa, where he approached the monk Sāradhvaja.

While searching, he saw him seated at the edge of a walking path in a certain hermitage, having entered into meditative absorption (*samādhi*), breathing in and out calmly, unmoving and free from mental construction,

with body upright and mindfulness directed before him, manifesting inconceivable transformations of meditative power; his head was visible from the left, right, above, or any direction, and his body displayed an inconceivable, immeasurable, and infinite variety of colors and forms.
In every single moment of mind, he saw [the Bodhisattva] manifesting [this state];

as he was thus absorbed in that which is profound, peaceful, unblinking, and objectless, with his body covered in bristling hair, he saw an inconceivable miraculous display of the bodhisattva’s liberations proceeding from all the pores of his skin.

By means of that miraculous display of the gates of liberation, in every single moment of mind, he pervades the entire realm of phenomena with infinite and diverse miraculous transformations and conceptualizations, for the sake of maturing all sentient beings, for the application of worship to all Tathāgatas, for the purification of all Buddha-fields,

for the cessation of the mass of suffering of all sentient beings, for the total cutting off of the paths to all miserable rebirths, and for the opening of the doors to happy rebirths for all sentient beings.

For the sake of pacifying the fever of afflictions of all sentient beings, for the sake of dispersing the obscuration of ignorance of all sentient beings, and for the sake of establishing all sentient beings in omniscience.

From the soles of his feet, he saw emerging multitudes of guild-leaders, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-fields; they were engaged in various forms of service and attendance, possessed bodies clothed in garments that surpassed the appearance of the guild-leaders found throughout all world-systems, their bodies adorned with various ornaments, wearing diverse crowns, crests, and tiaras, and surrounded by retinues resembling young boys.

And he was gathering all the brahmins and householders, as well as destitute beings, by means of provisions of food and drink, all types of services and attendants, all ornaments, all garments, all flowers, all garlands, all perfumes, all ointments, all objects of desire, all jewels, all dwellings, all methods of serving with vessels, and all methods of providing requisites.

He saw them pervading the ten directions as they went along, comforting the suffering world, gladdening the minds of sentient beings, purifying the dispositions of sentient beings, and bringing sentient beings to maturity in enlightenment.

Emerging from their two knees, they appeared in the forms of learned kṣatriyas, learned brāhmaṇas, learned worldlings, and learned masters of various crafts; they appeared in the forms of those learned in the human realm, and in the forms of those who are skillful and learned in the knowledge of worldly and transcendent ritual procedures;
they appeared in the forms of those esteemed as teachers of the world, manifesting in many forms and arrangements with diverse arrays, uttering words that were pleasing to the mind.

They gladden sentient beings who are dejected; they favor sentient beings who are destitute of the wealth of the Dharma; they bring happiness to suffering sentient beings; they uplift sentient beings who have fallen into ruin;
they comfort sentient beings whose vessels of transport have failed; they protect sentient beings who are afraid; and they cause the sound of the roots of virtue to be heard.

He saw them pervading the ten directions as they went along, uttering the sound of the turning away from evil, enjoining beings to undertake wholesome dharmas, establishing beings in beneficial conduct, generating a surge of joy, proclaiming the articles of attraction such as pleasant speech, and demonstrating to the world the quality of consistency between words and deeds.

From the circle of his navel, there issued forth hosts of sages of various forms and kalpic appearances, possessing the physical stature of all beings in the world of sentient beings, wearing deerskins, rags, and bark garments, holding staffs and water-pots, with perfectly peaceful deportment; they stood in the sky above, proclaiming the praises of the Buddha, sounding the voice of the Dharma, and uttering the resonance of the Buddha.

They were emitting [rays], manifesting the assembly of bodhisattvas, extolling the holy life (brahmacarya), enjoining sentient beings to the guarding of the sense faculties, elucidating the meaning of the lack of intrinsic nature (niḥsvabhāva), establishing the world in the goal of primordial wisdom (jñāna),
composing the methods of worldly treatises, and [teaching] the method of the path for departing toward the knowledge of the omniscient one.
He saw them pervading the ten directions, proceeding while demonstrating [the path] and establishing sentient beings in the sequential practice.

From both sides, there issued forth from all directions of the world countless Naga maidens with inconceivable numbers of bodies and forms; displaying inconceivable Naga-transformations, they sustained the expanse of the sky with inconceivable arrays of fragrant clouds as ornaments,
adorned the entire vault of the sky with inconceivable arrays of flower-clouds as ornaments, and [adorned it] with inconceivable arrays of garland-clouds as ornaments.

Adorning the entire realm of space, they covered the whole dharma-realm with ornaments of inconceivable clouds of jewel parasols; with ornaments of inconceivable clouds of jewel banners; with ornaments of inconceivable clouds of jewel pennants and rains of various jewel ornaments;
with ornaments of the raining down of inconceivable, infinite clouds of great maṇi-jewels; and with ornaments of the raining down of inconceivable clouds of jewel necklaces and variegated flowers.

It was adorned by the raining down of clouds of the Buddha-dharma from Bodhisattvas seated cross-legged upon inconceivable jewel thrones; it was adorned by the raining down of clouds of divine jewel ornaments and throngs of celestial nymphs singing songs of dharma in chorus; it was adorned by the scattering of rains of clouds of powder from all the finest jewel-kings and upward-pointing filaments of jewel-lotuses, decorated with inconceivable nets of pearls;
and it was adorned by the raining down of clouds of infinite rays of light, embellished with all kinds of precious gems, from clouds of inconceivable jewel crowns.

They presided over the expanse of space, which was adorned with clouds of flowers, garlands, parasols, banners, and flags from inconceivable hosts of devas; and it was further adorned by clouds of celestial nymphs who, with their bodies raised and palms joined in reverence, scattered golden flowers and released the sound of thundering clouds of hymns praising the virtues of all Tathāgatas, while raining down clouds of mountain-like heaps of all kinds of jewels and fragrances, and clouds of sublime incense fumes.

Sudhana the merchant’s son saw [those rays] covering the circles of assemblies of all the Tathāgatas, adorning the expansions of all world-systems, gladdening all sentient beings, making offerings to all Buddhas, and pervading the entire realm of phenomena moment by moment.

From the Śrīvatsa on his chest, there issued forth as many lords of the asuras as there are atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields; displaying inconceivable magical transformations of the asuras, they agitated great clouds, shook hundreds of thousands of world-systems,
struck together all the kings of the mountain ranges, and made all the palaces of the gods tremble.
They were eclipsing all the circles of Māra, crushing the entire army of Māra, shattering the intoxication, pride, and arrogance of all the world,

warding off those with corrupt minds and making them serene, turning back those with harmful intentions, pacifying the unwholesome states of beings, dispersing the mountains of afflictions, and quelling the battles of strife.

By means of various playful displays of the miraculous transformations of asura-māyā, they cause sentient beings to feel spiritual urgency, making them recoil from evil, terrifying them away from saṃsāra,
lifting them up from all states of existence, establishing them in the homeless state, settling sentient beings in the thought of awakening (bodhicitta),
purifying the bodhisattva-practice of bodhisattvas, and establishing bodhisattvas in the perfections (pāramitās).

The merchant’s son Sudhana saw [the bodhisattvas] leading others into the stages of a bodhisattva, generating the illumination of the methods of the Buddha-dharma for bodhisattvas, and pervading the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) in every single moment of thought through the various established systems of the methods of dharma.
From his backbone, there issued forth bodies of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas as numerous as the atoms in incalculable buddha-fields;
they proclaimed selflessness and the absence of a sentient being to those beings who were to be disciplined by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and who were attached to a self;
they illuminated the impermanence of all conditioned phenomena to those attached to eternalism; and they taught the meditation on the foul to those whose conduct was dominated by passion.
To those of hateful temperament, they proclaimed loving-kindness; to those of deluded temperament, dependent origination through specific conditionality;

to those of equal temperament, they illuminated the method of the Dharma associated with the object of knowledge; to those delighting in sense objects, they spoke of non-attachment; to those whose intentions were fixed on a dwelling in tranquility, they inspired them toward the excellence of their vows throughout the gateways of all directions.

The merchant's son Sudhana saw them illuminating the performance of beneficial deeds for all sentient beings through the gateways of the ocean-like turnings of the principles of all phenomena, while pervading the entire realm of reality (dharmadhātu).

From his two shoulders issued forth yakṣa and rākṣasa lords, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable buddha-fields; their bodies were distorted into various shapes, their complexions, heights, and girths were diverse, their modes of deportment varied, they were mounted upon various vehicles, surrounded by various retinues, intent on protecting the realm of sentient beings, engaged in the manifestation of various splendors and radiances, and resounding with the thunderous roar of various voices.
By means of various unconfused methods of accomplishment, pervading the sky in all directions and intermediate directions, for the sake of protecting the wholesome conduct of all sentient beings,
for the protection of all noble assemblies, for the embracing of all bodhisattvas, for the preservation of all who have correctly resolved and correctly practiced,
and for the performance of the service and worship of all Buddhas through the activity of Vajrapāṇi.

For the sake of turning back all beings fallen into the miserable states from rebirth in the various realms of woe, for the sake of pacifying all fears and calamities such as diseases in all worlds, they are engaged in performing deeds for the benefit of beings and are eager to protect the world;
they are fulfilling the wheel of the accumulations of merit and knowledge, setting in motion the wheel of Dharma, and [subduing] the wheel of opposing disputants.
Sudhana, the merchant’s son, saw them being restrained and pervading the entire realm of phenomena.
From his abdomen issued forth *kinnara* lords, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-fields, each surrounded by hundreds of thousands of incalculable *kinnara* maidens;
and likewise issued forth *gandharva* lords, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-fields, each surrounded by hundreds of thousands of incalculable *gandharva* maidens;
and they all proclaimed the nature of phenomena (*dharmasvabhāva*) accompanied by the melodies of hundreds of thousands of incalculable divine musical instruments.

They were uttering hymns of praise to the Buddhas, illuminating the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), extolling the conduct of Bodhisattvas, lauding all gateways to complete enlightenment, plunging into all gateways of the wheel of Dharma, delighting in all gateways of miraculous transformations,
illuminating all gateways of final nirvana, and [proclaiming] all gateways of the Buddha's teaching.

The merchant’s son Sudhana saw [the bodhisattvas] embracing all beings, gladdening the faces of all sentient beings, purifying all buddha-fields, illuminating all gateways to the Dharma, turning back all gateways to obscuration, gathering all gateways to roots of goodness, and pervading the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

From the gateway of his mouth, there issued forth universal monarchs, equal in number to the atoms of incalculable Buddha-fields, accompanied by retinues of fourfold armies made of the seven precious jewels; they emitted magnificent arrays of light rays of great generosity,
bestowed all mines of jewels, distributed all sources of mani-gems, enriched the poor, and turned the world away from the slaughter of living beings.

They were establishing beings in a mind of loving-kindness, separating them from taking what is not given, bestowing hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of well-adorned maidens, turning them away from sexual misconduct, establishing them in celibacy, and deterring them from false speech while enjoining them to the supreme state of non-contention.
They were turning others away from slanderous speech, raising their voices with the application of supreme gathering [of beings], turning the world away from harsh words,
uttering speech that was pleasing and gentle,
and turning sentient beings away from idle chatter associated with what is meaningless and unrighteous.
They were establishing others in the definitive discernment of the distinctions between words of profound meaning;
they were turning the world away from all faults of speech;
and they were uttering words bound by compassion.
They were removing the impurities of the heart from the world,
establishing beings in the supreme state of fewness of desires and contentment,
and turning the world away from malice.
They were engaging others in the purification of their own mental continuums,
uprooting the entire web of views in the world, and dispersing all varieties of doubt.
They were causing all the peaks of doubt to fall away,
removing the darkness of all uncertainty and hesitation,
and discerning the Dharma by dividing it up for the world.
proclaiming dependent origination through the principle of specific conditionality, enjoining sentient beings toward the method of the truth of intrinsic nature,
and turning back all obscurations;
Sudhana, the merchant’s son, saw them entering into the way of non-obstruction, illuminating the method of the Buddha’s purpose, and pervading the dharma-realm in the ten directions.
From his two eyes issued forth hundreds of thousands of solar discs, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-fields; illuminating all the great hells,
they dispelled the great darkness in the world and removed the gloom of delusion from sentient beings.
They pacified the suffering of cold for those beings who had gone to the miserable states of the cold hells; they emitted a brilliant white light over the fields made of clay,
and they emitted a light the color of beryl over the fields made of gold.
In fields made of beryl, they emit a golden-colored radiance;
in fields made of silver, they emit a golden-colored radiance;
and in fields made of gold, they emit a crystal-colored radiance.
In the crystal lands, they emit a golden-colored radiance;
in the golden lands, they emit a musāragalva-colored radiance;
and in the musāragalva lands, they emit a golden-colored radiance.
In the fields made of red pearls, they emitted a golden-colored radiance;
in the fields made of gold, they emitted a radiance the color of red pearls;
and in the fields made of emerald, they emitted a golden-colored radiance.
In fields made of gold, they emitted a radiance with the color of emerald;
in fields made of sapphire, they emitted a radiance with the color of the king of sun-essence jewels;
and in fields whose substance was the king of sun-essence jewels, they emitted a radiance with the color of the king of sapphire jewels.
In the fields made of red pearls, they emitted a radiance with the color of the finest jewels containing circles of moonbeam nets;
and in the fields with bodies of the finest jewels containing circles of moonbeam nets, they emitted a radiance with the color of red pearls.
In fields made of a single jewel, they emitted light of various jewel colors;
in fields made of various jewels, they emitted light of a single jewel color.

In this way, within all the circles of the assemblies of bodhisattvas, Sudhana the merchant’s son saw them engaged in the work of immeasurable beings, pervading the entire dharma-realm of all sentient beings.
From the tuft of hair between his eyebrows, there issued forth bodies of the moon, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields; these bodies surpassed all the lords of the gods,
turned away all delight in sensual pleasures in the entire world,
and led them toward the joy of beholding the Buddhas.
He saw them pervading the dharma-realm in the ten directions, engaged in the discipline of immeasurable sentient beings.

From their foreheads issued forth Great Brahmās, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-fields; possessing tranquil deportment, they uttered the Brahma-voice, entreating all Buddhas, praising all Buddhas, gladdening all Bodhisattvas,
and engaging in the welfare of immeasurable beings as they pervaded the entire realm of phenomena in the ten directions.
The merchant’s son Sudhana saw it.

From their heads issued forth Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, displaying bodies adorned with various colors and forms, manifesting limbs variegated with the secondary marks (*anuvyañjana*), emitting clouds of light-mandalas of infinite extent,
and [displaying] clouds of ways of relinquishing gifts, recipients, and objects, beginning from the former practices of the Bodhisattva path of all Buddhas.
issuing from every pore of his body, displaying oceans of past deeds associated with the various perfections,
praising the practice of giving to the world, turning back the stain of avarice, and enjoining sentient beings to relinquish all grasping.
They were presiding over a world adorned with various ornaments of all kinds of jewels,
establishing beings in the perfection of generosity and settling them in the mastery over requisites,
while extolling all the qualities of the primary marks.
He saw them teaching the causes for the arising of the marks of a Buddha;
and he saw Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, emerging and extolling the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*),
manifesting from every pore of their bodies oceans of past lives associated with the perfection of ethical discipline of all Buddhas.

Turning all sentient beings away from the spheres of all worldly destinies and directing them toward the sphere of the Tathāgata, they felt revulsion for the realm of desire and scattered the veil of perversion throughout the world.
He saw them pacifying false conceptualizations and establishing beings in the ethical discipline of a bodhisattva;

praising the ethical discipline of great compassion, they were establishing beings in the ethical discipline of practicing the Buddha-way for the sake of attaining the ethical discipline of a Tathāgata;

and having demonstrated that the states of existence of beings are like a dream, they were establishing beings in mastery over the afflictions of grasping at sense objects, so that they might reach the convergence of the nature of dreams.

And issuing forth Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, illuminating the world with their golden-colored skin, they established sentient beings in a state free from anger and despair— a state characterized by a mind that is unblemished, undestroyed, and unimpeded— and from every pore they emitted clouds of the Tathāgata’s former practices associated with the perfection of patience, in order to utterly sever the destiny of all animal births.
He saw [the Buddhas] establishing beings in the power of patience and illuminating beings with mastery over the Dharma;
and he saw Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, emerging and displaying the infinite power of the Bodhisattvas' vigor.
By the power of being irreversible in their undertaking of omniscience,
they were describing the lack of weariness in seeking the ocean of learning from all sentient beings,
and were enjoining sentient beings to perform worship and service for all Tathāgatas.
Establishing sentient beings in the undertaking of great vigor for the reversal of the entire mass of suffering,
emitting from all their bodies clouds of past vows associated with the perfection of vigor,
and demonstrating the conduct of the bodhisattvas' perfection of vigor.

He saw them scattering the mountains of indolence for sentient beings, establishing sentient beings in the perfection of vigor, and enjoining the world toward mastery over karma, all while being engaged in their empowerment.
And from them issued forth Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, who established beings on the path of mindfulness of the Bodhisattva,
dispelled the darkness of all obscurations and hindrances, and turned beings away from all pride and negligence.
Establishing them in the dharma of heedfulness,
causing the banners of arrogance and agitation to fall,
and proclaiming the ocean of the factors of a Buddha’s meditative concentration.
They were praising the perfection of meditation in the world,
emitting from every pore clouds of past lives associated with the perfection of meditation,
and establishing sentient beings in mastery over the mind.
In every moment, he saw them pervading the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

He saw Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, emerging from all the pores of their skin, intent upon seeking the Buddha-dharma; they were emitting clouds of past spiritual practices (*pūrvayoga*) and thundering forth clouds of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) with the sounds of oceans of all vocal qualities.
They were emitting the lightning of right view,
resounding with the cries of the true nature of phenomena,
and shattering the mountain peaks of the view of self among sentient beings.
They were extracting the thorns of all views,
dispelling the darkness of doubt, uncertainty, mental hesitation, and skepticism,
and praising the mastery of resolute conviction.
In every single moment of mind, he saw [the Bodhisattvas] pervading the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
He saw them emerging as Bodhisattvas, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-fields, manifesting the mandala of the methods of all Buddhas’ skill in means (*upāyakauśalya*),
and emitting from every pore clouds of past-life narratives associated with that skill in means.
They were manifesting the practice of skillful means in the world,
illuminating the departure via the Mahāyāna,
and extolling the entire mandala of all Buddhas.
They were extolling and demonstrating the bodhisattva conduct that is indivisible from both saṃsāra and nirvāṇa,
and they were establishing sentient beings in the perfection of the bodhisattvas' skillful means.
He saw them manifesting in the world the mandala of mastery over the rebirths of all bodhisattvas, pervading the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with the mere arising of a thought;
and he saw bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable buddha-fields, emerging and thundering from every pore of their skin clouds of oceans of the names of all Tathāgatas.
They emitted from the circles of all their pores clouds of past deeds associated with the complete purification of the perfections of the vows of all bodhisattvas;
they extolled the perfection of vows;
and they established sentient beings in all the masteries of the bodhisattvas.

He saw them manifesting in the world the great wheel of the chariot of vows, which is fixed to the furthest limit of the future, which pursues all phenomena, turns back all afflictions, and shatters the mountain of ignorance;
he saw them pervading the realm of reality at every moment of thought through the miraculous transformations of various vows.
He also saw Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, emerging and illuminating the power of the Bodhisattvas.
They were emitting sounds proclaiming the perfection of the powers of a bodhisattva,
sending forth clouds of past practices for the arising of the perfection of the power-paramita from every pore of their skin,
and demonstrating a power that cannot be crushed by any maras or proponents of opposing doctrines.

They manifested the power of their bodies being indestructible even by the impact of all the vajra mountains of the cosmic perimeter; they displayed the power of their bodies remaining unextinguished even while dwelling within the ocean of the fires that consume all kalpas;
and they demonstrated the power of supporting the entire expanse of world-systems upon the palm of their hand within the vault of space.
In every single moment of mind, he saw them establishing sentient beings in mastery over supernatural powers (*ṛddhivaśitā*), never ceasing to pervade the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
He also saw Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, emerging forth and illuminating the circle of wisdom (*jñānamaṇḍala*) for sentient beings;
they were endowed with the immeasurable purity of wisdom and were emitting from every pore clouds of past spiritual practices (*pūrvayoga*).
They were manifesting in the world the stage of knowledge endowed with the superknowledges of all the qualities and wisdoms of the Buddhas;
they were demonstrating the stage of knowledge endowed with the superknowledges of the designations of all the Buddhas;
and they were illuminating the stage of knowledge endowed with the superknowledges that accomplish all vows.
They were proclaiming the stage of knowledge characterized by the superknowledge of the wisdom that accomplishes the vow to gather in all sentient beings;

they were proclaiming the stage of knowledge characterized by the superknowledge of entering into the selflessness and lack of intrinsic nature of all sentient beings; and they were illuminating the stage of knowledge characterized by the superknowledge of surveying the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings.
They were discerning the stage of knowledge endowed with the superknowledge of knowing the faculties of all sentient beings;
they were extolling the stage of knowledge endowed with the superknowledge of observing the inclinations and resolute convictions of all sentient beings;
and they were revealing the stage of knowledge endowed with the superknowledge of entering the ocean of the karma of all sentient beings.

The merchant’s son Sudhana saw those who, having manifested the ground of knowledge characterized by the superknowledges of wisdom for entering the ocean of vows of all sentient beings, were establishing beings in the perfection of wisdom, pervading the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) in every single moment of thought.

From the aperture of the *uṣṇīṣa* on his crown, there issued forth Tathāgata forms as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields, adorned with the purity of the excellent primary and secondary marks; they shone like mountains of refined Jāmbūnada gold, possessing measureless, blazing circles of light that pervaded all ten directions;
they manifested infinite and centerless Buddha-transformations and rained down clouds of Dharma that were undifferentiated for the entire world.

That is to say: for the Bodhisattvas who have reached the sublime seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), they rain down the rain from the cloud of Dharma named "Cloud of Knowledge Facing the Distinctions of the Entire Foundation of the Dharmadhātu"; for the Bodhisattvas who have attained consecration (*abhiṣeka*), they rain down the rain from the cloud of Dharma named "Universal Foundation Cloud";
and for the Bodhisattvas consecrated in the great Dharma-princely succession (*mahādharmayauvarājya*), they rain down the rain from the cloud of Dharma named "Entry through All Gateways."
They were raining down the rain from the cloud of Dharma called Universal Array for the Bodhisattvas who have become youths;

raining down the rain from the cloud of Dharma called the Firm Peak of Great Compassion for the irreversible Bodhisattvas; and raining down the rain from the cloud of Dharma called the Vajra of Knowledge that Discerns the Distinctive Nature of All Phenomena for the Bodhisattvas of pure resolute intention.

They were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Universal Array for Gathering the World" for those bodhisattvas perfected through previous practices; they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Cloud of Manifestation Facing the Circles of the Assemblies of Tathāgatas of the Three Times" for those bodhisattvas born of their parents;
and they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Resonance of the Ground of the Essential Nature of All Dharmas" for those bodhisattvas who practice yoga.

They were raining down the rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Source of Clouds Born from the Method and Means of Great Compassion" for the beginner bodhisattvas; they were raining down the rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Source of the Accumulation of the Treasury of Exertion" for the bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds on enlightenment;
and they were raining down the rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Treasury of the Tathāgata’s Vows and the Grasping of Inexhaustible Liberations" for the bodhisattvas of vast resolve.
They were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Inexhaustible Treasury of the Universal Foundation" for the beings of the form realm;
they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Resounding Sound of the Ocean of Immeasurable Methods" for the gods of the Brahma-realm.
They were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Inexhaustible Treasury of the Requisites for Power and the Arising of Strength" for the Vaśavartin gods;

they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Sound of Sweeping Away the Accumulations for Omniscience with the Variegated Banner" for the Mārakāyika gods; and they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Variegated Yoke of the Jewel of Knowledge" for the Nirmāṇarati gods.
They were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Variegated Banner of the Bodhisattva’s Vow" for the Tuṣita gods;

they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Treasury of Recollection of All Tathāgatas" for the Yāma gods; and they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called the "Arising of the Force of Joy from Beholding the Tathāgata" in the palaces of Śakra, lord of the gods.

In the palaces of the lords of yakṣas, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma named "The Pervasive Cloud of the Tathāgatas’ Miraculous Transformations in the Space of the Dharmadhātu";

in the palaces of the lords of gandharvas, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma named "The Resonant Sound of the Chanting of the Dharma of All Tathāgatas"; and in the palaces of the lords of asuras, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma named "The Vajra Mandala of the Method of Gnosis."

In the abodes of the lords of the Garuḍas, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma named "The Means for the Manifestation of All Tathāgatas"; in the abodes of the lords of the Kinnaras, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma named "The Resonant Sound of the Concert of All Dharmas";
and in the abodes of the lords of the Nāgas...
They were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called "Arisen from the Dread of the Realms of Existence through the Resonance of the Bodhisattvas' Miraculous Displays";
they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Force that Increases the Ocean of Joy" in the abodes of the lords of the Mahoragas;
and they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Domain of the Knowledge that Distinguishes All Worlds" in the human worlds.

In the worlds of hell, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Ornament of the Support for the Utterance of the Noble Path, the Sound that Pacifies All Sufferings of Saṃsāra"; among the animal births, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Body of the Mandala of Clouds of Recollection of the Tathāgata, the Sound of Practicing the Paths of Blameless Action";

and among those in the world of Yama, they were raining down a rain from the cloud of Dharma called "The Arising of the Mind of Renunciation toward All Beings through the Utterance of the Perfections of All Tathāgatas."

Sudhana, the merchant’s son, saw them raining down a shower from the cloud of Dharma named "The Resounding Voice that Consols and Attains the Cessation of All Suffering for Beings Fallen into the Lower Realms," pervading the entire realm of phenomena.

And from every single pore of his skin, he saw circles of light-ray networks emerge, equal in number to the atoms within incalculable Buddha-fields; these radiated throughout the ten directions and the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), manifesting arrays of incalculable displays of power and form, and appearing in an incalculable variety of activities.

That is to say: from a certain circle of light-ray networks emerging from a pore, he beheld the miraculous manifestation of the practice of pure giving and the relinquishment of all one's possessions; from another circle of light-ray networks emerging from a pore, he beheld the miraculous manifestation of the mandala of the undertaking of the ethical vows and observances of all bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time;
and from yet another circle of light-ray networks emerging from a pore, [he beheld] the forms of the practice of patience of all bodhisattvas who have attained the three periods of time.

Behold the miraculous display of the Bodhisattvas’ endurance of the severing of their hands, feet, and heads; their miraculous display of enduring the falling upon them of clubs, staffs, swords, and arrows; and their miraculous display of enduring the breaking of their entire bodies and the tearing out of their hearts and eyes.
Behold also those other assumed bodies of Bodhisattvas throughout the three times, which, for the sake of seeking the dharma of omniscience, [endure these things].

He saw even those bodily and mental torments— the severing of his major and minor limbs— which were endured, tolerated, and disregarded by those afflicted with great compassion, as being the very forms of the reflected images of all the bodhisattvas’ miraculous displays of the practice of patience.

From a certain circle of light-rays emerging from the pores of his skin, he beheld the miraculous transformations of all bodhisattvas throughout the past, future, and present— manifestations distinguished by the supreme intensity of their heroic conduct— which caused the world to tremble, agitated the oceans, stirred the hearts of sentient beings, terrified all non-Buddhist teachers, routed the hosts of Māra, illuminated the directions with the Dharma, and displayed the valorous strides and miraculous feats of great bodhisattvas; and from another circle of light-rays emerging from the pores of his skin, he beheld those examinations of all bodhisattva practices and those assumptions of various physical forms.

Those [deeds] for the sake of embracing noble birth and the perfection of the form-body; those embracings of the instructions of spiritual friends; those bases for practicing the teachings of spiritual friends;
and those mountain caves, palaces, celestial mansions, and regions that correspond to the dwelling places for the perfection of the factors of the Tathāgata’s meditative absorption.
Those which were the bodies of sages,
by whom those factors of meditative concentration were accomplished,
and those which were the sovereignties of kings—
Sudhana, the merchant's son, beheld all those gateways to renunciation, as well as the undertakings of vows and the modes of deportment.
From a certain circle of light-rays emerging from the pores of his skin, he saw bodies engaged in the pursuit of all dharmas through the practice of the perfection of wisdom;
with those bodies, each single word of the Dharma was sought from all sentient beings by means of renouncing everything they possessed,
and it was sought from all spiritual friends through every form of service and attendance, born of faith and reverence.

And he saw all that which had been sought from the presence of the Tathāgata according to the measure of his own body, and just as the single word of the Dharma is connected with the perfection of wisdom, so too were all the words of the Dharma connected with the perfection of wisdom— those which had been sought by means of bodies appearing in births throughout the entire world—
all of this Sudhana, the merchant’s son, beheld from each and every circle of light-ray networks emerging from a single pore.

From a certain circle of light-rays emanating from the pores of his body, he saw the applications of the means of gathering all beings, which extend across the ocean of the destinies of sentient beings as skillful methods for maturing all bodhisattvas.

And from each single pore-circle of light-rays, he saw every single being being gathered through the employment of skillful means—by assuming previous forms of existence and manifesting bodies in modes resembling the bodies of all other beings.

From a certain circle of networks of light-rays from the pores of his body, there appeared the Blessed One’s conduct that accomplishes the vows of all previous eons, his conduct that accomplishes the vows for the maturation of all sentient beings, and his conduct that accomplishes the vows for the purification of all buddha-fields;

as well as those circles of the accomplishment of all vows which had been accomplished at the feet of various Tathāgatas, serving as the antidote for each respective defect of cyclic existence among all the defects of cyclic existence.
The merchant’s son Sudhana saw all of that from each and every circle of light-ray networks emerging from the pores of his body.
From some circles of light-ray networks emerging from the pores, he saw oceans of past deeds associated with the practice of all the perfections of power (*balapāramitā*).

From some circles of light-ray networks emerging from the pores, he saw oceans of past deeds associated with the investigation of the conduct of omniscience (*sarvajñāna*), which serve as bodies for awakening sentient beings asleep in the slumber of ignorance.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, contemplating and examining the monk Sāradhvaja as he remained thus absorbed in meditative concentration,
recollecting the sphere of that samādhi and liberation,
and reflecting upon that inconceivable bull-like power of the bodhisattva samādhi, [continued his search].
Entering that inconceivable ocean of methods for benefiting sentient beings,
following that inconceivable gateway of the formation of arrays facing all streams,
he was filled with resolute faith.
Entering that gateway of knowledge which is the purification of the array of the realm of phenomena, receiving that empowerment of the Buddha, and fathoming that knowledge, he—
Generating that power of the bodhisattva’s mastery,
strengthening that power of the bodhisattva’s vow,
and expanding that power of the bodhisattva’s conduct.
He spends even one day and night in the presence of the monk Sāradhvaja;
he spends two as well, and even seven days and nights in his presence.
He spent even half a month, even two months,
up to six months or six days and nights in the presence of the monk Sāradhvaja.
Then, after the passing of six months and six days and nights, the monk Sāradhvaja arose from that samādhi.
Sudhana said, "How wonderful this is, Noble One!"

To whatever extent this samādhi is profound, to that extent it is vast; to that extent its range is immeasurable, to that extent its array of inconceivable transformations is infinite; to that extent its light is incomparable, to that extent its array is incalculable;

to that extent its sphere is unassailable, to that extent its object is undifferentiated; to that extent it illuminates all directions equally, and to that extent this samādhi is the application for the benefit of immeasurable sentient beings.
For indeed, he has appeared for the sake of pacifying the immeasurable mass of suffering of all sentient beings;
that is to say, he has appeared for the purpose of pacifying the mass of suffering of poverty,
for the purpose of severing the path to the hell realms, for the purpose of rescuing those in the animal realm, and for the purpose of closing the doors to all states of non-leisure.

It is present for the purpose of leading one toward the path to heaven; for the purpose of bringing about the joy and happiness of gods and humans; for the purpose of experiencing the delight in the objects of meditative concentration;
for the purpose of increasing the happiness belonging to the conditioned realm; for the purpose of demonstrating the gateway to liberation from the three realms;
and it is present for the purpose of illuminating the causes for the arising of the thought of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*).

In the sense of increasing the causes for the arising of the accumulations of merit and wisdom; in the sense of increasing the force of vast and great compassion; in the sense of generating the power of the great vows; in the sense of attaining the illumination of the bodhisattva path; in the sense of adorning the vehicle of the great perfections;

in the sense of accomplishing the entry into the distinctions of the Great Vehicle; in the sense of the vision of the knowledge of the conduct of Samantabhadra; and in the sense of attaining the light of knowledge regarding the stages of the bodhisattvas.
It is present for the purpose of attaining the purity of the array of the departure through the vows and conduct of all bodhisattvas,
and for the purpose of the empowerment that steps into the domain of omniscience.
What is the name of this noble samādhi?
He said: "Noble son, there is a perfection of wisdom named 'Attainment of Universal-Eyed Equanimity.
This samādhi is its radiance, and it is called the 'Array of Purity of Universal Gateways.'"

"Noble son, because this samādhi called the Array of Universal Gate Purification has been well-cultivated—having arisen from the light of the perfection of wisdom attained through universal equanimity—there arise ten hundred thousand incalculable sets of samādhis, preceded by the Array of Universal Gate Purification.
He asked: "Noble one, is the range of this samādhi limited to this much?"

He said: "Noble son, for one who has entered this samādhi, there is mastery over the perceptions of world-systems; mastery over the entry into world-systems; and mastery over the traversing of world-systems."
The empowerment in the arrays of world-systems; the empowerment in the purifications of world-systems; the empowerment in the cleansing of world-systems.
There is empowerment in the perceptions of seeing the Buddhas;
there is empowerment in the contemplation of the majesty of the Buddhas;
there is empowerment in the knowledge of the Buddhas' miraculous transformations.
There is empowerment for entering into and following the powers of the Buddhas;
there is empowerment for entering into the oceans of the Buddhas' qualities;
there is empowerment for receiving the clouds of the Buddha-dharma.

There is empowerment in the pursuit of the undifferentiated knowledge that turns the wheel of all the Buddha-dharmas; there is empowerment in the entry into and immersion within the oceans of the circles of the Buddha’s assemblies;
there is empowerment in the penetration and following of the ten directions.
There is empowerment in the constant observation of the teaching of the Buddha-dharma;
there is empowerment in the surveying of the directions of the Buddhas;
there is empowerment in the non-abandonment of the direction of great compassion.
There is empowerment in the pervasion of the directions with loving-kindness; there is empowerment in the insatiability of entering the directions to behold the Buddhas;
there is empowerment in the pursuit of entry into the ocean of all sentient beings.
It is an empowerment for following the ocean-like knowledge of the faculties of all sentient beings;
it is an empowerment for the knowledge that distinguishes the faculties of all sentient beings. Noble son, this is the dwelling in the perfection of wisdom that I know.

What can I possibly know of those who have entered the ocean of the dwelling in the perfection of wisdom; whose intellects are utterly purified regarding the sphere of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); who possess the knowledge that follows the course of all phenomena; who pervade the immeasurable sphere with their vast intelligence; who wield mastery over the illumination of great dhāraṇīs; who are perfectly purified by the light of the mandala of all samādhis; who have emerged through the preeminence of the miraculous transformations of the higher knowledges (*abhijñā*); and who have entered the ocean of inexhaustible analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*)?
To know the conduct of the Bodhisattvas, who possess sweet voices that resound through the depths of the earth and have become the refuge for the entire world;
or to speak of their virtues;
or to demonstrate their sphere of activity.
to manifest the sphere of experience, or to extol the power of the great vows, or to illuminate the gateway to liberation;
or to illuminate the full realization,
or to elucidate the path,
or to follow the stream of meditative concentration;
Or to know the object of the mind,
or to realize knowledge or equanimity.
Go, son of good family, right here in the southern region to a place called Samudravetāḍī.
There, to the east of the city of Mahāprabha, is a park named Samantavyūha.
There dwells a laywoman named Āśā, the wife of the lord of men Suprabha.
Go to her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one apply oneself?"

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana—satisfied, elated, joyful, and filled with gladness and cheer; having received the essence from the presence of the monk Sāradhvaja; having taken up the Dharma as his livelihood; having entered the domain of meditative absorption; having obtained the illumination of wisdom; having attained the radiance of samādhi; and having a mind following the light of the method of Dharma through the purification of resolute belief—[departed].
His light followed the gates of purification, and his wisdom extended throughout the illumination of all directions; having bowed his head at the feet of the monk Sāradhvaja,
circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, and gazed upon the monk Sāradhvaja,
he prostrated himself again and again, looking up and gazing intently, falling down, bowing, paying homage, bending low, attending to him in mind, and reflecting upon him.
Cultivating, thoroughly cultivating, uttering an inspired exclamation, making the sound "hā," bringing the virtues before him,
following them, recollecting, causing others to recollect, strengthening them, not abandoning them, bringing them to mind, fixing them, applying his vow,
longing for the vision, grasping the signs of the voice, maintaining them, with a mind following that retention, he recollected their color and shape.

Reflecting upon the excellence of knowledge, entering the domain of meditative concentration, continuing the stream of his vows, examining the sphere of his range, and receiving the illumination of wisdom, he departed from the presence of the monk Sāradhvaja.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana— having attained the virtues of spiritual friends, being sent forth by spiritual friends, overcome by the intensity of the desire to see spiritual friends, practicing according to the instructions of spiritual friends, possessing a love that follows after spiritual friends, and perceiving the vision of the Buddhas as a mine of spiritual friends— [proceeded].
Beholding spiritual friends as those who reveal the Buddha-dharma;
beholding spiritual friends as teachers in the dharmas of omniscience;
and beholding spiritual friends as having become eyes for the purpose of illuminating the sky of the Buddhas.
Proceeding by stages, he approached the Samantavyūha garden in the region of Samudravetālī.
There he beheld the Samantavyūha garden, surrounded by walls made of every kind of jewel, adorned with rows of trees made of every kind of jewel,
beautifully decorated and strewn with fine, lovely pollen from flowers of every kind of jewel, and graced by trees made of every kind of jewel.
It was strewn with various flowers from trees of every kind of jewel; its fragrance issued forth in all directions from rows of trees of every kind of incense;

it rained down a shower of various hanging jewel-garlands released from the treasuries of trees bearing garlands of every kind of gem; and its surface was adorned and spread over with various artistic patterns made of the finest jewels from trees of every king of mani-gems.

It was a place where the regions were beautifully divided by canopies formed by the hanging of various colored garments from all the kalpa-tree flowers; it resounded with the sweet sounds of all musical instruments, stirred by the wind from the divine and extraordinary music of the drum-trees; its ground was leveled, without depressions or elevations, and its magnificent arrays were adorned by streams of diverse ornaments hanging down, released from the treasuries of the trees that bore every kind of ornament.
Furthermore, in that Great Garden of Universal Arrays, there were one hundred thousand times ten million palaces, their turrets and arrays adorned with every kind of great jewel and gem.
There were one million gabled pavilions provided with canopies of Jāmbūnada gold;
one million celestial palaces with interiors adorned with Vairocana jewel-gems;
and one million lotus ponds made entirely of jewels, built with jeweled bricks and featuring staircases variegated with the seven precious gems.

They were surrounded by railings made of various jewels and gems, scented with the fragrance of flowing divine sandalwood water, their surfaces strewn with golden sand and scattered with ten palaces of gold and precious gems;

they possessed stairways arranged in the four directions and were filled with water endowed with the eight qualities; they resounded with the sweet cries of swans, cranes, peacocks, cuckoos, kalaviṅkas, and kuṇāla birds; they were encircled by rows of jeweled palm trees and covered with networks of golden bells that produced delightful sounds when stirred by the wind.

It was covered by canopies of great upper-jewel-gems, surrounded by groves of trees made of various jewels, illuminated by nets of jewel-gems and raised parasols and banners; and there were one million ponds, filled with mud of black sandalwood paste, covered with lotuses of variegated colors made of every kind of jewel, their pure waters shining with great jewel-lotuses.
In the center of that garden stood a great celestial palace named Vicitradhvaja, resting upon a ground of ocean-womb jewels.

It was adorned with pillars of lapis lazuli gems, its peaks rose up from Jāmbūnada gold, and it was fitted with panels featuring the array of the Jagadvirocana gem-jewel in its interior. Its floor blazed with a network of countless jewel-gems, and it was graced by the incense of the Ajitavati fragrant king-gem.
It was perfumed by the wafting fragrance of well-arranged fragrant king-gems, and by the Vibodhana fragrant king-gem that dispels the latent tendencies of the sharp faculties.

And within that great celestial palace of variegated banners, immeasurable seats were arranged— namely, lotus-seated thrones made of *padmagarbha* jewels, *digrocanamaṇiratna* lotus-seated thrones, *vairocanamaṇiratna* lotus-seated thrones, *jagadrocanamaṇiratna* lotus-seated thrones, *citrakośamaṇiratna* lotus-seated thrones, *siṃhapañjaramaṇiratna* lotus-seated thrones, and *vimalamaṇiratna* lotus-seated thrones.
Their calyxes were composed of precious jewels; their calyxes were lotuses made of universal-gate jewel-gems; their calyxes were lotuses made of jewel-gems with arrays of light;
their calyxes were lotuses made of king-jewels that radiate light with rays equal to the array of pure jewel-gems established upon the ocean;
their calyxes were lotuses made of jewel-gems trodden upon by diamond lions.
And that great celestial palace, Vicitradhvaja, had many turrets made of inconceivable jewels, arrayed with various gems, possessing an inconceivable radiance of color and beautiful forms.
And that garden, Samantavyūha, was covered above by a hundred thousand great canopies, namely:
canopies of garments, canopies of trees and creepers, canopies of flowers, canopies of garlands, canopies of perfumes, and canopies of jewel-gems.

It was covered by hundreds of thousands of canopies, foremost among which were canopies of gold, canopies of ornaments, canopies of *vajra-prabhāsa* jewels, canopies of apsarases manifested by the king of nāgas, Airāvaṇa, and canopies of *śakrābhilagna* jewel-gems. It was thus overspread by these ten primary kinds of canopies.
And it was covered by ten hundred thousand great nets of jewels,
namely: nets of jewel-filled tinkling bells, nets of jewel parasols, nets of jewel images,
nets of ocean-womb pearls, nets of blue beryl gem-jewels, nets of lion-garlands, nets of moonstone gem-jewels, and nets of incense-formed bodies.
It was covered by hundreds of thousands of nets of great precious jewels, foremost among which were nets of *rantama* gems and nets of necklaces of *ranta* gems;
and it was illuminated by hundreds of thousands of great radiances, namely, by the radiance of the *jyotiraśmi* jewel-gems.

By the radiance of the *ādityagarbha* jewel, by the radiance of the *candradhvaja* jewel, by the radiance of the *gandhapradhūpanārci* jewel, by the radiance of the *śrīgarbha* jewel, by the radiance of the *padmagarbha* jewel, by the radiance of the *jyotirdhvaja* jewel, by the radiance of the *mahāpradīpa* jewel, by the radiance of the *samantadigvairocana* jewel, and by the radiance of the *mahāgandhameghaniścaritavidyunmālā* jewel;
That great garden was perpetually illuminated by one hundred thousand radiances from ten such preeminent great jewel-gems;

it was adorned with the downpour of one hundred thousand clouds of ten kinds of great ornaments; it resounded with the thundering of one hundred thousand clouds of ten kinds of black sandalwood incense that follows the seasons;

it was beautified by the hanging down of one hundred thousand clouds of divine garlands surpassing those of the gods; and it was showered with one hundred thousand clouds of various multicolored garments surpassing those of the gods.

That great garden was adorned with hundreds of thousands of clouds of ornaments surpassing those of the ten heavens; it was showered upon by hundreds of thousands of sons of gods who, desiring a vision of him, bowed down with faces cast toward the ground; it was showered upon by hundreds of thousands of clouds of apsarases who, having practiced virtuous conduct together with him in the past, offered up their respective bodies; and it was showered upon by hundreds of thousands of clouds of bodhisattvas who approached out of thirst for hearing the Dharma.
There sat the laywoman Āśā upon a great auspicious throne filled with gold, adorned with a pearl net from the depths of the ocean, wearing a bound crown;

her arms were arrayed with exquisite divine golden armlets and bracelets, and her arms shone with the light-rays of the *śrīkāya* jewel-gems; she wore deep blue, pure, hanging jeweled earrings, her head was graced and covered by a great net of jewels, she wore ear-ornaments of lion-faced jewel-gems, and her neck was draped with a necklace of wish-fulfilling king-jewel gems.
Her body was radiant with a light covered by a net of all kinds of jewels, and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings bowed their bodies before her.
There, immeasurable beings from the eastern direction came into the presence of the laywoman Āśā—
whether they were Great Brahmas, Brahmapurohitas, Brahmakāyikas, Vaśavartins, or those belonging to the realm of Paranirmitavaśavartins.

or the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods, or those belonging to the Nirmāṇarati realm, or the Saṃtuṣita gods, or those belonging to the Tuṣita realm, or the Suyāma gods, or those belonging to the Suyāma realm, or the lords of the gods, or those belonging to the Trāyastriṃśa realm, or the lords of the yakṣas, or the yakṣas, or the lords of the gandharvas, or the gandharvas,
or the lords of the kumbhāṇḍas, or the kumbhāṇḍas, or the lords of the nāgas, or the nāgas, or the lords of the asuras, or the asuras, or the lords of the garuḍas.
Or whether they be Garuḍas or lords of Kinnaras, or Kinnaras or lords of Mahoragas, or Mahoragas or Yamas or daughters of Yama,

or Pretas of great supernatural power or Pretas, or lords of humans or humans; likewise, those who are in the south, or the west, or the north, or the northeast, or the southeast, or the southwest, or the northwest, or below (Gv 81).
They come from the upward direction—whether they be Great Brahmas, Brahmapurohitas, or Brahmakāyikas; Vaśavartins or Vaśavartikāyikas;
or even lords of men or humans—afflicted by various diseases and overwhelmed by various defilements.
Those who were adhering to various types of views and obstructed by the veil of karma,
upon merely seeing the laywoman Āśā, had all their illnesses pacified;
with minds free from the stains of afflictions and the thorns of views removed, they shattered the mountains of all obstructions and entered the mandala of unobstructed purity.
In that pure mandala, all roots of goodness are kindled, all sprouts of the faculties flourish,
and the oceans of the methods of omniscient wisdom converge.
The oceans of methods for all gateways of dhāraṇīs revolve; the oceans of methods for all gateways of samādhis become manifest;
and all gateways of vows are brought forth.
All gateways of conduct proceed;
all gateways for the accomplishment of virtues are purified;
they proceed by way of leading to all superknowledges through the vastness of the mind.
They become unattached to the body and follow after everything.
Then, having entered the Samantavyūha grove, the merchant’s son Sudhana looked all around and saw the laywoman Āśā seated upon a noble throne. He approached the laywoman Āśā;

having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the laywoman Āśā, circumambulated her hundreds of thousands of times, and said this to her: "Noble lady, by me [is sought] unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening..."
I have generated the thought of enlightenment,
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct, nor how one should practice it.
I have heard, Noble Lady, that you give instruction and advice to the bodhisattvas;
therefore, may the Noble Lady tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct, and how should one practice it?
She said, "Noble son,
I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called 'The Banner of Sorrowless Security.

Noble son, I am one whose sight is not in vain, whose hearing is not in vain, whose attendance is not in vain, whose dwelling together for even a single night is not in vain, and whose remembrance is not in vain."

Noble son, I do not come within the range of the vision of those beings who have not planted roots of merit, nor do I appear through the perception of sight to those who have not been taken hold of by spiritual friends, nor to those who have not brought to mind the Perfectly Enlightened One.
"Noble son, by the mere sight of me, sentient beings become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Furthermore, noble son,
Tathāgatas come from the eastern direction, sit here upon this jewel throne, and teach the Dharma."
Just as it is in the eastern direction, so it is from all ten directions.
Thus, noble son, I am never separated from the sight of the Tathāgata.
They are never separated from hearing the Dharma,
nor are they separated from the company of bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, noble son, these eighty-four hundred thousand billion nayutas of living beings who dwell here in this great park, the Samantavyūha—

All these beings are irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; they are my companions in conduct. Furthermore, O son of good family, whatever other beings dwell here, they too are irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
"The Bodhisattvas who have entered into the irreversible Saṅgha are my companions in conduct.
She asked, "Noble Lady, how long ago did you first resolve your mind toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
She replied, "Son of good family, I recollect my former lives."
[Dīpaṃkara], the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha;
in the presence of that Tathāgata, I practiced the holy life (brahmacarya),
and I made offerings to that Tathāgata.
And I received the teaching of the Dharma from him. After him, there was a Tathāgata named Vimala; I went forth into homelessness under his dispensation.
And I upheld the wheel of Dharma;
after that, there was a Tathāgata named Ketur,
whom I pleased.
After him there was a Tathāgata named Meruśrī; after him there was a Tathāgata named Padmagarbha;
after him there was a Tathāgata named Vairocana.
After him was the Tathāgata named Samantacakṣus;
after him was the Tathāgata named Brahmaśuddha;
after him was the Tathāgata named Vajranābhi.
After him, there was a Tathāgata named Varuṇadeva.

In this manner, noble son, by way of the succession of births and the succession of eons, as I descend into and recollect the succession of Buddhas, I remember thirty-six Tathāgatas equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, who were Arhats and immediate [successors] to one another.
Those whom I have pleased, attended upon, honored, and worshiped; from whom I have heard the teaching of the Dharma;
and under whose instruction I have practiced the holy life—beyond these, O son of good family, the Tathāgatas fully know.

As many Tathāgatas as have been propitiated by me— O son of good family, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because from the very first production of the thought of awakening they pervade the entire realm of phenomena;
O son of good family, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because through the method of great compassion they enter into all worlds.
Noble son, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because they follow through to the very foundation of the dharma-realm in the ten directions by means of their great vows;
noble son, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because they pervade the entire world with great loving-kindness;
noble son, they are immeasurable.

Bodhisattvas, O son of good family, are immeasurable because they enter into all eons in all fields through their bodhisattva conduct; bodhisattvas are immeasurable because, by the power of meditative concentration,
they do not turn back from the bodhisattva path.
Noble son, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because they follow the method of the *dhāraṇī* that sustains all worlds through the power of the earth;
noble son, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because they follow and sustain the knowledge of the three times through the power of the light of wisdom;

noble son, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because they manifest wheels of light-networks according to the inclinations and desires of sentient beings in all fields through the power of the superknowledges (*abhijñā*).
Noble son, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because, through the power of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), they satisfy the entire world with the utterance of a single sound;
noble son, bodhisattvas are immeasurable because, through the purity of their bodies, they pervade all buddha-fields with their own bodies.

Sudhana said, "Noble Lady, how long will it be before you awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment? She replied, "Indeed, noble son, the bodhisattvas do not generate the mind for enlightenment with reference to a single sentient being— that is, for the sake of their maturation and discipline—
nor for the sake of a hundred beings."
not for a thousand beings, not for a hundred thousand beings, nor for ten million beings;
The mind of enlightenment is not generated by bodhisattvas for the sake of a hundred million beings, nor for a thousand million beings, nor for a hundred thousand billion beings.
Not for the sake of a heap of beings,
not for a mass of beings,
nor for an elite group of beings.
Neither for one superior to beings, nor for one inferior to beings,
nor for one equal to beings.
Neither of the simile of beings,
nor of the felloe of beings,
nor of the rim of beings.
Neither for the destruction of beings,
nor for the slaughter of beings,
nor for the alienation of beings.
Neither for the comprehension of a being, nor for the departure of a being, nor for the transition of a being.
Neither of the dispersal of beings, nor of the disintegration of beings,
nor of the retrogression of beings.
Neither of the distinction between beings, nor of the division of beings,
nor of the end of beings.
Neither of the weighing of beings, nor of the incomparable being, nor of the covering of beings.
Neither of one who reveals beings,
nor of one who conceals beings, nor of one who disparages beings.
Neither of the equality of beings, nor of the obstruction of beings,
nor of the investigation of beings.
Neither of a being who has strayed,
nor of a being who is perverted,
nor of a being who has emerged.
Neither of the emission of beings,
nor of the divinity of beings,
nor of the destruction of beings.
Neither of the agitation of beings, nor of the distress of beings, nor of the envy of beings.
Neither of the light of beings, nor of the faculties of beings, nor of the darkness of beings.
Not for one who is dull-witted regarding sentient beings,
