Yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct, nor how one should practice it.
I have heard, however, that the Noble One gives instruction and advice to bodhisattvas.
"May the Noble One tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, and how should he practice?

He replied, "Noble son, when I was being taught the methods of writing, numbering, seals, and calculation by Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, I was introduced to the gateway of knowledge that illuminates all arts and super-knowledges."

Therefore, noble son, whatever in this world consists of the knowledge of scripts, numbering, calculation, seals, and deposits; the various crafts and sciences, the tantras of the elements, the eloquence regarding the application of sensory objects, the means for warding off consumption, epilepsy, spirits, ghosts, and seizing demons, and the knowledge concerning villages, cities, market towns, ports, parks, penance groves, dwellings, and settlements— [all these I have mastered].

The knowledges of the dimensions of palaces, windows, and gabled chambers according to their intended designs; the knowledges of the construction and application of various mechanical vehicles and chariots; the knowledges of the signs of security and insecurity, and of fear and fearlessness; the knowledges of the application of practices in agriculture, commerce, and worldly transactions; the knowledges of the examination of the characteristics and movements of all major and minor limbs;
the knowledges of following the purification of the paths of action leading to happy and miserable rebirths; and the knowledges of honoring the collections of wholesome and unwholesome dharmas.

I fully know all those: the knowledges of the accumulations for happy and miserable destinies; the knowledges of the accumulations for the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; the knowledges of the accumulations for the stage of the Tathāgata; and the knowledges of causes, actions, applications, and conventional designations.

And within them, I cause sentient beings to enter, I establish them, I settle them, I instruct them, I discipline them, I strengthen them, I refine them, I console them, I honor them, I transform them, I elevate them, I increase them, I provide them with signs, I bring them to their ultimate limit, I purify them, and I make them stainless.
I heat it, I make it radiant, and I expand it.
O son of good family, I know this method of calculation for bodhisattvas. What, then, is that method?
A hundred times one hundred thousand is a *koṭi*;
a *koṭi* of *koṭis* is an *ayuta*;
a hundred times an *ayuta* is a *niyuta*.
A niyuta of niyutas is a bimbara;
a bimbara of bimbaras is a kiṃkara;
a kiṃkara of kiṃkaras is an agara.
The foremost among those who have no home,
the most excellent among the most excellent, the highest among the highest, the supreme among the supreme.
The highest of the high,
the limit of limits, the watch of watches, the rim of rimes.
The non-going of those who go, the understanding of those who understand, the deer-like nature of those who are like deer,
and the detachment of those who possess detachment.
Dispassion among the dispassionate, freedom from blemish among those free from blemish, transition among those who transition,
and expansion among those who expand.
Visara among the visarās, Vibhaja among the vibhajas, Vijaṅgha among the vijaṅghas, Viśodha among the viśodhas.
Viśodha is the marriage of those who are to be purified;
Vivāha is the division of those who are to be united; Vibhakta is the separation of those who are divided; Vikhata is the dispersal of those who are separated.
Vikhata is the falling away of those who have fallen away;
ḍalana is the descending of those who descend; avana is the abiding of those who abide.
Thavana is the reversal of reversals;
viparya is the time of reversals;
samaya is the crossing over of times.

The cause of those who have transcended, the cause of those who are transcending; the investigation of those who have investigated, the investigation of those who are investigating; the inversion of those who have inverted.
The inverted is the emergence of those who are inverted;
the emerged is the excellence of those who have emerged;
the excellent is the non-clinging of those who are excellent.
The blue of the blue ones,
the green of the green ones, the agitation of the agitated ones, and the yellowish-white of the yellowish-white ones.
Hari is the best among those who have ploughed; Hari is the light of lights;
the vision is the end of visions.
Having seen the end of those who have seen the ends, the cause of those who have causes, the *ela* of those who have *elas*,
and the *dumela* of those who have *elamas*.
Dumelaṃ is the peace of the Dumelās;
kṣemuḥ is the peace of the Kṣemus; eludam is [the peace] of the Eludas; bhāludam is [the peace] of the Eludameludas.
Bhāluda is the equality of bhāludas; equality is the clarity of equalities;
clarity is the measure of clarities.
The mantra of the knower among knowers is the "no-mantra";
the no-mantra among no-mantras is the "delusion-mantra";
the delusion-mantra among delusion-mantras is the "going-mantra."

The mantra of going is the non-mantra of those who go; the mantra of bowing is the non-mantra of those who bow; the mantra of non-bowing is the non-mantra of those who do not bow; the mantra of non-non-bowing is the non-mantra of those who do not non-bow; and the mantra of differentiation is [the non-mantra] of those who differentiate.
The mantra of Vimanta among the Vimantas, the supreme mantra among supreme mantras, the Śiva-mantra among Śiva-mantras,
and Delu among the Śiva-mantras.
Delu [is the root] of the delūs; velu [is the root] of the velūs; geluḥ [is the root] of the gels;
kheluḥ [is the root] of the khelūs.
From *khelu* comes *khelūnām*, *neluḥ*,
and *nelūnām*;
from *nelu* comes *bheluḥ*.
Bhelu was the chief of the Bhelus; Keli was the chief of the Kelus; Seli was the chief of the Selus; Peli was the chief of the Pelus.
Pelu is the [name] of the pelus; melu is the [name] of the melus;
saraḍa is the [name] of the melus.
Saraḍa is the chief of the Saraḍas; Bherudu is the chief of the Bherudas; Kheludu is the chief of the Kheludas; Māludu is the chief of the Māludas.
From *māludu* comes *mālūdūnām*,
from *samula* comes *samulānām*, from *athava* comes *athavānām*, and from *kamala* comes [the same].
Kamala is the best among lotuses; Agava is the best among Agavas; Ataru is the best among Atarus; Heluva is the best among Heluvus.
Heluva is the destroyer of those who possess causes; Mirahu is the movement of those who move;
Caraṇa is the blowing of those who breathe.
Dhamana among those who blow,
Pramada among women, Nigama among market-towns, and Upavarta among market-towns.
The mountain above, the instruction on the mountains,
and the inexhaustible instruction on instructions;
It is the inexhaustible among the inexhaustible, the arisen among those that have arisen, the "mine" among what is mine,
and the "I" among those who conceive of an "I."
The *avadāna* is the foremost among *avadānas*,
the blue lotus (*utpala*) among blue lotuses, the lotus (*padma*) among lotuses, and the *saṃkhyā* among numbers.
Number is the goal of numbers;
movement is the goal of movements; approach is the goal of approaches; and comparison is the goal of comparisons.
The comparison of comparisons is incalculable;
the incalculable of incalculables is an incalculable revolution;
the incalculable revolution of incalculable revolutions is immeasurable.
The immeasurable is the immeasurable of the immeasurables;
the limitless is the limitless of the limitlessses, which is a limitless revolution;
the limitless revolution is the boundless of the limitless revolutions.

The boundless [nature] of the boundless is the boundless revolution; the boundless revolution of the boundless revolutions is the all-pervasive; the all-pervasive [nature] of the all-pervasive is the all-pervasive revolution.
An incalculable revolution of those that are not incalculable revolutions;
an incalculable revolution of those that are incalculable incalculable revolutions; an incomparable revolution of those that are incomparable incalculable revolutions.
The incomparable is the transformation of the incomparable;
the transformation of the incomparable is the inconceivable of the incomparable transformations;
the inconceivable is the transformation of the inconceivable of the inconceivable.

The inconceivable chapter is the immeasurable of inconceivable chapters; the immeasurable is the immeasurable of immeasurables, which is the chapter of the immeasurable; the chapter of the immeasurable is the ineffable of the chapters of the immeasurable.
The ineffable [number] of ineffables is the ineffable revolution; the ineffable revolution of ineffable revolutions is the ineffable-of-the-ineffable;
the ineffable-of-the-ineffable of ineffable-of-the-ineffable revolutions is the ineffable-of-the-ineffable revolution.
Before him there was a great heap of sand measuring many yojanas.
Counting that heap of sand, weighing it, and pouring it out, he calculated its number: "There are this many grains of sand;
indeed, there are this many grains of sand, even unto incalculable revolutions."

Having demonstrated that heap of sand by means of the instruction on the conventions of calculation, he said this: "Noble son, this application of calculation proceeds well for Bodhisattvas through the succession of world-systems.
By this method of calculation, Bodhisattvas count the expansions of world-systems in the eastern direction;
likewise in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions."
By this method of calculation, Bodhisattvas enumerate the expansions of world-systems.
Noble son, this method of calculation proceeds for Bodhisattvas in the successive enumerations of the names of world-systems in the ten directions.
By this method of calculation, Bodhisattvas enumerate the succession of names of world-systems in the ten directions.

Just as it is in the successive enumerations of the names of world-systems, so too does this very method of calculation proceed for Bodhisattvas in the successive enumerations of aeons, the names of Buddhas, the names of Dharmas, the names of sentient beings, the names of karmas, and indeed in all successive enumerations of names throughout the ten directions.
By this method of calculation, bodhisattvas proceed through all successions of names for bodhisattvas in the ten directions;
by this method of calculation, bodhisattvas enumerate the entire succession of names for bodhisattvas in the ten directions.
Noble son, this is the extent of my knowledge regarding this light of the bodhisattvas' wisdom, which possesses the superknowledges of the craftsmanship of knowing all phenomena.
How could I possibly [describe] the bodhisattvas who have entered into the enumeration of all worlds and have entered into the enumeration of the methods of all phenomena?

To know the conduct or to speak of the virtues of those Bodhisattvas who have entered into the enumeration of the three times, who have entered into the enumeration of all sentient beings, who have entered into the enumeration of all aggregates of phenomena, who have entered into the enumeration of the enlightenment of all Buddhas, and who exercise mastery over the wheel of names of all dharmas— this is impossible.
to indicate its range, or to manifest its domain,
or to describe its power.
Whether to demonstrate his intention,
or to illuminate his equipment,
or to explain his vow.
either to demonstrate the conduct,
or to illuminate the purification of the perfections, or to fully reveal the purification of the realization;
Or the object of meditative concentration to be described,
or the light of knowledge to be followed.
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region there is a city named Samudrapratiṣṭhāna. There dwells a laywoman named Prabhūtā.
Go to her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having heard the words of the spiritual friend, his body bristling with joy, gave rise to a great surge of delight, and his mind became exultant. Having attained the jewel of an exceedingly rare and wondrous resolve, he was dedicated to the vast mental and physical activities for the welfare of the world;

he gained mastery over entering the succession of the arising of Buddhas; he reached the highest pinnacle of wisdom regarding the purity of the mandala of Dharma; and he attained the supreme vision of the manifestation of liberation through its divisions as they follow everywhere.
His range of perception was unimpeded across the three times; his mind was born from an inexhaustible ocean of merit; he wielded mastery over the illumination of great wisdom;

and he shattered the door-bolts of the prison of the city of the three worlds. Having bowed his head at the feet of the youth Indriyeśvara, he circumambulated the youth Indriyeśvara hundreds of thousands of times, looking back at him again and again. Of Indriyeśvara...
He departed from the presence of the boy. // 13 //
(Gv 105) 16. Prabhūtā.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, receiving the cloud of the instructions of his spiritual friend, [proceeded].

Like the ocean never satiated by the rains of great clouds, he was born from the sprouting of the shoots of the sense-faculties upon the auspicious ground of his being, which had been ripened by the rays of knowledge from the sun of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). His body and mind were refreshed by the web of rays from the full moon of spiritual friends’ instructions; thirsty for the water of the spiritual friends’ teachings, like a herd of deer scorched by the rays of the summer sun, his mind—like a white lotus (*pauṇḍarīka*)—was awakened by the water of the Himalayan streams that is the instruction of spiritual friends.
Like a lotus pond whose blossoms have opened as swarms of bees depart,
his mental continuum was illuminated by the jewel-like conduct resulting from the instructions of spiritual friends;
like an island of jewels, it was strewn with various kinds of gems.
Endowed with the accumulation of merit and wisdom through the instructions of spiritual friends, he was like a great jambu tree laden with flowers and fruit;
having increased his store of learning through the instructions of spiritual friends,
he was like a great cloud in the sky produced by the exquisite play of the lord of great serpents.

He was a mountain-peak of diverse, stainless dharmas arising from the instructions of spiritual friends, like Citrakūṭa graced by the world of the thirty-three gods; surrounded by a multitude of pure qualities born from the instructions of spiritual friends,
he was a conqueror,
unconquered.

Surrounded by the host of the thirty-three gods, like Śakra the crusher of the hosts of the lords of the Asuras, he proceeded in due order toward the city of Samudrapratiṣṭhāna, searching for the laywoman Prabhūtā. He pointed her out to the great multitude of people, saying: "Noble son, this is the laywoman Prabhūtā; she resides in her own home in the middle of the city."
Then Sudhana, the merchant's son, approached the residence of the laywoman Prabhūtā; having arrived, he stood with palms joined in the gateway hall.

He beheld the house of the laywoman Prabhūtā as vast and expansive, surrounded by walls of jewels, with gates distributed in the four directions, adorned with an incalculable and immeasurable array of jewels, produced through the ripening of inconceivable merit.
Having entered that house and looking all around, he saw the laywoman Prabhūtā seated upon a jeweled throne.
A woman who was new, young, in the full bloom of her first youth, beautiful, gracious, and lovely to behold, endowed with the excellence of an exceedingly pure complexion—
her hair loose, her limbs unadorned, and dressed in white garments—
with the exception of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, no sentient being whatsoever would approach that house.
He does not stand overpowering others, whether by means of his body,
or by the sovereignty of his mind,
or by his splendor.
Whether by her complexion or her splendor,
whatever beings— whether gods or humans— behold the female lay follower Prabhūtā, they all perceive Prabhūtā as the Teacher.
And in that house, ten thousand koṭis of seats had been prepared, surpassing those of gods and humans, perfected through the karmic maturation of the bodhisattva’s deeds.

Yet, in that house he saw no accumulation of food or drink, nor any accumulation of clothing, ornaments, or articles of enjoyment, except for a single cooking pot placed before him. And he saw ten thousand women standing before him, with the complexion of apsarases, the form of apsarases, and the grace of apsarases.
Those women—possessing the movements of apsarases, the enjoyments of apsarases, and the refinements of apsarases; wearing divine garments of kalpa-cotton; with limbs adorned with divine ornaments;

possessing voices as delightful as the songs of apsarases; and having the proportions and stature of apsarases—stood before him as servants, responding to his every word. They attended upon him, gazed at him, contemplated him, paid him homage, looked upon him, and bowed down to him.
They bow down and pay homage;
and the fragrance that wafts from their bodies pervades all of that.
They incense the city;
and whatever beings smell that fragrance, they all become free from malice, free from enmity, free from harmful intent, and their minds are devoid of envy and avarice.

They possess minds free from deceit and guile; they are gentle, with unobstructed minds; their minds are neither dejected nor arrogant, but even, friendly, benevolent, and established in restraint; they have no desire for the possessions of others.
And those who hear their voice—
They all become thrilled, joyful, and humble in heart;
and those who behold them perceive themselves as free from passion.
Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son bowed his head at the feet of the laywoman Prabhūtā, circumambulated her hundreds of thousands of times,
and standing before her with palms joined in reverence, he said: "Noble lady, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
Yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it.
I have heard, however, that the Noble Lady gives instruction and advice to bodhisattvas.
"May the Noble Lady tell me this: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, and how should they practice?
She replied, "Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the 'Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit with Its Array.'"
From this single cooking pot, noble son, I satisfy beings of various inclinations with foods according to their wishes— various soups, various flavors, various colors, and various fragrances.
From this single cooking pot, noble son, I satisfy even a hundred beings with foods according to their respective desires.
even a thousand beings, even a hundred thousand beings, even ten million beings,
even a hundred koṭis of beings, even a hundred thousand koṭis of beings,
even a hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of beings,
I satisfy, serve, and gladden even inexpressibly inexpressible numbers of sentient beings with various inclinations by means of whatever foods they desire.
I gladden, I delight, and I satisfy them.
I make them joyful in mind;
yet this little cauldron neither diminishes nor decreases.
It does not diminish, it is not exhausted, and it does not come to an end.
He does not reach a boundary, nor does he arrive at a conclusion.
By this method, O son of good family, even if there were beings as numerous as the atoms of dust in Jambudvīpa, [he would still not reach a limit].
Likewise, even those equal in number to the atoms of a world-system of four continents, even those equal in number to the atoms of a thousandfold world-system,
and even those equal in number to the atoms of a two-thousandfold world-system.
Even if there were beings as numerous as the atoms in a triple-thousand great thousandfold world system,

or even as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields— beings who have approached me with various inclinations— I would serve them with whatever foods they desire, with various soups, various flavors, various colors, and various fragrances.
I satisfy them, I gladden them, I cause them to rejoice.
I satisfy them and make them joyful,
yet this little pot does not diminish.
It does not decline,
it does not diminish, and it is not exhausted.
It does not reach exhaustion, it does not approach a limit, and it does not reach an end, a boundary, or a final conclusion.

If, noble son, all sentient beings included within all the world-systems of the ten directions— possessing various inclinations and various intentions— should approach me, I would satisfy them all with foods according to their desires, and I would make them as joyful as possible.
Just as with various foods, so too with various methods of drink, various supreme flavors, various beds, various garments,

various flowers, various garlands, various perfumes, various incenses, various ointments, various powders, various jewels, various ornaments, various jeweled chariots, various parasols, various banners, various flags, and various kinds of excellent requisites, I shall act so as to make them joyful in mind.

Furthermore, noble son, whatever śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in a single world-system in the eastern direction who, possessing their final bodies, attain the fruit of śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha enlightenment— all of them have partaken of my food.
Just as it is in one world-system in the eastern direction, so it is in a hundred world-systems, in a thousand world-systems, and so forth.
In hundreds of thousands of world-systems, in ten million world-systems, and in hundreds of millions of world-systems.
In thousands of millions of world-systems, in hundreds of thousands of millions of world-systems, and in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of world-systems.

O son of good family, in as many world-systems as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa— as many world-systems as there are atoms in four-continent world-systems, as many world-systems as there are atoms in thousandfold world-systems, as many world-systems as there are atoms in two-thousandfold world-systems, and as many world-systems as there are atoms in three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-systems— and furthermore, O son of good family, in whatever world-systems in the eastern direction, even as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, there are Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas who, bearing their final bodies, attain the fruit of Śrāvaka and Pratyekabuddha enlightenment;
Having all partaken of my food,
[they shall go] just as in the eastern direction,
so too in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions.
"Whosoever, noble son,
are the bodhisattvas bound to one more birth in any single world-system in the eastern direction,
they all, having consumed my food, sit upon the seat of awakening, defeat Māra along with his host, and fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Just as in one world-system in the eastern direction,
so too in a hundred world-systems, in a thousand world-systems, [and so forth].

In hundreds of thousands of world-systems, in ten million world-systems, in a hundred times ten million world-systems, in a thousand times ten million world-systems, in a hundred thousand times ten million world-systems, and in a hundred thousand times ten billion world-systems— namely,

in those world-systems equal in number to the atoms of Jambudvīpa, in those equal to the atoms of four-continent world-systems, in those equal to the atoms of thousandfold world-systems, in those equal to the atoms of two-thousandfold world-systems, and in those equal to the atoms of three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-systems;

"O son of good family, whatever bodhisattvas in the eastern direction— up to as many world systems as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields— are bound to only one more birth, they all partake of my food, sit at the seat of awakening, defeat Māra along with his hosts, and awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
As it is in the eastern direction,"

In this way, O son of good family, in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, and downward directions— and likewise in the upward direction, in every single world-system— whatever bodhisattvas there may be who are bound to only one more birth;
Having partaken of my food, they all sit at the seat of awakening, defeat Māra along with his army, and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Just as it is in one world-system in the upward direction,
so it is in hundreds of world-systems, thousands of world-systems, hundreds of thousands of world-systems, ten million world-systems, and hundreds of millions of world-systems.

In thousands of world-systems, in hundreds of thousands of world-systems, in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of world-systems— namely, in those world-systems equal in number to the atoms of Jambudvīpa,

in those world-systems equal in number to the atoms of four-continent world-systems, in those world-systems equal in number to the atoms of thousandfold world-systems, in those world-systems equal in number to the atoms of two-thousandfold world-systems, and in those world-systems equal in number to the atoms of three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-systems.

O son of good family, whatever bodhisattvas bound by only one more birth there may be in the upward direction— in as many world systems as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields—
all of them, having partaken of my food, sit at the seat of awakening, defeat Māra along with his host, and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.
"Noble son, do you see these ten thousand women who are my retinue?
He replied, "I see them, Noble Lady.
She said, "Noble son, headed by these, there are ten hundred thousand incalculable numbers of women who share the same conduct as I."

They share a single vow, a single root of goodness, a single array of departure, and are purified by a single path of resolute conviction; they are purified by a shared recollection, purified by a shared destiny, possess immeasurable shared awakening, have attained shared faculties, have a shared mental pervasion, share the same range of objects, have entered the shared method of the Dharma, and have reached a shared certainty regarding the meaning.

They illuminate the meaning of the concordant Dharma; they are purified by concordant forms; they possess concordant powers and immeasurables; they are unconquered by concordant fortitude; they possess the resonance of the voice of the concordant Dharma;
and they are purified by concordant tones.
In all worldly affairs, they are purified by corresponding virtues; through the praise of immeasurable qualities, they are purified by corresponding actions;
and through the purification of the ripening of blameless karma, they pervade with corresponding great loving-kindness.

They possess the pervasion of great compassion that is concordant [with their purpose] by way of protecting the entire world; they possess the purity of bodily action that is concordant [with their purpose] by way of never wearying of maturing the entire world;

and they possess the purity of vocal action that is concordant [with their purpose] within the expressions and conventions of the dharma-realm by way of manifesting bodies that satisfy all sentient beings according to their inclinations.
Approaches to assemblies in all the circles of the Buddha’s retinues; simultaneous arrivals in all Buddha-fields;
and simultaneous direct knowledges in the pursuit of all methods of the Dharma, for the sake of honoring and serving all Buddhas.
They are purified by conduct in common with all the stages of a bodhisattva for the attainment of all bodhisattva levels.
Noble son, these ten thousand women pervade the ten directions in a single instant;
that is to say, they provide food to the bodhisattvas who are bound to only one more birth, taking food from this very vessel.
Taking food from this very vessel, they pervade the ten directions;
they pervade the ten directions in order to provide alms-food to those in their final existence who belong to the vehicles of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Having pervaded them, they satisfy all the hosts of pretas with food.
O son of good family, with this very pot I satisfy the gods with divine food,
the nāgas with nāga food,
and the yakṣas with yakṣa food.
the gandharvas with the food of gandharvas, the asuras with the food of asuras,
and the garuḍas with the food of garuḍas;
He sustained the kinnaras with kinnara food, the mahoragas with mahoraga food,
and humans with human food.
"I satisfy non-human beings with the food of non-humans.
Wait a moment, noble son, and you shall see it for yourself.
As soon as these words were spoken by the laywoman Prabhūtā, [the non-human beings appeared].
Then, at that very moment, immeasurable beings entered through the eastern gate of the house, having been invited by the laywoman Prabhūtā on account of her previous vows.
Likewise, immeasurable beings entered through the southern, western, and northern gates of the house, having been invited by the laywoman Prabhūtā on account of her previous vows.
Once they were seated upon those seats, the laywoman Prabhūtā satisfied them with foods according to their wishes—various soups, various flavors, various colors, and various fragrances.
He offers them a choice of food,
satisfies them,
and gladdens their hearts.
He gladdens, satisfies, and makes them joyful,
just as one does with various kinds of food.
Thus, with various methods of drinking,
various excellent flavors,
and various seats,

He satisfies them with various couches, various vehicles, various garments, various flowers, various garlands, various perfumes, various incenses, various ointments, various powders, various ornaments, various jewel-encrusted chariots, various parasols, various banners, various flags, and various kinds of excellent requisites.
He satisfies the gods with divine food until they are fully satisfied and their minds are gladdened;

he likewise satisfies the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans with their respective foods until they are fully satisfied and their minds are gladdened.
And that pot does not diminish, it does not waste away, nor does it become depleted.
It does not diminish, it does not come to exhaustion, and it does not reach a limit.
It does not reach an end, nor a limit, nor a final consummation.
Then the laywoman Prabhūtā said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the 'Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit.
What could I possibly know of the bodhisattvas who possess inexhaustible merit, given the inexhaustibility of the great ocean of their vast merit?"
Because they have well-accumulated a vast store of merit that is like the sky; because they fulfill the aspirations of the entire world like a wish-fulfilling king of jewels;
and because they protect the roots of virtue of all beings like a great circle of merit.

To know their conduct or to speak of their virtues— to know those who are like great clouds of merit by raining down jewels into the hands of the entire world, who are like stewards of the treasury of great merit by opening the gates of the city of Dharma, and who are like great lamps of merit by dispelling the darkness of poverty for all living beings— is impossible.
Go, son of good family,
right here in the southern region to a city named Mahāsaṃbhava;
there dwells a householder named Vidvān.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the laywoman Prabhūtā, circumambulated the laywoman Prabhūtā hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at her again and again, departed from the presence of the laywoman Prabhūtā, unsatiated by the sight of her. 14.
The Wise One:
Then indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having attained the liberation of the illumination of the inexhaustible treasury of merit, reflected deeply upon that ocean of merit.
Beholding that sky of merit,
taking hold of that mass of merit,
and ascending that mountain of merit, he—
Gathering that accumulation of merit, plunging into that mass of merit, and descending upon that ford of merit.
Purifying that mandala of merit,
beholding that treasury of merit,
and recollecting that method of merit,
Attending to that path of merit and purifying that lineage of merit,
he proceeded by stages toward the city of Mahāsaṃbhava and sought out the wise householder.
Seeking them out and looking about with a longing for spiritual friends,
he is permeated by the constant flow of the vision of spiritual friends.
Through an intention sustained by the influence of spiritual friends, through a practice that follows spiritual friends,
and through an energy untiring in its service to spiritual friends;
All roots of goodness are dependent upon spiritual friends;
all accumulations of merit are fixed upon spiritual friends;
and the practices of skillful means are increased by spiritual friends.
Through skill in attending upon spiritual friends without depending on others,
through all roots of goodness increasing,
and through the bodhisattva’s resolute intention becoming purified.
With the faculties of the bodhisattva increasing,
all roots of goodness being brought to maturity,
and the accomplishments of the great vows increasing;
As his great compassion expanded,
perceiving himself as having drawn near to omniscience, he received the illumination of the Dharma from all the Buddhas regarding the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Seeking the wise householder, he beheld him in the middle of the city at a crossroads, seated upon a celestial throne made of the seven precious gems, its feet fashioned from various diamonds and sapphire jewels, white with the blazing glow of golden threads, containing within it the pure *vimalagarbha* jewel, and its frame adorned with a hundred varieties of the five precious substances. It was illuminated by the ever-increasing radiance of the ten powers of a Tathāgata.

He was seated upon a noble throne (bhadrāsana) that was arrayed with various divine garments, with divine silk banners and flags raised aloft, covered by a lattice of many jewels, overspread with a great canopy of precious gems, and hung with garlands of great golden jewels and flowers;
while a parasol made of Jāmbūnada gold was held over him with a handle of pure beryl, and he was being fanned with spotless yak-tail whisks like those of the king of swans.

It was perfumed by the offering of various fragrances; on the left and right, five hundred musical instruments were being played with sounds more sweet than the divine; for the sake of generating joy in sentient beings, clouds of celestial flowers rained down upon the city of Mahāsambhava; they had transcended both divine and human forms, possessed the perfected intentions of bodhisattvas, were adorned with ornaments surpassing the divine, and served as attendants who responded to every command.
Surrounded by ten thousand living beings who shared in his former roots of merit and followed his same conduct,
Sudhana the merchant’s son, having seen him, approached the wise householder.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the wise householder and circumambulated the wise householder hundreds of thousands of times.
Having circumambulated him and stood before him with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus: "Noble One, for the sake of all sentient beings,
I have set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment— that is to say, for the pacification of the suffering of all sentient beings, for the establishment of all sentient beings in ultimate happiness,
for the rescue of all sentient beings from the ocean of saṃsāra, and for the leading of all sentient beings to the island of the jewel of the Dharma."
For the purpose of drying up the moisture of craving in all sentient beings; for the purpose of generating the moisture of great compassion in all sentient beings;

for the purpose of turning back the craving for the pleasures of desire in all sentient beings; for the purpose of producing the craving for the wisdom of a Buddha in all sentient beings; for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to cross over the wilderness and desolate wastes of saṃsāra; and for the purpose of generating delight in the garden of the qualities and dharmas of a Buddha in all sentient beings.
For the sake of leading all sentient beings out from the cities of the triple world, and for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to the city of omniscience;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how they should practice it.
"I have heard, noble one, that you give instruction and admonition to the bodhisattvas.
May the noble one tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, and by training in what way do bodhisattvas become a refuge for all sentient beings?"
When this had been said, the wise householder spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
It is well that you have resolved your mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Rare, noble son, are those beings [who do so]."
Those who, having generated the mind set on unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and seeking the conduct of a bodhisattva, are never satiated by the sight of spiritual friends;
they do not grow weary of approaching spiritual friends;
and they do not feel distress in their service to spiritual friends.
They do not give rise to despondency because of the difficulty of encountering a spiritual friend;
they do not turn back because of their persistent search for a spiritual friend;
and they do not retreat because their hearts are intensely longing and thirsty for a spiritual friend.
They do not turn back from gazing upon the faces of spiritual friends;
they do not falter on the paths of the instructions of spiritual friends;
and they do not grow weary in the service and attendance of spiritual friends.
"Do you see, noble son, this retinue of mine?
He replied, "I see it, Noble One."

He said: "Noble son, all these have been inspired by me to set their minds upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. By me they have been brought forth into the family of the Tathāgatas; by me they have been nourished through the application of the perfections."
By me have they been led forth by all pure dharmas;
by me have they been made to increase in the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
by me have they been raised up from the lineage of the world.
By me these have been established in the lineage of the Tathāgatas; by me these have been turned back from the wheel of rebirth in the world;
by me these have been turned toward the turning of the wheel of Dharma.
"By me these beings have been rescued from falling into the miserable states and the destinies of the three times;
by me they have been established through the realization of the equality of all phenomena.
For it is in this way, noble son, that bodhisattvas become saviors of all beings."
Noble son, I am a recipient of merits arising from the treasury of the mind;
thus, I give food to those who seek food and drink to those who seek drink.
To those seeking the finest flavors, he gave the finest flavors; to those seeking solid food, solid food;
to those seeking soft food, soft food.
To those desiring things to be licked, [he gave] things to be licked; to those desiring things to be sucked, [he gave] things to be sucked;
to those desiring clothing, [he gave] clothing.
To those seeking flowers, [he gave] flowers; to those seeking garlands, garlands; to those seeking perfumes, perfumes.
To those who desired incense, he gave incense; to those who desired ointment, he gave ointment; and to those who desired powder, he gave powder.
Ornaments and decorations for those who desired ornaments and decorations, jewels for those who desired jewels,
and gold for those who desired gold.
silver to those seeking silver, pearls to those seeking pearls, and shelter to those seeking shelter.
He provided shelter to those seeking shelter, seats to those seeking seats, and beds to those seeking beds.
To those who desired medicinal requisites for the sick, he gave medicinal requisites for the sick; to those who desired vehicles, he gave vehicles; to those who desired mounts, he gave mounts.

To those seeking elephants, horses, chariots, cattle, donkeys, buffaloes, and sheep, he gave elephants, horses, chariots, cattle, donkeys, buffaloes, and sheep; to those seeking umbrellas, banners, and flags, he gave umbrellas, banners, and flags;
and to those seeking female and male slaves, he gave female and male slaves.
To those who desired a retinue of young men, he gave a retinue of young men; to those who desired women, women;
and to those who desired maidens, [he gave maidens].
To those seeking maidens, he gave maidens; to those seeking crest-jewels for crowns, he gave crest-jewels for crowns;
to those seeking crest-jewels together with their skins, he gave crest-jewels together with their skins.

To those who desire a mass of hair that is dark blue and pure, I give a mass of hair that is dark blue and pure; and to those who desire all manner of various requisites, I give all those various requisites.
Wait a moment, noble son, and you shall see it for yourself.
As soon as these words had been spoken by the wise householder, immeasurable beings who had been invited by the wise householder through his previous vows gathered together from various directions,
various regions and districts, various cities, various market towns, various ports, various villages, and from various classes of beings.

From various classes of beings, from the diverse distinctions among those classes of beings, from the revolutions through various states of existence, from the various perceptions and modes of movement regarding their respective abodes, they are purified of various sense-bases; they seek various kinds of food, desire various kinds of food, possess various inclinations, and long for pure food and drink;

they seek meat and crave various distinctions in eating; they are established in birth-places distinguished by various states of existence—namely, among humans, they seek various types of solid food such as boiled rice, sour gruel, soup, fish, and meat.

Just as among humans, so too in all investigations of the realms of existence, those seeking various kinds of food and drink approached [the Bodhisattva]; that is to say, invited by the vow of the Bodhisattva through the sound of the drum of unimpeded generosity, they approached that wise householder, begged, looked upon him, gazed at him, and made their requests known.
Then, the wise householder, perceiving that those beggars had assembled, reflected for a moment and looked toward the expanse of the sky.
From that sky, various kinds of food and drink—possessing diverse flavors, diverse colors, and diverse fragrances—descended and came to rest upon the palms of his hands.
Taking them, he [provided] those beggars who had gathered there, who possessed various inclinations, with the types of food and drink according to their respective desires.

He satisfies, provides for, gratifies, gladdens, delights, and fully pleases them with all kinds of excellent requisites, making their minds joyful. Having satisfied them further with various material gifts, he should teach them the Dharma.
That is to say: illuminating the cause for the accumulation of the vast equipment of wisdom; illuminating the cause for the non-occurrence of all poverty;
and illuminating the cause for the arising and attainment of great wealth.
Illuminating the cause for the attainment of the realization of the method of the knowledge of phenomena; illuminating the cause for the accumulation of a vast store of merit;
and illuminating the cause for the attainment and arising of the food of the sustenance of joy.
He elucidated the cause for the arising of the attainment of a body adorned with the primary and secondary marks;
he elucidated the cause for the arising of the attainment of the purity of invincible power;
and he elucidated the cause for the arising of the attainment of uninterrupted wisdom.
He should teach the Dharma, illuminating the cause for the arising of the attainment of the inexhaustible power of merit that crushes all the forces of Māra.

To those who approach seeking food, he should satisfy them by taking various kinds of food from the expanse of the sky; observing that they will thereby obtain longevity, beauty, strength, happiness, and eloquence, he teaches the Dharma for their acquisition [of these qualities].
To those who approach seeking drink, he should satisfy them with various kinds of drinks—noble, excellent, blameless, and gladdening to the mind.

Having satisfied them, he should teach the Dharma so that they may turn away from the thirst for and delight in cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*), and so that they may generate the thirst for and delight in the Buddha-dharma.
To those who have approached seeking the finest of tastes, he satisfies them with various kinds of excellent flavors— sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent—
and further teaches them the Dharma so that they may attain the mark of a Great Man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*) which is the supreme excellence of taste.

Having gathered those seeking vehicles who had arrived from various directions and river-currents by means of gifts of various kinds of vehicles, he would teach them the Dharma for the purpose of ascending the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*).
Knowing that those seeking clothing had approached from various directions, he reflected for a moment and looked up toward the expanse of the sky.
Then, from that expanse of the sky, there appeared [robes] of various hues and many colors—pure blue, yellow, red, white, madder-red, and crystal-colored.
Holding various garments in the palms of his hands, he stood before them;
having bestowed those upon the supplicants, he should teach them the Dharma for the sake of attaining the pure, golden-colored skin of a Tathāgata endowed with supreme modesty and decorum.
Having provided each supplicant individually with every kind of requisite as they had arrived, he should teach them the Dharma according to their respective needs.

Then the wise householder, having demonstrated to the merchant’s son Sudhana that inconceivable range of the bodhisattva liberation, spoke thus: "Noble son, I know only this liberation called 'Born from the Treasury of the Mind'."
How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the virtues of those Bodhisattvas who have attained mastery over requisites and have obtained the jewel-hand,
or demonstrate their miraculous transformations—

those who, covering all world-systems without exception with their hands, rain down clouds of various colored jewels in the circles of the assemblies of all Tathāgatas for the purpose of performing worship to the Buddhas?

In this way, they rain down clouds of ornaments of various colors; clouds of multi-colored gabled pavilions; clouds of variegated garments of various colors; clouds of the delightful and sweet sounds of various divine musical instruments, cymbals, and vocal performances; clouds of perfumes of various colors; and clouds of all kinds of requisites—incense, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and every other implement—as well as clouds of every form of worship for all Buddhas.

In all the circles of assemblies of the Tathāgatas and in all the abodes of sentient beings, that is to say, for the sake of honoring and attending upon all Buddhas, and for the sake of maturing and disciplining the realm of all sentient beings.
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region there is a city named Siṃhapota. There dwells a merchant-leader of the Dharma named Ratnacūḍa.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana— satisfied, uplifted, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and cheer—

demonstrated his status as a disciple out of reverence for the Dharma toward the wise householder; and through that empowerment, he beheld all the qualities of a Buddha and beheld omniscience as dependent upon him.
Demonstrating unbreakable affection for spiritual friends,
showing that the instructions of spiritual friends are ultimately inconceivable,
and conforming to being under the guidance of spiritual friends;
Listening to the words of the instructions of the spiritual friend,
contemplating the faculty of faith originating from the spiritual friend,
and sent forth by the instructions of the spiritual friend.

With a mind intent on pleasing and following his spiritual friend, he bowed his head at the feet of the wise householder, circumambulated the wise householder hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of the wise householder. // 15 //
(Gv 114) 18. Ratnacūḍa.
Then Sudhana, the merchant's son, reflecting upon that water of merit, [proceeded].
Beholding that field of merit,
purifying that Sumeru of merit,
and immersing oneself in that ford of merit.
Opening up that treasury of merit, beholding that storehouse of merit,
and purifying that mandala of merit.
Accumulating that mass of merit,
generating that power of merit,
and increasing that momentum of merit,
Traveling by stages, he approached the city of Siṃhapota. While searching for the merchant-chief Ratnacūḍa, he saw him in the midst of the marketplace.
Having bowed his head at his feet and circumambulated him, he stood before him with palms joined and spoke thus: "Noble sir, I have generated the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva."
How should I practice? Therefore, may the Noble One kindly instruct me in the path of the bodhisattva, by which path I may set forth toward omniscience.
Then Ratnacūḍa, the merchant-leader, took the merchant’s son Sudhana by the hand, went to his own residence, showed him that house, and said this: "Behold, noble son, my residence.
As he looked around, he saw that house to be pure, radiant, made of Jāmbūnada gold, vast and lofty.

It was encircled by a wall of silver, beautifully adorned with crystal palaces, embellished with hundreds of thousands of peaks of beryl, and featured pillars raised high of musāragalva stone; it was well-appointed with lion thrones made of red pearls, with lion-banners raised high bearing *jyotīrasa* jewel-gems, spread with canopies of *vairocana* jewel-gems, covered with a variegated golden net of wish-fulfilling gems, and arrayed with an incalculable number of jewel-gems as ornaments.
It was provided with lotus ponds filled with cool water and made of emerald, surrounded by trees made of every kind of jewel; it was vast, extensive, ten stories high, and possessed eight gates.
Having entered that house, he surveyed it thoroughly on all sides.
In the first city, he saw the renunciation of all methods of food and drink; in the second city, the renunciation of all methods of clothing;
and in the third city, the renunciation of all jewels, ornaments, and decorations.

In the fourth city, he beheld the renunciation of the great earth, the auspicious jewel of a maiden, who delights in the enjoyment of the inner palace; and in the fifth city, he beheld the ocean of samādhis and the method of dhāraṇīs belonging to bodhisattvas established on the fifth stage, who are devoted to the joy of the communal recitation of the Dharma, whose thoughts and actions are directed toward the welfare and happiness of the world, and who bring forth all treatises.
And he saw the assembly of those who were bringing forth the emergence from concentration, the investigation of concentration, and the light of knowledge;

[those] in the sixth city who had attained the dwelling of the perfection of wisdom, possessed profound wisdom, had the superknowledge of the tranquility of all phenomena, had emerged through the gateways of the wombs of the stages, concentrations, and dhāraṇīs, as well as the universal gateways, whose range was unobstructed, and whose conduct was non-dual.

He saw an assembly of bodhisattvas who were performing a communal recitation of the Dharma, following the chapters of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, analyzing them, and elucidating them; they were chanting these gateways to the *Prajñāpāramitā*, namely:
the gateway to the *Prajñāpāramitā* called "The Womb of Peace" (*śāntigarbha*).

And there is the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Well-Differentiated Knowledge of All Worlds," the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Immovable Revolving," and the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Stainless Radiance."

The gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the womb of Duryodhana," the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the maṇḍala that illuminates the world," and the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the maṇḍala of the method of following."

The gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Womb of the Ocean," the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Attainment of Universal-Eyed Equanimity," and the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Following the Inexhaustible Treasury."

The gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the ocean of the principles of all phenomena," the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "following after the oceans of all worlds," and the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "unimpeded eloquence."
And there is the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Abode of Successive Dependence upon the Clouds of Dharma.
Taking these gateways to the perfection of wisdom as the foremost, there are a full ten hundred thousand times countless gateways to the perfection of wisdom.
He saw those bodhisattvas standing in well-arranged circles of assemblies with inexpressibly magnificent arrays, chanting together;

in the seventh city, he saw the gathering of bodhisattvas who had attained the patient acceptance that all things are like echoes, who were perfected in the certainty of skillful means and knowledge, and who received the clouds of Dharma from all the Tathāgatas; in the eighth city, he saw [the gathering of] those who had attained the superknowledges leading to non-retrogression, who wander through all world-systems, and who have achieved the manifestation of their presence in all circles of assemblies.

He beheld the assembly of bodhisattvas whose bodies were perfectly distinguished throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), whose spheres of activity were inseparable from the feet of all Tathāgatas, who had merged into the body of all Buddhas, and who were the foremost speakers in the circles of assemblies of all Tathāgatas.
In the ninth city, he beheld the assembly of bodhisattvas bound to only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*).

In the tenth city, he beheld the oceans of vows for the departure through the conduct of first generating the thought of enlightenment belonging to all Tathāgatas; the spheres of the miraculous displays of all Buddha-dharmas; the circles of assemblies in all Buddha-fields; the resonances of the wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas; and the arrays of the empowerments for the discipline of all sentient beings.
Having seen Ratnacūḍa, the merchant of Dharma, he said this to him: "Noble one, from where has this kind of perfected excellence been purified by you?
Where were your roots of merit planted, such that you possess such a perfection of karmic fruition?"

He said: "I remember, noble son, that in the past, beyond even more than Buddha-field-atom-dust-like eons, in a world-system called Cakravicitra, a Tathāgata named Anantaraśmidharmadhātusamalaṃkṛtadharmarāja appeared in the world."

He was one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. Furthermore, that Tathāgata, together with a hundred koṭis of śrāvakas headed by Jñānavairocana and a hundred thousand koṭis of bodhisattvas headed by Jñānasūryatejas, entered the great garden grounds of Maṇidhvajavyūharāja.

I was invited by King Dharmeśvararāja. When that Tathāgata had entered the city and was in the midst of the marketplace, I caused the sound of musical instruments to be played and offered one ball of incense as an act of worship for that Blessed One, together with his assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas.
When that ball of incense was burned, for seven days all of Jambudvīpa was covered by clouds of incense-mists of infinite colors, resembling the bodies of all sentient beings.
And from those very clouds of incense-mists, such a sound issued forth: "The Tathāgata is endowed with an immeasurable, vast aggregate [of merit] throughout the three times;
he is omniscient, free from all obscurations, and has abandoned all afflictions along with their habitual tendencies."
"This offering is planted by all the Tathāgatas;

it bestows the fruit of immeasurable omniscience and culminates in omniscience"— this is what this sound, of such a nature, issued forth from those clouds of incense-masses through the empowerment of the Buddhas, for the sake of ripening our roots of virtue and for the sake of generating the force of the roots of virtue of inconceivable beings.
And that root of merit, noble son, consisting of the Tathāgata’s empowerment and the miracle of manifestation, was dedicated by me toward three aims.
Toward which three? Namely:
for the total eradication of all poverty; for never being deprived of hearing the true Dharma; and for the complete fulfillment of seeing all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends.
Noble son, this is the extent of my knowledge regarding this bodhisattva liberation called "The Array of the Unobstructed Circle of Vows.
How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the qualities of bodhisattvas who are mines of inconceivable and immeasurable jewels of virtue?
Those who have entered the ocean of the Buddha’s indivisible body; those who receive the rainclouds of the indivisible Dharma;
and those who have set out upon the ocean of indivisible qualities.
Those who have spread throughout the net of the conduct of Samantabhadra;

those who have entered the domain of unadulterated samādhis; those whose roots of goodness are a single, solid mass with all bodhisattvas without distinction; and those who dwell in the non-conceptual state of the Tathāgatas without distinction.

Those who have entered the undifferentiated equality of the three times; those who are untiring in dwelling through all unadulterated eons; those who are established on the ground that is the range of the undifferentiated universal eye.
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region is a district named Vetravatyā.
There, in the city of Samantamukha, there dwells a merchant-chief of perfumes named Samantanetra.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the Dharma-merchant Ratnacūḍa, circumambulated the Dharma-merchant Ratnacūḍa hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at him again and again,
departed from the presence of the Dharma-merchant Ratnacūḍa. 16.
Samantanetra.
Then, indeed, Sudhana the merchant’s son, having entered into the vision of infinite Buddhas and attained association with infinite Bodhisattvas, [proceeded].
Illumined by the method of the infinite path of the bodhisattvas, his mind was made certain by being moistened with the method of the infinite dharmas of the bodhisattvas;
he attained purification through the path of infinite resolve for the bodhisattvas, acquired the radiance of the infinite faculties of the bodhisattvas,

was established in the power of the infinite intentions of the bodhisattvas, possessed a mind following the infinite conduct of the bodhisattvas, and was born from the power of the infinite vows of the bodhisattvas.

The Bodhisattva Anantabodhisattvāparājitadhvaja, who dwells in the light of the wisdom of infinite bodhisattvas, who has attained the illumination of the Dharma of infinite bodhisattvas, proceeded by stages toward the region named Vetravāmūlaka; searching for the city of Samantamukha in every direction, intermediate point, district, and locality— whether low, high, level, or uneven— he went on without weariness of purpose and without resting.

With a mind of equanimity, with irreversible vigor, with an inexhaustible consciousness, never forgetting the instructions of the spiritual friends, with the habitual tendencies of the heart always engaged in the service of spiritual friends,
with faculties that perceive through universal gates, free from all negligence, and with ears and eyes wide open, he searched everywhere and beheld the city of Samantamukha.
In the center of the district of Vetramūla, amidst ten thousand towns, he saw a well-established market town with firm walls, lofty ramparts, and adorned with eight crossroads.
In its center, on the street of perfumers, he saw the perfumer Samantanetra seated there.
Having seen him, he approached the perfumer Samantanetra, bowed his head at his feet, and standing before him with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus:
I have generated the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it.
He said: "Excellent, excellent, noble son! It is well that you have resolved your mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Noble son, I know the diseases of all sentient beings, even those arising from wind."
Those arising from bile, those arising from phlegm,
and those agitated by their own kind.
Even those who have been attacked by others,
even those afflicted by non-human beings,
and even those who have encountered dangerous attacks from others.
Even those arising from the application of various mantras, weapons, and vetālas, or from the ignition of fire, or from the agitation of water,
or from the occurrence of various fears and terrors;
And I understand the pacification of all those diseases; that is to say, I understand oleation, emesis, purgation, non-unctuous enemas, bloodletting, nasal therapy, ear-drops, fomentation, ointments,
the counteracting of poisons, the warding off of spirits and seizures, nourishing treatments, bathing, fumigation, growth-promotion, and the purification of the complexion.
I know how to generate strength for those beings,
O son of good family,
who approach me from the ten directions.
I pacify all those diseases for them;

having had their bodies well-bathed and anointed, their limbs adorned with appropriate ornaments, and their bodies clothed in suitable garments, and having satisfied them with various foods of the finest flavors,
I make them possessed of immeasurable wealth and prosperity.
Furthermore, for those who are dominated by attachment, I teach the Dharma for the abandonment of attachment by means of the application of the contemplation of the foul;
for the abandonment of hatred, I teach the Dharma by means of the praise of great loving-kindness;
and for the abandonment of delusion, I teach the Dharma by means of demonstrating the distinctions of the discernment of phenomena.

I teach the Dharma for the sake of abandoning the afflictions associated with the practice of equal portions. By means of elucidating the gateway of specific thorough knowledge, I illuminate the cause for the arising of the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*).
By means of elucidating discourses associated with all the qualities and dharmas of the Buddhas, I illuminate the cause for the arising of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*).

By revealing the suffering of immeasurable saṃsāra, I illuminate the cause for the arising of the attainment of boundless qualities. By praising the accumulation of the vast provisions of merit and wisdom, I illuminate the cause for the arising of the aspiration for the Mahāyāna.
By demonstrating the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings, I illuminate the cause for the arising of the attainment of the conduct of the Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

I elucidate the cause for the arising of the attainment of a Buddha-body adorned with the primary and secondary marks, by means of entering into the expansion of the web of conduct through dwelling in all fields and throughout all eons.
I elucidate the cause for the arising of the attainment of the Tathāgata’s universal purity, by means of praising the perfection of generosity.
By elucidating the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), I reveal the cause for the arising of the inconceivable purity of the Tathāgata’s form and color.

By elucidating the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*), I reveal the cause for the arising of the body of the Tathāgata Duryodhana. By elucidating the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*), I reveal the purity of the physical existence (*ātmabhāva*) of the Tathāgata Abhibhūtānabhibhūta.
By elucidating the perfection of meditative concentration, I illuminate the purity of the Dharma-body;
by elucidating the perfection of wisdom, I illuminate the purity of the Buddha-body that appears before all worlds;
by elucidating the perfection of skillful means, I illuminate the purity of the body that causes the minds of all beings throughout the ages of all kalpas to enter into awakening.

By means of elucidating the perfection of aspiration, I illuminate the purity of a physical form that transcends all buddha-fields; by means of elucidating the perfection of power, I illuminate the purity of a body that satisfies the intentions of the entire world according to their inclinations;
and by means of elucidating the perfection of wisdom, I illuminate the purity of a body whose appearance is supremely auspicious.
That is to say, by means of proclaiming the turning away from all unwholesome states;
and having thus gathered them through the gift of Dharma and supported them with an accumulation of infinite wealth and jewels, I dismiss them.
Furthermore, noble son, I also know the methods for all fragrant incenses, perfumes, scents, and ointments, namely those headed by the King of Incomparable Fragrance.
headed by Sindhuvārita-gandharāja, headed by Ajitāvati-gandharāja, headed by Vibodhana-gandharāja, headed by Aruṇāvati-gandharāja,
headed by Kālānusārin-gandharāja, headed by Uragasāra-candana-gandharāja, and headed by Meghāguru-gandharāja.
I know all methods of incense, headed by the Gandharāja Akṣobhyendriya.

Furthermore, noble son, I know the "Incense Image" that brings satisfaction to all sentient beings and provides the means for seeing, honoring, and attending upon the Buddhas through universal gateways.
Moreover, noble son,

because I satisfy all sentient beings, and because from the fragrant image of the universal gate that beholds and makes offerings to the Buddhas, all my intentions are fulfilled, by which I sustain clouds of ornaments for the protection of all sentient beings.

That is to say, noble son, I empower clouds of fragrant palaces and ornaments, up to clouds of ornaments for the worship and service of the Tathāgatas in all their aspects. Whenever I desire to worship the Tathāgatas,
then from this "Fragrant Image" which satisfies all sentient beings and provides the vision, worship, and service of the Buddhas through universal gates, I manifest immeasurable [clouds].

Having issued forth clouds of fragrant casket-pavilions, I empower the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with the adornment of clouds of all fragrant casket-pavilions in all the circles of assemblies of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions;
[I empower it] with the adornment of clouds for the purification of all Buddha-fields, the adornment of clouds of fragrance-abodes, and the adornment of clouds of fragrance-walls.

an array adorned with clouds of fragrant incense-pavilions, an array adorned with clouds of fragrant archways, an array adorned with clouds of fragrant latticed windows, an array adorned with clouds of fragrant turrets, an array adorned with clouds of fragrant crescent moons,

an array adorned with clouds of fragrant parasols, an array adorned with clouds of raised fragrant banners, an array adorned with clouds of fragrant pennants, and an array adorned with clouds of fragrant canopies.

I empower this entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) with the adornment of clouds of fragrant bodies and nets, the adornment of clouds of fragrant radiance, the adornment of clouds of pure arrays of fragrant illumination, and the adornment of raining down clouds of every fragrance.
Noble son, I know this Dharma-door called the "Fragrant Image" which satisfies all sentient beings and provides the worship and service of beholding the Buddhas through universal gateways.

How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the virtues of those Bodhisattvas who are like the King of Medicine, whose sight is never in vain, whose hearing is never in vain, whose dwelling together is never in vain, whose remembrance is never in vain, whose following of their vows is never in vain, and whose names, when grasped, are never in vain— by the mere sight of whom all the afflictions of all sentient beings are pacified?

By the mere sight of whom beings turn back from all states of woe; by the mere sight of whom beings find scope within the Buddha-dharmas; by the mere sight of whom the entire mass of suffering of sentient beings is stilled.
Upon seeing whom beings become free from fear of all the realms of cyclic existence;
upon seeing whom beings attain fearlessness by being led toward omniscience and its qualities;
upon seeing whom beings do not fall into the abysses of old age and death—
Upon merely seeing them, sentient beings obtain the bliss of nirvana by abiding in the equality of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region there is a city named Tāladhvaja.
There dwells a king named Anala.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the perfumer-merchant Samantanetra, circumambulated the perfumer-merchant Samantanetra hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at him again and again,
departed from the presence of the perfumer-merchant Samantanetra. 17.
Anala.
Then, indeed, Sudhana, the merchant’s son, recollecting that succession of spiritual friends, [proceeded].
Attending to those gateways of the instructions of the spiritual friends,

gladdening his own mind by thinking, "I am sustained by the spiritual friends," and reflecting, "I am protected by the spiritual friends; I shall no longer turn back from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment," he attained joy of heart.
Clarity of mind, joy of mind, contentment of mind, rapture of mind, delight of mind, tranquility of mind,

vastness of mind, adornment of mind, non-attachment of mind, non-obstruction of mind, seclusion of mind, convergence of mind, mastery of mind, sovereignty of mind, conformity of mind to the Dharma, pervasion of the field of the mind, and a mind adorned by the vision of the Buddhas.
He attained a state of mind that was never separated from the mental attention to the Ten Powers.
Traveling by stages from country to country, village to village, and region to region, he arrived at the city of Tāladhvaja and inquired: "Where is King Anala?"
Another group of people said this to him: "Noble son, this King Anala is seated upon the lion throne in the hall of justice, performing royal duties;
he governs the provinces and punishes those who deserve punishment."
He restrains those who should be restrained; he inflicts punishment upon those who have committed offenses;
and he settles the disputes of those who are quarreling.
He consoles the distressed,
subdues the arrogant,
and turns others away from the slaughter of living beings.
He turns him away from taking what is not given;
he pacifies his longing for that which is possessed by others;
and he restrains him from false speech.
He causes them to abstain from divisive speech; he causes them to desist from harsh speech;
and he turns them away from idle chatter.
It causes one to be separated from covetousness, distances one from ill-will, and disjoins one from false view.
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, approached King Anala.

He beheld King Anala seated upon a throne with feet made of countless varieties of radiant jewels, variegated with *nārāyaṇa-vajra* gems; its surface was beautiful with ornaments exquisitely fashioned from many jewels, and it was perfectly finished, white with a network of golden threads.
It was illuminated by lamps of many mani-jewels;

its interior was composed of lotuses made of the *vaśirāja* mani-king jewel; it was well-adorned with many divine garments of precious gems; it was graced with offerings of various divine fragrances and incense; it was resplendent with hundreds of thousands of raised jeweled banners and parasols; and it was beautified by hundreds of thousands of jeweled pennants hanging down.
He was seated upon a great lion-throne made of jewels, blazing with clusters of garlands of various precious gems hanging down from it and spread over by a canopy of diverse divine jewels;
he was youthful, young, handsome, pleasing, beautiful to behold, with hair that was deep blue, curling to the right, and shaped like a parasol,
his head crowned with a *uṣṇīṣa*, a broad forehead, eyes with wide, deep-blue lashes like those of a cow, and a sweet, prominent, beautiful, and high bridge to his nose.

His lips were beautifully joined like vermilion and gold; his forty teeth were perfectly aligned, white, and complete; he had a jaw like that of a lion and full, well-developed cheeks. His eyebrows were as long and beautiful as a bow, and his forehead was adorned with a mark made by a tuft of hair as white as the moon. His ears were long, hanging down, and released [from the head], and his face was as gentle as the full moon. His neck was rounded and beautiful like a conch shell, his chest was adorned with the Śrīvatsa, and the upper half of his body was like that of a lion.
With shoulders as broad as the back of a lion, well-rounded thighs and shoulders, long arms, fingers joined by a web, and hands and feet marked with wheels;

with soft, youthful, and well-developed palms and soles; possessing the seven protuberances, a waist like a diamond, large and straight limbs, well-rounded thighs, the private organ withdrawn into a sheath, shanks like those of an antelope, long fingers, long heels, a fathom-wide aura, golden skin, and body hairs that grow singly, upward, and curl to the right.
His body was perfectly proportioned like a royal nyagrodha tree, adorned with the primary marks and secondary signs; his head was crowned with a tiara of wish-fulfilling king-jewels,

his forehead was decorated with crescent-shaped ornaments of Jāmbūnada gold, his ears were graced by long-hanging earrings of pure sapphire, and his broad, expansive, and pure chest was illuminated by the radiance of necklaces of priceless jewels and gems.

His arms displayed graceful movements, adorned with celestial and supreme jeweled armlets and bracelets; they were covered by a canopy of Jāmbūnada gold, finely divided by hundreds of rods of the ten precious gems,
containing a most pure core of great Jyotīrasa jewels, emitting a charming and sweet sound from garlands of jeweled bells,
and attaining the radiance of great maṇi-jewels in all directions.

He saw him being held over with a great jeweled parasol having a handle made of pure lapis lazuli gems; he had attained the sovereignty of a great king, his rule was unimpeded by foreign powers, and he possessed the majesty of one free from fear of enemy armies.
Surrounding him, ten thousand ministers had gathered and were seated, engaged in royal affairs.
And ten thousand men, resembling hell-wardens and like the servants of Yama, stood arrayed before him;
they bore deformed feet, were fierce, distorted, and inspiring of terror, with blood-red eyes, their lips bitten and faces contorted with three-fold frowns;
they held weapons such as swords, axes, spears, javelins, *bhuśuṇḍi*-missiles, and tridents, and their faces and bodies were uneven, deformed, and ill-proportioned.

He saw [them] cloud-colored, with terrifying forms and the roar of fierce voices, possessing a brilliance difficult to behold, causing great fear, generating terror in the hearts of hundreds of thousands of living beings, and intent upon the restraint and subjugation of those beings who were to be restrained;
there he saw many hundreds of thousands of living beings, thieves who seized the property of others and plundered the enjoyments of other beings.

Those who rob travelers, those who burn villages, towns, cities, and market-towns, those who destroy families, those who break into houses, those who commit crimes, those who administer poison, those who cause riots, those who kill human beings, those who violate the wives of others, those who have entered upon wrong paths, those with wicked minds, those who are covetous, those who perform various evil and cruel deeds— all of these were bound with tight fivefold bonds.
He saw those being led into the presence of King Anala;
he observed King Anala inflicting upon them punishments appropriate to their offenses—
by his command, some having their hands and feet cut off, while others had their ears and noses severed.

He saw some having their eyes plucked out, some having their limbs, minor members, and heads cut off, some with their entire bodies set ablaze by fire, and others whose bodies were being drenched with severed, mutilated, and heated alkaline water; thus he saw them undergoing various kinds of intense, harsh, bitter, unpleasant, and life-destroying tortures.
And in that place of execution, he saw heaps of hands, feet, eyes, ears, noses, heads, limbs, and minor members, each as large as a mountain.
He beheld a lake of blood, three yojanas deep and many yojanas in length and breadth.

And there he saw hundreds of thousands of corpses, their limbs, minor members, and heads dismembered, strewn about and being devoured by wolves, jackals, dogs, crows, vultures, hawks, kuraras, and terrifying ravens.
He saw some that were blue and blue-colored, festering, bloated, and torn apart— extremely distorted and loathsome.
