And this noble son, the bodhisattva practice gateway of the uninterrupted entrance of great compassion is engaged in the ripening and disciplining of beings throughout the entire world without distinction; it is the service that attends to the gathering and disciplining of beings through the communication of streams from all directions.
Thus, noble son, established in the bodhisattva practice of the unimpeded entrance of great compassion, I do not waver from the presence of the feet of all the Tathāgatas,
yet I remain present before the needs of all sentient beings;
I also gather sentient beings through generosity.
I gather sentient beings through pleasant speech, purposeful action, and consistency between words and deeds;
I also bring sentient beings to maturity by manifesting the form-body (*rūpakāya*).
By means of the purity of displaying forms with inconceivable color and shape, and by emitting a network of light rays, I gladden and bring sentient beings to maturity.

I gather and bring to maturity sentient beings by uttering sounds according to their inclinations, by manifesting modes of conduct according to their preferences, by teaching the Dharma in accordance with their various dispositions, by means of various miraculous transformations, by stimulating the minds of sentient beings engaged in the accumulation of wholesome qualities, by manifesting immeasurable and diverse emanations suited to their inclinations, by appearing in forms similar to those of sentient beings born into various classes of existence, and even by dwelling together in a single residence.

By means of this, noble son, while purifying this entrance to the bodhisattva practice called "The Unhesitating Entrance of Great Compassion," I have generated the vow to be a refuge for the entire world;

that is to say, for the sake of removing the fear of falling into the abyss for all beings, for the sake of pacifying the fear of terror for all beings, for the sake of turning back the fear of delusion for all beings,
for the sake of completely cutting off the fear of bondage for all beings, and for the sake of averting the fear of attempts to deprive all beings of life.

In order to remove the fear of all sentient beings regarding a deficiency of necessities; to pacify the fear for their livelihood; to cause all sentient beings to transcend the fear of ill repute; to pacify the fear of cyclic existence for all sentient beings; to bring about the disappearance of the fear of timidity in assemblies for all sentient beings;

to cause all sentient beings to pass beyond the fear of death; to turn back the fear of miserable rebirths for all sentient beings; and to provide illumination so that all sentient beings do not regress on their path through the darkness of ignorance and treacherous destinies.
For the sake of the absolute removal of the fear of encountering what is disagreeable to all sentient beings; for the cessation of the fear of separation from what is dear to all sentient beings;

for the dispelling of the fear of dwelling with what is unpleasant to all sentient beings; for the prevention of the fear of being joined with bodily affliction for all sentient beings; for the liberation from the fear of mental affliction for all sentient beings; and for the complete transcendence of suffering, dejection, and despair for all sentient beings.
I have accomplished the vow to be a refuge for the entire world. And the gateway of my mindfulness has been established throughout all worlds to pacify the fears of all sentient beings.
My wheel of my own name has been made known throughout all worlds so that all sentient beings may be free from fear.
The tranquility that consists of the infinite variety of forms of all living beings is established within my body, so as to perceive each being according to the appropriate time.

Therefore, noble son, by this means I liberate sentient beings from all fears, cause them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and make them irreversible for the attainment of the Buddha-dharmas.
Noble son, I have attained this entrance into the bodhisattva practice called "Unhesitating Entry into Great Compassion.
How could I possibly [describe] the bodhisattvas Samantabhadra, who are purified by the mandala of the vows of all Buddhas?

They have reached the course of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; they possess an uninterrupted stream of the formation of wholesome dharmas; their ears are always concentrated upon the meditative absorptions of all bodhisattvas; they possess a stream that never turns back from the practice of dwelling together with all beings throughout all eons; their stream follows the path of all times and vehicles; they are skilled in the stream of the revolutions and cycles of all world-systems; and their stream brings about the pacification of the unwholesome minds of all sentient beings.

To know the conduct or to speak of the virtues of those who are streams that increase the roots of goodness in the minds of all sentient beings, and streams that cause all sentient beings to turn back from the stream of saṃsāra.
In this regard, it is said: Having performed circumambulations and praised him with reverence, Sudhana, well-restrained, departed for the Southern Path.
There he beheld the seer Avalokiteśvara, who dwells in compassion, situated within a cave on a mountain of jewels. // 1 //

Seated upon a lion throne adorned with jewels and gems on a mountain slope made of diamond, the steadfast one, Padmagarbha, surrounded by gods, asuras, nagas, kinnaras, and rakshasas, as well as by the sons of the Jina, teaches them the Dharma. //2//
Upon seeing him, incomparable joy arose within Sudhana; approaching, he bowed at the feet of that ocean of virtues and said:
"Noble one, having conceived compassion for me, please grant me the instruction so that I may attain this *Bhadracaryā*. (3)

Bowing his head to the stainless arm, which was adorned with a hundred merits and emitted a vast, auspicious cloud-net of light, the pure being Avalokiteśvara stood upon the crown of Sudhana’s head and spoke these words: 4. Bowing to the stainless arm, variegated with a hundred merits and emitting a vast, auspicious cloud-net of light, the wise and pure being Avalokiteśvara, standing upon the crown of Sudhana’s head, spoke these words.
O Son of the Buddha, I know one gateway to liberation: the womb of the dense wisdom of compassion of all Victors.
It has arisen for the sake of gathering and protecting all the world; yet even so, self-love still persists everywhere within me. (5)

I rescue all people from manifold calamities—those who have fallen into deep bonds, those seized by enemies, those pierced in their limbs, and likewise those confined in prisons; having heard my name, those held in bondage are set free. (6)
Those who have committed offenses against kings and are condemned to death, or those cast down by arrows that do not penetrate their bodies,
or those whose limbs are being cut by sharp-edged weapons as they revolve— all these are safe if they there remember my name. (7)
Those kings who are caught in the midst of disputes and have fallen into contention shall conquer all their enemies and then obtain prosperity;
they shall increase in fame, and their wealth and kinsmen shall become invincible by remembering my name. (8)

Those who remember my name, having conquered all enemies, go forth without fear from the dangers of thieves, the dangers of foes, and the entry into wildernesses teeming with lions, tigers, leopards, yak-oxen, and predatory beasts. (9)

Even those with malicious minds who, for the sake of killing, hurl blazing lumps of charcoal from the mountain slopes, or who cast lotus sprouts into the ocean or into fire—whosoever remembers my name, [for them these things become] like [cool] water. (10)
Even if cast into the waters of the ocean, they do not die; there, in a river, they are not swept away, nor are they burned in the midst of fire.
No misfortunes whatsoever shall occur, and there will be the accomplishment of all goals, simply by recollecting my name for even a moment. (11)
Whether they face punishment by fetters, imprisonment, shackles, or likewise unjust penalties, humiliation, and contempt;
or if they encounter being pinned down, verbal abuse, beating, threats, and intimidation—by remembering my name, they obtain liberation. (12)

Those who are enemies, seeking out faults and weaknesses, and those with constantly malicious minds, as well as those who speak ill of me—upon merely seeing them, they will become friendly-minded; having heard my praise and remembered my name, this shall come to pass. (13)

Even when vetāla-mantras and kakhordas are constantly employed for the purpose of killing them, their enemies become paralyzed; no poisons whatsoever will take effect upon the bodies of those who remember any of my names. (14)
By the lords of nāgas, hosts of rākṣasas, garuḍas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and pūtanas with fierce minds intent on mockery;
by those who steal vitality and cause terror—even in the midst of dreams—all are pacified once they have recollected my name. (15)

By following my name for even a moment, there shall be no separation from mother, father, friends, kinsmen, or relatives, nor any union with the unpleasant; there shall be no loss of wealth, nor shall one fall into poverty. (16)

And having passed away from here, that pure being who remembers even my name does not go to the Avīci hell, nor to the animal realm, nor to the hungry ghosts, nor to the inopportune states; he is reborn among gods and humans. (17)
They shall not be blind, nor one-eyed, nor deaf; nor shall they have mottled limbs, nor be fierce, nor lame.
Furthermore, they shall be lovely to behold, with all their faculties unimpaired, for many millions of eons, by having remembered my name. (18)

Those who cry out "Avalokiteśvara! shall go to my happy realm; whoever scatters a handful of flowers over my body, whoever offers incense and burns it, and whoever gives an umbrella, performing extensive worship with a serene mind in my Buddha-field, he too shall become one worthy of offerings. (19)
Having passed away from here, that pure being is reborn in the presence of the Buddhas throughout the world-systems of the ten directions;
he beholds those Buddhas and hears their Dharma, provided they are some who remember my name. (20)
These and others cannot be exhausted or measured as long as I remain in the world to train sentient beings.
My sons of the Buddha, I have cultivated but a single liberation; I do not know all the qualities of those who possess such qualities. (21)
The world-system in the ten directions has been made like a checkerboard by Sudhana, who has attended upon spiritual friends;
yet he is not satiated by hearing the Dharma from the sons of the Conquerors—how could there not be joy in hearing the Dharma? (22)

Then, at that time, a bodhisattva named Ananyagāmī, having arrived through the expanse of the sky from the eastern direction, alighted upon the summit of the Cakravāla mountain range of this Sahā world-system.
As soon as the bodhisattva Ananyagāmī set his feet upon the summit of the Cakravāla mountain range of the Sahā world-system,
at that very moment, this Sahā world-system shook in six ways.

And it became established as consisting of many jewels. And from the body of the Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin, such a radiance was emitted that by that radiance all the light of the suns and moons was eclipsed.

The radiance of all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, and the world-protectors, as well as the light of fire, jewels, and celestial bodies, was eclipsed; all the great hells were illuminated, and the dense thickets of the realms of animals, the world of Yama, and the various destinies were illuminated.
Immediately thereafter, all the sufferings of the miserable realms were pacified;
the afflictions of all sentient beings no longer caused them harm,
and the various pains of grief and mental thorns subsided.

And this entire buddha-field, raining down clouds of all kinds of jewels, raining down clouds of every kind of offering— consisting of arrays of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags— approached the Blessed One. And his physical form appeared within the dwellings of all sentient beings, manifesting itself before them to satisfy them according to their inclinations.
And on that Mount Potalaka, he was seen approaching the presence of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Then the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Noble son, do you see the Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin here in this assembly circle?
He replied, "I see him, Noble One.
He said, "Noble son, approach this Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin and ask him: 'How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?'"
How should one practice?
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
circumambulated the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. // 28 //
(31) Ananyagāmī.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana had his mind attained to the verses of wisdom of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

Unsatiated by the sight of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and unable to restrain his speech, he approached the Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin; having bowed his head at the feet of the Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin and standing before him with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus: "Noble One, I have generated the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it.
I have heard, however, that the Noble One gives instruction and advice to bodhisattvas.
May the Noble One tell me this: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, and how should he practice?
He said, "Noble son, I am a possessor of the bodhisattva liberation called 'Issuing from All Gates.
He asked, 'Venerable sir, at the feet of which Tathāgata did you obtain this bodhisattva liberation called 'Issuing from All Gates'?
And how far away from here is that world-system?"
"How long has it been since you departed from that world-system?

He replied, "Noble son, this matter is difficult for the world—including its gods, humans, and asuras, and including the community of śramaṇas and brahmins—to comprehend: namely, the prowess of a bodhisattva, the irreversibility of a bodhisattva’s vigor, and the invincibility of a bodhisattva’s vigor."

"Noble son, it is not possible for those who are not sustained by spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), who are not attended by the Buddhas, who have not accumulated roots of merit (*kuśalamūla*), whose intentions are not purified, who have not attained the faculties of a bodhisattva,
and who are devoid of the eye of wisdom (*prajñācakṣus*)— to hear this, or to retain it, or to have faith in it, or to enter into it. He said, "May the Noble One speak to me."
"I shall resolve with conviction and have faith through the power of the Buddha and by being sustained by a spiritual friend.
He said, "Noble son, I come from the eastern direction, from the world-system called Śrīgarbhavatī, the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Samantaśrīsaṃbhava.
Noble son, at the feet of that Tathāgata Samantaśrīsaṃbhava, I attained this bodhisattva liberation called 'Emerging from All Gates' (Samantamukhanirjavana)."
Then, noble son, as I set out from the world-system Śrīgarbhavatī, incalculably incalculable eons, equal to the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields, have passed away.
With each single arising of thought, I transcend expressions of speech equal to the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields;
and with each single expression of speech, I traverse Buddha-fields equal to the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields.
And all those buddha-fields are never devoid of Tathāgatas;

I enter into all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and with a supreme, mind-made worship— sealed with the seal of the unconditioned realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), authorized by the Tathāgatas, and generating great joy in all bodhisattvas— I pay homage to the Tathāgata.
And as many oceans of sentient beings as I behold in those world-systems,
I enter into all their oceans of mind; having fully understood the wheel of faculties of them all, I manifest a form-body according to their inclinations and resolute convictions.
I proclaim the sound of the Dharma; I emit a circle of light;
I provide an abundance of various requisites.
I empower my own body for them,
that is to say, so that their application toward ripening and disciplining [beings] shall never cease;
and just as I emerge from the eastern direction, [so do I emerge from all other directions].
In this way, I set out toward the southern direction, the western, the northern, the northeastern, the southeastern, the southwestern, the northwestern, the downward, and the upward directions.
Noble son, this is the bodhisattva liberation called "Rushing Forth through All Gateways" that I know.

What could I possibly say of the bodhisattvas who have reached everywhere, who face the direction of equanimity, whose range of knowledge is undifferentiated, whose bodies are well-distributed throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), who move in accordance with the inclinations and aspirations of all sentient beings, and whose bodies pervade all buddha-fields?

To know the conduct or to speak of the virtues of those who have followed all phenomena as they truly are, who have attained the equality of the paths of the three times, who follow the equality of the paths of all directions, who illuminate the paths of all worlds, who are free from conceptualization regarding the path of the Tathāgatas, who have followed all paths without attachment, and who are established in the path that is without abode.
Go, son of good family,
right here in the southern region there is a city named Dvāravatī;
there dwells the deity Mahādeva.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one practice?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin, circumambulated the Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of the Bodhisattva Ananyagāmin. // 29 //
(Gv 167) 32. Mahādeva.
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, his mind following the vast conduct of a bodhisattva and intent on nothing else, [proceeded].

Desiring the sphere of knowledge of the bodhisattva, beholding the excellence of qualities in the domain of the accomplishment of the great superknowledges, having attained the joy of donning the armor of firm vigor, his intention following the play of inconceivable liberations, he was proceeding upon the stage of bodhisattva qualities, investigating the stage of meditative concentration, establishing himself on the stage of mnemonic formulas, and entering the stage of aspirational prayers.
Training himself on the stage of analytical knowledge (*pratisaṃvid-bhūmi*) and bringing the stage of power (*bala-bhūmi*) to completion, he proceeded by stages toward the city of Dvāravatī.
Upon arriving there, he inquired about Mahādeva.
A great multitude of people informed him: "Noble son, this Mahādeva is teaching the Dharma to sentient beings with a coarse physical form at the crossroads in the temple of the city."

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, approached Mahādeva, bowed his head at Mahādeva’s feet, and standing before him with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus: "Noble one, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva."
"How should I practice? I have heard, Noble One, that you give instruction and counsel to the bodhisattvas;
therefore, may the Noble One tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?

Then the god Mahādeva, extending his four arms toward the four directions, brought water from the four great oceans with supreme swiftness; having washed his own face and scattered golden flowers over the merchant’s son Sudhana, he spoke thus:
"Noble son, it is indeed very difficult to behold Bodhisattvas."
Extremely rare to hear, appearing as wonders in the world due to their preeminence, they are the supreme lotuses among men, protectors of the world,
the refuge of the world,
and the foundation of the universe.
They are great illuminators for sentient beings,
guides who show the path of safety to those who have lost their way, and leaders for the purpose of introducing them to the methods of the Dharma.
They act as guides for the purpose of leading one to the city of omniscience.

Regarding this, noble son, it occurred to me: "The name 'Destroyer of False Views' belongs to the bodhisattvas; by means of it, they reveal their own bodily reflections to those whose minds are stainless, and they appear before those whose physical actions are purified."
They cause the light of Sarasvatī to descend upon those who are free from faults of speech;
they remain ever present before those whose intentions are pure.
Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called the Cloud Net.
He asked, "Noble one, what is the scope of this Bodhisattva liberation called 'The Cloud-Net'?
Then the god Mahādeva, standing before the merchant's son Sudhana, manifested a heap of gold as large as a great mountain,
as well as heaps of silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, musāragalva, emerald, and heaps of *jyotīrasa* jewel-gems.

A heap of vimalagarbha jewel-gems, a heap of vairocana jewel-gems, a heap of jewel-gems facing all directions, a heap of crest-jewel gems for crowns, a heap of various jewel-gems, a heap of armlets, a heap of earrings and ornaments, a heap of bracelets, a heap of waist-bands, a heap of anklets, a heap of various jewel-gems, and a heap of ornaments for all the major and minor limbs.
A heap of wish-fulfilling king-jewels, all flowers, all perfumes, all incenses, all garlands,
all ointments, all powders, all garments, all parasols, all banners, all flags, all musical instruments, all dancers, and all objects of desire.

Having displayed hundreds of thousands of millions of incalculable maidens, she said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Come, noble son; take these and give gifts, perform meritorious deeds, and make offerings to the Tathāgatas."
Having gathered sentient beings through the means of attraction that is generosity, enjoin them to the perfection of relinquishment;
teach the world through giving; and demonstrate the nature of renouncing what is difficult to give up.
Just as I, noble son, provide for you the necessary means, so too do I bring about a continuum perfumed by renunciation in immeasurable beings whose intentions toward giving have ceased;
having caused them to plant roots of merit in the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and in the spiritual friends who are bodhisattvas, I establish them in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Furthermore, noble son, for those beings who are intoxicated by the pleasures of desire and greedy for the enjoyment of sense objects, I manifest those very sense objects as impure.

For those possessed by anger, filled with pride, intoxication, arrogance, and conceit, and who are to be disciplined through conflict, I manifest infinite bodies that are fierce, like rākṣasas, deformed and terrifying, devouring flesh and blood; and by means of these, I cause them to abandon all their stubbornness and agitation.

I rouse lazy beings who have abandoned their practice by showing them the terrors of fire, water, kings, thieves, and calamities, and thereby establish them in the exertion of vigor. Thus, through various such means, I turn them away from all unwholesome conduct and establish them in the practice of all wholesome dharmas—

for the destruction of all that is contrary to the perfections, for the accumulation of the equipment of all the perfections, for the transcending of the precipitous path of the mountains of all obscurations, and for the entry into the unobscured Dharma.
Noble son, this is the bodhisattva liberation called "Cloud Net" that I know.

But what could I possibly know of the bodhisattvas who are like Indras, crushing the asuras of the afflictions; or those who are like waters, extinguishing the mass of fire-flames of suffering for all the world?

To know the conduct or to describe the virtues of those who are like masses of fire for drying up the waters of craving of the entire world, who are like winds for scattering the mountains of all grasping and attachment, and who are like vajras for shattering the mountain of the firm notion of self— [this is impossible].
Go, son of good family!

Right here in Jambudvīpa, in the region of Magadha, at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), there dwells a goddess of the earth named Sthāvarā. Approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?

Then Sudhana, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of the god Mahādeva, circumambulated the god Mahādeva hundreds of thousands of times, and after looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of the god Mahādeva. 30.
(Gv 169) 33. Sthāvarā.
Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son proceeded by stages until he arrived at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) in the kingdom of Magadha, where the earth goddess Sthāvarā resided.
One hundred thousand earth deities addressed one another with these words: "He is coming, he who will become the refuge for all sentient beings;
this very embryo of the Tathāgata is coming."
He who shall shatter the eggshell of ignorance for all sentient beings—
he, born of the lineage of the Dharma King, is coming;
he who shall bind on the unattached, excellent, and stainless crown of the Dharma King.
"This is that hero who wields the weapons of wisdom, Nārāyaṇa, and the vajra; he who shall crush the wheel of all opposing disputants.
Then, those hundred thousand earth-deities, headed by Sthāvarā, caused a great earthquake.
Having produced a sound like the roar of deep thunderclouds and having illuminated the entire trichiliocosm with a magnificent radiance,
their bodies were adorned with ornaments and decorations of every kind of jewel; they hung in the expanse of the sky like clusters of lightning flashes,
while all the sprouts of every tree began to grow.
With all the flowering trees in full bloom,
all the river currents raining down, and all the springs, lakes, ponds, and reservoirs rising up;
with great rains of fragrant water falling down,
with great winds blowing that carried forth heaps of masses of flowers,
and with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of musical instruments being played;
With divine celestial chariots, ornaments, and crowns spreading forth;
with bellowing bulls, elephants, tigers, and lions;
and with roaring lords of the gods, asuras, serpents, and spirits.
Great lords of mountains, clashing and leaping up,
and hundreds of thousands of millions of heaps of treasures rising upward from the surface of the earth.
Then the earth goddess Sthāvarā said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Welcome to you, noble son!
This is that very spot of earth where, while standing, you planted roots of merit, and where I am present before your eyes.
Do you wish to see a portion of the fruit of that maturation?"

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the earth goddess Sthāvarā and having circumambulated the earth goddess Sthāvarā hundreds of thousands of times, stood before the earth goddess Sthāvarā with palms joined in reverence and said this: "I desire [to hear], Noble Lady."
Then the earth goddess Sthāvarā, having struck the great earth with her two soles and revealed it as adorned by hundreds of thousands of millions of incalculable treasures of precious jewels,
spoke thus: "Noble son, these hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of treasures of precious jewels shall follow you and precede you."
They are for your enjoyment according to your desire;
they have arisen from the ripening of your merit and are protected by the power of your merit.
Having received from them what you require, do that which must be done.
Furthermore, noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called "The Womb Difficult to Conquer through Knowledge.
Endowed with this bodhisattva liberation, I have been constantly following the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara since his appearance, and I am perpetually engaged in his protection.
From that time forth, noble son, I have investigated the mental conduct of the Bodhisattva, plunged into the sphere of his wisdom, and entered the entire mandala of his vows.
I follow the purification of the conduct of a bodhisattva, I pursue the method of all samādhis, and I pervade the vastness of mind of all the supernormal knowledges of a bodhisattva.

The state of sovereign mastery over the powers of all bodhisattvas; the state of being unassailable by any bodhisattva; the state of pervading the entire network of all buddha-fields; the state of receiving the predictions of all Tathāgatas; the state of manifesting complete enlightenment at all times; the method for turning the wheel of all dharmas;
the method of the cloud of Dharma consisting of the proclamation of all sūtras; and the method of the illumination of the great vision of the Dharma.
I follow, uphold, and receive the method of the knowledge for maturing and disciplining all sentient beings, as well as the method for manifesting the miraculous transformations of all Buddhas.

And this Bodhisattva liberation, O son of good family, called the "Womb of Knowledge Difficult to Conquer," was obtained by me from the presence of the Tathāgata Sunetra in the world-system Candradhvajā, during the eon Avabhāsavyūha, more than as many eons ago as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru.

O noble son, as I was taking in, bringing forth, increasing, and expanding this bodhisattva liberation called the "Womb of Knowledge Difficult to Conquer," I remained never separated from the vision of the Tathāgatas until the end of the Fortunate Aeon (*bhadrakalpa*).
And herein, I have pleased Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields.
And I beheld the miraculous manifestation of all those Tathāgatas as they approached the seat of enlightenment;
and I became a witness to the roots of goodness of all those Tathāgatas.
Noble son, this is the bodhisattva liberation called the "Womb of Knowledge Difficult to Conquer" that I know.

What is it possible for me to know of those bodhisattvas who are followed by all the Tathāgatas, who uphold all the teachings of the Buddhas, who have entered the depths of the wisdom of all the Tathāgatas, whose speed is such that they pervade the realm of phenomena in a single moment of thought, whose bodies are equal to the Tathāgatas, whose stainless womb is the intention of all Buddhas, who always manifest the arising of all Buddhas, and who are the undivided messengers of the bodies of all Buddhas?
To understand their conduct or to speak of their virtues.
Go, son of good family; right here in Jambudvīpa, in the region of Magadha, there is a city named Kapilavastu.
There dwells a night goddess named Vāsantī.
Go to her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the earth goddess Sthāvarā, circumambulated the earth goddess Sthāvarā hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at her again and again,
departed from the presence of the earth goddess Sthāvarā.
(Gv 171) 34. Vāsantī.
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, set out for the great city of Kapilavastu, recollecting the instruction of the earth goddess Sthāvarā.
Recalling that liberation of the Bodhisattva which is the womb of Duryodhana,
expanding that cultivation of the Bodhisattva’s samādhi,
and reflecting upon that method of the Bodhisattva’s Dharma.

Contemplating that playful sport of the bodhisattva’s liberation, surveying that subtle beginning of the bodhisattva’s knowledge of liberation, and entering that ocean of the bodhisattva’s knowledge of liberation.
Resolutely believing in that differentiation of the knowledge of the bodhisattva's liberation,
following after that formation of the infinite knowledge of the bodhisattva's liberation,
and plunging into that ocean of the knowledge of the bodhisattva's liberation.

Having circumambulated the great city of Kapilavastu and entered through the eastern city gate, he stood in the center of the city crossroads. Not long after the sun had set, he— having received the instructions of all the bodhisattvas with respectful devotion, thirsting for a vision of the night goddess Vāsantī, his mind certain that spiritual friends would lead him to the attainment of Buddha-knowledge, and empowered by a body within the range of the universal eye of wisdom— remained there.

With a mind directed toward all quarters that seeks the sight of spiritual friends, with a heart characterized by the perception of the womb of knowledge of noble resolve, with the eye of wisdom extended toward all objects of focus, and surveying the ocean of the knowable in all directions with the eye of meditative concentration that follows the pervasive expansion of the ocean of knowledge regarding the methods of the entire realm of phenomena;

With an attentive disposition directed by the expansion of the great eye of wisdom, he beheld the night goddess Vāsantī in the vault of the sky above the great city of Kapilavastu, seated upon a great jeweled lion-throne whose interior was filled with the essence of all excellent fragrant lotuses and which featured a multi-colored, incomparable jeweled gabled chamber; she possessed a body of golden hue, with hair that was deep blue, soft, and thick, and eyes that were deep blue— she was beautiful, serene, and lovely to behold.

Her body was adorned with all manner of ornaments and decorations, and she wore excellent garments of red color. She bore a crown of Brahma’s matted locks embellished with a lunar disc, and her body manifested the appearance of the reflections of all the hosts of stars, planets, constellations, and luminaries.
Furthermore, as many beings as there were in that vast realm of sentient beings who had been liberated by her from the unfortunate states, the calamities, the miserable destinies, and the downfalls—
He also saw those who had entered the pores of her body:
as many as were established in the heavenly world,
and as many as were ripened for the enlightenment of the disciples, the solitary buddhas, and omniscience.
He also saw those who had entered all her pores;
by means of various skillful methods, they were ripened through the manifestation of bodies, the manifestation of forms, and the manifestation of colors—
and he beheld them as well, situated within her pores.

He also heard those very sounds resonating from the pores of her skin— those vocal productions, the articulations of the components of speech, and the various applications of the methods of mantras and the Dharma by which beings had been brought to maturity.
By means of those timely accomplishments; by means of those adaptations to the inclinations and resolute convictions of sentient beings according to their dispositions;

by means of those bodhisattva practices, bodhisattva strides, gateways to the miraculous transformations of bodhisattva samādhis, bodhisattva preeminences, bodhisattva abodes, bodhisattva gazes, bodhisattva surveys, bodhisattva miracles, and the lion’s yawns of the great being-bodhisattvas;
He also knew those playful displays of the bodhisattva-liberations by which sentient beings had been brought to maturity, all of which were contained within the pores of her skin.

Having seen and heard those oceans of methods of the Dharma joined with various skillful means, he was satisfied, uplifted, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and serenity; he prostrated with his entire body before the night goddess Vāsantī, and rising up, he circumambulated the night goddess Vāsantī hundreds of thousands of times. Then, before the night goddess Vāsantī—
Standing before her with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus: "O Goddess, I have indeed resolved my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Beholding all the qualities of a Buddha through the empowerment of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), I make myself dependent upon spiritual friends.
O Goddess, show me the path to omniscience, established upon which a bodhisattva goes forth to the stage of the ten powers."
When this had been said, the night goddess Vāsantī spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!

Since you are thus possessed by the inspiration of the spiritual friend, desirous of hearing the words of the spiritual friend, and practicing according to the instruction of the spiritual friend—it is certain that as you practice the instruction of the spiritual friend, you will draw near to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."

Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called "The Entrance to the Taming of the World by the Radiance of the Dharma that Dispels the Darkness of All Sentient Beings. Toward sentient beings with distorted minds, I maintain a mind of loving-kindness;
toward those who have entered upon the paths of unwholesome action, I maintain a mind of compassion.
She possesses a mind of sympathetic joy toward those who have entered upon the paths of wholesome action;
a mind of equanimity toward sentient beings whose minds are both even and uneven; and a mind intent on purification toward those who are afflicted.
A mind that correctly applies itself toward those who have fallen into adversity;
a mind that generates noble resolve in those with inferior inclinations;
and a mind that increases the force of great vigor in those with weak faculties.

My mind is intent on turning back the wheel of the cycle of rebirth for those who delight in saṃsāra; my mind is intent on establishing all beings who are oriented toward the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas upon the path to omniscience.

Indeed, noble son, it is by being thus engaged in such mental attention that I am endowed with this bodhisattva liberation called "the gateway to the training of the world through the illumination of the Dharma that disperses the darkness of all beings."

Those beings who, during the night of blinding darkness, when humans have retired, when it is frequented by hosts of spirits, crowded with throngs of thieves, when beings move in uneven directions, when it is shrouded in a web of dark clouds and mist,
filled with smoke, dust, and filth, agitated by violent winds and rain, and devoid of the light of the moon, sun, and stars—
In the night when the power of sight is absent, they may be situated upon the ocean,
or on dry land, or on mountains, or in forest wildernesses, or within groves, or in foreign lands,
or between villages, or in intermediate directions, or on various paths, or in the great ocean.
or their vessels may be wrecked, or they may perish while on land,
or they may fall into great precipices while on mountains;
Or they may find themselves in a great forest wilderness, deprived of food and drink;
or, obstructed by dense forests and thickets of cane, they meet with misfortune and calamity;
or, having traveled to another land, they are slain by bandits.
Those who have gone to another village perish through their erratic conduct; those who have gone to another region become utterly confused;
and those who have gone to another intermediate direction become bewildered.
Or those who have entered upon other paths meet with destruction;

for those beings, noble son, I become a refuge through various gateways of skillful means— namely, for those who have gone to sea, so that they may disperse the dark winds and clouds, cross over turbid waters, and escape the circles of violent winds.
In order to pacify the force of great waves, to liberate from the fear of whirlpools, to illuminate the directions, to provide a correct path across the waters, and to show the shore;
in order to bring them to the island of jewels, I manifest the path in the form of a guide, in the form of a caravan leader,
and for some in the form of a king, a lord of the earth, a lord of tortoises, a lord of asuras, or a lord of garuḍas.
In the form of a king of the *kinnaras*, in the form of a king of the *mahoragas*, in the form of a deity of the ocean, and in the form of a fisherman, I become a refuge.
And I dedicate that root of merit in this way: "May I become a refuge for all sentient beings in order to turn back the entire mass of suffering.
For those beings who have come to dry land during the night of the blinding darkness of delusion, which is strewn with bamboo, thorns, pebbles, and potsherds—"

Upon this earth, which is infested with venomous serpents, where movement is difficult due to depressions and elevations, which is thick with rising dust and pollen, agitated by violent winds and rains,

characterized by the painful touch of cold and heat, fraught with fear of predatory beasts and lions, and frequented by hosts of executioners and thieves— for those beings who are bewildered regarding the directions, he appears in the form of the sun, the risen moon, and great falling meteors.

In the form of a garland of lightning, in the form of a jeweled necklace, in the form of the circle of planets, in the form of the radiance of the celestial palaces of the constellations and hosts of luminaries, in the form of a deity, and in the form of a bodhisattva, I become a protector for sentient beings.
And I generate this thought: "By this root of virtue, may I become a protection for all sentient beings, for the sake of dispelling the darkness of all afflictions."
For those beings who have fallen into mountain precipices, terrified by the fear of death; for those driven by the desire for fame; for those longing for renown, reputation, and the banner of glory;

for those seeking enjoyments, possessed by greed, and intent on acquiring requisites; for those whose highest aim is worldly prosperity; for those bound by affection for children and wives; for those lost in the thicket of wrong views; and for those afflicted by various sufferings, fears, and calamities—he has become their refuge through manifold means and gateways.
I become— namely, by manifesting mountain caves as dwellings, by manifesting fruits and roots as food, by manifesting waterways and wells,

by manifesting remedies for cold and heat, by showing the correct path, by the sound of the kalaviṅka’s cry, by the cooing of the king of peacocks, by the form of the radiance of medicinal herbs, and by the form of the splendor of mountain deities.
For those who have entered mountain caves and mountain crevices and are afflicted by various sufferings, I become their refuge by producing level ground to dispel the blinding darkness.

And I generate this thought: "Just as I provide protection for these beings dwelling in the mountains, may I likewise become a refuge for those fallen into the precipice of the mountain of cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*), who are seized and obsessed by old age and death."

I am also for those beings who are entangled in the nets of dense forest thickets, during nights of blinding darkness; whose paths are obstructed by various grasses, water, thorns, trees, and creepers, despite their vast range of objects and diverse provisions; who have entered various groves of trees, creepers, and forest thickets; whose hearts are terrified by the roar and cries of tigers; whose minds are agitated by the failure to accomplish their tasks; and who are afflicted by various fears and calamities.
I become one who correctly shows the path of travel for those who do not know the direction for escaping from the dense forest.

And I generate this thought: "By this root of merit, may I liberate from all sufferings those beings who have entered the thicket of various views, who are entangled in the net of craving, and who are oppressed by the fear and calamities of the manifold sufferings of saṃsāra."

Even for those beings who have entered the wilderness of the forest and fallen into darkness, I generate happiness through various means and gateways, show them the path, and establish them in fearlessness and security; then I form this thought: "By this root of merit, may I liberate from all sufferings those beings who have entered the wilderness of the forest of saṃsāra and have set out upon the path to the miserable destinies."
"I would establish them on the path to omniscience, which is the ultimate security and peace.

Noble son, even when sentient beings are possessed by attachment to their own countries and provinces and are experiencing the suffering resulting from such clinging, I uproot them from that attachment to their homeland through various skillful means, and I generate this thought:"

"By this root of merit, may I uplift all sentient beings from their attachment to the abode of the aggregates (*skandha*) and establish them in the non-abiding omniscient wisdom (*anālaya-sarvajña-jñāna*).

Furthermore, noble son, even those sentient beings dwelling in villages—bound by the fetters of home and household, suffering amidst various domestic calamities in the pitch-black darkness of night—I shall liberate them from the manifold gates of anxiety; and having inspired in them a mind of spiritual urgency (*saṃvega*), I shall [support them] with the gift of wealth."
Having gathered them together, having properly gladdened them, and having established them in the dharma that is without abode,

I generate this thought: "By this root of goodness, may I uproot all sentient beings— who are dependent upon the village of their own sense-bases— from the range and domain of the realms of saṃsāra, and establish them in the range of omniscience."
And those, noble son, who on a night of blinding darkness are individually confused regarding all directions— the cardinal and intermediate points—
and perceive uneven precipices on level ground, or perceive depressions on elevated ground;

Perceiving those who are low as being high, I provide illumination through various means for them who are bewildered regarding the directions, paths, and regions; and for those desiring to go forth, I show them the door;
for those desiring to travel, I show them the way.
To those desiring to cross over, I show the ford;
to those desiring to enter, I show the abode;
to those desiring to look about, I show the directions.

I manifest the surface of the earth with its depressions and elevations; I manifest level and uneven regions of the earth and various kinds of material forms; and for those traveling along the roads, I manifest villages, towns, market towns, provinces, and royal capitals.
To those afflicted by the thirst of heat, I manifest delightful springs, lakes, pools, ponds, lotus-pools, rivers, forests, groves, and gardens.
To those longing due to separation from loved ones, I manifest their mothers, fathers, sons, wives, friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood relations, as well as various other pleasing forms.
And I generate this thought: "Just as I provide light for these beings who are in the pitch-black night, whose eyes are impaired by cataracts, and who are disoriented regarding the directions."
I produce illumination for the sake of perceiving various forms and states;

even so, I do so for those born into the long night of saṃsāra, who are utterly disoriented in all directions, fallen into the darkness of ignorance, whose eye of wisdom is shrouded by the film of unknowing,
who are inverted in their perceptions, thoughts, and views, and who perceive the impermanent as permanent, suffering as happiness, and the non-self as self.

For those who perceive a self, who perceive the beautiful in the foul, who are firmly dependent on the grasping of a self, a sentient being, a life-force, a nourisher, and a person; who are dependent on the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields; who are deluded regarding cause and fruit; who have set out upon the path of unwholesome courses of action—namely, those who take life, those who take what is not given, those who engage in sexual misconduct, those who speak falsely, those who speak divisively, those who speak harshly, those who engage in idle chatter, and those who are covetous.

Those with malevolent minds, those who have fallen into false views, those who do not recognize their mother, those who do not recognize their father, those who are not true śramaṇas, those who are not true brāhmaṇas, those who do not know what is blameworthy, those who do not know what it is to be a man, those stained by passion for unrighteousness, those overcome by improper gain, those enveloped by the dharma of false views, those who slander the Tathāgatas, those who have entered into the extreme discourse against the Wheel of Dharma, those who bear the banner of Māra, those who kill bodhisattvas, and those who harbor hatred toward the Mahāyāna— those who sever the thought of awakening.

Having dispelled the darkness of ignorance with the great light of wisdom for those beings who disparage bodhisattvas, who commit matricide or acts of treachery, who harbor enmity without having caused harm, who revile the noble ones, who follow the sphere of unrighteous conduct of base persons, who misappropriate the property of stūpas or the Saṅgha, who act improperly toward their parents, and who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution— thereby bringing them face-to-face with the great abyss— and having inspired them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening;
By means of the Great Vehicle of Samantabhadra, may I reveal the path to the stage of the knowledge of the Ten Powers;

may I also reveal the stage of the Tathāgata, the domain of the Tathāgata, the ocean of the method of omniscient knowledge, the range of the Buddha-knowledge, the domain of the Buddha, the perfection of the Ten Powers, the power of the Buddha-dhāraṇīs, and the state of being the single body of all Buddhas.
And having revealed these to them, I would establish them in the wisdom of the equality of all Buddhas.

Furthermore, noble son, for those beings who are ill, exhausted by long-term diseases, physically weak, decrepit, aged, overcome by old age, helpless, miserable, poor, fallen into ruin, arrived in foreign lands, wandering in unknown directions, imprisoned, subjected to torture, guilty of offenses, or cast into royal dungeons— I [act as their protector].
I remain here to protect beings from the fear of threats to their lives.
Noble son, I apply myself by every possible means to remove the illnesses of sick beings;
and for those who are aged and overcome by decay, I provide care and service, gathering them in through the non-withholding of necessary provisions.
I provide protection for sentient beings who are without a protector;
I gather together those who are miserable and poor with heaps of wealth and gold;
and I gather together those who have fallen into states of ruin by means of sharing a common purpose.
I lead those who have reached foreign lands back to their own country; I lead those who have entered upon wrong directions toward the right direction;
and I liberate those who have fallen into bondage from their bonds.

I shall liberate those who have not reached their causes from the sufferings caused by those very causes; I shall grant the assurance of life to offenders who have been released from execution by the king.
And I generate this thought: "Just as I become a refuge for these beings in protection from various fears and calamities,"
In this way, having gathered them through this unsurpassed gathering of the Dharma, may I liberate them from all afflictions;
may I cause them to transcend birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair;
and may I liberate them from all fears of falling into miserable destinies.
I would establish them in the embrace of spiritual friends;
I would gather them through the gift of the jewel of the Dharma;
and I would engage them in blameless deeds.
I would cause them to be inspired to purify the body of a Tathāgata;
I would establish them in the penetration of the ultimate realm that is free from old age and death.

Furthermore, noble son, for those beings who have entered upon wrong paths and wrong courses, who are deeply attached to the thicket of various views, whose sphere of activity consists of false intentions, who engage in uneven actions of body, speech, and mind, who live without restraint, who rely on various vows and austerities, who perceive one who is not a perfectly awakened Buddha to be a perfectly awakened Buddha, and who perceive a perfectly awakened Buddha to be one who is not perfectly awakened, and who are devoted to the mortification and tormenting of their own bodies— I [act].

For those who are devoted to springs, lakes, ponds, pools, rivers, mountains, cascades, and the inclines of the cardinal and intermediate directions, and who have fallen under the influence of evil friends,
I become their refuge through various means and gateways. Thereafter, I turn them back from that evil course of views and from the path leading to the precipice of all miserable rebirths.
Having established them in worldly right view, I engage them in divine and human prosperity.

And I generate this thought: "Just as I liberate these beings from such suffering caused by improper conduct, so too shall I establish all beings on the noble, supramundane path of the perfections; having made them irreversible in omniscience, I shall lead them to omniscience through the Great Vow of Samantabhadra."
And one should not depart from the stage of a bodhisattva until the realm of all sentient beings has become irreversible.

Then, at that time, the night goddess Vāsantī, further demonstrating this very direction of the bodhisattva liberation called "The Entrance to the Discipline of the World through the Radiance of the Dharma that Dispels the Darkness of All Beings," surveyed the ten directions by the power of the Buddha and addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana in verses:

For the sake of dispelling the darkness of delusion and ignorance, and for the purpose of generating the manifestation of the Dharma, this peaceful method of liberation of mine—the guide to the happiness of the world—has appeared after considering the proper time. (1)
My loving-kindness is vast and utterly pure, having been well-cultivated by me for infinite eons in the past;
having pervaded the lower realms, it illuminates the world—this is the supreme method, O Sudhana, you who are firm in wisdom. // 2 //
O ocean of compassion, my birth in this world is immeasurable, for it is there that the Victors of the three times arise.
By this means I shall pacify the suffering of the world; O Sudhana, wise one, this is the supreme method.
Bringing forth worldly happinesses as well as those noble happinesses within the conditioned, O son of the Conqueror, enter this method with exalted joy and rapture. // 4 //

O Son of the Victor, always turning away from the defects of the conditioned and from the fruit of liberation through the knowledge of the Śrāvakas, purify the power of a Buddha and enter this method. // 5 //
My eye is vast and utterly pure, by which I behold the realms in the ten directions;
and upon the surfaces of those realms, I see the Self-Existent Ones seated beneath the sovereign trees of enlightenment.

I see thousands of Buddhas, their bodies adorned with the marks, emitting various and manifold rays of light; they possess pores that release oceans of radiance, and are surrounded by assemblies. // 7 //
And within those paths of the fields, I behold those beings who, in all the gateways of death and rebirth, wander through the ocean of destinies as fools, experiencing their own karma.
My ocean of streams is utterly pure, wherein all sounds without exception converge;
having heard every ocean of mantras belonging to all living beings, I retain them through mindfulness. 9.
With the articulation and sounds of all vocal qualities, he adorns the voice of the peerless ones;
indeed, having heard that which sets in motion the wheel of the Victors, I maintain it through mindfulness. 10.

O Son of the Victor, enter this method: the vast and utterly pure power of the nose, which is unimpeded regarding the principles of the ocean of Dharmas, and which leads to the entry into the dwelling of all liberations. 11.
My tongue is vast and well-developed, copper-colored, radiant like a jewel, and pure;
with it I instruct beings according to their inclinations—enter this method, O Son of the Conqueror! (12)
My Dharma-body is exceedingly pure, abiding universally throughout all three times;
yet, by the power of their own resolute faith, sentient beings perceive my form-body according to their respective inclinations. // 13 //
My mind is unattached and free from outflows; my voice and speech are like the rumbling of clouds.
All the lords of men gather there, yet no conceptualization exists within me. 14.
Upon the surfaces of inconceivable fields, I understand the oceans of the minds of those beings;
I know their faculties and inclinations, yet no conceptual construction exists within me. 15.
My vast supernatural power is perfectly accomplished; may it shake inconceivable realms.
May my bodily radiance shine forth, by which I shall subdue all beings who are so difficult to tame. 16.
May my merit be vast, utterly pure, an inexhaustible treasury, and universally adorned;
by means of it, may I perform worship for the Victors and become a source of sustenance for the entire world. (17)
My wisdom is vast and perfectly pure, by which I understand the oceans of phenomena; I sever the doubts of all people—enter this method, O Son of the Victor! (18)
I have entered the ocean of Buddhas, leading [beings] by the supreme method through all three times; and within them I descend with my vow—this incomparable method is perfectly fulfilled. (19)
In every atom, I behold oceans of realms and the entries into the three times;
therein I see oceans of Buddhas and their universal ground of the stages of method. (20)
Behold, Virocana, the one awakened to enlightenment, who has pervaded all directions and realms;
from the king of Bodhi trees at every path of dust, he is emitting the Dharma of peace. // 21 //
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, said this to the night goddess Vāsantī: “Goddess, how long has it been since you set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
And how long have you possessed this liberation, by the attainment of which you are thus engaged in performing the welfare of sentient beings?”

When this had been said, the night goddess Vāsantī spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "In the past, O Son of the Victor, in a time long gone, beyond aeons as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was an aeon named Praśāntaprabha,
in which one billion buddhas appeared."
In that [universe] there was a world-system named Ratnaśrīsaṃbhavā.
In that world-system, moreover, there was a central four-continent realm named Ratnacandrapradīpaprabhā,
and in it a royal capital named Padmaprabhā.
In that royal capital, there was a king named Sudharmatīrtha, a righteous Dharma-king, a universal monarch (cakravartin) who ruled over the four continents and was endowed with the seven treasures.
Having conquered this great earth, bounded by the oceans and mountains, and free from all thorns [of opposition], he dwelt therein through the power of righteousness.
King Sudharmatīrtha had a wife named Dharmamaticandrā.
During the first watch of the night, she became intoxicated with passion and, exhausted from amorous play, fell asleep in the middle watch while inside the inner apartments.
Then, to the east of that royal capital Padmaprabhā, in the great forest grove called Śamathaśrīsaṃbhava, [there dwelt] Sarvadharmanigarjitarāja.

The Tathāgata named [Sarvavyūhaprabhāmaṇirāja] attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment beneath the great Bodhi tree, which was the source of the miraculous manifestations of all Buddhas and whose body was like a king of jewels radiating all arrays.
By him, that entire world-system Ratnaśrīsaṃbhava was pervaded and illuminated with a magnificent light of manifold colors.

And in that royal capital, Padmaprabhā, there was a night goddess named Suviśuddhacandrābhā. She approached the queen Dharmamaticandrā and, awakening her with the sound of her ornaments clashing, spoke thus: "O Queen, you should know that in the great forest grove called Śamathaśrīsaṃbhava dwells the King of the Roar of All Dharmas."

The Tathāgata named [Nāma] had awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Before that queen, he extensively proclaimed the praise of the Buddha’s qualities, the miraculous transformations of a Buddha, and the vows for the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Furthermore, noble son, that queen, illuminated by the power of the Tathāgata, set her mind upon unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment with a resolute intention.
He performed great worship and honor for that Tathāgata, together with his assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas.
What do you think, noble son—was she someone else at that time, on that occasion, who was the queen’s consort named Dharmamaticandrā?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way.
At that time, on that occasion, I was the king’s wife named Dharmamaticandrā.

O son of good family, by virtue of that aspirational resolve and those roots of merit planted in the Tathāgata, for as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, I have never been reborn in the miserable states—
neither in the hells, nor among animals, nor among hungry ghosts—
and I have never been reborn in low-born families.
I was never deficient in my faculties,

nor was I ever afflicted by suffering. Always having attained divine majesty among the gods and human majesty among humans, I was never separated from spiritual friends— namely, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
I have never been born during times of adversity.

Indeed, noble son, while planting roots of merit under Buddhas and those awakened after them, I have come through aeons as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru by way of happiness, tranquility, security, and the right path;
yet my bodhisattva faculties are not yet fully perfected.

When those eons, equal in number to the atoms in Mount Sumeru, had passed— ten thousand eons prior to this present Fortunate Eon— at that time, there was an eon named Aśokaviraja (Stainless and Free from Grief) in a world-system named Rajovimalatejaḥśrī (Splendor of Stainless Radiance).
Furthermore, noble son, that world-system Rajovimalatejaḥśrī was both afflicted and purified, being the source of the arising of five hundred Buddhas.

Furthermore, among those five hundred Buddhas, the first Tathāgata to appear in the world was named Sumerudhvajāyatanaśāntanetraśrī; he was endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

And I was a merchant’s daughter named Prajñāvabhāsaśrī, the daughter of the merchant Vighuṣṭakīrti; I was beautiful, pleasing, and lovely to behold, endowed with the most excellent and abundant splendor of complexion.

And that night goddess Suviśuddhacandrābhā, by the power of her vow, [was born] as Viśuddhanetrābhā in the royal capital Vicitradhvajā, within the world-system Virajovatī consisting of four continents.
There was a night goddess named Nāma;

when the night had become tranquil and my parents were asleep, she caused that house to tremble, revealed her own form with a sublime radiance, and spoke the praise of the Buddha's qualities, [describing] how that Tathāgata had attained perfect awakening during his first week.
He was seen seated at the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
Then, together with my parents and a great assembly of kinsmen, placing that night goddess Suviśuddhacandrābhā at our head, I approached that Tathāgata.
Having performed a magnificent worship of that Tathāgata, at the very moment of seeing him, I attained the samādhi called "The Source of Seeing the Buddha for the Discipline of the World."
I attained the samādhi called the "Mandala Illuminating the Knowledge of the Three Times," through the attainment of which I recollected those eons as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru,
and that mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta) became manifest to me.

Having heard the teaching of the Dharma from that Tathāgata, she attained this bodhisattva liberation called "The Entrance to the Discipline of the World through the Radiance of the Dharma that Dispels the Darkness of All Sentient Beings.
By virtue of its attainment, I pervade with my body world-systems as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
and those Tathāgatas who reside in those world-systems—
All of them come within the range of my vision, and I perceive myself as having gone to the feet of each of them; and I see whatever beings have been born in those world-systems.
All of them also come within the range of my vision;
I understand their various vocal expressions and conventional signs, and I understand their thoughts, intentions, faculties, and inclinations.
I know the ripening [of beings] among their virtuous friends from former lives,
and I manifest my body to them in accordance with what will satisfy their inclinations.

And that liberation of mine increases with every moment of thought. Immediately following that mind of liberation, with the very next thought-moment, I pervade with my body as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a hundred world-systems.
With the subsequent thought-moment, I pervade with my body as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a thousand world-systems.
Immediately following that thought, I pervade with my body as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of world-systems;
likewise, at every moment of thought, I pervade with my body as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of world-systems.
And those Tathāgatas who reside in those Buddha-fields—
All of them come within the range of my vision, and I perceive myself at the feet of each of them; and whatever Dharma teaching those Blessed Buddhas give, [I hear].
I take up all of that,
I maintain it, I thoroughly investigate it, and I contemplate it;
and I enter into the oceans of former practices and the oceans of vows of those Tathāgatas.

Whatever purification of the buddha-fields those Tathāgatas possess, I too bring forth all that for the sake of purifying the buddha-field; and whatever sentient beings are born within those oceans of world-systems, [I likewise bring forth for their benefit].

All of them also come within the range of my vision; and to whatever extent there are differences in the dispositions, faculties, and inclinations of those beings, I assume a body of corresponding variety, that is to say, for the sake of their ripening and discipline.
In this way, with every moment of thought, this liberation increases through the practice of expanding and pervading the vast expanse of the *dharmadhātu*.
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "The Entrance to the Discipline of the World through the Radiance of the Dharma that Dispels the Darkness of All Sentient Beings.
What could I possibly know of the bodhisattvas who have emerged from the vows and conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, which are infinite, without center, and all-pervading?

They have attained mastery in entering the vast expanse of the ocean-like methods of the realm of phenomena; they sport in the vajra-banner samādhi that is the wisdom of the realization of all bodhisattvas;

they have emerged from the great vows to sustain the lineage of all Tathāgatas in all world-systems; they have perfected an ocean of great merit that purifies every moment of mind throughout the expanse of all world-systems;
and in every moment of thought, they possess mastery over the wisdom that ripens and disciplines [beings] throughout the entire realm of phenomena in all world-systems.

In order to know the conduct of those who possess the eye of the sun of wisdom that dispels the great darkness of all obscurations for all sentient beings; those whose prowess consists in making the Great Vehicle known to the realm of all sentient beings; those who are moons of intelligence that dispel the cataracts of doubt, uncertainty, and hesitation in the entire world; those whose circle of pure vocal resonance causes the uprooting of attachment to the ocean of all states of existence; those who have mastery in manifesting miraculous transformations upon the paths of the atoms within the entire realm of phenomena; and those who are undivided from the mandala of the wisdom of the three times.
Whether to speak of their qualities,
or to enter their sphere of activity,
or to demonstrate the play of liberation.
Go, son of good family;
right here in this Magadha region, on the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), there dwells a night goddess named Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā,
by whom I was inspired to set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Being urged again and again, approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one practice?"
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, praised Vāsantī, the night goddess, with these verses of praise:
"Today I behold your pure body, adorned with the marks like Mount Meru."
O Mañjuśrī, you who have risen above the world and illuminate the world, like the splendor of form. // 22 //
Your Dharma-body is exceedingly pure, equal throughout all three times, and free from conceptual construction;
therein the entire world converges, and yet it arises and dissolves without attachment. (23)
I see your body manifested as reflections throughout the expanse of all realms of existence;
and within the pores of your skin, I see multitudes of stars along with the suns and moons.

Your mind is vast and perfectly pure, by which it pervades the directions like the sky; therein all lords of men have converged, and thus your supreme wisdom is free from the stain of conceptual construction. 25.
From the pores of your skin, clouds as numerous as the atoms of the fields emerge in various forms;
they pervade the ten directions, raining down every kind of magnificent array for the Buddhas. (26)
Bodies like all the worlds emerge limitlessly from the pores of your skin;
having pervaded the worlds in the ten directions, they purify sentient beings through various skillful means. (27)
Within the pores of my skin, I behold inconceivable realms, diverse and adorned with various arrays;
all those which were purified by you within the states of existence for sentient beings, appearing according to their respective inclinations. (28)

Great gain is well-obtained and their life is well-lived by those who, with uplifted minds, hear your name; and those people who seek a vision of you become oriented toward the path to awakening. (29)
Even for inconceivable eons, one should strive to see you in the states of woe;
for by merely hearing [of you], their minds are gladdened, and by the mere sight of you, they pacify their afflictions. (30)

O Destroyer of Death, even if there were bodies as numerous as the atoms in thousands of realms, and they were to remain for aeons like yours, they would never reach the end of describing the qualities of a single pore of your skin. (31)

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, having praised the night goddess Vāsantī with these verses, bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Vāsantī, circumambulated her hundreds of thousands of times,
and looking back again and again, remained insatiable in his service to the spiritual friend Vāsantī.
He departed from the presence of the Night Deity. // 32 //
(35) Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā.
Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son, following the purification of the bodhisattva-mind-mandala in the first stage of the night goddess Vāsantī, proceeded.
Contemplating the arising from the womb of enlightenment,
entering the ocean of the bodhisattva's vows,
and purifying the path of the bodhisattva's perfections.
Entering the mandala of the bodhisattva stages,
expanding the mandala of the bodhisattva conduct, and recollecting the ocean of the bodhisattva's departure [from saṃsāra],
Beholding the great ocean of the radiance of omniscience,

expanding the great cloud of bodhisattva compassion that is intent upon protecting all worlds, and manifesting the mandala of the vows for the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra by the night goddess Vāsantī— an empowerment sustained throughout all buddha-fields until the end of time—

Having approached the night goddess named Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, he bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā and circumambulated her hundreds of thousands of times.
Standing before the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus: "Noble goddess, I have resolved my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva courses in the stages of the bodhisattva conduct."
"How does one emerge? How is one perfected?
He replied, "Excellent, excellent, noble son!"

Since you have generated the mind set on unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and ask about the perfection of the departure from the bodhisattva stages, listen, noble son: endowed with ten qualities, bodhisattvas become perfected in the conduct of a bodhisattva. What are these ten?
Namely: through the purity of attaining the samādhi that perceives the manifestation of all Tathāgatas before one's eyes;
through the purity of the eye that surveys the infinite bodies of the various marks of all Buddhas;
and through the entry into the perception of the ocean of the colors of the Tathāgatas, which is without end or middle.
By means of entering the measureless extent of the entire realm of phenomena through oceans of mandalas of light from the immeasurable qualities of the Buddhas;

by means of entering the emergence of oceans of rays of light from every pore of all Tathāgatas, which manifest for the benefit of various sentient beings according to the likeness of all sentient beings; and by means of beholding oceans of rays of light in all jewel-colored hues from each and every single pore.

By means of entering into the empowerment that disciplines sentient beings through the pervasion of an ocean of Buddha-emanations throughout the expanse of all dharmadhatus in every moment of thought; by means of entering into the mandala of sounds that resound with the thundering of all sutras, which are the proclamations of the Dharma wheels of all times and are joined with an ocean of the vocal qualities of all sentient beings;
and by means of entering into the ocean of the names of Buddhas, which are without end or middle.
By way of the removal of obstacles through the training of sentient beings by displaying the inconceivable miraculous transformations of a Buddha—
noble son, bodhisattvas endowed with these ten qualities become perfected in the bodhisattva practice.
"Indeed, noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called 'Universal Valor in the Bliss of Peaceful Meditation.
Noble son, all the Tathāgatas of the three times come within the range of my vision,
and I penetrate the purity of the buddha-fields of those Tathāgatas."
Even the oceans of circles of assemblies,
even the oceans of miraculous displays of meditative absorptions that are without end or center,
and even the oceans of past connections;
I also enter into the oceans of their names, and I enter into the diversity of those Tathāgatas’ turning of the wheel of Dharma, as well as the variety in the measure of the Tathāgatas’ lifespans.
I also enter into the diversity of their vocal qualities, and I penetrate the fact that those Tathāgatas have bodies that are the infinite realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu),
yet I do not adhere to those Tathāgatas as having substantial existence.
For what reason? Because those Tathāgatas are without a destination, since all destinations in the world have ceased for them.
For those Tathāgatas have no coming,
because they are not produced by way of intrinsic nature;
for those Tathāgatas are unarisen.
Because they have a body equal to the nature of non-arising;
for those Tathāgatas are unceasing, since their characteristic is non-arising.
For those Tathāgatas are unreal,
because they are a representation consisting in the vision of phenomena that have reached the state of illusion;
yet those Tathāgatas are not false.
Because they have arisen for the sake of the entire world,
those Tathāgatas are indeed non-transmigrating, as they have transcended death and rebirth.
For those Tathāgatas are indeed undestroyed, by virtue of the nature of phenomena which is non-destructible;
for those Tathāgatas possess but a single characteristic.
Because they have completely transcended all paths of speech;
for those Tathāgatas are without marks, since they culminate in the intrinsic nature of the markless character of phenomena.

Furthermore, noble son, as I thus enter into all the Tathāgatas, I expand, enter, follow, equalize, bring forth, level, cause to enter, increase, contemplate, deeply contemplate, take as a form, make into my range of activity, solidify, and illuminate this bodhisattva liberation called "Universal Valor in the Bliss of Tranquil Meditation," by means of the radiance of the maṇḍala of the Tathāgata’s meditative concentration.
I illuminate, array, distinguish, accumulate, and honor.

And abiding therein in great compassion, which is free from the activity of all conceptual constructions, I cultivate the first dhyāna for the sake of one-pointedness of mind in the activity of protecting all sentient beings, for the sake of the pacification of all mental activities, and for the sake of one-pointedness of mind characterized by joy and happiness through the gathering of all sentient beings by the power and prowess of primordial wisdom.

I cultivate the second dhyāna for the sake of the purity of the sphere of equanimity toward all beings who have fallen into the cycle of existence; I cultivate the third dhyāna for the sake of pacifying the burning heat of the afflictions and suffering of all beings;
I cultivate the fourth dhyāna for the sake of expanding the mandala of the vow for omniscience and for skill in the actualization of the oceans of all samādhis.

In order to enter the ocean-like methods of liberation of all bodhisattvas, to attain the superknowledges and wisdom of the playful sport of all bodhisattvas, and to accomplish the miraculous transformations of all bodhisattva practices, I purify the method of wisdom for entering the dharma-realm through universal gates;
thus do I cultivate this bodhisattva liberation called "The Universal Stride into the Gates of Peaceful Meditation."
