Furthermore, noble son, while cultivating this liberation, I ripen sentient beings through various skillful means; that is to say, when the night has become tranquil, I generate in sentient beings who are intoxicated by pleasure the perception of impurity,

the perception of aversion, the perception of weariness, the perception of obstruction, the perception of bondage, the perception of a rākṣasī, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, the perception of ownerlessness, and the perception of lack of dependence on another.
I produce the perception of old age and death,
and the perception of lack of delight in the enjoyment of all objects of sensual desire.

And those beings, cultivating that thought, becoming disenchanted with all delights of sensual pleasure and taking pleasure in the delight of the garden of Dharma, go forth from the home to the homeless state.
For those who have gone to the forest, I generate a faith that is in accordance with the Dharma;
I cause the sounds of distressed, terrifying, and loud cries to vanish;
and when the night has become tranquil, I reveal the profundity of the Buddha-dharma.
I provide conditions conducive to abandonment;
as they go forth, I open the door to the home and show them the path.
I create light;
I dispel the darkness of gloom;
I cause fear to vanish.
I praise renunciation;
I speak the praises of the Buddha,
the praises of the Dharma, the praises of the Saṅgha, and the praises of spiritual friends.
I praise approaching spiritual friends.
Cultivating this liberation, noble son, I cause the disappearance of unrighteous lustful passions in beings who are stained by unrighteous lust,
and I cause the disappearance of those thoughts and mental orientations in those overcome by improper greed and whose range of activity consists of false intentions.
I provide the necessary conditions for the non-arising of unarisen evil and unwholesome states, and for the disappearance of arisen evil intentions.

Of wholesome roots that have not yet arisen— those associated with the perfections, those associated with the [bodhisattva] practices, those associated with the accomplishment of the vow for the departure toward the knowledge of omniscience, those associated with the method of loving-kindness,
those associated with the pervasive great compassion for all sentient beings, and those associated with the production of various divine and human supports of happiness.
I provide the conditions for the arising of intentions and for those already arisen, through various methods;
indeed, I provide the conditions for all intentions that are conducive to omniscience.
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "Universal Valor in the Bliss of Tranquil Meditation.

How could I possibly describe the bodhisattvas who have set out through the vows and conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, who have attained the knowledge of the infinite modes of the realm of phenomena,
whose minds are nourished by all roots of goodness, and who have attained the illumination of the mind through the power of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas?

In order to know the conduct of those whose minds dwell within the domain of all Tathāgatas; whose minds are unobstructed regarding all co-dwellings; whose minds possess the perfected vow for omniscience; whose minds have entered the oceans of all buddha-fields; whose minds are extended toward beholding the oceans of all Buddhas; whose minds receive the clouds of Dharma from all Tathāgatas; who dispel the darkness of all ignorance; and whose minds generate the light of omniscience—the path that brings about the end of the craving for delight in saṃsāra—[I have come].
Or to speak of his virtues.
Go, noble son;
right here, immediately following me, at the seat of enlightenment of Vairocana, there dwells a night goddess named Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, who circumambulates it.
Approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva apply himself to the activities of a bodhisattva?"

Then, at that time, the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, further demonstrating this very Bodhisattva liberation called "Universal Prowess in the Bliss of Tranquil Meditation," addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana with these verses:
"The Tathāgatas, supreme throughout all times, appear before those whose minds are inclined toward them through resolute faith."
Within them, the vast eye is purified, by which they shall descend into the oceans of Buddhas. // 1 //
Behold the stainless body of the Jina, beautiful and adorned with the primary marks;
behold also the miraculous manifestation of the Jina, which pervades the realm of phenomena at every moment. // 2 //

This Sugata Virocana, having fully awakened at the seat of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, pervaded the vast realm of phenomena and turned the wheel of Dharma for the world according to their inclinations. // 3 //
Through his wisdom, the Victor revealed the nature of phenomena— which is bodiless, perfectly peaceful, and non-dual—
while manifesting a form-body adorned with auspicious marks, pervading the entire world. (4)
The vast and inconceivable Buddha-body pervades the entire realm of phenomena without exception; it is seen equally in all directions, and the Victors manifest themselves everywhere. (5)
Resembling the atoms of all fields, they rest within the circles of light of the Buddha-bodies; manifesting beautiful colors to one another, they pervade the realm of phenomena at every moment.
Immeasurable, inconceivable, and inexhaustible clouds of light rays issue forth from the pores of the Victor;
having pervaded the entire world without exception, they pacify the heat of the afflictions for all living beings. // 7 //
Oceans of emanations of the Buddhas, inexhaustible, issue forth from the circles of the Victor’s pores;
having pervaded the vast expanse of the realm of phenomena, they pacify the sufferings of miserable rebirths for living beings. // 8 //
The sweet voice of the Buddha resounds, possessing the splendor of an ocean of beautiful vocal qualities;
raining down a vast shower of Dharma, it generates the aspiration for enlightenment in living beings. // 9 //
Having previously practiced their conduct throughout an ocean of eons,
they beheld the Victorious One Vairocana, whose characteristics are the manifestation of all buddha-fields.
The Tathāgata has arisen in all worlds, standing equally present before all beings; yet the range of their respective inclinations cannot be fully known even by all of them together. (11)
O supreme Bodhisattva, even a single hair-pore of the Sugata contains more than all the rest;
those inconceivable methods of liberation cannot be fully known by anyone. 12.
This deity, rejoicing as she faces the Lord of the World immediately after me, is named Jyotirarcinayana; ask her how one practices the conduct of awakening.

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, circumambulated the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā hundreds of thousands of times,
and looking back at her again and again, [departed] from the presence of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā.
He departed from his presence. // 33 //
(36) Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana was permeated by the inspiration of the instructions of the spiritual friends; his mind was brought forth through the practice of the words of the spiritual friends.
With a mind that maintains the perception of a sick person toward the physicians who are spiritual friends; with a mind undistracted by the mental application of seeing spiritual friends;

with a mind that has attained the opening for shattering all the mountains of obscurations through seeing spiritual friends; with a mind that has attained entry into the ocean of the method of great compassion that protects the realm of all sentient beings through seeing spiritual friends; [through] seeing spiritual friends...
Having attained a mind illuminated by the wisdom of the ocean-like principle of the realm of phenomena, he approached the night goddess named Pramuditānayanajagadvirocanā.

Then, indeed, the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, for the sake of Sudhana the merchant’s son, further established him in approaching spiritual friends by means of the arising and ripening of the accumulation of roots of goodness; she established him in approaching spiritual friends through the great accumulation of provisions;
she established him in approaching spiritual friends with great valor.
He established the practice of approaching spiritual friends with the vigor of difficult-to-attain deeds; he established the practice of approaching spiritual friends that has been long-established;
he established the practice of approaching spiritual friends for entry into the infinite and middleless directions.

He established the approach to spiritual friends as arising from dwelling together over a long period of time; he established the approach to spiritual friends as arising from the fulfillment of infinite tasks and communications;
he established the approach to spiritual friends as the progression through the accumulation of the array of the infinite middle way.
He established the approach to spiritual friends as arising from the valor of universal gates; he established the approach to spiritual friends as the valor of neither departing nor arriving.
Then indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, through his heroic exertion in the accumulation for omniscience by approaching spiritual friends;

through his prowess in accomplishing the ocean of great vows by approaching spiritual friends; and through his resolve to experience suffering for the sake of even a single sentient being until the end of future eons by approaching spiritual friends—

By means of the armor of great vigor, with a stride that traverses the entire realm of phenomena without delay within a single atom; by means of approaching spiritual friends, following as swiftly as the ocean-like expanse of all directions;
and by means of approaching spiritual friends, dwelling together in the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout kalpas as numerous as those at the end of time upon the path of a single hair.
For one who has attained the conduct of a bodhisattva, there is the approach to spiritual friends through the stabilization of the knowledge of all-knowledge in every moment of thought;

the approach to spiritual friends through the resolve to traverse the path of the array of miraculous manifestations of all Tathāgatas attained throughout the three times; and the approach to spiritual friends by traversing the path that flows forth from the stream of the principles of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

Without departing from the focus on the methods of the entire realm of phenomena, and pervading the whole realm of phenomena, he approached the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā by means of his visit to spiritual friends.
He saw the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā seated upon a lion throne of flower-womb within the circle of the Blessed One’s assembly,
having entered the bodhisattva samādhi called Samantabhadra-joy-vast-pure-impulse-banner.
And he saw from all the pores of her skin [emanating] that which is pleasing to all beings, which is desired by all beings, and which is conformable to the sight of all beings.
From clouds issuing forth that illuminate the practice of the various perfections, such as giving, which are pleasing to behold for all sentient beings— namely,
clouds that manifest the practice of giving through communications according to the inclinations of all sentient beings;

for the sake of favoring all sentient beings without conflict, for the sake of not looking back at any material thing, for the sake of never abandoning the equal application toward all sentient beings, and for the sake of equanimity of mind toward all sentient beings.
For the sake of not abandoning the non-contempt for all sentient beings, for the sake of relinquishing all internal and external things,
for the sake of demonstrating the relinquishment of great hardships, and for the sake of demonstrating the practice of giving to sentient beings in all worlds according to their inclinations—

[these clouds] issued forth from the inconceivable clouds of emanations of the relinquishment of the difficult practices of Bodhisattvas attained throughout the three times, and in the ten directions...
He saw the mental representations of all sentient beings contained within the expanse of all world-systems in every direction coming toward him;
that is to say, by virtue of his attainment of the inconceivable, sovereign power and miraculous transformations of a bodhisattva.

From all the pores of his skin, there issued forth clouds of transformation-bodies that had entered into the births of all sentient beings; pervading all sentient beings included within all world-systems, they manifested the unshakability of undertaking all vows, illuminating a mandala of various ascetic practices equal in extent to the realm of beings, and demonstrating their state as the refuge for all worlds, their lack of regard for any sensory objects, and their turning away from dwelling in all of saṃsāra.
They were demonstrating how divine and human prosperity and adversity converge upon the same ground; they were illuminating the mandala of impurity;
they were turning back the world’s perversion of perceiving things as pure; and they were fully elucidating the nature of impermanence, instability, decay, and transformation.

They were demonstrating that all conditioned phenomena have the nature of suffering and non-self; they were causing them to find delight in dwelling within the range of the Tathāgatas without ever departing from it; and they were encouraging sentient beings to undertake the ultimate purification of the Tathāgata’s ethical discipline.

He saw them demonstrating the conduct of ethical discipline through vocal expressions that accord with the diverse inclinations of all sentient beings; he saw them demonstrating the state of being fragrant with the morality that satisfies all sentient beings;
and he saw them bringing all sentient beings to spiritual maturity.

And from all the pores of his skin, there issued forth clouds of emanated bodies of various colors, pervading the entire realm of sentient beings, demonstrating their endurance of having all their major and minor limbs severed, and their endurance of being subjected to physical oppression and assault by all sentient beings;
and demonstrating their endurance of untruthful speech, verbal abuse, reviling, disparagement, censure, beating, and threats from all sentient beings.

They were demonstrating the unshakeability of all sentient beings; they were demonstrating the absence of elevation or depression in the face of honor from all sentient beings; they were demonstrating the lack of conceit in all sentient beings; and they were demonstrating the inexhaustibility of the patience regarding the intrinsic nature of all phenomena and the state of inexhaustible gnosis.

He saw [the Bodhisattvas] demonstrating the practice of patience for the sake of abandoning all the afflictions of all sentient beings; turning back the state of having unstable and ugly physical forms for all sentient beings; praising the supreme, pure radiance of the Tathāgatas for all sentient beings; and bringing sentient beings to maturity.

And from every pore of his body, he emitted clouds of emanated bodies of sentient beings—equal in number to all sentient beings, possessing various colors, shapes, heights, and girths, and appearing in various modes of birth.
Having pervaded sentient beings according to their inclinations, they manifest the heroic prowess of the great accumulation for omniscience;

the heroism that scatters all the Māras and the Kali age; the unshakeable and irreversible heroism in the undertaking of awakening; the heroism that ferries all sentient beings across the ocean of saṃsāra;
the heroism that turns back the paths leading to all unfavorable conditions, miserable states, and lower realms; and the heroism that shatters the mountain of ignorance.
They were displaying the tireless vigor of making offerings and attending upon all Tathāgatas; the vigor of receiving and upholding the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas;
the vigor of shattering and scattering the mountains of all obscurations; the tireless vigor of ripening and disciplining all sentient beings;
and the supreme purity of the vigor of a Tathāgata in purifying all Buddha-fields.
He saw them bringing sentient beings to maturity.
And from all the pores of his skin, there issued forth clouds of emanated bodies of various colors and forms; through diverse skillful means, they produced joy in sentient beings,
turned them away from dejection,
and caused them to feel revulsion for the pleasures of all sensual desires.
They were manifesting the nature of modesty in the world,
establishing beings in the restraint of the sense faculties,
and [teaching] the unsurpassed holy life.
They were praising [the path],
showing the realm of the Māra of the world of desire as something to be feared,
and even for those who were free from delight in sensual pleasures, they were displaying the entire range of objects of sensual delight in the world.
Establishing sentient beings in the delight of the garden of Dharma, bringing forth the bliss of the successive meditative absorptions, concentrations, and attainments,
and praising the state of mind that thoroughly examines all the afflictions of all sentient beings.
They were displaying the miraculous transformations of the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis,
demonstrating the preeminent power of the miraculous feats of bodhisattva superknowledges,
and engendering joy in sentient beings.
generating joy,
turning back dejection, and bringing about a state of mental well-being;
making the mind pliable, purifying their intentions,
and sharpening their faculties;
He saw beings generating physical bliss, increasing the surge of joy in the Dharma, and being brought to spiritual maturity.

And from every pore of their skin, there issued forth clouds of various bodies with forms corresponding to all possible states of rebirth, appearing before all sentient beings throughout all fields to manifest according to their inclinations;
they demonstrated tireless application in approaching all spiritual friends,
and they demonstrated tireless service and attendance upon all teachers, gurus, and spiritual friends.
They were demonstrating tireless vigor in receiving and upholding the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Tathāgatas; they were discerning the oceans of all gateways to the Dharma;
and they were extolling the method for entering the oceans of all Buddhas.
They were elucidating the method of the intrinsic nature and characteristics of all phenomena,
and demonstrating the gateway to meditative concentration for all phenomena.

He saw them displaying the wisdom-vajra that shatters the mountain of the views of all sentient beings; he saw them displaying the emergence of the solar orb of wisdom that dispels the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings through the convergence of many moments of mind; and he saw them maturing sentient beings toward omniscience by generating joy in them.

And from all the pores of his skin, there issued forth clouds of emanated bodies—equal in number to all worlds, noble, inconceivable, and appearing in various colors, forms, and arrangements—which stood facing all sentient beings according to their inclinations and aspirations. Through the instruction of various sounds and mantra-formulations, they demonstrated all mundane merit and supernormal powers; and by means of engaging in all mundane activities, by manifesting the arising of all that exists within the triple world, and by describing the path of liberation from the triple world.
They were praising the excellence of the path to omniscience by showing the direction for escaping the dense wilderness of all dogmatic views;

they were demonstrating the transcendence of the paths and stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; and they were demonstrating the state of being free from attachment and aversion toward conditioned phenomena and the unconditioned, as well as freedom from attachment and aversion toward both attachment and aversion themselves.
They were demonstrating their non-reliance on the pleasures of either saṃsāra or nirvāṇa;

they were demonstrating their uninterrupted succession through the dwelling in the Tuṣita heaven and other such stages; and they were demonstrating their uninterrupted progression from setting out for the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) to the attainment of perfect enlightenment (abhisaṃbodhi).
He saw them illuminating sentient beings regarding omniscience.
And from every single pore of his skin, clouds of emanated bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields issued forth;
these stood facing the entire world of sentient beings, extolling the vows and conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
and extolling the excellence of the vows that culminate in the purification of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

In every moment of thought, they were describing the purification of all oceans of world-systems; they were describing the uninterrupted performance of worship and service to all Tathāgatas; and in every moment of thought, they were describing the uninterrupted entry into the oceans of the methods of all dharmas.
They were praising the unceasing entry into the powers of the Tathāgata at every moment of thought,
and they were demonstrating the unceasing penetration into the oceans of all methods of the dharma-realm, as numerous as the atoms in the oceans of all world-systems, at every moment of thought.
They were praising the state of never ceasing to manifest the purification of the path to omniscience while dwelling for eons through empowerment in all buddha-fields until the end of time;

they were demonstrating the state of never ceasing to enter the powers of the Tathāgatas at every moment of thought; and they were demonstrating the state of never ceasing to enter the oceans of the methods of all three times.
He saw them displaying an uninterrupted manifestation of the miraculous transformations of all the Buddha-fields of the Bodhisattvas,
and establishing all sentient beings in omniscience by demonstrating the conduct of the Bodhisattva’s vows.

And from every single pore of all his pores, there issued forth clouds of emanated bodies equal in number to the minds of all living beings, standing facing all sentient beings, demonstrating the infinite power of the equipment for omniscience;
demonstrating the power of the mind of omniscience, which is of an indestructible, inexhaustible, and imperishable nature;
and demonstrating the power of the complete attainment of the supreme conduct of all bodhisattvas, which is irreversible, non-retrogressive, and never-ceasing through its sustaining power.
They were extolling the power of Bodhisattvas to remain unstained by all the defects of saṃsāra;

they were demonstrating the power of Bodhisattvas to scatter the entire mandala of Māra; and they were revealing the power of Bodhisattvas whose afflictions do not stain them, despite being amidst all the impurities of the defilements.

They were displaying the power of the Bodhisattvas for shattering the mountain of all karmic obstructions; they were displaying the power of the great compassion of the Bodhisattvas, which is tireless in the practice of the Bodhisattva path throughout cohabitation with all eons;
and they were displaying the power of the Bodhisattvas for shaking and agitating all Buddha-fields and gladdening all sentient beings.

He saw them displaying the power of the Bodhisattvas that crushes all hosts of Māras and adversaries; manifesting in the world the power of the knowledge that turns the great wheel of Dharma; and illuminating all sentient beings toward omniscience.
And from every single pore of all his pores, there issued forth oceans of clouds of emanated bodies of infinite colors, which had taken up the mentalities of all living beings;

these clouds pervaded the infinite realms of sentient beings in the ten directions, manifesting to beings according to their inclinations and aspirations the courageous stride of the knowledge of the bodhisattva conduct,
and manifesting the knowledge for entering the oceans of all realms of sentient beings.

They were demonstrating the knowledge of entering the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings; they were demonstrating the knowledge of fully understanding the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings;
they were demonstrating the knowledge of entering the ocean of the conduct of all sentient beings.

They were demonstrating the knowledge that never fails to observe the proper time for the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings; they were demonstrating the knowledge that resonates throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
and they were demonstrating the knowledge that, in every moment of thought, pervades the ocean-like methods of knowing the entire realm of phenomena.

They were displaying the knowledge of the dissolution and evolution of all oceans of world-systems; they were displaying the knowledge of the distinctions in the arrays of the foundations and structures of all world-systems;
and they were displaying the knowledge of approaching all Tathāgatas with miraculous displays of worship, honoring them, attending upon them, and receiving clouds of Dharma-wheels.
Thus, he saw them generating joy in sentient beings by demonstrating the practice of the perfection of wisdom;
he saw them clarifying their minds, producing gladness, engendering rapture, turning back dejection, purifying their minds, and bringing about mental fitness;
he saw them sharpening their faculties, generating the power of resolute conviction, and making them irreversible from omniscience.

And just as he saw beings in the world reaching maturity through the manifestation of the practice of the perfections (*pāramitā*), so too did he see [all] the accumulations for the first production of the thought of awakening belonging to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā— her applications for pleasing spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), her applications for approaching, honoring, and attending upon the feet of the Tathāgatas, and her applications for the diligent practice of wholesome dharmas— through the proclamation of all the dharmas of the bodhisattvas.
And those difficult acts of renunciation in the practice of the perfection of generosity,
the applications for the purification of the perfection of ethical discipline,
and the applications for the great departure involving the renunciation of sovereignty, power, retinue, and enjoyments as a great king;
Those which are the accomplishments of patience through difficult practices, great vows, ascetic penances, and mandalas in the world;
that which is the unshakability in the application of undertaking the vows of a bodhisattva;

and those oceans of dharmas consisting of the firm undertakings of a bodhisattva, which involve the practice of enduring the ill-deeds, harsh words, and evil thoughts of all realms of sentient beings.
The applications for enduring physical and mental afflictions;

that which is the patience regarding the nature of the non-perishing of all karma, the patience of conviction in all phenomena, and the patience of contemplation on the intrinsic nature of all phenomena;
and that which is the vigor of the application and undertaking toward omniscience.

That which is the vigor for the complete accomplishment of all Buddha-qualities; those practices of the perfection of vigor; the accumulations of the perfection of meditation, the applications to the perfection of meditation, and the pure practices for the complete accomplishment of the perfection of meditation;
and those miraculous displays resulting from the attainment of the bodhisattva samādhis.
Those entries into oceans of gateways to meditative concentration,
those practices of the perfection of meditation, and those accumulations of the perfection of wisdom;
Those methods for purifying the solar disc of the great wisdom of the Bodhisattva;
those arising from the great cloud of wisdom;
and those accumulations which are the treasury of wisdom.
Those applications of the method for investigating the great ocean of great wisdom;
those applications of the method of great skill in means;
and those former practices associated with the purification of great skill in means.
Those which are the bodies of the great perfections of the bodhisattva’s great vows,
those which are the completions of the great perfections of the great vows,
and those which are the practices of the great perfections of the great vows—
Those former practices associated with the perfection of the great vows,
those great accumulations for the attainment of the perfection of power,
and those conditions for the perfection of power;
Those great oceans of the method of the perfection of power,
those expositions of the perfection of power, and those past accounts associated with the perfection of power;
Those which are the methods of the perfection of wisdom,
those which are the applications of the perfection of wisdom, and those which are the methods for the purification of the perfection of wisdom.
Whatever directions there are of the perfection of wisdom, whatever followings of the perfection of wisdom there are, and whatever expansions of the perfection of wisdom there are—

Those which are the convergences upon the method of the perfection of wisdom, those which are the methods of the communication of the perfection of wisdom, and those which are the followings of the expansion of the perfection of wisdom;
those which are the pervasions of the perfection of wisdom,
those which are the expansions of the perfection of wisdom,
and those which are the bodies of the perfection of wisdom;
Those methods that are oceans of the perfection of wisdom;
those former practices associated with the complete accomplishment of the perfection of wisdom;
and those origins, attainments, and realizations consisting of the entry into and the discernment of the various modes of practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Those dharmas associated with the method of convergence into the perfection of wisdom, which follow the knowledge of the inclusion of dharma and non-dharma,
follow the knowledge of karma, follow the knowledge of fields, follow the knowledge of eons, follow the knowledge of the three times, follow the knowledge of the arising of Buddhas,

follow the knowledge of the Buddhas, follow the knowledge of the Bodhisattvas, follow the knowledge of the origination of the Bodhisattva-mind, and follow the knowledge of the establishment of the Bodhisattvas.
They follow the knowledge of the arising of bodhisattvas; they follow the knowledge of the setting forth of bodhisattvas;
they follow the knowledge of the vows of bodhisattvas.
They follow the knowledge of the Bodhisattva’s wheel of Dharma; they follow the knowledge of the Bodhisattva’s discernment of phenomena;
they follow the knowledge of the Bodhisattva’s ocean-like method of the Dharma.
They follow the knowledge of the ocean of bodhisattva dharmas;
they follow the knowledge of the turning of the wheel of bodhisattva dharmas;
they follow the knowledge of the treasury of bodhisattva dharmas.
He saw the Bodhisattva-dharmas that follow the knowledge of the course of the Bodhisattva-dharmas—
those Bodhisattva-dharmas associated with the perfection of knowledge regarding objects of focus that are infinite and without middle, belonging to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā—
and he saw them ripening sentient beings as they issued forth from every single pore of her body as clouds of multicolored bodies of beings emerging from each individual pore.

That is to say, he saw [the Bodhisattva] maturing sentient beings by emitting clouds of bodies resembling those of the gods of the Akaniṣṭha, Sudarśana, Sudṛśa, Atapa, Bṛhat, and Śuddhāvāsa heavens. Likewise, he saw him maturing sentient beings by emitting clouds of bodies resembling those of the gods of the Bṛhatphala, Puṇyaprasava, Anabhraka, Śubhakṛtsna, Apramāṇaśubha, and Parīttaśubha heavens.
He saw him maturing sentient beings by emitting clouds of bodies resembling those of the gods of the Śubhakṛtsna, Apramāṇaśubha, and Parīttaśubha heavens.
He saw clouds of bodies resembling the gods of the Ābhāsvara, Apramāṇābha, and Parīttābha realms emerging, ripening sentient beings;
he saw clouds of bodies resembling the gods Mahābrahmā, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmapārṣadya emerging, ripening sentient beings;
and he saw clouds of physical forms resembling the hosts of Apsarases, the gods with their sons, and the sovereign deities of the Vaśavartin heaven emerging, ripening sentient beings.
He saw clouds of beings emerging from his own body, resembling the divine king Sunirmita together with hosts of apsaras and sons of gods, bringing those beings to maturity;
he saw clouds of beings emerging from his own body, resembling the divine king Santuṣita together with hosts of apsaras and sons of gods, bringing those beings to maturity;
he saw clouds of beings emerging from his own body, resembling the divine king Suyāma together with hosts of apsaras and sons of gods, bringing those beings to maturity.

He saw clouds of beings emerging from it who, assuming forms identical to those of the hosts of apsarases, the sons of gods, and Śakra, the king of the devas, were bringing sentient beings to maturity.

He saw clouds of beings emerging from it who, assuming forms identical to those of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the gandharva king, the sons of gandharvas, and the daughters of gandharvas, were bringing sentient beings to maturity.

He saw clouds of beings emerging from it who, assuming forms identical to those of Virūḍhaka, the kumbhāṇḍa king, the sons of kumbhāṇḍas, and the daughters of kumbhāṇḍas, were bringing sentient beings to maturity.

He saw clouds of emanations resembling the Naga King Virūpākṣa, his Naga sons, and his Naga daughters, issuing forth and bringing sentient beings to maturity; he saw clouds of emanations resembling Vaiśravaṇa, the Great Yakṣa King, his Yakṣa sons, and his Yakṣa daughters, issuing forth and bringing sentient beings to maturity;
and he saw clouds of emanations resembling Druma, the Kinnara King, his Kinnara sons, and his Kinnara daughters, issuing forth and bringing sentient beings to maturity.

He saw clouds of beings emerging from the bodies of those resembling Sumati, the lord of the great nāgas, the sons of the great nāgas, and the daughters of the great nāgas, bringing those beings to maturity.

He saw clouds of beings emerging from the bodies of those resembling Mahābalavegasthāma, the lord of the garuḍas, the sons of the garuḍas, and the daughters of the garuḍas, bringing those beings to maturity.
He saw clouds of beings emerging from the bodies of those resembling Rāhu, the lord of the asuras, the sons of the asuras, and the daughters of the asuras, bringing those beings to maturity.
He saw clouds of emanations issuing forth with bodies resembling Yama, the King of Dharma, Yama’s sons, and Yama’s daughters, maturing sentient beings;
he saw clouds of emanations issuing forth with bodies resembling all lords of men, as well as men, women, boys, and girls, maturing sentient beings;
and likewise, he saw clouds of emanations issuing forth with bodies resembling every kind of sentient being included within all realms of existence, maturing sentient beings.
He saw clouds of emanated bodies resembling all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and ṛṣis, bringing sentient beings to maturity;
he saw clouds of emanated bodies resembling the deities of the elements of wind, water, and fire, bringing sentient beings to maturity;
and he saw clouds of emanated bodies resembling the deities of the oceans, rivers, mountains, forests, medicinal herbs, trees, and the earth, bringing sentient beings to maturity.

He saw clouds of emanated bodies issuing forth that were like the deities residing in gardens, cities, the seat of enlightenment, the night, the day, the sky, the directions, and the feet [of the Buddha], maturing sentient beings;

likewise, he saw them pervading the ten directions with clouds of emanated bodies resembling Vajrapāṇi, remaining present before all sentient beings throughout the vast expanse of the principle of the Dharma-realm, maturing them.

And those gateways to the accumulation of the first production of the thought of enlightenment belonging to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā; the methods for the uninterrupted succession of virtuous thoughts achieved in previous births; and the uninterrupted successions of the praise of generating the thought of enlightenment, the uninterrupted successions of the grasping of death and rebirth, the uninterrupted successions of the grasping of physical forms, and the uninterrupted successions of the cycles of names.

The uninterrupted succession of approaching spiritual friends; the uninterrupted succession of encountering the arising of Buddhas; the uninterrupted succession of grasping the words, phrases, and syllables of the Dharma; the uninterrupted succession of the mind that practices the path of the Bodhisattvas;
the uninterrupted succession of attaining meditative concentration; and the uninterrupted succession of beholding the Buddhas resulting from the attainment of meditative concentration.
The uninterrupted successions of the radiance of the eye that perceives buddha-fields; the uninterrupted successions of the wheels of knowledge regarding the succession of eons;

the uninterrupted successions of the succession of knowledge for penetrating the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); the uninterrupted successions of the succession of knowledge for surveying the realm of sentient beings (*sattvadhātu*); the uninterrupted successions of the succession of knowledge regarding death and rebirth for entering the ocean of methods within the realm of phenomena; and the uninterrupted successions of the succession of knowledge for the discernment of the purification of the divine ear.

The uninterrupted successions of gateways for entering the flow of the eloquence that contemplates the minds of the entire realm of sentient beings; the uninterrupted successions of gateways for entering the first divine eye;

the uninterrupted successions of the communication of the first divine ear; the uninterrupted successions of the knowledge of the minds of other beings for the first time; the uninterrupted successions of the knowledge of recollecting the former abodes of oneself and other beings for the first time; and the uninterrupted successions of the conditions for attaining the supernormal power of the formative activity of non-abiding in existence for the first time.

The uninterrupted successions of the pervasive expansion of the great supernatural power and valor of the bodhisattvas; the uninterrupted successions of the attainment of the bodhisattva liberations; the uninterrupted successions of the entry into the inconceivable methods of the ocean of bodhisattva liberations; the uninterrupted successions of the miraculous transformations of the bodhisattvas;

the uninterrupted successions of the valorous strides of the bodhisattvas; the uninterrupted successions of the advances of the bodhisattvas; and the uninterrupted successions of the categories of the bodhisattvas' perceptions.

He saw the successions of uninterrupted entries into the path of the bodhisattva, up to the successions of uninterrupted entries into the very subtle wisdom of the bodhisattva by the night goddess Pramuditā-nayana-jagad-virocanā; these he saw issuing from every pore of her body as clouds of emanation-bodies, teaching the Dharma to sentient beings.
He saw them illuminating, shining, demonstrating, proclaiming, analyzing, expanding, enumerating, pointing out, making known, and summarizing;
he saw some teaching with the sound of the agitation and roar of wind-circles, and others with the resonant sound of the contraction of masses of water.
For some, it was by the sound of the roaring of blazing flames;
for some, by the sound of the thunderous roar of the ocean;
and for some, by the sound of the resonance of the earth’s trembling.

For some, it was by the sound of the thundering roar from the collision and agitation of great mountain kings; for some, by the sound of the sweet resonance and roar from the shaking of celestial cities;
and for some, by the sound of the clashing of divine palaces.
To some with the voice of the Lord of Devas, to some with the voice of the Lord of Nāgas, and to some with the voice of the Lord of Yakṣas.
To some [he spoke] in the language of the lords of gandharvas, to some in the language of the lords of asuras,
and to some in the language of the lords of garuḍas.
for some with the voice of a mahoraga, for some with the voice of a deva, and for some with the voice of a kinnara king;
to some with the voice of the lord of men, to some with the voice of the lord of Brahmā, and to some with the sound of the singing of apsarases;

He saw some beings manifesting the sphere of liberation of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā through the sound of celestial musical instruments being played; some through the resonant sound of the king of jewels; and some through the various sounds of the bodies of all sentient beings.

In this way, through clouds of the bodies of bodhisattvas with the various voices of bodhisattvas, and through clouds of the emanation-bodies of Tathāgatas with the methods of the diverse tones and vocal qualities of the speech of Tathāgatas, he saw the sphere of liberation of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā— her attainment, accomplishment, and perfection arising from her first production of the thought of enlightenment,
along with her playful mastery of liberations— as it was being made known to all sentient beings.
With each single cloud of emanation-forms, he saw, at every moment of thought, unspeakably many Buddha-fields in the worlds of the ten directions being purified;
and he saw infinite and boundless oceans of sentient beings being liberated from all the sufferings of the miserable realms.
He saw the realm of beings, infinite in its center and extent, being established in the prosperity of gods and humans;
he saw oceans of beings, infinite in their center and extent, being lifted out from the ocean of saṃsāra;
he saw oceans of beings, infinite in their center and extent, being established on the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

In every moment of thought, the merchant’s son Sudhana beheld, heard, investigated, entered, penetrated, contemplated, followed, pursued, and thoroughly entered infinite and boundless oceans of sentient beings revolving on the tenth stage; he established himself in equanimity through the power of the inconceivable sovereign majesty and miraculous display of the bodhisattva liberation of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, known as the "Vast Banner of Joyful Samantabhadra."
Because they have practiced in common with him in the past, because they are sustained by the empowerment of the Tathāgata, because their inconceivable roots of merit have reached maturity,
and because they have become vessels for the conduct of Samantabhadra the Bodhisattva.

Then, having attained the ocean-like radiance of the surge of joy of the great bodhisattvas and being empowered by the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, the merchant’s son Sudhana stood before the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā with palms joined in reverence, and he praised the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā with these appropriate verses:

The profound nature of the Victors, in which you have been well-trained for immeasurable eons—you pervade the worlds of the ten directions and proclaim it in succession according to the inclinations of beings. // 1 //

Having realized that [beings] are selfless, without a protector, deluded, devoid of true perception, and perpetually wandering, you displayed mastery over various bodies through supernatural power and thereby disciplined the world. // 2 //

Completely free from fever and profoundly peaceful, with a Dharma-body that is non-dual and pure, you guide the entire world—which does not rely on duality—by the thundering of clouds of emanations. // 3 //
And you never have any dependence upon the aggregates, sense-bases, or elements;
with the sovereignty of a perfect form complete in all its limbs, you discipline the world through your proclamations. // 4 //
Freed from the internal and the external, you have emerged from the ocean born of duality;
within the sea of saṃsāra, you manifest infinite reflections throughout all states of existence. // 5 //
In you there is never any movement, conceit, or agitation, nor any conceptual proliferation;
you teach and guide the world by showing the true nature of phenomena to those fools who delight in conceptual proliferation.
With a one-pointed mind for many eons, through dwellings in oceans of all samādhis, you emit from every pore clouds of emanations in all directions as an offering to the Sugatas. // 7 //
In every moment, you enter into infinite ways of the Buddha's powers;
through your various manifestations, you demonstrate the application of all means of integration according to the needs of each being.
Having surveyed the ocean of existence, variegated by karma and consisting of diverse forms, you teach the unobstructed path regarding all phenomena and purify sentient beings. 9.
"Form" is variegated with characteristics; through the conduct of Samantabhadra, O Goddess, you manifest form in the world according to the inclinations of sentient beings. (10)
Then,

having praised the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā with these appropriate verses, the merchant’s son Sudhana said this to her: "O goddess, how long has it been since you set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?"
"O goddess, for how long have you possessed this bodhisattva liberation called 'The Banner of the Vast, Stainless Impulse of Universal Goodness and Joy'?"
Then the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana with these verses:
"I remember many past eons, more than the atoms of a buddha-field; beyond those, there was a field called Maṇiprabhasukhābha, and therein was an intermediate eon named Praśāntaghoṣa. (11)
It was filled with a hundred thousand times ten million nayutas of four-continent worlds;
it was as vast in measure as a mountain of jewels and was most wonderfully adorned in its central four-continent world.
Filled with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of ten royal cities,
the central capital Gandhadhvaja-maṇiprabhāsa was delightful.
In that city there was a lord of the people, a universal monarch, handsome, endowed with the thirty-two marks and his body adorned with the secondary characteristics. (14)
Spontaneously born within the womb of a lotus, his body possessing a golden hue and sublime radiance, he traverses the sky and pervades the entire land of Jambudvīpa with his light. 15.
He had a full thousand sons, the best of heroes, with excellent forms; he also had a full ten million ministers, all wise, skillful, learned, and intelligent.

Ten full crores of women, resembling celestial nymphs and skilled in the arts of love, attended upon the king with affectionate hearts, benevolent intentions, and minds imbued with loving-kindness. (17)
Thus that great king of the earth dwells by the power of the Dharma over all the four continents, which are richly prosperous and bounded by the circle of mountains. 18.
I was the excellent wife of a universal monarch, with a voice like that of Brahmā and a well-proportioned body; pure-radiant and golden-hued, I shone forth light for a thousand yojanas. (19)
When the rays of the sun had set and the king, together with his sons and retinue, was asleep, and the sound of musical performance had subsided, I went to bed and fell into a pleasant sleep. (20)
In the middle watch of the night, the Buddha Śrīsamudra appeared;
there the Jina displayed infinite miraculous transformations, pervading the ten directions. // 21 //

Śrīpūjita [emanated] oceans of light equal in number to the atoms of all buddha-fields, with bodies of various miraculous transformations, by which he pervaded the ten directions without exception. // 22 //
The earth, together with its mountains, trembled and roared with a thunderous sound when the Jina was born; gods, asuras, humans, and nāgas were all filled with joy when the Jina was born. (23)
Oceans of the Buddha’s emanations issued forth from every single pore;
having pervaded the worlds in the ten directions, they preached the Dharma according to the inclinations of beings.
And all those infinite transformations the Jina displayed for me in my dream;
having heard that profound roar, joy arose within me at the end of the dream. (25)
Ten thousand deities of the night stood above me in the expanse of the sky;
proclaiming the praises of the Jina with divine voices, they addressed me to awaken me. (26)
Arise, O wife of noble mind! This Victor has appeared in your kingdom—he who is difficult to behold even in hundreds of oceans of eons, and who brings happiness and purity. (27)
Filled with joy, I have awakened and beheld a stainless, pure radiance; seeing this light with my eyes, I behold the Buddha at the king of Bodhi trees. (28)
An ocean of light rays, variegated with the thirty-two marks, issues forth from his pores;
it rises up like Mount Sumeru on all sides, to the right and to the left of the Jina.
Seeing this, a joyful thought arose in me: "May I become like this!
And having witnessed the vast miraculous power of the Buddha, I made a sublime vow. (30)
Awakened by me, that king and his retinue of women,
having seen the vast radiance of the Buddha, all became thrilled in body.
Accompanied by ten million yānas, surrounded by many millions of billions of living beings, and with his entire army, he approached the presence of the Jina, O Lord. // 32 //
For no less than twenty thousand years, I performed worship to the Jina;
I offered the seven kinds of jewels, as well as the earth together with the oceans, to the Sugata. (33)

He teaches all the oceans of sūtras, clouds of qualities, and magnificent arrays arising from the ocean of vows— all originating from the Tathāgata— according to the inclinations of beings in the world.
Then that goddess of night, born of compassion, awakened me for my own benefit;
at that moment, a longing arose in me: "May I become like her and awaken those who are heedless. (35)
This was my first aspiration-mind directed toward supreme, excellent enlightenment; while remaining within the ocean of saṃsāra, I was not bound by the cycles of existence. (36)

Ten billion nayutas of Buddhas were honored by me after I had conceived faith; yet, while wandering through saṃsāra among gods and humans, I longed for the pleasures of delighting in sense objects. (37)
The first Jina was Śrīsāgara; immediately after him was Guṇapradīpa.
The third Jina was Ratnaketu, and the fourth Buddha was Gaganaprajña. (38)
The fifth Jina was Kusumagarbha; the sixth Jina was Asaṅgamaticandra. The seventh Jina was Dharmacandraprabhurāja, and the eighth was Jñānamaṇḍalaprabhāsa. // 39 //
There, the moon among bipeds was the ninth, Racanārciparvatapradīpa;
the tenth was Triyadhvaprabhaghoṣa. These were the ones I honored in the Joyous Stage (pramuditā). (40)
Having honored all these lords of men, beginning with these ten as my leaders,
I have not yet attained that eye by which I might cross over this ocean of guidance.
Thereafter, the entire field of beings became radiant with every kind of jewel;
in that eon named Devaśrī, five hundred Buddhas appeared.
The first was Śaśimaṇḍala; the second was Bhāskarapradīpa; the third Buddha was Jyotidhvaja, and immediately after him was Maṇisumeru. // 43 //
Kusumārcisāgarapradīpa, Jvalanaśirīṣa, Devaśirigarbha, Obhāsarāja, Prabhaketu, and the tenth, Samantajñānaprabharāja. // 44 //
Making these ten the foremost, I have honored all those lords of men;
though I delighted in the abode of the aggregates, I regarded the Dharma—which is without an abode—as my dwelling. (45)
Subsequently, in this world-system called Suvicitra, during that very eon, there was a Tathāgata named Dharmapradīpameghaśrī; at that time, he was known by the name Brahmaprabha. (46)
In that place, I have honored immeasurable Jinas along with their retinues;
having conceived reverence, I heard the Dharma from all those Sugatas. (47)
The first Victor was Ratanameru; immediately after him was Guṇasamudra;
then Jina Dharmadhātusvaraketu; and the fourth was Dharmasamudragarjana. // 48 //
Dharmadhvaja, Dharaṇitejas, Dharmabalaprabha, Gaganabuddhi, and Dharmārcimeruśikharābha; among them, the last was named Meghaśrī. 49.
Making these ten the foremost, I have honored all those lords of men;
yet I had not awakened to this true nature of phenomena (dharmatā) by which one may enter these oceans of Jinas.
Immediately after that, there was a Sugata named Sūryapradīpaketuśrī;
his buddha-field was called Buddhamati, and it existed during the aeon known as Somaśiri.
In that [assembly], I made offerings to eighty nayutas of those who possess the ten powers,
through various, infinite, and vast modes of worship, many of which were most beautiful.
The first was Gandharvarāja; the second was Buddhadrumarāja; the third was the Jina Guṇasumeru, and immediately after him was Ratnanetra. (53)
Vairocanaprabhaviyūha, the Buddha Dharmasamudratejaśrī, Lokendratejaśiribhadra, and finally Sarvadharmaprabharāja. // 54 //
Having honored all these Sugatas, making these ten the foremost, I have yet not obtained that wisdom by which I might descend into the ocean of the true Dharma. (55)

Immediately thereafter, there was a field that was perfectly pure, possessing the indestructible and firm splendor of a diamond-jewel; it was a cloud of universal radiance, variegated and established with manifold arrays. (56)

In that [eonic period], many pure beings will be most excellent, drawn away from the stains of the afflictions; it will be an array of the arising of thousands of Buddhas, with peaceful minds and sublime splendor. (57)
The first Jina was Vajranābhi; the second was the bearer of unimpeded power;
the Jina was Dharmadhātupratibhāsa; and [the fourth] was Sarvadikpradīpaprabharāja. // 58 //
The fifth Victor was Karuṇatejas; the sixth Victor was Vratasamudra. The seventh Victor was Kṣāntimaṇḍalapradīpa, and the eighth was Dharmamaṇḍalaprabhāsa. // 59 //
Obhāsasāgaraviyūha was the last among them, followed by Praśāntaprabharāja;
having these ten as my leaders, I made offerings to all those lords of men.

And this true nature of phenomena has not been fully awakened to by me—it is equal to space and pure by its very nature—abiding in which I might wander on my course throughout the expanse of all buddha-fields. (61)
Immediately after that, there was a beautiful field named Gandhapradīpameghaśrī, which was both defiled and purified; at that time, the eon was called Susambhava.
Ten million Jinas appeared there, and those ten eons were adorned by them;
those Leaders taught the Dharmas, which I have retained through the power of my memory.
The first Jina was Vipulakīrti; then Dharmasamudravegaśrīrāja, Dharmendrarāja, Guṇaghoṣa, Dharmaśrī, and Devamakuṭa. // 64 //
The seventh among them was the lord of men named Jñānārcitejaśrī;
the eighth Victor was Gaganaghoṣa, and the ninth was Samantasaṃbhavapradīpa. // 65 //
And the last Buddha among them was named Ūrṇaśrīprabhāsamati;
all those Lords of Men were honored by them, yet this unattached path was not purified.
Immediately following that is the world-system named Ratnadhvajāgramati, which is beautifully arranged and possesses bodies of various wonderful forms made of jewels. // 67 //
And in that eon called Sārocaya, five hundred Buddhas appeared;
he honored them all, those self-arisen ones, desiring this liberation. (68)
First was Guṇamaṇḍala by name, then Śāntanirghoṣa and Sāgaraśrī; then Ādityatejas, Girirāja, Lakṣaṇameru, and Megharutaghoṣa. // 69 //
Dharmendrarāja, Guṇarāja, Puṇyasumeru, and Śāntaprabharāja—
having placed these ten at the head, I have honored all these lords of men.
I have purified the path of the Victors, upon which all the Victors without exception have converged;
yet I have not yet attained that patience which belongs to those who enter this further method of the Victors. (71)
Immediately following that was the world-system named Surucirābha-śāntanirghoṣahāramati; it was completely pure and inhabited by beings with few afflictions. // 72 //
In the eon named Sukhābhirati, there were eighty nayutas of Buddhas;
all those lords of men were honored by me, and the path of the supreme Victors was purified. (73)
The first Jina was Kusumarāśi, followed by Sāgaragarbha, Saṃbhavagiri, Devendracūḍa, Maṇigarbha, Kāñcanaparvata, and Ratanarāśi. // 74 //
Then Dharmadhvaja, Vacanaśrī, and finally Jñānamati Buddha—having honored these ten as the foremost among them, I worshipped those lords of gods and men. (75)
Subsequently, there appeared a field named Sunirmitadhvajapradīpa;
in that place, during an eon called Sahasraśrī, there were many millions of billions of Buddhas. (76)
Śāntadhvaja, Śamathaketu, Śāntapradīpa, Meghaśrīrāja, Obhāsayantaprabharāja, Meghavilambita, and Sūryatejas. // 77 //
Dharmapradīpaśrī, Meruarciśrī, and Devaśirigarbha; and the last among them was Siṃhavinardita, the Lamp of the Wise. // 78 //
Having honored these ten as my leaders, O Moon-like Sugatas, I have not yet attained that patience which allows one to enter this ocean of methods. (79)
Following that, there is a field named Samantābhaśrī;
its eon is called Anālayavyūha, and therein are twenty-six nayutas of Buddhas.
The first was Samantaguṇamegha; immediately after him was Gaganacitta; then the Buddha Susaṃbhavavyūha; and Garjitadharmasāgaranirghoṣa. // 81 //
The Jina Dharmadhātusvaraghoṣa and Nirmitameghasusvaraśrī; the Buddha Samantadiśatejas and Dharmasamudrasambhavaruta. // 82 //
Then, Guṇasāgara, Giripradīpa, and the ninth, Jinasurya, appeared here; finally, among them, Ratanaśirīpradīpaguṇaketu was propitiated. (83)
When that Lord of Men, Ratanaśrīpradīpaguṇaketu, went forth [into homelessness], I was Queen Śaśivakrā; I honored the King as he was departing. (84)
The Lord of Men proclaimed for me this sūtra, the "Array Born from the Ocean of Vows Free from Attachment"; having heard it, I have retained it by the power of my mindfulness.
I have attained the vast eye, the peaceful samādhi, and the power of dhāraṇī;
moment by moment, I behold oceans of Victors throughout the succession of fields.
For within me has arisen the method of loving-kindness, whose essence is compassion, a cloud of universal radiance;
a mind for enlightenment equal to space, vast in its light and immeasurable in its Buddha-powers.
Having seen the world perverted—clinging to permanence, pleasure, and radiance;
shrouded by the darkness of ignorance regarding the true meaning; agitated by afflictions; and possessed of false perceptions—(88)
Wandering in the thicket of views, following the power of craving, and performing uneven deeds, [beings] arise in various forms within the realms of existence, variegated by their karma. (89)
Those who have been born through births by way of the doors of death from all realms of existence experience physical and mental afflictions of birth, old age, and death. // 90 //
Then, for the sake of their welfare and happiness, an unsurpassed thought arose in them:
"May there be the appearance of those possessed of the ten powers throughout the entire expanse of all buddha-fields."
From that, there arose a cloud of vows, whose essence is inclined toward the happiness of all the world;
it is born from the accumulations, infinite, and follows the ocean-like methods of the path.
Possessing a vast splendor like a cloud of departure, with a serene facial radiance extending across all paths,
he emits vast clouds of perfections throughout the expanse of the realm of phenomena.

With vast momentum in traversing the stages, he moves through the methods of all the oceans of the three times; moving with non-attachment through the stages, he reaches all Victors in a single instant. 94.
Moreover, O son of the Sugata, I have entered the conduct of Samantabhadra;
I penetrate the ocean-like method of those ten distinctions within the depths of the realm of phenomena.

"What do you think, noble son? Was that king named Viśāmpati, the universal monarch who existed at that time and on that occasion and remained established for the sake of not severing the lineage of the Buddhas, someone else?
Indeed, noble son, you should not view it in this way.
It was Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta who, at that time and on that occasion, was the king named Viśāmpati, the universal monarch who had set out for the sake of not severing the lineage of the Buddhas."
The night goddess by whom I was awakened was emanated by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
What do you think, noble son— was that queen of the universal monarch named Bhadramati, the jewel among women, someone else at that time and on that occasion?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way:
at that time, on that occasion, I was the wife of the universal monarch named Bhadramati, the jewel among women.
Having been awakened by that night goddess and encouraged toward the vision of the Buddha,

I, noble son, have for this long time generated the mind set on unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Because of that generation of the mind, for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, I have never been reborn in the miserable states or the lower realms.
Constantly and continuously, I have been destined for the realms of gods and humans,
and everywhere I was never separated from the sight of the Tathāgata.

This has continued until the moment I beheld the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnaśrīpradīpaguṇaketu, at which point I attained this bodhisattva liberation called "The Banner of the Vast, Immaculate Impetus of Universal Goodness and Joy."
By the attainment of which I have thus appeared for the purpose of maturing and disciplining all sentient beings.
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called the Banner of the Vast, Immaculate, and Swift Impulse of Samantabhadra’s Joy.

How could I possibly describe those bodhisattvas who, at every moment, have attained the great ocean of the impetus for the setting forth toward omniscience at the feet of all Tathāgatas; and who, at every moment, never cease entering the ocean of great vows through all the gateways of setting forth?
In every moment of thought, they are skilled in accomplishing the mandala of conduct throughout all future eons within the methods of the ocean of all vows;

and in each individual practice, they are skilled in manifesting bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields; and with each single body, they pervade the ocean of all methods within the entire realm of phenomena.

They were skilled in manifesting the conduct of bodies that accord with the inclinations of sentient beings in all buddha-fields within each and every ocean of the principles of the dharma-realm; they were skilled in entering infinite and centerless oceans of Tathāgatas within each and every atom of a field;
and they were skilled in entering the supreme miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas that pervade the entire dharma-realm for each and every Tathāgata.

And [they beheld] the conduct of each individual Tathāgata—those skilled in entering the supreme miraculous displays of the Tathāgatas that pervade the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); those skilled in entering the accumulation and attainment of the provisions for the bodhisattva path throughout the kalpas of the past; those skilled in receiving and upholding the stainless wheel of Dharma of each individual Tathāgata; and those skilled in entering the ocean-like methods of the miraculous displays of all Tathāgatas of the three times.
To know or to speak of his virtues.
Go, noble son;

right here, immediately within this very circle of the Tathāgata’s assembly, dwells a night goddess named Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī. Approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva enter the circle of the bodhisattva's conduct?"
How should it be purified?

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, circumambulated the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā hundreds of thousands of times,
and looking back upon the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā again and again, [departed from] the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.
He departed from his presence. // 34 //
Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, placing his faith in that bodhisattva liberation called "The Banner of the Vast, Stainless, and Swift Impulse of Universal Goodness and Joy" belonging to the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, [proceeded further].
Realizing, entering, extending, pervading, following, pursuing, attaining, cultivating, and thoroughly developing it;

practicing the instructions of the spiritual friends; and in order to achieve uninterruptedness in the teachings of advice and instruction, he recollected the exhortation and instruction sent by the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.
With all the circles of his faculties directed toward every quarter in pursuit of seeing a spiritual friend; with the practice of attaining the sight of a spiritual friend;

with a mental attention seeking a spiritual friend that is free from all pride; with a resolve determined to produce the great equipment [of merit and knowledge]; with the prowess of pleasing a spiritual friend; and with all roots of goodness focused one-pointedly on the spiritual friend—he entered into an unbreakable intention regarding the conduct of a spiritual friend’s skill in all means (*upāyakauśalya*).

Having been born from an ocean of the force of great vigor, which increases through reliance upon spiritual friends, and having made a vow to dwell in equality with all spiritual friends throughout every eon, he approached the presence of the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī.

As he was approaching, the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, in order to manifest the bull-like power of the infinite liberation of bodhisattvas— which reveals the training of the world by facing all worlds—

manifested a body perfected with various primary and secondary marks, and from the circle of hair between her brows, she emitted a ray of light named Samantajñānārciḥpradīpavimalajyotidhvaja, accompanied by an infinite and boundless retinue of rays.
Having illuminated the entire world, that ray descended upon the head of the merchant’s son Sudhana and pervaded his whole body. As soon as the merchant’s son Sudhana was touched by that ray,
he immediately attained the samādhi called *atyantavirajomaṇḍala*.

By virtue of obtaining [this teaching], whatever atoms of light, or atoms of water, or atoms of earth, or atoms of diamond, or atoms of various great precious jewels there may be within that circle of ground in the path between the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā and the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī—

Or whether they were atoms of flower-powder, atoms of jewel-arrays, or atoms of all objective supports— in each and every one of all those atoms, he saw world-systems as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field undergoing dissolution and evolution,
together with their masses of water, masses of fire, masses of wind, masses of earth, and the sentient beings within those world-systems.

They possessed various foundations, various shapes, and various supports; they featured various arrays of earth-surface, various surrounding mountains, various arrays of rivers and ponds, various configurations of oceans, various arrays of celestial and distinct palaces, various forms of trees, and various ornaments of the sky;

they included the ornaments of the cities and palaces of devas, the ornaments of the cities and palaces of nāgas, the ornaments of the cities and palaces of yakṣas, the ornaments of the cities and palaces of gandharvas, and the ornaments of the cities and palaces of asuras.

together with the ornaments of the cities and abodes of the kinnaras, together with the ornaments of the cities and abodes of the mahoragas, and together with the ornaments of the cities and abodes of humans;
[He saw] all the ornaments of the cities and dwellings of all sentient beings situated in every direction and intermediate direction,
including the realms of the hellish states of existence and the realms of the animal realm.
the realms of the world of Yama, the spheres of death and rebirth within the course of human existence, and the various distinct modes of rebirth;
He beheld the convergence of infinite varieties of destinies, and within those world-systems, he saw their diversity; that is to say,
he saw some world-systems as defiled.
some who were completely pure, some who were entirely defiled,
and some whose destinies were purified;
some as defiled-pure,
some as pure-defiled,
and some as entirely pure;
some with flat surfaces,
some standing on their heads, and some with inverted positions;

In those world-systems, among all the destinies of beings and all the births of beings, he saw the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī appearing before every being who was to be disciplined, through her vision that is undifferentiated across all worlds— according to the lifespan of beings, according to their various spheres of inclination,
according to their physical forms, according to their self-designations, speech, designations, etymologies, and conventional usages, and according to their modes of application.
Based on the ripening and disciplining of those [beings] who were under his influence, he saw all sentient beings standing before him without distinction.
Namely: for the sake of turning back the fear of the various sufferings of hell for those beings included within the various states of hell;
for the sake of turning back the fear of devouring one another for those beings born in the various animal realms;
and for the sake of turning back the fear of the sufferings of hunger, thirst, and so forth for those beings included within the realm of Yama.
For the sake of turning back all the suffering and fear of the *nāgas* for those beings included within the *nāga* realm;
for the sake of turning back all the suffering and fear of the desire realm for those beings included within the entire desire realm;
and for the sake of turning back all fear of darkness for those beings included within the human realm during nights of blinding gloom.
For the sake of turning back all fear of disrepute, infamy, and ill-repute for those beings who are attached to such things;
for the sake of turning back the fear of timidity before an assembly for those beings who are attached to that fear;
and for the sake of turning back the fear of death for those beings who are terrified by the fear of death.
For the sake of turning back the fear of falling into the miserable destinies for those beings terrified by the fear of falling into the miserable destinies;
for the sake of turning back the fear of lack of livelihood for those beings terrified by the fear of lack of livelihood;
and for the sake of turning back the fear of the destruction of roots of virtue for those beings terrified by the fear of the destruction of roots of virtue.
For the sake of turning back the fear of losing the thought of awakening in those beings who are terrified by the loss of the thought of awakening;

for the sake of turning back the fear of encountering evil friends in those beings who are terrified by the encounter with evil friends; and for the sake of turning back the fear of being separated from spiritual friends in those beings who are terrified by separation from spiritual friends.

For the sake of turning back those beings who are terrified by the fear of falling into the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, so that they may be freed from the fear of falling into the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas;

for the sake of turning back those who are terrified by the fear of the various sufferings of dwelling in saṃsāra, so that they may be freed from the fear of the various sufferings of saṃsāra; and for the sake of turning back those beings who are terrified by the fear of encountering all things of a discordant nature, so that they may be freed from the fear of encountering all things of a discordant nature.

For the sake of turning back the fear of rebirth in an unfavorable time among those beings who are terrified by the fear of rebirth in an unfavorable time; for the sake of turning back the fear of rebirth in an unfavorable family among those beings who are terrified by the fear of rebirth in an unfavorable family;
and for those terrified by the fear of committing sinful deeds...

He saw her standing before all beings in an undifferentiated manner, for the sake of turning back the fear of committing evil deeds; for those terrified by the fear of the obscurations of karma and afflictions, for the sake of turning back the fear of the obscurations of karma and afflictions; and for those beings terrified by the fear of the bonds of dwelling in the various realms of perception, for the sake of turning back the fear of dwelling in the various realms of perception.

That is to say: because it is brought forth by the power of the vow to protect all sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, or born spontaneously; whether possessing form or formless; whether possessing perception, lacking perception, or neither possessing nor lacking perception—and because it is produced by the force of the ocean-like method of great compassion, through the power of the speed and prowess of the vast bodhisattva samādhis, through the power of the heroic valor of the bodhisattva’s great supernormal knowledges, and through the power of accomplishing the vows and conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, for the sake of pervading the entire world with great love that is free from longing.

Because she was endowed with the bull-like prowess of the vast miraculous displays of the bodhisattva liberations, and because she possessed the application of the knowledge that gathers all beings and increases the force of joy arising from the accumulation of happiness for all beings,
she saw her facing toward the purification of all buddha-fields,
facing toward the realization of the knowledge of all phenomena, facing toward the worship and service of all Buddhas, and facing toward the upholding of the teachings of all Tathāgatas.
It was oriented toward the accumulation of all roots of goodness; oriented toward the increase of all bodhisattva practices; established in being unobstructed toward the minds of all sentient beings;
established in being oriented toward the ripening of the faculties of all sentient beings; oriented toward the purification of the ocean of the inclinations of all sentient beings;
oriented toward turning back all obstructive dharmas for all sentient beings; and oriented toward dispelling the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings.
She saw her facing an inexhaustible succession of all virtues, for the sake of generating the light of the knowledge of the omniscient one.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having seen this inconceivable display of the power and miraculous transformations of the bodhisattva liberation that reveals the training of beings facing all worlds, was born of great joy and attained an oceanic surge of immense delight toward the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī.
Prostrating with his entire body, he gazed upward at her face.

Then, the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī caused that perfection of the pure marks and signs of a bodhisattva’s form to disappear, and she established herself in the form of a night goddess, manifesting all manner of miraculous transformations.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, standing before the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaśrī with palms joined in reverence, at that time spoke these verses:

“I have beheld your vast body, O noble one, adorned with excellent marks and jewel ornaments; it is made beautiful by the various and manifold secondary signs, just as the sky is by the host of stars. (1)

Then there appeared a circle of light, as vast as the atoms within infinite realms, beautiful with its most excellent body, possessing various kinds of incomparable colors and lusters, by which the infinite reaches of all directions were pervaded. // 2 //
From every pore of your body, you emit vast nets of light rays that are equal in number to the minds of all beings;
from the tips of these rays, beautifully adorned lotuses appear, upon which your emanations dwell to bring an end to suffering in the world. // 3 //
You emit clouds and masses of fragrant light, beautiful in every direction and abiding in the form of the world;
raining down flowers from all sides, it pervades all the Victors throughout the realm of phenomena. 4.
Your vast and stainless mass of light is like Mount Meru, the king of mountains ablaze with jewels;
by means of it, you illuminate the entire world and dispel the darkness of delusion. // 5 //
From your mouth, vast, pure clouds of suns constantly issue forth;
they emit the radiance of the solar orb throughout the vast domain of Vairocana.
O Cloud, from your eyes there shall always issue forth the stainless radiance of moonlight;
spreading throughout the world in the ten directions, it illuminates those in the world who are afflicted by the darkness of ignorance.
With your marks, you traverse the directions like a manifested ocean, equal in extent to the body of the world;
pervading the vastness of the realm of phenomena, they bring to maturity all infinite assemblies.
Indeed, your body is seen extending throughout the reaches of all directions, bringing joy to the entire world;
you pacify and subdue every fear, immeasurable as it may be, arising from kings, fire, thieves, and water. 9.
When I was sent to your presence and arrived here reflecting upon your virtues, then a beautiful, stainless circle of light issued forth from between your eyebrows. (10)
Illuminating the directions and hundreds of oceans, producing vast light throughout the world,
and displaying many various miraculous transformations, he then entered into my body.
When the circle of light rays descended upon me, then there arose a wondrous and sublime bliss;
I attained hundreds of dhāraṇīs and samādhis, and I beheld the Jinas in all directions. (12)
When I sought to know the number of atoms in the earth as it was stepped upon in successive strides,
I beheld fields equal in number to the atoms of a field within the dust of a single atom.
Established in the realm of passion, manifold and diverse, there are many hundreds of fields that are not entirely free from affliction;
in these, people experience sufferings amidst the sounds of lamentation, weeping, and cries of distress. (14)
