Furthermore, there are many fields that are defiled and pure, where happiness is slight and suffering is vast; in these places, the compassionate Jinas arise, as do the Jina’s disciples and the Pratyekabuddhas. (15)
Furthermore, there are ways of fields that are pure yet afflicted, accumulated with the array of many bodhisattvas;
they are beautiful to behold, adorned by men and women, where the splendid lineage of the Jinas resides. (16)
This vast and stainless ocean of fields rests upon the atom-dust, following a level surface;
for it was practiced by Vairocana in the past and purified over hundreds of vast eons.
In all the expansions of buddha-fields, the Victors are seen seated upon the best of trees;
awakening to enlightenment and manifesting miraculous powers, they turn the wheel of Dharma and discipline the world.
I see you following her even into the vast realm of Vairocana, where you worship all the Victors with immeasurable thousands of millions of offerings. (19)
Then, having spoken these verses, the merchant's son Sudhana said this to the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī: "It is marvelous, O goddess, how profound this bodhisattva liberation is!
What is the name of this liberation?"
"How long has this been attained by you?
And how does a bodhisattva, practicing in what way, purify this bodhisattva liberation?
He replied, "Noble son, this matter is difficult to realize for the world with its gods, including the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
For what reason?
Because this is the domain of those bodhisattvas who follow the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva— those whose essence is great compassion,
who are dedicated to the protection of the entire world, and who are committed to purifying the paths of all unfortunate states, miserable rebirths, and evil destinies.
Those who have set out for the purification of all fields into the supreme Buddha-field; those who have set out to ensure that the lineage of the Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields is never interrupted;

those who have set out to uphold the teachings of all Buddhas; those who have entered the ocean of great vows consisting of dwelling together with the bodhisattva conduct throughout all eons; those who have set out to purify the light of knowledge free from darkness regarding the ocean of all phenomena; and those who, in a single instant, have attained the dwelling in the light of knowledge concerning the ocean of the ways of all three times.
This is the domain of the bodhisattvas;
nevertheless, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, I shall explain it.

Long ago, noble son, in the past, beyond eons as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, there was an eon named Virajomaṇḍala in the world-system Vairocanatejaḥśrī. It was characterized by the appearance of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru. Furthermore, that world-system Vairocanatejaḥśrī was adorned with palatial abodes made of diamond, arrayed like clouds of every kind of jewel.
Then that world-system was established upon an ocean of all-pure-light jewel-kings; its substance consisted of jewels made of the essence of all fragrant kings;
it was completely pure yet not defiled in its circular expanse; it was covered by canopies of clouds of every kind of ornament; it was surrounded by thousands of circles of jewels of every array;
and its arrays were exquisitely fashioned across hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of four-continent worlds.
Among them, some four-continent world-systems are the abodes of beings whose karma is defiled; some are the abodes of beings whose karma is a mixture of the defiled and the pure;
and some are the abodes of beings who are both pure and defiled, yet possess highly refined roots of virtue and few transgressions.
It was the dwelling place of certain bodhisattvas who were exclusively and utterly pure.

Furthermore, to the east of that world-system Vairocanaśrī, at the junction of the Cakravāla mountains, there was a four-continent world-system named Ratnakusumapradīpadhvajā. Its ground was pure and unsullied; it provided the enjoyment of *śāli* rice that grew without being ploughed or sown, produced through the ripening of past karma. It possessed enjoyments of gabled palaces, mansions, and celestial chariots, was completely covered by wish-fulfilling trees, emitted clouds of fragrance from the constant release of the sheaths of various fragrant trees, and constantly rained down clouds of garlands from various garland-trees.

The trees were laden with various flowers, releasing floods of rain from blossoms of inconceivable color and fragrance; they were constantly emitting powders from trees of many colors, raining down powders of all kinds of perfumes and the finest of jewels; they were illuminated by the radiance emitted from the treasuries of great *maṇi* jewels on various jewel-trees; the trees of divine musical instruments produced sweet sounds released into the expanse of the sky when stirred by winds like clouds of every kind of music;
they brought forth the bliss of day and night through the sun and moon; and the level ground was everywhere illumined by *maṇi* jewels.
In that world-system of four continents, there were indeed hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of royal capitals.
Each individual capital was surrounded on all sides by a thousand rivers;
and all those rivers carried a profusion of various celestial flowers, while their pleasant, sweet sounds resounded like the music of divine instruments.

The banks were adorned with magnificent arrays of trees made of every kind of jewel, decorated with various gems, and provided with boats that moved about for the enjoyment of diverse pleasures according to one's desire.
Within each interval between the rivers, there were established hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of cities;
and each city was surrounded by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of villages.
All those villages, towns, and market towns were surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of divine gardens, palaces, and celestial mansions.
Furthermore, in the center of that four-continent world-system, in the midst of Jambudvīpa, there was a central royal capital named Ratnakusumapradīpā;
it was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-supplied with food, crowded with many people, gods, and humans, and was the abode of beings who had undertaken the ten paths of wholesome action.

Now, in that royal capital named Ratnakusumapradīpā, there was a universal monarch named Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, a sovereign of the four continents who was born spontaneously from within a lotus calyx; his body was adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, he was righteous, a king of Dharma, and possessed of the seven jewels.

He had a full thousand sons who were brave, heroic, possessed of excellent physical forms, crushers of enemy armies, and whose limbs were perfectly complete in every respect. His harem consisted of ten million billion women, all of whom were born from roots of merit similar to those of a universal monarch, shared his conduct, were adorned with bodies of precious jewels, possessed virtuous minds, and were equal in beauty to celestial maidens.
Their bodies were the color of Jāmbūnada gold, with hair-pores from which various divine fragrances were emitted;
their bodies released the pure radiance of divine scents.
He also had ten billion ministers, headed by the Jewel of the Commander-in-Chief.

That universal monarch, King Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, had a wife named Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā, who was a jewel among women; she was beautiful, gracious, and lovely to behold, endowed with an abundance of supreme and most auspicious complexion.

She had deep blue hair and deep blue eyes, a golden-colored skin, and a voice like that of Brahmā; her body constantly emitted a radiance of divine fragrance and light of many colors for a thousand yojanas in every direction.
She expanded [her light].

And from that queen Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā was born a daughter of a universal monarch named Padmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrī, who was perfect in all her limbs, beautiful, gracious, lovely to behold, and such that one could never tire of looking at her.
Noble son, just as no one is ever satiated by the sight of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*),
even so, no one was ever satiated by the sight of that daughter of the universal monarch, Padmabhadrābhirāminetraśrī, with the exception of those who were already satiated by wisdom.
At that time and at that moment, living beings possessed immeasurable lifespans and did not have fixed lifespans.
There was no untimely death. And at that time, a diversity of physical forms among sentient beings was perceived,
as well as a diversity of complexions, a diversity of voices, a diversity of names, a diversity of lineages, and a diversity of lifespans.

There was also perceived a variation in height and girth; a variation in enthusiasm, strength, prowess, and stamina; a variation in what was pleasing or unpleasing to the senses; and a diversity of noble or inferior inclinations.
Among them, those beings who were of beautiful complexion, possessed noble inclinations, had complete limbs, and were handsome and lovely to behold—
They spoke these words: "O man, I am more beautiful than you!
Thus, those beings who possessed well-proportioned bodies looked down upon all those whose bodies were ill-proportioned.
Through that root of unwholesomeness arising from their mutual contempt, they declined even in the measure of their lifespan; they also declined in complexion, in strength, and in happiness.

To the north of that royal capital, Ratnakusumapradīpā, there was a tree of the seat of awakening named Samantāvabhāsanadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja. It manifested at every moment the array of the seats of awakening of all Tathāgatas; its root was of the essence of indestructible vajra-jewel kings, its vast and towering trunk was heaped with all kinds of jewels and gems, and its trunk, branches, twigs, leaves, shoots, flowers, and fruits were composed entirely of every kind of jewel.

It was perfectly formed, beautifully and symmetrically distributed, with branches arranged in equal proportions and hanging down; it possessed an inexhaustible array that radiated everywhere, emitting light like lightning from the flames of various jewels, and resounded with the echoes of the miraculous displays within the domain of all Tathāgatas.

In front of that seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), there was a pond of fragrant water named Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of jewel-trees;
and all those jewel-trees had the same shape as the tree of enlightenment (bodhivṛkṣa).
Furthermore, the shores of that great pond of fragrant water, Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa, were densely covered with various well-arranged jewels and gems.
They were hung with strings of all kinds of jewels, beautified by arrays of all palaces made of pure jewels, and adorned with arrays of all pure ornaments.
Furthermore, the entire site of enlightenment was surrounded on all sides by immeasurable lotus-wombs and great jewel-pavilions of inconceivable arrays.
Moreover, that lake of fragrant water belonging to Ratnakusumavidyuddharmanigarjitameghaghoṣa—
From the center, there appeared a great jewel-king lotus named "Cloud Array Illuminating the Joints of the Petals of the Realm of All Tathāgatas of the Three Times."

There, upon that great lotus, there appeared a Tathāgata named Samantajñānārciśrīguṇaketudhvaja, the first of those Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, who was the very first in that eon to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Having matured sentient beings through hearing the Dharma for many thousands of years, he then matured them for ten thousand years by means of the miraculous manifestation of radiant rays. During those ten thousand years, it was proclaimed that "that Tathāgata will appear. Then, from that great jewel-king lotus—named *Sarvatryadhvatathāgataviṣayapatrasaṃdhividyotitaraśmimeghavyūha*—there issued forth a ray of light called *Sarvasattvavirajaḥpradīpa*.
By that ray of light, those beings who were touched perceived: "In ten thousand years the Tathāgata will appear," and "In nine thousand years that Tathāgata will appear.
Then, from that great Bodhi tree, a ray of light named Virajovatī-śrīgarbhā issued forth.
By whichever ray those beings were touched, they beheld all subtle forms, [hearing] that "that Tathāgata will appear after eight thousand years.
From that very Great Bodhi tree, there issued forth a ray named Sarvasattvakarmavipākanirghoṣā;
by that ray, those beings who were touched entered into the oceans of their respective karmas.
And they obtained the knowledge of recollecting their past karma: "In seven thousand years, that Tathāgata will appear.
From that very Great Bodhi tree, a ray of light named Sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhavanirghoṣā issued forth;
touched by that ray, those beings remained with all their faculties complete and unimpaired: "In six thousand years, that Tathāgata will appear."
From that very same great Bodhi tree, there issued forth a ray of light named *Nidarśananirghoṣā*, which reveals the inconceivable domain of the Buddhas;
touched by it, those beings manifested through their sublime excellence, [knowing] that "in five thousand years, that Tathāgata will appear.

Furthermore, from that very same great Bodhi tree, there issued forth a ray of light named *Sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhinigarjitapratibhāsavijñāpanā*, which makes known the manifestation of the purification of all Buddha-fields.
By that [light], those beings who were touched beheld the purification of the Buddha-field in all its aspects, and [perceived] that "that Tathāgata will arise after four thousand years.
From that very Great Bodhi tree, a ray of light named "Lamp of the Non-differentiation of the Domain of All Tathāgatas" issued forth;
by that [light], those beings who were touched entered into the all-pervading miraculous manifestation of that Tathāgata, [perceiving] that "that Tathāgata will arise after three thousand years."
From that very same Great Bodhi tree, there issued forth a ray of light named *Sarvajagadabhimukhapradīpā* (The Lamp Facing All Worlds),
by which those beings, when touched, perceived the Tathāgata facing them with resolute faith, [knowing] that in two thousand years that Tathāgata would appear.

From that very same Great Bodhi tree, there issued forth a ray of light named *Tryadhvajñānavidyutpradīpā* (The Lightning-Lamp of Knowledge of the Three Times) and [another] named *Tathāgatapūrvayoganirghoṣā* (The Resounding Sound of the Tathāgata’s Previous Vows).
When those beings were touched by it, they conceived and entered into an ocean of the Tathāgata’s former connections, thinking:
"In a thousand years, that Tathāgata will appear.
Then, from that great Bodhi tree, a ray of light named *Tathāgatapradīpa* (The Lamp of the Tathāgata) which is knowledge free from darkness issued forth.

By that [light], those beings who were touched attained the state of possessing eyes everywhere, in order to behold all the Tathāgatas’ miraculous displays and all the Buddha-fields and their sentient beings; for it was said, "In a hundred years, that Tathāgata will appear.
Then, from that very Great Bodhi tree, there issued forth a ray of light named "The Source of the Roots of Virtue Maturing into the Vision of the Buddhas by All Worlds."
Touched by that [light], those beings conceived the notion of the Tathāgata’s appearance, thinking: "In seven days, that Tathāgata will appear.

Then, from that very same Great Bodhi tree, there issued forth a ray of light named *Sarvasattvapraharṣaprītiprāmodyasamudayanirghoṣā* (The Sound Arising from the Joy, Delight, and Rapture of All Beings), by which those beings touched were filled with a great surge of joy at the sight of the Buddha.
Thus, noble son, having ripened sentient beings for ten thousand years through these and other such immeasurable methods of ripening by means of light rays, on the completion of the seventh day,

he caused that entire world-system to tremble with immeasurable methods of shaking and established it as utterly pure. Furthermore, in every moment of thought, he manifested within that buddha-field all the various inconceivable arrays of the buddha-fields of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions.
Then, during the final week, all those beings in that world-system who had been ripened by the sight of the Buddha stood facing toward the seat of awakening.
Then, indeed, from all the circular mountain ranges,
from all the Sumerus, from all the mountains, from all the rivers, from all the oceans, from all the trees, from all the surfaces of the earth,
from all the cities, from all the walls, from all the palaces, from all the celestial mansions, and from all the garments, ornaments, and articles of enjoyment in that world-system—

From all the trees of musical instruments, from all the ensembles of wind and stringed music, and from every single array of emanations— each from its respective focal point— they resounded with the manifestation of the domain of all Tathāgatas, emitting clouds of all fragrant incense, clouds of all jewel-rays,
clouds containing the essence of all fragrant incense and light, clouds of all fragrant jewel-figures, and clouds of all jewel-garments and precious ornaments.
They manifested clouds of Sumeru mountains of all kinds of jewel-flowers; they emitted clouds of all kinds of aromatic powders; they illuminated clouds of light-rays from all Tathāgatas;
they sent forth clouds of the circles of radiance of all Tathāgatas; they struck together clouds of all musical instruments and cymbals;
they released clouds of the resonant sounds of the vows of all Tathāgatas; and [they produced] clouds of oceans of the sounds of the vocal qualities of all Tathāgatas.
Uttering these sounds and manifesting clouds of diverse appearances of the primary and secondary marks of all Tathāgatas,

they displayed inconceivable portents of the arising of a Tathāgata; then, ten times as many great jewel-king lotuses as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields surrounded that Great Jewel King Lotus— the Padma whose radiance illuminates the petals and joints of the sphere of all Tathāgatas of the three times— and settled upon its awakening.

And upon the filaments and pericarps of those great jewel-lotuses, which were accompanied by retinues of great jewel-kings, there appeared lion thrones containing great maṇi-jewels, equal in number to the atoms of ten buddha-fields. And upon those jewel-containing thrones, bodhisattvas equal in number to the atoms of a hundred thousand buddha-fields appeared, seated cross-legged.
Immediately upon the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja, attaining unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,

at that very moment all the Tathāgatas in the world-systems of the ten directions, having likewise awakened to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, turned the wheel of Dharma before sentient beings according to their inclinations; by means of that,
immeasurable sentient beings were turned away from all miserable states and downfalls from that world-system.
Immeasurable beings were established in rebirth in the heavens;
immeasurable beings were established on the level of the śrāvakas;
immeasurable beings were matured for the awakening of the pratyekabuddhas.
Immeasurable beings were ripened for the awakening that issues from the radiance of momentum;
immeasurable beings were ripened for the awakening of the banner of stainless valor;
immeasurable beings were established in the awakening that issues from the abode of the manifestation of the Dharma.
Immeasurable beings have been matured for the awakening that issues from the cultivation of the purification of the faculties;
immeasurable beings have been matured for the awakening that issues from the practice and realization of the equality of the powers;
immeasurable beings have been established in the awakening that issues from the manifestation of the vehicle within the domain facing the city of Dharma.
Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening that issues from the vehicle of the method thoroughly penetrated by supernatural power pervading everywhere;
immeasurable beings were established in the awakening that issues from the method of the convergence of the application of conduct;
immeasurable beings were established in the awakening that issues from the method of the engagement in meditative concentration.
Immeasurable beings were established in the awakening that issues from the gateway of the mandala of the complete purification of the sphere of all objective referents;
immeasurable beings were inspired to generate the mind directed toward the awakening of a bodhisattva;
and immeasurable beings [were established] on the bodhisattva path.
They have been established;
immeasurable beings have been established in the purification of the path of the perfections;
immeasurable beings have been established in the first bodhisattva stage.

Thus, as that Tathāgata turns the wheel of Dharma through his inconceivable miraculous display of the bull-like power of a Buddha, in every moment of thought, infinite and immeasurable beings [attain] the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth [stages].
Immeasurable beings were established in the tenth stage;
immeasurable beings were introduced to the bodhisattva practice distinguished by its specific vows;
and immeasurable beings were established in the purification of the vows and conduct of the Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

Thus, as that Tathāgata turned the wheel of Dharma through his inconceivable Buddha-power and miraculous display of sovereignty, at every moment of thought, the infinite and boundless realm of sentient beings attained discipline;
and in that world-system, all sentient beings, according to their inclinations, understood the teaching of the Dharma released by that Tathāgata through his various personal forms and skillful means.

Furthermore, in that royal capital named Ratnakusumapradīpā, for the sake of disciplining those beings who were intoxicated with pride regarding their physical beauty, complexion, and sensory enjoyments,
and who were mutually disparaging one another, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra manifested a magnificent form and appearance and arrived at that royal capital.
By his sublime radiance, that entire royal capital was illuminated;
and there was the radiance of that royal capital,
as well as the radiance issuing from the body of the universal monarch Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa.
Whatever radiance belongs to the jewel-woman,
whatever radiance belongs to the jewel-trees, and whatever radiance belongs to the great maṇi-jewel,
Whatever radiance there was from the moon, the sun, the planets, the constellations, and the luminaries,
and whatever radiance there was throughout all of Jambudvīpa—
all of that was no longer perceived.

Just as, for example, when the sun has risen and the darkness has vanished, the light of the moon, the planets, the stars, and the luminaries, as well as the radiance of fire or jewels, is no longer perceived;
even so, overwhelmed by the radiance of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, all other lights in Jambudvīpa were no longer perceived.
Just as, for example, before a statue made of Jāmbūnada gold, a figure made of ink does not shine, does not gleam, does not glow, and does not radiate.
In the same way, in the presence of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, the form-bodies of those beings do not shine,
do not gleam, and do not radiate.
They do not shine.
This thought occurred to them: "Who could this be— a god or a Brahmā— before whom we do not shine, before whom we do not gleam?"
We do not burn, nor do we shine, whether by our body, or by our radiance, or by our purity, or by our complexion, or by our splendor;
nor are we able to grasp his sign.

Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, standing in the sky above the celestial palace of the universal monarch King Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa in the midst of that royal capital Ratnakusumapradīpā,
addressed this to the universal monarch King Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa: "Indeed, that which..."
"Great King, you should know that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha has appeared in the world;
he dwells right here in your own realm, at the seat of enlightenment named Samantadharmāvabhāsadharmameghanirghoṣadhvaja."

Then, indeed, the princess Samantajñānārcipadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā, having seen the physical body of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and having heard the sound of his ornaments and his miraculous radiance, was struck by a surge of great joy and delight;
at that very moment, she formed this thought: "By whatever roots of merit I have accumulated, may I [attain] such [a state]."
May I obtain a body with such ornaments and such marks.
Such was his deportment,
such was his supernatural power;
for by him, having produced illumination for sentient beings on this dark night, the appearance of a Buddha was made manifest.
In the same way, may I also dispel the darkness of ignorance for all sentient beings and create the great light of wisdom;
and wherever I may be reborn, may I never be separated from this spiritual friend.
Then, noble son, the universal monarch Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, together with his fourfold army, together with the seven precious jewels,
and together with his retinue of women, [set out].
Together with his sons, ministers, merchants, and countryfolk,
and with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, he set out from that capital city of Ratnakusumapradīpā, rising a yojana high.
Having ascended into the sky, he pervaded the entire Jambudvīpa and the whole four-continent world-system with a great radiance; then,

in order to inspire all sentient beings to behold the Buddha, he manifested his reflection upon all the jewel-mountains and stood facing all the beings included within that four-continent world-system, so that they might behold that Buddha.
He praised him with a song in verse:
"A Buddha has appeared in the world, the savior of all embodied beings;
let everyone rise and go to see the Guide of the World. (20)
Tathāgatas arise only occasionally, even after tens of millions of eons;
they proclaim the Dharma for the benefit of all embodied beings. (21)
Having seen the world perverted, shrouded by the cataract of ignorance, and struck by the sufferings of saṃsāra, he gave rise to great compassion. (22)
For incalculable tens of millions of eons, you have practiced the conduct of awakening for the sake of maturing sentient beings and for the pacification of all suffering. (23)
For the sake of attaining the nectar of the Buddha’s enlightenment, they relinquished their hands, feet, ears, noses, and heads throughout kalpas of infinite duration. (24)
Guides of the world are difficult to encounter in this world even in ten million eons;
hearing them, seeing them, and attending upon them are never in vain. (25)
This best of speakers is seen seated upon the seat of enlightenment;
having conquered Māra along with his army, he has awakened to supreme enlightenment. (26)
Behold the Buddha-body, from which a mandala of uninterrupted rays of light, emerging in various colors, brings refreshment to the world. (27)
Sentient beings who are illuminated by the countless clouds of light rays issuing from the pores of the Buddha experience incomparable joy. (28)
"With each of your own minds, worship the Leader;
having generated great vigor, let us go into his presence. (29)

Then, indeed, King Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīcūḍa, having exhorted all the beings dwelling in his own realm with these verses, [honored the Buddha] with ten thousand clouds of various offerings perfected by the roots of goodness of a universal monarch.
Raining down from all sides upon the seat of awakening the banner of the sound of the clouds of the Dharma that illuminates everywhere,
he approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja, making the sky covered by clouds of parasols made of every kind of jewel,
and making the sky spread with clouds of canopies of every kind of flower.
He made the sky an ornament covered by clouds of all kinds of garments; he adorned the firmament with clouds of nets of bells made of every kind of jewel;
and he presided over the expanse of the sky, which was adorned by clouds of fragrant rays incensed by oceans of every type of perfume.
He presided over the expanse of space adorned with clouds of arrays of thrones made of all kinds of jewels and draped with garments of precious gems;

he presided over the expanse of space adorned with clouds of raised banners of every kind of jewel; he presided over the expanse of space adorned with clouds covering all celestial mansions and palaces.
Abiding in the expanse of the sky adorned with clouds of all kinds of flowers, abiding in the expanse of the sky adorned by the raining down of clouds of all arrays of offerings,
he approached the feet of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samantajñānaratnarcisrīguṇaketurāja.

Having prostrated with his head at the feet of the Blessed One and circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, he sat down before the Blessed One upon a great jewel-lotus-womb throne that radiated light in all directions.

Then, indeed, the daughter of the universal monarch, Samantajñānaratnārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā, removed her own ornaments from her body and scattered those ornaments over the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja.
Then those ornaments, above the crown of the head of that Blessed One, became a great jeweled parasol of precious gems,
encircled by a network of various wonderful jewels, held by the bodies of the lords of nāgas, perfectly positioned and rounded with all the ornaments upon his body,
surrounded by a circle of ten parasols of ornaments, utterly pure, and possessing a manifold array in the shape of a peaked pavilion.

It was covered by clouds of all kinds of jewel ornaments, overspread with arrays of trees made of the finest of all jewels, and adorned with ocean-like collections of fragrances and the finest of all jewels.

In its center, he beheld a great Bodhi tree named "Hanging Branches of All Jewels Arising from the Dharmadhātu," which displayed infinite intermediate arrays and manifested various circumambulatory arrangements;
there he saw the Tathāgata named Vairocana, surrounded by bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
He saw him surrounded and honored by all the various bodhisattvas who had emerged from the vows and conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, dwelling in inconceivable and undifferentiated arrays;
he also saw all the lords of the worlds facing toward him.
He beheld the infinite and middleless miraculous display of the Buddha Vairocana.
He also entered into the succession of eons of his former bodhisattva conduct,
and he entered into the eons of the dissolution and evolution of that world-system; therein,
he entered into the succession of the lineages of Buddhas of the past in that world-system.
And in that world-system, he beheld the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
he saw him at the feet of all the Tathāgatas, intent upon making offerings to the Buddhas and facing toward the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings;
and he saw all the Bodhisattvas appearing as reflections within the body of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

And there he saw himself following after each and every Tathāgata at the feet of all the Tathāgatas; he saw himself at the feet of all the Bodhisattvas who had attained the bodily reflections of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, in the abodes of all sentient beings, and in those world-systems;
and in each individual world-system, he saw world-systems as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.
along with their joints and arrays,
along with their foundations,
and along with their structures.
with their bodies present,
purified by various arrays,
and completely covered by clouds of various arrays;
Inconceivable and innumerable various conceptualizations, various explanations of the lineages of Tathāgatas, and various entries into the ways of the three times.
those who have entered the expansions of various directions,
those who are included within the expansions of various dharma-realms,
and those who have entered the depths of various dharma-realms;
established upon various levels of space,
with various arrays of the bodhi-tree,
and with various radiances from the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas;
Various arrays of buddha-simhāsanas;

oceans of various circles of assemblies of tathāgatas; various successions of circles of assemblies of tathāgatas; various elucidations of the skillful means of tathāgatas; and various methods for turning the wheel of Dharma by tathāgatas.

He saw them emitting the resonant sounds of the various vocal qualities of the Tathāgatas, teaching the oceans of instructions on the various methods of mantra, and echoing the clouds of various sūtras;
and having seen this, he experienced even more intensely the surges of great joy and serene faith.
As that great surge of joy arose within her, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samantajñānaratnārciḥśrīguṇaketurāja,
proclaimed the sūtra called *Sarvatathāgatadharmacakranirghoṣa*, accompanied by a retinue of sūtras as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
Upon hearing that sūtra, she entered one million gateways of samādhi, which were gentle and pleasant to the touch.
It is just like the consciousness of a fetus that has entered its mother's womb on that very day;
it is just like the manifestation of the karma of sentient beings;
it is just like the cause for the seed and sprout of a *sālakalyāṇa* tree planted on that very day.
In this very way, those samādhis are gentle and lovely; namely,
the samādhi called "Manifesting the Presence of All Tathāgatas," and the samādhi called "Illumination Following the Expansion of All Buddha-fields."
The samādhi called "Entry into the penetration of all three times";
the samādhi called "The resonance of the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas";
the samādhi called "Awakening to the ocean of the vows of all Buddhas."
The concentration named "Proclaiming the Sound of All Departures for Those Oppressed by All the Sufferings of Saṃsāra";
the concentration named "The Array of Vows for Dispelling the Darkness and Obscurity of All Sentient Beings";
and the concentration named "The Unwavering Vow for the Liberation of All Sentient Beings from Suffering."
The samādhi named "Source of the Accomplishment of the Happiness of All Sentient Beings";
the samādhi named "Womb of Unwearied Maturation and Discipline of All Sentient Beings";
the samādhi named "Banner for Entering the Path of All Bodhisattvas."
There is a samādhi called "The Array of the Arising of the Ascending through All Bodhisattva Stages.
With this as the foremost, one hundred thousand doors of samādhi have entered her.

With a mind that is subtle and concentrated, a mind free from agitation, a joyful mind, a comforted mind, a mind free from appearances, a mind following after spiritual friends, a mind focused on the profound object of omniscience, a mind extended like an ocean through the practice of loving-kindness, a mind detached from all attachments, a mind not dwelling within the spheres of the world, and a mind entering the sphere of the Tathāgatas.

Their minds were illuminated by oceans of the forms and colors of all Buddhas; their minds were unshakable, unmoved, unimpeded, indivisible, neither elevated nor depressed, untiring, irreversible, and never despondent;

their minds were intent upon the realization of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, their minds followed the ocean of the principles of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, and their minds followed the principles for the discernment of all phenomena.

A mind intent on entering the ocean of all sentient beings; a mind intent on protecting the entire world; a mind born from the illumination of the vast ocean of Buddhas; a mind intent on entering the ocean of the vows of all Tathāgatas; a mind intent on shattering the mountains of all obscurations; a mind intent on gathering the vast equipment of merit;
a mind directed toward the attainment of the ten powers of a Tathāgata; and a mind that has attained the illumination of the domain of all Bodhisattvas.
With a mind directed toward the accumulation of all the requisites for enlightenment, and with a mind pervading the oceans of all directions, she focused upon the great vow of Samantabhadra.
Through oceans of vows as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields, she brought to fulfillment the former vows of all the Tathāgatas for the sake of purifying her own Buddha-field;

that is to say, for the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings, for the thorough knowledge of the expansion of the oceans of methods of the Dharma-realm, and for the entry into the oceans of methods of the Dharma-realm.

For the sake of entering into the bodhisattva conduct throughout all buddha-fields until the end of time; for the sake of dwelling together with the entire mandala of bodhisattva conduct until the end of time;

for the sake of approaching all Tathāgatas; for the sake of pleasing all spiritual friends; for the sake of fulfilling the worship and service of all Tathāgatas; and for the sake of ensuring that the bodhisattva conduct—which causes the growth and awakening of the wisdom of omniscience—remains uninterrupted at every moment of thought.
With these ten oceans of gateways for accomplishing vows, equal in number to the atoms in ten buddha-fields,
he brought forth his vow within the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, for the sake of accomplishing that vow of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
That Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurāja, stirs up his former roots of merit; he illumines them, reveals them, discloses them, analyzes them, and fully elucidates them;
he makes them firm so that they may not be lost, and he expands them so that they may be widely diffused.
He establishes them for the sake of making omniscience their standard of measure;
that is to say, for the sake of attaining the oceans of the Tathāgata’s former vows, which are beyond numbering, beginning from the first production of the thought of enlightenment.

Long ago, noble son, in the past, ten eons ago, in the world-system called Maṇisūryacandravidyotitaprabhā, during the teaching of the Tathāgata Candradhvajaśrīketa, a girl named Samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā— who had been exhorted by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra— restored a dilapidated image of the Tathāgata seated upon a lotus.
Having been restored, it was painted;
having been painted, it was adorned with jewels.
Having relied upon the bodhisattva Samantabhadra as a spiritual friend, he generated the mind directed toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
By virtue of that root of goodness, she was no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms; she was always reborn among the families of the lords of gods and the lords of men.
In every place, she was handsome, pleasing, and beautiful to behold, endowed with an abundance of supreme and pure complexion.
And she was never separated from the sight of the Tathāgata and the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
And by that very same spiritual friend, she was matured, exhorted, and reminded in each successive birth;
and now, moreover, she has pleased the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra through never ceasing to revere him.
"What do you think, noble son—was that universal monarch named Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīprabhācūḍa at that time and on that occasion someone else?
You should certainly not view it in this way, noble son.
That Bodhisattva Maitreya was, at that time and on that occasion, the universal monarch named King Vairocanaratnapadmagarbhaśrīprabhācūḍa."
Furthermore, noble son, you might think that at that time and on that occasion, the king’s wife named Saṃpūrṇaśrīvakrā was someone else.
You should not view it in this way;
she was this very night goddess named Praśāntarutasāgaravatī.
"She who was seated immediately next to me—
what do you think, noble son, was that at that time and on that occasion someone else who was the princess named Samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way."
At that time, on that occasion, I was the princess named Samantajñānārciḥpadmabhadrābhirāmanetraśrīcandrā.
Because I, while still a girl, had restored the dilapidated image of the Tathāgata Indradhvajaketu within the teaching of that Tathāgata— having it raised up like a lotus—
that became for me the cause leading all the way to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
And when I was encouraged toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, that, noble son, became my first production of the thought of awakening.
And when the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samantajñānārciḥśrīguṇaketurāja, approached me and I scattered ornaments over him, [that too became a cause for my awakening].

Having witnessed the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata and having heard the Dharma from that Blessed One, I then attained this bodhisattva liberation called "The Manifestation of the Training of Beings Facing All Worlds. And I have pleased and satisfied all those Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru.
They were honored with all kinds of requisites, offerings, and hospitality;
and whatever Dharma was taught by those Tathāgatas, all of that was heard by me.
And I have practiced according to the instructions and admonitions of those Tathāgatas;

and I have attained intense reverence for those Tathāgatas, such that by means of that reverence, in a single moment of thought, I behold all those Tathāgatas, those circles of Bodhisattva assemblies, and all those Buddha-fields.

When that world-system Vairocanaśrī had come into being, and when that eon Virajomaṇḍala had passed, there was immediately thereafter a world-system named Maṇicakravicitrapratimaṇḍitavyūhā and an eon named Mahāprabha. In that [eon], five hundred Buddhas appeared.
I have propitiated them all.
And indeed, in that eon called Mahāprabha, there appeared a Tathāgata named Mahākaruṇameghadhvaja at the beginning of the eon;
when he was going forth from the world, I, having become a night goddess, made offerings to him.
Immediately after him, a Tathāgata named Vajranārāyaṇaketu appeared.
While I was a universal monarch (*cakravartin*), I made offerings to him,
and he revealed to me the sūtra entitled *Sarvabuddhotpādasambhava*, accompanied by a retinue of sūtras as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
I heard it and took it up;
immediately thereafter, a Tathāgata named Jvalanārciḥparvataśrīvyūha appeared,
and while I was the daughter of a guild-leader, I made offerings to him.
And by him, for me, the sūtra named *Tryadhvāvabhāsagarbha* was fully revealed, accompanied by a retinue of sūtras as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa;
that too was heard and mastered by me.
Immediately after that, a Tathāgata named Sarvadharmasamudrābhyudgatavegarāja appeared in the world.
When I was an asura king, I honored him,
and he revealed to me the sūtra entitled *The Distinction of the Knowledge of the Depths of the Entire Dharmadhātu*, accompanied by five hundred subsidiary sūtras;
that I heard and mastered.
Immediately after him, there appeared a Tathāgata named Gambhīradharmaśrīsamudraprabha.
When I was a daughter of the Naga king, I honored him by raining down a cloud of wish-fulfilling kingly jewels.
He, in turn, revealed to me a sūtra called *Prītisāgaravivardhanavega*, which had a retinue of one hundred thousand times ten million sūtras.
Having heard it, I took it up.
Immediately thereafter, a Tathāgata named Ratnaśikharārciḥparvatapradīpa appeared. While I was a sea goddess, I approached him and honored him with rains of clouds of jewel-lotuses.
And by him, the sūtra called *Dharmadhātusāgaranayaprabha* was revealed to me, accompanied by a retinue of sūtras as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
having heard it, I took it up and retained it through mindfulness.
Immediately after him, there appeared a Tathāgata named Guṇasamudrāvabhāsamaṇḍalaśrī.

At that time, having become a seer endowed with the five superknowledges, surrounded by sixty thousand seers, and manifesting great miraculous transformations while raining down clouds of fragrant flowers from my mountain peaks, I approached and made offerings to him.
He then proclaimed for me a sūtra called *Anālayadharmapradīpa*, accompanied by a retinue of sixty thousand sūtras.
Having heard it, I took it up;
immediately thereafter, a Tathāgata named Vairocanaśrīgarbha appeared,
and I was then the earth goddess named Samatārthasaṃbhavā.

Accompanied by an immeasurable retinue of earth deities, I approached that Tathāgata for the purpose of making offerings, emitting clouds of jewel-flowers from the treasuries of all the jewel-trees and raining down clouds of all kinds of jewel-necklaces. Then, he revealed to me the sūtra entitled *Sarvatathāgatasambhavajñānākaragarbha*, with its immeasurable retinue of sūtras.
Having heard it from him, I retained it and did not let it perish.

Indeed, O son of good family, after those five hundred Buddhas, the very last Tathāgata to appear in the world was named Dharmadhātugaganapūrṇaratnaśikharaśrīpradīpa. And at that time, I was [a queen] named Abhirāmaśrīvakrā.
I was a dancing girl.

When that Tathāgata was entering the city and a performance had begun, through the power of the Buddha, I stood high in the expanse of the sky and approached him while praising that Tathāgata with a thousand verses.
Then, he emitted from the circle of hair between his brows a ray of light called "The Array Illuminating the Dharmadhātu," and my entire body was suffused with its radiance.
As soon as I was touched by that ray, I attained a liberation called "The Womb of the Revolving Methods of the Dharmadhātu."

Thus, noble son, having taken these as the foremost, I have propitiated all five hundred Buddhas who appeared there in the eon called Mahāprabha, in the world-system adorned with various arrays of jewel-wheels, and I have made offerings to those Tathāgatas.
Whatever Dharma was taught to me by those Tathāgatas,
I remember it all;
not even a single word or syllable from that system of Dharma has been lost to me.
And as I approached each of those Tathāgatas, I accomplished the welfare of immeasurable sentient beings by praising the Buddha-dharma.

And from the presence of each of those Tathāgatas, I obtained an ocean of the body of the Dharma-realm named "Vastness of the Dharmadhātu, the Matrix of Wisdom of the Three Times," which is the illumination of the lightning of omniscience and the convergence and union with all the practices of Samantabhadra.
Even now, noble son, in every moment of thought, Tathāgatas of infinite extent appear before me.
And with the mere sight of all those Tathāgatas, flashes of omniscience—never before attained, never before seen—descend upon my mind.
Yet, I do not waver from the conduct of a Bodhisattva, the Samantabhadra practice.
For what reason?
Because this attainment of the lightning-flash illumination of omniscience is described as being without end or middle.

Then, at that time, the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, further demonstrating that very bodhisattva liberation called "The Manifestation of the Training of Beings Facing All Worlds," addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana in verses through the empowerment of the Buddha:
Listen, Sudhana, to these words of mine, which are profound, difficult to perceive, and hard to fathom;
they contain the method for penetrating all the realms of the three times, and possess the universal radiance of the orb of the light of Dharma. (30)

Listen to this method of detailed exposition: how my first thought was produced for the sake of awakening through the aspiration for the qualities of a Buddha, and how this liberation of awakening was attained by me. 31.
Beyond that, as many eons ago as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, there was here a world-system called Vipula-vimalā, belonging to the Tathāgata Vairocanadhvaja-pradīpa-śrī. 32.
There was an eon called Virajamaṇḍala, in which the lineage of the Jinas remained unbroken;
during that time, as many Daśabala Buddhas free from affliction were born as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru.
In that [eon], the first Sugata was Guṇaketurāja, whose splendor was like the flame of a jewel;
the second was Dharmadhvaja; the third was Śrīsumeru, the Victor; and the fourth Victor was Guṇakesarīśvara. // 34 //
Jina Śāntirāja, Samitāyu, Yaśaparvata, Guṇasumeruśrī, Jinabhāskara, and the Blessed One Śaśimukha—these ten are the first in this system. (35)
The Jina Gaganālaya, Samantaprabha, Diśasaṃbhava, and Smṛtisamudramukha;
the Jina Abhyudgata, Sumeruśrī, and the Sugata Dharmārciparvataśrī. // 36 //
Padmodgata, the compassionate Jina, is the ninth; Dharmadhātukusuma is the tenth.
As he illuminates the ocean of Buddhas, this is the second stage in this method. (37)
Prabhaketurāja, Matijñāna, Jñānamati, Citrārtha, Indraśiri, Devamati;
the Victor Vegarājamati, Jñānaśirī, Avabhāsarāja, and Prabhaketuśirī. (38)
The Jina named Vikrāntadevagati and the tenth, Dharmadhātupaduma—by thus demonstrating this vast method, the third stage occurs within this method. (39)
After him was the Blessed One Ratnārciparvataśrī; after him, Guṇasamudraśrī; then Dharmaprabha, Padmagarbhaśrī, and the Sugata Gaticandranetranayana. // 40 //
Gandhaprabha, Maṇisumeruśrī, Gandharvakāyaprabharāja, Maṇigarbharāja, Śiritejavatī, and the tenth Victor, Praśamarūpagati. // 41 //
Immediately after him were the Victors Vipulabuddhi, Ratnaprabha, Gaganameghaśrī, Varalakṣaṇaśrī, and the Victor Vratamaṇḍala, who was radiant with his own body’s light. // 42 //
The Jina Nārāyaṇavrata, the Jina Guṇacakravālaśrīrāja who is like the summit of Mount Sumeru, the Blessed One Aparājitavratadhvaja, and Drumaparvata was the tenth among those Jinas. // 43 //
The Jina Sālendrarājaśirigarbha, whose radiance is the reflection of the body of Lokendra; the Blessed One Abhyudgataprabhaśrī, whose light is stainless; and Dharaṇitejaśrī. 44.
The Jina Gambhīradharmaguṇarājaśrī, Dharmasāgaranirghoṣamati, Merudhvaja, Śiriprabhāsamati, and the tenth Jina, Ratanarājaśrī. // 45 //
Brahmaprabha, Gaganaghoṣa, and likewise the Jina Dharmadhātupratibhāsaśrī; the Blessed One Ālokamaṇḍalaprabha, and Daśabhedajñānaprabheketumati. // 46 //
Gaganapradīpa, Abhirāmaśrī, Vairocanaprabhaśrī, Sugata; Puṇyaprabhāsaśrī, Śāntaśrī, and the tenth, Mahākaruṇameghaśrī. // 47 //
Then there was the Victor Tathatāprabha, then Balaprabhāsamati, then the Victor Sarvajagābhimukharūpa; after that, the Victor Abhyudgatābhu, and immediately following him, the Victor Samaśarīru.
Then Dharmodgata became a Sugata; immediately after him was Anilavegaśrī;
then Śūradhvaja, Ratanagātraśrī, and the tenth was Tryadhvapratibhāsaprabha. // 49 //
The first was Praṇidhānasāgaraprabhāsaśrī; the second was Vajrāśayagiriśrī;
the third Jina was Harisumeruśrī; [the fourth was] Smṛtiketurājaśrī; and the fifth was Dharmamati. // 50 //
After him was the Victor Prajñāpradīpaprabhaketuśrī; then the Victor Vipulabuddhi; then the Victor Dharmadhātunayajñānagatidharma; and [finally] Samudramatijñānaśrī. // 51 //
Dharmadhara, Ratnadānaśrī, Guṇacakravālaśrī, Meghu the Jina; Kṣāntipradīpaśrī, Tejavativegaprabha, and Śamathaghoṣa the Jina. // 52 //
Śāntidhvaja, Jagatpradīpaśrī, the Buddha Mahāpraṇidhivegaśrī, the Blessed One Aparājitadhvajabala, and the Victor Jñānārcisāgaraśrī. // 53 //

The Lord of Dharma, the Victor of unimpeded mind, whose intellect is like the roar of the ocean of all mantras; he who possesses the glory of the sounds and tones of every musical note, and whose intellect is the sacrificial pillar of fame for those who exercise sovereign power. // 54 //
The Blessed One faces all directions and regions; he possesses a body equal to the inclinations of sentient beings.
The Buddha is the glory of dwelling for the sake of others; the Bhadra-jina is the glory of the body of primordial nature. // 55 //
These were the Jinas who were foremost there at that time, those Victors who became Lamp-makers;
for as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, they were honored by me in the manner of an ocean of Jinas. (56)
Throughout as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, whatever Victors were born, all those Sugatas were honored by me once I had entered this method of liberation. (57)
In the past, for infinite eons, you have practiced this path of liberation; having heard it now, you too shall quickly attain this method before long through your diligent practice. (58)
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "The Manifestation of the Training of Beings Facing All Worlds.
How could I possibly describe the bodhisattvas who dwell amidst the various inclinations of the ocean of bodhisattva conduct that is without end or middle;
who possess diverse mental dispositions and bodies; who have perfected the oceans of their various faculties; and who have thoroughly penetrated the manifold vows of bodhisattvas?
To understand their conduct or to speak of their virtues.
Go, son of good family! Right here at this seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) is the night goddess named Praśāntarutasāgaravatī,
who sits upon a lotus throne immediately behind me on a lap adorned with a king of jewels marked by a flame-banner, accompanied by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of incalculable night goddesses.
Go to her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, circumambulated the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī hundreds of thousands of times,
and looking back at her again and again, departed from the presence of the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī. // 35 //
(Gv 220) 38. Praśāntarutasāgaravatī.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana [received] from the night goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī that manifestation of the training of beings facing all worlds.

Cultivating, entering, resolving upon, plunging into, expanding, pervading, mastering, illuminating, and fully embracing the liberation of the bodhisattvas, he approached the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī;
having arrived there, he bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī.

Having circumambulated the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī hundreds of thousands of times, he stood before the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī with palms joined in reverence and said this: "Noble goddess, I have set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Relying upon spiritual friends and training in the conduct of a bodhisattva, I am entering into the bodhisattva path."
"Engaging in the conduct of a bodhisattva and established in the conduct of a bodhisattva, I desire to set forth toward omniscience.
Therefore, noble goddess, tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, and how should they practice?"
Then the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
It is well that you, by relying upon a spiritual friend, seek out the ocean of the bodhisattva's conduct.
Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called 'The Array of Moments of Mind Arising from the Impetus of Vast Joy.'"
Sudhana said: "O Goddess, what is your activity? What is your domain? What is your application? What is your sphere of investigation?"
"What is the scope of this Bodhisattva liberation, which is an array of moments of mind arising from the force of vast joy?

She replied: "Noble son, I have entered into the equality of the purification of the ocean of the mind’s intention; I have entered into the indestructible array that is stainless amidst the dust and impurities of all worlds; my mind is set upon an irreversible and non-retrogressive undertaking; my mind is unshakable, adorned with the qualities of a mountain of jewels; and my mind is non-abiding and free from attachment."

Her mind was directed toward the protection of the entire world; her mind was insatiable in beholding the oceans of all Buddhas; her mind was purified in its resolve for the powers of all bodhisattvas;

her mind dwelt in an ocean of mindfulness arrayed with the illumination of great wisdom; and she had set out to cross over the wilderness of sorrow for all sentient beings, being devoted to turning back the suffering and dejection of all beings.
She has set out to turn back the engagement with names, forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles for all sentient beings;
she has set out to pacify the suffering of the separation from the pleasant and the union with the unpleasant for all sentient beings;
and she is devoted to turning back the suffering of delusion arising from the conditions of sense objects for all sentient beings.
She has become a refuge for all beings who have fallen into ruin; she is devoted to demonstrating the escape from the suffering of dwelling in the saṃsāra of all beings;
she has set out to turn back birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair for all beings;
and she has set out to bring about the supreme happiness of the Tathāgata for all beings.
I find satisfaction by providing the means for the well-being of all beings residing in every village, city, market town, district, kingdom, and capital;
I arrange for their righteous protection, defense, and guardianship,
and I gradually bring them to maturity in omniscience.
That is to say, I produce a sense of disenchantment in those beings who dwell in great palaces and celestial mansions; I dispel their various forms of mental distress,
and I teach the Dharma for the sake of severing all attachments and for the thorough realization of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

I teach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings who are gathered with their mothers, fathers, brothers, sisters, kinsmen, and blood relations— those for whom affection has arisen over a long period— in order that they may obtain the company of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;

and for the sake of sentient beings who are gathered with their wives and children, in order that they may abandon the thirst for all the pleasures of saṃsāra, develop a mind of equanimity toward all beings, and attain great compassion.
I teach the Dharma;
I teach the Dharma so that beings situated in the midst of marketplaces may encounter, behold, and assemble with the noble Saṅgha and the Tathāgata;
I teach the Dharma so that beings intoxicated by the pride of wealth may fulfill the perfection of patience.

For those beings who delight in dance, song, and instrumental music, I teach the Dharma for the sake of finding delight in the garden of the Dharma. For those beings who are greedy for the pleasures of the sensory realms, I teach the Dharma so that they may enter into the realm of the Tathāgata. For those beings possessed by anger, I teach the Dharma for the sake of establishing them in the perfection of patience.
I teach the Dharma for the sake of purifying the perfection of vigor in lazy beings;
I teach the Dharma for the sake of causing beings with distracted minds to attain the Tathāgata’s perfection of meditative concentration;
and I teach the Dharma for the sake of turning back the thicket of views and the darkness of ignorance in beings who have fallen into the thicket of views and the darkness of ignorance.

I teach the Dharma so that beings with impaired wisdom may attain the perfection of wisdom; I teach the Dharma so that beings who are attached to the triple world may escape from the suffering of saṃsāra;
I teach the Dharma so that beings of inferior inclinations may fulfill their aspiration for the awakening of a Tathāgata.
I teach the Dharma for the fulfillment of the vow to bring benefit to all sentient beings for those beings who are intent on their own welfare;
I teach the Dharma for the purification of the bodhisattva’s perfection of power for those beings whose resolute intention is weak;
I teach the Dharma for the purification of the bodhisattva’s perfection of wisdom for those beings whose minds are shrouded in the darkness and gloom of ignorance.
I teach the Dharma for the sake of purifying the form-body of those beings with deformed bodies;

I teach the Dharma for the sake of purifying the unsurpassed Dharma-body of those beings with misshapen bodies; I teach the Dharma for the sake of the exquisite golden-colored skin of the Tathāgata and for the purification of a body with the soft touch of kācilindika cloth for those beings of poor complexion.
I teach the Dharma so that suffering sentient beings may attain the ultimate happiness of the Tathāgata; I teach the Dharma so that happy sentient beings may attain the happiness of omniscience;
and I teach the Dharma so that sick and afflicted sentient beings may achieve the perfected body of a Bodhisattva, which is like a reflection.
I teach the Dharma so that beings who are addicted to various pleasures may attain delight in the conduct of a bodhisattva;

I teach the Dharma so that impoverished beings may obtain the treasury of the bodhisattva’s Dharma-store; and I teach the Dharma to beings who have gone to pleasure gardens so that they may apply themselves to the quest for the Buddha-dharma.

I teach the Dharma to beings who have set out upon the path so that they may practice the path to omniscience; I teach the Dharma to beings who have entered villages so that they may attain escape from the entire triple world;
I teach the Dharma to beings who have gone to regions and districts so that they may transcend the paths of the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha and be established in the stage of the Tathāgata.

I teach the Dharma for the sake of illuminating the city of the King of Dharma for those beings who have entered the city; I teach the Dharma for the sake of attaining the knowledge of the equality of the three times for those beings who have gone to the intermediate directions; [and I teach it] for those who have gone to the cardinal directions.
I teach the Dharma so that sentient beings may attain the superknowledge of knowing all phenomena.

For those sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by attachment, I teach the Dharma through the gateway of the foul in order to turn them away from the thirst for delight in all of saṃsāra. For those sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by aversion, I teach the Dharma so that they may enter the ocean of the methods of great loving-kindness.
I teach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by delusion, so that they may attain the superknowledge of wisdom that discerns the ocean-like gateways of all dharmas.

I teach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings whose conduct is characterized by equal proportions of the afflictions, so that they may attain the excellence of the ocean-like methods of aspiration for all vehicles. I teach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings who are inclined toward delighting in the realm of saṃsāra, so that they may turn away from their delight in the realm of saṃsāra.
I teach the Dharma so that sentient beings who are touched by all the sufferings of saṃsāra may remain undefiled by all the sufferings of saṃsāra.

I teach the Dharma to manifest the state of non-arising for those sentient beings who are to be disciplined by the Tathāgata. I teach the Dharma so that sentient beings whose intentions are fixed on the abode of the aggregates may dwell in the sphere of the Dharma that is without abode.

I teach the Dharma for the sake of revealing the specific array of the path to sentient beings whose intentions are withdrawn; I reveal the patient acceptance of the equality of all phenomena to sentient beings who have fallen into excessive pride;
and I reveal the purification of the bodhisattva’s intention to sentient beings whose intentions are occupied with the realm of deceit and guile.
In this way, noble son, having gathered all sentient beings through the gift of Dharma, turning them away from all paths of suffering and miserable rebirths,

showing them the happiness of the prosperity of gods and humans, lifting them out of the triple world, establishing them in omniscience, and maturing them through various gateways of skillful means, I rejoice, having attained the illumination of an ocean of surges of great joy.
I rejoice; I am joyful in mind.
Furthermore, noble son, I am beholding the oceans of circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas in all directions and intermediate directions.

Of Bodhisattvas who have practiced various vows, whose bodies are purified in various ways, who possess various arrays of circles of light, who emit circles of radiance with infinite-colored rays, whose light of wisdom has issued forth from oceans of various methods for omniscience, who have entered into oceans of various samādhis, whose spheres of activity consist of various miraculous transformations, whose voices resound like oceans of various qualities of tone, and whose bodies are adorned with various ornaments.
They had entered into the various methods of the Tathāgatas; their bodies extended throughout the vast expanse of various oceans of realms; they had entered into various oceans of Buddhas;

they had entered into various oceans of the principles of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*); they were illuminated by the domain of the wisdom of the various liberations of the Tathāgatas; they had attained the illumination of various oceans of knowledge; they dwelt in the methods of various oceans of meditative concentrations (*samādhi*); their spheres of activity consisted in the playful mastery of various dharmas, liberations, and disciplines; and they were oriented toward the various gateways to omniscience.

[They were] those who possessed various arrays of the space of the dharma-realm; those who pervaded the sky with various clouds of arrays; those who gazed upon oceans of various circles of assemblies; those who had gathered from world-systems with various surges of joy; those who followed after the expansions of various buddha-fields; those who had assembled from oceans of various directions; those sent forth by Tathāgatas; those who had set out from the feet of various Tathāgatas; and those accompanied by retinues of various hosts of bodhisattvas.

I generate oceans of surges of various joys for those who rain down clouds of various arrays, who have entered the various methods of the Tathāgatas, who investigate the various oceans of the Dharma of the Tathāgatas, who have entered the various oceans of gnosis, and who sit within the illumination of the wombs of various arrays;
having generated these oceans of surges of various joys, they enter, behold, and investigate oceans of the circles of assemblies of the Tathāgatas.
As they contemplate the immeasurability of those powers of the Tathāgata, oceans of great surges of joy arise within them.

Moreover, noble son, as I penetrate the inconceivable purity of the form-body of the Blessed One Vairocana, adorned with the primary marks, I obtain a vast, expansive circle of light that displays oceans of infinite and centerless colors at every moment of thought; beholding this within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), I attain, moment by moment, oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, as I saw great oceans of light rays issuing from every single pore of the body of the Blessed One Vairocana— each equal in number to the atoms within infinite and boundless Buddha-fields—

and as I saw each individual ray accompanied by a retinue of oceans of light rays equal in number to the atoms within infinite Buddha-fields, pervading the entire realm of all Buddhas and pacifying the sufferings of all sentient beings, I obtained oceans of surges of great joy at every single moment of thought.

Furthermore, noble son, as I behold from the head and the two shoulders of the Blessed One Vairocana, at every moment of thought, clouds of mountains of all jewel-flames— equal in number to the atoms of all buddha-fields— issuing forth and pervading the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), I obtain vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, from every single pore of the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, in each moment of thought, there issued forth clouds of light-rays of various fragrances, equal in number to the atoms of all buddha-fields and colored like them, pervading all buddha-fields.
Having seen them, I obtain oceans of surges of joy.

Furthermore, noble son, as I beheld the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, in every moment of thought I saw from each single mark clouds of Tathāgata-forms adorned with marks, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, emerging and pervading the oceans of all world-systems; seeing this, I attained vast oceans of surges of great joy.
Furthermore, noble son, from each and every secondary mark (*anuvyañjana*) on the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, in every moment of thought,
there issue forth clouds of emanated bodies of the Tathāgata, radiant with eighty secondary marks as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields,
pervading the oceans of all buddha-fields and resounding with the roar of the turning of the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
Having seen them, I obtain vast oceans of the impulse of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, as I gazed upon the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, in every moment of thought, from each single pore, I beheld clouds of Buddha-miracles as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields— clouds that displayed the purity and array of the path of the six perfections along with the first production of the thought of enlightenment, and the miracles of ascending through the bodhisattva stages;
seeing these, I attained vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, from every single pore of the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, at every moment of thought, I see emerging clouds of bodies of lords of gods, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, pervading all world-systems.

These clouds display the miraculous transformations of the lords of gods and stand before those beings who are to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of lords of gods, teaching them the Dharma; seeing this, I obtain vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, from every single pore of the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, at every moment of thought, I behold inconceivable clouds of bodies of lordly nāgas— equal in number to the atoms within unspeakable Buddha-fields— performing the miraculous transformations of lordly nāgas and standing before those beings who are to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of lordly nāgas, teaching the Dharma; seeing this, I obtain vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, as I gazed upon the body of that Blessed One Vairocana, in each moment of thought, from every single pore of his skin, I saw clouds of bodies of yakṣa lords, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields,

accompanied by the miraculous transformations of those yakṣa lords, pervading the entire realm of phenomena. Seeing them standing before those beings who were to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of yakṣa lords and teaching the Dharma, I attained vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, as I gazed upon the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, in every moment of thought, from each single pore of his skin, I saw clouds of bodies of Gandharva lords, equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields,

accompanied by the miraculous transformations of Gandharva lords, pervading the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). Seeing them standing before those beings who were to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of Gandharva lords, teaching the Dharma, I obtained vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, as they were beholding the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, in every moment of thought, from each single pore of his skin, there issued forth clouds of bodies of the lords of the asuras, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.

These clouds manifested the miraculous transformations of the lords of the asuras and stood before those beings who were to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of the lords of the asuras.
Seeing those who were teaching the Dharma to sentient beings throughout the entire realm of phenomena, I attained vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, while beholding the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, at every moment of thought, they saw from each single pore of his skin clouds of bodies of Garuḍa lords, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, emerging with the miraculous transformations of Garuḍa lords; and seeing them standing before all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of phenomena who were to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of Garuḍa lords, teaching the Dharma, they perceived those sublime [visions].
I attain oceans of the impulse of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, while gazing upon the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, he saw that in every moment of thought, from each individual pore of his skin, there issued forth clouds of bodies of Kinnara lords as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields; these clouds displayed the miraculous transformations of the Kinnara lords and stood before all beings throughout the realm of phenomena who were to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of Kinnara lords, teaching them the Dharma.
I obtain vast oceans of surges of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, while beholding the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, in every moment of thought, I saw from each single pore of his skin clouds of bodies of great serpent kings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,

emerging with the miraculous transformations of great serpent kings. These appeared before all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of phenomena who were to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of great serpent kings, and I saw them standing face-to-face, teaching the Dharma in a magnificent manner.
I attain oceans of the impulse of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, while beholding the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, he saw that in every moment of thought, from each single pore of his skin, there issued forth clouds of bodies of lords of men, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields. These manifested the miraculous transformations of lords of men; standing before all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of phenomena who were to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of lords of men, they were seen teaching the Dharma with great majesty.
I attain oceans of the impulse of great joy.

Furthermore, noble son, as they gaze upon the body of the Blessed One Vairocana, from each and every pore of his body, moment by moment of thought, there issue forth clouds of bodies of Brahma-kings, equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields. Performing the miraculous transformations of Brahma-kings,

they stand before all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of phenomena who are to be disciplined by the manifestation of the bodies of Brahma-kings, and teach the Dharma with the resonant sound of the voice of Brahma.
Seeing them teaching the sublime, vast dharmadhātu, accompanied by omniscience at every moment of thought,
I obtain oceans of surges of great joy.
I do not obtain what has been obtained before; I do not realize what has been realized before;
I do not enter what has been entered before.
I do not pervade those never before manifested; I do not see those never before seen;
nor do I hear those never before heard.
For what reason?

Although all phenomena are to be fully understood through the characteristic of the intrinsic nature of phenomena, all phenomena nevertheless possess a single characteristic, enter the path of the three times, and are described as being without end or middle.
Noble son, this is but a glimpse of this ocean of methods for the liberation of bodhisattvas called the Array of Moments of Mind Arising from the Force of Vast Joy.
Moreover, this liberation is indeed without end or middle, because it leads one into the ocean of methods of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
This liberation is inexhaustible, because it is inseparable from the production of the mind set on omniscience.
This liberation is infinite, because it is to be known by the eye of a bodhisattva;
this liberation is incomparable, because it pervades the depths of the principle of the undifferentiated realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
this liberation faces all directions, because all miraculous transformations converge upon a single object of focus.
This liberation is unfailing because it is the non-dual practice of the body of all phenomena;
this liberation is unarisen because its practice is like an illusion;
this liberation is like a reflection because it arises as the reflection of the vow for omniscience.
This liberation is like a magical creation, because the conduct of a bodhisattva is perfectly fashioned as such.
This liberation is like the great earth, because it is the refuge for the entire world.
This liberation is like the mass of water, because it moistens the entire world with great compassion.
This liberation is like a mass of fire, because it completely consumes the moisture of craving in all sentient beings;
this liberation is like a mass of wind, because it establishes all sentient beings in omniscience;
this liberation is like the ocean, because it is the repository for the ornaments of virtues of the entire world.
This liberation is like Meru, the king of mountains, because it rises above the ocean of jewels of knowledge regarding all phenomena.
This liberation is like a circle of wind for the array of methods, because it arrays the procedures for the liberation of all phenomena.
This liberation is like space, because it provides the room for the miraculous manifestations of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times.
This liberation is like a great cloud, because it rains down the clouds of Dharma facing toward all sentient beings.
This liberation is like the sun, because it dispels the blinding darkness of ignorance for all sentient beings.
This liberation is like the moon, because it is perfectly polished by the great ocean of merit and wisdom.
This liberation is like a Tathāgata because it is all-pervading;
this liberation is like a reflection because it is perfectly manifested by the dharmas of karma;
this liberation is like an echo because it resounds with the proclamation of all dharmas according to one's inclinations.
This liberation is like a reflection, because it makes itself known to all sentient beings according to their inclinations;
this liberation is like the king of trees, because it is in full bloom with the miraculous transformations of all Buddhas;
this liberation is like a diamond, because its nature is indivisible.
