This liberation is like the wish-fulfilling king of jewels (*cintārājamaṇiratna*), because it brings forth an ocean of transformations that are without end or middle.
This liberation is like the king of pure-garb jewels (*vimalagarbhamaṇirāja*), because there is no obstruction to the perception of the transformations of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times.
This liberation is like the jewel of the banner of joy (*nandidhvajamaṇiratna*), because it possesses the equal resonance of the wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas.

"O noble son, such is this Bodhisattva liberation called 'The Array of Moments of Mind Born from the Force of Vast Joy,' which indeed consists of an instruction following upon the presentation of immeasurable analogies."
Then the merchant’s son Sudhana said this to the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī: “Goddess, by practicing in what way does a bodhisattva attain such a liberation as this?

She replied: “Noble son, these ten are the great accumulations of the bodhisattvas, their great canopies of Dharma, their great expansions, their great radiances, their great illuminations, their great manifestations of power, their great fortunes, and their great distributions.”
They are of great origin and great power,
through the practice of which this kind of liberation is accomplished by bodhisattvas.
What are the ten?

That is to say: the generosity of a bodhisattva is a great canopy of Dharma, extended to satisfy the ocean of all sentient beings according to their inclinations; the ethical discipline of a bodhisattva is a great canopy of Dharma, extended through the practice of entering the ocean of the qualities of all Tathāgatas;
the patience of a bodhisattva is a great canopy of Dharma, extended through the profound realization of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

The vigor of a bodhisattva, which has set forth irreversibly toward the undertaking of omniscience, is a great canopy of Dharma. The meditative concentration of a bodhisattva, which has set forth to pacify the burning afflictions of all sentient beings, is a great canopy of Dharma.
The wisdom of a bodhisattva, which has set forth as the wisdom of the ocean of all phenomena, is a great canopy of Dharma.
The skillful means (*upāya*) of a bodhisattva is a great canopy of Dharma that extends to the ripening and disciplining of the ocean of all sentient beings.

The vow (*praṇidhāna*) of a bodhisattva is a great canopy of Dharma that extends to the oceans of all buddha-fields, for the sake of entering upon the conduct of a bodhisattva in all fields throughout kalpas reaching to the furthest limit of time.

The power of a bodhisattva, which extends throughout the ocean-like principles of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), is a great canopy of Dharma for the sake of never ceasing to manifest perfect awakening in every buddha-field at every moment.

The wisdom of a bodhisattva, which extends through the powers of a Tathāgata, is a great canopy of Dharma for the sake of the cognition of unobstructed knowledge regarding all phenomena of the three times.
Noble son, these are the ten great accumulations and great canopies of Dharma of the bodhisattvas.
For those bodhisattvas who are established in these [dharmas], this very kind of liberation is accomplished;
it becomes purified, comes into being, increases, arises, manifests, is perfected, becomes substantial, becomes vast, is brought to completion, and remains stable.

Sudhana asked, "Goddess, how long has it been since you set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment? She replied, "Noble son, to the east of this world-ocean system called Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra, beyond ten thousand world-ocean systems, there is [a world-system] called Sarvaratnavimalaprabhāvyūha."
There is an ocean of world-systems named [Nāma].
In its center is a lineage of world-systems named Sarvatathāgataprabhāpraṇidhinirghoṣa.
In its center, within the lower world-system, is a world-system named Kanakavimalaprabhāvyūha, variegated by clouds of all kinds of jewels.

It was established upon an ocean of nets of necklaces of all kinds of jewels; its body was an array of vajra-jewel-kings of all fragrances; it had the dimensions and shape of a peaked pavilion; it was pure and unstained; and it was covered by clouds of celestial palaces and mansions.
Therein was an eon named Samantāvabhāsadhvaja (Banner of Universal Radiance).
In that world-system, there was a seat of enlightenment named Sarvaratnagarbhavicitrābha.
There, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata named Avivartyadharmadhātunirghoṣa, fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
And at that time, on that occasion, I was a deity of the seat of enlightenment named Puṇyapradīpasaṃpatketuprabhā, residing at that Bodhi tree.
Having seen that Tathāgata’s miraculous display of perfect enlightenment through her, I conceived the aspiration for unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.
And upon seeing that Tathāgata, I attained the samādhi called "Illumination of the Ocean of Tathāgata Qualities.

Immediately thereafter, in that very world-system, in the royal capital named Samantasaṃpūrṇaśrīgarbhā, at that very seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), a Tathāgata named Dharmadrumaparvatatejas attained perfect enlightenment.
And having passed away from there, I became a night goddess named Jñānaśrīpuṇyaprabhā right at that very seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).

Having witnessed the miraculous display of turning the wheel of Dharma by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmadrumaparvatatejas, I attained the samādhi called "The Sphere of Radiance Equal to the Manifestation of All Worlds."
Immediately after that, right there at that seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), I pleased the Tathāgata named Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣarāja.

Upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi called Sarvadharmabhūmisaṃvardhanasthāna. Immediately after that, right there at that same seat of awakening, I pleased the Tathāgata named Ratnaraśmipradīpadhvajarāja.

Upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi called Cloud of Radiance from All Trees. Immediately thereafter, at that very seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), I pleased the Tathāgata named Guṇasumeruprabhatejas.
Upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi called Illumination of the Ocean of Buddhas.
Immediately after that, on that very same seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), I pleased the Tathāgata named Dharmameghanirghoṣarāja.

Upon seeing him, I attained a samādhi called Dharmasāgarapradīpa. Immediately after that, on that very same seat of enlightenment, while I was a celestial maiden, I pleased the Tathāgata named Jñānolkāvabhāsarāja.
Upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi called "The Illuminating Lamp that Pacifies the Suffering of All Sentient Beings.
Immediately thereafter, on that very seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*),
I pleased the Tathāgata named Dharmavikurvitavegadhvajaśrī.
Upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi named *tryadhvatathāgatasaṃprasthānāvabhāsagarbha*.

Immediately thereafter, at that very seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), I pleased the Tathāgata named *dharmapradīpavikramajñānasiṃha*. Upon seeing him, [I attained] the splendor of the light of the wheel of knowledge that is unimpeded throughout all worlds.
I attained a samādhi.
Immediately thereafter, on that very seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), I propitiated the Tathāgata named Jñānabalaparvatatejas.
Upon seeing him, I attained a samādhi called "The Radiance of the Conduct and Faculties of All Beings throughout the Three Times."
Thus, noble son, at that time in the world-system Kanakavimalaprabhā during that Samantāvabhāsadhvaja eon, I propitiated as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields;
some while I was a lord of gods, some while I was a lord of nāgas, some while I was a lord of yakṣas, and some while I was a lord of gandharvas.
Some were propitiated by him appearing as a lord of the asuras, some as a lord of the garuḍas, some as a lord of the kinnaras, some as a lord of the mahoragas,
some as a lord of humans, some as a lord of the brahmās, some as a deity, some as a human,
some as a woman, some as a man, some as a boy, and some as a girl.
And I have honored all those Tathāgatas with whatever articles of worship were available; I have attended upon all those Tathāgatas,
and I have heard the teaching of the Dharma from all those Tathāgatas.
Having passed away from there, I practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field in that very same world-system;

having passed away from there, I was reborn here in this Sahā world-system, within this ocean of world-systems called Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra. There, I pleased the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Krakucchanda.
And upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi called "The Radiance Free from All Darkness. Immediately thereafter, I pleased the Tathāgata Kanakamuni;
and upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi called "Pervasive Following the Illumination of All Oceans of Realms."
Immediately after that, the Tathāgata Kāśyapa was propitiated;
and upon seeing him, I attained the samādhi called "The Resounding Sound of the Ocean-like Roar of the Mantras of All Beings.
Immediately after that, this Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, was propitiated.

Seeing them manifesting, at every moment of thought, oceans of gateways to the miraculous displays of the Tathāgatas’ perfect enlightenment at that seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), I attained this bodhisattva liberation called the Array of Moments of Thought Arising from the Force of Vast Joy; upon its attainment, [I perceived] as many [Tathāgatas] as there are atoms in ten inexpressibly inexpressible Buddha-fields.
I have entered into oceans of methods for the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

Within all those Buddha-fields contained within these oceans of methods for the entire realm of phenomena, I enter and behold, in each and every atom, as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in ten inexpressible numbers of Buddha-fields.
And in each and every one of those fields, within every single Buddha-field, I behold the Blessed One Vairocana, having reached the supreme seat of enlightenment,
manifesting the miraculous display of perfect awakening at every moment of thought; and by each such miraculous display of perfect awakening,
I see him pervading the entire ocean of methods of the whole realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
And I perceive myself at the feet of each one of those all Tathāgatas;
and whatever those Tathāgatas in those world-systems, having reached the seat of awakening, teach as Dharma, all that I hear.

And those oceans of emanations of all those Tathāgatas, which issued forth from every pore of their skin, thundering oceans of clouds of Dharma and displaying various miraculous transformations throughout the oceans of realms contained within the oceans of directions of the entire *dharmadhātu*, in all lineages of world-systems and in all expansions of world-systems;

I uphold and practice all that they do as they turn the wheel of Dharma through various modes of perception, according to the inclinations of beings born in various states of existence throughout the entire range of all sentient beings.
I contemplate;

I grasp with the *dhāraṇī* that possesses the power and stride of seizing all meanings, words, and syllables; I purify with the wisdom that follows the essence of the purity of the mandala of all phenomena;
and I follow along by means of the superknowledge that discerns the ocean of all phenomena.
I pervade with a vast awareness spanning the three times; I bring about equilibrium through wisdom that accords with the equality of the Tathāgatas;
and I bring forth the methods of all dharmas.
Within the clouds of all phenomena, I manifest clouds of sūtras;
within the clouds of all sūtras, I establish oceans of Dharma; and within the oceans of all Dharmas, I gather together the revolutions of the Dharma.
In all the turnings of the Dharma, I perceive clouds of Dharma;
in all the clouds of Dharma, I generate waves of Dharma; in all the waves of Dharma...
I attain oceans of surges of joy in the Dharma;
within all these oceans of surges of joy in the Dharma, I bring forth the surges of attaining the stages;
and within all the surges of the stages, I bring forth the surges of the oceans of samādhis.
Within the ocean-clouds of all samādhis, I obtain oceans of visions of Buddhas; within the oceans of visions of all Buddhas, I obtain oceans of radiances;
and within all oceans of radiances, I establish the stages of the mandala of knowledge of the three times by means of a yoga that pervades the infinite and centerless oceans of directions.

By means of the yoga of entering the ocean of the immeasurable former practices of the Tathāgatas; by means of the yoga of the illumination of knowledge regarding the ocean of the immeasurable former yogas of the Tathāgatas;
and by means of the yoga of attaining the light of the immeasurable knowledge of the Tathāgatas.

by means of the yoga of the illumination of the purification of the mandala of the immeasurable morality of the Tathāgatas; by means of the yoga of the purification of the stages of the immeasurable patience of the Tathāgatas;
and by means of the yoga of attaining the illumination of the wisdom of valor and the increase of the force of the immeasurable great vigor of the Tathāgatas.
By means of the yoga of attaining the illumination of the practice for purifying the ocean of the meditative attainments of the mandalas of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ dhyāna;
by means of the yoga of the illumination of the cognition that purifies the ocean of the methods of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā);
and by means of the yoga of entering the ocean of the methods of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ perfection of skillful means (upāyakauśalya).
By means of the yoga of entering the ocean of methods for the immeasurable perfections of the vows of the Tathāgatas;
by means of the yoga of attaining the wisdom that dwells together with and increases the immeasurable perfections of the power of merit and gnosis of the Tathāgatas;
and by means of the yoga of attaining the investigation of the ocean of methods for the immeasurable perfections of the gnosis of the Tathāgatas.

By means of attaining the illumination of wisdom that enters the stages of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ former bodhisattva practices; by means of dwelling for oceans of eons in the miraculous manifestations of the transitions as they enter the immeasurable stages of the Tathāgatas;
and by means of entering the circles of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ former bodhisattva stages.
through the yoga of dwelling together with immeasurable Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas on their stages;
through the yoga of purifying the immeasurable stages of the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas; and through the yoga of investigating the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas' gnosis;
By means of attaining the illumination of the immeasurable wisdom of the Tathāgatas;
by means of the cognition that follows upon seeing all the previous Buddhas while having become an immeasurable Tathāgata and Bodhisattva;
and by means of dwelling for oceans of eons while beholding oceans of previous Buddhas while having become an immeasurable Tathāgata and Bodhisattva.
By means of attaining the illumination of the knowledge that produces bodies pervading all oceans of realms without exception, having been former bodhisattvas under immeasurable Tathāgatas;
by means of the yoga of pervading the entire *dharmadhātu* without remainder through the vast former bodhisattva practices of immeasurable Tathāgatas;

and by means of the yoga of manifesting the maturation and discipline of all sentient beings through the various skillful means and joys of the former bodhisattva practices of immeasurable Tathāgatas.
by means of the yoga of the pervasive radiation of the light-rays of all the immeasurable oceans of Tathāgatas in every direction without exception;
by means of the yoga of manifesting miraculous transformations facing sentient beings of the immeasurable Tathāgatas;
and by means of the yoga of the illumination of the wisdom that traverses the stages of the immeasurable Tathāgatas.

By means of attaining the illumination of the wisdom of the miraculous transformations of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ perfect awakening; by means of receiving and upholding without exception the clouds of all dharmas through the turning of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ wheel of Dharma;
and by means of attaining the illumination of the wisdom that discerns the ocean of the immeasurable marks of a Tathāgata.
By means of attaining the illumination that makes known the conduct of the immeasurable oceans of the bodies of the Tathāgatas,
and by means of attaining the illumination of the wisdom regarding the vast domain of the immeasurable Tathāgatas;
and of those Tathāgatas, moment by moment of thought, beginning from their first production of the thought of enlightenment until the disappearance of the True Dharma, I enter into all of it.
Furthermore, as for what you ask— how long it has been since you attained this bodhisattva liberation called the Array of Moments of Mind Arising from the Force of Vast Joy—

I attained it after buddha-aeons as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, beyond that time, in the world-system Kanakavimalaprabhā, when I heard the Dharma teaching of the Tathāgata Avaivartikadharmadhātunirghoṣa from the goddess of the Bodhi tree named Puṇyapradīpasampatsamantaketuprabhā, and [set my mind] upon supreme [enlightenment].

Having generated the mind set on perfect enlightenment and practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva for as many eons as there are atoms in those buddha-fields, they were reborn here in this Sahā world-system and propitiated the Tathāgatas of the Fortunate Aeon, beginning with Krakucchanda and ending with Śākyamuni.
And I shall please all those yet to come;
just as in this world-system, so too in all world-systems I shall please the future lineages of Buddhas.
I shall worship [it].
For even today, noble son, that world-system, Kanakavimalaprabhā, still exists with the lineage of Buddhas uninterrupted.
Therefore, noble son, one should apply oneself here in this method with the great prowess of a bodhisattva.

Then, at that time, the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī, further demonstrating this very Bodhisattva liberation called "The Array of Moments of Mind Arising from the Impetus of Vast Joy," addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana in verses:
"Listen, Sudhana, to these words of mine, regarding how this auspicious liberation was attained."
And having heard it, one should generate the strength of joy and enter this method of liberation. // 1 //
Having practiced throughout an ocean of many eons in the past, he purifies his own mental disposition;
generating the vast force of resolute conviction, he turns toward the city of omniscient wisdom. // 2 //

Having heard of the Sugatas, supreme throughout the three times, and having conceived vast devotion toward them, I have attended upon them and their retinues with every happiness for many hundreds of eons. // 3 //
Having seen the former Sugatas whom I honored while practicing for the benefit of beings, and having heard this incomparable Dharma, a vast power of joy has arisen within me. (4)

At that time, while entering this method of liberation, I constantly honored my mother, father, and elders with benefit and happiness; I performed service for them, remaining established in reverence. (5)
May those who are aged, afflicted by disease, destitute of wealth, those with impaired faculties, the suffering, and the many who are protectorless—
having established them in happiness with a mind of loving-kindness, may I provide them with great riches and become their protector for hundreds of lifetimes.

In former times, while wandering through this city, I protected those who had fallen into the ocean of existence from various fears— those arising from kings, fire, thieves, and water, as well as from lions, elephants, and the terror of enemies.

Those beings in the states of existence, who are constantly scorched by afflictions within the three realms and likewise impelled by unwholesome karmas, have fallen into the precipices of the mountain of saṃsāra; I have protected them throughout the courses of rebirth. (8)

Those fears of falling into the abyss of suffering and miserable rebirths—intense, unceasing, and harsh—and those many fears of birth, old age, death, and disease in the world, have all been entirely extinguished by me. (9)

May my vow extend through future eons until the very end: to pacify the intense sufferings of saṃsāra for all beings, to generate every form of happiness for them, and to bring about the ultimate bliss of a Buddha. 10.
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "The Array of Moments of Mind Arising from the Impetus of Vast Joy.

How could I possibly describe those bodhisattvas who have entered the ocean of methods of the entire realm of phenomena; who are completely liberated from all internal and external suffering without exception; who have attained the knowledge that encompasses the perceptions of all eons; and who are skilled in the knowledge of the arising and passing away of all oceans of world-systems?
To know their conduct or to speak of their virtues.
Go, noble son;
right here at this seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), within the assembly circle of the Blessed One Vairocana, there is a night goddess named Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī.
Approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?
(Gv 231) Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana addressed the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī with these appropriate verses:
"O Goddess, having been instructed by a spiritual friend, I have come into your presence."
I see you seated upon thrones, with bodies of infinite extent. // 11 //

This sphere of yours cannot indeed be known by those who rely on existence through the objects of color, shape, and signs; nor by those who perceive entities, nor by beings of inferior capacity who possess perverted views. (12)

It is not possible for the world, including the gods, to know the cause of your complexion and form, even if they were to observe it throughout infinite eons; for such is your form, which reveals an infinity.

O Goddess, you have risen above the storehouse of the aggregates, yet you are not established in the sense-bases; transcending the world and having cast off all doubt, you are seen manifesting your miraculous powers within the world.

Having attained the imperturbable, you are faultless and unattached; your supreme eye of wisdom has been purified, by which you behold, O Buddha, all the manifestations of the Buddhas performing their miraculous transformations throughout the path of dust, as numerous as all the atoms of dust. (15)
For your body contains the embryo of the Dharma-body, and your mind consists of unattached wisdom;
illuminated by all-pervading radiance, you produce infinite light in the world. 16.
From the mind arises infinite karma; by karma, the entire world is variegated.
Having realized that the nature of the world is the mind, you manifest bodies equal in number to all beings. // 17 //
Having understood this world to be like a dream, and all Buddhas to be like reflections, and all phenomena to be entirely like echoes, you move through the world without attachment. (18)
O Goddess, although you abide in the three times, you manifest your own body to beings at every moment;
yet there is no dualistic activity in your mind, and you teach the Dharma in all directions.
For in this realm of passion, there are indeed infinite great oceans; likewise, the great oceans of sentient beings are immeasurable.
These oceans of the Sugatas, which have no end or center, are the very domain of one who practices the conduct of liberation. 20.

Then, having praised the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī with these verses, Sudhana the merchant’s son circumambulated her hundreds of thousands of times, looked back at her again and again, and departed from the presence of the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī. // 36 //
Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana [attained] that bodhisattva liberation called the Array of Moments of Consciousness Arising from the Impetus of Vast Joy.
Cultivating and honoring it, he recollected the instruction and admonition of the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī;
bringing it to completion,
he recollected the knowledge of the principle of reality (dharmatānaya), which possesses an immeasurable intention through the various methods within each single word and syllable.
Binding [the mind] to mindfulness,
discerning with intelligence,
and following along with comprehension.
Expanding it with the intellect,
dwelling having touched it with the body, and penetrating it.
Entering [the city] in due order, he approached the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī;
there he saw the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī seated upon a great lotus throne whose interior was composed of the finest jewels that illuminate all cities and palaces.
She was seated, surrounded by an inexpressible number of night goddesses; her body faced all directions and all beings of the world; her body was equal in form to the entire world;

her body faced every sentient being; her body was unstained by the entire world; her body was identical in substance to the entire world; her body rose above the entire world; her body was intent upon the ripening and disciplining of the entire world; and she resounded in all directions.
With a body that does not migrate into any world-system; with a body that has utterly eradicated all obscurations; with a body that is the very nature of the Tathāgata;
with a body that reaches the ultimate consummation of the discipline of all worlds.

Having seen her, he was satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness; he bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī, circumambulated the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī hundreds of thousands of times,
and stood before the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī with palms joined in reverence.
Having stood there, he spoke thus: "O Goddess, I have indeed set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Therefore, tell me, O Goddess, how a bodhisattva, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, becomes a benefactor to sentient beings;
and how he gathers sentient beings through the supreme means of attraction."
"How does a bodhisattva, authorized by the Tathāgata, become engaged in the work of a bodhisattva, such that for a bodhisattva so engaged, the King of Dharma becomes near?
When this was said, the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
You, who have reached the culmination of the maturation and discipline of the entire world; who have reached the culmination of the application of sustaining the lineage of all Tathāgatas;

who possess the application of knowledge that radiates throughout the expansion of all directions; who are oriented toward entering the ocean of the methods of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
who pervade both the knowable and knowledge with infinite wisdom equal to the plane of space; and who receive and sustain the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.

You inquire about the method of practice for raining down the clouds of Dharma upon the ocean of all worlds according to their inclinations. Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called "Entry into the Profound Miraculous Display of Pleasing Sounds.
Furthermore, noble son, being endowed with this liberation, I am engaged in the application of focusing upon the bound crown of a great, unimpeded Dharma-preacher.

They have made vows to distribute the entire Dharma-treasury of all Tathāgatas; they have attained the power of great compassion and loving-kindness for the sake of establishing all sentient beings in the thought of awakening (bodhicitta);
they are set out to perform beneficial deeds for all sentient beings in order to accumulate the equipment of roots of goodness through the uninterrupted thought of awakening;
they have set out upon the stage of being charioteers for the entire world in order to establish all sentient beings on the path to omniscience.

In all worlds, they apply themselves as the sun of the Dharma arising from the cloud of Dharma, in order to illuminate all worlds through the production of immeasurable roots of goodness; their minds extend with equanimity toward the entire world without ceasing, for the sake of the knowledge that purifies the application of the formative forces of the roots of goodness of all living beings; they apply themselves with pure minds, having set out to be caravan leaders for all sentient beings by means of skillful conduct in all paths of wholesome action, and they have abandoned all paths of unwholesome action.

They apply themselves to the practice of establishing all sentient beings in wholesome dharmas; they apply themselves to the practice of showing the path of security to all sentient beings; they have set out preceded by the magnificent array of the vehicle for all sentient beings; they apply themselves to the practice of establishing all sentient beings in the turning of the wheel of all wholesome dharmas; they have set out to please and serve all spiritual friends with unbreakable devotion; and they apply themselves to the practice of establishing all sentient beings in the teaching of the Tathāgatas.

I dwell having relied upon spiritual friends, with the undertaking and application of all pure dharmas preceded by the gift of Dharma; with a noble, firm, and indestructible intention born from the arousal of the mind set on omniscience; with a vast circle of mind that takes as its object the firm powers of the Buddhas, which have the essence of Vajra and Nārāyaṇa;

with a mind intent on shattering the mountains of all afflictions and karmic obstructions; engaged in the undertaking of the equipment for omniscience; applied to the practice of the exertion of volition that takes as its object the face-to-face encounter with omniscience, which is without end or middle; and devoted to the application of gathering all pure dharmas.

Furthermore, noble son, while purifying this gateway to the light of the Dharma that makes known all sentient beings, and being established in the accumulation of the equipment of roots of goodness, I survey, follow, and expand throughout the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) in ten ways.
By which ten?
Namely: I follow the immeasurable realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) by attaining the light of vast wisdom;
I follow the realm of phenomena that is without end or middle for the sake of perceiving the miraculous manifestations of all Tathāgatas.

I follow the boundless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) in order to fulfill the worship and service of the Tathāgatas by traversing all Buddha-fields; I enter the limitless realm of phenomena in order to manifest the conduct of a bodhisattva within the oceans of all world-systems;
I enter the uninterrupted realm of phenomena in order to enter the unadulterated mandala of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.

I enter the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) that has attained one-pointedness, in order to enter the mandala of the Tathāgata’s voice which makes known [the Dharma] to all sentient beings according to their inclinations.
I enter the realm of phenomena that is inherently stainless, in order to enter the perfection of my former vows, having reached the ultimate goal of disciplining the entire world.
I enter the realm of phenomena that accords with the equality of the entire world, in order to enter the vast expansion of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

I enter the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) as having a single ornament, for the sake of entering the ornament of the miraculous manifestations of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
I enter the indestructible realm of phenomena, for the sake of the nature of reality that is pure and indestructible through the pervasion of the entire realm of all wholesome qualities.

Noble son, by these ten modes, I survey, follow, and extend throughout the entire realm of phenomena in order to accumulate the equipment of all roots of goodness and to enter into the majesty of the Buddhas.
For the purpose of following after the inconceivable domain of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, noble son, with mental engagements that follow after the majesty of the Tathāgata, I teach the Dharma to sentient beings through ten thousand cycles of the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala.
What are these ten?
Namely: by means of the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala named "The Convergence of the Ocean of All Dharmas."
And by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala that is the empowerment of all phenomena;
by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala that receives all clouds of phenomena;
and by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala that is the lamp of the mindfulness of all Tathāgatas.
And by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala named the Lamp-Womb Containing the Ocean of the Karmas of All Sentient Beings;
and by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala named the Immaculate Convergence of the Ocean of the Methods of All Vehicles;
and by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala named the Resounding Revolving Wheel of the Names of All Tathāgatas.
And by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala called "The Convergence of the Ocean of Vows for the Nirvāṇa of the Buddhas of the Three Times";
by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala called "The Force of the Revolving Toward All Dharmas";
and by the dhāraṇī-maṇḍala named "The Radiance of the Penetration of Omniscience."
And, noble son, having made these ten circles of dhāraṇīs the foremost, I teach the Dharma to sentient beings through ten thousand cycles of the circles of dhāraṇīs.
Furthermore, noble son, I teach the Dharma to sentient beings through the wisdom consisting of hearing;

I teach the Dharma to sentient beings through the wisdom consisting of reflection and the wisdom consisting of cultivation. I teach the Dharma to sentient beings even starting from a single cycle of existence.

(Gv 235) I teach the Dharma to sentient beings even by beginning with the revolutions of all oceans of existence; I teach the Dharma by beginning with the ocean of the names and wheels of even a single Tathāgata;
I teach the Dharma by beginning with even a single ocean of world-systems.
I teach the Dharma even by taking as my starting point the oceans of all world-systems;

I teach the Dharma even by taking as my starting point a single ocean of a Buddha’s prophecy; and I teach the Dharma even by taking as my starting point the oceans of the prophecies of all Tathāgatas.
I teach the Dharma beginning with even a single ocean-like assembly-circle of a Tathāgata;
I also teach the Dharma beginning with oceans of all the assembly-circles of the Tathāgatas.
I teach the Dharma beginning with even a single wheel of the Dharma of a Tathāgata.
I teach the Dharma by taking as my starting point even the oceans of the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; I teach the Dharma by taking as my starting point even a single sūtra;
and I teach the Dharma by taking as my starting point even those sūtras that are the convergence of the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
I teach the Dharma beginning with even a single assembly of the Tathāgatas' circles;
I also teach the Dharma beginning with oceans of all the Tathāgatas' circles of assemblies.
I also teach the Dharma beginning with even a single thought of omniscience.
I teach the Dharma by beginning with the oceans of all the factors of the thought of awakening;
I teach the Dharma by beginning with even a single vehicle; and I teach the Dharma by beginning with the oceans of all the vehicles of departure.
By means of these and other ineffable methods of teaching and accomplishments, noble son, I teach the Dharma to sentient beings.

Thus, noble son, entering into the oceans of Tathāgatas that are inseparable from the principle of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), and effecting the gathering of the unsurpassed Dharma for all sentient beings through my teaching of the Dharma, I have reached the ultimate limit of the conduct of the Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Dwelling together through oceans of eons, I cultivate this bodhisattva liberation that enters into the profound transformations of such delightful sounds,

by means of increasing it in each single moment of thought through the method of cultivating the sphere of this liberation. And with each single method of cultivating the sphere of this liberation, in every moment of thought, I pervade the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
Sudhana said: "It is wonderful, O Goddess, how profound this bodhisattva liberation is!
Noble Lady, for how long have you possessed this bodhisattva liberation?
She replied: "In the past, noble son, in a time gone by as many eons ago as there are atoms in a world-system of cosmic revolutions..."

Beyond eons past, there was a world-system named Dharmārcinagarameghā (Cloud-City-Arcing-Dharma), which was established upon a network of Sumeru mountains made of fragrant jewels as numerous as the atoms in a four-continent world-system; it was adorned with lotus clusters resonating with the sounds of the former vows of all Tathāgatas; its body was an ocean of jewel-kings produced from the ocean of the karma of all sentient beings;
it was shaped like a great lotus; it was both pure and defiled; and it was surrounded by a circular range of mountains consisting of flowers as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru.

There were Sumeru-like mountains of fragrant jewels, as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, rising up as ornaments; there were great sets of four continents, as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, serving as ornaments.
And in each set of four continents, there were unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of cities.
In that world-system, noble son, there was an eon named Vimalaprabha, which gave rise to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru.
And in that world-system called Dharmārcinagarameghā, there was a central four-continent realm named Vicitradhvajā.
In its center was a royal capital named Samantaratnakusumaprabhā.
Not far from that royal capital was a site of enlightenment named Dharmarājabhavanapratibhāsa.

There, upon that site of enlightenment, there appeared a Tathāgata named Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja, who was the first of those Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms within Mount Sumeru. At that time, there was a universal monarch (cakravartin) named Vimalavakrabhānuprabha.
From that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja, he received the sūtra called *Sarvadharmasāgara*. Having received it, he set the wheel of Dharma in motion;
and after [the Buddha] had entered parinirvāṇa, he went forth and upheld the teaching.

At the time when the teaching was disappearing, when the teaching had split into a thousand parts and the exposition of the Dharma had divided into a hundred systems of reasoning, and when the impurity of the final eon had arrived—

[a time] for beings shrouded by the obscurations of all karma and afflictions, for monks who had fallen into quarrels, strife, and disputes, who were indifferent to the virtues of the Buddha’s teaching, devoted solely to sensual pleasures, and delighted in talk of kings and thieves.

For those who delighted in talk of women, countries, and the ocean, and who were devoted to the mantras of the Lokāyata, the righteous one uttered a cry of exhortation to produce a sense of spiritual urgency: "Alas! This great torch of the Dharma, accumulated over many eons, is about to vanish! Thus he delivered a discourse intended to arouse a sense of renunciation.

Rising upward into the expanse of the sky to the height of seven palm trees, he emitted clouds of light rays of infinite colors and projected from his body magnificent arrays of great nets of light in various hues; having thus pacified the heat of the afflictions in the world with his multicolored radiance,
he established infinite and boundless beings in awakening.
And having rekindled that teaching of the Tathāgata once more, it remained for sixty thousand years.
At that time, there was a bhikṣuṇī named Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā, the daughter of that very same universal monarch Vimalacakrabhānuprabha, who had a retinue of one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs.
Upon hearing that sound of spiritual urgency and seeing that great miracle, she and her retinue generated the mind set upon awakening (bodhicitta).
Furthermore, those one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs became irreversible from unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.

She attained the samādhi called "Convergence in the Presence of the Tathāgatas," the dhāraṇī called "Radiance of the Emanations of the Dharma-Wheels of All Tathāgatas," and the perfection of wisdom called "Entry into the Ocean-like Method of All Dharmas. Furthermore, the bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā attained the samādhi called "Lamp Illuminating the Arising of the Teachings of All Tathāgatas."
And he attained this subtle and gentle bodhisattva liberation called "Entry into the Profound Transformation of Delightful Sounds";
by virtue of attaining it, all those miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja became manifest before him.

What do you think, noble son? Was that universal monarch named Vimalavaktrabhānuprabha at that time and on that occasion someone other than the one who, having gone forth in the teaching of the Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja, set in motion the wheel of Dharma?
And when the teaching of the one who has entered final nirvana was on the verge of disappearing, how was the teaching upheld and the great torch of Dharma made to blaze?
Indeed, son of good family, you should not view it in that way.
At that time and at that occasion, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra was the universal monarch named Vimalavaktrabhānuprabha.

What do you think, noble son, was that daughter of King Vimalavaktrabhānuprabha, the universal monarch—named Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā—who had a retinue of one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs, anyone other than this? It was none other than her.
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way:
"Was I at that time, on that occasion, the bhikṣuṇī named Dharmacakranirmāṇaprabhā?
It was I who upheld the teaching of that Tathāgata Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja.
And that entire assembly of one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs was rendered irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;

they were established in the samādhi called "The Convergence in the Presence of the Tathāgata," and established in the dhāraṇī called "The Vajra-Light of the Dharma-Wheel of All Tathāgatas" and in the perfection of wisdom called "Entry into the Ocean-like Method of All Dharmas."
And immediately after that Tathāgata, I pleased the Tathāgata named Vimaladharmaparvatajñānaśikharābha;

Thus, noble son, with this hundred of Buddhas as the foremost, there arose in that Vimalābha eon Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of Mount Sumeru.
Furthermore, noble son, among those Tathāgatas equal to the atoms of Mount Sumeru, the very last was the Tathāgata named Dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparāja.

Indeed, noble son, I have made offerings to all those Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, beginning with Sarvadharmasāgaranirghoṣaprabharāja and ending with Dharmadhātunagarābhajñānapradīparāja;
and I have rendered service to all those Tathāgatas.
I heard the Dharma teachings of them all,
and I went forth in the religious life under the teaching of all those Tathāgatas;
and I upheld the teaching of all those Tathāgatas.

And from the presence of all those Tathāgatas, I have attained this bodhisattva liberation called "Entry into the Profound Miraculous Display of Delightful Sounds" through various methods of attainment;
and from the presence of all those Tathāgatas, I have brought to maturity oceans of sentient beings that are without end or middle.
Since then, as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a Buddha-field have appeared.
I have honored all those Tathāgatas through the practice of the Dharma.
Furthermore, O son of good family, from that time onward, while sentient beings wandering in the night of saṃsāra sleep in the slumber of ignorance, I remain awake;
I protect their city of the mind.
And having raised them up from the city of the three realms, I establish them in the city of the dharma of omniscience.

"Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called ‘Entry into the Profound Transformation of Pleasing Sounds,’ which turns one away from worldly idle chatter, directs one toward non-dual speech, and culminates in the establishment of truth. How could I possibly describe the liberation of those bodhisattvas who, through the knowledge of the nature of all paths of speech being unimpeded, [speak] at every moment of thought?"

They have mastery over the perfect awakening to all phenomena; they have entered the ocean of the sounds and voices of the speech of all sentient beings; they are skilled in the refinement of the ocean of all mantras; they know the methods and principles of the ocean of the enumeration and names of all phenomena; they have mastery over the ocean of dhāraṇīs that encompass all phenomena; they are skilled in producing clouds of Dharma according to the inclinations of all sentient beings; and their conduct reaches its consummation in the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings.
To know their conduct or to speak of their virtues;

to understand the practice of gathering all sentient beings; or to comprehend the unsurpassed undertaking and application of the bodhisattva’s activities, the bodhisattva’s pursuit of subtle gnosis, the preeminent mastery in discerning the treasury of the bodhisattva’s dharma-deposits, and the ascending of the lion-throne for discourse on the bodhisattva’s deeds.
or even to know it. Why is that?
Because those good men have entered the dhāraṇīs of the sphere of the ground of all dharmas.
Go, noble son;
right here at the feet of the Blessed One Vairocana, this night goddess named Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā has assembled, seated immediately behind me.
Go to her and ask: "How do Bodhisattvas train in omniscience, and by practicing in what way do they establish all sentient beings in omniscience?"

(Gv 240) Then, at that time, the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī, further demonstrating this very bodhisattva liberation called "Entry into the Profound Transformation of Delightful Sounds," addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana in verses:
Profound and difficult to perceive is this liberation of the sons of the Victors, which enters into the universal foundation characterized by space;
through it, they do not fail to penetrate all the Victors dwelling in the three times, nor the infinite and centerless expansions of the realm of phenomena. // 1 //

He attains infinite methods of liberation through the arising of the accumulations—dharmic natures that are inconceivable and immeasurable—and he likewise penetrates the universal, unimpeded momentum within the paths of the three times amidst the ways of loving-kindness. // 2 //

Thus, in the past, at the beginning of eons as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, there was a realm named Dharmārcimeghanagara; its world-system was called Śrī and its eon was Vimalābhamahāprabha. // 3 //
In that very eon, within the unbroken lineage of the Victors, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru appeared.
Among them, the Buddha Dharmasamudraprabhagarjitarāja was the first, the leader at the beginning of that eon. // 4 //
The Victor named Dharmameghanagarābhapradīparāja was the very last of those Sugatas;
having approached them all, I made offerings to them and heard their Dharma, giving rise to great joy. (5)

First, I beheld the golden-colored ray of light, the Dharma-king Samudraprabhagarjitaghoṣa; adorned with the thirty-two marks and resembling Mount Meru, upon seeing him, the thought arose in me: "May I become a Sugata. (6)
Upon seeing that Tathāgata, there arose within me a powerful and primordial resolve for supreme enlightenment;
through the conditions for the emergence of the expansion of omniscience, it is as stainless as the realm of space and has suchness as its intrinsic nature. (7)
By which all the Buddhas of the three times, together with the oceans of their sons, are completely pervaded on every side;
and by which all the oceans of fields also become a great ocean arising from the nectar of compassion—may that [ocean] come forth. 8.

My mind has been generated for the sake of pervading all fields without exception with my body, to manifest my body according to the inclinations of the world, to illuminate and shake all fields without exception, and indeed for the sake of ripening all beings. (9)
In the second [vision], even as I approached the Jina, I beheld those Lords of Jinas who abide in the ten oceans of fields;
I beheld the Jina in the final ocean of fields, within fields as numerous as the atoms in the oceans of worlds. (10)

In as many eons as there are atoms in all the revolutions of the fields of the ends of existence, those Victors who have appeared as lamps for the world—I have approached them all and made offerings to them, so that I might thus purify this ocean of the method of liberation. (11)

Then indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana attained the bodhisattva liberation called "Entry into the Profound Transformation of Delightful Sounds"; he descended into an ocean of gateways to samādhis that have no center or limit; his mind was born from an ocean of gateways to vast dhāraṇīs;

he obtained the illumination of the great supernormal knowledges of a bodhisattva; he entered an ocean of the realization of great joy; and his mind increased through an ocean of the force of vast joy.
He praised the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī with these verses of similar form:

"O Goddess, your wisdom indeed ranges through the vast ocean of Dharma; you have traversed the ocean of existence, which is without end or middle. O long-lived one, free from fever, whose womb is the essence of the body of sublime knowledge, you shine forth, having approached this assembly. (12)
Having realized that the nature of phenomena is like the clarity of space, you penetrate all three times without attachment;
you weigh even the objects of perception with non-conceptualization, and in a single moment of mind, they too are found to be inconceivable. 13.
With the eye of wisdom you behold the nature of phenomena as being devoid of sentient beings; yet out of compassion, you descend into infinite oceans of beings.
Plunging with your intellect into the most profound liberation, you guide them all and bring immeasurable numbers to maturity. (14)
You are skilled in the method for investigating the mandala of the Dharma, and awakened to the method for penetrating the intrinsic nature of phenomena;
cultivating the stainless path of all the noble ones, you lead forth the entire world while purifying it. (15)

O Goddess, you are the unsurpassed, supreme charioteer of sentient beings; receiving the stainless wisdom of omniscience, you pervade all beings throughout the realm of phenomena, and by proclaiming the Dharma, you pacify all fear in the world. 16.
O Goddess, by means of the path of Vairocana’s vows, you shall proceed, endowed with vast and stainless intelligence free from attachment;
attaining the power of the Victors everywhere, you shall behold the miraculous transformations of the Victors in all realms.
Your mind is difficult to approach, luminous like the sky, stainless and primordially pure, free from the defilement of all afflictions;
within it converge all the fields of the three times, along with all the Buddhas and their hosts of sons, together with all sentient beings. (18)

Day and night, moments, instants, seasons, fortnights, months, and years—along with the eons of destruction and their conceptual reckonings; even the oceans of eons, numbering as many as the oceans of world-systems, and the oceans of perceptions of living beings—you reveal all these in a single instant. (19)

As many as there were beings passing away and being reborn throughout the ten directions—whether they possessed form or not, and whether they were conscious or unconscious—he, entering by way of the truth of conventional reality, revealed their path and led them onto the supreme path to enlightenment. (20)

Emerging from the family of the net of Vairocana’s vows and from the singular, vast embodiment of all Sugatas, you, whose dharma-body is utterly pure and whose mind is unattached, manifest forms in the world according to the inclinations of beings. (21)
Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having praised the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī with these appropriate verses,
bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī and circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times.
Having circumambulated her again and again and gazed back at her, he departed from the presence of the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥśrī. // 37 //
(Gv 243) 40 Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā. Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana [entered] the bodhisattva liberation called "Entry into the Profound Transformation of Delightful Sounds."
Increasing, honoring, and expanding [his resolve] to a great degree, he approached the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā.

There he saw the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā seated upon a lion throne within the hollow of a jewel-tree sprout, inside a gabled pavilion formed by the branches of trees made of all kinds of fragrant jewels.

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā and standing before her with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus: "Noble goddess, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
And I do not know how a bodhisattva should practice the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should train; therefore,
O goddess, please tell me that.
How do bodhisattvas practice the conduct of a bodhisattva,
how do they train,
and having practiced and trained in what way do they set forth toward omniscience?
When this had been said, the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana:
"By my power, noble son, at the time of the sun's setting in the Sahā world-system, the lotuses bloom and become fragrant.
All the throngs of women in the city, having gone to the gardens and engaged in amorous play, conceive the desire to return home."
Sentient beings who have gone upon the paths become intent on protecting the entire world during the time of night;

those sentient beings who take refuge in mountain clefts, thickets, and caves enter into those mountain clefts, thickets, and caves; and those sentient beings who take refuge in tree dwellings become intent upon their tree dwellings.
Beings who depend on caves enter into caves;
beings who depend on villages, cities, market towns, and districts enter into villages, cities, market towns, and districts;
and beings who depend on water descend into the water.
Beings who have come from other directions and countries produce the thought of their own country and direction in order to dwell in comfort during the night.

Furthermore, noble son, for the sake of counteracting the fear of the great darkness of birth, aging, and death, I praise the application of effort toward the cultivation of roots of merit for those multitudes of men and women— whether young or mature— who are intoxicated by the pride of youth, who are distracted by the pleasures of dance, song, and music, and who are released into the qualities of sensual desire.
I establish beings who are stingy in the practice of giving; I settle beings of immoral conduct in ethical discipline;
and I praise loving-kindness for those beings whose minds are full of malice.
I establish beings with agitated minds in patience; I establish lazy beings in the undertaking of the vigor of a bodhisattva;
I establish beings with distracted minds in the meditative concentrations.
I establish beings of poor wisdom in the perfection of wisdom; I establish beings who are inclined toward the Lesser Vehicle in the Great Vehicle;
and I establish beings who are attached to the triple world and wandering within the mandala that culminates in the realms of existence in the perfection of the bodhisattva’s vow.

I establish in the bodhisattva’s perfection of power those beings who have fallen under the sway of obscurations, who are oppressed by karma and afflictions, and who are destitute of the strength of merit and wisdom.

I establish in the bodhisattva’s perfection of knowledge those beings who are shrouded in the darkness of ignorance and who have entered the gloom of the ignorance consisting of the notions of "I" and "mine."
"Furthermore, noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called 'The Radiance of the Arising of Vast Joy and Contentment.

Sudhana asked: 'O Goddess, what is the scope of this bodhisattva liberation called "The Radiance of the Arising of Vast Joy and Contentment"? She replied: 'Noble son, this liberation is the radiance of the Tathāgata’s merit, the beings, the gathering [of disciples], the wisdom, and the skillful means.'"
For what reason?
Noble son, whatever happiness sentient beings experience,
all of that is through the power of the Tathāgata’s merit, by way of the path of the Tathāgata’s instruction, and through the practice of the Tathāgata’s word.

Noble son, it is indeed through training in accordance with the Tathāgata, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, through practicing the path of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, through planting the roots of merit that belong to the Tathāgata,
through the natural outflow of the Tathāgata’s teaching of the Dharma, through the illumination of the sun of the Tathāgata’s wisdom,
and through the light of the white karma of the Tathāgata’s lineage, that the happiness of sentient beings arises.
For what reason?

Because, noble son, as I was entering this bodhisattva liberation called "The Radiance of the Arising of Vast Joy and Contentment," I beheld the ocean of the former bodhisattva conduct of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One Vairocana.

Recalling, descending, and plunging [into the ocean of the Tathāgata’s wisdom], I know thus and follow thus: how the Blessed One, while taking as his objective the former stage of a bodhisattva, [beheld] sentient beings who were obsessed with the notions of "I" and "mine," fallen into the darkness of ignorance,
entered the dense forest-thicket of views, come under the sway of craving, bound by the fetters of passion, and possessed of minds characterized by hatred and resentment.

Seeing sentient beings whose mental continuums were agitated by delusion, who were shrouded by envy and stinginess, whose minds were overwhelmed by afflictions, who were experiencing the great suffering of saṃsāra, who were oppressed by the misery of the poverty of saṃsāra, and who were turned away from the sight of the Buddha,
a mind of great compassion arose.

A mind that, for the sake of all sentient beings, gathers and maintains the jewels that are the requisites for the entire world; a mind that brings about the requisites for the saṃsāra of all sentient beings; a mind free from grasping at any object; a mind not covetous of any sensory domain; a mind not attached to any pleasures; a mind not greedy for any enjoyments; a mind that does not expect a karmic reward for any giving; and a mind that has no longing for the prosperities of any world.

A mind deluded regarding causes and conditions, a mind that thoroughly investigates and correctly contemplates phenomena as they truly are, and a mind that brings forth reliance upon the welfare of all sentient beings appeared.

Thus, with his mind having entered into the true nature of all phenomena as they are, he has attained equanimity through great loving-kindness toward the realm of all sentient beings; he employs the spreading of the great cloud of compassion for the entire world; he possesses the circle of the great Dharma-umbrella that covers the entire world of sentient beings; he wields the weapon of the great vajra of primordial wisdom that shatters the mountains of the afflictions of all sentient beings; and his mind is intensified by the force of joy arising from the happiness of the entire world.

With a mind of aspiration to bring about ultimate happiness for all sentient beings; with a mind that rains down all things for all sentient beings according to their inclinations and intentions; with a mind of equal application in never abandoning any sentient being; with a mind that satisfies all sentient beings with the wealth of the noble ones; with a mind that attains the supreme jewel of the knowledge of the ten powers; having attained the empowerment of the great superknowledges of a bodhisattva, [he pervades] the realm of phenomena and reaches the limit of the supreme realm of space with a cloud of various great miraculous transformations of a bodhisattva.
Pervading the entire realm of sentient beings and standing face-to-face with all beings, he set in motion a great cloud of all modes and all objects,
raining down a great cloud-shower of all kinds of jewel ornaments— namely,
for the sake of the appropriate enjoyment of all sentient beings, an infinite variety of things in diverse measures and an immeasurable range of conduct regarding various implements.
He followed the practice of gathering all kinds of various gifts, the conduct of relinquishing manifold objects, and the construction of arrays of inexpressible varieties of requisites;

he pursued the diverse accumulation of giving characterized by various marks, which satisfies sentient beings according to their inclinations and follows the method of infinite renunciation; he accomplished the gratification of sentient beings according to their inclinations through the relinquishment and distribution of all things, and applied himself to the protection of the entire world from the suffering of conditioned existence without interruption.
Expecting no recompense from any sentient being, having developed a mind that has attained equanimity toward the entire world, purifying the jewel-like mind of all the world,

increasing the practice of gathering [beings] by raining down the necessary provisions according to the inclinations of all the world— which arises from the ocean of the massed roots of goodness of all Buddhas—

and entering the ocean of merit for omniscience in all the world, he acts moment by moment for the sake of the successive purification of the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings without exception.
He brought them forth:

in every moment of thought, for the sake of fulfilling the circular arrays of the pure ornaments of unsurpassed Buddha-fields, which are untainted throughout the succession of all fields without exception;

in every moment of thought, for the sake of purifying the manifestation of the ocean of all methods of Dharma without exception; and in every moment of thought, for the sake of fulfilling the method of knowledge that pervades the entire expanse of the realm of space.

In every moment of thought, for the sake of purifying the method of knowledge that enters into all sentient beings without exception; in every moment of thought, for the sake of attaining the illumination of the method of knowledge that disciplines the entire world without exception; in every moment of thought, for the sake of the irreversibility in turning the wheel of Dharma at all times without exception; in every moment of thought, for the sake of becoming a benefactor to the entire world by manifesting skill in the empowerment of the knowledge of the omniscient ones without exception;
in every moment of thought, throughout the movements within the enumerations of all world-systems, in all oceans of world-systems that have arisen...
In the convergences of oceans of all world-systems; in the descriptions of the expansions of various world-systems; in the arrangements of the successions and connections of various world-systems;

in the descriptions of various foundations and manifold bodies; in the descriptions of the diversity of various arrays and eons; in the convergences of oceans of various directions—whether afflicted, pure, both afflicted and pure, exclusively pure, vast, great, immeasurable, contracted, subtle, coarse, level, inverted, upward-facing, or facing the cardinal and intermediate directions.

While practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout the vast expanse of all world-systems—arranged in various arrays of diverse gateways, terminuses, and configurations of instruction—he entered the fixed course of a bodhisattva. In order to manifest the pervasive power of the various miraculous transformations of bodhisattva conduct, he, at every moment of thought, perceived the bodies of all Buddhas of the three times without exception, as well as the inclinations and intentions of the minds of other beings; thus he attained the force of the ocean of merit for omniscience toward the entire world.
Increasing [it], they removed it.

In this way, noble son, when the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, was formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, he did so within a world-system devoid of the accumulations of merit and wisdom; one filled with ungrateful beings, shrouded in the darkness of ignorance, obsessed with the notions of "I" and "mine," enveloped by the cataracts of the darkness of nescience, given over to improper reflection, fallen into the thicket of the wilderness of views, and deluded regarding cause and effect.

Having generated great compassion for those who have fallen under the power of karma and afflictions and have plummeted into the midst of the abyss of suffering in the vast wilderness of great saṃsāra, where they experience the various sufferings of poverty, he brings forth vast clouds of the practice of the perfections (*pāramitā*). Praising the firm establishment of the roots of virtue, he turns back the suffering of the poverty of saṃsāra for all sentient beings and causes them to shine with the great accumulation of merit and wisdom.

Illuminating the direction of the causal mandala, manifesting the direction of the non-contradiction between action and dharma, shining upon the direction of the realization of the Buddha-dharma mandala, illuminating the direction of the inclinations of all sentient beings, demonstrating the direction of the arising of the fields of all sentient beings, following after the direction of the non-interruption of the lineage of all Tathāgatas,
upholding the direction of the teachings of all Buddhas, turning back the direction of all unwholesome dharmas, [and revealing] the direction of the equipment for omniscience...

Praising the realm of all sentient beings and pervading it, he brought forth a great cloud of perfections and established sentient beings in the ultimate gathering of the Dharma, satisfying them according to their inclinations;
he inspired them to undertake the equipment for omniscience.
He caused them to enter the perfections of the great bodhisattvas;
he supported them with the attainment of all noble riches;
and he caused the oceans of roots of goodness of sentient beings to increase through the surges of joy in omniscience.

Having introduced them to the gateways of the miraculous manifestations of all Tathāgatas, and having gathered them through the ultimate inclusion in the bliss of the state where no substrate remains (anupadhiśeṣa), he caused them to face toward the majesty of the Tathāgata and established them in the bodhisattva’s knowledge of gathering [beings].
Sudhana said, "Goddess, for how long have you set out for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?
She replied, "Noble son, this matter is difficult to bring about; it is difficult to understand, difficult to resolve with faith, difficult to enter, difficult to express, and difficult to realize.
It cannot be entered by the world with its gods, nor by all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."

Except through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, through being sustained by spiritual friends, through the mind being supported by the vast accumulation of merit and knowledge, through the purity of intention, and through a state of mind that is undepressed, unafflicted, straightforward, uninjured, unshrinking, free from darkness, and illuminated by the light of all-pervading wisdom.
With minds dedicated to establishing the welfare and happiness of all sentient beings; with minds that cannot be overcome by any of the mandalas of Māra or by the afflictions;

with minds that provide the opportunity for the attainment of the knowledge of omniscience; not desiring the pleasures of any saṃsāra but focusing instead on the bliss of the Tathāgatas; having set out to pacify the suffering and mental distress of all sentient beings; and being oriented toward the practice of entering the ocean of the qualities of the Tathāgatas.
They had as their sphere of activity the sky-like contemplation of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena; they were purified by the path of noble resolve and turned away from the stream of saṃsāra;

they were oriented toward the ocean of the gnosis of all Tathāgatas and were certain of entering every city [of the Dharma]; they possessed the vigor to traverse the domain of the Tathāgatas and strode with confidence upon the stage of Buddhahood; they were oriented toward the perfection of the powers of omniscience, culminating in the attainment of the ten powers.
It is possible for sentient beings to enter, resolve upon, grasp, follow, and understand this state.
Why is that?
Because, noble son, this state is the domain of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, which is beyond the reach of all bodhisattvas.
How much less so by all other sentient beings!

Nevertheless, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, I shall explain this for the sake of the perfect purification of the disposition of those noble beings, and for the sake of the mastery over the resolute intention of those beings who practice the roots of virtue.
And for your attainment of the turning of the wheel of Dharma through the prophecy resulting from your inquiry into the resolute intention.

Then, at that time, the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā, further illustrating this very matter, surveyed the domain of the Tathāgatas attained throughout the three times and spoke these verses:
"O son of the Buddha, the domain of the Buddhas is profound and infinite, which you indeed inquire about."
Indeed, it is not possible to tell all of that even in eons comparable to the atoms of inconceivable buddha-fields. // 1 //

It is not possible for greedy beings, nor for those with corrupt minds, nor for those shrouded in the blinding darkness of delusion, nor for those whose intentions are impaired by hypocrisy, to understand the peaceful nature of the Victors' Dharma. // 2 //

This sphere of the Buddha cannot be known by those who follow the influence of envy and stinginess, nor by those whose intentions are defiled by deceit and guile, nor by those shrouded by the obscurations of afflictions and karma. // 3 //

This stage of the Buddha cannot be known by those who dwell in the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields; nor by those who rely on the view of a self-identity; nor by those whose minds are distorted by views and perceptions. // 4 //
The peaceful realm of the Victors is difficult to know; by its very nature, it is stainless and free from conceptual construction.
Indeed, this Dharma cannot be fully understood by those attached to cyclic existence or those who rely upon becoming. (5)

Those who are born into the family of the Buddha-lineage, who are empowered by all the Tathāgatas, and who uphold the lineage and family of the Kings of Dharma—this is indeed the domain of those sages. (6)

Those whose minds are satiated by the ocean of pure dharmas, who are well-sustained by spiritual friends, and whose clouds of mind take the powers of the Sage as their object, attain patience upon hearing this. (7)

Those whose resolute intentions are stainless and free from conceptual construction, who—like clouds of the lamp of wisdom—have destroyed the darkness throughout the cardinal and intermediate directions in the sky; this is the sphere of activity for those pure ones. (8)
Those who, with an intention of compassion, pervade the oceans of worlds throughout all three times,
and whose loving-kindness follows after all sentient beings without exception— they have entered here into the way of the Victors.

Those who are indeed free from grasping, whose minds are joyful, who always delight in the giving of all that exists, and who act with equanimity toward all sentient beings—for them, this is the stage of those free from grasping. 10.

This is the domain of those stainless ones who possess unafflicted minds and blameless conduct, whose minds are disciplined through the complete removal of remorse, and who are devoted to practicing the instructions of the Buddha. (11)

Those whose minds are indeed unshakeable, whose minds are immovable, whose minds are bound to the intrinsic nature of phenomena (dharmasvabhāva), and whose minds are not in conflict even amidst the oceans of karma—for those inexhaustible ones, this is liberation in this world. 12.
Those whose minds are untiring, whose minds do not turn back, and who are endowed with the mastery of manly vigor.
Accumulating the provisions for omniscience with infinite vigor—this is the sphere of activity of those of excellent vows. (13)

For those whose minds are tranquil and composed, who have attained ultimate peace and are free from feverish affliction, and who move upon the ocean of the factors of omniscient meditation—for those who have reached such serenity, this is the method. (14)

Those whose minds are completely liberated from all attachments, whose minds have penetrated the intrinsic nature of phenomena, and who have reached the destination within the realm of the Victor’s Dharma—for them, this is not the path of the lamp of wisdom. (15)

Those whose minds have penetrated the intrinsic nature of sentient beings, whose hearts are not greedy for the ocean of existence, and who are moons reflected in the minds of sentient beings—for those knowers of the path, this is liberation. (16)

I shall follow the path of those Samantabhadras who abide throughout the three times, who have arisen from the ocean of the lineage of vows of the oceans of Victors, and whose conduct in all realms extends to the furthest limits of time. (17)

This is the liberation of those who, through oceans of methods within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), have entered all the oceans of worlds throughout every eon of dissolution and evolution—indeed, for them, there is no such thing as an eon. (18)

Those who behold Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within all the realms of every direction, seated at the foot of the king of trees, having awakened to enlightenment and training all beings—this is the path of those whose vision is unimpeded. (19)
You have come from the great ocean of eons, serving spiritual friends; seeking the Dharma and searching for the Dharma without weariness, you are capable of retaining it upon hearing it. (20)
In order to thoroughly purify your intention, through the power of the Sage’s empowerment, this inconceivable,
immeasurable, and unimpeded sphere of Vairocana proceeds forth by means of my words. (21)

Long ago, noble son, in the past, beyond oceans of world-systems as numerous as the atoms in a great ocean of eons, there was a world-system ocean named Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana (Radiant Peak of Jewel-Golden Mountains).

Furthermore, noble son, in that world-system ocean Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana, there was a Tathāgata named Jñānaparvatadharmadhātudikpratapanatejorāja (King of the Radiant Splendor Illuminating the Directions of the Dharma-Realm Mountain of Wisdom).

Furthermore, noble son, when that Tathāgata named Jñānaparvatadharmadhātudikpratapanatejorāja was formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, he purified the world-ocean-system called Maṇikanakaparvataśikharavairocana.
Within that world-ocean-system, there is a detailed exposition of the extension of world-systems as numerous as the atoms of earth and mountains.
In each single expanse of world-systems, there are as many descriptions of world-systems as there are atoms within the lineage of world-systems.
In each single lineage of worlds, there are as many descriptions of the enumeration of eons as there are atoms within a world-system.
And in each single eon, there are many descriptions of successive eons.
In each and every subsequent eon, there were explanations of the various distinctions among many world-systems,
as well as explanations of the diverse miraculous transformations accompanying the arising of Tathāgatas.
And in each instance of a Tathāgata’s arising, there were explanations that revealed sūtras as numerous as the atoms within a world-system.

And in each and every sutra, there were explanations of the predictions for bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a world-system, and instructions on the training of infinite and boundless beings, set forth through the methods of various vehicles and characterized by the discipline of various miraculous transformations.
Furthermore, within that ocean of world-systems called Vairocana-Peak-of-Jewel-and-Gold-Mountain, there was a central lineage of world-systems named Array of Banners with Doors Facing All Directions.
Furthermore, noble son, in that central lineage of world-systems called Samantadigabhimukhadvāradhvajavyūha, there was a world-system named Sarvaratnavarṇasamantaprabhāsaśrī.
It was arrayed with the interstices of all world-systems as reflected in the jewel-kings of the bodhimaṇḍas of all Tathāgatas; it was established upon an ocean of flowers made of every kind of jewel;
its body consisted of jewel-kings that manifested the radiance of the emanations of all Tathāgatas; it was shaped like a city of the gods; and it was both pure and defiled.
Furthermore, in that world-system, there were four-continent world-systems as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru.
Among those four-continent world-systems, which were as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was a central four-continent world-system named Sarvaratnaśikharadhvaja.
In that world-system of Sarvaratnaśikharadhvaja, there were four continents, each measuring hundreds of thousands of immeasurable yojanas in length and breadth.
And in each individual continent, there were ten thousand great cities.
Furthermore, in that world-system of four continents, in the center of Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital named Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā, surrounded by ten thousand cities.
Moreover, in that Jambudvīpa, the lifespan of human beings was ten thousand years.
Now, in that royal capital called Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpa, there was a universal monarch named Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa.
Furthermore, King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa had five hundred ministers,
