and his inner court consisted of sixty thousand women.
He had seven hundred sons, all of whom were brave, heroic, possessed of excellent physical forms, handsome, of great splendor, and of great strength.
Furthermore, during the reign of that King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, the entire continent of Jambudvīpa was under a single umbrella, with all rival forces and adversaries subdued.

And at that time, when the destruction of the intermediate kalpa had arrived within that world-system, when the five corruptions had appeared in the world, and when the ten paths of wholesome action had disappeared, [beings] were engaged in the ten unwholesome paths of action.
For the most part, sentient beings were destined for miserable rebirths;

by reason of undertaking the ten paths of unwholesome action, they became short-lived, possessed of meager resources, deformed, discolored, and ill-proportioned in body; they experienced little happiness, were frequently beset by painful sensations, and were habitually prone to speaking words of mutual deception.

They were characterized by mutual animosity, engaged in harsh speech, and possessed of incoherent talk; overcome by greed for sense objects, they harbored corrupt mental intentions and had entered the dense wilderness of various false views.

For those who were stained by unrighteous passion, overwhelmed by perverse greed, and enveloped by false doctrine, the god did not release showers of rain in due season, whereby the multitudes of seeds and the multitudes of crops upon the earth [perished].
They would grow forth.

Furthermore, those beings, afflicted by various diseases, ran in all directions and intermediate points toward dry grass, shrubs, medicinal herbs, forests, groves, and trees, having no place of refuge.

Having gathered together, they all approached the royal city of Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpa; having surrounded it on all sides, some raised their arms aloft, while others joined their palms in reverent salutation.
Some had their bodies trembling,
some had their limbs raised upward, and some fell headlong.
Some prostrated with their entire bodies; some knelt upon the surface of the earth; and some extended their arms toward the expanse of the sky.
Some were naked and without clothing;
some had distorted faces and eyes. Facing King Sarvadharmanirnāda-cchatramaṇḍala-nirghoṣa, they raised a great cry of distress, shouting: "We are being oppressed! We have been abandoned by the gods!"
We were tormented by the suffering of hunger and thirst;
we were consumed by various fears;
we were destitute of protection.
"O Lord, we are without refuge and without resort;

we have entered the cage of suffering, our lives are at an end, and we face death. Thus they uttered various lamentations, crying out with diverse tones, various phrases, and various distorted expressions of the face and eyes; with words of invocation containing various notions, and with phrases indicating various meanings, they raised a great cry.

And those men, women, boys, and girls in that royal capital who were tormented by hunger and thirst, whose limbs were without ornaments, naked and unclothed, with wicked and discolored complexions and bodies that were rough and harsh—
those beings were suffering, dejected, and unhappy, longing for the end of suffering and weary of the fear of suffering.
They approached King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, that great man of wisdom who had become their refuge,
seeking him as a shelter with the perception of attaining all happiness, the perception of attaining the company of all that is dear,
the perception of attaining a treasure for those whose hope for life was sustained, the perception of seeing a ford, and the perception of setting out upon the great path.

With the perception of the Mahāyāna as a vessel, the perception of the great island of the jewels of primordial wisdom, the perception of the attainment of the great purpose, and the perception of the attainment of all the delights and pleasures of the celestial realms.
King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa heard from all sides that great sound of lamentation and outcry from the vast multitude of supplicants.
Upon hearing it, hundreds of thousands of incalculable gateways of great compassion entered his mind.

With a mind intent upon the contemplation of the volition of the method of great compassion, he experienced one-pointed concentration for a moment and uttered ten phrases of speech endowed with great compassion.
What are the ten?
Alas! Sentient beings are without support, having fallen into the great precipice of saṃsāra.
When will that time come when we shall become a refuge for those sentient beings who have fallen into the great precipice of saṃsāra, by establishing them on the ground of the Tathāgata’s refuge?
"Alas! These beings are without protection, afflicted by the calamities of various afflictions.

When will that time come when we shall become a protection for those beings who are without protection and afflicted by the fears and calamities of manifold afflictions, by establishing them in faultless courses of action?"

"Alas! Beings in this world are without refuge, overwhelmed by the fear of old age and death. What will become of them? How shall we become a refuge for those beings who are without refuge, by turning them away from all the fears of saṃsāra?
Alas! Beings are without a final resort, afflicted by the various fears and calamities of the world."

"May that come to pass wherein we shall become a refuge for those beings who are afflicted by the various fears of the world and are without a protector, by establishing them on the path to omniscience which is ultimate security and peace.
Alas! The entire world has fallen into the darkness of ignorance, shrouded by the gloom of doubt and uncertainty.
Oh, when will that time come when we shall become like torches for all sentient beings by dispelling the darkness of their ignorance?"
"Alas! How deprived of light are sentient beings!
When will that time come when we shall become makers of the great light of wisdom for all sentient beings, by way of revealing the face of knowledge free from darkness?
Alas! How devoid of the radiance of wisdom is the realm of all sentient beings, their mental dispositions clouded by envy, stinginess, deceit, and hypocrisy!"
When will that time come when we shall become illuminators of unsurpassed wisdom, by establishing all sentient beings in ultimate, complete purification?
Alas! This entire world, deprived of a guide, has fallen into the treacherous currents of the great ocean of saṃsāra.
When will that time come when we shall become guides for all sentient beings, by leading them into the way of the ocean of karma?
"Alas! The entire world is ill-behaved, being bereft of a leader.

When will that time come when we shall become leaders for all sentient beings, through the Tathāgata’s empowerment, by bringing them to maturity and discipline in every way, without ever missing the proper occasion?
Alas! The entire world is without a guide, having become like those blind from birth."
When will that time come when we shall become guides for all sentient beings by means of leading them into the method of unobstructed, omniscient knowledge?

Having uttered these ten phrases associated with great compassion, he caused a proclamation by bell to be made in that royal capital and had the sound of the drum of great renunciation struck, saying: "We shall satisfy the entire world; whatever anyone requires, we shall bestow it upon them."
Consequently, throughout the entire Jambudvīpa—in all royal capitals, and in all villages, cities, market towns, provinces, and ports—all treasuries of provisions were opened;
various kinds of supplies were stationed at every crossroads, streets, and squares; and everything necessary for the livelihood of the entire world was well-prepared.
All the treasuries and storehouses were opened; great accumulations of precious jewel-treasures were displayed;
and many diverse heaps of jewels were set forth.
Food, drink, clothing, vehicles, flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, various fragrances, and robes of diverse colors were laid out;

couches, seats, garments, palaces, celestial mansions, and houses were adorned and filled with all manner of wealth and gold. Dispelling the darkness by means of the array of the king of jewels known as the "Luminous Banner," he manifested bodies corresponding to his own form within each of those houses for the sake of fulfilling every desire and intention of those beings exactly as they wished.

And for the sake of pacifying all the diseases of all sentient beings, he provided a complete abundance of physicians, medicines, attendants, and various necessities and conditions for sustaining life;
and he provided various vessels made of diverse jewels, filled with appropriate and manifold requisites— namely, vessels of diamond-jewels filled with various fragrant jewel-gems,
and vessels of various fragrant gems filled with diverse, noble, and multicolored garments.

He caused to be established in all regions and districts very many vehicles and draft-animals of various forms and shapes, adorned with diverse jewels, yoked with well-bred horses, elephants, and oxen; as well as various chariots worthy of kings, all kinds of jeweled ornaments and articles of enjoyment, and all varieties of seats variegated with many gems, spread with diverse canopies, covered with nets of jeweled bells, and beautified by raised parasols, banners, and flags.

He proclaimed the giving away of villages, cities, market towns, and provinces; he proclaimed the enjoyment of various kinds of delightful gardens, groves, and ascetic hermitages; the renunciation of all households, wives, and children;

the renunciation of all priceless jewels; and even the renunciation of his own heart, marrow, intestines, sinews, kidneys, fat, flesh, blood, skin, hide, hands, feet, arms, ears, nose, eyes, tongue, teeth, lips, and head.
He even proclaimed the relinquishing of all forms of both external and internal things, down to the very last.
Having established this procedure for the relinquishment of such requisites, he caused a great sacrificial arena to be constructed;

it was situated to the east of that royal capital, Ratnasālavyūhameghapradīpā, in front of the city gate named Maṇiśikharatejas, with perfectly even dimensions and an entrance into the earth that was most extensive, its surface pure and level, free from depressions or elevations.

It was free from ravines and precipices; all stumps and thorns had been removed; gravel and pebbles had been leveled away; it was a collection of all kinds of precious mineral deposits; its surface was strewn with the finest of all jewel-gems; it was adorned with many arrays of various jewels and gems; it was scattered with flowers of diverse precious stones; it was filled with all kinds of fragrant powders; it was perfumed with all manner of incense; it was illuminated by lamps of radiant jewels; and its ornaments consisted of clouds of masses of splendor, beauty, and all kinds of fragrant incense that completely covered the sky.

It was beautifully adorned with well-arranged rows of trees made of every kind of jewel; it was embellished with various mansions, celestial palaces, and gabled chambers; umbrellas, banners, and flags were raised aloft; it was illuminated by hanging ribbons of various jewels; it was covered by a net of diverse jeweled flowers; it possessed a circular canopy of umbrellas formed by a net of jewels and the finest of all fragrant kings; it resounded with the chiming of jeweled bells from golden lattices; it was overspread with a canopy shimmering with various gems; and it was strewn with the powder of the finest of all fragrant kings.
It was delightful, strewn with all kinds of jewel-flowers, resounded with the charming sounds of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of musical instruments,
perfectly pure with arrays of various ornaments made of all kinds of jewels, and brought forth as the maturation of the karma of bodhisattvas.
In its center, a great lion-throne appeared, situated upon a ground-surface variegated and studded with ten kinds of jewels.

It was resplendent with a surrounding enclosure of ten altars made of various jewels; its array was beautifully adorned and well-proportioned by the intervals between the enclosures formed by the branches of ten jewel-trees.
Its base was firmly established upon a ground of indestructible vajra-wheels, and its circular seat was supported by the forms of images made of every kind of jewel.

It was decorated with hundreds of turrets composed of many jewels and embellished by a variegated array of diverse jewel-inlays; jeweled banners were raised everywhere, perfectly distributed throughout.
It was adorned with a manifold array of various jeweled banners hanging down, embellished with nets of jewel-bells, and spread over with nets of gold variegated by various divine gems.
Its magnificent arrangement was beautified and covered as befitting its splendor by nets of diverse jewel-flowers, nets of great king-gems, nets of variegated garments, and nets of jewels;

it emitted clouds of fragrance from the palms of hands formed of many scented gems, and it was pervaded by an expansion of king-gems of inconceivable color and scent, emitting clouds of all kinds of fragrant powders in various delightful shapes.

It was attended by offerings of all kinds of divine perfumes and incenses; it was adorned with various colored garments and jewel-gems that possessed a touch of supreme divine comfort; hundreds of thousands of diverse divine musical instruments were played everywhere, producing a pleasing and sweet resonance; its magnificent array was decorated with rows of jewel-stairways, banners, and well-proportioned railings; and it was illuminated by the radiance of various mani-figures and forms produced through manifold miraculous transformations of many jewel-gems.

There, King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa was seated; he was handsome, gracious, and beautiful to behold, endowed with the excellence of a most sublime complexion, possessed of the pure marks of a Great Man, with a crown of hair radiant like Vairocana-jewel-gems, and a body with the indestructible adamantine compactness of Nārāyaṇa, its joints bound together with hidden and firm sides.

He was complete in all his limbs, universally auspicious, universally pleasing, and universally beautiful; endowed with the excellence of all forms, he arose from the great Dharma-king’s treasury; he had attained mastery over all requisites, was utterly purified in his mastery over the Dharma, wielded sovereignty over his own mind, possessed an unimpeded mandala of speech, and was endowed with unshakable wisdom.
This was the instruction on the infinite qualities and praises of the correct application of the well-established Dharma.
Furthermore, as King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa sat upon his great lion throne,
a great canopy appeared in the sky directly above his head, with a handle made of various elevated jewels and gems.

It had a great inner chamber containing a vast treasury of great jewels, perfectly spread with hundreds of thousands of rods of every kind of gem; its array was ablaze with the glorious splendor of many rays of light, and its roof was pure and radiant like Jāmbūnada gold.
It was endowed with a most magnificent canopy of golden nets variegated by the inlay of various jewels, from which hung down diverse pearl necklaces.
It was covered on all sides by nets of various gems, and draped with hanging clusters of jewel-bells, golden mani-gems, and strings of precious threads.
It was adorned with a magnificent array of great jewel-garlands hanging down on all sides, attended by the sound of divine, sweet, and charming music being released,

and resounded with the ringing of bells that exhorted all sentient beings toward the paths of wholesome action. Indeed, King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, being fanned with jeweled whisks, shone forth, blazing with a splendor that surpassed even that of Śakra, the Lord of the Devas.
As soon as he had sat down upon that lion throne, the entire multitude of people stood facing him with palms joined in reverence, paying homage to that very king.
Then, indeed, when hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of incalculable living beings had assembled before King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa—

beings who were various supplicants, recipients of various goods, intent upon various requisites, belonging to various species, included within various destinies, possessing minds of various desires, having various inclinations and intentions, gathered from various directions, and engaged in the enjoyment of various sensory objects—

Among those whose minds long for various enjoyments, who conceive various intentions, who belong to various classes of humans, who are born into various families, who have gathered from various regions, who employ various etymologies, words, and mantra-formulations, who release various circles of tones, who use various objects and expressions, and who utter various phrases and words—
While they were gazing upon that single Sumeru of great merit, their minds became certain that "this alone is the one Great Man of Wisdom";
while they looked up toward him, thinking, "The moon of the Great Being is supported by great merit and has attained the intention for great renunciation";

and while they had fallen into the volition of the Bodhisattva’s vow and were fashioned by the volition of the Bodhisattva’s vow—seeing that vast assembly of supplicants, he felt a love for those beggars in his heart.
There arose joy in his mind and clarity of mind; there emerged the perception of the spiritual friend as vast as the universe and the surging force of great compassion;
and there manifested the impetus of irreversible vigor for the purpose of satisfying all supplicants throughout the future eons.
Clouds of minds that pervade all worlds with the relinquishment of equal application arose.

Furthermore, upon merely seeing those supplicants, King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa became even more joyful than he would have been by obtaining the sovereignty of a universal monarch over the triple-thousandfold world system lasting until the end of the kalpa,
or than by obtaining the throne of the lordship of Śakra lasting for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas.
Not by the attainment of the sovereign throne of Suyāma, the king of gods, at the conclusion of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas;

nor by the attainment of the sovereign throne of Saṃtuṣita, the king of gods, at the conclusion of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas; nor by the attainment of the sovereign throne of mastery over the Sunirmita gods, at the conclusion of immeasurable kalpas.

Neither by the attainment of the sovereign throne of the Vaśavartin king of gods, nor by the attendance of the beautiful-faced and enchanting celestial maidens until the end of inconceivable eons, nor by the throne of Brahmā until the conclusion of the bliss of the Brahma-abodes for ineffable eons.

Not by the bliss of the Ābhāsvara devas, which lasts for an infinite number of kalpas; not by the bliss of the Śubhakṛtsna devas, which remains inexhaustible for incomparable kalpas; nor by the dwelling in the peaceful liberation of the Śuddhāvāsa devas, which lasts for limitless kalpas.

For example, noble son, suppose there were a man whose conduct was entirely driven by longing, who had been separated for a long time from his father, mother, brothers, sisters, friends, ministers, kinsmen, blood relations, sons, daughters, and wife;
having become lost in a vast wilderness and desiring to see them, upon finally meeting with them, a great surge of joy and intense resolve would arise because he could never look at them enough.
In the very same way, noble son, as soon as King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa saw those supplicants, a great surge of joy arose within him.
The bliss of mental satisfaction descended;
a great surge of mental exaltation arose;
and a mighty current of joyous radiance was produced.
The force of the impulse of noble faith and resolve has been increased through the awakening of the Buddha;
faith, having taken root, has flourished toward omniscience;
and the power of the purity of the resolute intention regarding all the qualities of a Buddha has been further increased.
The bodhisattva’s faculties attained flexibility;
a surge of great faith, filled with joy for the mind, arose;
and through the force of that vast exhilaration of heart, his inclination toward the faculties of a spiritual friend became supple.
For what reason?
Because that King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa was dedicated to the objective of omniscience,
took refuge in the true nature of omniscience, was oriented toward the gateway of the path to omniscience, and was engaged in the mental application of satisfying all living beings.

He was oriented toward the practice of entering the ocean of all the qualities of the Buddhas; he was intent on shattering the mountains of the obstructions of all māra-activities and afflictions; he remained steadfast in his respectful acceptance of the instructions of all the Tathāgatas; he was filled with the application of purifying the ocean of all roots of goodness through universal gateways; his mental continuum had moved away from all dogmatic attachments; he was unattached to the objects of all worldly realms; and his sphere of activity was the sky-like intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

Toward all those supplicants, there arose the perception of them as an only son; there arose the perception of them as parents, the perception of them as those worthy of offerings, the perception of them as spiritual friends, the perception of them as rare, the perception of them as performers of difficult deeds, the perception of them as those of great benefit, the perception of them as supreme benefactors, the perception of them as supports for the path to awakening, the perception of them as teachers, and the perception of them as the Master.

He satisfied all those beggars— arrived as they were, obtained as they were, assembled at the proper time as they were, situated in their respective regions and directions as they were, seeking specific objects as they were, according to their tastes, their intentions, their desires, their longings, and their searches for particular things— by means of his unimpeded mandala of great loving-kindness, through his refusal to turn away from supplicants, and by the radiance of his great generosity.
With an application equal toward all sentient beings and by way of renunciation, he gave food to those seeking food,
drink to those seeking drink, clothing to those seeking clothing, and flowers to those seeking flowers.

In this manner, he gave perfumes, incense, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, jewels, ornaments, seats, beds, palaces, celestial mansions, monasteries, groves, parks, and ascetic hermitages;

he also gave horses, elephants, chariots, infantry, mounts, yoked vehicles, and carriages; as well as gold, silver, gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, native gold, and wrought silver; and even his own home, celestial mansion, inner apartments, and retinue.
Having opened and distributed all his treasuries, he gave them to those in need, saying, "Let whoever has need of something take it.
He gave away even the provinces to those who desired provinces,
the villages to those who desired villages, and the cities to those who desired cities.
Having practiced equanimity toward all sentient beings through the relinquishment of all his possessions, he covered all those supplicants with the giving away of every single thing.
Moreover, at that time, a merchant’s daughter named Ratnaprabhā, accompanied by a retinue of sixty maidens, had assembled in that very sacrificial enclosure.
She was beautiful, gracious, and lovely to behold, endowed with the most excellent abundance of a radiant complexion;

her skin was gold-colored, her hair and eyes were deep blue, and she possessed a pleasing fragrance, a voice like that of Brahmā, fine garments, and exquisite ornaments. She was perfected in mindfulness, intelligence, comprehension, modesty, fortitude, decorum, and proper conduct.

She was respectful toward her teachers, conducting herself with supreme situational awareness, possessing profound gestures, and endowed with intelligence. She had previously cultivated roots of merit for the sake of grasping, practicing, and awakening to the teachings; her mental continuum was serene and overflowing with the Dharma.

With pure and virtuous intentions, her mind directed toward the welfare of others through the vast resolve that ranges as freely as space, she was oriented toward the direction of the Buddhas and yearned for the wisdom of omniscience.

That merchant’s daughter, Ratnaprabhā, stood not far from the great lion throne of King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, having circumambulated it clockwise, with palms joined in reverence as she paid homage to the king.
She did not take anything at all.
Standing to one side, she formed this thought in her mind: "I have gained a great benefit, in that I have obtained the sight and the company of such a spiritual friend."

Having conceived the perception of that King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa as a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), as one who is compassionate, as one who bestows favor, and as a Buddha, she— her mind free from deceit and guile and having attained a surge of supreme, vast joy, serene faith, and gladness—
removed her own ornaments from her body and approached King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa.
She threw them toward him;
they came to rest upon the surface of the earth beneath the middle of his lion-throne dais.

Having scattered those ornaments, she made this aspiration: "Just as this King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa [is for] sentient beings who are without a protector and have fallen into darkness..."
Likewise, may I also come to be in the future time;
whatever this one knows to be the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), may I know that very same thing.
By whatever vehicle he shall depart, by that same one shall I also depart; on whichever very path he has set out, [by that shall I also go].
In that regard,
I too shall practice so that I may become just like him— irresistible in form, possessing inexhaustible enjoyments, with an infinite retinue, invincible, unconquered, and unassailable.
"And wherever his rebirth may occur,
may I also be reborn there."
Perceiving that she was thus engaged in such mental attention, King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa looked at her and said: "Take it, girl, whatever you need.
Indeed, girl, I am one who has renounced all possessions and is committed to the satisfaction of all sentient beings."
When she was thus addressed by King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, she attained an even greater degree of serene faith.
With a mind full of clarity, and having generated the force of noble and vast roots of virtue, she then addressed King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa with these verses:
"O Lion among Kings, before you were born, this Sālaviyūhameghā [was here]."
It was devoid of beauty and its splendor destroyed, like a terrifying abode of hungry ghosts. // 22 //
Those humans were killers of living beings, takers of what was not given, and unrestrained;
they spoke falsehoods and harsh words, and they uttered slanderous and senseless speech. (23)

Those whose minds harbor covetousness toward the speech and thoughts of others, who possess malevolent intent toward other persons, and whose sphere of activity is evil due to their reliance on wrong views—by means of such false application, they fall into an evil destiny. (24)

For those people who practice unrighteousness, who are shrouded in the blinding darkness of ignorance and delusion, and who, through the failure of their vision, perceive things erroneously, the god does not send rain for many years. (25)
When the rain did not fall, the seeds were destroyed; the crops did not sprout, nor did the trees.
The lakes, ponds, and river currents dried up, as did the thirst-quenching herbs and all the forest vegetation.
All rivers became completely dried up, and all gardens appeared like desolate forests;
the earth became filled with white bones, O One of Pure Vision, because of your non-arising. (27)

For when all those beggars born from the continuity of supplicants have been fully satisfied, then, like a cloud arising, you satisfy all things—both the lowlands and the highlands—in the four directions. (28)
Furthermore, no one is ever robbed by thieves, nor attacked by soldiers, nor deceived by rogues, nor even slain;
nor do those without protectors meet their death, for you have become the protector of the entire world that was once protectorless. (29)

Those humans who delight in taking life, who kill others and drink their blood, and who devour one another's flesh—may they, through these offerings from you, become possessed of a mind of loving-kindness. (30)

At that time, a single woman became the end of a hundred and the beginning of a thousand; covered with robes made of grass and leaves, those women entered [the city] like hungry ghosts, their bodies shrouded in such garments. (31)
When you were born as the Lord of this world, rice appeared without being sown or ploughed, wish-fulfilling trees blossomed with their sheaths opened, and wise men and women were seen. (32)
Formerly, those who stood on the wrong path made hoards for the sake of half-months and months;
today, however, well-adorned and wearing costly garments, they sport like gods dwelling in the Nandana grove.

For men, indeed, were once impassioned by unrighteous passion, engaging in the improper and treacherous pursuit of sensual desires; likewise, women—whether maidens or those protected by themselves or others—fell into poison through such attachment in the past.

Seeing other women— possessing forms equal in beauty to the finest apsarases, well-clothed and fully adorned, their bodies anointed with sandalwood paste— they were as satisfied with their own wives today as if they were the Tuṣitas.

Having previously spoken four kinds of speech—false, harsh, slanderous, and incoherent—under the influence of deceit, they now practice the Dharma, freed from wrong views, having abandoned this fourfold speech. (36)
Neither the charming sound of musical instruments, nor the voices of celestial songs, nor even the voices of Brahmā or the warbling of kalaviṅka birds can touch the path of your speech. (37)

Indeed, a parasol stands upon the junction of your head—a parasol adorned with jewels, with a golden lattice, a handle of beryl, and a treasury of light within its core, surrounded on all sides by a network of excellent gem-encrusted necklaces. (38)

Surpassing all other vocal qualities in the world that arise from bells, they move through the world with the components of a Buddha’s voice, producing the peaceful sound of the proclamation of the True Dharma. (39)

Those beings who, having heard it, pacify their afflictions throughout the successions of fields in all directions—the wheel of names belonging to the oceans of Sugatas, the oceans of eons, and the ocean of the wise—[attain this]. (40)

From the beginningless past, through the succession of successive fields, and by the power of whose name, the bells of the wheels of the True Dharma resound throughout all directions without exception. (41)
Resounding with the sound of a bell, unattached and pervading the entire Jambudhvaja,
it rings forth, proclaiming the respective karmic ordinances of Brahmā, Indra, the Lord of Devas, and the Lords of the World.

And having heard those sounds of the bells, those god-like men, having abandoned their respective storehouses of karma, practice what is virtuous after forsaking evil; they all establish themselves in the awakening of a Buddha.
Jyotiprabha was his father, the king, and Padmaprabhā was his mother, the queen; during the period of the fivefold increase of the kaṣāyas, how did he obtain the kingdom of Dharma? (44)
For him there was a vast garden, filled with magnificent arrays of blossoming flowers and jeweled lamps;
it was further beautified by five hundred lotus ponds and surrounded by hundreds of trees.
Each of these had a celestial palace with beautiful shores rising on a thousand pillars;
it was variegated with thousands of arrangements of railings and adorned all around with lattices and crescent moons that shone brightly.
When the god did not rain for many years because unrighteousness was powerful and [the merit of the world] was incomplete,
then the water in the lotus ponds vanished entirely, and all the trees withered, their foliage and bark dried up.
Seven nights before you were born, there appeared miraculous omens;
seeing which, beings spoke with certainty, saying, "A Savior shall indeed arise for us."
Then, O King, at the hour of midnight, the earth shook in six ways;
and even in the blameless Puṣkiriṇī pond, a radiance appeared in its center like that of the sun. (49)

Furthermore, five hundred lotus ponds appeared, filled with water possessing the eight excellent qualities; and trees with well-formed branches became endowed with great splendor, provided with flowers and fruits.
Those lotus-pools, filled with water, satisfied that entire forest without exception;
and by the streams flowing forth from them, the land of Jambudvīpa became completely filled with water.
Trees grew from medicinal herbs, plants, and grasses, becoming laden with fruits and flowers; and as many seeds as there were upon the earth, all of them sprouted when drenched by the waters.
At that time, every region of the earth that was flooded by water became level; indeed, all the uneven parts of the earth—both low and high—became entirely even.
At that moment, in an instant, the treacherous regions with their chasms and precipices became level;
thorns, pebbles, and the like disappeared, and mines of excellent jewels emerged.
Throngs of men and women gathered nearby, parched with thirst, drank the waters and uttered this exclamation: "Ah! To whom does this experience of such bliss belong today? (55)
At that time, King Jyotiḥprabha, together with his sons, wives, and the assembly of ministers,
surrounded by thousands of millions of people, set out on an exalted excursion to the pleasure garden.
The blameless Puṣkariṇī, fragrant and filled with perfumed water, was situated in the center; having ascended the palace, the king remained there with his wife at the Sudharmatīrtha. (57)
On that very night when the waters first arose,
the entire earth— including its mountains and its garlands of celestial palaces— trembled once again in that same manner.
And from the center of Aninditā, a great thousand-petaled lotus emerged,
pervading the sky with a mass of clouds possessing the brilliance of a thousand suns and a radiance like the summit of Mount Sumeru.

Likewise, that vajra-staff has a pure essence of auspicious beings, with broad and pure petals of the lord of jewels, a pericarp of precious Jāmbūnada gold, and is rich with filaments radiant as the king of fragrances. // 60 //
O Lord, you were born there in its pericarp with your body poised in the cross-legged posture;
you shine forth, your limbs adorned with the primary marks, while being worshipped by hundreds of gods.
Descending from the roof of the palace, the king, with a joyful mind, took you in his hands and gave you to the queen, speaking these words: "This is your son; be of contented heart."
Tens of millions of treasures appeared, and trees burst open their sheaths;
the sky resounded with the music of celestial instruments when you, the Lord of the World, were born.
Indeed, all those beings in Jambudvīpa who were turned toward you became filled with joy; joining their palms in reverence, they exclaimed, "O, protector of this protectorless people! (64)
Light emanating from your body illuminated the earth on all sides;
having destroyed the darkness of ignorance for all beings, it pacified every remaining disease. (65)
Those hosts of yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, and piśācas who were harassers always departed;
even the venomous serpents, though possessing great poison and intent on killing living beings, did not roam about at that time.
Non-gain, blame, ill-repute, suffering, calamities, diseases, and misfortunes—having attained peace, these ceased; instead, benefit arose for the world and great joy welled up. (67)
At that time, the entire world was characterized by loving-kindness, perceiving one another as equal to a mother;
it was free from enmity, devoid of malice, and possessed of the practice of the path to omniscience. // 68 //
The miserable realms have been overturned by the King of Dharma, and the great highway to heaven has been opened;
you have shown the path to omniscience and accomplished a vast benefit for the world. (69)
We have attained the supreme gain by beholding you, who are like a great ocean;
you are born as the protector of the world’s helpless, a marvelous leader when all was long lost.

Then, having praised, extolled, and lauded King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa with these verses, the merchant’s daughter Ratnaprabhā circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, prostrated herself, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, paying homage.
Then King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, having looked upon the merchant’s daughter Ratnaprabhā, spoke thus: "Excellent, excellent, daughter!
You have entered into the superknowledge that knows the specific qualities of other beings. Rare, daughter, are those beings in all the world,"
"Those who lack conviction in the virtues of other beings,

O maiden— beings shrouded in darkness, ungrateful, impaired in intellect, agitated in mind, with wavering continuums, dark-hearted, naturally ruined in disposition, fallen from right practice, and ignorant of the specific virtues of other beings— it is impossible for them to [perceive] the qualities of a bodhisattva."
To bring forth the qualities of a Tathāgata, or to conceive of the specific superknowledges of all qualities and wisdom—
without doubt, young lady, you have set out for enlightenment.

Since you comprehend such qualities of a bodhisattva through your noble mastery of the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), our courageous effort in gathering sentient beings in Jambudvīpa has not been in vain, for you, endowed with such wisdom, have appeared within our realm.
Then, King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa [offered] a priceless great jewel.
Taking with his own hand a priceless jewel-garment variegated with luminous, radiant gems, he gave it to Ratnaprabhā, the merchant’s daughter;
and to each of all the maidens in her retinue, he likewise gave various precious garments.
And he spoke thus: "Daughter, accept this precious garment; having taken it, use it for yourself.
Then the merchant’s daughter Ratnaprabhā, together with her retinue, prostrated herself upon the surface of the earth with both knees.
Taking that precious garment with both hands and placing it upon her head, she stepped forward and put on that precious garment.
All the maidens of her retinue likewise each put on their own precious garments.
Having put on those precious garments, she, together with her own retinue of maidens, circumambulated King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa.
Upon all those precious garments of theirs, the reflected images of all the lunar mansions and luminous bodies were seen shining brightly.
Seeing this, the multitude of people said: "O girl, this retinue of yours is magnificent!
Like a night goddess adorned by a host of stars, you shine most brilliantly surrounded by them."
Then the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana:
"What do you think, noble son—was the king named Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa someone else at that time, in that age? You should certainly not view it in such a way."
This Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was at that time and on that occasion the king named Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa.

Furthermore, noble son, would you think that at that time and on that occasion the queen named Padmaprabhā, the wife of King Jyotiṣprabha and the mother of King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, was someone else?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way.
This very Queen Māyā was, at that time, the king’s wife named Padmaprabhā,
by whom that spontaneously born prince was received upon her lap.
Furthermore, noble son, you might think that at that time and on that occasion, the king named Jyotiṣprabha, who was the father of King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa, was someone else.
You should certainly not view it in this way.
At that time, King Śuddhodana was the king named Jyotiṣprabha.
Furthermore, noble son, you might think that at that time, on that occasion, the merchant’s daughter named Ratnaprabhā was someone else;
however, it should not be viewed in this way.
I was that merchant’s daughter named Ratnaprabhā at that time and on that occasion.

Furthermore, noble son, you might think that the beings who were born there in Jambudvīpa at that time and on that occasion, and who were gathered by King Sarvadharmanirnādacchatramaṇḍalanirghoṣa through the four means of attraction, were others. [But they were not.]
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way.

All these bodhisattvas have gathered here in this very assembly-circle of the Blessed One; they have been established in the irreversible bodhisattva stage of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment—some in the first stage, and so forth.

Some were established on the second stage, some on the third, some on the fourth, some on the fifth, some on the sixth, some on the seventh, some on the eighth, some on the ninth, and some on the tenth bodhisattva stage;

[they were established] by means of various diversities of vows, various departures toward omniscience, various accumulations, various arrivals at the ocean [of merit], various modes of exit, various purifications of the array of paths, various heroic displays of miraculous transformations, and various arrays of paths.
Having attained various abodes of liberation, they dwell here in this circle of the assembly, residing in various celestial palaces of the Dharma.

Then, at that time, the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā, further demonstrating this very Bodhisattva liberation called "The Radiance of Contentment Arising from the Storehouse of Vast Joy," addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana in verses:
"My eye, O Son of the Victor, is vast, by which I behold all directions."
He likewise perceives the various and vast oceans of fields and the oceans of sentient beings wandering in saṃsāra. // 71 //

In all the expansions of the fields, you constantly pervade the ten directions with your miraculous powers, [beholding] the stainless Victors seated upon the Bodhi-tree thrones, and you discipline the multitude through your proclamations of the Dharma. // 72 //
My ocean of hearing is perfectly purified, by which I hear every sound without exception;
with a heart full of joy, I intensely hear all the teachings spoken by all the Sugatas.
My non-dual knowledge is unattached and extends to the objects of the minds of other beings; from a single moment of mind, I enter the entire, vast ocean of the world's minds. (74)
By the power of mindfulness and concentration, I shall traverse those oceans of eons in the past—those many hundreds of oceans of various births belonging both to myself and to all worlds. (75)

In a single moment, I know all the eons, as numerous as the atoms in the oceans of fields; and I know all sentient beings wandering through the realms of existence, along with the Buddhas and their multitudes of miraculous transformations. (76)

And I indeed remember the original vow of those knowers of the world; how they attained their conduct through vast methods of setting out and arising, and having reached that which is to be practiced. (77)

And those transitions to the stages of consecration belonging to those who possess a flood of supreme qualities through peerless samādhis, as well as all the vast modes of awakening—may I enter them all in a single moment of thought. (78)

By whatever means and objects the Sugatas set in motion the supreme wheel in the world; that which is the immeasurable quality of nirvāṇa, and also the fixed rule for the abiding of the Dharma. // 79 //

Those stainless oceans of methods of vehicles and those vast means for disciplining sentient beings that have been revealed in the world by the Immeasurable Ones—I enter into them individually through various methods. (80)
For this way of liberation is the light of supreme wealth consisting of the abundant joy that is the treasury of delight;
it has been cultivated by me for many hundreds of vast eons—may you too quickly enter into this way.

Noble son, this is the bodhisattva liberation called "The Radiance of Contentment Arising from the Vast Treasure of Joy" that I know. How could I possibly describe those who have descended into the oceans of vows for the setting forth toward omniscience at the feet of all Tathāgatas;

who have fulfilled their vows through the accomplishment of the oceans of previous vows of all Tathāgatas; and who possess the valorous wisdom that traverses a single bodhisattva stage and traverses the oceans of all bodhisattva stages?

To know the conduct or to describe the qualities of those Bodhisattvas who have purified their conduct through vows that converge upon every single practice within the ocean of all Bodhisattva practices, and who possess mastery over the dwelling that converges upon the ocean of all Bodhisattva liberations within each and every Bodhisattva liberation.
Go, son of good family;
right here at this seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) is the night goddess named Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, who has approached the presence of the Blessed One.
Having approached her, ask: "How should a bodhisattva bring sentient beings to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
How are all buddha-fields to be purified?
How are all Tathāgatas to be propitiated through ultimate propitiation? And how should a bodhisattva apply himself to all the qualities of a Buddha?

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā, circumambulated the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā hundreds of thousands of times,
and looking back at her again and again, [departed] from the night goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃvāsā.
He departed from his presence. // 38 //
Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana approached the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.

He saw the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā seated upon a throne made of the essence of jewel-kings that reflects the dwellings of all worlds within that very circle of the assembly; her body was covered by a net of jewels reflecting the principles of the *dharmadhātu*,

her form manifesting the reflections of all moons, suns, lights, planets, stars, constellations, and lunar mansions, and her body appearing to the visual consciousness of sentient beings according to their respective inclinations.

The body that makes known its own form as resembling the physical forms of all sentient beings; the body that displays a vast manifestation of oceans of infinite and centerless colors; the body that displays the methods for abiding in all modes of conduct; the body that makes known itself facing toward all directions; the body that faces toward the ripening of sentient beings in all directions; and the body that faces toward all worlds, pervading all directions with various miraculous transformations like the thundering of clouds of universal Dharma.
Her body hangs down like space, facing the welfare of the world at all times; her body prostrates itself at the soles of the feet of all Tathāgatas;

her body is preceded by the happiness of accumulating roots of merit for all sentient beings; her body maintains a mindfulness that never turns away, fulfilling the success of her vows to face all Tathāgatas and receive and uphold the clouds of Dharma; her body radiates an infinite and centerless light that pervades all directions; her body displays a light released in every direction, a lamp of Dharma that dispels the darkness of the entire world.

She was one who manifested a body of stainless wisdom through phenomena that have reached the state of illusion; she manifested a body of phenomena free from the dust and darkness [of ignorance]; she was a body born from the reality-nature (dharmatā) of phenomena that have reached the state of illusion; her mind was awakened to the reality-nature and its darkness was dispelled; she had attained the illumination of the light of equal-faced wisdom; her mental and physical bodies were entirely free from fever and anguish; she emerged from the element of the indestructible essence of the Dharma-body; and she possessed a pure body whose nature is unstained by intrinsic nature and sustained by the non-abiding empowerment of the Tathāgata.

Having seen her, he bowed his head in prostration and, recollecting the methods of vision as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, he prostrated himself upon the surface of the earth and remained there for a very long time.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana rose from that ground and, with palms joined in reverence, beholding the body of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, attained ten purities of perception;
through the attainment of which he acquired a state of commonality with all spiritual friends.
What are the ten?
Namely: he conceived the notion of his own mind toward spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) for the sake of dwelling upon all objects with the vigor that initiates the quest for omniscience;
and he conceived the notion of the intrinsic nature of the purification of the maturation of his own karma for the sake of pleasing spiritual friends and attaining the vast roots of merit.

He attained the designation "adornment of the bodhisattva conduct" for the sake of dwelling in the conduct adorned by all vows; he attained the designation "accomplishment of all Buddha-dharmas" for the sake of practicing the path of the instructions of all spiritual friends;
he attained the designation "attainment of contact" for the sake of manifesting the illumination of the supreme dharma-abode within the domain of all Buddhas.
He attained the perception of a single departure for the sake of purifying the vow and conduct of departing by means of the vehicle of Samantabhadra.
He attained the perception of a mine of oceans of merit for omniscience for the sake of gathering and increasing all pure dharmas.

He attained the perception of the fulfillment, increase, and protection of perfectly complete wholesome dharmas for the sake of increasing the force of vigor for the wisdom of omniscience in the enlightenment of a Buddha.

He attained the perception of the fulfillment of all roots of goodness for the sake of fulfilling the intentions of all sentient beings; he attained the perception of the accomplishment of all aims regarding spiritual friends for the sake of establishing mastery over all the activities of bodhisattvas.
He attained these ten purifications of perception.

By obtaining these, he attained as many commonalities with the assembly of bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a buddha-field—commonalities belonging to the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.
That is to say: the commonality of mindfulness regarding the methods for recollecting all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions throughout the three times;
and the commonality of intelligence regarding the definitive discernment of the unconfused methods of the ocean of all dharmas.
The commonality of the realms of existence, through skill in the methods of non-differentiation and differentiation that follow the course of the mandalas of the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
the commonality of awakening, through a mind equal to space for the sake of attaining the illumination of the oceans of the ways of all three times;
and the commonality of the purification of the faculties, for the sake of attaining the illumination of the knowledge of the oceans of the faculties of all Bodhisattvas.
For the sake of practicing the path adorned by the qualities of the bodhisattva way—the array for gathering all beings in every manner—they attain a commonality of mental purity;

for the sake of attaining the illumination of the sphere of activity of the Tathāgatas' wisdom, they attain a commonality of the sphere of activity; and for the sake of attaining the illumination of the path that enters the ocean of methods of omniscience in all its aspects, they attain a commonality of following the methods.
The commonality of penetrating the meaning, for the sake of attaining the penetration of the knowledge of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena;
and the commonality of dwelling in the Dharma,
for the sake of shattering the mountains of all obscurations.

For the sake of attaining a pure body adorned with the various secondary marks (*anuvyañjana*), characterized by manifesting the diverse forms of the world according to their inclinations through the commonality of the purity of the form-body (*rūpakāya*);
for the sake of increasing the focal point of omniscience through the perfection of the powers of a bodhisattva, [attaining] the commonality of the powers (*bala*);
and for the sake of purifying the sky-like intention of the mind, [attaining] the commonality of fearlessness (*vaiśāradya*) regarding the oceans of all methods of the Dharma.
The commonality of vigor, for the sake of attaining tirelessness in dwelling together with the bodhisattva conduct throughout all eons;
the commonality of eloquence, for the sake of attaining the light of unobstructed knowledge regarding all phenomena;
and the commonality of being unconquerable, for the sake of the purification of one's own person which transcends all worlds.
For the sake of purifying the pleasing of all circles of assemblies, they attain a state of similarity in speech that is neither dejected nor timid;

for the sake of roaring with the sound of the ocean of all methods of Dharma, they attain a state of similarity in resonance; and for the sake of [mastering] the oceans of methods of verbal communication and expression throughout the entire world, they attain a state of similarity in the purity of the components of their voice.

the commonality of purity in qualities regarding the purity of practicing the qualities of the Tathāgata’s instruction; the commonality of non-contradiction with the lineage of the Buddha’s Dharma and deeds for the sake of the purity of the maturation of blameless karma;
and the commonality of establishing the ground for the sacrifice of Dharma for the sake of the arising of all Buddhas and the turning of the wheel of Dharma.
The commonality of the purity of the holy life, for the sake of dwelling in the knowledge of the domain of all Tathāgatas;
the commonality of great loving-kindness, for the sake of pervading the ocean of all sentient beings at every moment through various methods of loving-kindness;
and the commonality of entering the ocean of the method of great compassion, for the sake of raining down clouds of Dharma to protect the realm of all sentient beings.
The commonality of bodily action for the sake of the commonality of employing skillful means to mature all sentient beings;
the commonality of purity of vocal action regarding the expressions and desires for all conventional dharmas;
and the commonality of mental action for the sake of directing the minds of all sentient beings toward the objective support of omniscience.

The state of being endowed with the adornment of all various arrays, in order to approach all Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields; the state of being endowed with the act of approaching [the Buddhas] throughout the oceans of all Buddha-arisings;
and the state of being endowed with the request for the turning of the wheel of Dharma from all Tathāgatas.
The commonality of worship and service, for the sake of performing all forms of worship and service to all Tathāgatas at all times;

the commonality of maturing and disciplining all sentient beings within the realm of all sentient beings; and the commonality of attaining illumination regarding the methods of the Dharma for all sentient beings.
the commonality of attaining meditative concentration within the oceans of all methods of concentration;
the commonality of universal pervasion for the sake of pervading the miraculous displays of the conduct of bodhisattvas throughout the oceans of all buddha-fields;
and the commonality of the bodhisattva’s dwelling within the oceans of all methods of bodhisattva miraculous displays.
the commonality of retinue in all dwellings for the practice of the bodhisattva path; the commonality of entry into all subtle entries into all world-systems;
and the commonality of mental differentiation throughout the vastness of all buddha-fields.

the commonality of the diversity of followings in the followings of the diverse entries into the oceans of all buddha-fields; the commonality of the pervasive expansion of universal methods in the infinite cognitions that discern the divisions of all buddha-fields;
and the commonality of being exalted throughout all buddha-fields.

The commonality of non-retrogression, for the sake of the non-retrogressive empowerment that radiates and converges throughout all directions; the commonality of dispelling darkness, for the sake of attaining the illumination of the circle of wisdom that awakens at the seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Buddhas;
and the commonality of attainment within the oceans of all the circles of the Buddha's assemblies.

the commonality of pervading the network of bodies throughout all buddha-fields; the commonality of direct gnosis regarding the continuous succession of oceans of methods of Dharma within those fields;
and the commonality of practice in the application of facing all methods of Dharma in their proper sequence.
The commonality of aspiration for the sake of purifying the undertaking of intense desire for the Dharma;
the commonality of purity regarding the undertaking of the ornaments of the qualities of a Buddha through the actions of body, speech, and mind;
and the commonality of a well-disposed mind for the sake of purifying the mandala of knowledge of all phenomena through a mental mandala that is impartial and free from conceptual construction.

the commonality of the undertaking of vigor in the applications for completing the accumulation of all roots of goodness; the commonality of the array of conduct in the perfect accomplishment of all bodhisattva practices;
and the commonality of dwelling in non-attachment in the penetration of the signs of all phenomena.
the commonality of the method of skillful means in the various miraculous displays of knowledge regarding the dwelling in the Dharma;

the commonality of the purity of the sense bases in the undertaking of viewing sentient beings without partiality according to their inclinations; and the commonality of attaining the gateways to the samādhis of bodhisattvas in the attainment of the non-conceptualization of all phenomena.
The commonality of the basis in the manifestations of all Tathāgatas; the commonality of the treading upon the stages in the attainment of all the stages of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
and the commonality of the foundation in all the established positions of Bodhisattvas.
The commonality of receiving instructions in all the prophecies of the Buddhas;

the commonality of meditative absorption in the methods of all oceans of samādhis in a single instant; and the commonality of the establishment of meditative absorption in the various activities of the Buddhas characterized by diverse marks.

The commonality of recollection regarding the oceans of methods for all objects of mindfulness; the commonality of the conduct of a bodhisattva regarding the exertions throughout kalpas reaching to the furthest limits of the future for the sake of a bodhisattva’s tasks;
and the commonality of serene confidence for the purpose of increasing the ocean-like surge of joy and devotion toward the immeasurable wisdom of the Buddhas.
The commonality of increase for the sake of producing the infinite equipment of the Buddha-knowledge that is irreversible from all mountains of obscurations;
the commonality of rebirth at the times for maturing and disciplining all sentient beings;
and the commonality of dwelling within the gateways of the method of omniscience.
The commonality of the objective sphere in entering the spheres of the preeminence of the principle of the dharma-realm;
the commonality of non-abiding for the sake of uprooting all bases of consciousness;
and the commonality of the teaching of all dharmas in the entries into the knowledge of the equality of dharmas.

The state of sharing in the assembly of application for the sake of receiving one's own body through the empowerment of all Buddhas; the state of sharing in the superknowledges regarding the methods of practice for making known all worlds;
and the state of sharing in the attainment of unconditioned miraculous powers for entering the oceans of realms in all directions.

The commonality of the stage of retention, for the sake of attaining the illumination of the ocean of all dhāraṇīs; the commonality of entering the transitions of the wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas regarding all discourses on the Dharma in the sūtras;
and the commonality of entering the profound Dharma regarding the entries into the methods of all phenomena that are like the expanse of space.

The commonality of radiance throughout the expansion of all world-systems; the commonality of brilliant splendor in the manifestation of perceptions for the world according to its inclinations; and the commonality of trembling in the display of miraculous transformations within the empowerment of buddha-fields for sentient beings.
He attained a state of commonality in the discipline of sentient beings through seeing, hearing, and recollecting [the Buddha], whose conduct is never in vain;
he attained a state of commonality in liberation for the sake of awakening to the knowledge of the ten powers and the perfection of the ocean-like methods of all vows.
Thus, the merchant’s son Sudhana, with a mind full of serene faith, [beheld] the light of the vigor of the vow to protect all living beings.

Beholding the night goddess, through the attainment of these ten purifications of perception, he acquired, headed by her, as many sons of like nature as there are atoms in a Buddha-field from the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having entered into the vision of as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms, through the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā; having attained the purity of the perception of spiritual friends as being without end or middle;
and having entered into the state of commonality with as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms.
Having adjusted his robe over one shoulder and bowed with palms joined toward the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, at that moment he spoke these verses:
"Just as I possess mastery over my own mind, so too is my aspiration for awakening firm and irreversible."
For even in my own mind, O Goddess, such a firm conviction has likewise arisen spontaneously this very day. // 1 //
All my sins have been purified without exception, and a radiant, auspicious fruition has been attained;
by the sight of you, Sudarśanā, inexhaustible pure dharmas have been accumulated by me. // 2 //

My mind is adorned with a multitude of diverse virtues engaged in the welfare of sentient beings—those very virtues by which I have practiced the conduct throughout all fields for aeons reaching to the furthest limit. (3)
Indeed, you have demonstrated to me, Noble One, the non-origination of all phenomena for my benefit;
out of a sense of favor toward me, please grant me the supreme instruction in the Dharma for my welfare. // 4 //
The path leading to the miserable realms has been overturned, and the pure path to heaven has been revealed;
the path to omniscience, followed by all the Sugatas, has also been shown to you. (5)
Today, in your presence, a supreme perception of departure—unparalleled and marvelous—has arisen within me;
it is pure, like space, stainless, and immeasurable, the gateway to the dharma of omniscience.
Through the perception that you are the source of all merit for the sake of omniscience, immeasurable [merits] have arisen in me toward you;
oceans of merit, vast as space, arise in my mind at every moment. (7)
O Noble One, uplift me with the perfections and increase me with inconceivable merits;
thus nourished by all auspicious qualities, I shall before long obtain the diadem of omniscience. (8)

For toward spiritual friends, I always maintain the perception that they are the fulfillment of the path to omniscience; for this reason, all my pure virtues will quickly become fully perfected. // 9 //
Since all things originate from him, and he is perfected and endowed with auspicious qualities,
by propitiating him who possesses infinite virtues, I shall proclaim for the worlds the path of the Omniscient One.
O Noble One, you have become my teacher; you are the guide for me in the immeasurable qualities of the teachings of the Omniscient One.
It would not be possible for me to repay you, even in incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of eons.

Then, having spoken these verses, the merchant’s son Sudhana said this to the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā: "O goddess, you have shown me this inconceivable sphere of the bodhisattva liberation.
Tell me, goddess, what is the name of this liberation?"
“O goddess, for how long have you set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
Or after how much time will you realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
When this was said, the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana as follows: “I am named Sarvasattvaparipākasaṃcodanakuśalasaṃbhava...”
"Noble son, this is the liberation. Noble son, endowed with this liberation, having awakened to the equality of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena,
having entered into the primordial nature of all phenomena, and relying upon the dharma that is without abode, I have transcended all worlds and attained a state of perfectly distinct form."

Having entered into the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), they possess a color that is non-dissimilar, a color that is irreversible, a color that is non-conceptual, and a color that is neither blue, nor yellow, nor red, nor white; having entered into the nature of phenomena, their physical forms (*ātmabhāva*) consist of various distinct colors and appearances,
yet they are non-dissimilar, non-diverse, without variation, non-conceptual, and a color that is neither blue, nor yellow, nor red, nor white.
He possesses a complexion of many colors, an immeasurable complexion, a pure complexion, a complexion that emits all manner of arrays, a complexion visible from every direction,

a complexion corresponding to all living beings, a complexion surpassing all worlds by facing them directly, a complexion that reflects a universal radiance, a complexion pleasing to behold, a complexion perfectly purified by the primary and secondary marks, and a complexion radiant with blameless conduct.

He possesses a complexion that displays great strength and prowess; a complexion that is profound and difficult to approach; a complexion that cannot be surpassed by any in the world; a complexion that is diverse from moment to moment; a complexion that displays clouds of manifold colors; a complexion of various forms and shapes; a complexion that displays immeasurable miraculous transformations; a complexion of most beautiful speech; a complexion of all that is well-formed in mind; a complexion that is conducive to the maturation of all sentient beings; and a complexion that brings forth virtue by appearing before those to be trained according to their inclinations.

Their color is of unimpeded, all-pervading radiance; their color is clear, unturbid, serene, and luminous; their color is adorned by the development of an indestructible body; their color proclaims the inconceivable method of the Dharma; their color is sovereign, unconquered, and capable of overcoming all; their color is free from the darkness of gloom; their color dispels all obscurity; their color is perfectly purified by all that is white; their color is an ocean of the qualities of a Great Being; and their color is perfectly purified by long-standing reverence for former teachers.

They possess the excellence of a supreme, vast, and preeminent complexion, purified like the sky of their resolute intention; they possess the excellence of proclaiming an ocean of qualities that is indestructible and inexhaustible; they possess the excellence of a complexion that is undifferentiated and relied upon by all worlds; they possess the excellence of a complexion that pervades all directions without attachment; they possess the excellence of manifesting an ocean of many various complexions through the expansion of moments of mind across unspeakable oceans of realms;

they possess the excellence of increasing the great surge of joy in all sentient beings; they possess the excellence of gathering in an ocean of all sentient beings; and they possess the excellence of the thundering roar of clouds from an ocean of all the Buddha-qualities from every single pore.

His color was purified by the ocean of the inclinations and aspirations of all sentient beings; his color manifested the definitive determination of the meaning of all dharmas; his color was illuminated by a net of light rays of various colors; his color possessed stainless radiance equal in measure to space; his color rested upon the radiance of the dustless purity of the king of pure jewels;

his color was a reflection of the stainless nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); his color was a manifold manifestation from an ocean of incomparable methods of color; and his color illuminated all directions.
She possesses a color that manifests the world according to the proper time; a color born from tranquility, self-control, and the directions; a color that pacifies all afflictions;
a color that brings forth the field of merit for the entire world; a color that pacifies all methods; a color that unfailingly pervades the world;

a color that brings forth the prowess of great wisdom; a color that unfailingly pervades everywhere with an unattached body; and a color that unfailingly displays her excellent body to the world from every side.

Her color was the manifestation of an ocean of great loving-kindness; her color was the manifestation of the Sumeru mountain of great merit; her color was the attainment of appearing in all states of existence throughout the world while remaining unattached to any world;

her color was the purification of the power of great wisdom; her color was dwelling in the recollection of all worlds; her color was the radiance of all jewels; her color was the manifestation of the womb of Vairocana; her color was in accordance with the faith of all living beings; her color was oriented toward the aspects of omniscience; her color was the gladdening of the world with smiling eyes.
They possess a color that is the supreme illumination of the array of all jewels; a color that is an ungraspable radiance turned away from the entire world; a color that is not fixed in attachment;
a color that displays the sovereign power of miraculous transformations through empowerment; a color that displays the sovereign power of all various miraculous transformations;
a color that illuminates the roots of goodness of the Tathāgatas; and a color that extends throughout the ocean-like principles of the entire faultless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

He possessed a complexion that attained the manifestation of approaching the circles of assemblies of all Buddhas; a complexion produced from an ocean of various colors; a complexion born as the natural outflow of well-practiced conduct; a complexion that leads according to what is necessary for guidance; a complexion whose sight never satiates any world; a complexion that radiates a manifold, brilliant light; a complexion encompassing all the three times; a complexion that displays oceans [of forms]; and a complexion that emits an ocean of rays of light of every color.

Their color was ineffable; their color displayed an ocean of various and immeasurable light-mandalas; their color surpassed all the world through the descent of every kind of fragrance; their color displayed clouds of solar discs as numerous as the atoms in ineffable Buddha-fields from each and every pore;
their color was sustained by clouds of the forms of stainless lunar discs; and their color emitted clouds of Sumeru-like flowers of uninterrupted beauty.

They possessed colors that emitted clouds of garlands from trees of various manifestations raining down all manner of ornaments and garlands; colors that displayed clouds of lotuses made of every kind of jewel;

and colors that pervaded the entire realm of phenomena with clouds of physical forms consisting of masses of all fragrant incenses. Moment by moment, they sustained clouds of caskets containing powdered incense, which, having pervaded the oceans of all methods within the entire realm of phenomena in the ten directions, [remained there].

of beings to be disciplined by sight, those to be disciplined by hearing, those to be disciplined by mindfulness, those to be disciplined by the manifestation of the emanation of the wheel of Dharma, those to be disciplined when the time for maturation has arrived, those to be disciplined by the display of the form-body, those to be disciplined by attendance, those to be disciplined by awakening, those to be disciplined by the display of various miraculous transformations, and those to be disciplined by the display of the communication of inconceivable miraculous transformations.
By the power of the inclinations of sentient beings; by the power of time; by the power of turning back unwholesome karma; by the power of establishing the arising of wholesome karma;

by the power of accomplishing former great vows; by the power of the momentum toward omniscience; by the power of the Dharma that attains the vast miraculous transformations of the bodhisattva liberations; by the power of generating the strength of great compassion accomplished for the sake of protecting the entire world; and by the power of the intention to produce the purification of the ocean of great loving-kindness.
I set it forth because it has been well received through the empowerment of the Tathāgata.

"In this way, noble son, having established myself in this bodhisattva liberation called ‘The Exhortation to the Roots of Goodness According to the Intentions for the Maturation of All Beings,’ and having entered into the undifferentiated nature of phenomena, I manifest a body, color, and form that is without end or middle."
From each single form of conduct, by means of the manifestation of oceans of infinite and intermediate colors, and from each single color of conduct,

having emitted clouds of infinite and intermediate rays of light and displayed the reflections of Buddha-fields, and in each Buddha-field having displayed the arising of infinite and intermediate Tathāgatas from each single ray, for each one...
And while displaying the infinite and boundless miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata, I stir up my former roots of virtue; I plant roots of virtue that have not yet been planted;
and I cause those already planted to flourish extensively.
I cause the roots of virtue that have been expanded to increase further;
and in every moment of thought, I establish the infinite and boundless realm of sentient beings in the stage of non-retrogression toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Furthermore, noble son, as for what you have asked: "Goddess, how long has it been since you set out for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?
For how many hundreds of eons have you practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva?"—I shall explain this matter to you as well, through the power of the Buddha.
Noble son, the circle of gnosis of the bodhisattvas has as its object that which is beyond conceptualization, non-conceptualization, and discursive construction.
Within it, neither the length nor the brevity of an eon is manifested or perceived;

nor is the defilement of an eon, the purity of an eon, the smallness of an eon, the greatness of an eon, the multiplicity of eons, the diversity of eons, the various forms of eons, or the disparity of eons.
Or it is manifested, or it is made known.
Why is that?

Noble son, the mandala of wisdom of bodhisattvas, which is pure by its very nature and essence, free from the entire web of conceptualizations, and having transcended all mountains of obscurations, arises within their intention.
And that radiance illuminates all sentient beings— those who are to be disciplined according to their inclinations, their ripening, and the appropriate time.
Just as, noble son, in the orb of the sun there is no reckoning of day and night, nor does it dwell therein.
When the solar disk has set, night is perceived and manifested;
when the solar disk has risen, day is perceived and manifested.
In the same way, noble son, within the non-conceptual solar disk of a bodhisattva’s gnosis, all conceptual constructions, discriminations, and imaginings do not exist.
All the time-periods of the past, present, and future exist within the conceptual categories of dwelling throughout all of saṃsāra.

Nevertheless, by the radiance of the mandala of non-conceptual knowledge arising from the bodhisattva’s intention, and by the power of the time required to bring all sentient beings to maturity, the calculation of the number of eons spent dwelling in saṃsāra is manifested within the conceptual categories of those time-periods.

Furthermore, within the mandala of non-conceptual knowledge, the calculation of the number of eons spent dwelling from the prior limit to the subsequent limit is manifested within the conceptual categories of those time-periods.

For example, noble son, the orb of the sun, having reached the expanse of the sky, is perceived as appearing in all jewel-mountains, all jewel-trees, all jewel-kings, all jewel-mines, all oceans, all springs and lakes, all vessels of clear water, and in the minds of all living beings.
And it appears directly before sentient beings;
moreover, within all the atoms of every jewel, the solar disk is seen as having attained manifestation,
yet that solar disk does not actually exist within those jewel-mountains.
