It does not enter into jewel-trees, nor even into the atoms of dust; it does not become contained within the expansions of gems,
nor does it follow after the sources of jewels.
It does not descend into the oceans;
it does not enter into all water vessels;
yet it is seen to be present within them everywhere.

In the same way, noble son, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has set out from the ocean of existence and emerged into the sky of the Tathāgata’s realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), dwelling in the sphere of the sky-like intrinsic nature of phenomena and residing in the peaceful abode of the sky, is seen appearing within all states of existence and births through bodies corresponding to all sentient beings, for the sake of maturing and disciplining them.
He is not defiled by the faults of saṃsāra,
he is not tormented by the sufferings of death and rebirth, and he does not dwell amidst conceptual constructions of the kalpas.
And he has no perception of that eon as long, nor does he have a perception of it as short.
Why is that?
Because the bodhisattva has utterly transcended the perversions of perception, mind, and view, being entirely free from inversion.
Perceiving all worlds as they truly are like a dream, having entered all worlds as being like an illusion, having attained the knowledge that the realm is devoid of sentient beings,
and seeing phenomena as they truly are, he appears facing all sentient beings by the power of his vast circle of compassion and his great vows, for the sake of their ripening and discipline.

For example, noble son, just as a boat on great rivers and the like is constantly and continuously engaged in ferrying beings across, never ceasing its activity throughout its lifespan, yet it has no attachment to this shore, nor to the far shore, nor does it remain in the midst of the water;
In the same way, noble son, a bodhisattva, by means of the power of the vessel of the great perfections, has set out to ferry across all sentient beings from the current of the river of saṃsāra;
yet he feels no terror regarding the hither shore, nor does he form a notion of security regarding the further shore.
Moreover, he is constantly and continuously engaged in the task of ferrying sentient beings across.

Through his dwelling in the conduct of a bodhisattva, which is resolutely undertaken throughout immeasurable eons, he applies himself to the vastness of those eons; he does not practice the conduct of a bodhisattva while being attached to a perception of long duration that merely looks for the passing away of the eons.
For example, noble son, the realm of phenomena is as vast as the element of space, like the mandala of the sky; whether all world-systems are undergoing dissolution,

evolution, or have already passed away, it remains free from conceptual construction, pure by nature, undefiled, unobstructed, untiring, neither long nor short, not sinking down, and sustaining all fields throughout the time of the future limit.

In the same way, noble son, the bodhisattva— whose mandala of the sky-like expanse of the knowledge of intention is encircled by the whirlwind of great vows— does not grow weary while supporting sentient beings from falling into all the precipices of miserable rebirths,
nor does he tremble while leading them onto the path of happy rebirths.
Establishing others on the paths to omniscience, he does not become weary;
he is not disturbed by any afflictions,
nor is he defiled by the faults of saṃsāra.
For example, noble son, in a person who has emerged from an illusory state and whose every major and minor limb is complete, ten states pertaining to the body do not exist.
What are these ten? Namely:
either coming or going;
Whether cold or heat,
hunger or thirst, joy or a state of anger and resentment;

Neither birth, aging, sickness, nor death, nor any affliction exists [for such a being]. In the very same way, noble son, for a bodhisattva who has emerged from the realm of illusory knowledge, whose body is the undifferentiated dharmadhātu,
and who is born into all states of existence throughout all eons in order to mature all sentient beings— [therein] ten...
Phenomena do not exist.
Which ten? Namely:
either the longing for saṃsāra, or weariness with birth, existence, and rebirth in the realms of saṃsāra, or the pursuit of attachment to sense objects.

Whether it be a mind of resentment, a desire for enjoyment, the torment of all afflictions, the experience of painful sensations, the fear of rebirth in the realms of sense objects, a longing for existence, or dogmatic attachment—
nevertheless, noble son, by the power of the Buddha, I shall explain this in order to increase the strength of the vast bodhisattva vows of future bodhisattvas.

In the past, noble son, in a time long ago— further back than even the most distant eon equal to the atoms of dust in an ocean of world-systems— at that time and on that occasion, there was a world-system named Ratnaprabhā.
Furthermore, noble son, in that world-system Ratnaprabhā, there was an eon named Suprabha.
Furthermore, in that eon called Suprabha, ten thousand Buddhas appeared.

Among those ten thousand Buddhas, O son of good family, the first Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha to appear in the world was named Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparāja; he was endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, and unsurpassed.
The charioteer who subdues men, the teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One— he by whom supreme, perfect enlightenment was first fully realized.
Furthermore, O son of good family, that Tathāgata was in the midst [of the assembly].
He was born not far from the royal capital called Rativyūhā, which belonged to the four-continent world-system.
To the east of that royal capital Rativyūhā, there was a forest grove named Suprabha.
Within that Suprabha forest grove, there was a seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) named Ratnakusumamegha.
On that very seat of enlightenment, the Cloud of Jewel Flowers, there appeared a lion throne with a lotus-womb made of Vairocana-jewels,

upon which the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, sat down and fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. At that time, the lifespan of human beings was ten thousand years.

Then, when all those who take life, those who take what is not given, those who engage in sexual misconduct, those who speak falsehoods, those who are malicious, those who speak harshly, those who engage in idle chatter, those who are covetous, those with malevolent intent, and those with wrong views had appeared in the world— and thus when the ten unwholesome paths of action had become widespread and firmly established— the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, [acted].

For a full thousand years, having gone to the seat of awakening, he taught the Dharma to the bodhisattvas and to the lords of the world who had previously performed services for the Victors, in order to ripen the roots of virtue of the humans of Jambudvīpa.
And at that time, in that royal capital named Rativyūha, there was a king named Jayaprabha.
He [punished] men who took what was not given, thieves, evildoers, those who took life, those who engaged in sexual misconduct,
liars, slanderers, those who spoke harsh words, those who used frivolous speech, the covetous, and those with malicious intent.

There were many hundreds of thousands of those with wrong views, who were stained by passion for what is not the Dharma, overcome by improper greed, possessed of false teachings, having committed evil, having performed cruel deeds, having failed to perform meritorious acts, and having failed to provide protection for those struck by fear; who were not filial toward their mothers or fathers, who were not like true *śramaṇas* or *brāhmaṇas*, who lacked noble knowledge, and who were offenders— cast into prison for the purpose of subduing them.

Furthermore, King Jayaprabha had a son named Vijitāvin, who was handsome, pleasing, and beautiful to behold, endowed with a most excellent and abundant complexion, and possessed of the twenty-eight marks of a great man.

Now, while he was seated upon the Sarasvatī-saṃgīti palace, surrounded by a vast retinue of women, he heard the terrifying sound of wailing from those beings imprisoned in the jail, bound with various kinds of tight fetters.
Having heard this, he became agitated and his mind was filled with distress; moved by great compassion, he descended from that palace, entered that prison,
and beheld those beings cast into the depths of the dungeon— bound by various shackles, fetters, anklets, bracelets, chains, and bits,
their bodies bound to one another, plunged into great darkness, enveloped in smoke and gloom, and their bodies afflicted by violent winds.

Their limbs were covered with prominent veins; they were tormented by hunger and thirst, naked and without clothing, their bodies smeared with dust and dirt, their forms shrouded in matted hair, bound with heavy iron shackles, and undergoing various tortures. They experienced manifold painful sensations, uttering diverse cries of lamentation and wailing.

Seeing them, he gave rise to great compassion; with a noble and compassionate intention born within him, his mind set on accomplishing the welfare of others, he comforted those beings who had entered the depths of the prison. To liberate them from their bonds, he granted those beings freedom from fear. Then, approaching King Jayaprabha, he spoke thus: "Your Majesty should know that out of compassion, I have granted freedom from fear to the beings imprisoned in the jail."
They would be released.
Then King Jayaprabha, having assembled all five hundred ministers, questioned them: "What is your opinion?
They replied, "These plunderers of the royal treasury have exerted themselves for the king's death."
While searching through the king's inner apartments, they were captured;
for these men deserve death,
and their punishment shall indeed be execution, or death while imprisoned.
Even he who acts for their benefit is guilty of an offense against the king.
Then, indeed, that prince Vijitāvin, deeply afflicted by great compassion, said to those ministers: "Let it be exactly as you say;
therefore, release these innocent men."
"O Noble One, I am willing to endure all the painful sensations for their sake;
whatever must be done for them by you, do that for me.
For the sake of liberating them from bondage, I shall sacrifice my body and life, even if it means being subjected to various forms of torture."
For what reason?
If I am not able to release these beings from this bondage,
how then can I [release] those beings who have entered the prison-house of the three realms, who are bound by the snares of craving, and who have fallen into the thicket of ignorance?

Those cast into the darkness of delusion, tormented by the suffering of poverty, entered upon the deep and dense miserable destinies, with disfigured and discolored bodies, deprived of the functioning of all their faculties, with wandering minds, seeing no way out, lacking light,
attached to the triple world, destitute of the equipment of merit and wisdom, and fallen away from the sphere of knowledge.

In order to liberate those whose minds are defiled by various afflictions, who are cast into the cage of suffering, who have fallen under the power of Māra, and who are oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair.

Then, indeed, Prince Vijitāvin liberated all those beings who were held in bondage from that prison by means of his own self-sacrifice, along with his entire retinue and his whole mass of wealth; having liberated them and cast off whatever source of suffering those beings possessed, he did not turn back.
Then those five hundred ministers, with their arms raised and crying out, approached King Jayaprabha and said this: "May Your Majesty know concerning Prince Vijitāvin—"
Out of desire, this royal treasury is being plundered;
there is even a threat to the lives of all of us.
If Your Majesty should carry out the punishment of Prince Vijitāvin, [we shall suffer the same fate].
The life of the King will not last for long.
Then King Jayaprabha, enraged, ordered Prince Vijitāvin, along with those offending men, to be executed.

Upon hearing this, his mother, his own progenitor, became deeply distressed; surrounded by a thousand women, with her hair disheveled and her body devoid of ornaments, she tore at her face, beat her breast, and wailed with a piteous cry, weeping as dust was scattered over her head.
Approaching the king together with her retinue, she prostrated at his feet and made this request: "O King, release Prince Vijitāvin!
O King, grant life to the prince!"
Then the king, having placed Prince Vijitāvin before him, spoke thus: "Release these guilty men, prince;
if you do not release them, then for their sake you shall undergo execution."
He accepted his execution with a mind that was unshrinking, undaunted, intent upon the objective of omniscience, dedicated to the welfare of others, and preceded by great compassion.
His mother, Queen Jayaprabhā, requested the King for half a month’s leave to see her son, saying: "For half a month, let the prince give gifts to whoever has need of them;
thereafter, he may be dealt with as you wish."
"Let it be so," the king consented.
Then, to the north of that royal capital Rativyūhā, there was a great park named Sūryaprabha, which had been prepared as a sacrificial enclosure for former sacrifices.
Having gone forth there, the prince gave to each person whatever they required.
As he was performing that unobstructed sacrifice, various methods of giving were bestowed for half a month.

Food was given to those seeking food; drink, clothing, flowers, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, jewels, ornaments, various decorations, and all kinds of requisites were released to those who desired them.
Then, on the final day, the entire multitude of people assembled.
The king, the ministers, the groups of women, the guild-leaders, the householders, the people of the towns and the countryside,

and all the various religious sects assembled together. And that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, having awaited the time for the ripening and disciplining of sentient beings, [proceeded].
He approached that sacrificial enclosure, surrounded by hosts of the lords of gods, surrounded by hosts of the lords of nāgas, honored by the lords of nāgas,

bowed to by the bodies of the lords of yakṣas, praised by the lords of gandharvas, his body prostrated before the lords of asuras; with a serene mind adorned by crest-jewels, he was strewn over with the ritual offerings of the lords of garuḍas, worshipped by the lords of kiṃnaras with joyful hearts, and urged on by hymns and songs of praise.
With his face gazed upon by the lords of the mahoragas,

that great multitude of people and the prince Vijitāvin beheld from afar the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, as he was approaching— gracious, beautiful to behold, and with senses at peace.

With a peaceful mind, guarded, and having conquered the senses, he was like a well-tamed elephant; clear and serene, like a limpid lake, he shone with the great miraculous power of a Buddha’s transformations and the great majesty of a Buddha’s bull-like prowess.

He surpassed all through his sovereign authority as a Buddha and illuminated everything through the greatness of a Buddha, his body adorned and graced by the marks and secondary signs of a Great Buddha.

Illuminating the entire world with the radiance of the Buddha’s halo, shining upon it with the rays of the Buddha, emitting from every pore wheels of fragrant jewel-flames, causing the entire world to tremble by shaking the Buddha-fields,
and abandoning the afflictions of all sentient beings through the display of the Buddha’s prowess by raining down clouds of every kind of array.
They approached with the deportment of a Buddha, which increases the surge of joy in all sentient beings, and by the power of the vision of a Buddha;
and having seen him, they conceived a serene faith in the presence of the Blessed One.

Then, indeed, Prince Vijitāvin and that great multitude of people, having approached from afar toward the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, with hearts full of serene faith, prostrated themselves with their entire bodies, bowed their heads at his feet, and having honored him with manifold kinds of worship, spoke these words: "Come, Blessed One! Come, Sugata!"
"We have been attended to by the Tathāgata;
we have been sustained by the Sugata.
Then the prince Vijitāvin, pointing out the seat of honor for that Blessed One, spoke thus: "May the Blessed One be seated."
"This seat has been prepared.
Then, as the Blessed One approached, that seat was empowered by the power of the Buddha with a lotus-womb made of the king of fragrant jewels by the deities whose bodies consist of pure essences.
Thereupon, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja sat down upon that seat.
And among the retinues seated around him,
by the mere sight of him, all the illnesses of every being in that assembly were pacified;
they became free from all obscurations and hindrances, and remained established as fit vessels for the noble dharmas.
Then, indeed, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, perceiving those beings to be worthy vessels, delivered a discourse in due order;
that is to say, he fully revealed the sūtra entitled *Hetumaṇḍalaprabhāsa*.

From within his mouth, he emitted a sound endowed with a thousand qualities of voice, joined with all the factors of dharma, and resonating with the utterances and sounds of the ocean of mantras for the entire world.
Then, at that very moment, from that assembly, the dust-free and stainless Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena arose for eighty million living beings;
many millions of living beings attained the stage of those beyond training (aśaikṣa),
and ten thousand living beings were disciplined in the Mahāyāna.
That is to say, they were introduced into the method for fulfilling the great vows of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Thus, as that Blessed One turned the wheel of Dharma through the great miraculous power of a Buddha, beings in the ten directions, equal in number to the atoms in hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields, were led to discipline in the Mahāyāna.

And infinite beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions, within the vast assemblies of various Buddha-fields, were turned away from the states of woe. Furthermore, beings beyond counting were established on the path to rebirth in the heavens.
And Prince Vijitāvin attained this Bodhisattva liberation, which arises from the roots of goodness that impel beings toward maturity according to their inclinations.

Furthermore, noble son, you might think that at that time and on that occasion, the prince Vijitāvin was someone else who, having renounced his own life, having renounced his entire mass of wealth and retinue, and having renounced all the pleasures of the human world of living beings, liberated those beings who were held in bondage from that bondage. But it should not be seen thus. Why is that? It was indeed I, noble son, who at that time and on that occasion was the prince Vijitāvin. And it was by me, noble son, that at that time and on that occasion, having renounced my own life, having renounced my entire mass of wealth and retinue, and having renounced all the pleasures of the human world of living beings, those beings who were held in bondage were liberated from that bondage. Why is that? Because, noble son, there is no other who has performed such a deed as I have done. Noble son, even if one were to spend a hundred thousand million aeons, one could not fully describe the extent of the roots of merit accumulated by me through that single act of giving. Why is that? Because, noble son, it is for the sake of the Dharma that I have given up my body, my life, my wealth, my retinue, and all the pleasures of the world of living beings. Noble son, this is the supreme gift, namely, the gift of the Dharma; this is the unsurpassed gift, namely, the gift of the Dharma. Noble son, the gift of the Dharma surpasses all other gifts."
And was that unimpeded great sacrifice performed?
And was that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, propitiated?
And upon seeing that Tathāgata, was the mind set upon unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?
And this Bodhisattva liberation, which arises from the roots of goodness that impel the maturation of all sentient beings according to their inclinations, has been attained.
Furthermore, noble son, you should not view it in that way;
for at that time, in that period, I was the prince named Vijitāvin.

When I was that Prince Vijitāvin, I was intensely moved by great compassion, dedicated to the welfare of the entire world, unattached to the three realms, seeking no karmic fruition, taking no delight in fame or renown, not exalting myself, not disparaging others,
non-attached to all things, having shaken off the notion of existence, and finding no pleasure in the three realms.
Turning away from the pleasures of the worldly realm, not turning away from the realm of the Tathāgata, with a pure intention for awakening, perfected by the vajra-like resolute intention,

through the application of great loving-kindness toward all the world, joined with the pacification of the suffering of great compassion for all the world, he took hold of the resolute intention of the powers of the Tathāgata,
purified the path of the Bodhisattva, adorned the way of departure through the array of the Mahāyāna, and gazed upon the path to omniscience.
These difficult deeds have been performed in this way.
Noble son, it has been a long time since I attained this bodhisattva liberation, which arises from the roots of goodness that impel the intentions of all sentient beings toward their maturation.
What do you think, noble son— were those five hundred ministers at that time different from these [present ones],
by whom King Jayaprabha was falsely informed and incited to my execution?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way.
These are those five hundred men whom Devadatta incited to kill the Blessed One;
they have been disciplined by the Blessed One and prophesied for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment— namely, that in a future time,
after eons equal in number to the atoms of Mount Sumeru, in a single eon named Suprabha, there will be five hundred Buddhas.

The various arrays of qualities of diverse buddha-fields; the various origins from different births, families, and lineages; the various designations of mothers and fathers; the various displays of miraculous transformations at birth; the various miraculous displays of renunciation; the various displays of the radiance of diverse bodhi-trees; the various gateways for approaching the sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa); the various displays of the destruction of Māra’s armies; and the various displays of miraculous transformations at the moment of perfect awakening.

The various turnings of the wheel of Dharma with their methods, etymologies, and explanations; the various instructions on the methods of the sūtras; the various utterances of vocal paths and sounds; the various arrays of the circles of assemblies; the various emissions of arrays of light from the spheres of radiance; the various measures of lifespan; the various empowerments of the teachings; the various manifestations of the teachings; and the various names of those whose bodies are great compassion.
Among them, first, there will be a Tathāgata named Mahākāruṇika who will attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in the world-system Ratnaprabhā;
in that very same world-system, second, a Tathāgata named Sarvajagaddhitapraṇidhānacandra will arise;
and third, Mahākaruṇāsiṃha.
A Tathāgata named [First Name] will arise; a fourth Tathāgata named Sarvalokahitaiṣī will arise; and so on, until finally a Tathāgata named Vaidyarāja will arise.

What do you think, noble son— were those men who at that time and on that occasion were offenders and evildoers against the king, whom I delivered from that bondage by sacrificing my own body and life, others than these? Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way.
These are the Tathāgatas of the Bhadrakalpa, headed by Krakucchanda;

and there are ten other hundreds of thousands of incalculable bodhisattvas, through the sight of whom— the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Anantabalavighuṣṭanirnāditaśrīsaṃbhavamate— the resolve for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment was generated.
Those who are currently practicing the conduct of awakening in the ten directions,

as well as these [bodhisattvas], cultivate and expand this bodhisattva liberation, which arises from the roots of goodness that incite beings according to their inclinations for the sake of maturing all sentient beings.
"What do you think, noble son—was that King Jayaprabha at that time and on that occasion someone else?
It should not be viewed in this way.
That Satyaka Mahāvādī was, at that time and on that occasion, the king named Jayaprabha."
What do you think, noble son—was that royal retinue at that time and on that occasion, including the women of the harem, the gatekeepers, the courtiers, or the followers, anyone else?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way;
for they were these very sixty thousand Nirgranthas.
Those who were brought into the presence of the Blessed One by Satyaka Mahāvādī, having approached the Blessed One for debate as upholders of the banner of debaters—
all of them were prophesied by the Blessed One for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Tathāgatas will arise in the world with various arrays of buddha-fields, in various kalpas, and with various names.

Furthermore, noble son, that Prince Vijitāvin, having been granted permission by his parents, liberated those beings who were in bondage; then, abandoning the vast earth abounding in wealth, gold, and jewels, and renouncing his wife and children,
he went forth into homelessness in the presence of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja.

Having gone forth, he practiced the holy life for five thousand years. During that interval, he brought ten thousand gateways of meditative concentration to perfection and attained ten thousand gateways of dhāraṇī.
Ten thousand methods of the superknowledges entered him;
he obtained ten thousand great treasuries of the bodhisattvas;
and ten thousand impulses toward omniscience arose within him.
Furthermore, ten thousand gateways of patience were purified by him;
ten thousand mental concentrations were brought forth;
and ten bodies of the powers of a bodhisattva were fully developed.
Ten thousand gateways to the knowledge of bodhisattvas entered him;
ten thousand methods of the perfection of wisdom were born within him;
and ten thousand visions of Buddhas from the ten directions became manifest before him.
He had also brought forth ten thousand bodhisattva vows. Endowed with such qualities, he traversed ten thousand Buddha-fields in the ten directions in every single moment of thought.
And in each world-system, in every moment of thought, he recollected ten thousand Buddhas from the past to the future.

And of those Tathāgatas, ten thousand oceans of Buddha-emanations, extending throughout the ten directions, were perceived; in every moment of thought, he saw all sentient beings included within ten thousand Buddha-fields,
passing away and being reborn according to their various modes of existence.

He entered into the passing away and rebirth of those beings— whether they were being born low or exalted, in happy or miserable states, beautiful or ugly, and wherever they went according to their desire. He also entered into their mental transformations, mental conducts, the uninterrupted flow of their thoughts, the diversity of their inclinations, the oceans of their faculties, the range of their applications, the termination of their karma, and the timing for their maturation and discipline.
[They] were.

Furthermore, noble son, that prince Vijitāvin, having passed away from there, was reborn in that very same royal family in the capital city Ratnavyūhā in Jambudvīpa, and he attained the sovereignty of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*). Having become a universal monarch, immediately after the parinirvāṇa of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganameghapradīparāja, [he encountered] Dharmagaganābhyudgataśrīrāja...
The Tathāgata named [Śakra] was pleased.
Immediately thereafter, at that very seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), having become Śakra, the lord of gods, he pleased the Tathāgata named Devendragarbha.
Immediately thereafter, in that same world-system, having become Suyāma, the king of gods, he pleased the Tathāgata named Dharaṇīśrīparvatatejas.
Immediately after that, in that very same world-system, having become the king of the gods in the Tuṣita heaven, he pleased the Tathāgata named Dharmacakraprabhanirghoṣarāja.
Immediately after that, in that very same world-system, having become the king of the gods in the Sunirmita heaven, he pleased the Tathāgata named Gaganakāntarāja.
Immediately after that, in that very same world-system, having become the king of the gods in the Vaśavartin heaven, he pleased the Tathāgata named Anavamardabalaketu.
Immediately after that, in that very same world-system, having become the lord of the asuras, he propitiated the Tathāgata named Sarvadharmanigarjitarāja.
Immediately after that, in that very same world-system, having become the lord of the Brahmās, he propitiated the Tathāgata named Dharmacakranirmāṇasamantapratibhāsanirghoṣa.
Thus, noble son, with these Tathāgatas as the foremost, ten thousand Buddhas appeared in that very world-system called Ratnaprabhā during that very eon called Suprabha.
And all those Tathāgatas were pleased by the prince Vijitāvin.
Furthermore, noble son, immediately after that great eon called Suprabha, there was an eon named Suraśmi.
And in that Suraśmi eon, ten thousand Buddhas appeared.
And in that kalpa, I was a king named Mahāmati.
While I was a king, I pleased the Tathāgata named Lakṣaṇaśrīparvata. Immediately thereafter, in that same kalpa, while I was a householder, I pleased the Tathāgata named Saṃvṛtaskandha.
Immediately after that, in that very same eon, while he was a minister, he pleased the Tathāgata named Vimalavatsa.
Immediately after that, in that very same eon, while he was the lord of the asuras, he pleased the Tathāgata named Veśadhārī.
Immediately after that, in that very same eon, while he was a tree deity, he pleased the Tathāgata named Lakṣaṇasumeru.
Immediately after that, in that very same kalpa, having been a caravan leader (sārthavāha), he pleased the Tathāgata named Vimalabāhu.
Immediately after that, in that very same kalpa, having been a city deity (nagaradevatā), he pleased the Tathāgata named Siṃhavikrāntagāmī.
Immediately after that, in that very same kalpa, having been Vaiśravaṇa, he pleased the Tathāgata named Devendracūḍa.
Immediately after that, in that very same eon, having become a king of the gandharvas, he pleased the Tathāgata named Dharmodgatakīrti.
Immediately after that, in that very same eon, having become a lord of the kumbhāṇḍas, he pleased the Tathāgata named Avabhāsamakuṭī.
"In this way, noble son, having taken these ten Tathāgatas as my leaders, I propitiated sixty koṭis of Buddhas in that world-system called Suraśmi.

I honored all those Tathāgatas with various bodies of rebirth. And as I approached each individual Tathāgata, a boundless and limitless realm of sentient beings was ripened for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
And as she approached each Tathāgata, she attained various gateways of samādhi,
various gateways of dhāraṇī, various methods of accomplishment, various methods of accomplishing the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), various ways of following the method of omniscience,
various methods of attaining the gateways of the light of the Dharma, various investigations following the methods of knowledge, and illuminations for entering the oceans of directions.

I have attained illuminations that enter into and descend upon oceans of various buddha-fields; I have attained illuminations that manifest oceans of visions of various Tathāgatas; they have entered, become purified, increased, spread forth, and extended.
And just as the Tathāgatas were propitiated there in the world-system Surasmi, so too [have they been propitiated here].
Likewise, throughout all eons as numerous as the atoms in oceans of world-systems, whatever Tathāgatas have appeared, and whatever Tathāgatas have come from other world-systems to teach the Dharma—
I have heard the teaching of the Dharma from all those Tathāgatas.
Having heard them, I retained them; I have pleased and satisfied all those Tathāgatas,
and I have upheld the teaching of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

And from the presence of all those Tathāgatas, I obtained this bodhisattva liberation called "The Source of the Roots of Goodness Arising from the Exhortation According to the Intentions for the Maturation of All Sentient Beings," through various methods of attainment and various gateways to the method of liberation.
Then, at that time, the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, illuminating and demonstrating this method of liberation, addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana in verses:
"You ask me indeed about this supreme, inconceivable liberation which you have fully absorbed; listen to all of it from me exactly as it is, as I explain it through the power of the Sugata. (12)
Having transcended all infinite, vast, and inconceivable eons, as well as incomparable and innumerable oceans of buddha-fields,
there was indeed a delightful world-system called Ratnaprabhā.
In that [eon] there was an eon named Suprabha, the source of immeasurable Victors;
indeed, those Lords of Sages were propitiated by me while I was cultivating this liberation.
In that [city] was the vast and wondrous capital named Rativyūha;
for at that time, the beings there were of pure mind, though their applications were uneven. (15)
In this [world], there was a king named Jayaprabha, who governed those beings with righteousness;
his son was named Vijitāvin, who was pleasing to behold, his limbs adorned with the primary marks.
Seeing those thousands of offenders who had been released for execution by that king at that time, the prince, overcome with compassion, entreated the king for their release. (17)
Having heard this, the king then summoned his assembly of ministers and told them everything; they all bowed down to him and said, "O King, this plot was devised for the purpose of killing you. (18)
Persuaded by them, the king then ordered that son to be executed;
yet that prince, with an undaunted countenance and indifferent to his own death, did not abandon those who were condemned to die.
Then, having heard that he had been released at his word, his mother, together with the ladies of the inner apartments, approached the king in distress and entreated him:
"O King, release the prince for half a month, so that he may bestow all manner of gifts throughout the world. (20)
Having been granted permission by that king, he bestowed appropriate gifts;
for half a month, day and night, he gave to those who had arrived from all directions.
Whatever any heretic desired for his own slaughter, he would grant him;
then, letting out cries of distress, the entire populace emerged from the capital city.

At that time, the Sugata—the King who is the Lamp for the Sky of the Sound of the True Dharma—standing beneath the Bodhi tree, perceiving that the faculties of the world had ripened, went out of compassion to that sacrificial enclosure. (23)
Having approached that assembly, the Sugata, through the miraculous manifestation of the array of the Tathāgata, spoke the *Dharmapradīpāmbudadharmaghoṣa*, the king of sūtras. (24)
Having disciplined the multitude that is without end or middle, he then prophesied their supreme enlightenment;
having set out for the excellent and foremost enlightenment, that son of a king was indeed victorious and exultant.
Having pleased the Buddha and performed extensive worship for him, he spoke joyfully:
"May I become an island, a guide for the worlds, a protection, a refuge, and a final resort. (26)
Seeking the path to perfect enlightenment, he went forth into homelessness in the presence of that sage;
thoroughly examining the intrinsic nature of phenomena, he remained there for hundreds of eons practicing his discipline.

Feeling compassion for the entire multitude of beings who have fallen into the state of an ocean of suffering and are without a protector, and having cultivated the path to perfect enlightenment, he then attains this liberation. (28)
Having pleased all those Sugatas who appeared in that eon with a serene mind,
he made magnificent offerings to them and upheld the Wheel of Dharma.
Thereafter, in the great oceans of eons as numerous as the atoms within oceans of buddha-fields,
he fully honored and pleased all those Victors who were then appearing.
I was he who bore the name Vijitāvin; seeing men held in the bonds of prison, I cast off my body for their liberation, and thus indeed did I attain liberation at that time. (31)

That which was cultivated throughout great oceans of eons, as numerous as the atoms within oceans of buddha-fields, and which was increased at every moment by these infinite, centerless, and incomparable methods; (32)
I have seen some of those lords of sages, and that which was attained by me has been fully realized;
this liberation of mine has been demonstrated to me through various successive paths.
For many millions of eons, I have trained myself in their inconceivable reality of liberation;
established therein, I drink in simultaneously the clouds of the true Dharma released by the Victors.

Pervading all fields in every direction with their bodies without attachment, they enter, moment by moment, the inconceivable lineages designated as the three times within the paths of those fields. (35)
They stand facing each individual ocean of the threefold world-system in its entirety;
and they manifest their own clouds of bodies as reflections within the Victors. (36)
Wandering through all directions, they shine forth before all the Tathāgatas;
raining down the entirety of the magnificent arrays, they perform worship for the Victors. (37)
Furthermore, they ask questions numbering as many as the oceans of Buddhas—questions that are vast and infinite;
and they also sustain the immeasurable clouds of Dharma of the Victors as they pour down their rain.
They go into the range of vision in all directions, without exception, within the circles of the Jinas,
seated upon various forms of thrones and displaying manifold transformations. (39)
With thousands of physical forms of infinite colors, they pervade all directions;
they manifest forms that are without end or middle, yet they appear as a single unified mass.
From each and every pore, they emit incalculable great oceans of light rays;
by means of various skillful methods, they pacify the burning fire of the afflictions for all living beings.
Abiding there, they emit from each and every pore clouds of emanation-bodies;
having pervaded all directions with those wonders, they discipline sentient beings with rains of the water of Dharma. 42.

This entrance into the method is of inconceivable form; it is the common refuge of all the sons of the Victors, relying upon which they practice their conduct in all realms throughout kalpas as limitless as the future. (43)

Proclaiming the Dharma according to their inclinations, they cause beings to turn away from the net of false views; having established them in heaven and liberation, they reveal the stage of omniscience. 44.

In all worldly births, through inconceivable and infinitely variegated physical forms, they proclaim the Dharma according to the inclinations of beings, appearing in the likeness of every sentient being. (45)

Having attained this peaceful liberation, you are undaunted by these and other immeasurable oceans of realms, which are inconceivable and as subtle as atoms, and by the great oceans of their descriptions. (46)
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "the source of roots of goodness arising from the exhortation according to the inclinations for the ripening of all sentient beings.
How could I possibly [know] those bodhisattvas who have transcended all worldly destinies, who have attained the manifestation of births in all worlds,
who are engaged in shattering the mountain of obstructions to omniscient gnosis, and who have penetrated the characteristics of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena?

To know the conduct of those who are dedicated to dispelling the darkness of all afflictive obscurations; who possess roots of goodness skilled in accomplishing the discernment of all phenomena; who have direct realization of the knowledge of the selflessness of phenomena; who never cease their efforts in ripening and disciplining all sentient beings; who have thoroughly penetrated the principle of the non-dual realm of phenomena; and whose intellects have extended into the oceans of all methods of verbal expression; or to enter into the oceans of their virtues.

To fully comprehend the power of knowledge, or to discern the state of contemplation, or to attain mastery over meditative concentration, or to understand the miraculous transformations of liberation.
Go, noble son;

right here in Jambudvīpa, in the Lumbinī grove, there dwells a deity of the Lumbinī grove named Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī. Approach her and ask: "How are Bodhisattvas born into the family of the Tathāgatas?"
How do they become bringers of light for the worlds?
How is it that, practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout eons reaching to the furthest limit of the future, they do not become weary?
Then, Sudhana, the merchant’s son, [approached] the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.

Having bowed his head at her feet, circumambulated the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā hundreds of thousands of times, and having paid homage and prostrated, he departed from the presence of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā while gazing at her with palms joined in reverence. // 39 //
(42) Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, recollecting that instruction from the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā, [proceeded].
Cultivating and expanding that bodhisattva liberation— the arising of roots of goodness through the exhortation according to the inclinations for the ripening of all sentient beings—
he proceeded by stages toward the Lumbinī grove.
Having arrived at the Lumbinī grove and circumambulated it, he searched for the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī.

He saw the goddess of Lumbinī in the groves of Lumbinī, possessing the splendor of delight in a circle of radiant light, seated upon a lion throne with a core of jewel-lotuses within a gabled pavilion formed by the branches of trees made of every kind of jewel; surrounded and honored by twenty hundred thousand nayutas of forest goddesses,
she was teaching the Dharma, a sūtra called "The Exposition of the Ocean of Births of All Bodhisattvas."

Seeing her thus proclaiming [the Dharma] to those bodhisattvas born into the lineage of the Tathāgatas, increasing the force of the ocean of their virtues, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, approached her.

Having approached, she bowed her head at the feet of Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, and standing before her with palms joined, she spoke thus: "O Goddess, by me [the vow] for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment..."
The thought of enlightenment has been generated; yet I do not know how Bodhisattvas are born into the family of the Tathāgatas,
and how, while practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva, they become bringers of light to sentient beings.
When this had been said, the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana:
"Noble son, there are these ten births of bodhisattvas, endowed with which bodhisattvas are born into the families of the Tathāgatas;
having emerged, the bodhisattvas increase through the skillful means of the bodhisattvas."

They do not stand aloof, they do not despair, they do not turn back, they do not become lax, they do not grow weary, they do not sink down, they do not become deluded, they do not shrink back, they do not tremble, and they do not fail to follow the pursuit of the direction of omniscience;
they keep in mind the principle of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
They become matured for the awakening of a Buddha;
they expand the production of the thought of awakening;
and they increase in all the perfections.
They turn away from all worldly destinies;
they converge upon the stage of the Tathāgata;
and they bring to maturity their wisdom and superknowledges.
They become manifest in the Buddha-dharmas;
they come to possess a realized understanding within the domain of omniscience.
What are these ten?
Namely: the first birth of a bodhisattva is called "The Womb of the Application of the Vow to Attend upon All Buddhas";
the second birth of a bodhisattva is called "The Womb of the Arising of the Perfection of the Limbs of the Thought of Enlightenment";
the third birth of a bodhisattva is called "The Womb of the Arising of the Orientation toward the Application of Penetrative Contemplation on the Methods of the Dharma."
The fourth birth of a bodhisattva is named the Womb of Purity of Superior Intention Regarding the Three Worlds;
the fifth birth of a bodhisattva is named the Womb of the Radiance of Universal Illumination;
the sixth birth of a bodhisattva is named the Womb of the Arising of the Lineage and Family of All Tathāgatas.
The seventh birth of a bodhisattva is named the Womb of the Ornament of the Illumination of the Radiance of the Buddha’s Powers;
the eighth birth of a bodhisattva is named the Womb of the Arising of the Perfection of the Investigation of the Gates of Universal Knowledge;
the ninth birth of a bodhisattva is named the Womb of the Array of Emanations of the Dharma Realm.
The tenth birth of a bodhisattva is named "The Matrix of the Impetus for Advancing to the Stage of a Tathāgata."
In this regard, noble son, what is the first birth of a bodhisattva called "The Womb of the Application and Vow for Attending upon All Buddhas"?

Here, noble son, from the very beginning, a bodhisattva is dedicated to attending upon the Buddhas; honoring, revering, respecting, worshiping, serving, pleasing, and never displeaseing all the Blessed Buddhas, he remains insatiable in beholding the Tathāgatas.
With a mind intensified by the surge of joy toward the Buddha resulting from his application of honor to the Buddhas, and having given rise to the surge of serene faith from beholding the Tathāgata,
he accumulates merit with irreversible faith; remaining insatiable, he is devoted to gathering the equipment for the worship of all Tathāgatas, his application never slackening.

Noble son, this first birth of a bodhisattva, named "The Womb of the Application of Vows for the Worship and Service of All Buddhas," leads to the gathering and accumulation of the roots of goodness that constitute the equipment for omniscience.
In this regard, noble son, what is the second birth of a bodhisattva called "The Womb of the Arising of the Perfection of the Limbs of the Mind of Enlightenment"?
Here, noble son, a bodhisattva generates the mind for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
that is to say, the mind of great compassion for the sake of protecting all sentient beings.
The mind that delights in all Buddhas for the sake of their ultimate gratification; the mind that seeks all Buddha-dharmas for the sake of being indifferent toward all material things;
and the mind of the great departure for the sake of facing toward omniscience.
The mind of great loving-kindness is for the sake of the pervasive application of gathering all the world;
the mind that does not abandon any being is for the sake of the firmness of the armor of omniscience;
the mind free from deceit and guile is for the sake of attaining the illumination of knowledge as it truly is.
The mind that acts according to its words, for the sake of practicing the path of the bodhisattva;
the mind that does not deceive all Buddhas, for the sake of maintaining the vows of all Tathāgatas;
and the mind of the great vow for omniscience, for the sake of never ceasing the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings until the furthest limit of time.

With these as the foremost among the accumulations for the limbs of the thought of awakening, which are as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, that bodhisattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas.
Noble son, this is the second birth of a bodhisattva, called "the womb of the arising of the perfection of the limbs of the thought of awakening."
In this regard, noble son, what is the third birth of a bodhisattva, called "the womb of the manifestation facing the guidance of the application of contemplation on the methods of the Dharma"?

Here, noble son, a bodhisattva has a mind directed toward the contemplation of the arising of all methods of the Dharma; a mind transformed by being oriented toward fulfilling the aspects of the path to omniscience;
a mind characterized by the intention for the practice of irreproachable actions; and a mind directed toward the purification of the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhi-methods.

His mind is perfected in the practice of all the qualities of a bodhisattva; his mind brings forth the array of all the factors of the bodhisattva path; his mind possesses unflagging vigor, like a blazing conflagration at the end of an eon, arising from the vast objective support of omniscience; his mind brings forth the bodhisattva conduct that is without end or middle, proceeding toward the ripening and disciplining of the entire world;
and his mind enters into the manifestation and realization of all things through the perfection of the qualities of a bodhisattva who is well-established in all modes of conduct and training.
Noble son, this is the third birth of a bodhisattva, called "The Womb of Manifest Arising through the Yoga of the Direct Vision of the Method of Dharma."
In this regard, noble son, what is the fourth birth of a bodhisattva, called "the womb of the purification of the resolute intention regarding the worlds of the three times"?
Here, noble son, a bodhisattva becomes completely pure in the realm of resolute intention;
he attains illumination regarding the awakening of the Buddhas.
He has entered the oceans of the bodhisattva methods;
he becomes the essence, his mind sustained by the vajra-realm of firm resolute intention;
and he turns away from all rebirths within the realms of existence.
He becomes oriented toward the accomplishment of the miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas;
he attains the state of one who proceeds with distinction for the sake of increasing the sharpness of the bodhisattva faculties;
and he possesses a virtuous mind for the sake of the luminosity of his resolute intention.
He becomes immovable for the sake of increasing his firm and great vows;
he is attended by all the Tathāgatas for the sake of shattering the mountains of all obscurations;
and he becomes a refuge, the sustainer of the entire world.
Noble son, this is the fourth birth of Bodhisattvas, called "The Womb of the Purification of the Resolute Intent toward the Worlds of the Three Times."
In this regard, noble son, what is the fifth birth of the bodhisattvas, called "The Womb of Light Pervading All Directions"?
Here, noble son, a bodhisattva is perfected in application and is dedicated to the ripening and disciplining of the entire world.
He becomes one whose perception of all things has been shaken loose, being liberated in renunciation;
he becomes utterly pure, possessing infinite ethical discipline, and dwelling within the domain of the Tathāgata;
he becomes perfected in patience, having attained the illumination of patience regarding all the qualities of a Buddha.
He becomes one of great heroism, having set out upon a sublime path of deliverance in every respect;
he becomes liberated through meditative concentration, purified by the mandala of the knowledge of universal gateways of samādhi;
and he becomes one whose splendor is the vigor of wisdom, having attained the illumination of all phenomena.
He possesses the unattached eye, having entered into the ocean-like cognition of beholding the Buddhas;
he is empowered by mastery over the reality of all phenomena, having brought satisfaction to the entire world;
and he is well-engaged in the attainment of the methods of the Dharma exactly as they are.
Noble son, this is the fifth birth of the bodhisattvas, called the Womb of Light Pervading All Directions.
In this regard, noble son, what is the sixth birth of bodhisattvas, called "the womb arising from the lineage and family of all Tathāgatas"?

Here, noble son, a bodhisattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas, is reborn as one following in their footsteps, and becomes perfected within the gates of the methods of all the Buddha-dharmas.
He becomes purified in regard to the great vows of the Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present;
he becomes a single mass of roots of goodness among all the roots of goodness of the Tathāgatas;
and he becomes one body with all Buddhas.
By means of supramundane white dharmas,
he dwells in the dharma of the Great Self within the samādhi that perceives the Buddha’s empowerment;
he practices the dharma of the purification of sentient beings according to the proper time.
He possesses unceasing eloquence in inquiries concerning the Buddha-dharma.
Noble son, this is the sixth birth of bodhisattvas, called "the womb arising from the lineage and family of all Tathāgatas."
In this regard, noble son, what is the seventh birth of bodhisattvas called "The Womb of the Ornament of the Illumination of the Light of the Tathāgata’s Powers"?
Here, noble son, a bodhisattva does not turn back from the illumination of entering the powers of the Buddhas as they travel to Buddha-fields;
nor do they retreat from attending upon the ocean of the various qualities of bodhisattvas.
He is not terrified by means of the knowledge of all phenomena as they truly are, being like an illusion; he penetrates the entire world as resembling a dream;
and he brings forth the basis for the perception of all forms as resembling a reflection.
He attains mastery over the miraculous transformations of supernormal knowledge, which are like magical emanations;
he displays his face in all births within the realms of existence, which are like reflections;
and he understands that the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas are like echoes.
He attains the supreme perfection of the teaching on the method of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), being devoted to the teaching of various methods and means for diverse purposes.
Noble son, this is the seventh birth of bodhisattvas, called "The Matrix of the Ornament of Light from the Illumination of the Powers of the Tathāgata."
In this regard, noble son, what is the eighth birth of a bodhisattva, called "The Matrix of the Arising of the Perfection of the Investigation into the Gateways of Universal Gnosis"?

Here, noble son, a bodhisattva, while still in the state of a youth (*kumārabhūta*), becomes established in the station of a bodhisattva; abiding therein, he investigates the method of the gnosis of omniscience.
In each and every gateway of the method of knowledge, immeasurable eons would pass away even as he describes the immeasurable sphere of activity of the bodhisattvas;
he becomes master of all the samādhis of the bodhisattvas, having attained the supreme perfection;
and in every moment of mind, at every moment of consciousness, he is reborn at the feet of the Tathāgatas residing in inexpressible numbers of Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
With undifferentiated objects of focus, he enters undifferentiated meditative absorptions;
and within undifferentiated phenomena, he demonstrates mastery over undifferentiated knowledge.
Furthermore, with infinite objects of focus, he enters the realm that is without objects of focus.
Through limited objects of focus, he enters the stage of infinite exposition;
he penetrates the immeasurable nature of phenomena, whether limited or vast;
and he enters into the entire world as being identical to representation-only.
Through cultivation, he follows all objective referents of phenomena and all paths of cognition.
Noble son, this is the eighth birth of bodhisattvas, named "The Source of the Perfection of the Investigation into the Gateways of Universal Gnosis."
In this regard, noble son, what is the birth of bodhisattvas called "the womb of the array of emanations of the realm of phenomena"?
Here, noble son, in every moment of thought, a bodhisattva sustains various arrays of buddha-fields;
furthermore, he has attained the supreme perfection of fearlessness in the emanation of sentient beings.
He attains skill in the emanations of the Buddhas;
he becomes purified by the fearlessnesses regarding the emanations of the Dharma;
and his sphere of activity becomes the excellent, unattached realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
He is skilled in the empowerment of all bodily communications according to the inclinations [of beings]; he has attained skill in the inconceivable discipline of sentient beings;
and he is one who demonstrates various modes of conduct and perfect awakenings.
He becomes skilled in accomplishing the path to unobstructed omniscience;
immediately thereafter, he demonstrates skill in setting the wheel of Dharma in motion;
and he becomes skilled in accomplishing infinite and boundless means for training sentient beings.
And when the time has come for the discipline of sentient beings, he remains ever-composed, being the treasury of the womb of Vairocana’s wisdom.
Noble son, this is the ninth birth of bodhisattvas, called the "Womb of the Array of Emanations of the Dharmadhātu."
In this regard, noble son, what is the tenth birth of a bodhisattva called "The Matrix of the Impetus for Advancing to the Stage of a Tathāgata"?
Here, noble son, a bodhisattva becomes solitary within the sphere of the oneness of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times,
and he enters the sphere of the uninterrupted continuity of all world-systems.
He knows the uninterrupted arising of the minds of all sentient beings throughout their deaths and rebirths in the past and future limits;
he understands the domain of the uninterrupted knowledge of the conduct of all bodhisattvas;
and he understands the uninterrupted sequence of the perfect awakenings of all buddhas of the past, future, and present.
He understands the uninterrupted continuity of skillful means that benefits all phenomena.
He understands the uninterrupted continuity of all eons—whether in the process of dissolution or evolution, whether past, future, or present—including their names and their detailed instructions.

Furthermore, he brings forth the knowledge that empowers the manifestation of the array of perfect awakening for beings who have been ripened according to their capacity and for whom the time has arrived.

Furthermore, he demonstrates the uninterrupted skillful method for bringing about the manifestation of perfect enlightenment and the turning of the wheel of Dharma during the arising of all Buddhas; through his skill in accomplishing the means for disciplining infinite realms of sentient beings—this, noble son, is the tenth birth of Bodhisattvas, named "The Matrix of the Impetus for Treading upon the Ground of the Tathāgatas."
Noble son, these are the ten births of bodhisattvas, in which bodhisattvas are born, take birth, gather [merit], grow, fulfill, arise, fully arise, and reach perfection;
they abide in the practice of the adornment of a single array for the sake of awakening to all buddha-fields without exception.
They maintain their empowerment throughout kalpas reaching to the furthest limit of the future in order never to slacken their commitment to the way of the realm of sentient beings.

They fully awaken to the stream of the infinite succession of teachings—the various, manifold, and diverse successions of instructions based on the ocean of all phenomena and their many objects of focus.
They manifest the inconceivable bull-like sovereignty of a Buddha, which extends to the very limits of the realm of phenomena and the ultimate realm of space.

They manifest the turning of the wheel of Dharma within oceans of the diverse conducts of immeasurable sentient beings, which are comprised of their ripening and discipline; they sustain all world-systems so that they are never devoid of the arising of Buddhas; and they make known the purity of the ocean of inexpressible vocal qualities of all clouds of Dharma as they proceed toward all objects of perception.
Having attained unobstructed mastery in their dwelling within the immeasurable, they manifest circles of Bodhisattvas adorned with the beautiful arrays of all phenomena.

To sentient beings according to their inclinations and aspirations, they proclaim the infinite and middleless treasury of Dharma for the sake of perfecting all worlds through their conformity to the immeasurable stage of Buddhahood.
Then, at that time, the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, illuminating this very purpose of the Bodhisattva’s birth,
surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s empowerment and addressed the merchant’s son Sudhana in verses:
“Those who, with a pure and untroubled high resolve, behold the Jina, never become satiated.”
Established in their first birth, those of excellent wisdom make aspirations for the clouds of arrays at the limit of the future of all the Victors. // 1 //

Having pervaded the entire world throughout all three times without exception—every field, every phenomenon, and likewise every Buddha—the second birth of those inconceivable ones is said to be the mind adorned with the vow to liberate sentient beings. // 2 //
Those who drink from the Cloud of Dharma are never satiated; their minds are resolved in certainty, and their bodies are unimpeded throughout the three times.
With bodies as pure as the realm of space and with equanimous minds, this is indeed their third incomparable birth. // 3 //

Those bulls among men who descend into the ocean of great compassion with resolute intentions as firm as the essence of a diamond and like Mount Sumeru, expanding the vast ocean of the method of omniscience—for them, this is the fourth birth in this world. 4.

Those who, having pervaded the world in the ten directions with loving-kindness, bring forth oceans of stainless perfections, and ripen beings with the radiance of the Dharma—this is the fifth birth of those Great Beings. 5.

Having penetrated the intrinsic nature of phenomena, with unattached minds, they are born into the peerless Buddha-family of the three times; those who descend into the ocean of the principles of the realm of phenomena—this is the vast sixth birth of those wise ones. // 6 //

Those whose dharma-bodies are utterly pure and whose minds are unattached, who pervade all buddha-fields without exception with their own bodies, and who have entered into the realization of the entirety of the powers of a Buddha— this is the seventh inconceivable birth of the Buddhas. (Gv 290) 7.
Those who have attained mastery in the method of the ocean of knowledge investigate the gateway to the method of omniscience;
they enter the entire ocean of the method of meditative concentration—this is considered the eighth birth for those who take their refuge in suchness. // 8 //

Those who purify the vast expanse of the field of Dharma, those who are dedicated to the ripening of all sentient beings, and who display the magnificent array of Buddha-miracles—this is the ninth birth of those great-souled ones. 9.

Those sons of the Victors who have entered according to their strength into the Victors, increasing the vast momentum toward omniscience, and who are unimpeded in the methods for penetrating the depths of the realm of phenomena— for them, this is the tenth birth.
"Noble son, by means of these ten births, a bodhisattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas and thus becomes a bringer of light for all sentient beings.

Moreover, noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called ‘The Manifestation of the Miraculous Transformations of the Births of Bodhisattvas in All Objects Throughout Immeasurable Kalpas.

He asked: ‘Goddess, what is the scope of this bodhisattva liberation called “The Manifestation of the Miraculous Transformations of the Births of Bodhisattvas in All Objects Throughout Immeasurable Kalpas”?’"
She said: "Noble son, I am perfected in the vow to manifest and approach the births of all bodhisattvas.
Indeed, noble son, I enter the vast ocean of the birth of the Blessed One Vairocana;
that is to say, I enter the birth of the bodhisattva within this blessed three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system."
I was born here in this Jambudvīpa of the four continents, in the Lumbinī grove, through the fulfillment of my former vows, at the time when the birth of the Bodhisattva was being manifested.
While I have been dwelling here cultivating the recollection of the Bodhisattva’s birth,
after a hundred years had passed while I remained here, the Blessed One was about to descend from the Tuṣita heaven.
Then, in this Lumbinī grove, ten portents appeared.
What are the ten?
Namely: this entire Lumbinī grove became level, free from depressions, elevations, and unevenness, and devoid of chasms and precipices.
This first omen appeared.
Furthermore, this entire Lumbinī grove became free of pebbles and gravel, cleared of stumps and thorns, its ground leveled like a diamond-hard surface, and it stood strewn with many jewels.
This second omen appeared.
Furthermore, this entire Lumbinī grove became beautifully adorned with rows of *śāla* and *tāla* trees made of every kind of jewel;
this third prior sign appeared.
Furthermore, this entire Lumbinī grove sprouted with shoots of divine fragrance surpassing [all others], produced from caskets of every kind of aromatic powder.
A canopy formed by a mass of clouds of every kind of banner was established as an ornament at the foot of the tree, which was adorned with figures of fragrant jewel-bodies;
this fourth preliminary sign appeared.
Furthermore, this entire Lumbinī grove became filled with every kind of ornament, produced from treasuries of various divine flowers, garlands, and jewelry; it remained thus perfectly arrayed.
This fifth omen appeared.
Furthermore, in this entire Lumbinī grove, great treasuries of precious jewels manifested within every tree.
This sixth omen appeared.
Furthermore, in this entire Lumbinī grove, all the water-born jewel-lotuses in every lotus pond sprouted buds, emerged from the surface of the earth, and remained floating upon the water;
this seventh preliminary sign appeared.

Moreover, as many as there were sons of the gods belonging to the desire realm and the form realm in this world-system—whether they be nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, or lords of the world and lords of beings—[all came together].
They too all stood in this Lumbinī grove with their palms joined in reverence;
this was the eighth preliminary sign that appeared.

Furthermore, as many as there were daughters of the gods, daughters of the nāgas, or daughters of the yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas here in this world-system of four continents—
With all their minds full of joy, holding in their hands all the implements for worship, they stood with bodies bowed toward the branch of the *plakṣa* tree.
This ninth prior sign appeared.
Furthermore, from the circles of the navels of all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions, there issued forth the "Lamps of the Miraculous Display of the Birth of Bodhisattvas."
Rays of light issued forth and, having illuminated this entire Lumbinī grove, they remained there.
Within all those circles of the faces of the rays, the miraculous manifestations of the births of all those Tathāgatas were seen as reflected images.
Furthermore, the miraculous qualities of all Bodhisattvas arising from birth, accompanied by the voice of the Buddha, were heard as they issued forth from those circles of the faces of the rays.
This tenth preliminary sign appeared.

When the time for the Bodhisattva’s birth was at hand, these ten preliminary signs manifested; through their appearance, a thought arose among all the lords of the world that the Bodhisattva would be born.
Furthermore, noble son, from seeing these ten preliminary signs, I indeed obtained an inconceivable surge of joy.
Furthermore, noble son, as Queen Māyā was departing from the great city of Kapilavastu for this Lumbinī grove, ten great signs of illumination appeared as portents.
Through their appearance, the surge of joy in the light of the Dharma of omniscience increased for immeasurable beings.
What are these ten?
That is to say: a radiance appeared within the interiors of all the jeweled gabled palaces situated upon the surface of the earth;
a radiance appeared within all the buds of fragrant flowers;
and as all the jeweled lotuses without exception began to blossom, a radiance appeared from every one of their petals.
And from them there issued forth a sweet sound, well-produced and natural;
and that radiance of the first production of the thought of enlightenment by the Bodhisattvas in the ten directions, having illuminated this Lumbinī grove, rose up.
And whatever manifestation of miraculous power, consisting of the illumination of the Bodhisattvas’ progression through all the Bodhisattva stages throughout the ten directions,
appeared here in this Lumbinī grove;
and whatever light-illumination of the knowledge attained from the perfect fulfillment of all the perfections by the Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions [appeared here].
He appeared here in this Lumbinī grove;
and that illumination of the light of knowledge, which consists of the mastery over all vows of the bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions,
appeared here in this Lumbinī grove.
And that illumination of the light of knowledge for the ripening and disciplining of all bodhisattvas in the ten directions appeared here in this Lumbinī grove;
and that illumination of the light of knowledge for the realization of the principles of the dharma-realm of all bodhisattvas in the ten directions [appeared here].
He manifested here in this Lumbinī grove;

and that illumination of the light of the wisdom attained through the manifestation of the Buddha’s miraculous power, his birth, his renunciation, and his awakening to enlightenment for all bodhisattvas in the ten directions,
manifested here in this Lumbinī grove.
These ten signs of great illumination appeared,
by which the dense darkness of the mental dispositions of the boundless and centerless Bodhisattvas was illuminated.

There, noble son, when Queen Māyā had gone to her dwelling at the Plakṣa tree, all the lords of the world and all the sons of the gods belonging to the realm of desire, accompanied by their retinues of throngs of apsarases and celestial maidens, assembled there.

And by the splendor, majesty, complexion, and form of Queen Māyā, all the arrays of offerings and the bodies of all the sons of the gods of the realm of form who were free from the scent of impurity, as well as all the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas who had assembled with their retinues and were engaged in worshipping the Bodhisattva, were illuminated.
And whatever lights there were in this trichiliocosm, they were all eclipsed and surpassed;
moreover, the radiant splendors emitted from every pore of Queen Māyā remained unassailed by any other lights.

Unobstructed, unutterable, and unattached, they pervaded all directions; having pacified all the sufferings of those in the hells, all the sufferings of those in the animal realm, all the sufferings of those in the world of Yama, and all the sufferings and afflictions of all beings included within the states of existence, they remained, shone, blazed, and radiated light.
This, noble son, was the Bodhisattva’s first miraculous manifestation at birth in the Lumbinī grove.
Furthermore, noble son, at the time when this entire great trichiliocosm was contained within the womb of Queen Māyā and appeared as a reflection,

within that great trichiliocosm— in all the Jambudvīpas of hundreds of millions of four-continent world-systems, in royal capitals of various names, in groves of various names, and at the roots of various trees— [the Bodhisattva appeared].

Queen Māyā appeared in this very way, surrounded by all the lords of the world, standing ready for the birth of the Bodhisattva through the inconceivable miraculous power of the knowledge of the Bodhisattva’s mother.
Noble son, this was the second miraculous manifestation of the Bodhisattva’s birth in the Lumbinī grove.

Furthermore, noble son, from every single pore of Queen Māyā, from each individual opening of her pores, all those Tathāgatas whom the Blessed One had previously pleased, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped while practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva were clearly visible.
And whatever Dharma had been taught by those Tathāgatas was heard in its entirety from all those pores of the skin, accompanied by the qualities of a Buddha’s voice;
just as, for example, [images appear] in a mass of water, in golden dust, in a particle of gold-dust, or in a clear mirror-surface.

Just as in perfectly clear water the expanse of the sky is seen, adorned with the sun, the moon, the stars, and the hosts of planets, appearing as if with the resonance of the thundering from deep masses of clouds—
even so, noble son, within all the pores of Queen Māyā’s body, the miraculous manifestations of former Tathāgatas were seen, along with the sounds of their teachings on all dharmas. Noble son,
this was the Bodhisattva’s third miraculous manifestation at birth in the Lumbinī grove.
Furthermore, noble son, from every part of Queen Māyā’s body, from all the circles of her pores, and from each and every single pore,

there appeared as many [emanations] as there are in all fields, as many as there are in all oceans of world-systems, as many as there are in all lineages of world-systems, and as many as there are in all those designated as world-systems, wherein the Blessed One had performed the conduct of a bodhisattva.

In whatever sacred sites, in whatever configurations, in whatever arrays, in whatever bodies, in whatever mountain ornaments, in whatever ornaments of villages, cities, market towns, provinces, and ports, in whatever ornaments of gardens, rivers, lakes, ponds, and oceans,
in whatever ornaments of clouds in the sky, in whatever abodes of sentient beings, in whatever descriptions of vehicles, and in whatever names and numbers of eons;

In the arising of Buddhas; in those who have reached the pinnacle of purity; among sentient beings according to the measure of their lifespans; in births and rebirths according to the light [of the world];
in encounters with sentient beings; in reliance upon spiritual friends; in the application to wholesome dharmas; and in the diligent practice of the Dharma.
As he practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva in the buddha-fields,
all those expansions of buddha-fields were seen emerging from every pore of Queen Māyā’s body;
and as many bodies as the Blessed One had previously assumed while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, having attained the stage of non-retrogression, [all were likewise seen].
In whatever forms, in whatever dwellings, with whatever enjoyments, and through whatever experiences of pleasure and pain, and throughout whatever cycles of birth—
all that was visible within each and every pore.
And in all those various rebirths, Queen Māyā was the mother of the Bodhisattva.
And all those assemblies of bodhisattvas were seen appearing as miraculous manifestations within the pores of the goddess Māyā.
Noble son, this was the fourth miraculous manifestation of birth of the Bodhisattva in the Lumbinī grove.

Furthermore, noble son, however many bodies the Blessed One assumed while formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva— whatever their color, whatever their shape, whatever their form, whatever their enjoyments, whatever their experiences of pleasure and pain, and whatever their cycles of birth—
all of these appeared as reflections within every pore of Queen Māyā’s body. Noble son, this was the fifth miraculous manifestation of the Bodhisattva in the Lumbinī grove.
Furthermore, noble son, as many difficult renunciations as were made by the Blessed One while formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva—
whether the renunciation of hands and feet, or the renunciation of ears and nose, or the renunciation of tongues and fangs, or the renunciation of eyes and the head,
or the renunciation of flesh and blood, or the renunciation of bones and marrow, or the renunciation of the chest and heart, or the renunciation of skin and hide—

Or the relinquishing of external and internal things; or the relinquishing of sons, daughters, and wives; or the relinquishing of one's own person; or the relinquishing of enjoyments and jewels; or the relinquishing of villages, towns, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and capitals; or the relinquishing of wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses;
or the relinquishing of gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, gold, and silver; or the relinquishing of various kinds of jeweled ornaments.
Whether it was the relinquishing of beds and seats, the relinquishing of houses and palaces, or the relinquishing of all objects of enjoyment,
they relinquished these in the forms of the bodies of donor bodhisattvas,
and they received them in the forms of the bodies of recipients.
And those regions and objects which were relinquished,
those specific locations,
and those retinues of bodhisattvas—
All of them were seen appearing from every pore of the goddess Māyā.
Noble son, this was the sixth miraculous manifestation of birth of the Bodhisattva in the Lumbinī grove.

Furthermore, noble son, [the Bodhisattva], having gathered in the grove of the Lumbinī forest, appeared as one whose wisdom is born of the noble world. Noble son, this was the seventh miraculous manifestation of birth of the Bodhisattva in the Lumbinī grove.

Furthermore, noble son, there are all the enjoyments of the bodhisattvas that surpass the arrays and enjoyments of the palaces of all the lords of the gods, and that surpass the arrays and enjoyments of the palaces of all the lords of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and humans— namely,
the enjoyment of gabled palaces made of the king of jewels, the enjoyment of celestial mansions made of the king of jewels, and the enjoyment of nets made of the king of jewels.
