Whether they were enjoyments of the forms of king of jewels, or enjoyments of the images of king of jewels, or arrays of king of jewels, or enjoyments of all kinds of ornaments, or enjoyments of all kinds of supreme perfumes, or enjoyments of all objects that were beautiful and not disagreeable— all these,
emerging from the womb of Queen Māyā without being confused with one another, came forth and settled here in the Lumbinī grove in a universal array.
Noble son, this was the eighth miraculous manifestation of birth of the Bodhisattva in the Lumbinī grove.

Furthermore, noble son, from the womb of Queen Māyā, first of all, there emerged Bodhisattvas equal in number to the atoms in ten hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of ineffable Buddha-fields, possessing forms, colors, and postures identical to those of the Blessed One Vairocana, and adorned with the primary marks and secondary signs identical to his.

Emanating from the Blessed One, there issued forth beings with identical radiance, emitting identical rays, possessing identical marks and gestures, having identical prowess, performing identical miraculous transformations of light, having identical retinues, and having identical arrays; they proclaimed the oceans of the Blessed One’s virtues.
Noble son, this was the ninth miraculous manifestation of birth of the Bodhisattva in the Lumbinī grove.

Furthermore, noble son, when the time for the Bodhisattva’s birth had arrived, from beneath the adamantine surface of the great earth, right before Queen Māyā, there emerged a great jewel-lotus named Sarvaratnavyūhagarbha. Its interior was composed of the king of great invincible vajra-jewels, and its filaments were an array of light-rays from all the kings of jewels.
It was beautifully arranged with rows of petals equal in number to the atoms within ten buddha-fields, and its circular arrangement of petals consisted of various kinds of jewel-kings.
Its pericarp was pure as the king of wish-fulfilling gems; it was arrayed with rows of immeasurable filaments in the colors of all jewels;

it was covered by a net of arrays of countless kings of jewel-gems; it was overspread by a peak made of the indestructible Indra-kūṭa of the king of diamond-jewels of Nārāyaṇa; it was surrounded by the bodies of all the lords of gods; it was showered upon by clouds of fragrance from all the lords of nāgas; and it was surrounded by all the lords of yakṣas who offered handfuls of divine flowers with their joined palms.

It was manifested by clouds of praise accompanied by the sweet sounds of songs arising from the places where all the Gandharva-lords and former Buddhas were born; it was saluted with bodies bowed down by all the Asura-lords whose pride, intoxication, and arrogance had been destroyed; it was gazed upon by all the Kinnara-lords with joyful minds as they offered clouds of sky-adornments consisting of jeweled ribbons suspended by all the Garuḍa-lords; and it was showered by clouds of magnificent arrays of beautiful melodies produced by the joy of all the Mahoraga-lords.
Noble son, this was the tenth miraculous manifestation of birth of the Bodhisattva in the Lumbinī grove.
"Noble son, in the Lumbinī grove, these ten miraculous manifestations of the Bodhisattva’s birth appeared.
Thereafter, the Bodhisattva— of inconceivable, immeasurable, and delightful splendor— emerged from the womb of Queen Māyā, like the solar disc from the expanse of the sky,
or like a flash of lightning from a mass of clouds."
Like a great cloud at twilight emerging from between the peaks of a mountain, or like a great lamp emerging from the darkness of night—

thus did the Bodhisattva manifest his emergence from the womb of Queen Māyā, by way of the nature of phenomena that manifests the cognition of forms as being illusory, by way of the nature of phenomena that has not yet come into being, and by way of the nature of phenomena that manifests the cognition of the world as being without arising or cessation.
In this way, noble son, while dwelling here in the Lumbinī grove, I penetrate the oceans of the miraculous displays of the birth of the Blessed One Vairocana.
And just as I, noble son, penetrate the oceans of the miraculous displays of the birth of the Blessed One Vairocana in this blessed four-continent world-system,

so too do I everywhere penetrate the miraculous displays of the birth of the Blessed One Vairocana in all the hundreds of millions of Jambudvīpas within every single four-continent world-system throughout the entire triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system.

And just as I, noble son, [perceive] in this triple-thousand great-thousand world-system, in all the four-continent systems, hundreds of millions of Jambudvīpas, a hundred million [emanations] of the Blessed Vairocana— so too, in every moment of thought, with each single entry of mind, I perceive within all the atoms contained in the entire triple-thousand great-thousand world-system, which follow the wisdom of entering all Buddha-fields as many as the atoms therein, hundreds of millions of Blessed Ones equal in number to the atoms of those Buddha-fields.
I penetrate the manifestations of the birth of Vairocana.

With a mind that follows immediately thereafter, I penetrate the manifestations of the births of Bodhisattvas who are equal to that Buddha in each and every one of the thousands of Buddha-fields contained within the atoms of those Buddha-fields;
by this method, [I penetrate them] within the atoms of all Buddha-fields.
In each and every buddha-field, I enter into all the births and miraculous transformations of bodhisattvas, yet I do not reach their limit.

Within all atoms of dust, in each and every atom of dust, there are successions of buddha-fields, yet I do not reach their limit; nor, within each and every buddha-field among all those fields, do I reach the limit of the successions of the births of Buddha-beings.
Just as I enter here in this world-system into all the births and miraculous transformations of bodhisattvas,

so too, in world-systems throughout the ten directions that are infinite and without center, within every single atom, at every moment of thought, I enter into all the various modes of all the births and miraculous transformations of bodhisattvas through a single entry of mind, by means of the yoga of unceasing empowerment.
When this had been said, the merchant’s son Sudhana spoke thus to the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī:

"Goddess, how long has it been since you attained this liberation of the birth of a bodhisattva, which displays the miraculous manifestations of the births of bodhisattvas throughout immeasurable eons and all objective spheres?"
He said: "In the past, noble son, in a time long gone, beyond eons as numerous as the atoms in ten million buddha-fields,

there appeared in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja— one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans."
The Buddha, the Blessed One, entered [this state] in the world-system Samantaratnā during the eon known as Aśītibuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraprabhava.
Indeed, noble son, in that world-system Samantaratnā, there was a central four-continent system named Vicitravyūhaprabhā.
In the center of that four-continent system, there was a royal capital of Jambudvīpa named Meruviśuddhavyūhadhvajā.
In that royal capital, there was a king named Ratnārcinetraprabha.
Noble son, King Ratnārcinetraprabha had a queen named Suharṣitaprabheśvarā.
Noble son, she was just like Māyādevī, the mother of the Blessed One Vairocana, in this Jambudvīpa within this blessed world-system of four continents.
In the same way, noble son, at that time and at that moment, in that world-system of four continents called Vicitravyūhaprabhā,
in Jambudvīpa, there was a mother of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja, named Suharṣitaprabheśvarā.

Just as she had been the mother of those eighty *koṭī-niyuta* Buddhas, so too, noble son, at the time of the Bodhisattva’s birth, the goddess Suharṣitaprabheśvarā went forth to the great park named Suvarṇapuṣpābha-maṇḍala together with two million women. She was the mother of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja, who was the foremost of them and the first of the [present] eon.
There, by means of inconceivable bodhisattva-transformations, she gave birth to that prince, Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja.
At that time, in the center of a great park named Suvarṇapuṣpābhamandala, there was a gabled pavilion named Śubharatnavicitrakūṭa.
Within that pavilion, suspended from the branch of a tree that grants all desires, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja, was born to the goddess Suharṣitaprabheśvarā.
At that time, at the moment of that Blessed One’s birth, a nurse named Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā was present.

As soon as the Bodhisattva was born, the lords of the world bathed him with jars of supremely fragrant scented water, from which issued heaps of various sweet-smelling and delightful divine flowers, and with inconceivable, innumerable, and supreme offerings worthy of him.
Having honored her with offerings, they placed the Bodhisattva upon the lap of that nurse, Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā.
As soon as the Bodhisattva was taken up by the nurse and held against her shoulders with both hands,
at that very moment the nurse attained a surge of great joy and gladness, and she obtained the bodhisattva-samādhi called Samantacakṣurviṣaya.
Upon the simultaneous attainment of this samādhi, immeasurable Tathāgatas residing in various world-systems throughout the ten directions came within the range of his vision;
and he manifested the miraculous displays of the births of bodhisattvas directed toward all objects throughout immeasurable eons.
The Bodhisattva liberation entered is exceedingly subtle, just like the consciousness of the embryo that has entered the mother’s womb on that very day;
by the attainment of this liberation, she has brought forth this great vow for manifesting the miraculous displays of the births of all Tathāgatas.
"What do you think, noble son—was she, at that time and on that occasion, anyone else who was the Bodhisattva’s nurse named Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā?
You should certainly not view it in this way.
At that time and on that occasion, I myself was the Bodhisattva’s nurse named Vimalasaṃbhavaprabhā."
What do you think, noble son—were those two million three hundred thousand women at that time and on that occasion others?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way;
these very two million three hundred thousand goddesses were they.
"Those who dwell here in the Lumbinī grove are my attendants.
What do you think, noble son—was that queen named Supraharṣitaprabheśvarā, the mother of Prince Īśvaraguṇāparājitadhvaja at that time and on that occasion, someone else?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way."
This very Queen Māyā was, at that time and on that occasion, the goddess named Supraharṣitaprabheśvarā.
What do you think, noble son—is it to be thought that the king named Ratnārcinetraprabha at that time and on that occasion was someone else?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way.

This King Śuddhodana was, at that time and on that occasion, the king named Ratnārcinetraprabha. Indeed, noble son, from that point onward, in every single moment of thought, I have never been separated from entering the ocean of the miraculous displays of the birth of the Bodhisattva Vairocana, and from entering the ocean of the miraculous displays of his bull-like leadership in guiding sentient beings.

And just as I, noble son, in this Sahā world-system, by means of the eye of wisdom— which has entered into all atoms through the convergence of the entry into every atom of the Tathāgatas born from the ocean-like sea of the great vows of the Blessed One Vairocana— penetrate the oceans of realms within every single atom at every moment of thought;
And within those fields, I enter oceans of the arising of Tathāgatas;

just as I enter the great oceans of the miraculous displays of the births of Bodhisattvas of those Tathāgatas, so too, in every moment of thought, I enter oceans of the miraculous displays of the births of Bodhisattvas of the infinite and centerless Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions.

And just as I enter into this triple-thousand great thousandfold world system by way of the successive series of all its atoms, perceiving the manifestation of the births of perfectly enlightened Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
so too do I enter into the oceans of fields contained within the atoms of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of inexpressible Buddha-fields in the ten directions;
and within those, I enter into the vast oceans of Buddhas.
I see those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, appearing before me in the manifestation of their miraculous births while they were still Bodhisattvas;
likewise, I worship them when they have become Tathāgatas,
and I hear the teaching of the Dharma from those Tathāgatas.
And may I practice in accordance with the Dharma.

Then, indeed, the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, illuminating this very bodhisattva liberation that displays the immeasurable manifestations of the births of all bodhisattvas throughout all kalpas and in all places free from obscuration, surveyed the ten directions through the empowerment of the Buddha and at that time spoke these verses:
"O Son of the Buddha, listen to my words, having generated reverence for that which you ask."
The peaceful domain of the Victors is difficult to perceive; it is demonstrated through the methods of causes and conditions. // 1 //

I remember inconceivable past eons, as numerous as the atoms in ten million buddha-fields, where there were infinite leaders, like the very first eon, in which eighty nayutas of Jinas appeared. // 2 //
At that time, the Tathāgata named Īśvarājitaguṇadhvaja was the first among them;
knowing this, I went to see the Leader in that supreme forest, the source of golden flowers. (3)
By name he was Vimalasaṃbhavaprabha; I was his wise nurse.
As soon as he was born, possessing the supreme radiance of gold, the World-Protector placed him upon my shoulder.
Having seized that foremost of persons by the shoulder, I am not able to look upon his head;
looking at that inconceivable one, I do not see his end. (5)
His auspicious body, adorned with the marks, is stainless and beautiful to behold;
seeing it, which resembles a statue made of jewels, an incomparable surge of joy has increased within me. (6)
Having reflected upon his immeasurable virtues, my ocean of merit has increased beyond measure;
and seeing his oceans of miraculous transformations, a vast resolve for awakening has arisen within me.
Having prayed for oceans of praises of the Victors, my ocean of vows has been increased;
the expansion of all fields has been purified, and all paths to miserable rebirths have been turned away. // 8 //
For the purpose of worshipping the inconceivable Sugatas who have not yet appeared throughout the expanse of all buddha-fields,
and for the sake of liberating suffering beings, an ocean of vows has arisen within me. 9.
Then, having heard the Dharma from that Protector, he attained this circle of supreme liberation;
and having practiced the conduct to purify enlightenment, he did so for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field.
In all those places where the Leaders have been born, I have honored them all without exception;
and I have upheld their teaching in order to purify this ocean of liberation. (11)
Equal in number to the atoms within ten million buddha-fields were those Ten-Powered Ones who appeared in the past;
for them, I have upheld and cultivated the Wheel of Dharma, the circle of supreme liberation.
He perceives as many atoms as there are in the dust of these Buddha-fields; within each single atom, he sees oceans of fields purified by the Victors in the past. (13)
In those vast arrays of fields, I behold the Leaders being born in excellent groves;
within the expanse of a single mind, they display inconceivable and expansive miraculous transformations.
In some fields I see leaders seeking supreme, excellent enlightenment, remaining in the Tuṣita world amidst inconceivable billions of trillions of fields. (15)
Being born through vast miraculous transformations in hundreds of oceans of realms, I see the Leaders of Men, honored by excellent assemblies of women, preaching the Dharma. (16)

O Hero, in a single moment of mind that is like the atoms within ten million fields, I behold you manifesting in manifold ways for the sake of the world, yet in that very same instant, entering the peace of nirvāṇa. (17)
Whenever I behold the birth of the Victors, as I survey the oceans of realms, in birth after birth, with many millions of bodies, I have worshipped them and attained compassion. (18)

Desiring to proceed through the inexhaustible movements of the realms of existence by means of inconceivable methods for the ocean of fields, I rain down vast clouds of Dharma, facing toward all worlds within them. (19)
O Son of the Conqueror, I know this inconceivable and supreme mandala of liberation,
which cannot be fully shown even in the course of inconceivable billions of trillions of eons.
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "Manifesting the Miraculous Transformations of the Births of Bodhisattvas in All Objects Throughout Immeasurable Eons.

How could I possibly describe the bodhisattvas whose minds, in every single moment of thought, are born from the womb of the undertakings of all eons; who demonstrate the birth of the profound realization of the methods of all dharmas; and whose intentions are born from the vows to worship all Tathāgatas?
They have made the supreme vow for the full awakening to all the qualities of a Buddha; they are like reflections manifesting births in all families, lineages, and states of existence;

they take birth within the lotus-calyxes at the feet of all Tathāgatas; they possess the superknowledge of the proper time for maturing all beings in the world; they display miraculous transformations through births and rebirths that face every means of discipline; they display clouds of miraculous manifestations throughout the expanse of all buddha-fields; and they appear as reflections within the destinies, births, and families of all living beings.
To know their conduct or to speak of their virtues.
Go, son of good family;
here in this very great city of Kapilavastu dwells a Śākyan maiden named Gopā. Approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva wander through saṃsāra for the sake of maturing other bodhisattvas?"

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, and having circumambulated the goddess Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī hundreds of thousands of times, looking back at her again and again, departed from the presence of the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī. 40.
(Gv 300) 43 Gopā: Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana departed from the presence of Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī, the deity of the Lumbinī grove.

Having approached the great city of Kapilavastu, he proceeded toward the palace of the Bodhisattva Assembly named Dharmadhātu-pratibhāsa-prabha; there he went while cultivating, entering, expanding, practicing, perfecting, mastering, reflecting upon, discerning, and repeatedly contemplating this very Bodhisattva liberation called "The Manifestation of the Miraculous Births of Bodhisattvas with All Objects of Perception Throughout Immeasurable Kalpas."

As he was approaching, the goddess of the Bodhisattva-saṃgīti palace named Aśokaśrī, together with ten thousand household deities, went out to meet the merchant’s son Sudhana and spoke to him thus: "Welcome to you, Great Being, who strides with the power of great wisdom and knowledge;
you who move within the range of the vast Dharma-palace, which is the sphere of the aspiration-mind and the meditative focus for the cultivation of the inconceivable liberation of a bodhisattva."

Facing toward the city of Dharma; having attained the illumination of the ocean of Tathāgata qualities through unceasing entry into the methods and means of infinite bodhisattvas; facing toward the eloquence and wisdom that reflects the discipline of all worlds; with a mind directed toward conduct that accords with the mantras of the body of knowledge regarding the conduct of all sentient beings; possessing vows that increase the force of the ocean of joy arising from the sensations of all worlds; and having entered the path of penetrating the Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
As I behold you, with unblinking eyes and a sphere of activity purified by profound conduct and deportment,

before long you shall attain the purity of the supreme ornaments of the body, speech, and mind of a Tathāgata; you shall traverse the world with a body adorned by the primary and secondary marks and with a mind embellished by the light of the ten powers of knowledge.
And from the firmness of your vigor and prowess that I perceive,

before long you shall be endowed with the vision of the presence of all Tathāgatas of the three times, receiving the clouds of Dharma from all Tathāgatas, and experiencing the delight in the palaces of the peaceful Dharma consisting of all the meditations, liberations, samādhis, and meditative attainments of the Bodhisattvas.
You shall penetrate the profound liberation of the Buddhas;

for, as you receive the instructions from your spiritual friends through approaching, seeing, and attending upon them, and as you apply yourself to the realization of their qualities, you do not grow weary nor do you turn back.
You do not suffer distress,
nor does any obstacle, hindrance, or obstruction prevail against you, nor do Māras or the deities belonging to Māra’s host.
Therefore, before long, you will become a bringer of joy to all sentient beings.
When this had been said, the merchant’s son Sudhana spoke thus to the goddess of the Bodhisattva Assembly Hall, Aśokaśrī: “So be it, O goddess, just as you say.
Indeed, O goddess, I find supreme joy in the pacification of the fever of the afflictions of all sentient beings;

I find supreme joy in the turning back of the ripening of karma within the sphere of all sentient beings, in the arising of happiness for all sentient beings, and in the practice of irreproachable actions by all sentient beings.”
And when, O goddess, beings— whose minds are impelled by the application of various objects, karmic actions, and afflictions— fall into miserable destinies or even into happy destinies,
and experience various physical and mental sufferings and dejection, at that time the bodhisattvas become despondent, indeed supremely despondent.
"O Devatā, it is just as if a man who is entirely driven by craving were to have an only son who was dear and pleasing to him.
When that son’s limbs and members were being cut off, because he was one whose conduct was entirely driven by craving, he would become extremely dejected and unhappy.

In the very same way, O Devatā, when a Bodhisattva practices the conduct of a Bodhisattva, seeing sentient beings fallen into the three miserable destinies through the power of karma and afflictions, he becomes dejected, even extremely dejected."
Furthermore, at whatever time beings— by reason of undertaking good conduct of body, speech, and mind— are reborn among the gods in the heavenly world after the dissolution of the body,
and experience physical and mental pleasures within the destinies of gods and humans,
at that time the Bodhisattva becomes supremely happy, well-disposed, joyful, and delighted.
Filled with joy and gladness, O goddess, Bodhisattvas do not indeed seek omniscience for their own sake;

nor for the sake of producing the pleasures and delights of diverse saṃsāra; nor through a longing for the various arrays of delights included within the desire realm; nor under the influence of the perversions of perception, mind, and view; nor having fallen under the power of the fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, and outbursts.
They have not fallen under the sway of craving or false views; their minds are not bound by the perception of delight in associating with various beings;
nor are they greedily attached to the savoring of the blissful joy of meditative absorption.
They do not wander through the realms of cyclic existence, obstructed by various hindrances.

Rather, O Goddess, having generated great compassion toward sentient beings who have entered the ocean of existence and are oppressed by immeasurable suffering, Bodhisattvas bring forth the great vow to gather in the entire world.

Through the forceful momentum of the accomplishment of that great compassionate vow, they are seen practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva in cyclic existence, dedicated to the ripening and disciplining of sentient beings.
Seeking the knowledge of omniscience free from all obscurations for the sake of all sentient beings, they bring forth the vow to honor and serve all Tathāgatas.
By the power of that vow to honor and serve the Tathāgatas, they do not become weary in the conduct of a bodhisattva.
While practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, perceiving buddha-fields that are afflicted with defilements, they bring forth the vow to purify all buddha-fields.

Purifying oceans of defiled realms and observing the diversity of the sense-bases of all sentient beings, they bring forth a vow for the sake of purifying the non-dual, unsurpassed Dharma-body. Observing the state of defiled body, speech, and mind of sentient beings,
they bring forth a vow for the sake of purifying the adornments of the body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings.

Beholding all those whose sense-bases are incomplete and whose minds are unpurified, and purifying the mental activities of all sentient beings while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, they do not become weary.
Thus, O Goddess, bodhisattvas practicing the boundless and centerless conduct of a bodhisattva remain with untiring minds.
Practicing in this way, they become ornaments for the world including its gods, by generating the prosperity of both gods and humans.
They become like parents by establishing and sustaining the birth of Bodhisattvas; they become like nurses by leading them into the path of the Bodhisattva;
and they become like ever-attendant innate deities by protecting them from the fear of falling into miserable rebirths.
They become great ferrymen by virtue of delivering [beings] across the ocean of saṃsāra;
they become refuges by virtue of turning back all fear of Māra and the afflictions; they become ultimate resorts by virtue of leading [beings] to the state of supreme peace.
They become like sacred fords by means of entering the ocean of all Buddhas; they become like gatherers by means of bringing forth the island of the jewel of the Dharma;
they become like flowers by means of their minds being fully blossomed with all the qualities of a Buddha.
They become like ornaments by emitting the radiance of vast merit and wisdom;
they become supremely pleasing by virtue of their universal amiability;
and they become worthy of approach through the practice of faultless action.

They are Samantabhadras by virtue of having bodies perfectly complete with the excellence of all supreme features; they possess forms that are never-tiring to behold because their appearance is never disagreeable;
and they are illuminators because they emit rays of gnosis.
They become makers of light by upholding the lamp of the Dharma; they become makers of radiance by purifying the aspiration for enlightenment;
they become generals by turning back the activities of Māra.
They become like the sun by emitting the radiance of the web of light-rays of wisdom; they become like the moon by the rising of the moon of the intellect in the sky of the mind;
they become like clouds by raining down the great Dharma-cloud upon all the world.
In this way indeed, O goddess, bodhisattvas who practice accordingly become dear to all sentient beings.
Then the goddess Aśokaśrī, the deity of the Bodhisattva Assembly Hall, together with those ten thousand household deities,

rained down showers of divine flowers, garlands, perfumes, powders, ointments, jewels, and ornaments that transcended the mundane and were produced by mind; and having surrounded Sudhana, the merchant's son, as he was entering the Bodhisattva residence, she praised him with these verses:
The Jinas, suns of wisdom, arise in the world only occasionally, having generated the mind set on perfect enlightenment out of compassion for all sentient beings. (Gv 302) 1.
That vision is difficult to obtain even in many millions of eons;
you are the great sun of knowledge for the world blinded by ignorance.
Having seen the world perverted and shrouded by the cataract of ignorance,
you gave rise to great compassion and set out for the state of self-existence.
With a pure intention, you have exerted yourself for the sake of the awakening of a Buddha;
you attend upon spiritual friends, regardless of body or life.
You have no dependence in this world, no home, and no intimacy; you are without abode, unconfused, unattached, and your intention is like the sky. // 5 //
You practice the supreme conduct of awakening, possessing the brilliant radiance of the mandala of merit;
while the world rises and sets, you emit the rays of primordial wisdom.
You do not rise above the worlds, yet you are not defiled by worldly dharmas;
you move through the world without attachment, like the wind in the sky.
Just as a fire blazing at the end of an eon is ever-rising, you practice the conduct of awakening with a vigor like that of fire. (8)
O Lion-like One, Great Hero, endowed with firm vigor and prowess, you wander unconquered, perfected in the valor of wisdom. // 9 //
O Hero, whatever oceans of methods exist within this ocean of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), you shall enter them all by means of attending upon true spiritual friends. 10.

Then, indeed, the goddess of the Bodhisattva-saṃgīti palace, Aśokaśrī, having praised the merchant’s son Sudhana with these verses, followed behind him as he departed. Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having approached and entered the Bodhisattva-saṃgīti palace, which was radiant with the manifestation of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), looked all around, desiring to see Gopā, the Śākya maiden.

He saw the Śākya maiden Gopā seated in the center of the Bodhisattva Assembly Hall named *Dharmadhātupratibhāsaprabha*, upon a lotus-womb throne made of jewels that reflected the dwellings of all bodhisattvas, surrounded by eighty-four thousand women, all of whom were born into royal families and possessed roots of virtue similar to her own from their former practices of the bodhisattva path.

They were gathered together by previous acts of giving and gathering; they were characterized by the practice of gentle and sweet speech; they were gathered through the happiness directed toward the goal of omniscience;
they were well-gathered through the common purpose of attaining the state of a Buddha or Bodhisattva; they were well-supported by the acceptance of wives and children preceded by great compassion;
they were purified by following their own wives with the accompaniment of great loving-kindness; and they had been fully matured by the inconceivable skill in means of former Bodhisattvas.
And all those eighty-four thousand women were irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; they had entered the way of the bodhisattva perfections,
were independent of others regarding all the trainings of a bodhisattva, possessed minds free from all grasping, had minds turned away from delighting in all of saṃsāra,
were purified by the principle of the unattached realm of phenomena, and possessed the momentum of a mind directed toward omniscience.

They were free from the net of all hindrances and obstructions; they had transcended all pathways of the limbs [of existence]; their investigations were well-fashioned by the Dharma-body; they were oriented toward the ripening and disciplining of all worlds; their minds were born from a vast ocean of merit; they had emerged from the vows and conduct of the Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
they were increased by the powerful momentum of the vast strength of Bodhisattvas; and they were lamps of mind with the solar orb of primordial wisdom.

Then Sudhana, the merchant's son, approached Gopā, the Śākya maiden; having prostrated with his entire body at the soles of Gopā’s feet, he rose and stood before her with palms joined in reverence, saying:
"Noble Lady, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
And yet, I do not know how it is that bodhisattvas wander through saṃsāra and are not defiled by the faults of saṃsāra,
while simultaneously awakening to the nature of the equality of all phenomena.
They do not abide on the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas;
they have attained the illumination of the Buddha-dharmas,
yet they do not interrupt the conduct of a bodhisattva.
They become established on the stages of a bodhisattva,
they manifest the domain of all Tathāgatas,
and they transcend all worldly destinies.
They move about within all the realms of the world,
yet they are fully perfected in the Dharma-body;
and they manifest form-bodies of infinite radiance.
They are devoted to the dharma-body that is without characteristics,
yet they manifest bodies with the colors and forms of all living beings;
and they abide in all dharmas which are ineffable.
They teach the Dharma to sentient beings through all paths of speech, linguistic expressions, and illustrations;
they understand all phenomena to be devoid of a sentient being,
yet they do not turn back from their application in disciplining the realm of sentient beings.
They penetrate all phenomena as being neither arising nor ceasing,
yet they do not turn back from the application of honoring and attending upon all Tathāgatas.
They penetrate all phenomena as being without karmic maturation, yet they do not turn back from the application of the formative activity of wholesome karma.

When this had been said, Gopā, the Śākya maiden, spoke thus to Sudhana, the merchant’s son: “Excellent, excellent, noble son! It is well that you consider it necessary to inquire about such a course of conduct and such a nature of reality belonging to the Bodhisattvas; for this presentation of a question is appropriate for one who is intent upon the conduct of the vows of Samantabhadra.”
Therefore, noble son, listen; pay close and careful attention,
and I shall speak through the power of the Buddha.
Noble son, endowed with ten qualities, bodhisattvas fulfill this very bodhisattva practice—the universal radiance of wisdom that is like the surface of Indra’s net.
What are these ten? Namely:
by relying upon sublime spiritual friends; by attaining vast resolute conviction; and by the purification of a sublime and virtuous intention.
By virtue of having a mind supported by the vast ocean of merit and wisdom; by the attainment of hearing the great teaching on the Dharma concerning the appearance of Buddhas;
by dwelling in the intention of resolute faith in the Tathāgatas of the three times; by following the equality of the entire mandala of the conduct of all bodhisattvas;

by the attainment of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas; by the purification of the superior aspiration of natural great compassion; and by the attainment of the strengthening of the power of the mind that cuts off the entire wheel of saṃsāra.
Noble son, endowed with these ten qualities, they bring to fulfillment this very bodhisattva practice called "Universal Radiance of Wisdom," which is like the surface of Indra’s net.

In this regard, noble son, bodhisattvas of irreversible vigor, having attained these qualities, cultivate and frequently practice them through inexhaustible modes of realization, thereby pleasing their spiritual friends.
By what ten [qualities]?
Namely: by being indifferent to body and life; by having no need for the requisites of saṃsāra; and by following the equality of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

Because of the irreversibility of the vow for omniscience; because of the contemplation of the methods of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); because of the mind having transcended the ocean of all states of existence (*bhava*); because of being without abode, having entered the space-like state that is free from clinging; because of the unobstructed nature of all the vows of bodhisattvas; because of the expansion into oceans of all buddha-fields; and because of being thoroughly purified within the mandala of the unobstructed wisdom of bodhisattvas.
Noble son, by these ten ways, bodhisattvas, having pleased their spiritual friends, bring them satisfaction.

Then indeed, Gopā, the Śākya maiden, demonstrating this very method of meaning, surveyed the ten directions through the empowerment of the Buddha and at that moment spoke these verses: “Those whose pure and vast intellects are set forth for the sake of others, who are devoted to serving true spiritual friends and have abandoned deceit and guile; who have attained the perception of the Teacher and possess untiring vigor—they move through this world like a wondrous magical illusion. (11)

Those whose resolve is vast and luminous as space, into which the entire world of the three times converges—their fields, their sentient beings, their dharmas, and likewise their Buddhas—this is the conduct of those who radiate the light of wisdom. 12.

Those whose disposition is like space, infinite and without center, supremely pure through its freedom from defilement—in them arise all the qualities of the Tathāgatas, who are concentrated within the diverse manifestations of the magical net of conduct. (13)

Those of excellent intelligence, who are supported by vast, immeasurable, and inconceivable oceans of qualities that encompass the wisdom of the Omniscient One, possess a pure womb—the body of an ocean of merit—and they move through the world yet are not defiled by worldly impurities. // 14 //

Those who never reach satiety in hearing the thundering of the Dharma from the Victors through the methods of all vocal qualities, sounds, and tones—they are the lamps of the world; this is the conduct of those who illuminate the Dharma with the light of wisdom following the guiding principles. 15.

Those immeasurable Tathāgatas in the ten directions, who at every moment of mind enter into one another, they contemplate the entire ocean of Tathāgatas; this is the entrance for those who follow the intentions of the Buddhas. 16.
Those who behold the vast assemblies of the Victors enter the ocean of the methods of their meditative absorptions;
they also penetrate the infinite and centerless ocean of their vows—such is the conduct of those who are like the surface of Indra’s palace. // 17 //
Those Samantabhadras who, empowered by all the Victors in the ten directions, practice throughout eons until the very end of time;
Throughout the entire expanse of all fields, this is the conduct of those who radiate the light of Dharma, appearing as manifestations everywhere. // 18 //

Those steadfast ones who, like suns of wisdom within the mandala of great compassion, arise upon seeing the world fallen into calamity, dispelling the darkness of delusion in the world with the light of the Dharma—the conduct of those who resemble the sun is this very one. (19)
Seeing living beings revolving within the states of existence, those of excellent wisdom remain逆流 (against the current) of the stream of saṃsāra;
gathering the immeasurable wheel of the True Dharma, they practice the conduct of Samantabhadramati. // 20 //

Having trained in these methods, they manifest infinite and boundless bodies according to the inclinations of beings in the world; and by means of those bodies, which are like reflections and images, they bring sentient beings to maturity within the oceans of existence. 21.
Having pervaded the world of beings with vast methods of loving-kindness and having displayed their conduct among people of diverse inclinations,
these wise ones rain down the Dharma according to the dispositions of the world, leading millions of sentient beings toward enlightenment.
Then Gopā, the Śākya maiden, having spoken these verses, said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana:
“Noble son, I am indeed a possessor of the bodhisattva liberation called ‘The Sphere of Contemplating the Methods of the Ocean of All Bodhisattva Samādhis.
Sudhana asked: “Noble lady, what is the scope of this bodhisattva liberation called ‘The Sphere of Contemplating the Methods of the Ocean of All Bodhisattva Samādhis’?”
He said: "Noble son, having entered this bodhisattva liberation, I descend into this world-system for eons equal to the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
I know all those beings therein who are included within every state of existence."
I fully know as many gateways of death and rebirth as those sentient beings possess,
as well as as many gateways of manifestation as there are.
I also fully understand all the attainments resulting from the formative forces of karma, as well as all the various manifestations of the maturation of karma.

I also thoroughly know their undertaking of wholesome actions; likewise, I know their unwholesome actions, those that lead to liberation and those that do not, those that are fixed and those that are unfixed, those fixed in falsehood, those accompanied by latent tendencies and those free from latent tendencies, those endowed with roots of goodness, those whose roots of goodness have perished, and those whose roots of goodness are fully embraced.

I fully understand the undertaking of these actions—whether they are embraced by unwholesome roots, or embraced by both wholesome and unwholesome [roots], or whether they consist of cultivated wholesome roots, or uncultivated evil dharmas.
And throughout those eons, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, I enter into the oceans of names of all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who have appeared;
and I also know the oceans of the first production of the thought of enlightenment of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
I also understand the oceans of methods for entering into omniscience;
I also understand the actualizations of all oceans of vows;
and I also understand the oceans of ways in which previous Buddhas appeared in the world.
I also know the oceans of practices for honoring and serving former Buddhas;
I also know the oceans of the fulfillment of former bodhisattva conducts;
and I also know the oceans of the arrays of departure.
And I also know the oceans of the ripening and disciplining of sentient beings by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; I also know the oceans of their perfect awakenings;
and I also know their displays of the heroic power in turning the wheel of Dharma.
I also know the oceans of all the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas;
I also know the distinct assemblies of those Blessed Buddhas;
and within those assemblies, I also know the methods of deliverance for those who are śrāvakas.
I also fully know their former roots of merit;
I also fully know the various distinctions in the cultivation of the path;
and I also fully know the pure classifications of the excellence in attaining knowledge.
I also know those beings who were established in the awakening of a pratyekabuddha by those Tathāgatas;
I also know whatever roots of merit those pratyekabuddhas possessed in the past;
and I also know whatever realizations of pratyekabuddha-awakening those pratyekabuddhas attained.

I also fully understand those gateways of liberation consisting of the peaceful dwellings and miraculous transformations of those pratyekabuddhas; I also fully understand their various miraculous transformations;
and I also fully understand the ripening of sentient beings accomplished by those pratyekabuddhas.
I also fully understand the Dharma teachings of those Pratyekabuddhas,
and I also fully understand their infinite dwellings in meditative concentration and their various playful exercises in liberation.
I also know the final nirvana of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; I also know the oceans of circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas belonging to those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones;
and I also know the initial plantings of roots of merit by those bodhisattvas.

I also fully know the vows of their first production of the thought of enlightenment; I fully know the diversity of those vows, as well as the diversity of the arrays and accomplishments of the departure through all the bodhisattva practices;
and I fully know the diversity of the purification of the equipment for the factors of the path of the perfections.
I also understand the various distinctions in the practice of the bodhisattva path; I also understand the various distinctions in the accumulations for ascending the bodhisattva stages;
and I also understand the various distinctions in the momentum for ascending the bodhisattva stages.
I also understand the diversity of the maṇḍalas of samādhi for traversing the bodhisattva stages; I also understand the miraculous transformations involved in ascending the bodhisattva stages;
and I also understand the dwellings associated with ascending the bodhisattva stages.
I also thoroughly understand the foundations of the bodhisattva stages;
I also thoroughly understand the cultivation and investigation of the bodhisattva stages;
and I also thoroughly understand the methods for purifying the bodhisattva stages.
I also fully understand the dwelling upon the bodhisattva stages;
I also fully understand the signs of the bodhisattva stages;
I also fully understand the mastery of the bodhisattva stages.
I also understand the knowledge of ascending the bodhisattva stages;
I also understand the knowledge of gathering in bodhisattvas;
I also understand the knowledge of maturing bodhisattvas.
I also understand the communal dwellings established for bodhisattvas;
I also understand the vast arrays of the mandalas of bodhisattva conduct;
and I also understand the miraculous transformations of bodhisattva conduct.
I also know the oceans of bodhisattva samādhis;
I also know the oceans of the methods of bodhisattva liberation;
and I also know how those bodhisattvas, in every moment of thought, attain various oceans of samādhis.
I also understand the attainment of the illumination of omniscience;
I also understand the clouds of lightning-light of omniscience;
and I also understand the methods for attaining the patience of a bodhisattva.
I also understand their heroic strides in plunging into omniscience;
I also understand those bodhisattvas' entries into oceans of buddha-fields;
and I also understand their entries into the methods of the ocean of Dharma.

I also thoroughly know the diversity of all the characteristics of the oceans; I also thoroughly know the miraculous displays of the methods of all the bodhisattva abodes; and I also thoroughly know the oceans of the methods of various vows.
I also understand the vast diversity of the ocean of various miraculous transformations.
And just as I, noble son, enter into the various kinds of oceans of past and present eons in this world-system,
so too do I know the oceans of future eons, which continue in succession without interruption.
And just as I know them in the Sahā world-system, [so do I know them in all others].

In this way, I know all the successions of world-systems that converge within the Sahā world-system; and just as I know all the successions of world-systems that converge within the Sahā world-system,
so too do I know all the successions of world-systems contained even within a single atom of the Sahā world-system.
Just as I know the successions of all world-systems contained within the atoms of the Sahā world-system,
so too do I know those world-systems situated throughout the ten directions of the Sahā world-system without interruption.
And just as I know all the world-systems situated throughout the ten directions of the Sahā world-system without interruption, [so too do I know them].
In this way, I know all world-systems situated in the infinite succession of the ten directions within the Sahā world-system;
and just as I know all world-systems situated in the infinite succession of the ten directions within the Sahā world-system,
so too do I know all world-systems included within the lineage of the world-system called Samantadikprabhāsavairocana.
Just as I know the world-systems included within the lineage of the world-system called Samantadikprabhāsavairocana,
so too do I know all world-systems situated in the continuous succession of directions throughout the lineage of the world-system Samantadikprabhāsavairocana.
And just as I know this lineage of the world-system Samantadikprabhāsavairocana in all world-systems situated in the continuous succession of the ten directions, [so do I know all others].

In this way, I know all the world-system Sumerus within the arrayed ornaments of the Flower-Bottom Matrix, as well as those contained within the oceans of world-systems and the expansions of world-systems;
likewise, I know them in the systems of world-systems, in the wheels of world-systems, in the mandalas of world-systems, in the divisions of world-systems, in the rivers of world-systems,
in the whirlpools of world-systems, in the revolutions of world-systems, in the Sumerus of world-systems, in the emergences of world-systems, and in the lotuses of world-systems.
I also understand those things which are trees within world-systems, those which are salt-mines within world-systems, and even those designated as world-systems.
Just as I know [the oceans of world-systems] within this world-system ocean adorned with the array of the Flower-Surface Womb,

so too do I know, enter, and recollect the oceans of former vows of Vairocana in all the oceans of world-systems throughout the ten directions— boundless and limitless, reaching to the furthest reaches of the realm of phenomena and the limits of space.
I also enter into the oceans of past connections;
I also enter into the oceans of journeys to the eastern seas;
and I also enter into the dwelling in the bodhisattva conduct throughout kalpas of infinite extent.
I also enter into the methods for the purification of buddha-fields; I also enter into the methods for the means of maturing sentient beings;
and I also enter into the miraculous displays of approaching and honoring previous Tathāgatas.
I also enter into the methods of practice for honoring and attending upon former Tathāgatas;
I also enter into the methods for receiving the Dharma teachings of former Tathāgatas;
and I also enter into the methods for attaining the samādhis of former bodhisattvas.
I also enter into the methods for attaining mastery over requisites; I also enter into the methods for practicing the ocean of qualities of the Tathāgatas of the past;
and I also enter into the oceans of methods for the perfection of generosity.

I also enter into the methods for accomplishing the complete purity of the mandala of the bodhisattva’s ethical discipline and vows; I also enter into the methods for attaining the bodhisattva’s patience;
and I also enter into the oceans of the bodhisattva’s momentum of vigor.
I also enter the oceans of methods for the perfect accomplishment of all factors of meditative concentration;
I also enter the oceans of methods for the purification of the mandala of wisdom;
and I also enter the methods of skillful means for manifesting the appearance of bodies in birth throughout all worlds.
I also enter into the methods for purifying the maṇḍala of the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra;
I also enter into the pervasion of oceans of all buddha-fields;
and I also enter into the oceans of methods for purifying all buddha-fields.
I also enter into the oceans of the illumination of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
I also enter into the oceans of the miraculous displays of ascending to the enlightenment of all Buddhas; I also enter into the methods for attaining the illumination of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
I also enter the oceans of methods for entering the realization of omniscience;
I also enter the oceans of miraculous displays of perfect enlightenment;
and I also enter the oceans of methods for the playful mastery of the bull-like power in turning the wheel of Dharma.
I also enter into oceans of various circles of assemblies,
and within all those circles of assemblies, I also enter into the oceans of the former roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas;
I also enter into the oceans of the methods of their initial vows.
I also enter into the oceans of methods and principles for the ripening and disciplining of sentient beings;
I also enter into those oceans of sentient beings who were previously ripened by the Blessed One while he was practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva;
and I also enter into the oceans of methods and principles for increasing the roots of goodness in those bodhisattvas at every moment of thought.
I also enter into oceans of methods for attaining meditative concentration; I also enter into oceans of methods for attaining the gateways of dhāraṇīs;
and I also enter into oceans of methods for purifying the mandala of the knowledge of eloquence.
I also enter into the oceans of methods for the miraculous displays of ascending through all the bodhisattva stages; I also enter into the oceans of methods for accomplishing the net of conduct;
and I also enter into the successive oceans.
I also enter into the oceans of the methods of knowledge for entering the directions of the successive attainment [of the stages];
and I also enter into the oceans of the miraculous transformations of all their faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment, meditations, liberations, concentrations, attainments, and absorptions.
And just as I enter into, understand, and bring forth the oceans of bodhisattva conduct within the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) of the Blessed One Vairocana,

even so do I enter into, understand, and bring forth the oceans of all the unconfused bodhisattva conducts throughout the oceans of all world-systems in the ten directions— systems that reach to the limits of the realm of phenomena and extend to the ends of the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*).

In this way, I enter into, understand, and bring forth the infinite entry into the conduct of all bodhisattvas without distinction, the entry into the infinite net of illusions, the pervasion of the infinite realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the teaching through infinite gateways, and the teaching on the entry into the empowerment of boundless eons— pertaining to all the Tathāgatas throughout the oceans of all world-systems in the ten directions, reaching to the limits of the realm of space and supreme within the realm of phenomena.
For what reason?

Noble son, this is the domain of this bodhisattva liberation called "the range of the observation of the ocean of methods of all bodhisattva samādhis," such that having entered it, I understand the ways of the mental conduct of all sentient beings.
I understand the accumulation of all the roots of virtue of all sentient beings;
I understand the methods for the affliction and purification of all sentient beings;
and I understand the diversity of the karma of all sentient beings.

I thoroughly understand all the gateways to the samādhis of the śrāvakas; I thoroughly understand the entire ground of the samādhis of the śrāvakas; and I enter into the peaceful liberations and miraculous transformations of all the pratyekabuddhas.
I understand the ocean-like methods of all the bodhisattva samādhis; I understand the entry into the ocean-like methods of all the bodhisattva liberations;
and I also understand the entry into the ocean-like methods of the liberations of all the Tathāgatas.
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, said this to Gopā, the Śākya maiden: “Noble lady, how long ago did you attain this sphere of the ocean of methods for contemplating the samādhis of bodhisattvas?
She replied: “In the past, noble son, in a time gone by, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a hundred Buddha-fields, there was a world-system named Abhayamkarā.”
In that world-system, there was indeed an eon named Gatipravara.
Furthermore, in the center of that world-system, there was a four-continent realm named Kṣemāvatī.
In the center of that four-continent realm, there was a royal capital of Jambudvīpa named Drumameruśrī, which was the foremost among eighty-four thousand million cities.
Furthermore, that royal capital, Drumameruśrī,
and those eighty-four thousand million cities were each established upon grounds of blue beryl,

surrounded by walls made of the seven precious substances, and encircled by seven moats filled with fragrant water and strewn on their bottoms with golden sand; they were covered with blue lotuses, red lotuses, night-blooming water lilies, and white lotuses, which were as large as chariot wheels and possessed beautiful fragrances and networks of light of various colors.

They were surrounded by seven rows of palm trees and seven networks of jeweled railings; they were encircled by garlands of trees made of the seven precious gems and covered above by nets of clouds. Their ground surfaces were radiant with various patterns of jewels arranged in well-proportioned jeweled octagonal pavilions, frequented by hosts of perfected beings (*siddha*), and resounded with the delightful warbling and cries of flocks of noble birds. They were further adorned by hundreds of thousands of millions of pleasure groves.

Those great cities were flourishing with supernatural powers, crowded with hundreds of thousands of joyful men and women, showered incessantly by thousands of rains of flowers stirred by auspicious and desirable breezes,
and inhabited by hundreds of thousands of lords of the earth.

Furthermore, from all the jewel-trees, golden nets, and ornaments of those great cities, which were struck together by the wind and emitted sounds like many musical instruments, there issued forth this very kind of [sound].
The sound "Ānanda! issued forth: "Bathe! Drink!
Eat!"
Practice the Dharma,
generate the mind of awakening,
and attain mastery over the stage of non-retrogression.
May it be well with you. Thus.
In that royal capital, Drumameruśrī, there was a regional king named Dhanapati.
He had an inner court of eighty-four thousand women and five hundred ministers.

Furthermore, King Dhanapati had five hundred sons, all of whom were brave, heroic, possessed of excellent physical forms, crushers of enemy armies, gracious, and beautiful to behold, endowed with an abundance of most sublime and auspicious complexion.
Moreover, King Dhanapati had a chief queen named Padmaśrīgarbhasaṃbhavā, who was the leader of his eighty-four thousand women.
In her, there was a son named Tejodhipati, who was handsome, gracious, and beautiful to behold, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man.
These were the thirty-two marks of a great man that he possessed, namely: Prince Tejodhipati had well-established hands and feet.
He lifts his soles from the great earth evenly,
he sets them down evenly,
and as he sets them down, he touches the great earth evenly with the entirety of both soles.
On the soles of his feet, wheels appeared with a thousand spokes, complete with hubs and rims, perfect in every aspect, beautiful and lovely to behold;
and he possessed the quality of having high-arched feet,
which were clearly manifest, supremely adorned, and exceedingly radiant with a luster surpassing that of the flowers within the soles of his feet.
Both the palms of his hands and the soles of his feet were webbed, beautifully divided, without gaps, and not leaking,
just like those of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the king of swans.
His long heels were perfectly formed, pure, radiant, and emitted the luster of the colors of all kinds of jewels.
His fingers were long, rounded, and with well-proportioned joints;
he placed them evenly upon the earth and lifted them up.

The soles of his hands and feet were soft, with a touch more pleasant than that of kācilindika cloth; whomever he touched— whether a woman, a man, a boy, or a girl— with them, [he was filled with joy].
They all became joyful in mind, endowed with supreme happiness and mental well-being; and his *eṇeya* deer-like calves were manifested.
His calves were gradually tapering, well-proportioned, rounded, and beautifully formed, just like those of the king of the *eṇeya* deer.
No one was able to overtake him or catch up with him, nor did he experience any fatigue while walking;
furthermore, that Prince Tejodhipati possessed the seven protuberances.
On his two feet, two elevations had arisen: they were rounded, well-formed, perfectly full, with invisible seams, beautifully fashioned, and lovely to behold;
likewise, there were two on his hands, two on the tops of his shoulders, and one on the back of his neck.
Furthermore, the mark of a Great Man known as having the private organ enclosed in a sheath was manifested in him.
His private parts— the scrotum and the anus— were well-guarded, submerged, and covered,
just like those of a noble elephant or a noble horse.
No one at all— whether woman or man, boy or girl, old, middle-aged, or young, a teacher or one in the position of a teacher— could see them even when he was naked, except for his own personal use.
Or perhaps by some omen accumulated through desire;
furthermore, that prince Tejodhipati had the forepart of his body like a lion;
his body was gradually developed, his chest was broad and well-proportioned, and his stature was perfectly formed, surpassing even that of the noble king of beasts.
Furthermore, his shoulders were broad between them;

he possessed a well-developed body with well-proportioned height, established in a state of perfect symmetry throughout his entire frame. His limbs were neither deficient nor protruding, and his body was not distorted; his limbs emitted an exceeding radiance like that of a polished gemstone slab, and his shoulders were perfectly rounded.
His two shoulders became rounded, full, auspicious, and well-developed;
indeed, he attained the mark of a Great Man known as having long arms.
Furthermore, with both hands lowered, he could stroke his kneecaps.

He stroked [the body] with his own body, which remained in a state of equanimity. Indeed, he had attained the mark of a Great Man consisting of a broad and straight torso; moreover, he possessed limbs that were perfectly proportioned down to every minute atom, with limbs that were serene, heavy, radiant, and joyful.
Having attained the mark of a Great Man characterized by a neck like a conch shell (*kambugrīva*), he indeed possessed a throat that was never dejected.
All the channels for conveying taste around his neck and around his mouth were equal, uniform, and perfectly full; indeed,
he had attained the mark of a Great Man known as the lion-like jaw.
With his jaw well-compressed, his facial orb perfectly full, and his facial orb naturally well-formed and pure, he possessed a wide mouth-opening that was free from gaps.

He had acquired the mark of a Great Man consisting of forty even teeth; indeed, he possessed no fewer than ten teeth. Furthermore, whenever he partook of food, even a single morsel of food in his mouth would pass down into his stomach without being broken up, even down to a single drop of boiled rice.
Furthermore, he had attained the mark of a Great Man known as having teeth that are closely set and even.

His teeth were indeed closely set and even, with gaps between them that were seamless; they were uniform and well-proportioned, so that when he consumed food, there was no obstruction or entanglement caused by unevenness.
Nor was there any moisture, nor any exudation, nor any envelopment, nor any excessive discharge. Furthermore, he had acquired the mark of a Great Man known as even teeth;
his teeth were even, neither deficient, nor redundant, neither protruding, nor sunken, nor irregular; his teeth were uniform from top to bottom and in the middle, and not receding.
The youth had teeth that were inseparable;
his fangs were exceedingly white, free from affliction, perfectly clear, utterly pure, and beautifully situated and variegated.
Furthermore, he had indeed attained the mark of a Great Man known as having an exceptionally long tongue.
His tongue was broad, thin, soft, delicate, pliant, lovely, and agile; it could cover the entire circle of his face.

That prince possessed a Brahma-voice, a delightful tone, and his vocal activity—his utterances, conversations, and discourses—was as charming as the sound of all musical instruments, songs, and instrumental music.
He uttered speech that generates delight in the paths of language and is welcomed by the whole world.

With a voice surpassing that of Brahmā, he transcended the circle of the assembly and caused it all to resound. Furthermore, that youth had deep blue eyes; his eyes were clear, pure, radiant, serene, and beautiful.

That prince had beautiful eyes, lovely eyes, and smiling eyes; he possessed eyelashes like those of a cow and an organ of sight as pure as a ruby. His eye-socket was symmetrical, his eye-socket was perfectly even, his eye-socket was well-formed, his eye-socket was broad, his eye-socket was full, and his eye-socket was well-set.

Between his eyebrows, a *ūrṇā* was born—soft, pliable, delicate, and pleasant to the touch; it was clear, pure, and radiant, with the color of a snowball or frost, shining with the splendor of a circle of most brilliant white rays.

And upon his head, an *uṣṇīṣa* was manifested, well-formed, perfectly rounded, adorned with hair arranged in the center, appearing like a precious lotus with hundreds of thousands of millions of petals, established in perfect symmetry on all sides, and preeminent in its immeasurable and great worth.
That prince had delicate skin;
on his body there was no dust, nor filth, nor moisture, nor webbing, nor wrinkles, nor laxity, nor breaking, nor spreading, nor expansion, nor any unevenness—none of these existed.
That prince had a golden-colored skin, radiant like Jāmbūnada gold, with a halo of light extending a fathom in every direction, adorned by a single blazing circle of golden radiance.
His body was adorned with the radiance of fragrance-light rays emitted from every pore;
moreover, that prince had but a single hair on each pore.
On each and every pore, a single hair grew—blue in color like beryl, curling to the right in a spiral, perfectly gathered, well-settled, and firmly established.
That prince had body hair that stood upright; his hair was irreversible, non-retrogressive, and unentangled.
He possessed the mark of a great man consisting of hair the color of sapphire;
such was that prince.

His hair was blue, radiant with the color of the *vairocana* jewel, glossy, soft, well-curled, and spiraling to the right; its roots were well-formed, not disheveled, not pressed flat, nor entangled, but situated in perfectly uniform positions.

Indeed, that Prince Tejodhipati possessed the mark of a Great Man characterized by a body as symmetrical as a *nyagrodha* tree; he was perfectly circular in form, universally auspicious, and altogether pleasing to behold.
He was pleasing to behold from the front and never-tiring to look upon;
likewise from behind, from the right, and from the left. Whether walking, standing, sitting, speaking, or remaining silent, he was always pleasing to behold and never-tiring to look upon.
Noble son, Prince Tejodhipati’s body was thus adorned with these thirty-two marks of a Great Man.
He became one whose appearance was not disagreeable to any being, whose appearance fulfilled all intentions, and whose appearance brought joy to all beings.

Then, noble son, at another time, the prince Tejodhipati, having been granted permission by his father, set out from the royal capital Drumameruśrī to see the grounds of the park named Gandhāṅkuraprabhamegha. Accompanied by twenty thousand maidens and surrounded on all sides by throngs of men and women who were joyfully celebrating his great array of miraculous displays of merit, splendor, majesty, and good fortune, he mounted a chariot of Jāmbūnada gold with four wheels made of great vajra-jewels.

It possessed firm, indestructible axle-pins made of Nārāyaṇa-vajra; it was firmly established upon a base perfectly fashioned from the finest sandalwood; its framework was beautifully divided by all kinds of fragrant king-jewels;

its array was exquisitely adorned with flowers of every gem; its structure was covered by a net of all kinds of jewels; its center was supported by a lion-throne set within an array of great king-jewels; and it was encircled by five hundred maidens holding cords of precious gems.

He was surrounded by hundreds of thousands of living beings and accompanied by hundreds of thousands of celestial musical instruments that were sweet, charming, and faultless; he was borne under a great jewel-parasol with a handle raised from a king of blue lapis lazuli gems, which was yoked to a thousand noble steeds possessing the speed of wind clinging to the sky, and which was adorned with a canopy made of the finest white lapis lazuli gems, beautifully shaped and tapering in succession, possessing stainless and immeasurable radiance, and beautified by an inconceivable and marvelous array of all kinds of jewels arranged in various artistic patterns.

As he proceeded in that manner, a great eight-lane road appeared, free from depressions and elevations, cleared of pebbles, gravel, and debris, established upon a ground-surface composed of all the jewels of the royal realms of gold and silver, and strewn with golden sand; it was being showered upon by vast clouds of flowers being sounded, and perfumed by hundreds of thousands of millions of censers emitting fragrant, divine scents and incense.
It was strewn with various jeweled flowers, adorned on both sides by rows of jewel-trees, and surrounded by a railing of diverse jewels.

Above, it was covered with a network of jeweled bells and decorated with canopies spread out of various gems; its magnificent array was further beautified by hundreds of thousands of hanging jeweled banners, flags, and silk streamers. On both sides, within certain jeweled niches there, were placed jeweled vessels filled with various gems for the purpose of bestowing them upon the assembly of supplicants.

In some celestial palaces, arrangements of all kinds of jewel ornaments were placed for the purpose of adorning those supplicants who desired ornaments. In some celestial palaces, wish-fulfilling jewels (*cintāmaṇiratna*) were placed for the purpose of fulfilling all the intentions of all sentient beings.
In some celestial palaces, foods filled with various flavors of all kinds of food and drink were placed.
For the sake of providing whatever was needed by whoever required it,
in some celestial palaces were placed arrangements of divine food that were supremely delicious, charming, and possessed of every excellent color, fragrance, flavor, and texture;
in some celestial palaces were placed arrangements of all kinds of divine fruits possessing various tastes and flavors.

In some celestial palaces, hundreds of thousands of millions of divine garments were placed— variously brilliant and multicolored, dyed in red, adorned with the arrangement of various wonderful patterns, most precious, fine, and possessing delicate and beautiful colors—
for the purpose of being enjoyed according to the wishes of those seeking clothing.

In some celestial palaces, all kinds of divine, charming fragrances and colors were arranged as various methods of incense for those seeking ointments, so that they might enjoy them according to their wishes.
In some celestial palaces, heaps of all kinds of utensils were arranged for the enjoyment of sentient beings according to their inclinations and desires.
In some celestial palaces, there were women who were beautiful, gracious, and lovely to behold, adorned with various charming forms and attire, and arrayed in diverse, pleasing garments.

They were all well-adorned with ornaments, their bodies graced and embellished by the application of various types of ointments; they were experts in all feminine arts, crafts, illusions, and the rules of aesthetic skill, and were stationed there.
Furthermore, at that time, in that very royal capital of Drumameruśrī, there was a chief courtesan named Sudarśanā, who was enjoyed by the king.

She had a daughter named Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, who was beautiful, gracious, and lovely to behold; she was neither too tall nor too short, neither too stout nor too thin, neither too fair nor too dark, with deep blue eyes, deep blue hair, and a most charming countenance.

She possessed the voice of Brahmā, spoke sweet and pleasant words, was wise, and knew the rules of all arts; she was proficient in all treatises, skillful, untiring, respectful, gracious, and possessed a mind of loving-kindness. She was largely free from resentment, her appearance brought no dissatisfaction, and she had little passion, hatred, or delusion.
She was endowed with a sense of shame and dread of blame, gentle, upright, free from deceit, free from guile, and disciplined.

Accompanied by her mother and surrounded by many maidens, she mounted a chariot adorned with jewels and departed from the royal capital of Drumameruśrī. Following the king’s command, she traveled along searching for the prince Tejodhipati;
upon seeing Prince Tejodhipati, she conceived an intense feeling of passion.

Having conceived an excessive and persistent affection for Prince Tejodhipati, her mind became no longer independent, and she said this to her mother, Sudarśanā: "Mother, you should know this: if you do not give me to Prince Tejodhipati, I shall either meet my death or experience suffering equal to death."
She said: "Do not, young girl, give rise to such a thought.
For this prince is endowed with the marks of a universal monarch (cakravartin). It is possible that, upon the passing of his father Dhana-pati, he will occupy the sovereignty of a universal monarch."
He will become a universal monarch (cakravartin),
and then the jewel of a woman (strīratna) will appear to him, capable of traveling through the air.
Furthermore, girl, we are courtesans who provide pleasure to the entire world.
"We do not attend to a single being as a fixed rule for the rest of our lives;
indeed, we have set out at the command of King Dhanapati to serve Prince Tejodhipati.
Do not固ify this intention."
This state is difficult to attain.
And at that time, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Sūryagātrapravara—

one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. Furthermore, within that garden called Gandhāṅkuraśikharaprabhamegha, there was a seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) named Dharmameghodgataprabhāsa.

There, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara, dwelt having attained perfect enlightenment during his first week. While she was still mounted upon her chariot and trembling, that maiden saw him in a dream.
And when she had awakened, a deity who was a kinswoman from her former lineage informed her: "O maiden, this is the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara."

He dwells at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), radiant with the emergence of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmamegha), having attained perfect enlightenment during the first week, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas and honored by a multitude of gods,
nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, Indra, Brahmā, the Ābhāsvara gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods. And right there, all the earth-deities have assembled.

The deities of space, the deities of water, the deities of fire, the deities of wind, the deities of the ocean, the deities of rivers, the deities of mountains, the deities of night, the deities of the rising dawn, the deities of forests, the deities of trees, the deities of medicinal herbs, the deities of crops, the deities of cities,
the deities who travel on foot, the deities of the seat of awakening, the deities of the rays from the body, the deities of the assemblies of beings, and the deities of the sky.
And the deities of all directions assembled in order to behold that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sūryagātrapravara.

Having become confident through that vision of the Tathāgata and by hearing of the qualities of the Tathāgata, she, having found her opportunity, spoke these verses in the presence of the prince Tejodhipati at that time:
"I am preeminent in the world for my excellent form, and renowned in all directions for my virtues."
By the power of my wisdom, there is no one equal to me in knowing all the arts, pleasures, and the methods of illusion. // 1 //

Many hundreds and many thousands of living beings who gazed upon me under the influence of passion—even toward them, my son, my mind does not become attached; nor does it become attached to anyone else in the world. // 2 //
My mind is not repelled, nor is it attracted toward any being; I harbor neither enmity nor fault toward anyone, for my mind is devoted to the welfare of all. // 3 //
When you, O Prince, were seen—possessing supreme beauty and strength, and endowed with virtues—then all my senses were delighted, and a vast joy arose within me. (4)
O you with pure, radiant, jewel-like golden hair, beautifully curled and deep blue; O you with beautiful eyebrows, a lovely forehead, and a fine nose—to you, I offer this very self. 5.
Bearing the marks of excellence, possessed of great splendor, and with a form resembling a mountain of gold, you shine before me; I appear darkened, like a mere lump of ink.
With eyes like great lotuses of deep blue, with a face perfectly full and a lion-like gait, your speech is never obstructed; O one of supreme voice, please accept my offering. (7)
In your mouth, O tongue, you are abundant, copper-colored and slender, vast and radiant as a jewel;
with the excellent Brahma-voice and the beautiful resonance of its components, you gladden the world as you speak. // 8 //

In your mouth, O Hero among Men, your teeth are harmonious, resembling conch shells, stainless, and well-spaced; by displaying them while manifesting a smile, you bring satisfaction to the multitude. 9.
O you whose body is beautiful with the marks, it is radiant and pure even now;
adorned with these, you will become a handsome wheel-turning monarch, a lord of men. (10)
Then the prince Tejodhipati said this to the girl Sucalitaratiprabhāsaśrī: "Whose daughter are you, girl?
Or who is your protector?
It is not fitting for me, girl, to conceive a sense of ownership over a wife already taken by another."
At that time, he spoke these verses:

“O Sudarśanā, endowed with the qualities of beauty, possessed of auspicious marks, and having a body purified by merit—I ask you, tell me this matter: O lady of exquisite limbs, whose wife are you? (11)

Do you perhaps have a mother or a father, or a husband, or a master, or a wife? Or is there indeed some other being by whom the notion "this is mine" has been formed toward you, who possess such a gentle appearance? (12)
I hope that your mind does not delight in violence; indeed, do not take what belongs to others.
