The sky was adorned with canopies of all kinds of jewels and garments spread out above; it was covered by a net of all kinds of jewels; it resounded with the sounds of vajra-banners well-arranged in every direction; it was illuminated by the gentle movement of banners with ribbons of all kinds of jewels; it was decorated with the uniform adornment of banners featuring the finest of all fragrant jewel-kings;

it rained down a profusion of various flowers, incense, and diverse blossoms; and it produced a sweet sound, pleasing to the ear and mind, from the gentle movement of banners with all kinds of jewel-bells.

It was arrayed with palace doors and gateways fashioned from various jewels; it was adorned with networks of lotuses on the faces of lordly elephants, whose forms were composed of various jewel-gems and who emitted many-colored fragrant waters from their mouths that increased the splendor of the Vairocana-jewel kings;

it was arrayed with clouds of incense of infinite colors from the mouths of various vajra-lions; it emitted the resonant sounds of the Brahma-voice through the gateway of the great method of universal love from the faces of the Vairocana-jewel kings situated in the Brahma-abode; and it produced sweet-sounding proclamations from golden bell-strings bearing the names of the Buddhas of the three times, which were colored by the sweet resonance of the light of the bright fortnight emanating from the faces of various jewels and silver.

It resounded with the delightful sounds of rows of bells made of the great jewel-kings of the wheel of all Buddha-dharmas; it emitted the resonance of various vajra-bells arising from the vows of all bodhisattvas; it proclaimed through the names of rows of moon-bannered jewel-kings the manifestation of the reflections of all Buddhas; it manifested through rows of pure-womb jewel-kings the succession of births of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times; and it was adorned with rows of sun-womb jewel-kings.

A row of king-jewels named Illuminating Banner, which display rays of light along the paths of all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, reaching as far as the realm of space through the practice of all miraculous transformations;

a row of king-jewels named Vairocana, which emit the radiance of the light-mandalas of all Tathāgatas; and [a row] that emits clouds of emanations resembling the lords of all worlds to perform worship and service to the Tathāgatas.

He saw that seat, which was surrounded by an array of inconceivable jewels, and featured rows of wish-fulfilling gem-kings that at every moment pervaded the entire realm of phenomena through the miraculous transformations of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; rows of Merudhvaja gem-kings that resounded with the thunderous cries and songs of the Apsarases from the clouds of the palaces of all the lords of gods; and which proclaimed an exposition of inconceivable qualities and praises by emitting clouds of hymns of praise for the Tathāgatas directed toward all objects of perception.
And on that seat he saw Queen Māyā seated, with a form that transcends the three worlds,
a form that faces all worlds and has emerged from all states of existence,
a form manifested to the world according to its inclinations and unsullied by any worldly realm.
With a form produced from a vast accumulation of merit, resembling all the worlds;
with a form that manifests happiness for all beings and accords with the ripening and disciplining of the entire world;
with a form that extends toward all beings and is inseparable from the manifestation of the world throughout all time in space.
By means of the empowerment of the communication that culminates in the entire world, through a form that is without going,
through a form that goes to all worlds, and through a form that has ceased all worldly going and is without coming;
By means of a form that has not arisen in all the world, an unproduced form;
by means of a form that is unceasing, delighting in the dharma of non-arising;
by means of a form that is unreal, transcending all worldly conventions.
By means of a form that is attained as it truly is and is not false; by means of a form that is unassailed and is made known according to the world;
by means of a form that has ceased from death and rebirth and is indestructible.
By means of a form that is without characteristics due to the indestructibility of the nature of the *dharmadhātu*;

by means of a form characterized by a single characteristic, which transcends the paths of speech throughout the three times; and by means of a form resembling a reflection, which has emerged from the well-defined characteristics of the absence of characteristics.
By means of a form that informs the minds of all beings according to their inclinations, which is like an illusion;
by means of a form perfected through the illusion of gnosis, which is like a mirage;
and by means of a form resembling a shadow, which is the supreme basis for the perceptions of the world at every moment.

With a form that follows all worlds through his vow, like a dream; with a form that reaches the furthest limits of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), undifferentiated by the perceptions of beings according to their inclinations;
and with a form that is naturally pure as the realm of space and has emerged from great compassion.
With a form dedicated to the protection of the lineage of sentient beings, emerging through the gateway of non-attachment;
with a form that is infinite and centerless, pervading the realm of phenomena at every moment;
with an immeasurable form, free from turbidity, which serves as a refuge for all the world.
With a form that is well-established, having completely transcended all paths of speech;
with a form that is non-dependent, having been brought forth through the empowerment of the discipline of all worlds;
with an unobstructed form, engaged in the bodies of the world through empowerment.
With a form perfected through the illusion of aspiration and remaining unconquered; with a form that has transcended all worlds yet is not as it appears;
with a form manifested by the light of tranquility and being non-existent.
With a form resembling a wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi-rāja) that follows the world according to its karma;

with a non-conceptual form that fulfills the intentions of all sentient beings according to their inclinations by fulfilling their vows; and with a non-conceptual form manifested through the conceptualizations of the entire world.

By means of a form that is non-conceptual regarding the manifestation of the entire world through empowerment, by means of a pure form that is supreme in its non-cessation from saṃsāra, and which is non-discriminative and equal to suchness.

In this manner, the merchant’s son Sudhana beheld Queen Māyā in a form that was a manifestation of form without being form, a form characterized by the supreme pacification of the sufferings felt by the world, a form transcending all conceptualizations regarding sentient beings, a form made known through the conceptualizations of other beings,
a form issued from the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) free from volitional construction (*anabhisaṃskāra*), and a form turned away from karma that has become like an illusion.

With a form that transcends the objects of consciousness, born from the wisdom of the Bodhisattva’s vow; with a form that is without intrinsic nature, a body that has reached the limit of all paths of speech in the world;
with a form that, though extinguished by the torments of saṃsāra, has attained the supreme coolness of the Dharmakāya—she manifested a form-body according to the inclinations of the world.
By the power of the inclinations of sentient beings, she manifested a form-body that resembled all the worlds and yet transcended the form-bodies of all the worlds.

Therein, some beings saw the Goddess Māyā in the form of a Māra-maiden, yet with a form surpassing that of a Māra-maiden; some beings saw her with a form surpassing the Apsarases of the Vaśavartin heaven; some with a form surpassing the Apsarases of the Sunirmita heaven; and some with a form surpassing the Apsarases of the Saṃtuṣita heaven.

Some beings saw Queen Māyā in a form surpassing the apsarases of the Suyāma heaven; some in a form surpassing the apsarases of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven; some in a form surpassing the apsarases of the Cāturmahārājika heaven; some in a form surpassing the daughters of the Kumbhāṇḍa lords; some in a form surpassing the daughters of the Mahoraga lords; and some beings saw Queen Māyā in a form surpassing the daughters of the lords of men.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having transcended the perception of the forms of all worlds and not entering into the inclinations of other beings,

beheld Queen Māyā within the range of the mental inclinations of all sentient beings— she who is the merit upon which the entire world depends, whose body is accumulated with the merit of omniscience, who practices the perfection of generosity without interruption, who has attained equanimity toward all worlds, who is the assembly hall of great compassion where all beings converge, and who has emerged from the practice of the qualities of all Tathāgatas.

She had entered the ocean of all methods of patience; her intention was increased by the force of the vigor for omniscience; her vigor was irreversible due to the purity of the mandala of all phenomena; she had emerged from the contemplation of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena; her mind was perfected in the method of the factors of all meditations; she had attained the illumination of the Tathāgata’s mandala of meditation, which is uncommon and possesses the domain of undifferentiated factors of meditation; she was supreme in the various contemplations and resolutions for drying up the ocean of afflictions of all sentient beings; and she knew the procedures for investigating the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.

She possesses the wisdom that investigates the ocean of the principles of all dharmas; she is never satiated by beholding all the Tathāgatas; she is unceasing in her contemplation of the succession of Tathāgatas throughout the three periods of time;

she is oriented toward the gateway for seeing all Buddhas; she knows the methods for the various degrees of purification of the path to the realization of all Tathāgatas; she has the sky as her domain regarding all Tathāgatas; she knows the methods for the means of gathering all sentient beings; and she has attained the manifestation of ripening and disciplining the world according to its infinite and boundless inclinations.
She has entered into the various degrees of purity of the bodies of all Buddhas; she is endowed with the vow for the complete purification of oceans of all buddha-fields;

her vow is purified by its culmination in the empowerment that disciplines the entire realm of sentient beings; her mind radiates offerings throughout the domain of all Tathāgatas; she has emerged from the vigor of the miraculous transformations of all bodhisattvas; she is purified by the unsurpassed Dharma-body; and she manifests in infinite forms of physical bodies.

She who crushes the power of all Māras; who is endowed with the power of vast roots of goodness; who has attained the illumination of the power of the Buddhas through an intellect born from the power of the Dharma; who is perfected by the power of the sovereignty of all Bodhisattvas; who is born from the impetus-power of omniscience; who is illuminated by the lightning-flash of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas; whose wisdom ranges across the ocean of the minds of infinite and middleless sentient beings; who has entered into the vast intentions of the world; who knows the methods and rules for discerning the differences in the faculties of other beings; and who follows after skill in the knowledge of the differences in the inclinations of infinite sentient beings.

She whose body pervades the oceans of immeasurable realms in the ten directions; she who knows the methods and rules for the wisdom regarding the diversity of all world-systems; she who has attained skill in the methods and rules for the differentiation of all realms; she whose vision of wisdom extends throughout the oceans of all directions;

she whose intellect extends through the oceans of all times; she whose body bows in prostration toward the oceans of all Buddhas; and whose mind is intent upon receiving the oceans of clouds of all Buddha-dharmas.
She is intent on the practice of fulfilling all the qualities of the Tathāgatas; her intellect has extended into the arising of all the provisions for enlightenment;

she has mastered the courageous strides of investigating all the bodhisattva paths; she is fully perfected in all the factors for generating the thought of enlightenment; she is dedicated to the protection of all sentient beings; she radiates the light of clouds of praise from all the Buddhas; and she has emerged from the vows that give birth to all bodhisattvas and Jinas.

With these and other modes of vision, as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa, the merchant’s son Sudhana beheld Queen Māyā. Having seen her, he empowered his own body to become the same size as Queen Māyā, and with a body that followed her everywhere, he prostrated before Queen Māyā, who was facing all directions.
As he prostrated himself, infinite and intermediate gateways of meditative concentration (*samādhimukha*) entered him.

Having surveyed those gateways of meditative concentration, having rendered them signless, having cultivated them, having made them essential, having recollected them, having pervaded them, having extended them, having observed them, having expanded them, having brought them forth, and having sealed them, he emerged from those gateways of meditative concentration.
Having circumambulated Queen Māyā together with her retinue, her palace, and her seat, and standing before her with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus:
"Noble Lady, having resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, I was exhorted by the youthful Mañjuśrī to attend upon spiritual friends.
While attending upon those spiritual friends, I have gradually proceeded until I have now come into your presence."
"May the Noble Lady tell me this: how does a bodhisattva, training in the conduct of a bodhisattva, become perfected in omniscience?
She replied, "Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called 'The Array of the Illusory Manifestation of the Knowledge of Great Vows.
Endowed with this liberation, noble son, [I perceive] as many [Buddhas] of the Blessed One as there are in this ocean of world-systems."
The miraculous displays of the birth of Bodhisattvas in their final existence proceed throughout all world-systems and all Jambudvīpas of Vairocana;
and I am the mother of all those Bodhisattvas in their final existence,
for all those Bodhisattvas are conceived within my womb.
They emerge from my right side.

Here, noble son, in this very world-system of four continents, in the great city of Kapilavastu, I gave birth to the Bodhisattva Siddhārtha as a kinsman of King Śuddhodana, through a great and inconceivable [manifestation].
By means of the miraculous manifestation of the birth of a bodhisattva.

Indeed, noble son, at that time I was staying in the palace of King Śuddhodana. Then, when the moment for the Bodhisattva’s descent from the Tuṣita heaven had arrived, from every single pore of his body there issued forth arrays of the qualities and methods of all the mothers of Bodhisattvas, equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields.

Rays of light named "Radiance Arising from the Mandala of Qualities of the Mother of All Tathāgatas" issued forth; having illuminated the entire world-system, they fell upon my body and, entering through the crown of my head, permeated all my pores.

As soon as those bodhisattva rays had entered, O son of good family, they—bearing many names and emitting the magnificent displays of the miraculous transformations of the various mothers of bodhisattvas—[permeated me].

Then, at that very moment, within my body, there appeared all the arrays of the methods for the miraculous displays of the births of Bodhisattvas, as manifested by the circles of the faces of the Bodhisattva rays.

As soon as those Bodhisattva rays had entered my body along with their retinues, O noble son, there immediately appeared before those Bodhisattvas for whom those circles of the faces of the Bodhisattva rays were manifested, the miraculous displays of their modes of birth.
All of them came within the range of my vision;

that is to say, those lions of Buddhas seated upon the lion-thrones at the supreme and excellent site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), surrounded by circles of bodhisattva assemblies, honored by the lords of the world, and turning the wheel of Dharma;
and also those Tathāgatas whom those [Buddhas], while formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, had pleased.
All of them also came within the range of my vision:

their manifestations from the first production of the thought of enlightenment, their manifestations of the attainment of perfect awakening, the turning of the wheel of Dharma, and final nirvana; the pure arrays of all Buddha-fields;
and those emanation-mandalas of those Tathāgatas which, moment by moment, pervade the entire realm of phenomena.
All of those, too, came within the range of my vision.
Noble son, as those bodhisattva rays entered my body, my body became established as one that transcends all worlds, and my womb became as vast as the realm of space.
Nor did it exceed the physical proportions of a human body;

and all the magnificent arrays of the palaces where Bodhisattvas dwell in their wombs throughout the ten directions were entirely contained within my body, having entered therein, and were all clearly visible.
And as soon as I had appeared, noble son, within my body— which was an array of enjoyments consisting of a palace for dwelling in the womb of a bodhisattva—

there immediately appeared a bodhisattva together with bodhisattvas equal in number to the atoms in ten buddha-fields, who shared a single vow, practiced similar conduct, and possessed identical roots of virtue.

He was being honored by eighty thousand lords of the *nāgas*, headed by Sāgara the *nāga* king, as well as by thousands of lords of all the worlds— all of whom dwelt in a single array, abided in a single liberation, resided on the level of a single gnosis, emerged through a single miraculous transformation, had perfected a single vow, were consummated in a single conduct, were purified in their *dharmakāya*, possessed empowerments of form-bodies without end or middle, and had emerged through the miraculous transformations of the vows and conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and who were situated within jeweled gabled palaces like the womb of the lord of *nāgas*.

By means of a great bodhisattva-transformation—manifesting the descent from every Tuṣita abode; manifesting the attainment of birth in the four continents extending throughout all world-systems from each individual Tuṣita abode; accompanied by inconceivable skill in means for the ripening of sentient beings;
exhorting all heedless sentient beings; shaking off all attachments; and emitting a great net of light rays—
Having dispelled the darkness of all worlds, stilled the suffering of all states of woe, turned back all rebirth in the hells,

exhorted all beings toward their former karma, protected the realm of all sentient beings, and manifested his body before all beings, he descended from the Tuṣita heaven and entered my womb together with his retinue.

All of them moved about within my womb with strides that spanned the vastness of the triple-thousandfold world system, up to the vastness of world systems as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
and they visited all the circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas at the feet of all the Tathāgatas throughout the entire expanse of world systems in the ten directions.
In every moment of thought, inexpressible numbers [of beings] would enter my womb to behold the miraculous manifestation of the Bodhisattva’s dwelling in the womb.
Furthermore, the four Great Kings, the lords of the gods— Śakra, Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, Sunirmita, and Vaśavartin— as well as the Indras of the Brahma realms,
would approach the Bodhisattva who had entered the womb in order to see him, pay homage to him, and attend upon him.
For the sake of hearing the Dharma and for the sake of experiencing discourse,
my womb does not expand to accommodate such vast circles of assemblies;
nor does this body of mine become more distinguished than this human frame.
He receives all those assemblies of such magnitude,
and all those gods and humans behold various arrays of the pure enjoyments of bodhisattvas;
for what reason is that?
This was because he had well-expounded that very great vow, which is the bodhisattva liberation known as "Arrived at Illusion."
And just as I, noble son, receive the Bodhisattva within my womb here in Jambudvīpa of this Bhāgavatī four-continent world system,

so too do I receive him in all the Jambudvīpas of every four-continent world system throughout the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system by means of this array of miraculous transformations;
yet this body of mine neither becomes dual nor does it become non-dual.
It abides neither in unity nor in multiplicity,
precisely because of the well-spoken nature of this very Bodhisattva liberation that has reached the illusory state of the knowledge of great vows.
And just as, noble son, I became the mother of this Blessed One Vairocana, so too [is it].
Likewise, I have been the mother of the infinite and middleless Tathāgatas of the past;
wherever a Bodhisattva was born in the world by apparitional birth within the heart of a lotus, there I became the goddess Nalinī and received the Bodhisattva.
And the world perceives me as the mother of the Bodhisattva;
wherever he appeared in my lap, there I became his mother.
"In whichever Buddha-field he appears, there I shall become a deity of the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa).
Thus, noble son, by whatever means and gateways bodhisattvas in their final existence manifest their birth in the world, [I shall assist them].
By means of that many approaches to skillful methods, I become the mother of Bodhisattvas.

Just as I, noble son, have been the mother in this world-system during all the manifestations of the miraculous births of bodhisattvas for this Blessed One, so too was I the mother for the Tathāgata Krakucchanda and for Kanakamuni.
I became the mother of the Tathāgata Kāśyapa; likewise, I shall become the mother of all the future Tathāgatas of the Bhadrakalpa.
For example, when the time for the manifestation of the descent [from heaven] had arrived for the Bodhisattva Maitreya while he was in the Tuṣita abode,
and when the light-ray called "Illumination Manifesting the Miraculous Display of the Birth, Conception, and Dwelling in the Womb of All Bodhisattvas" was emitted,
all the bases of the methods of the Dharma-realm were illuminated; as many of those bases of the methods of the Dharma-realm as belong to me came within the range of my vision.
I shall appear in all those places where the Bodhisattva Maitreya must manifest birth and rebirth within the human world among the families of human lords in order to discipline sentient beings;
in all of them, I shall be the mother of the Bodhisattva.

And as it is with the bodhisattva Maitreya, so it is with Siṃha, who will attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment immediately after Maitreya; and likewise with Pradyota, Keta, Sunetra, Kusuma, Kusumaśrī, Tiṣya, Puṣya, and Sumanas.
Of Vajra, Viraja, Candrolkādhārin, Yaśas, Vajraśuddha, Ekārthadarśin, Sitāṅga, Pāraṃgata, Ratnārciḥparvata, Maholkādhārin, Padmottara, Vighuṣṭaśabda, Aparimitaguṇadharma,
Dīpaśrī, Vibhūṣitāṅga, Suprayāṇa, Maitraśrī, Nirmita, Aniketa, and Jvalitatejas.
Of Anantaghoṣa, Aninema, Aninetra, Vimativikiraṇa, Pariśuddha, Suviśālābha, Yaśaḥśuddhodita, Meghaśrī, Vicitrabhūta, Sarvaratnavicitravarṇamaṇikuṇḍala,
Sāgaramati, Śubharatna, Anihatamalla, Paripūrṇamanoratha, Maheśvara, and Indraśrī.
Of Agniśrī, Candanamedha, Sitaviśālākṣa, Śreṣṭhamati, Vibhāvitamati, Avaropaṇarāja, Uttāpanarājamati, Vibhūṣita, Vibhūti,
Keśaranandin, Īśvaradeva, Īśvara, Uṣṇīṣaśrī, Vajrajñānaparvata, Śrīgarbha,
Kanakajālakāyavibhūṣita, Suvibhakta, Īśvaradeva, Mahendradeva, and Anilaśrī.
Of Viśuddhanandin, Arciṣmat, Varuṇaśrī, Viśuddhamati, Agrayāna, Nihitaguṇodita, Arigupta, Vākyanuda, Vaśībhūta, Guṇatejas, Vairocanaketu, Vibhavagandha,
Vibhāvanagandha, Vibhaktāṅga, Suviśākha, Sarvagandhārcimukha, and Vajramaṇivicitra.
Of Prahasitanetra, Nihatarāgarajas, Pravṛddhakāyarāja, Vāsudeva, Udāradeva, Nirodhanimna, Vibuddhi, Dhūtarajas, Arcirmahendra, Upaśamavat,
Viśākhadeva, Vajragira, Jñānārcijvalitaśarīra, Kṣemaṃkara, Aupagama, and Śārdūla.
Of Paripūrṇaśubha, Rucirabhadrayaśas, Parākramavikrama, Paramārthavikrāmin, Śāntaraśmi, Ekokttara, Gambhīreśvara, Bhūmimati, Asita, Ghoṣaśrī, Viśiṣṭa, Vibhūtapati, Vibhūtabhūta,
Vaidyottama, Guṇacandra, Praharṣitatejas, Guṇasaṃcaya, Candrodgata, and Bhāskaradeva.
Of Bhīṣmayaśas, Raśmimukha, Śālendraskandha, Yaśas, Auṣadhirāja, Ratnavara, Vajramati, Sitaśrī, Nirghotālaya, Maṇirāja, Mahāyaśas, Vegadhārin, Amitābha,
Mahāsanārcis, Mohadharmeśvara, Nihatadhīra, Devaśuddha, Dṛḍhaprabha, and Viśvāmitra.

Vimuktighoṣa, Vinarditarāja, Vākyaccheda, Campakavimalaprabha, Anavadya, Viśiṣṭacandra, Ulkādhārin, Vicitragātra, Anabhilāpyodgata, Jaganmitra, Prabhūtaraśmi, Svarāṅgaśūra, Karuṇāvṛkṣa, Dhṛtamati-tejas, Kundaśrī, Arciścandra, Anihitamati, and Anunayavigata.
Of one whose mind is without objective support, who has accumulated the aggregates, who crushes the states of woe, who possesses undepressed flowers, who roars like a lion,
whose purpose is never diminished, who sees without obstruction, who crushes the hosts of others, who has wheels like the wind, who is unshakable as the ocean, and who is a beautiful ocean.
Of Aparājitameru, Anilayajñāna, Anantāsana, Yudhiṣṭhira, Caryāgata, Uttaradatta, Atyantacandramas, Anugrahacandra, Acalaskandha, Agrasānumati, Anugrahamati, Abhyuddhara,
Arcitanamasyānupagamananāman, Nihatatejas, Viśvavarṇa, Animittaprajña, and Acaladeva.

Of the Bodhisattva Acintyaśrī, Vimokṣacandra, Anuttararāja, Candraskandhārcitabrahman, Akampyanetra, Anunayagātra, Abhyudgatakarma, Anudharmamati, Anuttaraśrī, Brahmadeva, Acintyaguṇānuttaradharmagocara, Aparyantabhadra, Anurūpasvara, and Abhyuccadeva.

Thus, noble son, having placed these future Tathāgatas headed by Maitreya at the forefront, I alone shall be the mother of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the Fortunate Aeon within this triple-thousand great-thousand world system.
And just as it is here in this world-system,

so too in the immeasurable world-systems in the ten directions, entering into the methods of the dharma-realm that are without end or middle— just as I am the mother of the Tathāgata Maitreya through his inexpressible special qualities,
so shall I be the mother of the Tathāgata Siṃha through his inexpressible special qualities, and likewise up to the Tathāgata Rocama.
And just as it was for the Tathāgatas of the Fortunate Aeon, so too, in this ocean of world-systems called Sarvāvati Kusumatalagarbhavyūhālaṃkāra— in all lineages of world-systems,
in all expansions of world-systems, in all world-systems, and in all Jambudvīpas throughout kalpas reaching to the furthest limit— [it was thus].
Practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva in the Samantabhadra way, and by means of my empowerment for the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings throughout all eons,
I shall become the mother of all future Tathāgatas while they are still Bodhisattvas.

When this had been said, the merchant’s son Sudhana said to Queen Māyā: "Noble lady, how long ago did you attain this bodhisattva liberation called the Array of the Magical Manifestation of the Knowledge of Great Vows?

She replied: "In the past, noble son, in a time gone by, beyond inconceivable eons that transcend the sphere of thought, that are perceived only by the range of the vision of noble bodhisattvas, and that exceed the calculation of consciousnesses—further back than that—there was an eon named Śubhaprabha."

Furthermore, in that eon called Śubhaprabha, there was a world-system named Merūdgataśrī, which was both pure and defiled, composed of many jewels, including its surrounding mountain ranges, Mount Sumeru, and the oceans; it contained the movements of the five realms of existence and was variegated and beautiful to behold.
In that world-system Merūdgataśrī, there were ten hundred billion sets of four continents.
In the midst of those one hundred billion four-continent systems, there was a central four-continent system named Siṃhadhvajāgratejas, in which there were eight billion royal capitals.
In the midst of those eight billion royal capitals, there was a central royal capital named Dhvajāgravatī.
In that city there was a universal monarch named Mahātejaḥparākrama.
Furthermore, in that capital city named Dhvajāgravatī, there was a seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) called Citramañjariprabhāsa.
There, a deity of the seat of enlightenment named Netraśrī resided.
Furthermore, on that very seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) called Citramañjariprabhāsa, a bodhisattva named Vimaladhvaja was seated for the sake of attaining the qualities of omniscience.
To obstruct his attainment of the qualities of omniscience, a Māra named Suvarṇaprabha, accompanied by a vast army, approached him with his body made invisible.
That Māra possessed great majesty and prowess, had attained the masteries (vaśitā) of a bodhisattva, and was skilled in the manifestation of great miraculous transformations.
Then, having conjured a great host of beings even more vast and more formidable than that great army, he surrounded the seat of awakening on all sides in order to defeat Māra’s forces.
By him, indeed, the great army of Māra was scattered;
and by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vimaladhvaja, unexcelled perfect awakening was fully realized.
Then indeed, the goddess Netraśrī of the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), having conceived the notion of him as her son in the presence of the universal monarch Mahātejaḥparākrama,
prostrated at the feet of that Tathāgata and made this aspiration: "Blessed One, wherever I may be reborn,
may this universal monarch Mahātejaḥparākrama be my son there."
"And when he awakens to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment,
may I then become his mother.
Having made this vow, she pleased ten million *nayutas* of Tathāgatas at that very seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) called Citramañjariprabhāsa, during that very eon called Śubhaprabha.
"What do you think, noble son—was that goddess of the seat of awakening named Netraśrī at that time and on that occasion someone else?
Indeed, noble son, you should not view it in such a way.
At that time and on that occasion, I myself was that goddess of the seat of awakening named Netraśrī."

What do you think, noble son— was he someone else at that time, on that occasion, who was the universal monarch named Mahātejaḥparākrama, who had attained mastery over bodhisattvas and emerged with the display of great supernatural powers, by whom that vast army of Māra was scattered?
Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way.
This very Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, was at that time and on that occasion a universal monarch named Mahātejaḥparākrama.
From that point onward, O son of good family, wherever I was reborn, I [was always his daughter].

Everywhere he has attained the status of my son; while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva in all buddha-fields, in all gateways of destiny, in all gateways of rebirth, in all gateways of roots of goodness, in all the exertions and investigations of bodhisattva conduct, in all the methods of birth-stories, in all births as lords of gods, in all states as lords of the world, on all levels of sovereignty, and in all divisions of destinies.
Wherever he was reborn for the sake of maturing sentient beings,
in every instance I alone became his mother;
and in his final existence, I alone followed him everywhere as his mother.
In every moment, throughout all the gateways of the births of all bodhisattvas, as many miraculous displays of bodhisattva births as he manifested,
in every instance I alone was his mother;
and so too for the Tathāgatas of the past.
I have been the mother of infinite and immeasurable [Buddhas] without end or middle;
even now, I experience the role of mother for the infinite and immeasurable Tathāgatas of the present throughout the ten directions.
Furthermore, for as many Tathāgatas as there are, I was their Bodhisattva-mother in their final existence.
And from the circles of the navels of all those Tathāgatas, rays of light issued forth, illuminating their great bodies and their seats.
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "The Array of the Magical Manifestation of the Knowledge of Great Vows.
How could I possibly describe the bodhisattvas who have great compassion as their core, whose wombs are never satiated by the ripening and disciplining of others for omniscience?

[It is impossible] for anyone to know his conduct or describe his virtues, except for one who possesses mastery over the manifestation of the emergence from every pore of the body through the miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas.
Go, noble son;
right here in this very abode of the Lord of the Thirty-three, there is a daughter of the gods named Surendrābhā, the daughter of the divine son Smṛtimat.
Approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of Queen Māyā, circumambulated Queen Māyā hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at her again and again, departed from Queen Māyā’s presence.

(Gv 350) 45. Surendrābhā. Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana went toward the palace of the Lord of the Thirty-three, and toward the divine maiden Surendrābhā, the daughter of the divine son Smṛtimat.
He approached her;

having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the celestial maiden Surendrābhā, circumambulated the celestial maiden Surendrābhā hundreds of thousands of times, and standing before the celestial maiden Surendrābhā with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus: "By me..."
Noble lady, I have generated the mind set upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it.
"I have heard, Noble Lady, that you give instruction and counsel to the bodhisattvas.
Therefore, O Goddess, tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, and how should they practice?"

When this had been said, a daughter of the gods named Surendrābhā spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Noble son, I am a possessor of the bodhisattva liberation called ‘Array of Pure Unimpeded Recollection. Noble son, I remember that there was a kalpa named Utpalaka;
therein, I propitiated as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges."
As they were departing, protection was provided for them,
worship was performed,
and pleasure groves were prepared for their enjoyment.

And whatever display of all the Buddha-miracles was performed by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, while they were still Bodhisattvas— whether while in their mother’s womb, at the time of birth, when taking the seven steps, when uttering the great lion’s roar, while remaining in the stage of youth, while in the midst of the inner apartments, when departing the city, when awakening to perfect enlightenment, or when turning the wheel of Dharma.

Or by those who displayed [such deeds], the ripening and disciplining of sentient beings was accomplished; all of that—from the first production of the thought of awakening until the final conclusion of the True Dharma—I know, remember, recollect, retain, preserve, maintain, and follow.
There was an eon named Subhūti.
There, I pleased as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in ten Ganges rivers.
There was an eon named Subhaga, where I pleased as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a Buddha-field.
There was an eon named Anilambha.
There, I propitiated eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of Buddhas.
There was an eon named Suprabha; there, I propitiated Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa.
There was an eon named Atulaprabha.
There, I pleased as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in twenty Ganges rivers.
There was an eon named Utaptaśrī;
therein, I pleased as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges river.
There was an eon named Sūryodaya;
therein, I propitiated as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in eighty Ganges rivers.
There was also an eon named Jayaṃgama.
There, I pleased as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in sixty Ganges rivers.
There was an eon named Sucandra;
therein, I pleased as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in seventy Ganges rivers.

Thus, noble son, by this means I recall as many eons as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges, during which I was constantly and continuously never separated from the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.
And from the presence of all those Tathāgatas, I heard this bodhisattva liberation called the Array of Unimpeded Pure Recollection.
Having heard it, I have honored it and practiced according to what was taught.

Thus, I have constantly and continuously entered this liberation; and by means of this array of pure, unattached mindfulness, I have realized all the Buddha-transformations of those Tathāgatas, beginning from their stage as Bodhisattvas up to the final limit of the endurance of the True Dharma.
By means of this bodhisattva liberation, I recollect, maintain, thoroughly maintain, uphold, and keep in mind;
this, noble son, is the bodhisattva liberation that I know.

How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the virtues of the Bodhisattvas— who have departed from the darkness of ignorance, who have brought forth light during the night of saṃsāra, who are free from hindrances, who do not succumb to sleep, who are devoid of sloth and torpor, whose bodily formations are tranquilized, who are perfectly pure through their awakening to the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, and who awaken others to the purity of the ten powers?
Go, noble son; in the great city of Kapilavastu there dwells a teacher of boys named Viśvāmitra. Approach him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?

Then Sudhana the merchant’s son, joyful, elated, uplifted in mind, filled with gladness and happiness, his impetus of inconceivable roots of merit further increased, bowed his head at the feet of the celestial maiden Surendrābhā; having circumambulated the celestial maiden Surendrābhā hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at her again and again, he departed from the presence of the celestial maiden Surendrābhā. 43.
(Gv 352) 46. Viśvāmitra.

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, descending from the palace of the Lord of the Thirty-three, proceeded by stages until he arrived at the great city of Kapilavastu, where he approached the teacher of boys, Viśvāmitra.

Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of Viśvāmitra, the teacher of the boys, and having circumambulated Viśvāmitra, the teacher of the boys, hundreds of thousands of times, he stood before Viśvāmitra, the teacher of the boys, with palms joined in reverence and spoke thus: "Noble sir, I have generated the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
Yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it.
I have heard, however, that the Noble One gives instruction and advice to bodhisattvas.
"May the Noble One tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, and how should he practice?

When this was said, Viśvāmitra, the teacher of the boys, spoke thus to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Noble son, this merchant’s son named Śilpābhijña has been taught the knowledge of scripts by the Bodhisattva."
Go to him and ask;
he will instruct you in how one should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva and how one should practice. // 44 //
(47) Skilled in the Arts. Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son approached the merchant’s son Śilpābhijña.

Having bowed his head at the feet of the merchant’s son Śilpābhijña and standing before him with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus: "Noble sir, I have resolved my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva."

How should I practice? I have heard, noble one, that you give instruction and advice to the bodhisattvas; therefore, may the noble one tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?
He said: "Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation called 'Mastery of Arts.

Noble son, as I was reciting its matrix (*mātṛkā*) and pronouncing the syllable 'A,' through the power of the bodhisattvas, I entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called 'Undifferentiated Domain. As I pronounced the syllable 'Ra,' I entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called 'Infinite Extent and Differentiation.'"
As he recited the syllable *pa*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the penetration of the depths of the realm of phenomena" (*dharmadhātutalasaṃbheda*).

As he recited the syllable *ca*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the severing of the differentiation of the universal wheel" (*samantacakravibhakticchedana*). As he recited the syllable *na*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "attaining the state of no-abode" (*anilayapratilabdha*).
As he proclaimed the letter *la*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Stainless and Free from Attachment.
As he proclaimed the letter *da*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Application of Non-retrogression.
As he proclaimed the letter *ba*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Diamond Mandala."

As he proclaimed the syllable *ḍa*, the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "The Universal Wheel" was entered. As he proclaimed the syllable *sa*, the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "The Womb of the Ocean" was entered.
As he proclaimed the syllable *va*, the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "The Manifestation of Universal Growth" was entered.
As he proclaimed the letter *ta*, the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Sphere of Light" (*jyotirmaṇḍala*) entered him.

As he proclaimed the letter *ya*, the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Peak of Differentiation" (*saṃbhedakūṭa*) entered him. As he proclaimed the letter *ṣṭa*, the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Radiance that Pacifies Universal Burning" (*samantadāhapraśamanaprabhāsa*) entered him.

As he proclaimed the letter *ka*, he entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Uninterrupted Cloud. As he proclaimed the letter *ṣa*, he entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Hanging Down the Rain of the Face-to-Face.
As he proclaimed the letter *ma*, he entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "The Peak of Great and Variegated Speed."
As he fully proclaimed the syllable *ga*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the manifestation of the universal foundation.

As he fully proclaimed the syllable *tha*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the womb of the indivisibility of suchness. As he fully proclaimed the syllable *ja*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "penetrating the purification of the world’s saṃsāra."

As he proclaimed the syllable *sva*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the Array of the Recollection of All Buddhas. As he proclaimed the syllable *dha*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the Investigation and Analysis of the Mandala of Dharma.
As he proclaimed the syllable *śa*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called the Radiance of the Wheel of the Instruction of All Buddhas.
As he fully proclaimed the syllable *kha*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Matrix of Knowledge Regarding the Ground of Formative Causes.

As he fully proclaimed the syllable *kṣa*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Discernment of the Treasury of the Ocean of Quiescent Karma. As he fully proclaimed the syllable *sta*, he entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Radiance of Purity through the Dispelling of All Afflictions."
As he fully proclaimed the syllable *ña*, there entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called the "Gate of the Cognition of the Arising of the World.

As he fully proclaimed the syllable *tha*, there entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called the "Mandala of Knowledge that Turns Back Saṃsāra. As he fully proclaimed the syllable *bha*, [there entered] the "Array of the Cognition of All Mandalas of Abodes."
The gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "Entering" was entered.

For one who proclaims the syllable *cha*, the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Distinction of the Circle of the Parasol of Conduct through the Application of the Womb of Accumulation" was entered.
For one who proclaims the syllable *sma*...
One enters the gateway of the perfection of wisdom called "the whirlpool facing the directions where all Buddhas are seen.

For one who fully pronounces the syllable *hva*, one enters the gateway of the perfection of wisdom called "the womb born from the power of beholding the unfitness of all sentient beings. For one who fully pronounces the syllable *tsa*, one enters the gateway of the perfection of wisdom called "the plunging into the entry into the practice of the ocean of all virtues."
As he fully proclaimed the syllable *gha*, he entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "the firm ocean-womb that sustains the clouds of all dharmas.
As he fully proclaimed the syllable *ṭha*, he entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "proceeding toward the directions of the vows of all Buddhas.
As he fully proclaimed the syllable *ṇa*, he entered the gate of the perfection of wisdom called "the expression of ten million forms of the letters of the wheel."
As he proclaimed the syllable *pha*, there entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the mandala reaching the limit of the ripening of all sentient beings.
As he proclaimed the syllable *ska*, there entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the radiance-wheel of the unimpeded analytical knowledges within the womb of the stages.
As he proclaimed the syllable *sya*, there entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "the domain of the teaching of all Buddha-dharmas."
As he proclaimed the syllable *śca*, there entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Pervasive Resounding Roar of the Clouds of the Dharmas of Sentient Beings and Space.

As he proclaimed the syllable *ṭa*, there entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Lamp that Brings About the Ultimate Perfection of the Task of Selflessness for the Benefit of Sentient Beings. As he proclaimed the syllable *ḍha*, there entered the gateway to the perfection of wisdom called "The Essence of the Non-differentiation of the Wheel of Dharma."

Thus, noble son, as I was reciting my *mātṛkā*, I entered these forty-two gateways of the perfection of wisdom, headed by the gateway of the perfection of wisdom, and immeasurable and incalculable gateways of the perfection of wisdom besides;
noble son, I have attained this bodhisattva liberation of skillful knowledge and I know it.
How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the virtues of the Bodhisattvas who have attained perfection in all worldly and transcendent arts and crafts?

[I cannot know them] regarding their entry into all fields of art; their entry into all scripts, numerals, calculations, and systems of notation; their penetration of the application and knowledge of all mantras, medicinal herbs, and rituals;

their mastery over all spirits, planetary influences, seizures, epilepsy, sorcery, and vetālas; and their knowledge of the medical treatment of the realm of sentient beings and the compounding of medicines.

In the applications of the conjunction of the *dhātu* tantras, [he possesses] knowledge regarding gold, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, corals, rubies, emeralds, musāragalva, keśara, śrīgarbha, agaru, and all other gems—their origins, lineages, mines, and values;

in the construction of gardens, ascetic groves, villages, cities, market towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals; and in the entry into all worldly revolutions and reversals, including the science of the deer-wheel marks, all physical characteristics and signs, earthquakes, portents of fire in the directions, meteors, security and insecurity, abundance and famine.

Regarding the wisdoms that follow the reality of entering into the instructions on the indication and differentiation of all supramundane dharmas, there is no obscuration, nor deliberation, nor doubt, nor uncertainty, nor hesitation, nor delusion, nor sluggishness, nor affliction, nor despondency, nor ignorance, nor lack of realization.
Go, son of good family;

here in this very Magadha country, in the district of Kevalaka, in the city of Vartanaka, there dwells a laywoman named Bhadrottamā. Approach her and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the merchant’s son Śilpābhijña, circumambulated the merchant’s son Śilpābhijña hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of the merchant’s son Śilpābhijña. // 45 //
(Gv 355) 48. Bhadrottamā: Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana went toward the city of Vartanaka in the district of Kevalaka.
He went to where the female lay devotee Bhadrottamā was;
having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the female lay devotee Bhadrottamā and circumambulated her many hundreds of thousands of times.

Having circumambulated her and stood before the female lay devotee Bhadrottamā with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus: "Noble lady, I have generated the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva."

How should I practice? I have heard, Noble Lady, that you give instruction and advice to the bodhisattvas; therefore, may the Noble Lady tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?
She said: "Noble son, I know and teach a Dharma discourse called the *Anālayamaṇḍala*.
I have attained the samādhi of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), yet within that samādhi there is no empowerment of any phenomenon whatsoever."
Therein, the eye of omniscience operates; the basis is the ear of omniscience;
the basis is the nose of omniscience;
the basis is the tongue of omniscience.
The empowerment is the body of omniscience;
therein, the mind of omniscience proceeds as the empowerment;
the empowerment is the wave of omniscience.
The lightning of omniscience is sustained by empowerment;
the impulses of omniscience, which are circles illuminating the world, proceed from that empowerment.
This, noble son, I—
“I know the Dharma discourse called the ‘Maṇḍala Without Abode. But how could I possibly know the entirety of the unattached conduct of bodhisattvas? Go, noble son, to the southern region.”
There is a city there named Bharukaccha.
A goldsmith named Muktāsāra dwells there.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the laywoman Bhadrottamā, circumambulated her hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at her again and again, departed from the presence of the laywoman Bhadrottamā.
(Gv 356) 49. Muktāsāra.
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, traveling by stages toward the southern region, arrived at the city of Bharukaccha where Muktāsāra, the goldsmith, resided.

Having approached him and bowed his head at the feet of Muktāsārahairaṇyaka, he stood before him with palms joined in reverence and spoke thus: "Noble one, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it."
"I have heard, noble one, that you give instruction and admonition to the bodhisattvas.
Therefore, may the noble one tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva practice, and how should he practice?"
He said: "Noble son, I know the bodhisattva liberation called the Array of Unattached Mindfulness.
My quest for the Dharma at the feet of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions is never-ceasing.
Noble son, this is the bodhisattva liberation called the Array of Unattached Mindfulness that I know and understand."
How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the qualities of the Bodhisattvas, who roar the fearless lion’s roar and are established in great merit and wisdom?
Go, son of good family;
here in this very city of Bharukaccha there dwells a householder named Sucandra,
whose home is illuminated by that light.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of Muktasāra Hairaṇyaka, circumambulated Muktasāra Hairaṇyaka hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of Muktasāra Hairaṇyaka. // 47 //
(50) Sucandra. Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana went to where the householder Sucandra was.

Having approached him and bowed his head at the feet of the householder Sucandra, he stood before him with palms joined in reverence and said: "Noble one, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it."
I have heard, Noble One, that you give instruction and admonition to the bodhisattvas;
therefore, may the Noble One tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct, and how should one practice it?
He said: "Noble son, I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called Vimalajñānaprabhā (Stainless Wisdom Light).
Noble son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation of Vimalajñānaprabhā.
How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the qualities of those bodhisattvas who have attained immeasurable liberations?"
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region there is a city named Roruka.
There dwells a householder named Ajitasena.
Go to him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then the merchant’s son Sudhana, having bowed his head at the feet of the householder Sucandra and having circumambulated the householder Sucandra hundreds of thousands of times, looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of the householder Sucandra.
Ajitasena.
Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son, proceeding by stages, arrived at the city of Roruka and went to where Ajitasena was.

The householder Nāma approached Ajitasena the householder, bowed his head at his feet, and standing before him with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus: "Noble one, I have resolved my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva."
"How should I practice? I have heard, O Noble One, that you give instruction and advice to the bodhisattvas;
therefore, may the Noble One tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
How should one practice?

He said: "Noble son, I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'Inexhaustible Characteristic,' by the attainment of which there occurs the acquisition of the inexhaustible treasure of beholding the Buddhas."
Go, son of good family! Right here in the southern region, in the village of Dharmagrāma, there dwells a brahmin named Śivarāgra.
Approach him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice?"

Then Sudhana, the merchant's son, bowed his head at the feet of the householder Ajitasena, circumambulated the householder Ajitasena hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at him again and again, departed from the presence of the householder Ajitasena. 49.
(52) Śivarāgra. Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son, proceeding by stages, went to the village of Dharmagrāma and approached the brahmin Śivarāgra.

Having approached him and bowed his head at the feet of the brahmin Śivarāgra, he stood before him with palms joined in reverence and said: "Noble one, I have set my mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice."
I have heard, Noble One, that you give instruction and admonition to the bodhisattvas;
therefore, may the Noble One tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva practice, and how should one proceed?
He said: "Noble son, I practice by means of the empowerment of truth.
By that truth, by that word of truth, there is no bodhisattva whatsoever in the three times who has turned back from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, nor does anyone turn back."
"I shall not turn back;
by this empowerment of truthful speech, may this task of mine be accomplished. Then everything is accomplished for me exactly according to my intention.
"By this empowerment of truthful speech, noble son, I accomplish all my tasks.
Noble son, I know only this empowerment of truth.
How could I possibly know the conduct or describe the qualities of those bodhisattvas who have attained speech that follows the truth?"
Go, son of good family;
right here in the southern region there is a city named Sumanāmukha.
There dwells a boy named Śrīsaṃbhava.
And there is a maiden named Śrīmati;
go to them and ask how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct and how one should practice it.

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, having conceived a profound reverence for the Dharma, bowed his head at the feet of the brahmin Śivarāgra; he circumambulated the brahmin Śivarāgra hundreds of thousands of times, and looking back at him again and again, he departed from the presence of the brahmin Śivarāgra. 50.
(360) Śrīsaṃbhava and Śrīmatī. Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son, proceeding by stages, went to the city of Sumanāmukha, where the boy Śrīsaṃbhava and the girl Śrīmatī were.

Approaching them, he bowed his head at their feet and, standing before them with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus: "Noble ones, I have generated the aspiration for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it."

I have heard, O Noble Ones, that you give instruction and advice to the bodhisattvas; therefore, may you tell me: how should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct, and how should he practice?
Then the boy Śrīsaṃbhava and the girl Śrīmatī said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "In this regard, noble son, we have attained and realized the bodhisattva liberation called 'The Illusory.
Endowed with this liberation, noble son, we behold the entire world as illusory, arisen through the illusion of causes and conditions."
We recognize all sentient beings as having entered into illusion;
through the knowledge that karma and afflictions are illusion, we see the entire world as having entered into illusion;
and we see all phenomena as having entered into illusion, arising from the illusion of ignorance, existence, and craving.

We see the entire triple world as produced by the illusion of mutual conditions, situated within illusion; it is brought forth as an inconceivable domain, an illusion born from the inversion of awakening.
We see all sentient beings as situated in illusion, undergoing death, rebirth, birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair.
We see all realms as produced by the illusion of unreal conceptualization, produced by illusion.

We behold all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas as being like illusions, arising from the delusions of perverted perception, thought, and view, and from the false notion that illusory phenomena possess substantial reality. We understand the entire succession of the Bodhisattva’s conduct, vows, the ripening and disciplining of sentient beings, as being like illusions, produced by the conceptualization of illusion regarding knowledge and abandonment. We behold the entire mandala of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as being like illusions, consisting of the discipline of emanated conduct brought forth through the manifestation of illusion, and having the nature of illusion—an inconceivable domain manifested through the illusion of vow and wisdom.
"Noble son, we two understand only this illusory liberation of a bodhisattva.
How could we possibly know the conduct or describe the qualities of those bodhisattvas who have entered the web of manifestations produced by the illusion of infinite karma?"

Then the boy Śrīsaṃbhava and the girl Śrīmatī, having moistened the merchant’s son Sudhana with the inconceivable force of their roots of goodness and having made him hear of the scope of their own liberation, said this to him: "Go, noble son;
right here in the southern region is a district called Samudrakaccha."
Therein is a park named Mahāvyūha.
Therein is a great peaked pavilion named Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha, produced as the maturation of the roots of goodness of bodhisattvas,
born from the volition and mental attention of bodhisattvas, arisen from the vows of bodhisattvas, and brought forth by the masteries of bodhisattvas.

It was manifested through the power of the bodhisattvas' superknowledges, produced by the skillful means of the bodhisattvas, perfected by the power of the bodhisattvas' merit and wisdom, demonstrating the training of sentient beings through the great compassion of the bodhisattvas, accumulated through the array of the bodhisattvas' empowerments, and adorned by the dwelling in the inconceivable liberations of the bodhisattvas.
Therein dwells the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Maitreya, for the sake of benefiting the humans of that birthplace.
For the sake of ripening one's mother, father, kinsmen, and relatives;
for the sake of strengthening the Mahāyāna of those beings who have been born there and whose conduct is similar to one's own;
and for the sake of ripening the roots of virtue of other beings as well, according to their respective stages.
In order to demonstrate his own entry into the method of liberation;

in order to manifest the power of a bodhisattva’s mastery over rebirth that pervades everywhere, by way of being oriented toward manifesting births for all sentient beings so as not to neglect their ripening;
and in order to bring forth the power of a bodhisattva’s great compassion through the loathing of grasping at any world.
In order to realize the dwelling of a bodhisattva that has transcended all abodes and stations,
and to demonstrate the supreme state of homelessness while manifesting residence in all births within existence—
approach him and ask: "How should a bodhisattva inquire about the bodhisattva practice?"
How should a bodhisattva purify the bodhisattva path?
How should a bodhisattva practice the bodhisattva trainings?
How should a bodhisattva purify the thought of awakening?
How should a bodhisattva bring forth the bodhisattva vow?
How should a bodhisattva generate the accumulations of a bodhisattva?
How should a bodhisattva traverse the bodhisattva stages?
How should a bodhisattva fulfill the perfections of a bodhisattva?
How should a bodhisattva enter into the patiences of a bodhisattva?
How should a bodhisattva abide in the qualities of a bodhisattva’s practice?
How should a bodhisattva attend upon spiritual friends?
For what reason is that?
For that noble son Maitreya, O son of good family, has entered into all the practices of a bodhisattva and has mastered them;
he has penetrated into all the mental dispositions and intentions of bodhisattvas;
and he is present before all the activities of all sentient beings, as well as in their maturation and discipline.
By him all the perfections have been fulfilled;
he is well-established in all the bodhisattva stages;
by him all the bodhisattva patiences have been attained.
He has entered the fixed course of a bodhisattva;
by him all prophecies have been received;
he sports in all the liberations of the bodhisattvas.
By him all the empowerments of all the Buddhas have been sustained. He has been consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the consecration of the domain of omniscient knowledge.
O son of good family, that spiritual friend will moisten you and cause all your roots of virtue to increase.
He will make firm the generation of the mind of awakening; he will purify the element of his resolute intention; and he will cause all roots of virtue to increase.
He will manifest the force of the bodhisattva faculties;
he will cause them to enter the direction of the unobstructed dharma; and he will establish them in the pursuit of the stage of Samantabhadra.
He will extol the gateways for the departure through the vows of all bodhisattvas;
he will explain the perfection of the qualities of the vows and conduct of all bodhisattvas, which is the gateway to the method of hearing the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Furthermore, noble son, you should not be satisfied with a single root of goodness, nor limited to the illumination of a single gateway of the Dharma, nor content with a single mode of conduct, nor restricted to the accomplishment of a single vow.
Not by one who has ceased from the final consummation,
nor by one who perceives the entry into the three patiences as supreme,
nor by one who has ceased from the fulfillment of the six perfections.
One should not be satisfied with having reached the culmination of attaining the ten stages, nor with the vow for the purification and acquisition of a Buddha-field of measurable proportions,
nor with the satisfaction of pleasing and attending upon spiritual friends who have been made into a fixed measure.
For what reason?
Because, noble son, a bodhisattva must fully accomplish immeasurable roots of goodness; immeasurable provisions for enlightenment must be raised up.
Immeasurable causes for the thought of awakening must be gathered;
immeasurable methods must be studied;
and the immeasurable realm of sentient beings must be led to final nirvana.
One must penetrate the immeasurable realm of the inclinations of sentient beings;
one must fully comprehend the immeasurable faculties of sentient beings;
and one must accord with the immeasurable liberation of sentient beings.
The immeasurable activities of the realm of sentient beings must be understood;
the immeasurable discipline of sentient beings must be carried out;
and the immeasurable latent tendencies of the afflictions must be eradicated.
Immeasurable karmic obstructions are to be purified;
immeasurable views are to be overturned.
Immeasurable defilements of the mind are to be removed;
immeasurable purities of the mind are to be generated;
immeasurable thorns of suffering are to be uprooted.
The immeasurable ocean of craving for sentient beings must be completely dried up;
the immeasurable darkness of ignorance must be dispelled;
and the immeasurable mountains must be cast down.
The immeasurable bonds of saṃsāra must be eradicated;
the immeasurable ocean of birth must be dried up;
the immeasurable flood of existence must be crossed.
Immeasurable beings who are stuck in the mire of desire must be uplifted;
immeasurable beings confined within the city of the three realms must be led out;
immeasurable beings must be established upon the Noble Path.
Immeasurable greed, hatred, and delusion are to be pacified;
immeasurable snares of Māra are to be transcended;
and immeasurable deeds of Māra are to be turned back.
The immeasurable realm of a bodhisattva’s resolute intention is to be purified;
the immeasurable applications of a bodhisattva are to be increased;
the immeasurable faculties of a bodhisattva are to be generated.
Immeasurable inclinations of the bodhisattva must be purified;
immeasurable equanimity of the bodhisattva must be entered into;
and the immeasurable excellence of the bodhisattva’s conduct must be followed.
Immeasurable qualities of a bodhisattva are to be purified;
immeasurable modes of conduct of a bodhisattva are to be fulfilled;
and immeasurable worldly behaviors are to be conformed to.
Immeasurable ways of conforming to the world should be demonstrated;
immeasurable power of faith should be generated;
immeasurable power of vigor should be sustained.
The immeasurable power of mindfulness must be purified;
the immeasurable power of concentration must be purified;
the immeasurable power of wisdom must be generated.
One should strengthen the immeasurable power of resolute conviction;
one should fully acquire the immeasurable power of merit;
and one should increase the immeasurable power of wisdom.
One should arouse the immeasurable power of a bodhisattva;
one should fulfill the immeasurable power of a Buddha;
and one should discern the immeasurable gateways to the Dharma.
The immeasurable directions of the Dharma should be entered;
the immeasurable gateways of the Dharma should be purified;
and the immeasurable lights of the Dharma should be generated.
An immeasurable illumination of the Dharma should be produced;
immeasurable lineages of the faculties should be illuminated;
and immeasurable diseases of the afflictions should be purified.
Immeasurable medicinal teachings are to be gathered; the immeasurable realm of sentient beings, afflicted by the disease of the afflictions, is to be treated;
and immeasurable accumulations of the deathless are to be gathered.
Immeasurable Buddha-fields are to be traversed;
immeasurable Tathāgatas are to be honored;
and immeasurable circles of Bodhisattva assemblies are to be entered.
The immeasurable teachings of the Tathāgata must be upheld;
the immeasurable harms inflicted by sentient beings must be endured;
and the immeasurable paths to the unfortunate states and lack of opportunity must be severed.
Immeasurable happiness for sentient beings must be brought forth; immeasurable means of gathering sentient beings must be performed;
and immeasurable gateways of dhāraṇī must be purified.
One should bring forth immeasurable gateways of aspiration;
one should cultivate immeasurable powers of great loving-kindness and great compassion;
and one should not relax immeasurable applications in the quest for the Dharma.
One should follow the immeasurable powers of profound contemplation;
one should bring forth the immeasurable accomplishments of the superknowledges;
and one should purify the immeasurable lights of knowledge and wisdom.
The immeasurable realm of sentient beings is to be followed;
the immeasurable arising of existence is to be embraced.
The infinite differentiation of bodies must be demonstrated;
the infinite differentiation of mantras must be fully understood;
and the infinite diversity of the minds of sentient beings must be penetrated.
The vast domain of the bodhisattvas must be entered;
the expansive palace of the bodhisattvas must be traversed; the profound abode of the bodhisattvas must be scrutinized.
The domain of the bodhisattvas, which is difficult to comprehend, must be understood;
the course of the bodhisattvas, which is difficult to traverse, must be traversed; and the impulses of the bodhisattvas, which are difficult to approach, must be sustained.
The entrance into the bodhisattva-determination, which is difficult to enter, must be entered;
the manifold conduct of a bodhisattva must be fully understood;
and the bodhisattva’s miraculous transformations, which pervade all places, must be demonstrated.
The Bodhisattva must receive the clouds of Dharma in their full integration;
he must expand the net of Bodhisattva conduct, which is without end or middle; and the Bodhisattva must bring to fulfillment the perfections that are limitless.
A bodhisattva should accept immeasurable prophecies;
a bodhisattva should enter into incalculable gateways of patience;
and a bodhisattva should purify incalculable stages.
A bodhisattva should purify the gateways to the Dharma that are not limited;
a bodhisattva should purify buddha-fields that are inexpressible;
a bodhisattva should don the armor for incalculable eons.

Bodhisattvas should worship the Tathāgatas, who are immeasurable; bodhisattvas should accomplish inconceivable fulfillments of their vows. In brief, noble son, the conduct of bodhisattvas is said to be equal to that of all sentient beings, by way of maturing sentient beings.
It is described as equal to all eons because of dwelling in all eons;
it is described as equal to all rebirths because of manifesting birth everywhere;
it is described as equal to all times for the sake of awakening to the knowledge of the three times.
They are said to be equal in all dharmas through the practice thereof; they are said to be equal in all fields through the purification thereof;
they are said to be equal in all vows through the fulfillment thereof.
It is equal to all Buddhas through the accomplishment of their worship;
it is equal to all Bodhisattvas through the unity of their vows;
and it is equal to all spiritual friends through the pleasing of the conduct of Bodhisattvas.
Therefore, noble son, you should not give rise to weariness in your search for spiritual friends;
you should not give rise to a sense of having had enough in your audiences with spiritual friends;
and you should not fall into complacency in your inquiries of spiritual friends.
One should not turn back one's intention regarding association with spiritual friends;
one should not slacken one's application in serving spiritual friends with reverence;
and one should not be perverse in grasping the instructions and admonitions of spiritual friends.
One should not give rise to doubt regarding the acquisition of the qualities of a spiritual friend;
one should not harbor uncertainty regarding the demonstrations of the gateways to liberation provided by a spiritual friend;
and one should not produce resentment toward the spiritual friend’s employment of skillful means, his conformity with worldly conventions, and his adaptive conduct.
One must not turn back body or mind from increasing one's faith in spiritual friends.
Why is that?
Noble son, all the practices of the bodhisattvas, including their hearing of the teachings, are dependent upon spiritual friends.
The perfection of all bodhisattva qualities originates from spiritual friends;
the streams of all bodhisattva vows originate from spiritual friends;
and all the roots of virtue of bodhisattvas are produced by spiritual friends.
All the accumulations of a bodhisattva are aroused by spiritual friends;
all the illuminations of the gateways to the Dharma of a bodhisattva are brought forth by spiritual friends;
and all the purifications of the gateways to the departure toward enlightenment are produced by spiritual friends.
All the practices of the training of bodhisattvas are dependent upon spiritual friends;
all the qualities and dharmas of bodhisattvas are established in spiritual friends;
all the purifications of the resolute intentions of bodhisattvas have their root in spiritual friends.
The firmness of the resolve for enlightenment in all bodhisattvas is born from spiritual friends;
the illumination of the gateways of dhāraṇīs and eloquence in the ocean of all bodhisattvas is guided by spiritual friends;
and the treasuries of the gateways to the purity of all bodhisattvas are sustained by spiritual friends.
The illumination of all bodhisattva-knowledge is produced by spiritual friends;
the excellence of all bodhisattva vows is held in the hands of spiritual friends;
and the state of one-pointedness has spiritual friends as its primary cause.
They possess the lineage of spiritual friends and have a distinguished faith in the complete realization of all bodhisattvas;
they have entered the treasury of spiritual friends, which contains all the secret points of the bodhisattvas.
Spiritual friends are the mines from which all the qualities of a bodhisattva are extracted;
spiritual friends cause all the sprouts of the momentum of a bodhisattva’s faculties to grow; spiritual friends cause all the oceans of a bodhisattva’s wisdom to increase.
The treasuries of all bodhisattvas are guarded by spiritual friends;
the accumulations of merit of all bodhisattvas are protected by spiritual friends;
and the purities of birth of all bodhisattvas are produced by spiritual friends.
All the clouds of the Dharma of the bodhisattvas come from the mouth of the spiritual friend;
all entries into the paths of departure for the bodhisattvas are stored within the treasury of the spiritual friend;
and the enlightenment of all Buddhas is obtained through the propitiation of the spiritual friend.
All the practices of bodhisattvas are embraced by spiritual friends;
all the manifestations of bodhisattva qualities are illuminated by spiritual friends;
and all the traversals of the directions of the bodhisattvas are shown by spiritual friends.
The greatness of the profound resolve and the mind of all bodhisattvas is extolled by spiritual friends;
the power of great loving-kindness of bodhisattvas arises from spiritual friends;
and the power of great compassion of bodhisattvas is generated by spiritual friends.
All sovereign powers of the bodhisattvas are embraced by spiritual friends;
all factors of enlightenment are generated by spiritual friends;
and all beneficial provisions for the welfare of bodhisattvas arise from spiritual friends.
Supported by spiritual friends, noble son, bodhisattvas do not fall into the miserable realms;
embraced by spiritual friends, bodhisattvas do not turn back from the Mahāyāna;
and attended to by spiritual friends, bodhisattvas do not transgress the bodhisattva training.
Bodhisattvas who are well-guarded by spiritual friends do not fall under the influence of evil friends;
bodhisattvas who are protected by spiritual friends do not decline from the qualities of a bodhisattva;
and bodhisattvas who are embraced by spiritual friends transcend the stage of ordinary worldlings.
Bodhisattvas who have trained under spiritual friends do not fall into the state of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas;
bodhisattvas who are shielded by spiritual friends rise above the world;
bodhisattvas who have been nurtured by spiritual friends remain undefiled.
Through the worldly conditions,
