bodhisattvas who attend upon spiritual friends become practitioners who do not forget [the teachings] in any of their activities.
Bodhisattvas who are inspired by spiritual friends do not turn back from any undertakings.

Bodhisattvas embraced by spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) become invincible to karma and afflictions (kleśa). Bodhisattvas supported by the power of spiritual friends become unassailable by all Māras.
Bodhisattvas who dwell in reliance upon spiritual friends increase in all the factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga).
For what reason?
Noble son, spiritual friends are purifiers; they cause the removal of obscurations.
Spiritual friends are those who awaken one from the miserable states of existence.
Spiritual friends are those who restrain one from non-virtuous actions and from states of negligence;
they are the dispersers of the darkness of ignorance and the breakers of the fetters of false views.
They are those who cause one to emerge from saṃsāra; they are those who uproot one from the worldly abode;
they are those who liberate one from the snares of Māra.
They are the healers of painful thorns,
the liberators from the thicket of ignorance,
and the ones who lead others across the wilderness of wrong views.
They are deliverers from the floods of existence; they are uplifters from the mire of sensual desire;
they are those who turn others away from evil paths.
They are the revealers of the bodhisattva path,
the instigators through the bodhisattva vow,
and the establishers in the practices.
They are the guides toward the direction of omniscience,
the purifiers of the eye of wisdom,
and the increasers of the mind of awakening.
They are the generators of great compassion,
the proclaimers of the conduct,
and the instructors in the perfections.
They are those who cause others to return to the stages,
who distribute the patient acceptances,
and who bring all roots of virtue to fulfillment.
They are the arouser of all requisites;
the givers of all bodhisattva qualities;
and those who cause one to reach the presence at the feet of all Buddhas.
They are those who demonstrate all virtuous qualities,
who inspire others toward meaningful goals,
and who incite them toward right practice.
They are the revealers of the gateways to liberation;
the protectors from the paths of ruin;
and the illuminators of the gateways to the light of the Dharma.
They are those who cause the rain-clouds of the hearing of the Dharma to pour down;
they are the destroyers of all afflictions;
they are the turners away from all that is produced by false views.
They are the ones who establish [beings] in all the qualities of a Buddha.
Moreover, noble son, spiritual friends are like mothers, for they give birth to one within the families of the Buddhas;
spiritual friends are like fathers, for they provide vast benefit and welfare;
spiritual friends are like nurses, for they protect one from all evil.
Spiritual friends are like teachers because they cause one to realize the training of a bodhisattva;
spiritual friends are like guides because they lead one onto the path of the perfections;
spiritual friends are like physicians because they liberate one from the disease of the afflictions.
Spiritual friends are like the Himalaya mountains because they increase the medicinal herbs of wisdom;
spiritual friends are like heroes because they protect one from all fears;
spiritual friends are like ferrymen because they enable one to cross the great flood of the accumulations.
Spiritual friends are like helmsmen, for they lead one to the island of the jewel of the knowledge of the Omniscient One.

Therefore, noble son, with a mind thus composed through such mental attention, you should approach spiritual friends with a mind like the earth, by virtue of not turning back under the weight of any burden;
with a mind like a diamond, by virtue of an unbreakable intention;
and with a mind like the Cakravāla mountains, by virtue of being unshaken by any suffering.
With an even mind, by carrying out instructions as desired; with a mind like that of a disciple, by never contradicting any instruction;
with a mind like that of a servant to the world, by undertaking all tasks without revulsion.
With a mind like that of a nurse, by not being distressed by any afflictions;
with a mind like that of a servant, by being compliant in performing whatever tasks are required;
with a mind like that of one sweeping away dust, by abandoning pride and arrogance.
With a mind like the full moon, by not disregarding the proper or improper time;
with a mind like a well-bred horse, by avoiding all stubbornness;
with a mind like a vehicle, by bearing heavy burdens.
With a mind like an elephant, through being a tamed and noble steed;
with a mind like a mountain, through being immovable and unshakable; with a mind like a dog, through being free from anger.
With a mind like that of a caṇḍāla youth, through being free from pride and self-conceit;
with a mind like that of a bull whose horns have been cut off, through being devoid of all arrogance;
with a mind like that of a pupil, through the absence of haughtiness.
With a mind like a ship, by being untiring in coming and going; with a mind like a bridge or a causeway, by crossing over the commands of the spiritual friends;
with a mind like a good son, by gazing upon the face of the spiritual friend.
With a mind equal to that of a prince, by virtue of carrying out the commands of the King of Dharma.
And you, son of good family, should conceive the notion of being a patient toward yourself, the notion of a physician toward spiritual friends,
and the notion of medicine toward their instructions.
One should conceive of spiritual practices as the eradication of disease; and you, son of good family, should conceive of yourself as a traveler on a journey, and of spiritual friends as guides.
One should conceive of the instructions as the path,
and one should generate the conception of traveling through the directions of the buddha-fields regarding the practices.
And you, noble son, should conceive the notion of yourself as one who has reached the further shore, the notion of spiritual friends as ferrymen,
and the notion of their instructions as the crossing-places.
One should conceive of spiritual practices as a boat;
and you, noble son, should conceive of yourself as a farmer,
and of spiritual friends as serpent-kings.
In the instructions, you should conceive the notion of rain; in the practices, you should conceive the notion of the ripening of grain.
And, noble son, you should conceive the notion of yourself as being poor.
One should conceive of spiritual friends as Vaiśravaṇa, of their instructions as wealth, and of their practices as the removal of poverty.
And you, son of good family, should conceive the notion of being a pupil toward yourself, the notion of a teacher toward the spiritual friends,
and the notion of a craft toward their instructions.
One should generate the perception of attainment regarding the practices; and you, noble son, should generate the perception of fearlessness toward yourself,
and the perception of a hero toward spiritual friends.
Regarding the instructions, you should conceive of them as weapons; regarding the practices, you should conceive of them as the destruction of enemies.
And you, noble son, should conceive of yourself as a merchant.
One should conceive of spiritual friends as ship captains,
of their instructions as jewels,
and of one's practice as the act of gathering those jewels.
And you, son of good family, should conceive the notion of a true son toward yourself, the notion of mother and father toward the spiritual friends,
and the notion of the family livelihood toward their instructions.
One should produce the perception of the non-wastage of engagement in the practices.
And you, noble son, should produce the perception of yourself as a prince,
and the perception of spiritual friends as the chief ministers of the King of Dharma.

Within the instructions, one should conceive of them as the training of kings; within the practices, one should conceive of them as the royal crown-jewel ornament, the binding of the Dharma-diadem upon the head, and the surveying of the city of the Dharma-king.
Noble son, spiritual friends should be approached with a mind thus cultivated through such conceptions and mental attentions.

For what reason? Because, noble son, when bodhisattvas have thus purified their resolute intention toward spiritual friends and act in accordance with the instructions of those spiritual friends, they increase in all roots of virtue, just like the grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forest trees that depend upon the Himavat mountains.
They become vessels for all the qualities of a Buddha, like the great ocean for water; they become mines of all virtues, like the great sea for jewels;
and they heat the thought of enlightenment, like gold in the heat of fire.
They emerge above the world like Mount Sumeru from the ocean;
they remain unstained by worldly conditions.
They dwell together with all evil conduct, like a lotus with water,
or like the great ocean with a putrid corpse.
They increase in white virtues like the moon in the bright fortnight;
they illuminate the realm of phenomena like the sun illuminating Jambudvīpa.
They cause the bodies of the bodhisattva vows to grow, like children dependent upon their parents.
In brief, noble son, bodhisattvas who practice according to the instructions of spiritual friends acquire ten hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of inexpressible qualities;
they purify ten hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of superior intentions.
They increase ten hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of bodhisattva faculties;
they purify ten hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of empowerments;
and they thoroughly cleanse hundreds of thousands of incalculable dharmas to be practiced.
They transcend ten hundred thousand incalculable multitudes of Māras;
they dwell within ten hundred thousand incalculable gateways to the doors of the Dharma;
and they fulfill ten hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of incalculable gateways to the purification of the accumulations.
They fulfill ten hundred thousand incalculable sets of practices; they purify ten hundred thousand incalculable sets of practices;
and they bring forth ten hundred thousand incalculable great vows.

In brief, noble son, all the practices of bodhisattvas, all the perfections of bodhisattvas, all the stages of bodhisattvas, all the gateways to the samādhis of bodhisattvas, all the miraculous displays of the superknowledges and wisdom of bodhisattvas, all the illuminations of the dhāraṇīs and eloquence of bodhisattvas,
and all the immeasurability of the superknowledge of the wisdom of the dedication of merit of bodhisattvas— [all these are encompassed therein].

The accomplishment of all the vows of bodhisattvas and the complete attainment of all the qualities of a buddha depend upon spiritual friends; they have spiritual friends as their root, spiritual friends as their source, spiritual friends as their origin, and spiritual friends as the gateway to them.
They are born from spiritual friends, nurtured by spiritual friends, established in spiritual friends, caused by spiritual friends,
and brought forth by spiritual friends.

Then, having heard this instruction regarding the praise of the qualities of spiritual friends, the immeasurability of the bodhisattva conduct, and the vastness of the Buddha-dharma, the merchant’s son Sudhana was satisfied, elated, uplifted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness;
he bowed his head at the feet of the boy Śrīsambhava and the girl Śrīmatī, and [addressed] Śrīsambhava...

Having circumambulated the boy and the girl Śrīmatī hundreds of thousands of times, and having looked back at them again and again, he departed from the presence of the boy Śrīsambhava and the girl Śrīmatī. // 51 // // 52 //
(Gv 368) 54. Maitreya.

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, his mind saturated by the instructions of his spiritual friends, proceeded toward the region of Samudrakaccha, reflecting deeply upon those very instructions regarding the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Strengthening his physical strength by reflecting upon how, throughout the limits of the past, he had prostrated his body in service yet lacked the capacity for right conduct;
grasping his mental attention by reflecting upon the purity of body and mind throughout the limits of the past, in contrast to the motiveless wandering of the worldly mind;
and contemplating the great efficacy of present purpose by reflecting upon the fruitless flow of engaging in improper worldly activities throughout the limits of the past.

By means of the mental attention and reflection that manifests false conceptualizations arising from the unreal imaginings of the past, he generates the power of the correct formation of all the right intentions of a bodhisattva’s conduct;

and by means of the reflection on the unevenness of his own past applications and endeavors for self-interest, he strengthens the power of his resolute intention through its superiority in undertaking the welfare of all sentient beings.

By reflecting upon the relish for past conduct in the pursuit of the body, he attains the great breath of the application for the non-attainment of all Buddha-dharmas, thereby increasing the force of his faculties; and by reflecting upon the application of false, illusory, and perverted practices associated with the past time, he purifies his continuum through the bodhisattva vow associated with the non-perverted, correct vision of the present time.

By means of a mental attention that is unaccomplished in its undertaking of vigor regarding the past, yet present with the full attainment of all the qualities of a Buddha in the present; by means of the prowess of a great undertaking of vigor that exerts both body and mind;

and by means of a mental attention applied to embracing eons reaching to the furthest limit of the future—thereby upholding a physical existence that is not reckoned as having been cast into the five destinies or the miserable states throughout the succession of bodies from the prior limit, and which is the source of all Buddha-qualities, the sustenance for the entire world, and capable of all that is auspicious.

Increasing the force of vast joy and rapture, he [regarded] this physical existence—which has arisen in the present life as the source of old age, sickness, death, and grief, and as the locus of union and separation—as belonging to one who is dedicated to practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout kalpas reaching to the furthest limit of the future; who is dedicated to maturing sentient beings and embracing the qualities of a Buddha; who is dedicated to beholding the Tathāgatas, wandering through all buddha-fields, attending upon all Dharma-preachers, and upholding the teachings of all Tathāgatas; and who has become a companion in the search for all dharmas.

Beholding that which serves as the cause and condition for the very body of the Bodhisattva’s vow— one who is devoted to beholding all spiritual friends and accomplishing all the qualities of a Buddha— he increases the force of his faculties through inconceivable roots of goodness;
with such a mind, such mental attention, and such correct application, he is established in faith toward all Bodhisattvas.
With faith established through the aspiration for all bodhisattvas; with love established through the aspiration for all bodhisattvas;

with reverence established through clarity of confidence in the faculties of all bodhisattvas; with a sense of wonder arising from conviction in the teachings of all bodhisattvas; with a clarity of mind brought forth by the force of confidence in the faculties resulting from devotion to all bodhisattvas; and with [qualities] arisen from faith in all bodhisattvas.
By means of the accumulations of roots of merit,
and by means of various forms of worship arising from all the formative activities of bodhisattvas;
With bodies equal to all bodhisattvas, with palms joined in reverence, with gazes that perceive the various forms of the eyes arising from the bodies of the entire world,
with perceptions of the entire world superimposed upon the world, with the manifestation of arrays of vocal utterances and pure qualities arising from the vocal components of all bodhisattvas,
and through the fulfillment of the empowerment of all bodhisattvas of the past and present limits, they had attained a state facing the dwelling of the Tathāgata.

By means of that which pertains to perception—pervading everywhere through the awakening to the miraculous transformations of Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas; not distinct from even a single hair’s breadth, yet pervading and following along with the bodies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; through the manifestations of the light of superknowledge and wisdom established by the purification of the range of vision of all Bodhisattvas;

following along with the penetration of the net of all directions; by means of the sense-field of mind that pervades the divisions of the depths of the *dharmadhātu*; through the power of the accomplishment of vows; and pervading everywhere until the ultimate limit of the realm of space.

By means of the power of entering into faith and resolute conviction— which is undifferentiated across the three times, never-ceasing, an entrance-gate for penetrating all phenomena, and extended throughout the directions with the radiance of the instructions of all spiritual friends—
thus indeed did the merchant’s son Sudhana, his mind accompanied by the perceptions of reverence, esteem, worship, praise, prostration, looking up [in devotion], empowerment, and aspiration.

Thus, with the eye of wisdom extended across the ground that is the sphere of immeasurable knowledge, he prostrated with his entire body at the base of the door in front of the great peaked hall, the Vairocana-vyūhālaṃkāragarbha.

Having reflected for a moment upon this kind of application of creative power, he established himself with an unremitting self, through the strength of the accomplishment of his high resolve and vow, which was aroused by resolute faith.
Thus, in the presence of all manifestations of awakening, in the abodes of all spiritual friends, in all shrines of the Tathāgatas,
in all physical forms of the Tathāgatas, in all bodhisattvas, in all dwellings of the Buddhas, in all repositories of the jewels of the Dharma,

in the presence of all shrines that are the supports for śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and in the presence of all noble assemblies, objects of veneration, teachers, and finally one’s own mother and father.

He established himself in an unrelaxed state of self-presence before all manifestations of the bodies of the entire world, by means of a mental engagement with the knowledge that presides over perception— a mental engagement that follows the method of non-differentiation within the body of gnosis and which is universally pervasive.
And just as it was in front of the great peaked pavilion named Vairocana-vyūhālaṃkāragarbha, so too...

Thus, regarding all objects previously mentioned, he established a prostration that pervades the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). In this way, having empowered himself without cessation throughout eons reaching to the furthest limit of the future, he did so by means of the equality that is coextensive with the limits of the space-element,

the equality of the unobstructed nature of the realm of phenomena, the equality of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) that follows everywhere, and the equality of the non-conceptual state of the Tathāgata.

By means of the pervasion of the perception of knowledge as being like a shadow, by the equality of investigation as being like a dream, by the equality of the cognition of all worlds and beings as being like a reflection,
by the equality of the arising from causes and conditions as being like an echo, by the equality of non-arising, by the equality of appearance and disappearance,
and by the equality of the turning of conditions through dependence on non-existence, he gains resolute faith in the ripening of results as they arise according to karma.

Resolving that the fruit arises from its cause; resolving that all activity arises from accumulation; resolving that the appearance of all Tathāgatas arises from faith; resolving that the emanations for the worship of all Buddhas arise from such resolution; and resolving that the emanations of all Tathāgatas arise from reverence.

He was resolved upon the nature of all Buddha-dharmas arising from the accumulation of roots of goodness; he was resolved upon the accumulation of all mental arrays arising from wisdom and skillful means; he was resolved upon all Buddha-dharmas arising from his vows;

and he was resolved upon the arrays of ornaments, manifestations, and pervasions that establish the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) within the sphere of omniscience and the conduct of all bodhisattvas, arising from his dedication of merit.

By means of the knowledge of dedication free from the notion of annihilation, by the knowledge of non-arising that has eliminated the notion of permanence, by the knowledge of the accumulation of causes for entering into equal action— free from views of causal efficacy, free from views of correct action, and free from views of equal action— and by the knowledge not dependent on others, which is free from views of perversion.

By means of the knowledge of entering into dependent origination, which is free from the views of the notions of self and other; by means of the knowledge of entering the infinite and centerless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), which is free from the view of grasping at extremes;

by means of the knowledge of the manifestation of the equality of all foundations, which is free from the view of transmigration; and by means of the knowledge of non-arising and non-ceasing, which is free from the views of existence and non-existence.
By means of the knowledge of emptiness and non-arising which is free from all views;

by the power of the knowledge that accomplishes aspirations, which is not bound by the nature of lack of sovereignty; by the knowledge of the gateway to the limit of the signless, which dispels all notions of signs; and by the nature of reality in which the seed and sprout perish, and the equality of reality in the arising of the seal and its counter-seal.

By virtue of the nature of phenomena being like the seeing of a reflection; by virtue of the nature of phenomena being the cognition of the sound of an echo in the wind; by virtue of the nature of phenomena being the cognition of investigation that is equal to a dream; by virtue of the nature of phenomena being like the appearance of a mirage; by virtue of the nature of phenomena being the arising of actions equal to an illusion; by virtue of the nature of phenomena being the production of a formless mind in the world; and by virtue of the nature of phenomena being the accumulation of results according to causes and conditions.

By means of the nature of phenomena consisting in the ripening of the accumulation of karma according to its kind, the nature of phenomena consisting in the manifestation of skillful means, and the nature of phenomena moistened by the equality of the realization of dharma and non-dharma—

thus, through the mental attention and perception brought forth by the entry into such knowledge, the merchant’s son Sudhana prostrated himself before the great peaked pavilion named Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha.

Having reflected for a very long time, his mental continuum being moistened by the force of inconceivable roots of goodness, his body and mind refreshed, he then rose from the base of the door of the peaked pavilion. Gazing for a moment with unblinking eyes at the Great Peaked Pavilion— the Womb of the Arrayed Ornament of Vairocana— he joined his palms in reverence, circumambulated it hundreds of thousands of times, and directed his mind toward such perceptions and mental attentions.
He spoke these words: "This is the abode of those who dwell in the dwelling of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
this is the abode of those who dwell in the dwelling of non-conceptualization regarding all phenomena;
[this is the abode] of those who dwell in the dwelling of the undifferentiated realm of phenomena, and of those who dwell in the dwelling of the non-apprehension of the realm of sentient beings."

[They are] those who dwell in the dwelling of the non-arising of all phenomena; those who dwell in the dwelling of having no home in any world; those who dwell in the dwelling of having no abode or refuge in the entire world; those who dwell in the dwelling of being unstained by anything; those who dwell in the dwelling of not relying on any support; those who dwell in the dwelling of not relying on any physical form; those who dwell in the dwelling of having shaken off all conceptualizations regarding the afflictions; those who dwell in the dwelling of the lack of intrinsic nature in all phenomena; and those who dwell in the dwelling of being free from all discursive thought, conceptualization, and non-conceptualization.

They dwell in a state secluded from all perceptions, thoughts, and mental activities; they dwell in a state free from the accumulation and rejection of all perceptions; they dwell in a state of entry into the profound perfection of wisdom; they dwell in a state of skillful means that pervades the entire realm of phenomena through universal gateways; they dwell in a state of skillful means that pacifies all afflictions everywhere; and they dwell in a state of supreme wisdom that has abandoned all views, cravings, and pride.

This is the abode of those who dwell in the playful mastery of generating all meditations, liberations, concentrations, attainments, and superknowledges; who dwell in the practice of the range of all bodhisattva samādhis; who dwell in the state of relying upon the presence at the feet of all Buddhas; and who dwell in the state of entering into one eon as all eons, and all eons as one eon.

Those who dwell in the dwelling of the non-differentiation of all fields within a single field; those who dwell in the dwelling of the non-contradiction of all phenomena within a single phenomenon; those who dwell in the dwelling of the non-duality of all sentient beings within a single sentient being.

Those who dwell in the non-dual abode of the single Buddha and all Buddhas, and all Buddhas and the single Buddha; those who dwell in the abode of entering all objects of knowledge in a single moment;
those who dwell in the abode of traveling to all buddha-fields with the arising of a single thought.
Those who dwell in the abode that is the manifestation of the palaces of all sentient beings; those who dwell in the abode of the mental state intent on the welfare and happiness of the entire world;
those who dwell in the abode of having attained complete self-mastery.
This is their dwelling place:
those who have risen above the worldly abode yet appear within the dwellings of all worlds for the sake of maturing all sentient beings;
those who are independent of all fields yet traverse through all fields for the purpose of making offerings to the Tathāgatas.
Those who traverse all buddha-fields in order to embrace the array of all buddha-fields,
yet do not wander from their place;
those who have gone to the feet of all Tathāgatas, yet are free from attachment to the notion of "Buddha."
Those who dwell in reliance upon all spiritual friends as their support, and for whom there is no one equal to them in wisdom throughout the entire world;
those who dwell within the abodes of all the palaces of Māra, yet remain detached from the pleasures of the sensory qualities.
Those who dwell in the abiding that enters into all states of perception, yet whose minds are shaken free from all states of perception;

those whose bodies follow after the bodies of all living beings, yet do not dwell in the duality of self and sentient being; those whose bodies enter into all world-systems, yet do not dwell in the fragmentation of the realm of phenomena.
Those who have made vows to dwell throughout all future eons, yet do not abide in the perception of eons as being either long or short;
those who remain within the path of a single hair and do not waver.
And they are seen in all world-systems;

for them who dwell in the dwelling of entering the direction of the Dharma that is difficult to approach, who dwell in the dwelling that is difficult to comprehend, who dwell in the profound dwelling, who dwell in the non-dual dwelling, who dwell in the signless dwelling, who dwell in the dwelling that is without opposition, and who dwell in the dwelling of non-apprehension— (Gv 371)

This is the dwelling of those who dwell in the dwelling of non-proliferation; those who dwell in the dwelling of great loving-kindness and great compassion; those who dwell in the dwelling that is difficult for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas to fathom; those who dwell in the dwelling that has completely transcended the realm of all Māras; those who dwell in the dwelling that is unsullied by the realm of all worlds; those who dwell in the dwelling of all the bodhisattva perfections; and those who dwell in the dwelling that accords with the dwellings of all Buddhas.
Those who dwell having departed from all signs,
yet do not enter the fixed course of the disciples;
those who dwell in the dwelling of the non-arising of all phenomena.
And they do not fall into the state of non-arising;
those who dwell in the practice of the meditation on impurity, yet do not personally realize the dharma-nature of the fading away of passion.
And they do not dwell together with qualities of passion;
those who abide in the dwelling of loving-kindness have minds that have not fallen into the stain of hatred.
They dwell in the dwelling of dependent origination and are utterly undeluded regarding all phenomena;
they are those who dwell in the four dhyānas.
And they are not reborn by the power of meditative absorption;
for those who dwell in the practice of the four immeasurables do not go to the realm of form, yet they do so for the sake of maturing all sentient beings.
Those who dwell in the meditative absorptions of the four formless attainments,
yet do not go to the realm of the formless because they are sustained by great compassion;
and those who dwell in the meditative absorptions of tranquility and insight.
Yet they do not personally realize knowledge and liberation for the sake of maturing all sentient beings;
though they dwell in the abode of great equanimity,
they do not abandon the realm of sentient beings.
Those who dwell in the dwelling of emptiness, yet do not rely on any speculative views;
those whose range is the signless, yet who are intent upon the method for leading beings who course in signs.
Those who are free from all vows and have severed the vows of a bodhisattva;
those who are masters over all karma and afflictions,
yet appear to follow the power of karma and afflictions for the sake of maturing sentient beings.
Those who have fully understood the nature of death and rebirth, yet manifest birth, transition, and death;
those who have transcended all states of existence, yet...
And they go through all states of existence by virtue of their mastery over the discipline of all beings;
those who dwell in loving-kindness do not dwell in attachment toward anything whatsoever.
Those who dwell in compassion do not dwell anywhere with a view of uncertainty;
those who dwell in sympathetic joy are yet constantly agitated by their contemplation of all who suffer.
Those who dwell in equanimity regarding the affairs of others,
and those who dwell in the attainment of the nine successive meditative states,
do not loathe rebirth in the desire realm.
Those who dwell without relying on any form of rebirth, yet do not dwell in the realization of the limit of reality;
those who dwell in the three liberations, yet...
Nor do they dwell in the contact with liberation of the śrāvakas;
rather, they dwell in the contemplation of the four noble truths,
yet they do not dwell in the realization of the fruits.
Those who dwell in the investigation of profound dependent origination, yet do not dwell in ultimate falling away;
those who dwell in the cultivation of the noble eightfold path; and—
Nor do they dwell in ultimate departure;
yet they dwell having transcended the stage of ordinary worldlings, and they do not dwell in a manner that would cause them to fall to the stages of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
Those who dwell in the thorough knowledge of the five aggregates of clinging, yet do not dwell in the absolute cessation of the aggregates;
those who dwell having transcended the path of the four Māras;
And they do not dwell in the conceptualization of Māra;
those who dwell having transcended the six sense-bases,
yet do not dwell in absolute non-arising.
Those who dwell in suchness,
yet do not dwell in the sphere of the limit of reality;
those who dwell in the manifestation of departure by means of all vehicles.
And this is not the dwelling of those who abide in falling away from the Mahāyāna; rather, it is the dwelling of those who abide in all virtues.
Then, at that time, the merchant’s son Sudhana spoke these verses:
“Here is Maitreya, the possessor of great compassion and pure awakening, whose glory is loving-kindness, and who is devoted to the welfare of the world.”
The eldest son of the Victors, established on the stage of consecration, dwells contemplating the domain of the Buddhas. // 1 //

This is the dwelling place of all those highly renowned sons of the Conquerors, who are established in liberation and whose sphere is great wisdom; it is the abode of those peerless individuals who traverse the realm of phenomena without attachment. // 2 //

This is the dwelling of those who have emerged through the powers of self-control, generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and vigor; who have reached the further shore by means of the meditative concentrations and the power of the superknowledges; who are established in the powers of wisdom, skillful means, and aspiration; and who have attained the perfections of the Mahāyāna. // 3 //
This is the dwelling place of those with unattached minds and vast intentions, who delight in the sphere of space and are non-dependent;
who pervade all three times and are unobstructed, having clearly realized the nature of all states of existence. // 4 //

Those who have entered the method of the non-arising of all phenomena and contemplate the nature of phenomena as being like the essence of space—those skilled in wisdom whose dwelling is such that they do not rely on anything anywhere, just as a bird does not rely on the sky. // 5 //

Those who, having understood that passion, hatred, and delusion are by nature a false engagement produced by the cause of conceptual construction, and who thus cultivate non-conceptuality—the state consisting of dispassion—for those who have attained this path of peace and perfect tranquility, this is the dwelling place. // 6 //

Those who thoroughly examine the gates of liberation, the truths, the methods, the meanings, and the paths, as well as the aggregates, the sense bases, and the dependent nature of sentient beings—those wise ones do not fall [into error]; this is the dwelling of those skilled in tranquility, wisdom, and skillful means. // 7 //

Those who have entered the direction of unobstructed knowledge, for whom the conceptual constructions and discriminations regarding sentient beings in the Buddha-field have been stilled, and who do not scrutinize phenomena as being devoid of intrinsic nature—they belong to this abode of those whose ultimate goal is peace. (8)
Those who, having practiced without attachment, traverse this realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), free from conceptualization, having become like birds in the wind;
they have abandoned all dwellings and move without a home—for those whose minds are non-reliant, this is their dwelling. // 9 //

Those whose abodes are filled with the intention of loving-kindness and compassion—those who, through the light of their loving-kindness, pacify all states of woe for people who have fallen into the miserable paths of wrong views, who are weary, and who experience the bitter sensations of various sufferings; this is their dwelling place. (10)

This monastery belongs to those who, seeing the world here—fallen into the perils of saṃsāra, lost on the noble path, like a caravan blind from birth and deprived of its guide—lead it onto the path of liberation, acting like a leader of a merchant caravan. (11)

To those heroes, who are exceedingly difficult to conquer, belongs this [victory]: they who, having seen the world brought under the power of birth, sorrow, old age, and death, and bound by the noose of Namuci’s neck, have liberated it and led it toward the direction of fearlessness and security. 12.
Having observed these people afflicted by the diseases of the afflictions (*kleśa*), they gather the great medicinal herbs of the knowledge of immortality;
having generated vast compassion, they liberate them—this is the dwelling of those who resemble the Great King of Physicians. (13)

Those who, having observed the people suffering here, fallen into a pit of sorrow leading to the ocean of death and without protection, ferry them across by means of the great ship of the pure Dharma—may there be a dwelling for those who are like the sons of a boatman. 14.

Those pure beings whose minds are like the jewel of omniscience, who, having observed the people wandering in the ocean of afflictions, descend into the ocean of existence and rescue them—this is their dwelling, resembling that of a fisherman’s son. 15.

This is the dwelling of those who, having entered the storehouse of their vows and beheld the abodes of all sentient beings with a vision of compassion and loving-kindness, rescue the people dwelling in the ocean of existence, resembling the ship of the Lord of Garuḍas. (16)

Those who, like the moon and sun in the sky of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), move about having attained manifestation within the abodes of sentient beings; this dwelling consists of the spheres of their vows and the rays of wisdom that bring light to the world. (17)

Those steadfast ones who remain for ten million eons until the very end of time for the sake of maturing even a single sentient being—just as they would for one being, so too do they dwell for the sake of the entire world without exception; such are those who have the world as their ultimate refuge. 18.

Those who traverse the course of conduct for the sake of the world’s welfare throughout kalpas as numerous as atoms in a single field, with untiring vigor—just as it is in one field, so it is in all the ten directions; such is the dwelling of those whose resolve is as firm as a diamond. (19)

Those who, seated upon a single throne, undeludedly drink in the Clouds of Dharma from the Sugatas throughout the ten directions for millions of eons until the end of time, their minds never satiated—this is the dwelling that is equal to the ocean of wisdom. // 20 //

This is the dwelling of those whose conduct is unattached, who travel to ineffable oceans of buddha-fields and enter the oceans of assemblies of the Leaders; and who perform various oceans of worship for the Victors. (21)

And those steadfast ones who, having entered the noble ocean, plunge into the infinite and centerless ocean of vows, and who practice for an ocean of many eons for the sake of the welfare of the world—for those mines of all virtues, this is the dwelling place. (22)

Those who cross over the path of a single hair from a field, and enter into Buddhas and sentient beings throughout infinite and middleless eons, yet do not return nor reach the boundary—this is the dwelling of those whose vision is unattached. // 23 //

Those who, in a single moment of thought, enter into oceans of great eons, as well as into fields, Buddhas, and the movements of the world—they who abide in unobstructed wisdom and have risen to the perfection of virtues—this is their dwelling. 24.

Having counted all the atoms within every buddha-field, and having measured the entire mass of water by the size of its drops, those who bring forth vows of such magnitude— this is the dwelling of those who have attained non-attachment. (25)

Having entered the gateways of vows, dhāraṇīs, and samādhis, as well as the meditative concentrations, liberations, and gateways of aspiration, those mindful sons of the Sugatas, having attained these, traverse infinite eons here. (26)
Established here, these various and diverse sons of the Conquerors bring forth many treatises endowed with the meaning of discourse;
contemplating the fields of craft that bring happiness to the world, they dwell in the dwelling place of the virtuous. (27)

Established here in great supernormal knowledge and skillful means, they manifest throughout all the various realms of existence in the ten directions, displaying every distinction of birth and death; abiding in liberation as if it were an illusion, their conduct is unimpeded. (28)
Abiding here, they display the first arising of the thought of enlightenment and the practice of Dharma that culminates in the nature of reality;
having filled the entire realm of phenomena with dense emanations, they thus manifest hundreds of such miraculous transformations. (29)

Those who, with a single expansion of mind, awaken to enlightenment and enter into knowledge and wisdom that are without end or middle—considering how the world wanders through the banner of delusion—this is the dwelling of those whose state is difficult to approach. (30)

This is the dwelling of those whose minds are unattached, who traverse the unobstructed realm of phenomena, whose sphere of activity is non-apprehension, and whose intellects possess pure intentions. // 31 //
Those who move without attachment, dwelling without a home in all fields, and who abide in non-dual gnosis—this is the dwelling of those incomparable ones. 32.
Those who dwell in these phenomena that are equal to their own nature—unattached and peaceful—they, the stainless ones, have their abode in the sphere of space. 33.
Abiding here with a mind of compassionate intent, they behold the world struck by suffering and grief;
devoted to contemplating the welfare of the world, they dwell having attained great compassion. (34)
(376) Here they are seen, unimpeded, within the abodes of all sentient beings;
released from the snares of saṃsāra by means of the moon and sun disk samādhis. // 35 //
Here these sons of the Jinas stand at the feet of all the Jinas;
they are seen in all fields throughout infinite eons as they pass away.
Here, they pervade all directions without exception with clouds of emanations, which are equal in extent to the world-systems and as vast as the abodes of all the sons of the Victors. (37)
Having entered here, those heroes, weighing the entire range of the Victor’s domain, dwell for millions of eons and yet do not reach satiety. (38)
Here, through their wisdom, they manifest in every moment incalculable millions of samādhis, displaying the domain of the Buddhas according to their entry into samādhi. (39)
Here, those of vast intelligence, taking hold of moments, enter into the names of Buddhas throughout kalpa-fields; they exhaust immeasurable kalpas.
Established here for immeasurable eons, they enter [into realization] with a single mind;
free from the perceptions of conceptual construction, they have transcended being under the sway of worldly perceptions. // 41 //

Established here in the cultivation of meditative concentration, they perceive the three times; having reached the pinnacle of a single moment, they move about within the abode of liberation. // 42 //
Remaining here in this monastery, seated cross-legged with their bodies unmoving, they are seen simultaneously in all fields, having gone everywhere. (43)
Dwelling here, these bulls drink from the ocean of the Dharma of the Sugatas;
having entered the sea of wisdom, they have attained the perfection of inexhaustible qualities. // 44 //
Here, those whose thoughts are unobstructed contemplate the number of all buddha-fields, the number of eons, the number of dharmas, and the number of all Victors. (45)
Here these sons of the Jina remain, as many as the fields reckoned throughout the three times; in a single instant, they investigate their arising and passing away. (46)
Abiding here, they perceive the conduct, the vows, and the faculties of the Jinas and of all beings;
beholding these equalities, they move about within the abode of the sons of the Jinas.
Those who, within this [samādhi], see upon a single atom all atoms without obstruction—the oceans of assemblies, the buddha-fields, sentient beings, and the eons—[attain this state]. 48.
Upon the tips of all atoms, they clearly perceive all the surrounding fields, as well as the eons and the beings, all appearing as reflections and perfectly distinct. // 49 //
Here, they investigate the intrinsic nature of phenomena— the Buddhas of all fields, times, and eons— who are free from the intrinsic nature of existence through methods that are non-arising. (50)

Abiding here in the equality of sentient beings and perceiving the equality of all phenomena and the equality of Buddhas, they enter into the equality of realms and the equality of vows throughout the three times. // 51 //
Some discipline millions of beings, others honor millions of Buddhas;
still others contemplate the dharmas here—those steadfast ones established in this supreme palace. (52)
For even with millions of conceptualizations, my own mental constructs are unable to describe the scope of the vows and knowledge of those whose wisdom is vast and infinite. (53)
With palms joined in reverence and body bowed low, I pay homage to the abode of those blameless ones who delight in the unobstructed sphere of activity. (54)
Following that, I, mindful, bow down to the eldest son of the Jina, the noble Maitreya, whose conduct is free from obscuration and whose intellect is incomparable and pure. (55)

Thus, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having praised the bodhisattvas dwelling within the great peaked palace, the Matrix of the Array of Vairocana’s Ornaments, with such immeasurable hymns of bodhisattva praise; having bowed, paid homage, prostrated, gazed upon them, marveled at them,
brought them to mind, and fully honored them, [stood] before the great peaked palace, the Matrix of the Array of Vairocana’s Ornaments.
Remaining at the base, longing for a vision of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya and desiring an encounter with the Bodhisattva Maitreya,

he saw the Bodhisattva Maitreya approaching from a certain spot outside the gabled hall, accompanied by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of living beings and preceded by many lords of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.

He was being saluted on his left and right by Śakra, Brahmā, and the world-protectors, and was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of brahmins who were kinsmen and relatives from his native land; he was approaching toward the peaked palace whose interior was adorned with the array of Vairocana.

Upon seeing him, he became joyful, elated, uplifted, and thrilled, filled with gladness and happiness; turning toward where the Bodhisattva Maitreya was, even from afar, he faced the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
He prostrated with his entire body.

Then the Bodhisattva Maitreya, having looked at the merchant’s son Sudhana and pointing him out to the entire assembly with his right hand, praised him for his actual virtues and addressed them in verse: "Behold this Sudhana, whose intention is perfectly pure, the son of Dṛḍhadhana!
Seeking the conduct of supreme enlightenment, this wise one has come into my presence. (56)
Welcome, O you who arise from compassion and love! Welcome, O you whose mandala is vast loving-kindness!
Welcome, O you with eyes of peaceful tranquility! May you not grow weary as you carry out your wandering. 57.
Come, welcome, O you of pure intention; come, welcome, O you of untiring mind. Come, welcome, O you with unflagging faculties; do not grow weary, O gentle one, continue to practice. 58.
Arisen for the investigation of all phenomena, eager for the discipline of all beings, set out to attend upon all spiritual friends—welcome to you, O Immovable One of firm vows! (59)
Welcome, you who have come by the auspicious path; welcome, you who are established on the path of virtue;
welcome, you who have set out upon the path of the Victors—do not weary yourself in vain anywhere.
"Come, welcome! Because you are absorbed in virtuous qualities, you are welcomed by me; may there be an outflow of wholesome things.
Welcome, O one whose range is infinite! Your appearance is very difficult to obtain in the world. (61)
With minds equanimous toward gain and loss, free from blame, suffering, and ill-repute, like a lotus unstained by worldly dharmas—welcome, O you of unerring mind! (62)
Free from deceit and guile, O one of pure intention; free from pride and arrogance, O worthy vessel;
free from anger and wrath, O unassuming one—your sight is excellent, a most auspicious vision. (63)
Come, you whose face has the range of all directions as its domain! Come, you who arise from the treasury of all directions!
Come, you who increase the treasury of all Victors! Welcome to you, O you whose mind is untiring! 64.

Come, welcome! O you whose sphere of activity is the three times, whose mandala is the resolve for the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), born from the womb of all the qualities of the Buddhas—welcome to you, O tireless and gentle one! 65.
Come, Mañjuśrījñānapaṅkaja! Come, Meghaśirī, nourished by the waters!
Come, you who have been sent by all the Sons of the Victors; I shall show you the direction that is unobstructed. (66)
Behold what kind of web of vows it is—this inconceivable pervasion of the realm of phenomena, which draws forth the path of the bodhisattva’s conduct; let Sudhana come here to expand upon it. (67)
Seeking the domain of the Sugatas, searching for the stainless course of conduct, and inquiring about the ocean of vows, he has arrived here with an untiring mind. (68)
He has come here to inquire about that conduct in which the leaders of the past were trained, those of the future will likewise train, and that which belongs to the Sugatas currently remaining.
"O Mitra, these Dharma-preachers of mine, who teach the practice of all dharmas and show the path of the conduct of a bodhisattva—they have come here with this very intention. (70)

The Bodhisattvas increase my intelligence; they, the sons of the Buddha, bestow awakening upon me. These friends praised by the Buddhas have come here to this world, being skilled in the mind. // 71 //
These people are like mothers to me, acting as my nurses; they provide the milk of virtue and always protect the factors of enlightenment. They are my friends who ward off what is unbeneficial. (72)
They are like physicians who liberate from old age and death; they are like Śakra, raining down the nectar of immortality;
they are like the moon, with their auspicious and full disks; they are like the sun, showing the path to bliss. // 73 //
Like Mount Meru, he is equal toward friends and enemies; like the ocean, his mind is unshakeable. Like a helmsman and protector, he is free from thought-constructs; thus Sudhana has come here. (74)
These heroes who bestow fearlessness, the caravan leaders, the refuge, the ultimate resort, and the guides who grant me happiness—this is the very mind with which one serves such friends. (75)
They clearly perceive all directions of phenomena; they always reveal the qualities and wisdom of all Buddhas;
they purify all miserable states and lower realms; these friends of mine appear to me most excellently. (76)
These are the givers of the treasury of all Victors; these are the guardians of the storehouse of all Victors;
these are the holders of the secrets of all Victors—it is to such as these that the wise person resorts as friends. (77)
Therefore, the perfection of knowledge is purified, as are the perfections of form, enjoyments, family, and birth;
thus, such an intention is not difficult to attain, for he has come here for this very purpose. // 78 //
Behold this wise one of noble intention who serves these friends; observe how he behaves toward them, and you too should always train yourselves in that same gentleness. (79)

This one, having set out for enlightenment after seeing Mañjuśrī by virtue of the causes of former auspicious merit, is giving him instruction; look how he moves about tirelessly while performing it! (80)

Having abandoned and cast aside this home like that of the immortals, which possesses every pleasure and comfort, and having relinquished the abundance of nurses, mothers, fathers, and enjoyments, he serves this friend as if he were a slave. (81)
Having purified this intention, the wise one shall abandon this human basis;
he will enter the abode of all Buddhas—such will be the fruit resulting from this. (82)
Having seen living beings afflicted by the diseases of worldly existence, overwhelmed by hundreds of sufferings,
and tormented by the fear and grief of birth and death, he, whose mind is intent on compassion, acts for their benefit.

Having seen the world oppressed by the machine of suffering within the wheel of the five realms of existence, he firmly seeks the diamond-like wisdom that shatters the machine of suffering and the wheel of rebirth. (84)

Seeking to purify the field of sentient beings—which is overgrown with the weeds and thorns of passion and hatred, infested by the many snares of views, and its sprouts wounded—he searches for the firm plow of wisdom. (85)
The world has a mind shrouded by the thicket of delusion and ignorance; its guide is lost and its eye of wisdom destroyed.
For this world, he will become a caravan leader, the master who shows the direction of safety.

Carrying the vehicle of patience, the Dharma, and the three liberations, wielding the sword of wisdom that subdues the enemy afflictions, he will become a hero who bestows fearlessness and a guide for all the worlds. // 87 //

This one, well-trained on the path to the ocean of wisdom, gathers the ship of Dharma; he is the helmsman in the ocean of the three realms of existence, leading the way to the supreme jewel-island of peace. (88)

This sun of a Buddha, whose mandala consists of the vow of the rays of wisdom and who illuminates the worlds of all sentient beings, shall now arise with great radiance in the sky of the realm of phenomena. 89.

Cool as sandalwood with its fragrance of loving-kindness, possessing a radiant light through a mind of equanimity toward all beings, this moon of a Buddha shall arise, its orb perfected by pure dharmas. 90.
Firmly established upon the foundation of the resolute intention, the conduct of awakening has gradually arisen;
for this mine of the jewels of all dharmas shall become a supreme ocean of wisdom. 91.
Born from the king of serpents that is the thought of awakening, it rises into the sky of the realm of phenomena;
by raining down simultaneously from the clouds of Dharma, it causes the harvest of all white fruits to flourish. // 92 //

With a pure wick, removing the three stains and dispelling darkness, a firm vessel for loving-kindness, affection, and mindfulness, and possessing the brilliant light of the stainless fire of the thought of awakening, he will kindle this lamp of the Dharma. (93)

With the *kalala* of the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), the *arbuda* of compassion, the *peśī* of loving-kindness, and the *ghana* of the intention for joy, this embryo of a Buddha (*buddhagarbha*) grows, gradually giving rise to the limbs of enlightenment. (94)
He will cause the womb of merit to increase and he will also purify the womb of wisdom;
this is designated as the womb of wisdom, arising from the womb of his vow. // 95 //

One such as this—one armored in compassion and loving-kindness, whose intention is beneficial and whose mind is intent on liberating sentient beings—possessing a mind so utterly pure as this, is rare in the world including its gods and humans. (96)
Established with such a root of noble intention, increased by such firm application,
and possessing such power to cover the three realms of existence— this tree of wisdom that bears fruit is exceedingly rare. (96)
Seeking the arising of virtues, seeking to inquire about all dharmas, and seeking to tear asunder all doubts, he tirelessly attends upon all spiritual friends. // 97 //
He is the destroyer of Māra, the age of strife, and the afflictions; he is the purifier of the stains of views and craving;
he is intent upon liberating the entire world; he is your truly distinguished and wise friend. 98.
He will purify the miserable realms; he will reveal the heavens; he will lead the world to the path of liberation, established as he is upon the path of such virtues. (99)

He is the liberator from the suffering of all states of existence; he is the bestower of happiness in all realms of rebirth; he is the severer of the bonds of all becoming, and he shall be the destroyer of the course of worldly existence. // 100 //

He will liberate one from the peril of views, he will cut through the creeping vine of the net of craving; he will purify delight and attachment, and he will become a guide for the path out of the three realms of existence. // 101 //
He will be the refuge and final resort of the world, the illuminator of the entire universe; he will become the leader of the three realms, skilled in bringing all existence to an end. (102)

This wise one shall be the purifier of people sleeping in the afflictions, the ferryman who carries them across the mire of desire, the liberator of those attached to perceptions, and the one who effects both bondage and liberation. // 103 //

Illuminating the distinctions within the depths of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), purifying the distinctions within the depths of the world-systems (*lokadhātu*), and having reached the further shore of the distinctions within the depths of all phenomena—O Sudhana, you shall become such; therefore, be joyful! (104)
In accordance with your application, O gentle one, in accordance with your irreproachable faith, and in accordance with your virtuous intention, he shall fulfill everything for you. (105)
Before long you shall see all the Buddhas; before long you shall go to all the fields; before long you shall know all dharmas—such is the auspiciousness wrought by yourself. (106)
You will purify an ocean of fields; you will liberate an ocean of sentient beings;
you will fulfill an ocean of conduct—such is your ocean of practice.
You will become a vessel for virtues; you will be the source of auspiciousness.
You will become equal to the sons of the Victors, in accordance with the sphere of your resolute faith. 108.
The mandala of Māra has been conquered by you, and the mandala of karma has been purified by you;
the mandala of afflictions has been purified by you, just like the mandala of your vow. (109)
You shall purify the path of knowledge and illuminate the path of Dharma;
before long, you shall bring to an end the mechanism of the wheel of karma, afflictions, and suffering.
Relying upon the wheel of the world and the wheel of existence, which is deluded by the wheel of the fivefold realms of rebirth,
you shall set in motion the tree of the Wheel of Dharma that cuts through the wheel of suffering for all sentient beings. (111)
You will uphold the lineage of the Buddhas, you will purify the lineage of the Dharma, you will lead the lineage of the Saṅgha, and you will become a source from which the Jewels arise. // 112 //
You will turn back the net of craving, and likewise the dense thicket of the net of views;
you will liberate the world from the net of suffering, for such is the net of your vow that has been purified. (113)
You will bring the realm of sentient beings to maturity; you will purify the world-realm;
you will give rise to the realm of gnosis—such is the nature of your own disposition.

Rejoicing in the welfare and joy of all sentient beings, delighting in the lineage of the Bodhisattva family, and rejoicing in the vows of all Buddhas, you shall become, Sudhana, an increaser of joy. (115)
Beholding the dwelling places of all beings' destinies, beholding the reflections of all fields, and beholding the illumination of all phenomena, you shall become the Victor Sudarśana. // 116 //

With light that illuminates the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and light that brings peace to all miserable destinies, you shall become the one who brings an end to the suffering of the three realms of existence. // 117 //
You will show the gateway to heaven; you will open the gateway of the Buddhas for the world;
you will lead the world to the gateway of liberation, for such a gateway has been purified by you. (118)
You will turn back from the false path and lead the multitude to the noble path;
O you of firm intelligence, you seek the path to awakening thus, undisturbed and untiring.

You are eager to lead embodied beings who have entered the ocean of existence to the further shore beyond suffering; therefore, become such an ocean of great virtues and deliver the world from the ocean of existence. 120.
Having dried up the ocean of afflictions for embodied beings with the oceans of the excellent rays of the sun of wisdom,
you will establish them in the ocean of practice and cause them to be firmly established in the ocean of knowledge.
You will cause the ocean of wisdom to increase, you will purify the ocean of conduct, and before long, you will plunge into the ocean of the vows of all Buddhas. // 122 //
You will enter many oceans of fields and behold many oceans of assemblies; by the power of the ocean of wisdom, O wise one, you shall [attain]... // 123 //
You will behold tens of millions of clouds of Buddhas and perform vast clouds of worship;
you will hear tens of millions of clouds of Dharma and make such clouds of vows.
You shall pervade the abodes of all sentient beings, you shall go to the abodes of all fields, and you shall enter the abode of all Buddhas; for you have set out upon such a direction.
You shall enter the palace of meditative concentration; you shall attain the palaces of liberation;
established in the palace of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). // 126 //
You shall arise within the existence of all sentient beings, resembling the reflection of the moon and sun;
you shall go forth in the presence of the Victors, for such is the emergence of your great path.
You will move about, bowed down, within the excellent sphere of activity that is the sphere of activity of those who have no home in any world;
you will become one whose sphere of activity is perfectly tranquil—such indeed shall be your sphere of supernormal knowledge.

Just as one who knows how to pierce the surface of a magician’s net can pierce the surface of the field of perception, you will before long behold the radiant atom, like the wind moving unimpeded in the sky. 129.

You will enter the expanse of the realm of phenomena; you will traverse the expanses of the world-realms; you will behold the expanses of all Buddhas throughout the three times, O Sudhana—may you find joy! 130.
Do not give way to despondency; rather, find vast, dispassionate satisfaction in gentleness, by which you have seen this liberation such as it is, and having seen it, you shall see it again. 131.
O Subhājana, you are a worthy vessel for the virtues found within the instructions of the Jinas;
you are capable of upholding this method, and for that reason you behold this miraculous manifestation. // 132 //

How much more so for those sons of the Buddha, who dwell without a fixed abode and practice a sublime conduct, whose sight is extremely difficult to obtain even in ten million eons— those very ones have been seen by you as they move about, manifesting their virtues.
The gains are further vast and inconceivable; welcome to you, O human being!
For by you, Mañjuśrī, has been seen face-to-face that which makes one such a vessel for virtues. (134)
All paths to miserable rebirths have been increased [in their abandonment]; you are the purifier of all unfavorable conditions and states of woe.
All phenomena of suffering have been relinquished by you; may you be free from all weariness. 135.
You have turned back from the stage of the foolish and are well-established on the stage of the qualities of a bodhisattva;
having fulfilled the supreme stage of gnosis, you will attain the stage of a Buddha before long. 136.

The conduct of a bodhisattva is like the ocean, and the method of the Buddha’s wisdom is like space; the oceans of his vows are equal in measure to these—may he remain with a joyful mind throughout these existences. (137)
Those who associate with such friends as these—whose faculties are untiring, whose intentions are firm, and whose application is certain—will before long become leaders themselves. (138)

Having seen the many diverse practices of the bodhisattvas through which beings have attained discipline, you must never harbor any doubt regarding this practice of awakening, which is the gateway to all dharmas. (139)
Inconceivable is your perfection of merit, and your perfection of wealth, dharma, virtue, and faith;
by means of these perfections, O Son of the Buddha, you behold such [a sight] here today. (140)
Behold what a great gain is yours, as the sons of the Jina constantly reveal their respective vows; and you follow them all without exception. (141)
Such vessels for the conduct of Bodhisattvas are difficult to find even in hundreds of lifetimes;
therefore, those sons of the Conquerors have continuously shown me the way of liberation.
For millions of billions of eons, those people dwell together with the sons of the Sugata;
yet they do not perceive their sphere of activity, for they have not made themselves into vessels of such qualities.
You hear such a teaching as this and behold the very rare marvel in the world—the miraculous display of the great Bodhisattvas; therefore, Sudhana, be one whose mind is supreme. 144.
All the Buddhas attend to you, O Bodhisattva, for they abide in your gathering; and you abide in their instruction. Well done, Sudhana! Your life is well-lived. 145.

You abide in the family dharma of the Bodhisattvas and train in the virtues of the Sons of the Conquerors; you shall become one who increases the lineage of the Sugatas—rejoice, Sudhana, in this noble [state]! 146.
All Buddhas are your incomparable fathers; all Bodhisattvas are your brothers.
All factors of enlightenment are your kinsmen; you are well-born, the legitimate son of the Sugatas. (147)

You who uphold the lineage of the family of the Dharma King and increase the lineage of the family of Bodhisattvas—O Sudhana, you shall before long obtain the status of a Dharma King; be satisfied and have your faculties gladdened! (148)
Before long, you shall obtain the supreme and wondrous consecration of all the Buddhas; you shall become equal to the sons of the Jinas who are peerless—become such as they, become their equal. 149.
Whatever kind of seed a person sows, such is the fruit they receive;
find vast and inconceivable joy, for today I grant this to you. 150.

Even those who have practiced for ten million eons and followed the inconceivable conduct of ten million bodhisattvas do not attain such perfection as this which you have obtained in a single lifetime. (151)
All this fruit here arises from liberation, from one's intention, and from firm vigor;
whoever would find this course dear should maintain the conduct of Sudhana. 152.
The arising of all conduct and vows, the arising of conviction in all dharmas—these have been fully gathered by you, Sudhana; for this is indeed your constant practice of excellence. (153)
Just as that which arises from the consciousness of a serpent becomes that which arises from water,
so too that which is the domain of the wisdom of aspiration expands as the practice of awakening.
Sudhana, this practice of the one named Bhadra has been shown to you by her;
having understood this, he will at some time become one who serves here, devoted to those friends. (155)
Remember the millions of bodies you have previously wasted in vain for the sake of desire;
today, let this body, seeking awakening, be disciplined by the vow of one who is well-vowed. (156)
For many millions of eons you have endured every suffering within conditioned existence;
though you have encountered Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, you have never heard such a teaching as this. (157)
Now that this human moment has been obtained and such a friend as the Buddha’s feet is found, and the sublime conduct of awakening is heard—how could there not be purification? 158.
The appearance of Sugatas occurs again and again, and the hearing of the Dharma of friends is heard;
yet this method is not heard again if one’s intention has not been purified. (159)

Therefore, having generated faith, resolute conviction, and intention, and having developed supreme reverence for the teacher, free from the exhaustion of doubt and wrong views, listen again and again to such a method as this. (160)

For those by whom such a practice as this has been brought forth through their vows, upon merely hearing it, their gain is supreme and inconceivable; for them, this human existence is truly well-attained. (161)

For one who has purified their resolute faith, all the Sugatas are not difficult to encounter, nor are all the sons of the Jinas far away; for such a person, there is no longer any doubt regarding awakening. (162)

By him all forms of discipline have been mastered; by him all states of suffering have been abandoned; by him the collection of all virtues has been achieved—whoever has entered such a method as this. // 163 //
Before long, having cast off this body, you will go to a pure buddha-field;
you will enter the abode of the bodhisattvas and behold the Tathāgatas in the ten directions. 164.
O you of excellent wealth, whose former causes were dense, your present resolve is certain;
seeking excellence, you serve as friends, and by that you flourish like a lotus in the water. 165.

With the intention of pleasing all friends, with the intention of gratifying all Buddhas, and with the intention of inquiring about all dharmas, those of good vows do not give rise to weariness or fatigue. 166.
Arising from the practice of all dharmas, well-established in following every path,
son of the Buddha, well-established in your vow, arise, you who are a vessel for all virtuous qualities! 167.
Because you have performed this prostration to me with such perfection of resolute faith, you shall indeed before long arise in the presence of all the assemblies of Buddhas. 168.
Excellent, Sudhana, you whose mind is untiring and whose intention is the vow of all Buddhas!
You shall before long become one of firm vows, having reached the perfection of all the qualities of a Buddha.
"O being Mañjuśrī, ask Sudhana, who has reached the further shore of the liberation that is the domain of wisdom;
he will cause you to enter the supreme, excellent, and auspicious conduct at the end of this body."
Thus, Sudhana, having seen Maitrākṣa— whose range is unattached and who has arisen through his virtues— he displayed him before the assembly and proclaimed this treasury of his praises.
Having then heard such an instruction and this supreme exhortation from Sudhana,
his faculties overflowing with a surge of joy, he shed a great flood of tears.
With his body arising from the thrill of all his hairs standing on end, and his senses completely gratified,
Sudhana rose up with palms joined in reverence and performed a circumambulation of the one named Maitra.
By that splendor of Mañjuśrī, beautiful and delightful flower-garlands and jewels, born from the vows of the Bodhisattva, remained in their hands. (174)
Sudhana, his mind supremely joyful, cast those [flowers] with delight before Maitreya; then the Lord Maitreya stroked his head and spoke to Sudhana. (175)
Excellent, excellent, O Son of the Conqueror Sudhana! Since you possess such tireless perseverance, you shall become a vessel of virtues just like Mañjughoṣa and as I am myself. 176.

Having heard this, Sudhana uttered these inspired utterances: "Such friends as these are difficult to find even in hundreds of lifetimes; that I have met them here is a blessing, and my arrival here today is truly fruitful. (177)
Excellent! O Mañjughoṣa, you who have reached the perfection of the qualities of a being, by your power I have obtained these friends so difficult to find; may my meeting with you be swift. 178.
Then, Sudhana the merchant’s son stood before the Bodhisattva Maitreya with palms joined in reverence and said this: "Noble one, I have set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should train in the conduct of a bodhisattva, nor how one should practice it."

The noble Maitreya has been prophesied by all the Tathāgatas as being bound to only one more birth before attaining unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. And he who is bound to only one more birth before attaining unexcelled, perfect enlightenment has transcended all the stages of the bodhisattvas.
He has entered the fixed course of a bodhisattva;
by him all the perfections have been fulfilled;
he has descended into all the gateways of patient acceptance regarding all aspirations.
By him all the bodhisattva stages have been attained;
he sports in all the gateways of liberation;
by him all the samādhis have been brought to perfection.
He has reached the goal in all the courses of the bodhisattvas;
by him have been attained all the methods of illumination consisting of the dhāraṇīs and eloquence;
he has attained mastery over all the masteries of the bodhisattvas.
By him all the accumulations for awakening have been fully acquired;
he has sported in the methods of skill in wisdom and means;
by him the ways of the light of knowledge and the great supernormal powers and vidyās have been generated.
He has emerged from all the trainings;
by him all the bodhisattva practices have been purified;
by him all the gateways of departure through vows have been brought forth.
By him all the prophecies of the Tathāgatas were received;
he was master of the gateways of departure through all vehicles;
by him all the empowerments of the Tathāgatas were sustained.
By him the enlightenment of all Buddhas is gathered;
by him the treasuries of all Tathāgatas are sustained;
he is the keeper of the storehouse of all the secrets of the Tathāgatas.
He has reached the summit of the secret mandala of all bodhisattvas;
he is a hero amidst the disturbances caused by the lineage of all afflictions;
he is a guide for those who have entered the wilderness of saṃsāra.
He is the physician for those afflicted by the afflictions;
he is the foremost among all sentient beings;
he is Indra, the eldest among all noble persons.

He is the supreme among all noble śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; he is the helmsman for those who have entered the ocean of saṃsāra. By him has been drawn forth the great net of skillful means for the discipline of sentient beings.
By him were surveyed the faculties of beings that had reached maturity;
he was associated with all sentient beings and devoted to the protection of all bodhisattvas.
He was devoted to the communal chanting of the teachings;
he was established within the circles of assemblies of all the Tathāgatas;
and he had attained a reflected manifestation in all the abodes of the world.
He is unstained by any worldly phenomena;
he has transcended all realms of Māra;
he has entered the realm of all Buddhas.
He has attained non-obstruction regarding the entire domain of all bodhisattvas;
he is devoted to the worship of all Tathāgatas;
he has reached a state of one-pointedness regarding all the qualities of a Buddha.
The crown of consecration was bound upon him;
he presided over the great kingdom of Dharma;
and he was consecrated in the domain of the knowledge of the Omniscient One.
From that, there arises the source of all Buddha-dharmas;

for him who has attained awakening, there is sovereignty over the knowledge of the omniscient one. May the Noble One explain to me: how should a bodhisattva [conduct themselves] in the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one train,
how should one practice, so that by practicing in such a way, a bodhisattva attains awakening?
He esteems all the qualities of a Buddha; he delivers the realm of sentient beings just as they were invited; and he fulfills his vow just as it was undertaken.

It provides consolation to the world including the gods by undertaking the practice of great awakening; it does not deceive, for it personally distinguishes itself from all [other] Buddha-dharmas and the Saṅgha.
It ensures that the lineage of the Buddhas is not made empty, [preserving] the family of Bodhisattvas.
He upholds the guidance of the Tathāgata.

Then the Bodhisattva Maitreya, having surveyed that entire circle of the assembly and pointing out the merchant’s son Sudhana, spoke thus: "Behold, noble sons, this son of a merchant who is questioning me regarding the perfection of the qualities of the bodhisattva conduct.
Friends, this merchant’s son, by means of this exertion of vigor..."
By this purposefulness, by this undertaking of aspiration,
and by this firm resolve.
by virtue of irreversible vigor,
by this lack of satiety regarding the qualities of a Buddha,
and by this pursuit of excellence.
With this sense of having one's head and clothes ablaze,
with this longing to see spiritual friends,
and with this tireless devotion in attending upon spiritual friends, he sought out and questioned all spiritual friends.

Having attended upon Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and been dispatched from the city of Dhanyākara, he has traveled throughout the entire southern region, inquiring after more than one hundred spiritual friends, until he has now arrived in my presence with a resolute intention free from all weariness.
Sons of good family, such persons as these who have set out in the Mahāyāna and have undertaken the great vow are difficult to find.
Of those whose minds are resolved upon a great undertaking; whose bodies are armored with great compassion; whose thoughts are intent on protecting sentient beings through great loving-kindness;

who are exerted in the perfection of great vigor; who are dedicated to guarding the caravan of great beings; who have set out to ferry sentient beings across the ocean of great saṃsāra; who have embarked upon the path to omniscience; who are intent on procuring the great ship of Dharma; and who have made a firm resolve to procure the merit of the great jewel of Dharma.

For those who are dedicated to accumulating the provisions for the great sacrifice of Dharma, there is either the hearing of their names, or the seeing of their form-bodies, or dwelling within their sphere of activity, or sharing in their mode of conduct.
Why is that?
For this son of good family, noble beings, has arisen for the sake of protecting the entire world;
