Within that peaked palace, he beheld the trichiliocosm, the great thousandfold world system.
And within that trichiliocosm, he saw a hundred koṭis of four-continent worlds, a hundred koṭis of Jambudvīpas, and a hundred koṭis of Tuṣita abodes.
There, in those Jambudvīpas, he beheld the Bodhisattva Maitreya being born, seated within the womb of a lotus;
being awaited by Śakra and Brahmā, he took seven steps and surveyed the ten directions.

[He saw the Bodhisattva] roaring the great lion’s roar, manifesting all the stages of youth, entering the midst of the inner apartments, departing for the pleasure grove, setting out face-to-face toward omniscience, renouncing the world and undertaking the practice of austerities,
partaking of food, approaching the seat of awakening, subduing Māra, awakening to enlightenment, and gazing unblinking at the Bodhi tree.
He saw [the Buddha] gazing [upon the world], being entreated by Mahābrahmā, setting in motion the wheel of Dharma, and entering the celestial abodes;

[he saw him] through the various distinctions of manifesting the sphere of various perfect awakenings and turnings of the wheel of Dharma, the various distinctions of not turning the wheel of conceptualization, the various distinctions of the measure of lifespan, the various distinctions of the array of various circles of assemblies, and the various distinctions of manifesting the methods for purifying various buddha-fields.

Through the various distinctions in the manifestation of diverse conducts and vows; through the various distinctions in the means for maturing all beings by establishing diverse teachings of the Dharma;

and through the various distinctions in the demonstration of the sustaining power and the abiding of the instruction that analyzes diverse dispositions—in all these places, the merchant’s son Sudhana perceived himself as having come to the feet of each one.

In all the circles of assemblies, in all manifestations of activities, and in all variations of the measure of lifespans, he stood upon the ground of knowledge— which is resolved within the sphere of all perceptions— by means of his unforgetting wisdom established in mindfulness, throughout as many gabled palaces as there were in them.
He heard an inconceivable sound issuing from those beings—like the roar of thunderclouds—arising from the resonance of bells, tinkling ornaments, nets of musical instruments, songs, and so forth.

In some instances, it expressed the diversity of the thought of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*); in some, the diversity of vows for the practice of the perfections (*pāramitā*); in some, the diversity of the immeasurable stages (*bhūmi*);

in some, the diversity of the inconceivable miraculous transformations of the superknowledges (*abhijñā*); in some, the diversity of the various ways of honoring the Tathāgatas; and in some, the diversity of the arrays of Buddha-fields (*buddhakṣetra*).
In some places, he heard the various sounds of the clouds of the Tathāgata’s immeasurable Dharma, just as they had been previously proclaimed;

in other places, he heard the sound of the "setting out toward omniscience": "In such-and-such a world-system, a bodhisattva named so-and-so generates the mind of awakening, having heard such-and-such an entrance into the Dharma and being exhorted by such-and-such a spiritual friend."

At the very feet of the Tathāgata Mukha, in a kalpa of such a name, in a buddha-field of such a kind, having entered into such an assembly, having planted such roots of merit, having heard such qualities of a Tathāgata, with such a resolute intention, and with such a diversity of vows.

Having practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva for this many eons, he will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment after this many eons; he will have such a name, such a lifespan, such a perfection of the array of qualities of a buddhafield,
such a distinction of vows, such a method of disciplining sentient beings, and such an assembly of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas.
After he has attained final nirvāṇa, the true Dharma will remain for this many eons and possess such power.

In some place he heard a voice saying: "In such-and-such a world-system, a bodhisattva named so-and-so, practicing the perfection of generosity, performs hundreds of such difficult acts of renunciation."
Such-and-such a bodhisattva guards ethical discipline,
cultivates patience,
and exerts vigor.
Engaged in the discernment of wisdom, he enters into the meditative absorptions:

"Such-and-such a bodhisattva, for the sake of seeking the true Dharma, renounces his kingdom, renounces his jewels, renounces his sons, renounces his wife, and renounces his hands, feet, eyes, and head."
He throws himself into the fire, thinking:
"The Bodhisattva named so-and-so has emerged for the sake of the Tathāgata’s teaching; he acts as a Dharma-preacher and bestows the gift of the Dharma."
He performs the sacrifice of Dharma,
raises the banner of Dharma,
and beats the drum of Dharma.
He fills the conch of the Dharma,
pours down the rain of the Dharma,
and upholds the teaching of the Tathāgata.
He adorns the reliquaries of the Tathāgatas, has images of the Tathāgatas made,
and provides the requisites for the happiness of sentient beings.
He protects the treasury of the True Dharma.
In some places he heard a voice saying: "In such-and-such a world-system, a Tathāgata named so-and-so currently resides, stays, and maintains himself;

he teaches the Dharma with such a name for his consecration, in such an assembly, in such a Buddha-field, in such an eon, with such a lifespan, through such a teaching of the Dharma, and by such a discipline of sentient beings."

Through such an awakening of his vow, Sudhana heard from each individual object— be it a bell, a small bell, a network of bells, a musical instrument, or the like— an immeasurable variety of sounds proclaiming gateways to the Dharma.
Upon hearing all those sounds, the merchant’s son Sudhana, his heart overflowing with a powerful surge of joy, listened to those gateways of the Dharma.
In some places he attained the gateways of dhāraṇīs,
in some places the gateways of aspirations, and in some places the gateways of patient acceptances.
In some places, the gateways of conduct;
in some places, the gateways of aspiration;
in some places, the gateways of the perfections.
In some places, the gateways of the superknowledges;
in some places, the gateways of the light of knowledge and wisdom;
in some places, the gateways of liberation.
In some places, he attained the gateways for entering into meditative absorption.
And from those mirror-spheres, he perceived immeasurable manifestations of arrays of representations:
in some, the manifestation of the circles of the Tathāgatas’ assemblies; in some, the manifestation of the circles of the Bodhisattvas’ assemblies;
in some, the manifestation of the circles of the Śrāvakas’ assemblies; and in some, the manifestation of the circles of the Pratyekabuddhas’ assemblies.
In some places, there was the representation of the reflected appearance of the Tathāgata’s assembly circle;
in some places, the representation of the reflected appearance of defiled fields; in some places, the representation of the reflected appearance of pure fields;

in some places, the representation of the reflected appearance of both defiled and pure fields; and in some places, the representation of the reflected appearance of all Buddhas within a single world-system.
In some places, there was the representation of the manifestation of Buddha-worlds; in some, the representation of the manifestation of limited worlds;
in some, the representation of the manifestation of vast worlds; in some, the representation of the manifestation of subtle worlds;
in some, the representation of the manifestation of expansive worlds; and in some, the representation of the manifestation of worlds entering like a magical net.

In some places he saw the representation of a world-system appearing inverted; in some places, the representation of a world-system appearing with its bottom at the top; in some places, the representation of a world-system appearing as entering a level ground-surface; in some places, the representation of a world-system appearing as illuminated by the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts; and in some places, the representation of a world-system filled with gods and humans.
And upon those walking-paths and in their respective seats, he saw incalculable bodhisattvas engaged in various activities:

some walking back and forth, some exerting themselves, some gazing intently, some pervading all with great compassion, some bringing forth various systems of treatises connected to the welfare of the world, and some teaching them.

Some were engaged in private recitation, some in writing, some in questioning others, some devoted to the teaching and dedication of the three divisions [of the Dharma], and some were accomplishing their aspirational prayers.
And from those pillars, he beheld nets of light rays from all the finest jewels streaming forth:
in some places blue-colored, in some yellow-colored, in some red-colored, in some white-colored, in some crystal-colored, in some gold-colored,
in some sapphire-colored, in some rainbow-colored, and in some the color of Jāmbūnada gold.
In some places he saw [trees] with a color like universal radiance, supremely generating joy in body and mind and delighting the eyes;
and he saw those plantain trunks the color of Jāmbūnada gold, as well as figures made of every kind of jewel, with hands holding clouds of flowers, hands holding garlands of blossoms,

hands holding parasols, banners, and flags, hands holding perfumes, incense, and ointments, hands holding various wonderful golden threads of many jewels, hands holding various pearl necklaces, and hands holding necklaces of diverse gems.
He saw some with hands grasping every kind of array, others with their crest-jewels and crowns bowed down, with unblinking eyes and palms joined in reverence,
paying homage; and from those pearl necklaces, he saw fine clouds of water, endowed with eight qualities and perfumed with all fragrances, streaming forth.
And from those nets of Vaiḍūrya-jewel necklaces, he saw long rows of water trickling down;
he saw those jeweled parasols, adorned with the array of every ornament;
and he saw that interior decorated with a collection of jewel-bells, tinkling bells, nets, silk ribbons, garlands, and clusters of variegated jewel-sticks and precious gem-treasures.
And from those lotus ponds, he saw countless jewel-lotuses—blue, red, white, and yellow—emerging;
some were only the size of a span, some were the size of a fathom, and some were the size of a chariot wheel.
And within them, he beheld various kinds of magnificent arrays.

That is to say, he saw [beings] in the form of women, men, boys, and girls; in the forms of Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors; in the forms of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; and in the forms of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—possessing bodies with the shapes and forms of all living beings, of various and diverse colors, with palms joined in reverence, bodies bowed low, and paying homage.
And he saw the forms of Tathāgatas, their bodies adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, seated cross-legged.
And upon that great earth, which had a surface of lapis lazuli and was laid out like a checkerboard, he perceived inconceivable manifestations and perceptions from each individual square:
in some places a manifestation of a buddha-field, and in others a manifestation of a Buddha.
And whatever arrays of ornaments were in those gabled chambers, he saw them all reflected within each individual eightfold square.
And from the flower and fruit sheaths of all those jewel-trees everywhere, he saw half-bodies of various forms and diverse golden colors:
in some places, half-bodies of Buddhas; in some places, half-bodies of Bodhisattvas; in some places, half-bodies of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas;

in some places, half-bodies of Śakra, Brahmā, and the world-protectors; in some places, half-bodies of universal monarchs and lords of men; and in some places, half-bodies of princes, guild-leaders, householders, ministers, women, men, boys, girls, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.
Some had their hands hanging down from flower garlands; some had their hands hanging down from jeweled necklaces; some had their hands grasped by all kinds of ornamental arrays;
some were bowing with bodies bent, their palms joined in reverence with unblinking eyes as they paid homage; some were offering praises; some were absorbed in meditative equipoise;
some possessed a radiance of golden color; some possessed a radiance of silver color; and some possessed a radiance of a color as delicate as frost.

He saw some with the luster of sapphire gems, some with the luster of sun-crystal jewels, some with the luster of the color of all kinds of jewels, some with the luster of the color of campaka flowers, some with the luster of a mass of radiance, and some with physical forms variegated by the primary marks.
And from those half-moons, he saw countless reflections of moons, suns, planets, and stars emerge, illuminating the ten directions.
And he saw those walls of palaces, celestial mansions, and gabled halls, variegated with checkered patterns of every kind of jewel.
And upon all those jeweled checkers, he beheld the entire sequence of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Maitreya, just as Bodhisattvas had practiced their conduct in the past.
In one checker, he saw the Bodhisattva Maitreya’s gift of his head.

In some instances there was the gift of eyes; in some, the gift of garments; in some, the gift of crest-jewels and gems; in some, the gift of the crest-jewel of the True Dharma; in some, the gift of teeth; in some, the gift of tongues; in some, the gift of ears and noses; in some, the gift of hearts;
in some, the gift of marrow and flesh; in some, the gift of blood; in some, the gift of skin; and in some, the gift of flesh and nails.
In some instances, there was the giving of hands with webbed fingers; in some, the giving of his entire body; in some, the giving of sons, daughters, and wives;

in some, the giving of heaps of jewels; in some, the giving of villages, cities, market towns, provinces, kingdoms, and royal capitals; in some, the giving of Jambudvīpa; in some, the giving of the four continents; in some, the giving of all royal sovereignty; and in some, the giving of the auspicious royal throne.

In some places there was the gift of male and female slaves; in some places the gift of the inner apartments; in some places the gift of gardens and groves for ascetic practice; in some places the gift of parasols, banners, and flags;

in some places the gift of flowers, garlands, perfumes, and ointments; in some places the gift of medicinal requisites for the sick; in some places the gift of every kind of food and drink according to rule;
in some places the gift of all types of utensils; in some places the gift of all kinds of dwellings; and in some places the gift of bowls made of precious gems and bronze.

In some places he was giving away excellent chariots; in some places he was liberating those who had been cast into prisons; in some places he was releasing those condemned to death; in some places he was treating children; in some places he was showing the way to those who had lost their path;

in some places he was acting as a boatman on a river route, piloting a ship; and in some places, having become the king of horses, Bālāha, he [rescued] those who had reached the island of the rākṣasīs in the great ocean.

In some places he was seen as a great seer (maharṣi) protecting sentient beings; in some places as a sovereign wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) establishing beings in the ten paths of wholesome action; in some places as a physician administering medical treatment to the sick;
in some places attending upon his parents; in some places serving spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra); and in some places in the form and appearance of a disciple (śrāvaka).
Engaged in the discipline of sentient beings, he appears in some places in the form and color of a pratyekabuddha, in some places in the form and color of a bodhisattva,

and in some places in the form and color of a buddha; engaged in the discipline of sentient beings, he manifests rebirth through various special jātaka tales of a sentient being to bring sentient beings to maturity, and in some places, in the form of a dharma-preacher, he teaches those who have entered the teaching of the Tathāgata.

He was engaged in the private recitation of scriptures, applying himself to systematic reflection, adorning the shrines of the Tathāgatas, and having images of the Tathāgatas fashioned; he was encouraging sentient beings toward the worship of the Buddhas, engaging them in every form of Buddha-worship— such as the offering of perfumes and ointments, the anointing with fragrant oils, and the presentation of flowers and garlands—
and establishing sentient beings in the ten roots of goodness, the paths of action, the five precepts, and the eightfold *poṣadha*.

He was engaging sentient beings in taking refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha; in going forth into homelessness; in hearing the Dharma; and in the formal recitation, study, and systematic reflection upon it. Seated upon the lion throne for the sake of Dharma discussion, he was revealing the awakening of a Buddha. Such was Maitreya Bodhisattva.

Sudhana, the merchant’s son, beheld from each and every one of those eight-sided pavilions, through various successive forms, all that had been practiced by him over hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of incalculable eons while fulfilling the six perfections;
and in some of the gabled halls, he beheld the arrays of miraculous manifestations of all the spiritual friends whom the Bodhisattva Maitreya had served.
And as he approached all those spiritual friends, he perceived himself being addressed by them: "Come, Sudhana! Welcome!
Are you not weary?
Behold this inconceivability of the bodhisattvas!"

In this way, Sudhana, the merchant’s son, beheld from each individual peaked pavilion and each individual focal point these and other inconceivable manifestations of arrays within their spheres of activity;

through the power of mindfulness that was never lost, through the purity of vision that investigated all directions, through the unobstructed knowledge of skill in insight, and through the attainment of mastery over the empowerment of the bodhisattva-knowledge, as he proceeded within the range of the bodhisattva’s perception.
Established on the stage of knowledge,
he beheld all those miraculous manifestations within the scope of infinite arrays;
just as, for example, a man who has fallen asleep might see various distinct objects of form within a dream, namely:

He may see things delightful as houses and celestial palaces, or delightful as villages, cities, market towns, and provinces; or delightful as the enjoyment of clothing, food, and drink; or delightful as various pleasures and games involving song, instrumental music, cymbals, and choral performance.

Or he may perceive himself as being in delightful gardens, groves, and ascetic hermitages, or delightful as trees, rivers, lotus ponds, and mountains; or he may recognize himself as having come together with his mother, father, friends, kinsmen, and blood relations.
He might see the great ocean, or Sumeru, the king of mountains, or all the abodes of the gods, or Jambudvīpa;
he perceives himself as being situated at a distance of a hundred yojanas from these,
and he sees that house or chamber as vast.
He perceives it as being nothing but day, adorned with all excellent qualities;
he does not perceive it as night, nor as long, nor as short, nor does he perceive it as sleep.
He perceives for himself a state of well-being;
with the formations of the body calmed and free from sloth and torpor, having cast off all delight, he experiences a vast sense of joy and bliss and perceives for a long duration and on a vast scale—
whether for a day, a week, half a month, a year, a hundred years, or even longer than that.
And having awakened, he would remember it all.

In the very same way, Sudhana, the merchant’s son, through the empowerment of the Bodhisattva and by means of the knowledge that encompasses the dream-like convergence of the entire triple world, had his mind ceased from the sphere of limited perceptions and dwelt in the sphere of the vast, great, and unobstructed perceptions of a Bodhisattva.

Following the domain of the bodhisattvas, his intellect having entered into the inconceivable method of the bodhisattvas, he saw, perceived, experienced, investigated, marked, and observed all those arrays and miraculous transformations; and therein he perceived himself as being established.

For example, it is like a sick man who, while in his final moment of consciousness, when the mind directed toward rebirth has arisen and the existence resulting from karma has become manifest, sees— due to the ripening of the accumulation of karma as performed and conditioned by unwholesome deeds— either a hell, or an animal womb, or the realm of hungry ghosts, or men of Yama holding firm weapons; and he hears the cries and lamentations of the denizens of hell as they are being reviled.
And he would see that river of caustic liquid,
those mountains with razor-sharp edges,
and that thorny Śālmalī tree.
And he would see that forest of sword-leaves,
and those great hells, blazing,
fiercely aflame, and become a single mass of tongues of fire.
And he would see those iron cauldrons; he would perceive those being subjected to torture, and he would recognize those undergoing such sensations.
He might see and experience those agonies of the heat of fire belonging to the denizens of hell,
or, through the accumulation of virtuous karma, he might see a celestial palace.
He would see the assembly of gods and hosts of apsarases, as well as all manner of arrayed ornaments;
or he would see and experience the enjoyments of gardens, celestial palaces, rivers, lotus ponds, jewel-mountains, and wish-fulfilling trees.

He would also recognize the time of his life, thinking: "Having passed away from here, I have been reborn there. Even without being obscured, through the inconceivability of the sphere of karma, he would see, recognize, and experience this activity.
In this very way, the merchant’s son Sudhana, because of the inconceivability of the sphere of the bodhisattva’s activity, beheld all those arrays and miraculous transformations;
just as a man possessed by a spirit sees various forms and whatever he asks about them.
He explains this:
in just this way, through the power of the bodhisattva’s empowerment of wisdom, the merchant’s son Sudhana beheld all those arrays.

It was just as if a man who had entered the abode of the nāgas, by entering into the perception of the nāgas, perceived a day, or seven days, or half a month, or a month, or a year, or a hundred years as a mere perception.
Just as one who has cast off the perception of a nāga might see for a mere moment with the perception of a human,

even so, Sudhana the merchant’s son— having called to mind the Buddha through the perception of a bodhisattva— by virtue of the empowerment of that Bodhisattva Maitreya, perceived in that single moment many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons.

For example, there is a celestial palace of the Great Brahmā named Sarvajagadvaravyūhagarbha (Womb of the Array of the Best of All Worlds). Therein, the entire trichiliocosm appears through the power of manifestation, with all its objective referents remaining unmixed.
In the very same way, the merchant’s son Sudhana perceived all those arrays, each distinct from the others, within all objective referents.

One who has attained manifestation is like a monk dwelling in the meditative attainments of the totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*), who— alone and without a second, whether lying down, walking, sitting, standing, or seated— perceives, sees, and experiences the entire world through his entry into the objective sphere of the totalities, for the sake of the inconceivability of the distinctions of those in dhyāna.
In this very way, the merchant’s son Sudhana beholds and perceives all those arrays by means of his entry into their respective spheres;
just as the arrays and ornaments of all the cities of the Gandharvas appear in the expanse of the sky,
yet do not serve to obstruct anyone.

It is, for example, like human palaces that have entered the palaces of yakṣas; though contained within the yakṣa palaces, they appear distinct from one another, manifesting according to the purity of their respective desired objects.
It is, for example, like the ocean reflections of the entire triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system appearing within the great ocean.
It is, for example, like a magician who, through the empowerment of the power of mantras, spells, and medicinal herbs, perceives all forms and all activities.

In this very way, the merchant’s son Sudhana beheld all those arrays and miraculous transformations through the inconceivable portion of the bodhisattva Maitreya’s power of mastery and illusory wisdom— [wisdom] brought forth by the power of the illusion of the knowledge of phenomena, and attained through the illusory knowledge of the bodhisattva’s sovereign mastery.
Then the Bodhisattva Maitreya, having entered that gabled hall and withdrawn his supernatural empowerment, snapped his fingers at the merchant’s son Sudhana and said this: "Arise, noble son!
Such is the true nature of phenomena."
"Noble son, all phenomena have the characteristic of being non-manifesting and present; they are sustained by the wisdom of the Bodhisattva.
Thus, their intrinsic nature is unestablished, like an illusion, a dream, or a reflection.
Then, at that sound of the finger-snap, the merchant’s son Sudhana arose from that samādhi.
The Bodhisattva Maitreya said to him: "Noble son, have you seen the miraculous transformations through the bodhisattvas' empowerment?
Have you seen the outflow resulting from the power of the bodhisattvas' accumulations?
Have you seen the manifestation of the bodhisattvas' vow-knowledge?"
Have you seen the accomplishments of the bodhisattva practices? Have you heard of the gateways to the bodhisattva's departure [from saṃsāra]?
Have you seen the immeasurable array of the buddha-fields? Have you seen them?
Have you attained the preeminence of the Tathāgata’s vows and fearlessnesses?
Have you followed after the inconceivability of the bodhisattva liberations? Have you experienced the gateway of joy in the bodhisattva samādhis?
Sudhana said: "I have seen it, Noble One, through the empowerment of the spiritual friend and by the power of the spiritual friend.
Nevertheless, Noble One, what is the name of this liberation?
Maitreya replied: "Noble son, this liberation is named 'The Array-Womb of Mindfulness that Enters the Knowledge Taking All Three Times as its Object and is Unfailing.'"
"Noble son, a bodhisattva bound to only one more birth attains such inconceivable, ineffable liberations.
Sudhana asked, "Noble one, where has that array gone?
The bodhisattva Maitreya replied, "It has gone to the very place from which it came."
Sudhana asked, "From where have you come?
Maitreya Bodhisattva replied, "I have come from the manifestation of the empowerment of the bodhisattvas' wisdom;
by that very empowerment, I abide right there."

It has not gone anywhere, nor has it come; it has not become a heap, nor has it become a collection; it is not fixed, nor does it abide as a thing, nor is it established in existence; it is not located in a region, nor is it situated in a specific place.
Noble son, it is just as the cloud-network of the *nāgas* is neither internalized by body or mind, nor does it exist as a collection, yet it is not invisible;
by the power of the *nāga*s' intention, it releases immeasurable streams of water through the inconceivability of the *nāga*s' domain.
In the same way, noble son, those arrays do not exist internally, nor do they exist externally, yet they are not invisible,
by virtue of the bodhisattva’s empowerment and because of your own fitness as a vessel.
Just as, noble son, when a magician displays the entire range of magical illusions, those illusions do not come from anywhere, nor do they go away, nor do they migrate anywhere;
yet they are seen through the power of mantras and medicinal herbs—
exactly so, noble son, these arrays have not gone anywhere, nor have they come from anywhere, nor have they been gathered into a heap anywhere.
And they appear because of their excellent training in the inconceivable illusion of the bodhisattvas' wisdom, through the mastery of the knowledge of the empowerment of former vows.
Sudhana asked, "Noble one, from how far have you come? He replied, "I have gone to the state of non-coming."
Noble son, the movement of bodhisattvas is the movement of immovability and non-abiding;
it is the movement of being without abode or dwelling;
it is the movement of neither passing away nor being reborn.
The movement that does not transition to a fixed location; the movement that is without motion or arising;
the movement that is without regard for or abiding in a dwelling.
The state of no ripening of karma;
the state of neither arising nor ceasing;
the state of neither annihilation nor permanence.

Moreover, noble son, the range of great compassion belongs to bodhisattvas because of their regard for beings to be trained; the range of great loving-kindness belongs to bodhisattvas because of their protection of suffering beings;
the range of ethical discipline belongs to bodhisattvas because of their rebirth according to their aspirations.
The movement of aspiration belongs to bodhisattvas through their prior empowerment; the movement of supernormal knowledge belongs to bodhisattvas by way of manifesting all forms of happiness;
the movement of non-conditioned effort belongs to bodhisattvas by way of never departing from the presence of the feet of all Tathāgatas.
The movement of Bodhisattvas is one free from gathering and dispersing, due to the non-inclination of their body and mind;

the movement of Bodhisattvas is one of wisdom and skillful means, due to their conformity with sentient beings; the movement of Bodhisattvas is one of manifesting emanations, due to the equality of their bodies as reflections, images, and magical creations.
Moreover, noble son, as for what you asked— "From how far have you come?"—
I am coming, noble son, from my birthplace, from the village of Kuṭi in the region of Mālava.
There, there was a merchant named Gopālaka.

Having established him in the Buddha-dharmas and taught the Dharma to the people of that birthplace according to their capacity, and having encouraged his parents, kinsmen, relatives, as well as the brahmins and householders,
toward the Mahāyāna, Sudhana asked: "Noble one, what is the birthplace of the bodhisattvas?"
He said: "Noble son, there are these ten birthplaces of bodhisattvas.
What are the ten?
Namely, the generation of the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) is the birthplace of bodhisattvas."
The high resolve (*adhyāśaya*) is the progenitor of the Bodhisattva family; it is the birthplace of Bodhisattvas.

Born into the family of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), [the spiritual friend] is the progenitor... The establishment in the stages (*bhūmi*) is the birthplace of Bodhisattvas. The progenitor of the family of perfections (*pāramitā*) is... The accomplishment of aspirations (*praṇidhāna*) is the birthplace of Bodhisattvas.
In the family of the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena, [these two] are the parents...
Noble son, the practice of all dharmas is the birthplace of the bodhisattvas;
it is the mother and the birthplace within the family of all the Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present.
Noble son, these are the ten birthplaces of the bodhisattvas.
Noble son, the perfection of wisdom is the mother of bodhisattvas, skillful means is the father,
and the perfection of generosity is the milk.
The perfection of ethical discipline is the nursemaid;
the perfection of patience is the ornamentation;
the perfection of vigor is the nurturer.
The perfection of meditation is the purity of conduct; spiritual friends are the practice of training; all factors of enlightenment are companions;
all bodhisattvas are brothers; and the mind of awakening is the family.
Practice is the family dharma;
abiding on the stages is the attainment of patience;
noble birth is the accomplishment of the vow.
The acquisition of the family lore, the purity of conduct, the adherence to the family dharma, and the instigation toward the Mahāyāna.
The non-interruption of the family lineage; being bound to the single birth of consecration;
being a son among the Dharma-kings; the full realization of all Tathāgatas; and the complete purity of the family lineage.
For in this way, noble son, a bodhisattva has transcended the stage of ordinary worldlings,
has entered the fixed course of the bodhisattvas,
and has been born into the family of the Tathāgatas.
He becomes established in the lineage of the Tathāgatas;
he has set out so that the lineage of the Three Jewels may not be interrupted;
and he is devoted to the protection of the family of Bodhisattvas.
He is pure by birth and lineage;
he is irreproachable in both caste and birth;
he is blameless among all people.
There is no fault in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation including recluses and brahmins;
he becomes of noble birth, born into the supreme family of the Buddhas, his body being the essence of the great vows.

In this way, noble son, bodhisattvas who are enriched by noble lineage and birth do not feel revulsion toward rebirths in any world, because they have thoroughly understood all phenomena as being like reflections.

Because they have thoroughly understood that all births in existence are like magical emanations, they are not defiled while dwelling amidst births in any state of existence. Because they have realized the selflessness of all buddhahood, they do not become weary in the ripening and disciplining of all sentient beings.
Because they have the great loving-kindness and great compassion as their very body, they do not grow weary in their assistance to all sentient beings.

Because they are resolved that saṃsāra is like a dream, they do not feel terror even while dwelling through all kalpas. And because they have thoroughly understood the aggregates to be illusory in nature, they do not become exhausted by witnessing all births, transitions, and deaths.

Because they have become liberated through the natural state of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), they are not harmed by any objects. Because they have well-cultivated all perceptions as being like a mirage, they do not become deluded in any of the states of cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*).
Because they sport with all phenomena as being like an illusion, they remain unstained by the domains of all Māras.
Because they are manifested by means of the entire body, they cannot be deceived by any afflictions;
because they have attained mastery over rebirth, they have reached the further shore in all realms of existence.
Therefore, noble son, with a body that enters into rebirth within all world-systems, I possess specific powers equal to the forms of all living beings.

Through analytical distinctions comparable to all sentient beings, through varieties of names comparable to the entire world, through modes of conduct equal to the inclinations of all sentient beings,
through conformities to the world according to the measure of the discipline of all beings,
and through manifestations of birth and family origins equal to all forms of purity.

Through gateways for the manifestation of activity, by entering into the perceptions of all sentient beings, and by displaying and manifesting physical forms equal to the emanations of the vows of all bodhisattvas,

he pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). For the sake of ripening those beings who had previously shared his conduct but had lost the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), and for the sake of demonstrating the taking of birth in Jambudvīpa, he appeared here in the southern region among the Mālava people.

In order to discipline the parents, kinsmen, and relatives born into brahmin families in the village of Kūṭāgra within the various provinces— and specifically, to bring those who are proud of their caste to a state free from pride by means of a distinguished birth in a brahmin family, and to cause them to be born into the family of the Tathāgata— I have taken birth here. Noble son, it is here in the southern region that I, through this skillful means, am effecting the ripening and discipline of beings according to their inclinations and according to how they are to be guided, right here within this Vairocana-vyūhālaṃkāragarbha [palace].
I dwell in this gabled chamber;
having passed away from here, I shall manifest rebirth in the Tuṣita heaven in order to conform to the inclinations of sentient beings according to their dispositions.
For the sake of ripening those sons of the gods who dwell in the Tuṣita realm and share similar conduct;
for the purpose of manifesting the array of emanations of the merit and wisdom of Bodhisattvas who have transcended the entire realm of desire;
and for the purpose of turning them away from the thirst for sensual pleasures.
For the purpose of illuminating the impermanence of all saṃsāra; for the purpose of demonstrating that all births among the gods end in misfortune;
and for the purpose of chanting together with bodhisattvas bound to one more birth the great gateway to the Dharma called "The Aspect of Passing Away."
In order to gather those who have been matured together with me by causing them to be reborn there,
and in order to awaken those groups of beings to be trained who were sent by Śākyamuni,
I shall at that time attain omniscience, my intention being fully fulfilled.
And when I have attained awakening, noble son, you shall see me once again together with the spiritual friend Mañjuśrī.
Moreover, noble son, go to that very Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta;
having approached him, ask: "How should a bodhisattva train in the conduct of a bodhisattva? How should one practice?"
How should one enter the maṇḍala of Samantabhadra’s conduct?
How should it be brought forth?
How should the vow be made?
How is it to be expanded?
How is it to be followed? How is it to be mastered?
"How should one enter it,
and how should it be fulfilled?
Noble son, that spiritual friend will show you this."
For what reason?
Noble son, there exists a distinction of vows belonging to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas that is equal to that of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
Noble son, the conduct and the way of life of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta are vast.
The accomplishment of the vows of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is immeasurable; the accomplishment of all the specific qualities of a bodhisattva by Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is never-ceasing.
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is the mother of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas;
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is the instructor of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas.
Mañjuśrī, the Youthful, is dedicated to the ripening and disciplining of the realm of all sentient beings.

Mañjuśrī, the Youthful, possesses a vast wheel of names throughout all the world-systems in the ten directions. Mañjuśrī, the Youthful, is the personification of discourse within the ineffable circles of the Tathāgatas' assemblies.

Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was praised by all the Tathāgatas: Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta dwells in the knowledge of the profound Dharma; Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta perceives all phenomena according to their true nature;
Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has a range of experience difficult to attain within the methods of all liberations.
He has entered the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
O son of good family, he is your producer of spiritual friends and your nurturer within the family of the Tathāgatas.
He is the one who causes all roots of virtue to arise, the one who reveals the accumulations for enlightenment,
the one who inspires others toward true spiritual friends, and the one who leads them into entry upon all virtuous qualities.
He is the one who establishes [beings] in the great net of vows,
the one who causes them to hear regarding the accomplishment of all vows,
and the one who reveals all the secrets of the bodhisattvas.
He has shared conduct with all the inconceivable bodhisattvas throughout their cohabitations in previous births.
Therefore, son of good family, while you are still at the feet of Mañjuśrī, do not give rise to a limited mind.
Do not give rise to weariness regarding the attainment of the instructions on all virtuous qualities.
For what reason? Sudhana, as many spiritual friends as you have seen, [so many are there to be met].
As many gateways of conduct as have been heard, as many methods of liberation as have been entered,
and as many specific vows as have been penetrated;
All this should be seen as the power and the sustaining grace of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta;
and that Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta has attained the supreme perfection.

Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, bowed his head at the feet of the Bodhisattva Maitreya, circumambulated the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya hundreds of thousands of times, and, looking back at him again and again,
departed from the presence of the Bodhisattva Maitreya. 52.
(Gv 419) 55. Mañjuśrī:
Then Sudhana, the merchant’s son, having wandered through more than one hundred cities, arrived at the region of the Sumanāmukha direction.
Having gone there, he stood reflecting upon Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, gazing after him, longing for a vision of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, praying for it, and desiring his encounter.
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, extending his hand from more than a hundred yojanas away, [reached] while he was still situated in the city of Sumanāmukha.
Placing [his hand] upon the head of the merchant’s son Sudhana, he said: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!

It is not possible for those who lack the faculty of faith, whose minds are weary, whose minds are dejected, who have not practiced application, whose vigor has turned back, who are satisfied with minor virtues, who are absorbed only in a single root of goodness, who are unskilled in accomplishing the vows of conduct, who are not sustained by spiritual friends, and who are not attended by the Buddhas—to know this nature of reality."
"This is the method, this is the domain, this is the dwelling— to be known, or to be fathomed, or to be entered, or to be resolved upon, or to be conceptualized, or to be realized, or to be attained.

Having thus instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dharma, he caused him to be endowed with incalculable gateways of the Dharma, caused him to attain the great radiance of infinite wisdom, and caused him to enter the sphere of the knowledge of the Bodhisattva’s boundless dhāraṇīs, eloquence, meditative absorptions, superknowledges, and gnosis.
Having caused him to enter the maṇḍala of the conduct of Samantabhadra and having established him in his own country, he departed from the presence of the merchant’s son Sudhana. // 53 //
(Gv 420) 56. The Vow of the Conduct of Samantabhadra.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana had attended upon as many spiritual friends as there are atoms in a great trichiliocosm world-system.

His mind was accumulated with the provisions for omniscience; he practiced by receiving the instructions and admonitions of all spiritual friends with respectful compliance; he was extended toward the equality of intention toward all spiritual friends; his intellect was intent on neither pleasing nor displeasing any spiritual friend; he had entered the oceans of the methods of the instructions and admonitions of all spiritual friends; and the womb of his being was born from the ocean of the intention of great compassion.

He was one who illuminated the entire world with clouds of the method of great loving-kindness; his body was nourished by the force of great joy; he dwelt in the tranquil abode of the vast liberation of a bodhisattva;

his eye of renunciation extended toward universal happiness; he was perfectly fulfilled in the practice of the ocean of qualities of all Tathāgatas; he had set out upon the path of devotion to all Tathāgatas; his vigor for the equipment of omniscience was ever-increasing; and his intellect was well-transformed by the mental dispositions and intentions of all bodhisattvas.

He has descended into the succession of all Tathāgatas of the three times; he has awakened to the oceans of the methods of all Buddha-dharmas; he has followed the oceans of the methods of the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas;

his sphere of activity is the manifestation of appearances in all births within the worlds; he has entered the oceans of the methods of the vows of all Bodhisattvas; he has set out upon the Bodhisattva conduct throughout all eons; he has attained the illumination of the domain of omniscience; and he has been developed by the faculties of all Bodhisattvas.

He had attained the illumination of the path to omniscience; he had reached the light that dispels the darkness of all directions; his intellect had extended into the methods of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); he had become manifest with the illumination of the methods of all buddha-fields; he followed the current contrary to the stream in performing purposeful deeds for the sake of the vast multitude of all sentient beings; he had shattered the mountains of precipices of all obscurations and followed the nature of reality (*dharmatā*) which is free from obscuration; and he dwelt in the peaceful abode of the bodhisattva-liberation called the "Womb of the Realm of Phenomena" on the ground of the universal foundation.
Seeking the domain of all Tathāgatas, sustained by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, he remained there while investigating the domain of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
having heard the name of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and having heard of his conduct of awakening and his particular vows.

And having heard [this], having heard the distinction of the establishment in the setting forth that arises from the equipment, having heard the distinction of the path of departure through accomplishment, having heard the conduct and investigation of the stage of Samantabhadra, having heard the equipment for the stages, having heard the distinction of attainment,
having heard the momentum of the acquisition of the stages, having heard the treading upon the stages, and having heard the stabilization in the stages...
Having heard this, and having heard of the prowess and valor of the stages, having heard of the majesty of the stages, having heard of the empowerment of the stages,

and having heard of dwelling upon the stages, he became intensely yearning for a vision of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; and right there at that Vajrasāgaragarbha seat of awakening, facing the lion throne of the Tathāgata, he sat down upon a lotus throne with a core of all kinds of jewels.
With a mind as vast as the element of space, free from all attachments;
with a well-cultivated perception of all buddha-fields;
with a mind that has transcended all clinging.
With a mind unimpeded, having as its range all phenomena without obstruction; with an unobstructed mind, pervading the oceans of all directions;
with a pure mind, advancing into the domain of omniscience.
With a well-discriminated mind purified by the insight that adorns the seat of enlightenment,
and with a vast mind that has entered the ocean of all the qualities of a Buddha;
With a vast mind that pervades the ripening and disciplining of the realm of all sentient beings; with an immeasurable mind that purifies all buddha-fields;

with an infinite mind that attains reflection within the circles of all buddhas' assemblies, remains unexhausted throughout cohabitation in all eons, and culminates in the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities of a buddha of all Tathāgatas.

Thus, for the merchant’s son Sudhana, who was thus engaged in mental attention, there appeared ten preliminary signs for the sake of seeing the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra— due to the moistening of his own former roots of merit by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, and through his commonality of former roots of merit with the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
What are the ten? Namely, all buddha-fields were purified by the purification of the adornments of the enlightenment seats (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all Tathāgatas.
All buddha-fields were purified by being turned away from all unfavorable conditions, states of woe, and paths of miserable rebirth;
all buddha-fields were purified by the purification of the buddha-field arrayed as a lotus pond of Dharma;
all buddha-fields were purified by the attainment of refreshing joy for the bodies and minds of all sentient beings.
All buddha-fields were purified by being composed entirely of all kinds of jewels;

all buddha-fields were purified by being adorned with the primary and secondary marks of the entire realm of sentient beings; all buddha-fields were purified by being adorned with the primary and secondary marks of the entire realm of sentient beings.

All buddha-fields were purified by being established as clouds of every kind of arrayed ornament; all buddha-fields were purified by being established as the state of mutual minds of loving-kindness, benefit, and non-malice toward the realm of all sentient beings;
all buddha-fields were purified by being established as the arrays of ornaments of the seat of awakening.
All buddha-fields were purified by virtue of the manifestation of the mental application of the recollection of the Buddha for all sentient beings;
these ten preliminary signs appeared for the sake of seeing the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra.
Ten other great radiances appeared as a premonitory sign for the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra’s vision.
What are these ten?
Namely, within every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, the nets of all Tathāgatas shone forth.

From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, clouds of light-mandalas of all Buddhas— of many colors, various colors, and hundreds of thousands of various colors— issued forth and pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, clouds of all kinds of jewels issued forth, manifesting the reflections of all Tathāgatas, and pervaded the entire realm of phenomena.
From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, clouds of circles of light-rays of all Tathāgatas issued forth and pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, clouds of all kinds of perfumes, flowers, garlands, ointments, and incense issued forth.
Having issued forth, they thundered like clouds from the ocean of all the qualities and dharmas of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and pervaded the entire realm of phenomena in the ten directions.
From every single atom among all the atoms of dust in all world-systems, clouds of light from all the moons, suns, and stars issued forth, emitting the radiance of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
They pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, clouds of lamps manifesting the physical forms of all sentient beings issued forth; shining like the light rays of a Buddha, they pervaded the entire realm of phenomena.

From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, clouds of jewel-forms reflecting the bodies of all Tathāgatas issued forth and pervaded the entire realm of phenomena in the ten directions.
From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, clouds of radiant forms in the shape of the bodies of all Tathāgatas [issued forth].
Having issued forth, raining down clouds of vows empowered by all Buddhas, they pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

From every single atom among all the atoms of all world-systems, there emerged oceans of clouds reflecting the bodies of Bodhisattvas, manifesting the radiance of all forms and colors, engaged in the activity of emanating for the sake of all sentient beings, and accomplishing the fulfillment of every intention of all sentient beings.
Having issued forth, they pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
These ten great radiances appeared as the preliminary signs of the vision of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having seen these ten manifestations of prior signs,

obtained the opportunity to see the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; supported by the power of his own roots of goodness, filled with the radiance of the teachings of all Buddhas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, permeated by the vows of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, facing toward the sphere of activity of all Tathāgatas, he attained the empowerment of the power of certainty regarding the vast sphere of activity of Bodhisattvas.
Perceiving the attainment of the light of omniscience through the vision of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, with faculties directed toward the vision of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
having attained the impetus of great vigor for the vision of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, applying irreversible vigor while searching for the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
with a wheel of faculties facing all directions, and with a bodhisattva body that enters the range of the eye of Samantabhadra.

With a mind sent forth with all Tathāgatas as its object, following after the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra who has gone to the feet of all Buddhas without exception; with an intention that does not stray from the search for the object of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; with a womb filled with the perception of seeing the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in all objects; [and] extended upon the path of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra...

With the eye of wisdom, with an intention as vast as the realm of space, with a resolute determination well-sustained by the vajra of great compassion, with an empowerment extending through kalpas reaching the furthest limit of the future, with a vow of continuous pursuit following the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, with a purity of successive strides that accords with the equality of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, by dwelling within the domain of all Tathāgatas, and by abiding in the knowledge that establishes one upon the stages of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Endowed with this power, he saw the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra seated upon a lion throne in the center of a great jewel-lotus before the Blessed One Vairocana, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One; surrounded by an ocean-like assembly of bodhisattvas, encircled by a host of bodhisattvas, and honored by a community of bodhisattvas, his body rose up loftily, extending beyond all the circles of the assembly.
It surpasses all worlds, is beheld by all bodhisattvas, has the domain of infinite wisdom, possesses an unassailable range, and has an inconceivable object;
it conforms to the equality of the three times and has attained the equality of all Tathāgatas.
From every single pore of his skin—from each and every pore—he [emanated] as many [lights] as there are atoms in all world-systems.

He saw rays of light issuing from clouds, illuminating all world-systems as far as the limits of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), pacifying the suffering of sentient beings.

He saw clouds of circles of light, equal in number to the atoms within all Buddha-fields, issuing from his body, appearing in various colors and increasing the force of noble joy and gladness in all bodhisattvas.

From his crown, from his two shoulders, and from all the pores of his skin, he saw clouds of fragrant light-rays of various colors being emitted; having pervaded the circles of assemblies of all the Tathāgatas, they were seen raining down.

From each and every pore of his skin, he saw clouds of all kinds of flowers—equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-fields—being emitted; having pervaded the circles of assemblies of all the Tathāgatas, they were seen raining down.
From every single pore of his skin, he saw clouds of all kinds of fragrant trees being emitted, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields;

these clouds, reaching to the limits of the realm of space, adorned the entire realm of phenomena with the ornaments of fragrant tree-clouds. He saw them pervading the circles of assemblies of all Tathāgatas, which were furnished with inexhaustible treasuries of powdered incense and ointments, raining down [offerings].

From every single pore of his body, he saw clouds of all kinds of garments issuing forth from each individual pore, covering and adorning the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) as far as the limits of the space-element (ākāśadhātu).

From every single pore of his body, he saw clouds of all kinds of silk ribbons, clouds of all kinds of ornaments, clouds of all kinds of pearl necklaces, and clouds of wish-fulfilling jewel-gems (cintāmaṇiratna), as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, issuing forth from each individual pore.
Having pervaded the circles of assemblies of all the Tathāgatas, he saw them raining down [flowers] for the sake of fulfilling every intention of all sentient beings.
From every single pore of his skin, he caused clouds of jewel-trees, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, to issue forth;
these pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) to its limit in the expanse of space, adorning it with an array of clouds of jewel-trees that were completely filled.
He saw [the Tathāgatas] having formed the maṇḍalas of the assemblies of all the Tathāgatas, raining down great showers of jewels;

and from every single pore of their skin, he saw clouds of deva-hosts from the realm of form, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, emerging and praising the Bodhisattva while pervading all world-systems.

From every single pore of his skin, from each individual pore, he saw clouds of emanations produced by all the classes of gods belonging to the Brahma-realms emerging, and he saw them entreating the Tathāgatas who had attained perfect enlightenment to turn the wheel of Dharma.

From every single pore of his skin, from each individual pore, he saw clouds of bodies of the lords of gods of the entire desire realm emerging, and he saw them receiving all the wheels of Dharma of the Tathāgatas.

From every single pore of his skin, at every moment of thought, he saw clouds of all Buddha-fields belonging to the three times— equal in number to the atoms within all Buddha-fields— issue forth from each individual pore; pervading the entire realm of phenomena as far as the limits of space, they became the shelter, protection, and refuge for those beings who were without shelter, without protection, and without refuge.

From every single pore of his skin, at every moment of thought, he saw clouds of utterly pure buddha-fields— equal in number to the atoms in all buddha-fields, filled with the assemblies of bodhisattvas and the manifestations of all Buddhas— issue forth, pervading the entire realm of phenomena as far as the limits of space, and remaining there for the purification of sentient beings who possess noble aspirations.

From every single pore of his skin, at every moment of thought, he saw clouds of buddha-fields— equal in number to the atoms within all buddha-fields— issuing forth from each individual pore; these clouds, both pure and defiled, pervaded the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) as far as the limits of space, acting for the purification of afflicted sentient beings.

From every single pore of his body, at every moment of thought, he saw clouds of fields for purifying defiled minds, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, emerge from each individual pore; pervading the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) to its limit in the expanse of space, they functioned for the purification of those realms that were exclusively defiled.

From every single pore of his skin, at every moment of thought, he saw clouds of the bodies of all bodhisattvas— equal in number to the atoms within all buddha-fields— issue forth; pervading the entire realm of phenomena as far as the limits of space, they followed the conduct of all sentient beings and brought all beings to maturity for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

From every single pore of his skin, at every moment of thought, he saw clouds of bodhisattva bodies as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issue forth; pervading the entire realm of phenomena to the limits of the space-element, they proclaimed the names of all Buddhas in order to increase the roots of goodness of all sentient beings.
From every single pore of his skin, from each and every pore, he saw clouds of bodhisattva bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields emerge;

pervading the entire realm of phenomena to the limits of the space-element, they were seen in the expansion of all buddha-fields, bringing forth and gathering together all the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas from their first production of the thought of enlightenment.

From every single pore of his skin, from each individual pore, he saw clouds of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields emerge; in every single Buddha-field throughout all Buddha-fields, they illuminated the oceans of all bodhisattva vows for the sake of purifying the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. From every single pore of his skin, from each individual pore, he saw [clouds] as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields that fulfill the intentions of all sentient beings.
He saw [them] emerging from clouds of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra— which increase the force of joy in the attainment of omniscience— and raining down [upon all beings].
From every single pore of his body, from each and every pore, [he saw them] as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields.
He saw clouds of perfect enlightenment emerging, which manifest the realization of awakening in all Buddha-fields and increase the great momentum of the Dharma for the attainment of omniscience.

Then, having seen this miraculous display of the supernatural power of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, the merchant’s son Sudhana was thrilled, satisfied, elated, uplifted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness;
gazing upon the body of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra with even greater intensity, he beheld the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
From each individual limb, from each division of a limb; from each individual part of the body, from each division of a bodily part;
from each individual region of a limb, from each division of a regional limb-part; from each individual body, from each division of a body; from each individual pore of the skin.

From each single pore-aperture, he [manifests] this triple-thousand great-thousandfold world-system with its mass of wind, its mass of earth, its mass of fire, along with its oceans, its continents, its rivers, its jewel-mountains, its Sumerus, its Cakravāla ranges, its villages, towns, market-towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals, its forests, its abodes, its populations of beings, and its hell-realms.
[He beholds] the world of animals, the world of Yama, the world of asuras, the world of nāgas, the world of garuḍas, the world of humans, the world of devas,
and the world of Brahmā; the domain of the realm of desire, the domain of the realm of form, with its foundations, its supports, its structures,
with its clouds, its lightning, its celestial bodies, with its nights and days, its half-months, its months, its seasons, and its years.
It was peaceful yet with mental activity;
and just as he saw this world-system, so too did he see all world-systems in the eastern direction.
Just as in the eastern direction,
so too in the south, west, north, northeast, southeast, southwest, northwest,
below, above, and all around— in every direction and intermediate direction— he beheld all world-systems by means of the manifestation of his spiritual power.
He saw all the appearances of Buddhas together with their circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas and their sentient beings;

and he also saw, from a single mark of a Great Man on the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, all the successions of world-systems throughout the past limit within this Sahā world-system, including all those appearances of Buddhas.

He saw all the circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas, together with their sentient beings, their abodes, their nights and days, and their eons; likewise, he saw the entire expansion of all buddha-fields reaching to the furthest limits of the future.
Just as he saw here in this Sahā world-system the succession of all world-systems reaching from the limit of the past to the limit of the future, so too did he see them.

In this way, in all world-systems throughout the ten directions, he beheld the successions of all world-systems extending to the limits of the past and the future, each clearly distinguished and mutually unconfused, emerging from every single mark of a great man and every single pore of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra’s body.

And just as he saw the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra seated upon a lion throne within a great jewel-lotus matrix in the presence of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, displaying this very miraculous play, even so did he see this same miraculous play being displayed in the eastern direction, in the world-system Padmaśrī, in the presence of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī.
And just as it was in the eastern direction, [so it was in all directions].

In this way, he saw Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, seated upon a lion throne within a great jewel-lotus matrix at the feet of all Tathāgatas in all world-systems throughout every direction and intermediate direction, displaying this very same miraculous play;
and just as it was in the ten directions, so too...

In this way, he saw him seated upon lion thrones in the centers of great jewel lotuses at the feet of the Tathāgatas in all world-systems, manifesting this very same miraculous play. Likewise, throughout the ten directions, in as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms, and within each single atom—
in the vast circles of assemblies for the Buddha-dharma throughout the entire realm of phenomena— at the feet of every Tathāgata, he saw Samantabhadra.
He saw the Bodhisattva;
and from each of his individual bodies, he saw all objective referents belonging to the three times being made known through the power of manifestation,
and he saw all buddha-fields, all sentient beings, all appearances of Buddhas, and all circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas being made known through the power of manifestation.

And he heard the cries of all sentient beings, the voices of all Buddhas, the turnings of the wheel of Dharma by all Tathāgatas, all the miracles of instruction and teaching, the attainments of all Bodhisattvas, and the playful manifestations of all Buddhas.
Having seen and heard that inconceivable play of the great bodhisattva Samantabhadra, he attained ten dwellings of the perfection of knowledge (*jñānapāramitāvihāra*).
What are the ten?
Namely, in a single moment of thought, he attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge that pervades all buddha-fields with his body.

He attained the dwelling of the perfection of unimpeded knowledge for approaching the feet of all Tathāgatas; he attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge for honoring and serving all Tathāgatas;
and he attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge for receiving and inquiring about every single dharma of all Buddhas from each and every Tathāgata.

He attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge consisting in the realization of the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Tathāgatas; he attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge consisting in the inconceivable miraculous transformations of a Buddha; he attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge consisting in the teaching of a single dharma-phrase through the empowerment of eons reaching the furthest limit of time, by means of the inexhaustible analytical knowledges regarding all dharmas.
He attained the dwelling of the perfection of direct knowledge of the seal of all phenomena;

he attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge of the ocean of methods of the entire realm of phenomena; he attained the dwelling of the perfection of knowledge of dwelling within the range of perceptions of all sentient beings.
In a single moment, he attained the dwelling of the perfection of direct knowledge regarding the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
To Sudhana, the merchant’s son, who was thus endowed with that dwelling of the perfection of knowledge, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra extended his right hand and placed it upon his head.
As soon as the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra had placed his hand upon the head of the merchant’s son Sudhana, [he attained further realizations].
Then, at that very moment, as many gateways of meditative concentration (*samādhimukha*) as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields entered into him.
Through each single meditative concentration, he descended into seals (*mudrā*) as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields.
Furthermore, as many accumulations for omniscience (*sarvajñatā-saṃbhāra*) as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields—which had never been seen before—attained increase within him.
There appeared for him sources for the arising of all-knowledge equal in number to the atoms in all buddha-fields;
he had set out upon great departures toward all-knowledge equal in number to the atoms in all buddha-fields;
and he had entered oceans of vows equal in number to the atoms in all buddha-fields.
He has set forth upon paths leading to omniscience as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields;
he has extended himself into bodhisattva practices as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields;
and he has been strengthened by the impetuses toward omniscience as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields.
He was illuminated by the radiance of the wisdom of all Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields.
Just as here in this Sahā world-system, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, seated at the feet of the Blessed One Vairocana, extended his right hand and placed it upon the head of Sudhana,
so too in all world-systems, seated at the feet of all Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra extended his right hand and [placed it] upon the head of the merchant’s son Sudhana.
He established [them].

In this manner, seated at the feet of all Tathāgatas throughout all world-systems— even those contained within the atoms of every world-system in all directions and intermediate points— Samantabhadra Bodhisattva extended his right hand.
He placed it upon the head of the merchant’s son Sudhana;

and just as when the merchant’s son Sudhana was touched by the hand of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, who had gone to the feet of the Blessed One Vairocana, various gateways of the Dharma entered into him.
Thus, as the merchant’s son Sudhana was touched by clouds of hands emanating from all the bodies of Samantabhadra, gateways of the Dharma entered his mind through various methods.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra said this to the merchant’s son Sudhana: "Noble son, have you seen my miraculous manifestation?
He replied, "I have seen it, O Noble One;
yet even a Tathāgata, knowing fully, would only know this miraculous manifestation as inconceivable."
He said: "Noble son, for aeons equal to the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, I have wandered about longing for the mind of omniscience.
And in each great aeon, while purifying the thought of awakening, I have propitiated Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
And in each great aeon, I have performed great sacrifices renowned throughout all the worlds, characterized by the relinquishing of everything."
It is the dedication of all beings toward the accumulation of merit for omniscience;
and in each great eon, he has performed great acts of giving— unspeakably unspeakable numbers of gifts equal to the atoms in an incalculable number of Buddha-fields.
Excessive renunciations were made by him while aspiring for the qualities of omniscience;
and in each great eon, inexpressibly inexpressible numbers of self-existences were relinquished,
as well as great kingdoms.
Villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and capitals were renounced;
beloved and charming retinues, so difficult to give up, were renounced;
sons, daughters, and wives were renounced.
The flesh of his own body was relinquished;
blood was relinquished from his own bodies for those who asked;
and bones and marrow were relinquished.
The limbs and members were relinquished;
the ears and noses were relinquished;
the eyes were relinquished.

Out of regard for the wisdom of a Buddha, they renounced their tongues from their own mouths, being indifferent to body and life; and in each great eon, they renounced from their own bodies as many heads as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, aspiring for the head of supreme omniscience that rises above all worlds—
just as in each great eon.
Likewise, throughout oceans of great eons equal in number to the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields,

and in each single great eon, he honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields, acting as their supreme sovereign; he served them with robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick.
And I have gone forth in the teaching of those Tathāgatas, practiced all the instructions of the Buddhas, and upheld their teaching.
Noble son, throughout those oceans of eons, I do not recall ever having produced even a single thought of causing disruption within the teaching of the Tathāgata;
nor do I recall, throughout those oceans of eons, ever having produced even a single thought accompanied by resentment,
or a mind of self-grasping, or a mind of grasping at what belongs to a self, or a mind that perceives a difference between self and others, or a mind that wanders away from the path to enlightenment.

Or a mind weary of dwelling in saṃsāra, or a discouraged mind, or a mind clouded by obscurations and delusion— none of these can arise in me, except for the bodhicitta that is the invincible, hard-to-conquer womb of wisdom regarding the accumulations for omniscience. Thus, noble son, even if all the oceans of kalpas were to come to an end while I describe those applications of mine for purifying the buddha-fields through my former yogic practices, [they would not be exhausted].
Whatever applications I have for the protection, maturation, and purification of all beings, having attained a mind of great compassion; likewise,
whatever applications I have for honoring and attending upon the Buddhas, and whatever applications I have for serving my teachers for the sake of seeking the true Dharma— [all these I dedicate].

O noble son, among those oceans of Dharma, there is not even a single word or syllable that was not purchased by me through the renunciation of my own body for the sake of upholding the true Dharma, nor through the renunciation of my own life for the sake of protecting the true Dharma.

That which is not [attained] by one who has renounced all possessions, who is dedicated to the protection of all sentient beings, who is dedicated to the contemplation of his own mental continuum, who is dedicated to the actual realization of the dharmas of others, who is dedicated to the manifestation of the light of all worldly knowledge,
who is dedicated to the manifestation of all supramundane knowledge, and who is dedicated to generating the happiness of saṃsāra for all sentient beings.
Engaged in praising the qualities of all Tathāgatas,

even if oceans of kalpas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields were to pass while I described the excellence of my own former yogic accomplishments, they would come to an end.

By means of this, O son of good family, through such power of accumulations, power of the cultivation of root causes, power of noble resolve, power of the practice of virtues, power of the thorough investigation of all phenomena as they truly are, power of the eye of wisdom, power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment, power of the great vow, power of great compassion, power of the thoroughly purified superknowledges, and power of being sustained by spiritual friends— by these I [have attained this state].
The absolutely pure *dharmakāya*, undifferentiated throughout all three times, has been attained;

and the unsurpassed *rūpakāya* has been purified, risen above all worlds, making itself known according to the inclinations of all beings, pervading everywhere, extending into all buddha-fields, established universally, and manifesting all miraculous transformations in every direction.

"O noble son, behold this excellence of the attainment of my physical form, which has arisen from an ocean of infinite eons, whose appearance is difficult to encounter for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons, and the sight of which is rare. Noble son,
I do not even come within the range of hearing of those beings who have not planted roots of virtue, much less within the range of their sight."
There are, noble son, beings who, merely by hearing my name, become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
there are those [who do so] merely by seeing me.
There are those [who attain it] by mere touch; there are those by mere following; there are those by mere pursuit.
There are those who, by seeing me in a dream,
or by hearing my name in a dream, become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; some beings, by recollecting me for even a single day and night, reach full maturity.

Some, remembering me for half a month, some for a month, some for a year, some for a hundred years, some for a kalpa, some for a hundred kalpas, and some for as many kalpas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, proceed toward full maturity.
Some reach full maturity by recollecting me after a single birth;
some after a hundred births; and some after as many cycles of births as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Some beings reach maturity by seeing my radiance;
some by the manifestation of the emission of light rays;
and some by the shaking of the buddha-field.
Some reach maturity through the manifestation of the form-body, and some through being inspired with joy.
Thus, noble son, by means of skillful methods as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, sentient beings become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
