Furthermore, noble son, those beings who hear of the purification of my buddha-field are reborn in purified buddha-fields;
and those who behold the purification of my physical body, [are likewise reborn there].
They are reborn within my own body.
Behold, noble son, this purity of my physical form!

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, contemplating the body of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, beheld within each and every pore of his skin unspeakable oceans of Buddha-fields, filled with the appearance of Buddhas;
and in each and every ocean of Buddha-fields, he beheld Tathāgatas surrounded by oceans of assemblies of Bodhisattvas.

And he saw all those oceans of fields— with their various foundations, various configurations, various arrays, various perimeters, various clouds covering the sky, various appearances of Buddhas, and various sounds of the turning of the wheel of Dharma— just as he saw them in each single pore,
so too did he see them without exception in all the pores, in all the primary marks, in all the secondary characteristics, and in every major and minor limb.

And in each [of those pores], he saw clouds of emanated Buddha-bodies emerging from as many oceans of fields as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields; having gone forth, they pervaded all world-systems in the ten directions, bringing sentient beings to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Then, indeed, the merchant’s son Sudhana, having been instructed by the advice and exhortation of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra, entered into all the world-systems contained within the body of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra and brought sentient beings to maturity.

Furthermore, as for the accumulations of roots of goodness, the light of wisdom, and the visits, sightings, and services rendered to spiritual friends as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, which belonged to the merchant’s son Sudhana—

By the mere sight of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, they do not approach even a hundredth part of the accumulation of roots of merit; nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor a hundred-thousand-ten-millionth part.
They do not admit of any calculation, fraction, reckoning, comparison, or analogy, from the first production of the thought of enlightenment up to the sight of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
In the meantime, as many successions of oceans of Buddha-fields as he had entered, even more than that— inexpressibly inexpressible numbers of Buddha-fields equal to the atoms of dust—
successions of oceans of Buddha-fields entered into a single pore of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra at every moment of thought.
And just as it was in one pore, so it was in all.
In the same way, within every pore of his skin, at every moment of thought, he did not reach the limit of world-systems equal in number to the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields—

world-systems sustained by the empowerment of eons reaching beyond the furthest limit of the future— nor did he reach the end of successions of oceans of fields, matrices of oceans of fields, divisions of oceans of fields, convergences of oceans of fields, or the arising of unspeakably unspeakable oceans of Buddha-fields.
of the splendors of oceans of buddha-fields, of the arrays of oceans of buddha-fields, of the wombs of oceans of the arising of Buddhas, of the convergences of oceans of the arising of Buddhas,
of the origins of oceans of the arising of Buddhas, of the manifestations of oceans of the arising of Buddhas, of the oceans of circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas,
of the successions of oceans of circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas, and of the wombs of oceans of circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas.
of the differentiations of the oceans of the circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas; of the convergences of the oceans of the circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas;

of the origins of the oceans of the circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas; of the manifestations of the oceans of the circles of assemblies of bodhisattvas; of the entries into the realm of sentient beings; of the entries into the knowledge that perceives the faculties of sentient beings at every moment; and of the penetrations of the knowledge of the faculties of sentient beings.

He did not reach the limit of the ripening and disciplining of sentient beings, nor of the profound abodes of the miraculous transformations of Bodhisattvas, nor of the oceans of prowess in entering the stages of Bodhisattvahood;
in some fields, he wandered for an eon.
In some fields, he wandered for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields;
yet, he did not move from those fields.
And in every single moment of mind, he entered into oceans of fields that were infinite and without center.
And he brought sentient beings to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Gradually, he attained the equality of the ocean of vows and the conduct of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;

the equality of all Tathāgatas; the equality of traversing all buddha-fields and bodies; the equality of fulfilling the conduct; and the equality of manifesting the miraculous transformations of supreme awakening.

He has attained the equality of turning the wheel of Dharma, the equality of the purity of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), the equality of the utterance of sound, the equality of the application of the ocean of all vocal qualities, the equality of the powers and fearlessnesses, the equality of the Buddha-abodes, the equality of great loving-kindness and great compassion, and the equality of the inconceivable miraculous transformations of the bodhisattva-liberations.

Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, illuminating in this very way eons and successions of eons as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields throughout the succession of world-systems, made his vow with even greater intensity by singing these verses:
"However many lions among men there may be in the worlds of the ten directions, throughout all the three times,"
I pay homage to all of them without exception, with body, speech, and mind, full of serene devotion. // 1 //
With bodies as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, I pay homage to all the Victors, with a mind directed toward all the Victors through the power of the vow of the *Bhadracaryā*. (2)
Upon a single atom, Buddhas as numerous as atoms sit amidst the sons of the Buddhas;
in this way, I have full conviction that the entire realm of phenomena is completely filled with Jinas. (3)
And within those [oceans of worlds], proclaiming the oceans of inexhaustible praises of all the Victors through the sounds of oceans of all vocal qualities, I praise all those Sugatas. 4.

With the finest flowers and the finest garlands, with the finest musical instruments, ointments, and parasols, and with the finest lamps and the finest incense, I perform worship to those Victors. // 5 //

With the finest garments, the most excellent perfumes, and jars of powdered incense as vast as Mount Meru, and with all the most distinguished and sublime arrays, I perform worship to those Victors. // 6 //
And whatever unsurpassed, sublime worship there may be, I resolve upon it for all the Victors;
by the power of my resolve in the *Bhadracarī*, I pay homage to and worship all the Victors. (7)
Whatever sin I may have committed under the influence of passion, hatred, or delusion, whether by body, speech, or mind, I confess all of that. (8)

And whatever merit exists in the ten directions belonging to those in training, those beyond training, and the Pratyekabuddhas, as well as to the sons of the Buddhas and all the Victors—that I rejoice in all of it. (9)
And those lamps of the world in the ten directions who have awakened to enlightenment and attained non-attachment—to all those Protectors, I entreat you to turn the unsurpassed wheel. 10.

And to those who desire to manifest parinirvāṇa, I pray with palms joined: may they remain for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, for the benefit and happiness of the entire world. 11.
Whatever merit I have accumulated through prostration, worship, confession, rejoicing, supplication, and entreaty, I dedicate it all toward awakening. 12.
May the Buddhas of the past be honored; may those who dwell in the worlds of the ten directions now be present;
and may those yet to come quickly fulfill their aspirations and awaken to enlightenment. (13)
May whatever realms there are in the ten directions become pure and magnificent; may they be filled with Victors who have reached the king of Bodhi-trees and with the sons of the Buddhas. // 14 //
May whatever beings there are in the ten directions always be happy and free from illness; may the righteous welfare of the entire world be accomplished, and may their aspirations be fulfilled. 15.
And while practicing the conduct of awakening, may I remember my births in all states of existence;
in all lives, through death and rebirth, may I always be one who has gone forth into homelessness. 16.

Training myself in accordance with all the Victors and fulfilling the conduct of Samantabhadra, may I always practice the stainless and pure conduct of ethical discipline, unbroken and without flaw. (17)

Through the languages of gods, the languages of nāgas, and the languages of yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, and humans—indeed, through whatever languages exist in the world—I teach the Dharma in all those languages. (18)
May those who are indeed devoted to the perfections never lose sight of the mind of awakening;
and may all those evil obstructions be completely exhausted without remainder. (19)

May I wander liberated from karma, from afflictions, and from the path of Māra within the realms of the world, unstained like a lotus by water and unattached like the sun and moon in the sky. // 20 //

Pacifying all the sufferings of the miserable realms and establishing the entire world in happiness, may I act for the benefit of the whole world throughout the paths of all the realms in every direction. 21.
Following the conduct of sentient beings, fulfilling the conduct of awakening, and manifesting the sublime conduct, may I practice throughout all future eons. // 22 //
May I always meet with those who share my same conduct; may I practice the vow of a single way of life through body, speech, and intention. 23.
And may I always meet with those friends who desire my welfare and show me the way of the *Bhadracaryā*; may I never at any time cause them to be dissatisfied. (24)
May I always behold the Victors face-to-face, surrounded by their sons, O Lord;
and may I perform magnificent worship toward them throughout all future eons without weariness. (25)
Upholding the true Dharma of the Victors, illuminating the conduct of awakening, and purifying the practice of the auspicious conduct, may I practice throughout all future eons. (26)
And while wandering through all states of existence, may he attain inexhaustibility in merit and wisdom;
through insight, skillful means, meditative concentrations, and liberations, may he become an inexhaustible treasury of all virtuous qualities. // 27 //

Upon a single atom there are fields equal in number to all atoms; and within those fields, while practicing the conduct of awakening, he beholds inconceivable Buddhas seated in the midst of their sons.

In this way, throughout all directions without exception, within the paths of the ignorant, he enters oceans of Buddhas, oceans of realms, and oceans of practices and eons, as vast as the measure of the three times.

Through the ocean-like sounds of the various components of a single voice, may they always enter into the purity of the vocal qualities of all Victors and the voices of all Victors according to their inclinations— the eloquence of the Buddhas.
And within those inexhaustible sounds and voices, may I enter by the power of my intellect, turning the wheel of the method of all the Victors belonging to the three times. (31)
In a single moment, may I enter all future eons; and those eons whose measure is the three times, may I practice within them, having entered into ten million moments.
And those lions among men who have appeared throughout the three times, may I behold them all in a single instant;
and may I always enter their sphere of activity through the power of liberation that consists of the state of illusion. 33.
And those arrays of the fields of the three times, he brings forth upon the tip of a single atom;
in this way, he enters without exception into the arrays of the fields of the Victors in all directions. (34)

And those lamps of the world who are yet to come, in whom the awakening and the turning of the wheel [of Dharma] shall occur—in all those Protectors who abide in the ultimate peace of the manifestation of nirvāṇa, I shall approach. (35)

By the power of supernatural faculties with universal speed, by the power of knowledge with universal gates, by the power of conduct with universal virtues, and by the power of loving-kindness that reaches everywhere. // 36 //

By the power of merit, which is all-pervading purity, and by the power of knowledge, which has reached non-attachment, and by the power of wisdom, skillful means, and meditative concentration, he fully accomplishes the power of awakening. // 37 //
Purifying the power of karma, crushing the power of the afflictions, and rendering the power of Māra powerless, may I fulfill all the powers of the conduct of excellence. 38.
Purifying the ocean of fields, liberating the ocean of sentient beings, discerning the ocean of dharmas, and plunging into the ocean of gnosis. // 39 //
Purifying the ocean of conduct, fulfilling the ocean of aspirations, and making offerings to the ocean of Buddhas, may I practice throughout the ocean of eons without weariness. // 40 //

And whatever specific vows for the conduct of awakening there are of the Victors who have gone throughout the three times, may I fulfill them all without exception, having awakened to enlightenment through the conduct of Samantabhadra. 41.
To the eldest son of all the Victors, whose name is Samantabhadra—
to that wise one, I dedicate all this merit for the sake of his shared conduct. (42)
May there be purity of body, speech, and mind, as well as purity of conduct and purity of the field;
O Bhadra, may I become equal to that wise one in every respect. 43.
May I practice the *Bhadracaryā*, which is all-pervadingly auspicious, according to the vow of Mañjuśrī;
may I fulfill every single one of those deeds without exception throughout all future eons, untiring. (44)
There would be no measure to their conduct, nor would there be any measure to their virtues;
abiding in this immeasurable conduct, I know all their miraculous transformations. (45)
As far as the limit of space may extend, and as far as the limit of sentient beings without exception;
as far as the limit of karma and afflictions extends, so far shall the limit of my vow extend. (46)

And those who might give to the Victors chariot-ornaments in infinite realms throughout the ten directions, and divine and human excellences of happiness, for as many eons as there are atoms in a realm; (47)
And whoever, having heard this King of Dedication, should once give rise to resolute faith while aspiring for supreme enlightenment—this merit would be foremost and most distinguished. (48)
By him the states of woe are avoided; by him evil friends are avoided.
He quickly beholds that Amitābha who possesses this vow of the Excellent Conduct.
A great gain is well-attained and a life well-lived by them; welcome to this human birth!
For just as Samantabhadra is, so too shall they become before long. (50)
Whoever has committed the five evil deeds of immediate retribution through the power of ignorance, by reciting this *Bhadracaryā*, shall swiftly bring them to total exhaustion without remainder. (51)
Endowed with knowledge, form, characteristics, complexion, and lineage, he is unassailable by the hosts of heretics and Māras, and is honored throughout the entire triple world. (52)
Swiftly he goes to the king of Bodhi trees; having gone there, he sits down for the welfare of sentient beings.
He awakens to enlightenment, turns the wheel [of Dharma], and subdues Māra along with his entire army. 53.

Whoever upholds, recites, or teaches this Prayer of Excellent Conduct—the Buddha knows the ripening of its fruit here; it is a distinguished awakening, so do not harbor doubt, but generate [aspiration]. (54)
Just as the heroic Mañjuśrī knows, and likewise Samantabhadra, following their example, I dedicate all this merit. (55)
Whatever supreme dedication has been praised by all the Victors throughout the three times, with that I dedicate all this merit toward the practice of the Excellent Bhadra. (56)
And when I am making my end, having turned back all obscurations, may I behold Amitābha face to face and go to that realm of Sukhāvatī. (57)

Having gone there, may all these vows of mine be fully realized in their entirety; and having fulfilled them all without exception, may I bring about the welfare of sentient beings as far as they exist in the world. (58)
There, having been born in that beautiful and delightful, excellent, and radiant lotus within the circle of the Jinas,
may I receive the prophecy of enlightenment there in the presence of the Victorious Abhitābha.

Having obtained this prophecy, may I, by the power of my intellect, perform many deeds for the benefit of sentient beings in all ten directions through hundreds of millions of various emanations. (60)

Whatever slight merit I have accumulated by reciting this *Bhadracari-praṇidhāna*, may it all be perfected in a single instant, and through that, may the auspicious aspiration of the world be fulfilled. (61)

By the merit that has been acquired, which is infinite and exceedingly distinguished, through dedicating the *Bhadracaryā*, may the world, submerged in the flood of calamities, go indeed to the supreme city of Amitābha. (62)
The Blessed One spoke thus, and Sudhana the merchant’s son was uplifted in mind, as were those bodhisattvas headed by the noble Mañjuśrī,
and those monks who had been ripened by the noble Mañjuśrī.
And those bodhisattvas of the Bhadra Kalpa, headed by the noble Maitreya;

and those great bodhisattvas, equal in number to the atoms of the earth, who have been consecrated to the position of crown prince and are headed by the noble Samantabhadra, having gathered from various world-systems;
and those great śrāvakas, headed by the noble Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana.
And that entire assembly,
as well as the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, had spoken.

This is the portion of the practice of Sudhana’s attendance upon spiritual friends as obtained from the noble *Gaṇḍavyūha*, the great Dharma discourse; here ends the noble *Gaṇḍavyūha*, the king of jewels among Mahāyāna sūtras.
Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has explained their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
Twelve thousand.
